## Preface {#preface .unnumbered}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


::: flushright
*"Physics has diverged away from its heroic journey of exalting and
uncovering deeper, simpler physical models of reality."\
--- E. McGucken, FQXi Essay 2009*
:::

This textbook is written in the spirit of the great founding figures
upon whose shoulders physics stands: Galileo, who staked his life on the
bold claim that the Earth moves (*e pur si muove!*); Newton, who took
mathematics to be the language by which the heavens spoke (*Philosophiae
Naturalis Principia Mathematica*); Faraday, who saw lines of force where
others saw empty space; Maxwell, who wove those lines into the
electromagnetic field equations from which light itself is derived;
Planck, who let himself be *forced* to the quantum of action by the
empirical record; Einstein, who in his 1912 Manuscript wrote $x_4 = ict$
for the fourth coordinate and asked us to take the $i$ seriously; Bohr,
who taught that what nature is depends on how it is observed;
Schrödinger, who declared entanglement "not ... *one* but rather *the*
characteristic trait of quantum mechanics, the one that enforces its
entire departure from classical lines of thought" (Schrödinger 1935,
*Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc.* **31**, 555); and Wheeler, the last figure from the heroic age, who taught
the present author at Princeton and, looking out the window of his
Jadwin Hall office in 1989, said: *"Today's world lacks the
noble --- and it's your generation's duty to bring it back."* This book
is a partial answer to that call.

This textbook develops quantum mechanics in the same axiomatic mode that
Newton's *Principia* developed mechanics and that Euclid's *Elements*
developed geometry: from a single physical principle, by a chain of
theorems each proved with proof-environment rigor, with no postulate
inserted along the way.

The principle is the *McGucken Principle*:
$$\boxed{\ \dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic\ }$$ read physically as the statement
that the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light, in a
spherically symmetric manner, from every spacetime event. Every other
claim of quantum mechanics that mainstream pedagogy (illustrated by
Sakurai & Napolitano, Shankar, Griffiths & Schroeter, Cohen-Tannoudji et
al., and Weinberg) treats as an independent postulate appears here as a
numbered theorem with a proof.

The treatment is structured by the typical architecture of mainstream QM
pedagogy (with the five textbooks above as illustrative exemplars),
expanded to absorb every topic any of them covers, and rebuilt as a
chain of theorems descending from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. Each major
result is proved *twice* along the two channels of the **McGucken
Duality** (equivalently, the **$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ Duality** or the
**McGucken $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ Duality**;
Definition [13.18](#def:mcgucken-duality){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:mcgucken-duality"}): once along the
**$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ Geometric Channel** (the more foundational of
the two channels, the geometric-propagation route through the McGucken
Sphere expanding at $+ic$ from every event with iterated Huygens
propagation, henceforth referred to as the *Geometric Channel*), and
once along the **$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ Algebraic Channel** (the
operator-theoretic route through Stone's theorem, Stone--von Neumann
uniqueness, and the Wigner classification, henceforth referred to as
the *Algebraic Channel*). The two derivations share no
intermediate machinery beyond the principle and the final equation; the
result is forced twice, by derivationally disjoint routes. *No great
discovery was ever made without a bold guess*, Newton wrote; *for an
idea that does not at first seem insane, there is no hope*, Einstein
added. The double-derivation property of every QM theorem is the bold
guess proposed; the agreement of the two derivationally disjoint channels
is the audit.

**Origin and lineage.** The McGucken Principle originated in
undergraduate work conducted at Princeton under John Archibald Wheeler,
in projects on the Schwarzschild time factor, Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen
and delayed-choice experiments, and time-reversal asymmetry. It first
appeared in print as an appendix to the author's 1998--99 UNC Chapel
Hill doctoral dissertation. It was developed across five foundational
essays submitted to the Foundational Questions Institute (FQXi) between
2008 and 2013
[@FQXi-1-Time-2008; @FQXi-2-Heros-Journey-2009; @FQXi-3-Emergence-2011; @FQXi-4-Triumphs-2012; @FQXi-5-Honor-2013],
two books (2016--17), and the ongoing series of forty-plus technical
papers at
[`elliotmcguckenphysics.com`](https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/),
culminating in the May 2026 synthesis paper [@Syn-2026] from which the
chain of theorems in Parts II--III of this book is drawn. The reader is
encouraged to consult those papers for the historical and philosophical
context.

**On the audit standard.** Every theorem in this book is held to what we
shall call the Princeton-PhD-level standard: every step is either a
theorem of a deeper principle, an explicitly invoked assumption (labeled $A_1, A_2, \ldots$), or a citation to a standard
mathematical result. *In questions of science, the authority of
thousands is not worth the humble reasoning of one individual*
(Galileo); a derivation that rests on appeal to expert consensus where
it should rest on appeal to a principle has, in this book, no place. If
a derivation cannot be done rigorously, the gap is explicitly stated.

The reader is assumed to have completed an undergraduate course in
classical mechanics, electromagnetism, and special relativity at the
standard Halliday--Resnick or Kleppner--Kolenkow level, plus the
linear-algebra prerequisite carried by any Hilbert-space treatment. No
prior exposure to the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is assumed;
Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"} develops the framework from the principle.

**Standing convention.** Wherever $x_{4}= ict$ appears as an identification, it is to be read as the *integrated kinematic shadow* of
the dynamical principle $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The physical content
is the active spherical expansion; the coordinate label $x_{4}= ict$ is
its mere integrated shadow. Every theorem in this book traces to the
active expansion. The $i$ in $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the
perpendicularity marker of the fourth dimension; the $i$ in
$\psi = A\exp(-imc^2\tau/\hbar)$, in $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, in
$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$, in the path-integral phase
$e^{iS/\hbar}$, in the $+i\varepsilon$ prescription of Feynman diagrams,
and in the Wick rotation to Euclidean signature, is the *same*
$i$ --- the algebraic shadow of the same geometric fact.

Dr. Elliot McGucken\
May 2026

## Reader's Guide {#readers-guide .unnumbered}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


**Organisation.** The book has four parts.

[Part I: Foundations and the Diagnosis]{.smallcaps} (Chapters
1--4). Chapter 1 audits mainstream quantum-mechanics pedagogy (with five
leading textbooks as illustrative exemplars) against the McGucken
framework as a diagnostic. Chapter 2 develops the historical
and phenomenological introduction in the manner of Weinberg's Chapter 1
and Shankar's Chapter 3, but ends with the McGucken Principle as the
answer to the phenomenology rather than with a list of postulates.
Chapter 3 develops the mathematical toolkit (Hilbert spaces,
self-adjoint operators, Stone's theorem, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality,
the Wigner classification). Chapter 4 establishes the McGucken Principle
as the single postulate of quantum mechanics and constructs
the McGucken manifold $M_{G}$, the McGucken Sphere $S$ and its iterates
$M^{+}_{p}(t)$, and the Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel axiom sets (QA1--QA7 and
QB1--QB7).

[Part II: The Twenty-Three Quantum Theorems]{.smallcaps} (Chapters
5--13). The complete chain QM T1 through QM T23. Each theorem is proved
twice, once along the Geometric Channel and once along the Algebraic Channel, with
cross-references to the audit theorem (which proves the disjointness of the two chains, Theorem 125 in the corpus).

[Part III: Applications and Standard Topics]{.smallcaps} (Chapters
14--19). The harmonic oscillator, angular momentum and hydrogen,
identical particles, time-independent and time-dependent perturbation
theory, the variational principle and WKB, scattering theory, density
matrices and mixed states, and the path integral. These are the standard
graduate-textbook topics, derived from the theorem chain rather than
from an independent postulate list.

[Part IV: Synthesis]{.smallcaps} (Chapters 20--22). The measurement
problem, entanglement and Bell-inequality violation, and the resolution
of the conceptual difficulties of the textbook tradition via the
dual-channel architecture.

**Conventions.** Theorems are numbered consecutively within each chapter
(e.g., Theorem 3.4 is the fourth theorem of Chapter 3). Where a result
coincides with a theorem in the McGucken synthesis paper of May 2026,
the synthesis-paper theorem number is given in the statement (e.g.,
"Theorem 4.7 (= Theorem 69 in \[Syn-2026\])"). The reference
`[Syn-2026]` throughout refers to the present author's synthesis paper,
fully cited in the bibliography. Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel derivations are
tagged with their corresponding axioms (QA1--QA7, QB1--QB7) as those
axioms are introduced in Chapter 4.

**Audit standard.** Every theorem in this book satisfies the Princeton
PhD-level standard: each step is either a theorem from a labeled deeper
principle, an explicitly invoked assumption (labeled
$A_1, A_2, \ldots$), or a citation to a standard mathematical result. No
assertion-as-derivation; no proof environments around plausibility
paragraphs; if a derivation cannot be done rigorously, the gap is
explicitly stated.

## The Principle in One Page: Minkowski Space, the Schrödinger Equation, and the Born Rule {#ch:one-page}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.

The expansion is a physical motion. At every event of $M_{G}$ the fourth
dimension advances at $c$, and because the advance is spherically
symmetric it sweeps out, from each event $p$, a spherical wavefront of
radius $c(t-t_p)$: the McGucken Sphere. The Sphere is the physical object
this book works with, and the three results below follow from it in a few
lines each. The full derivations, with every step anchored, are Theorem
[4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"},
Theorem [7.1](#thm:QMT7){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT7"}, and
Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}.

**Minkowski space.** Write the expansion in differential form,
$dx_{4} = ic\,dt$, and square it:
$$dx_{4}^{2} \;=\; (ic\,dt)^{2} \;=\; -c^{2}dt^{2}.$$ The spatial part of
the expansion is isotropic, so the three spatial directions enter with
the Euclidean form $dx^{2}+dy^{2}+dz^{2}$. Adding the two gives the line
element
$$ds^{2} \;=\; dx^{2}+dy^{2}+dz^{2} \;-\; c^{2}dt^{2},$$ which is the
Minkowski metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. The perpendicularity marker
$i$ in $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is what supplies the minus sign, and the
spherical symmetry is what supplies the Euclidean spatial block. Lorentz
transformations are the maps preserving this line element, so
$SO^{+}(1,3)$ arrives as the isometry group of the geometry the expansion
generates.

**The Schrödinger equation.** The expansion proceeds from *every* event,
so every point reached by a wavefront is itself a source of the next
wavefront. That is Huygens' construction, and here it is a statement
about a physical front rather than a computational device. Composing
successive fronts from $\mathbf{x}'$ at $t$ to $\mathbf{x}$ at
$t+\varepsilon$ sums over the intermediate paths, each carrying the phase
the expansion accumulates along it, $\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$, with $\hbar$
the action per $x_{4}$-cycle. The sum over paths is the Feynman
propagator
$$K(\mathbf{x}, t+\varepsilon;\, \mathbf{x}', t) \;=\;
\Bigl(\tfrac{m}{2\pi i\hbar\varepsilon}\Bigr)^{3/2}
\exp\!\Bigl[\tfrac{i}{\hbar}\bigl(\tfrac{m(\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}')^{2}}{2\varepsilon}
- V\varepsilon\bigr)\Bigr],$$ and expanding it to first order in
$\varepsilon$ gives
$$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi \;=\; -\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\nabla^{2}\psi + V\psi .$$
The Schrödinger equation is the first-order content of iterated Sphere
propagation.

**The Born rule.** The wavefront at each event is a $2$-sphere, and the
expansion is spherically symmetric, so the rotation group $SO(3)$ acts
transitively on it. On a compact group the invariant probability measure
is unique (Haar), so the expansion distributes its weight over the
wavefront in exactly one way: uniformly. The density paired from $\psi$
and $\psi^{*}$ by the rank-$2$ Minkowski metric is bilinear, hence
$$P(\mathbf{x},t) \;=\; |\psi(\mathbf{x},t)|^{2}.$$ Probability enters
this book as the normalized measure the expanding Sphere carries, and it
is an output of the geometry rather than an input to it.

**The order of the derivation.** The expansion is first. The Sphere is
what the expansion generates. Huygens' Principle applied to successive
Spheres gives the path integral and the Schrödinger equation; the compact Sphere's unique
invariant measure gives probability; squaring the expansion gives the
metric, whose isometry group gives Lorentz covariance. Nothing in that
sequence is assumed at the start and recovered at the end.


## Glossary of Acronyms and Abbreviations {#glossary-of-acronyms-and-abbreviations .unnumbered}

The following acronyms and abbreviations are used throughout this book.
They are listed here in alphabetical order for quick reference, and each
is also defined on first use within the section where it first appears.

ADM

:   Arnowitt--Deser--Misner formulation of general relativity (3+1 spacetime split into spatial slices plus a lapse-and-shift evolution).

AdS/CFT

:   Anti-de-Sitter / Conformal Field Theory correspondence (Maldacena's gauge--gravity duality).

BCFW

:   Britto--Cachazo--Feng--Witten recursion (on-shell recursion relations for scattering amplitudes).

CCR

:   Canonical Commutation Relation, $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$.

CFT

:   Conformal Field Theory.

CGE

:   Cosmic Geometric Engine (object of McG${}_6$; the global cosmological-scale geometry).

CHSH

:   Clauser--Horne--Shimony--Holt inequality, a Bell-type inequality with classical bound 2 and quantum (Tsirelson) bound $2\sqrt{2}$.

CKM

:   Cabibbo--Kobayashi--Maskawa quark-mixing matrix of the Standard Model.

CMB

:   Cosmic Microwave Background radiation.

CP

:   Charge--Parity (the combined transformation; CP-violation = matter--antimatter asymmetry).

CPT

:   Charge--Parity--Time-reversal (combined inversion; CPT-theorem = exact symmetry of relativistic QFT).

EH

:   Einstein--Hilbert (action of general relativity, $S_{\mathrm{EH}} = (c^4/16\pi G)\int R\sqrt{-g}\,d^4x$).

EPR

:   Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen (1935 paper, "Can quantum-mechanical description of physical reality be considered complete?").

FRW

:   Friedmann--Robertson--Walker cosmological metric (homogeneous, isotropic universe).

GHZ

:   Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger entangled state (three-particle maximally-entangled state).

GR

:   General Relativity (Einstein 1915).

GRB

:   Gamma-Ray Burst.

GRW

:   Ghirardi--Rimini--Weber spontaneous-collapse model (continuous spontaneous localisation).

HUP

:   Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle, $\Delta q\,\Delta p \ge \hbar/2$.

IR

:   Infrared (low-energy / long-wavelength regime).

KG

:   Klein--Gordon equation, $(\Box + m^2 c^2/\hbar^2)\psi = 0$.

KMS

:   Kubo--Martin--Schwinger thermal-state condition (defining equilibrium in quantum statistical mechanics).

LHC

:   Large Hadron Collider (CERN, Geneva).

LIGO

:   Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory.

LIV

:   Lorentz Invariance Violation.

LTD

:   Light Time Dimension theory (synonym for the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework; the older name for the principle developed since 1998).

MC

:   Matter Coupling (the matter-interaction specification distinct from the postulate; see Def. [4.32](#def:postulate-plus-coupling){reference-type="ref" reference="def:postulate-plus-coupling"}).

McG$_6$

:   The six-object source-tuple of the McGucken positive-geometry programme; see Chapter [13](#ch:mcg6-positive-geometry){reference-type="ref" reference="ch:mcg6-positive-geometry"}.

MCC

:   Matter--Channel Categorical (object of McG${}_6$; the local matter-coupling category).

McT

:   McGucken Theory (general designation; see Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref" reference="postulate:mcp"} and [@Syn-2026]).

NV

:   Nitrogen--Vacancy (defect in diamond used for quantum sensing).

ODE

:   Ordinary Differential Equation.

QCD

:   Quantum Chromodynamics (the gauge theory of strong-force interactions; gauge group $SU(3)_c$).

QED

:   Quantum Electrodynamics (gauge theory of electromagnetism; gauge group $U(1)$).

QFT

:   Quantum Field Theory.

QM

:   Quantum Mechanics. In this book, QM T$k$ refers to the $k$-th of the 23 quantum-mechanical theorems QM T1--T23.

RGC

:   Relational Geometric Constructor (object of McG${}_6$; the relational/categorical geometry).

RTI

:   Relativistic Transactional Interpretation (Kastner--Schlatter, 2023, an interpretation of QM; *not* engaged by this book, see endnote).

SM

:   Standard Model of particle physics (gauge group $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$).

SP

:   Postulate (the geometric/algebraic statement of a theory's arena; see Def. [4.32](#def:postulate-plus-coupling){reference-type="ref" reference="def:postulate-plus-coupling"}). In this book SP is the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$.

SPDC

:   Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (source of entangled photon pairs).

SVD

:   Singular Value Decomposition.

TT

:   Transverse--Traceless gauge (a gauge for gravitational-wave polarizations).

UV

:   Ultraviolet (high-energy / short-wavelength regime).

WKB

:   Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin semiclassical approximation.

## The Diagnosis: Mainstream Quantum-Mechanics Pedagogy against the McGucken Framework {#ch:diagnosis}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


### On the heroic quest in physics: the simplest axioms and the unbroken thread of honor {#sec:heroic-quest}

::: flushright
*"It can scarcely be denied that the supreme goal of all theory is to
make the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible
without having to surrender the adequate representation of a single
datum of experience."\
--- Albert Einstein, "On the Method of Theoretical Physics," the Herbert
Spencer Lecture, Oxford, 10 June 1933 [@Einstein1933Spencer]*
:::

The diagnosis of
§§[1.2](#sec:postulate-versus-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:postulate-versus-theorem"}--[1.13](#sec:dual-channel-ledger){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:dual-channel-ledger"} is a technical instrument, but the
question it addresses is not technical. The question is whether the
foundations of quantum mechanics can be reduced to a single physical
principle, with everything else as a theorem. That question is not new.
It is the question Einstein raised before the Prussian Academy of
Sciences in January 1921 [@Einstein1921Geometry] when he asked how the
propositions of mathematics relate to the propositions of physics. It is
the question Hilbert raised at the Paris International Congress of
Mathematicians in August 1900 [@Hilbert1900Sixth] when he listed, as
Problem 6 of his twenty-three problems for the new century, the
"Mathematical Treatment of the Axioms of Physics." It is the question
Hilbert returned to in September 1917 [@Hilbert1917Axiomatic] in the
Zürich address whose title named the method this book uses:
*Axiomatisches Denken*, axiomatic thinking. And it is the question von
Neumann undertook to answer for quantum mechanics in his 1932
*Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik* --- what the historian
Chris Mitsch [@Mitsch2024] has named von Neumann's *axiomatic
completion* of quantum mechanics. This book is a continuation of that
quest.

#### The quest as articulated by the Giants {#ssec:heroic-giants}

The axis on which this book is graded is the same axis on
which Einstein, Hilbert, and von Neumann graded the theories they cared
about. The relevant statements are explicit in the historical record; we
record three.

###### Einstein, 1933 (Oxford).

The opening epigraph of this section is the verbatim text from p. 165 of
the journal version of the Herbert Spencer Lecture
[@Einstein1933Spencer]. The statement makes three things precise: (a)
the supreme goal of theory is the reduction of basic elements; (b) the basic elements should be simple and few; (c) the
reduction must not surrender the adequate representation of any single
datum of experience. The McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is
in this sense an attempt at exactly the form of theory Einstein
characterised as the supreme goal: one foundational element from which
the backbone of quantum mechanics is derived, with no datum
of experience surrendered.

###### Einstein, 1921 (Berlin).

In his 1921 address to the Prussian Academy of Sciences, "Geometrie und
Erfahrung" (Geometry and Experience), Einstein recorded the function of Hilbert's axiomatic method [@Einstein1921Geometry]:

> *As far as the propositions of mathematics refer to reality, they are
> not certain; and as far as they are certain, they do not refer to
> reality. ... Complete clarity as to this state of things became common
> property only through that trend in mathematics which is known by the
> name of 'axiomatics.' The progress achieved by axiomatics consists in
> its having neatly separated the logical-formal from its objective or
> intuitive content; according to axiomatics the logical-formal alone
> forms the subject matter of mathematics, which is not concerned with
> the intuitive or other content associated with the logical-formal.*

Einstein's diagnosis identifies the axis directly: the
axiomatic method separates the logical-formal content of a theory from
its intuitive or physical content. Mainstream quantum-mechanics pedagogy
as audited in §[1.6](#sec:comparison-table){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:comparison-table"} below (with the five textbooks of
§[1.4](#sec:toc-and-posture){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:toc-and-posture"} as illustrative exemplars) is graded on
whether the standard presentations of quantum mechanics preserve this
separation --- whether they make explicit which propositions are
postulated and which are derived, and whether the postulates are
reducible to a single physical principle. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is the
answer to Einstein's diagnostic question for the case of quantum
mechanics: the logical-formal content of the theory is derived as a
chain of theorems from the single physical postulate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with the intuitive content (the expansion of
the fourth dimension at the velocity of light) made explicit as the
physical referent of the principle.

###### Hilbert, 1917 (Zürich).

In his address "Axiomatisches Denken" delivered to the Swiss
Mathematical Society in Zürich on 11 September 1917
[@Hilbert1917Axiomatic], Hilbert recorded the role of axioms
in the development of a field of knowledge:

> *The fundamental propositions of an area of knowledge can be seen from
> an initial standpoint as the axioms of that field. The continuing
> development of that field of knowledge is then founded merely on the
> further logical development of the already presented framework of
> concepts.*

Hilbert's diagnosis identifies the function of axioms as
initial standpoints from which further development is logical rather
than postulational. The McGucken framework realises this for quantum
mechanics: $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the initial standpoint; the
twenty-three quantum theorems QM T1 through QM T23 of Part II are the
further logical development; no additional postulate is required.

#### The Wheelerean lineage and Wheeler's charge {#ssec:wheeler-charge}

The axiomatic tradition that descends from Hilbert, Einstein,
and von Neumann was carried into the second half of the twentieth
century most consistently by John Archibald Wheeler --- the student of
Bohr, teacher of Feynman, and close colleague of Einstein, "the last
notable figure from the heroic age of physics lingering among us" (Colby
Cosh, on Wheeler's death in April 2008). The present author had the
privilege of working with Wheeler at Princeton in the late 1980s, and
the dedication of this book records the charge Wheeler delivered from
his Jadwin Hall office in 1989: *"Today's world lacks the noble --- and
it's your generation's duty to bring it back."* The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework
is a partial answer to that charge.

The Wheelerean tradition combines two commitments. The first
is the commitment to *geometry as physics* --- the conviction, traceable
through Einstein's geometrisation of gravity to Riemann's foundational
lectures, that the fundamental laws of nature are geometric facts about
a real four-dimensional manifold. The second is the commitment to the
*nobility* of physics --- the conviction that the discipline is a domain
in which the pursuit of truth is itself a matter of
intellectual and moral seriousness. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework inherits both
commitments. The McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is a
geometric fact about a real four-manifold; the project of deriving the
twenty-three quantum theorems from this principle is undertaken as
Wheeler himself characterised work: as part of the unbroken
thread that runs from Galileo's *e pur si muove* through Newton's
*Principia* to Einstein's $x_4 = ict$ and into the present.

#### The literary parallel: the ungraspable phantom and the charge to set it right {#ssec:literary-parallel}

The pursuit of the simplest axiom in physics has a
parallel in the great heroic literary traditions of the West,
and the parallel carries argument. The Achillean tradition of the
*Iliad* [@HomerIliad], the Christic tradition of the New Testament
[@JohnGospel], the Shakespearean tradition of the Hamletian charge
[@Hamlet], and the Melvillean tradition of the ungraspable phantom
[@Melville1851] all share with the foundational quest in physics a
single feature: the hero is summoned by a deeper reality (an
ancestral charge, a divine commission, a parental ghost, the white whale
itself) to undertake an arduous pursuit, often against the comforts of
mere life, in order to recover or vindicate the truth. We record the
four parallels here as the philosophical-literary frame of this book,
since the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's commitment to the heroic-axiomatic
tradition is the philosophical content of the diagnosis of
§§[1.2](#sec:postulate-versus-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:postulate-versus-theorem"}--[1.13](#sec:dual-channel-ledger){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:dual-channel-ledger"}.

###### The Iliadic kleos.

Achilles is the canonical Western hero who chooses meaningful action
over comfortable longevity. Homer's *Iliad* [@HomerIliad] presents
Achilles' choice between *nóstos* (homecoming, long life) and *kleos*
(κλέος, imperishable glory through deeds remembered) as the founding
choice of the heroic tradition. The Achillean choice is for kleos: the
pursuit of a truth that outlasts the individual life. The foundational
physicist's choice is the same. To reduce the basic
elements of quantum mechanics to a single principle is to undertake the
Iliadic labour: to pursue, against the comforts of accepting the
textbook tradition as it stands, the deeper fact from which
the surface phenomena follow.

###### The Hamletian charge.

In Shakespeare's *Hamlet* [@Hamlet], Act 1 Scene 5, the protagonist is
summoned by the Ghost of his murdered father to set right what is rotten
in the state of Denmark. Hamlet's lament after receiving the
charge --- "The time is out of joint. O cursèd spite, / That ever I was
born to set it right!" --- is the canonical Western articulation of the
burden of being charged by a parental authority to restore an order that
has been broken. The parallel to the foundational physicist's
project is exact: the textbook tradition of quantum mechanics is, in the
diagnosis of
§[1.6](#sec:comparison-table){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:comparison-table"} below, "out of joint" --- fragmented
across twenty-two postulates rather than reduced to a single principle.
The Wheelerean charge in his Jadwin Hall office in 1989
(§[1.1.2](#ssec:wheeler-charge){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:wheeler-charge"}) functions, in the present author's
intellectual lineage, as the Hamletian commission: the senior figure of
the heroic age summons the next generation to set right what has been
allowed to fragment.

###### The Melvillean ungraspable phantom.

Herman Melville's *Moby-Dick* [@Melville1851] opens, in Chapter 1
("Loomings"), with Ishmael's meditation on the image at the heart of the
human relation to the world:

> *But that same image, we ourselves see in all rivers and oceans. It is
> the image of the ungraspable phantom of life; and this is the key to
> it all.*

The ungraspable phantom is the truth that recedes when
pursued and reappears as a different image when approached from a
different direction --- the white whale itself, whose form changes
through every chapter of the novel and whose ultimate nature is the
question the entire whaling voyage exists to answer. The foundational
physicist's pursuit of the simplest axiomatic content of quantum
mechanics is the pursuit of the ungraspable phantom: the
principle from which the canonical commutator, the Born rule, the
Hilbert space, and quantum nonlocality all flow as theorems is one
principle viewed from many angles, ungraspable from any single chapter
of the textbook tradition because the textbook tradition has split the
principle across many chapters as many postulates. The McGucken
framework is the proposal that the ungraspable phantom of foundational
quantum mechanics is, in fact, graspable --- as the physical expansion
of the fourth dimension at the velocity of light,
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

###### The Christic truth that sets free.

The Gospel of John [@JohnGospel] records, at 8:32, the canonical
formulation of the relationship between truth and freedom: *"And ye
shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free."* The Greek
original --- καὶ γνώσεσθε τὴν ἀλήθειαν, καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια ἐλευθερώσει
ὑμᾶς --- binds the act of knowing (γνώσεσθε) to the act of being made
free (ἐλευθερώσει). The foundational physicist's pursuit shares this
structure: the reduction of the twenty-two postulates of textbook
quantum mechanics to the single physical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is a liberation in exactly the Johannine
sense --- freedom from the postulational fragmentation that the textbook
tradition has accepted as the cost of doing business, freedom from the
necessity of accepting multiple independent facts as brute,
freedom from the apparent meaninglessness of a Hilbert space, a Born
rule, a canonical commutator, and a nonlocal correlation that have no
common physical source. The truth, in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, is that
they have a common physical source; and knowing that source is what sets
the foundations free.

#### The heroic stance of the McGucken framework {#ssec:heroic-stance}

The McGucken framework's pursuit of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ as the
single physical principle from which quantum mechanics is derived is, in
the philosophical sense intended above, an Achillean pursuit. The
framework's commitment is to the Einsteinian supreme goal of theory (the
irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible), the
Hilbertian axiomatic method (the logical-formal content separated from
the intuitive content, with the intuitive content made explicit as the
physical referent of the principle), the Wheelerean nobility of physics
(the discipline as a matter of intellectual and moral seriousness), the
Hamletian commission to set right what has been allowed to fragment, the
Melvillean pursuit of the ungraspable phantom now revealed to be
graspable, and the Johannine binding of truth to freedom. These
commitments are the philosophical content of the technical work of Parts I--IV, not decorative.

The diagnosis of
§[1.6](#sec:comparison-table){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:comparison-table"} below grades five leading quantum
mechanics textbooks against the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework on the axis Einstein,
Hilbert, and von Neumann would have used: how many independent
postulates does the framework require, and how few of them are reducible
to a single physical principle? The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's answer to this
Einsteinian-Hilbertian-von Neumannian question is: one. The
convergent-overdetermination signature of the dual-channel derivation
(§[1.9](#sec:remarkable-feature){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:remarkable-feature"} below) is the formal indicator that
the answer is a fact. The literary-philosophical content of
this section is the philosophical content of that fact: the
pursuit of the simplest physical foundation is a heroic pursuit in the
canonical Western sense, undertaken as Wheeler charged in
1989 --- against the loss of the noble, in continuity with the tradition
that runs from Galileo through Newton and Einstein into the present.

*And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.*

### Postulate versus theorem: the axis on which the textbooks are graded {#sec:postulate-versus-theorem}

When a textbook introduces a result --- Schrödinger's equation, the
canonical commutation relation, the Born rule, the Heisenberg
uncertainty relation, the Dirac equation, Noether's theorem, the path
integral, Huygens' Principle, spin, de Broglie's relation, the Pauli
exclusion principle --- does it call it a theorem proved from a deeper
axiom, or insert it as a postulate, an empirical generalization, a
definition, or a plausibility argument? That distinction --- the same
distinction that separates Euclid's *Elements* from a collection of
geometric facts, and Newton's *Principia* from a list of celestial
almanac entries --- is the axis on which the textbooks of
this chapter are graded.

The five textbooks chosen here are the ones most consistently cited as
the leading graduate-and-advanced-undergraduate quantum mechanics texts
of the modern era:

1.  Sakurai & Napolitano, *Modern Quantum Mechanics* (3rd ed., 2020)
    [@Sakurai2020];

2.  Shankar, *Principles of Quantum Mechanics* (2nd ed., 1994)
    [@Shankar1994];

3.  Griffiths & Schroeter, *Introduction to Quantum Mechanics* (3rd
    ed., 2018) [@Griffiths2018];

4.  Cohen-Tannoudji, Diu & Laloë, *Quantum Mechanics* (2nd ed.,
    vol. I, 2019) [@CT2019];

5.  Weinberg, *Lectures on Quantum Mechanics* (2nd ed., 2015)
    [@Weinberg2015].

The first four are the canonical pedagogical hierarchy from
undergraduate to graduate; Weinberg is the modern theorist's reference,
written by a Nobel laureate, deliberately structured around symmetry
rather than wave mechanics. Against these is set the *McGucken
Framework* [@Syn-2026], descending from the single Postulate---the
McGucken Principle, $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$---with every named result
of physics derived as a Theorem, Proposition, Corollary, or Definition.

### Three preliminary facts

Three preliminary facts are decisive for what follows.

1.  Of the five textbooks, only Shankar explicitly separates
    "mathematical theorems" from "physical postulates" as an organizing
    principle---the book's stated pedagogical innovation. Shankar's
    Chapter 4 is titled, verbatim, "The Postulates---a General
    Discussion," and presents quantum mechanics as a list of four
    postulates [@Shankar1994].

2.  Griffiths & Schroeter open their preface with the diagnosis that
    defines the field's disorder: there is no general
    consensus as to what the fundamental principles of quantum mechanics
    are, how it should be taught, or what it means. Every physicist can
    do quantum mechanics, but the stories told about what is being done
    are as various as the tales of Scheherazade. The Afterword on
    interpretation is deferred to Chapter 12 [@Griffiths2018].

3.  Cohen-Tannoudji, Diu & Laloë devote Chapter III, explicitly titled
    "The Postulates of Quantum Mechanics," to a numbered list (six
    postulates in the standard count) which the rest of the volume
    illustrates [@CT2019]. Sakurai develops the Stern--Gerlach
    experiment as motivation and then introduces the formalism
    axiomatically over Chapter 1 [@Sakurai2020]. Weinberg, after a
    historical introduction, gives the formalism in Chapter 3 ("General
    Principles of Quantum Mechanics") as a Hilbert-space axiomatization
    [@Weinberg2015].

None of the five derives the Schrödinger equation, the canonical
commutation relation, the Born rule, the Heisenberg uncertainty
relation, the Dirac equation, or the path integral from a deeper
physical principle. They postulate or motivate, then unfold
consequences. The status of these results in each book is
documented below, side by side with the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's
theorem-chain treatment of the same results.

### Tables of contents and posture {#sec:toc-and-posture}

Five widely adopted quantum-mechanics textbooks --- Sakurai &
Napolitano, Shankar, Griffiths & Schroeter, Cohen-Tannoudji & Diu &
Laloë, and Weinberg --- serve as illustrative exemplars of mainstream
quantum-mechanics pedagogy. Their tables of contents, listed below as
published, document the typical arc of a graduate or
advanced-undergraduate quantum-mechanics course: a development that
begins from postulated states-and-observables structure and proceeds
through specific applications. The analysis that follows extracts from
these exemplars the posture characteristic of mainstream
pedagogy generally --- a posture in which the core algebraic facts of
quantum mechanics (the Hilbert-space arena, the Born rule, the canonical
commutator, the Schrödinger equation) are introduced as independent
postulates or near-postulates rather than as theorems descending from a
deeper physical principle.

#### Sakurai & Napolitano: *Modern Quantum Mechanics* (3rd ed., 2020)

*Chapter list.* 1. Fundamental Concepts --- 2. Quantum Dynamics --- 3.
Theory of Angular Momentum --- 4. Symmetry in Quantum Mechanics --- 5.
Approximation Methods --- 6. Scattering Theory --- 7. Identical
Particles --- 8. Relativistic Quantum Mechanics. Appendices on
electromagnetic units, elementary Schrödinger solutions, and
angular-momentum addition.

*Posture.* The book opens with the Stern--Gerlach experiment
as physical motivation, then declares kets, bras, operators, eigenkets,
and observables as the basic structure. Compatible and incompatible
observables and the uncertainty relation appear in Chapter 1.4. Time
evolution is introduced in Chapter 2 by writing the Schrödinger equation
as a definition of the dynamics, justified by a time-translation
operator argument (a heuristic Stone-theorem invocation, not labeled as
such). Symmetry is treated in Chapter 4 representation-theoretically.
The word "theorem" in Sakurai overwhelmingly refers to results that are
already standard in linear algebra and group theory (spectral theorem,
Wigner--Eckart theorem); the laws of quantum mechanics themselves are
not derived from a deeper principle. *Sakurai inserts.*

#### Shankar: *Principles of Quantum Mechanics* (2nd ed., 1994)

*Chapter list.* 1. Mathematical Introduction --- 2. Review of Classical
Mechanics --- 3. All Is Not Well with Classical Mechanics --- 4. The
Postulates---a General Discussion --- 5. Simple Problems in One
Dimension --- 6. The Classical Limit --- 7. The Harmonic Oscillator ---
8. The Path Integral Formulation of Quantum Theory --- 9. The Heisenberg
Uncertainty Relations --- 10. Systems with $N$ Degrees of Freedom ---
11. Symmetries and Their Consequences --- 12. Rotational Invariance and
Angular Momentum --- 13. The Hydrogen Atom --- 14. Spin --- 15. Addition
of Angular Momenta --- 16. Variational and WKB Methods --- 17.
Time-Independent Perturbation Theory --- 18. Time-Dependent Perturbation
Theory --- 19. Scattering Theory --- 20. The Dirac Equation --- 21. Path
Integrals: II.

*Posture.* Shankar is the most theorem-conscious of the five.
Chapter 1 develops vector spaces, inner products, operators, Hermitian
and unitary operators, and spectral theorems as a self-contained
mathematics chapter. Chapter 3 motivates quantum mechanics by collecting
the empirical evidence that classical mechanics fails (photoelectric
effect, atomic stability, double-slit). Chapter 4 then states the
postulates as a numbered list---four postulates in Shankar's
count---covering states, observables, measurement (with the Born rule
built in), and time evolution (Schrödinger equation as a postulate). The
Heisenberg uncertainty relation in Chapter 9 is presented as a derived
inequality from the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality applied to Hermitian
operators; it is the only major result Shankar treats as a theorem
rather than a postulate, and even then the postulates feeding the proof
are themselves not derived. *Shankar postulates the principles, then
proves consequences with care.*

#### Griffiths & Schroeter: *Introduction to Quantum Mechanics* (3rd ed., 2018)

*Chapter list (Part I, Theory).* 1. The Wave Function --- 2.
Time-Independent Schrödinger Equation --- 3. Formalism --- 4. Quantum
Mechanics in Three Dimensions --- 5. Identical Particles --- 6.
Symmetries and Conservation Laws. *(Part II, Application.)* 7.
Time-Independent Perturbation Theory --- 8. The Variational Principle
--- 9. The WKB Approximation --- 10. Scattering --- 11. Quantum Dynamics
--- 12. Afterword. Appendix on linear algebra.

*Posture.* Griffiths opens Chapter 1 with the assertion that
"this equation \[the Schrödinger equation\] plays a role logically
analogous to Newton's second law: given suitable initial conditions, the
Schrödinger equation determines $\psi$ for all future time, just as, in
classical mechanics, Newton's law determines $x(t)$ for all future
time." The Schrödinger equation is thus inserted, not derived; the
analogy is to a postulate, not to a theorem. The Born rule is similarly
inserted as "statistical interpretation" in Chapter 1.2. The Heisenberg
uncertainty principle is announced in Chapter 1.6 and proved rigorously
in Chapter 3 from Hermitian-operator algebra (the same Cauchy--Schwarz
route as Shankar). The book postpones interpretation to the Afterword
and is candid that no consensus on foundations exists. *Griffiths is
least committed to a principle of all five.*

#### Cohen-Tannoudji, Diu & Laloë: *Quantum Mechanics* (2nd ed., vol. I, 2019)

*Volume I chapter list.* I. Waves and Particles --- II. The Mathematical
Tools of Quantum Mechanics --- III. The Postulates of Quantum Mechanics
--- IV. Application of the Postulates to Simple Cases (Spin 1/2 and
Two-Level Systems) --- V. The One-Dimensional Harmonic Oscillator ---
VI. General Properties of Angular Momentum --- VII. Particles in a
Central Potential. Volume II covers symmetries, perturbation theory,
scattering, identical particles. Each chapter is followed by an
extensive set of "Complements"---detailed applications and special
problems.

*Posture.* Chapter III is titled "The Postulates of Quantum
Mechanics" and gives a numbered statement of the postulates (six in the
standard Cohen-Tannoudji count): (P1) state vector in a Hilbert space,
(P2) observables as Hermitian operators, (P3) eigenvalue spectrum, (P4)
Born rule, (P5) projection postulate, (P6) Schrödinger evolution.
Subsequent chapters are applications of these postulates. The
architecture is explicitly axiomatic, but the axioms are independent
postulates rather than theorems descending from a deeper principle.
*This is the structure most often described as "canonical" in the
quantum-foundations literature.*

#### Weinberg: *Lectures on Quantum Mechanics* (2nd ed., 2015)

*Chapter list.* 1. Historical Introduction --- 2. Particle States in a
Central Potential --- 3. General Principles of Quantum Mechanics --- 4.
Spin --- 5. Approximations for Energy Eigenstates --- 6. Approximations
for Time-Dependent Problems --- 7. Potential Scattering --- 8. General
Scattering Theory --- 9. The Canonical Formalism --- 10. Charged
Particles in Electromagnetic Fields --- 11. The Quantum Theory of
Radiation --- 12. Entanglement.

*Posture.* Weinberg gives the historical motivation in
Chapter 1, then in Chapter 3 develops quantum mechanics as a
Hilbert-space theory with states, operators, the Schrödinger equation,
and the Born rule introduced as the "general principles." Weinberg is
unusually explicit about the foundational difficulty of the Born rule:
he devotes a section to "Where does the Born rule come from?" and
surveys the contenders (decoherence, many-worlds, Bohmian) before
concluding that no fully satisfactory derivation exists. He treats the
Born rule as the postulate most in need of a deeper account, and is
candid about not providing one. *Weinberg's spin chapter develops
representations of the rotation group rather than deriving spin from a
deeper geometric principle.*

### The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework: single-axiom architecture

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework [@Syn-2026] departs from the postulate-list
architecture of mainstream pedagogy by replacing the postulate list with
a single Postulate---the McGucken Principle,
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$---and deriving every named result of quantum
mechanics, general relativity, statistical mechanics, and the Standard
Model as Theorems descending from it. The May 2026 synthesis paper,
which audits and integrates this construction in 172 pages, contains:

-   1 Postulate (the McGucken Principle, with five clauses for
    invariance, spherical symmetry, monotonic $x_{4}$-advance, Lorentz
    consistency, and global validity);

-   366 Theorem-statements, organized into two derivationally disjoint
    derivation chains---Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry / Stone's theorem
    / Lorentz--Poincaré) and Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation / McGucken
    Sphere / Huygens iteration);

-   14 Propositions, 4 Corollaries, 34 Definitions, 16 Postulate
    cross-references;

-   0 lemmas (the architecture absorbs intermediate results
    into the theorem grade rather than splitting them off as a lower
    category);

-   0 additional axioms (everything beyond the McGucken Principle is
    either a Definition naming a geometric or algebraic object or a
    Theorem proved from the Principle and explicitly labeled assumptions $A_1, A_2, \ldots$).

Each theorem is assigned a grade: Grade 1 (forced by Postulate 1 alone),
Grade 2 (Postulate 1 plus explicitly labeled standard assumptions), Grade 3 (Postulate 1 plus an external mathematical
framework such as functional analysis on a Hilbert space, or
differential geometry on a Lorentzian manifold). The grading is itself
part of the architecture: no result is presented as both a postulate and
a theorem, and no result is asserted without being placed at a definite
grade.

The decisive point is that results which appear as
independent postulates in Cohen-Tannoudji and Shankar (the Born rule,
the canonical commutation relation, the Schrödinger equation, the
eigenvalue postulate, the projection postulate) appear in the McGucken
framework as numbered theorems with explicit derivations from
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The Born rule is Theorem 70 of [@Syn-2026],
derived from four requirements (real-valuedness, non-negativity, phase
invariance from $x_{4}$-expansion homogeneity, smoothness) which are
themselves theorems of the Principle. The Schrödinger equation is
Theorem 89, derived from the short-time Huygens propagation on the
McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{p}(t)$. The canonical commutation relation
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ is Theorem 69, doubly forced by Channels A
and B---i.e., proved twice along independent derivation paths. This
double-derivation property is the *derivational-disjointness theorem*
(Theorem 125 in the synthesis paper) and has no analogue in the textbook
tradition.

### Summary

The twenty-two-row table above grades mainstream quantum-mechanics
pedagogy against the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$), the single Postulate of the McGucken
framework. Counting across the twenty-two rows, the contrast
between the two columns emerges sharply.

-   **Mainstream pedagogy.** Approximately six to nine independent
    Postulates depending on the exemplar (the state-vector axiom, the
    observables-as-Hermitian-operators axiom, the eigenvalue/Born-rule
    axiom, the Schrödinger-evolution axiom, the canonical commutator
    either as postulate or as a near-postulate, the
    measurement/projection axiom, the spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ axiom, and
    depending on the exemplar a path-integral axiom and/or a
    Pauli-exclusion axiom). One to five Theorems (Heisenberg uncertainty
    universally; Dirac equation, Pauli exclusion, and Noether's theorem
    in graduate-level treatments). Five to six results derived within
    the framework's own postulate system from already-assumed axioms
    (harmonic-oscillator quantization, $L^2$/$L_z$ eigenvalues,
    hydrogen-atom levels, optical theorem). One to six results Inserted
    heuristically (more in informal treatments, fewer in formal ones).
    Three to four results Motivated by experiment or historical
    exposition (de Broglie, Planck--Einstein, Stern--Gerlach). Zero to
    two results Not covered. The imaginary unit $i$ is universally
    Inserted without derivation.

-   **McGucken framework.** 1 Postulate (the McGucken Principle
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), 22 Theorems (every single named result,
    with the majority proved *twice* via the two derivationally disjoint
    channels), 0 Derived-within-system (nothing intermediate is
    postulated), 0 Inserted, 0 Motivated-as-empirical (motivation is
    given separately from logical status), 0 Not-covered. Every row in
    the rightmost column is T.

The contrast is. Mainstream pedagogy treats quantum mechanics
as a list of independent axioms with consequences. The McGucken
framework treats quantum mechanics as a single physical claim --- the
fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light, in a spherically
symmetric manner, from every spacetime event --- with twenty-two and
more named consequences proved in two derivationally disjoint chains
(Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel), each chain forcing the same result by
independent routes, sharing no intermediate machinery, and ending at the
same formal theorem of quantum mechanics. This is, on the present
author's reading, the first time in the history of the subject that the
entire content of quantum mechanics has been derived as a chain of
theorems descending from a single physical principle along two
independent routes.

### The double-derivation property and its implication

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's single Postulate is the McGucken Principle
($\mathrm{McP}$: $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$). From this one principle,
every named result of QM descends along two derivationally disjoint
channels. The double-derivation of the canonical commutation relation,
Theorem 69 of [@Syn-2026], has no analogue in mainstream pedagogy: in
standard textbook treatments, $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ is asserted
once, either as a postulate or as a consequence of one. In the McGucken
framework it is forced *twice*, by paths that share no intermediate
machinery beyond the principle and the final equation:

-   **Geometric Channel.** Iterated McGucken-Sphere path-space (QB1+QB2) +
    Compton phase along proper time (QB4) + Trotter decomposition of
    $\hat{U}(t)$ (QB5) $\Rightarrow$ $\partial_q$ and $\partial_p$ of
    $e^{iS/\hbar}$ as Fourier-dual pair $\Rightarrow$
    $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ as the Fourier-dual structure of the
    path-integral measure.

-   **Algebraic Channel.** Translation invariance of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ +
    Stone's theorem $\Rightarrow$ self-adjoint generator
    $\hat{p}= -i\hbar \nabla$ + Stone--von Neumann uniqueness
    $\Rightarrow$ $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ on the unique
    irreducible representation;

The two routes share no intermediate machinery. Geometric Channel is geometric,
path-integral, and signature-bridging (it works equally in Lorentzian
and Euclidean signature; see Theorem 4 of [@Syn-2026]). Algebraic Channel is algebraic,
operator-theoretic, and Lorentzian-locked. The agreement of
the two routes is the derivational-disjointness theorem (Theorem 125 of
[@Syn-2026]).

The implication is the difference between a postulate-list and an
axiom-with-theorems. It is the difference between Ptolemaic epicycles
and Newton's inverse-square law. It is the difference between
empirically organized regularities and a principle from which the
regularities are forced.

### The remarkable feature: dual-channel convergent overdetermination {#sec:remarkable-feature}

The McGucken Quantum Formalism (MQF) of [@MG-Formalism-2026] establishes
the central technical content of the framework as a
derivational-mathematical fact: the canonical commutation relation, the
Schrödinger equation, the Feynman path integral, the Born rule, and
every other theorem of quantum mechanics is reached from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ along two derivationally disjoint chains sharing
no intermediate machinery. This is the property the present textbook
celebrates and verifies theorem-by-theorem across all twenty-three QM
theorems in Part II.

The property has a name. The Convergent Overdetermination Lemma
(Lemma 15.1 of [@MG-Formalism-2026]) states it formally for the
canonical commutation relation:

> *In the McGucken Quantum Formalism, the canonical commutation relation
> $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ is derivable from the foundational
> principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ through two independent routes via
> disjoint intermediate machinery: the Hamiltonian route of Propositions
> H.1--H.5, and the Lagrangian route of Propositions L.1--L.6. The two
> routes share no intermediate structure except the starting principle
> and the final algebraic identity.*

The Hamiltonian route uses Stone's theorem on strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary groups, the configuration-space representation,
and the Stone--von Neumann uniqueness theorem. The Lagrangian route uses
iterated Huygens-wavefront expansions on the McGucken Sphere, path-space
generation via time-discretisation, and Gaussian short-time integration
in the Feynman propagator. The two sets of machinery are disjoint.
Stone's theorem does not appear in the Lagrangian route;
Huygens-wavefront propagation does not appear in the Hamiltonian route;
the two routes share only $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at the start and
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ at the end. This is the overdetermination, established as a mathematical fact about the
framework, not as a philosophical interpretation.

#### The six novelties

[@MG-Formalism-2026] §13.2 catalogues six novelties of the
McGucken Quantum Formalism relative to the prior art of
operator-algebraic QM, path-integral QM, axiomatic QFT, geometric
quantisation, spacetime algebra, noncommutative geometry, and
categorical QFT. The mathematical apparatus used by MQF is taken from
prior art in every case and given full credit (§13.1 of the same paper):
Hilbert spaces and self-adjoint operators (von Neumann 1932); Stone's
theorem (Stone 1930); the Stone--von Neumann uniqueness theorem (Stone
1930, von Neumann 1931--32); the canonical commutation relation
(Heisenberg, Born, Jordan 1925); the Schrödinger equation (Schrödinger
1926); the Feynman path integral (Feynman 1948, with Dirac 1933
antecedent); Huygens' principle (Huygens 1678);
Wightman--Haag--Kastler--Osterwalder--Schrader axiomatic QFT; Wigner
classification, Coleman--Mandula, Weinberg reconstruction; Yang--Mills
gauge theory; Connes's spectral triples; the Atiyah--Segal--Lurie
categorical apparatus; Wilsonian renormalisation group. The novelty
resides not in the mathematical machinery but in the commitments that combine the machinery into a dual-channel framework
with convergent overdetermination.

1.  **Dual-channel derivation from a single principle.** The McGucken
    Quantum Formalism derives both the algebraic-symmetry channel and
    the geometric-propagation channel from the single principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The Hamiltonian route
    (Propositions H.1--H.5 of
    §[4.6](#sec:HL-architecture){reference-type="ref"
    reference="sec:HL-architecture"}) and the Lagrangian route
    (Propositions L.1--L.6) are parallel sibling derivations from the
    same principle. No prior framework realises this dual-channel
    derivation.

2.  **Convergent overdetermination of $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$.**
    The canonical commutation relation is derived through two routes via
    disjoint intermediate machinery, with the same $i$ and the same
    $\hbar$ reached by both chains (Lemma 15.1 of [@MG-Formalism-2026]).
    No prior framework derives a fundamental quantum-theoretical
    identity through two disjoint routes from a principle.

3.  **Geometric grounding of the imaginary unit $i$.** The $i$ appearing
    in $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, the Schrödinger equation
    $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$, the Feynman weight
    $\exp(iS/\hbar)$, and quantum theory generally is grounded in the
    imaginary character of $x_4$ in the integrated coordinate shadow
    $x_4 = ict$ of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The factor $i$ is a
    geometric feature of the McGucken Principle
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. Hestenes's spacetime-algebra framework
    [@Hestenes1966-STA] supplies an alternative geometric grounding ($i$
    as the spacetime pseudoscalar); the McGucken grounding is
    distinct ($i$ as the perpendicularity marker of $x_4$).

4.  **Geometric grounding of $\hbar$.** The action quantum $\hbar$
    appearing in $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, in $E = \hbar\omega$,
    and in $p = \hbar k$ is derived from $c$ plus the McGucken
    self-consistency principle ([@MG-Constants]), not taken as an
    external empirical input. The McGucken Lagrangian uniqueness
    analysis ([@MG-Lagrangian-2026], Proposition III.3) establishes
    $\hbar$ as derived from the McGucken self-consistency requirement.

5.  **The seven-duality property.** The seven McGucken Dualities of
    Physics ([@MG-Lagrangian-2026], §6.7) --- Hamiltonian/Lagrangian,
    Noether/Second-Law, Heisenberg/Schrödinger, wave/particle,
    locality/nonlocality, rest-mass/spatial-motion, time/space --- arise
    as parallel sibling consequences of the dual-channel content of
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. No prior Lagrangian framework in the
    282-year tradition (Newton 1788 through string theory 1968--present)
    generates more than two of the seven dualities; the McGucken
    framework generates all seven.

6.  **Categorical novelty of dual-channel quantum theory.** The category
    of dual-channel quantum-theoretical frameworks
    ([@MG-Formalism-2026], Definition 7.5.3) is not equivalent to any
    category of single-channel framework, nor to the standard
    formulations of spectral-triple or categorical-QFT frameworks
    (Proposition 7.5.4 of the same paper). The dual-channel
    quantum-theoretical category is a genuinely new categorical
    structure relative to the prior art, established as a
    formal-mathematical fact through the absence of a
    structure-preserving functor.

#### Why this matters

The mathematical apparatus needed to formalise the dual-channel content
has been substantially available in prior art since at least 1948 (Stone
1930, von Neumann 1931--32, Feynman 1948). What was missing was the
commitment to dual-channel content as a feature
of quantum theory --- the willingness to take the simultaneous presence
of algebraic-symmetry and geometric-propagation content in
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ as a commitment of the quantum
theory rather than as a coincidence of mathematical formulation. The
McGucken Quantum Formalism supplies this commitment.

The significance is that the entire quantum-theoretical
apparatus then descends as theorems through dual-channel routes from one
principle. The Hamiltonian and Lagrangian formulations, the Heisenberg
and Schrödinger pictures, wave--particle duality, locality/nonlocality
duality, and the seven-duality structure of physics all become parallel
sibling consequences of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with the canonical
commutation relation reached by two disjoint routes through convergent
overdetermination. This is the missing foundation that
transforms the prior art's rich apparatus from a collection of
equivalent mathematical formulations into a unified derivational program
from a single geometric principle.

The 23 derivational-disjointness audits, taken together, constitute 23
