> $x^0 = t = ct_{\mathrm{conv}}$.*

The MTW judgment is explicit. It says: the $i$ in
$x_4 = ict$ is an artefact of flat-spacetime convenience; it does not
generalise to curved spacetime; therefore it should be abandoned. The
geometrodynamics tradition, founded on the conviction that geometry is
the physical content of physics, here *abandons the
specific geometric content of $x_4 = ict$ in favor of a real time
coordinate*.

###### The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's reversal of the MTW judgment.

The McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ takes the opposite
position: the $i$ in $x_4 = ict$ is not a flat-spacetime convenience but
the algebraic shadow of the genuine perpendicularity of the fourth
dimension to the spatial three
(§[1.11.1](#ssec:mcgucken-wick-five-axes){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:mcgucken-wick-five-axes"}, Axis 1). The McGucken
framework's first move is precisely the move MTW elected not to make: to
take the $i$ seriously as a physical signature, not to abandon it. Box
2.1 of MTW records the cultural moment at which the geometrodynamics
tradition declined the geometric reading of $x_4 = ict$; the McGucken
framework records the alternative in which the geometric
reading is taken up. *The MTW judgment is not wrong in the narrow
technical sense --- the $i$ cannot be used in the formal apparatus of
curved-spacetime tensor calculus as a coordinate label; but in the
deeper sense, the $i$ is the algebraic mark of the
perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the spatial three, and abandoning the $i$
means abandoning the content that the McGucken Sphere and the
Geometric Channel derivation chain recover.*

###### The historical irony: the geometrodynamics tradition let go of the geometry.

The deepest irony in the historical-developmental thread is that the
tradition most committed to geometry-as-physics --- the Wheelerean
geometrodynamics tradition, in which the present author was trained at
Princeton --- was the very tradition that abandoned the $x_4 = ict$
geometric reading at the moment of writing the canonical graduate
textbook. The cultural-historical record is unambiguous: MTW's farewell
to $ict$ was the canonical step that the textbook tradition has followed
since 1973. The consequence is that quantum gravity, the
unification of general relativity and quantum mechanics that the
geometrodynamics tradition was supposed to deliver, has not been
delivered in the half-century since --- because the geometric content of
$x_4$ (the moving fourth dimension whose expansion is the McGucken
Principle) was let go of by the very tradition that should have
developed it. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework returns to the geometric content.
The McGucken Sphere on the moving manifold $M_{G}$ is the geometric
object that the MTW *Gravitation* programme set aside; the
four-dimensional null-cone structure that MTW Box 2.1 describes as "the
interlocking causal structure that makes the machinery of the physical
world function as it does" is, in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, identical with
the iterated McGucken Sphere structure of Geometric Channel, with quantum
nonlocality identified as the three-dimensional projection of
null-separated points on the expanding four-dimensional Sphere
(the QM T17 Geometric Channel section of
Chapter [17](#ch:nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:nonlocality"}).

###### Quantum nonlocality and the null cone are one physical phenomenon.

The MTW Box 2.1 passage, taken in its full content, supplies what
is --- from the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework perspective --- a precise statement
of quantum nonlocality at the level of Minkowski geometry. "When the
interval between two events is zero, one event may be on Earth and the
other on a supernova in the galaxy M31, but their separation must be a
null ray (piece of a light cone)." The two events at null separation
are, in the Lorentz-Minkowski reading MTW gives, locally connected by a
piece of light cone; in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reading, they are points
on the same McGucken Sphere expanding from a common past event, with the
Sphere as the geometric carrier of their shared identity. *Quantum
nonlocality and the four-dimensional null cone are the same physical
phenomenon viewed in two registers*: in the Lorentz-Minkowski register,
the null cone is the locus of locally-connected events; in the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework register, the McGucken Sphere is the joint wavefront
whose points share null-geodesic identity from a common source event.
The three-dimensional projection of null-separated points on the
four-dimensional Sphere appears to a three-dimensional observer as
"nonlocal correlation"; the four-dimensional structure is in fact local
on the Sphere. The MTW Box 2.1 description of the null cone as the
structure "that makes the machinery of the physical world function as it
does" is precisely the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reading of quantum nonlocality
as the surface signature of the four-dimensional Sphere geometry. The
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework recovers, in the geometric register, the content that MTW *Gravitation* described in the algebraic register but
did not develop into its quantum-mechanical implications because the
$x_4 = ict$ reading was abandoned.

###### The Cartesian opposition and the differential mortality of channels.

A final historical observation completes the developmental thread.
Descartes' 1637 *La Géométrie* [@Descartes1637] was not received as the
obvious-and-inevitable triumph of algebraic reduction over Greek
synthetic geometry. The opposition was substantial and was led by
figures of the first rank: Gilles Personne de Roberval [@Roberval1693]
at the Collège Royal in Paris, and Girard Desargues [@Desargues1639]
(founder of projective geometry). Both regarded Greek synthetic geometry
as the higher form of mathematical reasoning, and both regarded
Descartes' algebraic method as a clumsy substitute that lost the visual
clarity, the logical purity, and the genuine geometric content of the
synthetic tradition. The Cartesian opposition was overruled, in the
seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, not because the
synthetic-geometric tradition was wrong but because the
Cartesian-algebraic method was procedurally faster --- it converted
geometric problems into mechanical calculations that any trained
algebraist could execute, replacing the geometric genius required for
each new Greek proof with a step-by-step algorithmic procedure.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's differential-response theorem
(Theorem [1.5](#thm:channel-differential-response){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:channel-differential-response"}) supplies a reading of this seventeenth-century controversy at the level of
foundational physics. The Greek synthetic-geometric tradition is the
ancestor of Geometric Channel: it works with shapes (the McGucken
Sphere is its modern descendant), with spatial reasoning (the
geometric-propagation derivation chain), with constructions on real
four-manifolds. The Cartesian-algebraic tradition is the ancestor of Algebraic Channel: it works with coordinates, equations, and
algebraic-symbolic manipulations (Stone's theorem, unitary
representations, the Wigner classification are its modern descendants).
*The Wick rotation is the operation that exposes which of the two
traditions has the durability under axis-projection into the
moving fourth dimension*. The Greek synthetic-geometric content of the
McGucken Sphere is rotationally symmetric and survives the projection;
the Cartesian-algebraic content of the time-translation group depends on
the frame distinction the projection dissolves and does not survive. The
seventeenth-century Cartesian opposition --- Roberval, Desargues, the
classical humanist mathematicians who insisted that Greek geometry was
the higher truth --- was right, at the level of foundational physics, in
a sense that no one in the seventeenth century could have known: the
Greek geometric content has durability under the foundational
physical operations of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries; the
Cartesian-algebraic content does not.

###### The mythic punchline.

In the heroic-quest reading of
§[1.1](#sec:heroic-quest){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:heroic-quest"}, the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is positioned as
the contemporary continuation of the heroic-axiomatic tradition from
Galileo through Wheeler. The historical-developmental thread of this
subsection supplies the Hamletian dimension of that positioning. The
Wheelerean geometrodynamics tradition, in MTW's *Gravitation*, abandoned
the very $x_4 = ict$ reading that the McGucken Principle takes
seriously; the father of the geometrodynamics tradition (Wheeler
himself) presided over the textbook judgment that the geometric content
of $x_4$ was a flat-spacetime convenience to be abandoned. The McGucken
framework's project is therefore, in the Hamletian register of
§[1.1.3](#ssec:literary-parallel){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:literary-parallel"}, the project of *setting right what
was let go* --- returning to the geometric content of $x_4 = ict$ that
the geometrodynamics tradition itself put aside, and developing this
content into the four-pillar unification of
the QM T17 distinctive-feature subsection that quantum
gravity has been unable to deliver in the half-century since MTW's
farewell.

The mythic content of the differential response: *Descartes'
algebra is mortal under the Wick rotation; Greek geometry is immortal
under the Wick rotation; the McGucken Sphere, as the contemporary
expression of the Greek synthetic-geometric tradition on the moving
four-manifold, has the imperishable durability that Achilles'
κλέος (*kleos*) names in the Iliadic tradition.* The Algebraic Channel
derivation chain is mortal in the precise sense that
Theorem [1.5](#thm:channel-differential-response){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:channel-differential-response"}(A) makes formal: the
unitary group becomes a semigroup under $\Wick$, the Lie-algebra
commutator structure dissolves, the Wigner classification does not
apply. The Geometric Channel derivation chain is immortal in the precise sense
that
Theorem [1.5](#thm:channel-differential-response){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:channel-differential-response"}(B) makes formal: the
geometric content of the iterated Sphere is preserved through the
signature change, the Lorentzian Sphere becomes a Euclidean four-sphere
with the same rotational-symmetric content, the iterated-Sphere
intersection structure persists. Achilles lives on in the imperishable
glory of geometric content that survives the test; Descartes'
algebraic content, however successful in its seventeenth-century moment,
does not.

#### The most concise differentiation {#ssec:mcgucken-wick-concise}

The single-sentence differentiation: the orthodox Wick rotation is an
analytic continuation in a complex plane that has no physical referent
and no physical agent; the McGucken-Wick rotation is a coordinate
identity on a real four-manifold whose fourth axis is physically
expanding at the velocity of light per $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with
the rotation having kinematic accompaniment (Lorentz
contraction-and-velocity, time-rotation-and-spatial-curvature) and
physical agents (every measurement apparatus, every horizon in the
universe). The one is a formal device of complex analysis with no
physical content; the other is the operational signature of the
foundational physical invariant of contemporary physics at every
measurement event from the single-photon laboratory scale to the
cosmological-horizon scale.

The sharpest single contrast: the orthodox Wick rotation has no physical
referent and no physical agent; the McGucken-Wick rotation has
both --- the physical referent is the real fourth axis $x_4$ of $M_{G}$,
physically expanding at the velocity of light, and the physical agents
are every measurement apparatus and every horizon in the universe. Every
other differentiator catalogued above descends from this one.

This section establishes the McGucken-Wick rotation as a major thematic
anchor of the remainder of the book. The Hilbert chapter's catalogue of
twelve canonical insertions of $i$ across quantum mechanics is the full
development of how the perpendicularity marker $i$ of the McGucken-Wick
rotation propagates through every $i$-bearing equation of foundational
physics. The dual-channel ledger of
§[1.13](#sec:dual-channel-ledger){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:dual-channel-ledger"} below records the operational role
of the rotation as the *differential-response diagnostic* distinguishing
Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry, Lorentzian-locked) from Geometric Channel
(geometric-propagation, bi-signature), with the formal content of the
distinction established in
Theorem [1.5](#thm:channel-differential-response){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:channel-differential-response"} of
§[1.11.3](#ssec:mcgucken-wick-differential-response){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:mcgucken-wick-differential-response"}. The
kinematic-accompaniment insight of
§[1.11.2](#ssec:mcgucken-wick-kinematic-accompaniment){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:mcgucken-wick-kinematic-accompaniment"} above is what is
distinctive about the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's treatment of the
rotation: the recognition that rotating into the fourth dimension is
never static, because the fourth dimension is itself a velocity.

### Measurement as Physical Wick Rotation: Theorem 12.2 and the universal non-closure quantum {#sec:measurement-as-physical-wick-rotation}

The McGucken-Wick rotation discussion above established that the
transformation $\tau = x_4/c$ is a real coordinate identification on
the McGucken manifold, with the perpendicularity marker $i$ in
$x_4 = ict$ rotated out at the level of the coordinate. The present
section establishes the *physical realization* of this rotation: every
measurement event in a laboratory is a physical Wick rotation, with
the i-bearing complex wavefunction $\psi$ rotated into the real-valued
spatial-slice probability density $|\psi(E)|^2$ at the measurement
event $E$. The Born rule's exponent 2 is the algebraic signature of
this rotation, and the universal action quantum $\hbar$ that
parameterizes the rotation is the same $\hbar$ that appears across
nine independently-celebrated results in physics
(canonical commutator, Robertson uncertainty bound, Berry geometric
phase, spin-1/2 4$\pi$ closure, Bohr--Sommerfeld--Maslov,
Aharonov--Bohm, Dirac monopole, Wigner rotation, path-integral
interference). The unification of these nine results under one
upstream principle — every non-closure that involves $x_4$ inherits
the action quantum $\hbar$ as its algebraic signature — is the most
far-reaching content of the McGucken framework's reading of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.

::: {#thm:measurement-as-physical-wick-rotation .theorem}
**Theorem 1.44** (Measurement as Physical Wick Rotation;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 12.2). *Let $\psi$ be a wavefunction on
$M_{1,3}$ representing a quantum particle's forward $x_4$-expansion
from an emission event. Let $E \in M_{1,3}$ be a candidate measurement
event at which a localized absorber is prepared to register. Then the
measurement event at $E$ corresponds to the physical realization of
the Wick rotation*
$$x_4 = ict \;\longrightarrow\; x_4^W := -i x_4 = ct$$
*at the particle's worldline at $E$, with the wavefunction's
$i$-bearing complex amplitude $\psi$ rotated into the real-valued
spatial-slice probability density
$|\psi(E)|^2 = \psi^*(E)\psi(E)$. The Born rule's exponent 2 is the
algebraic signature of this rotation, derived from the rank-2
character of the Minkowski metric
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}) via the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing
(Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (eight-step verification of the physical-rotation correspondence).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**Step 1 (Perpendicularity-marker role of $i$).** The Minkowski
coordinate $x_4 = ict$ carries the imaginary unit $i$ as the
perpendicularity marker for $x_4$'s orthogonality to $x_1 x_2 x_3$
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}). Multiplication by $i$ implements
the rotation that takes a spatial direction into the perpendicular
$x_4$-direction.

**Step 2 (Wick rotation removes $i$ from the coordinate).** The Wick
rotation $x_4 \to -i x_4 = ct$ removes $i$ from the coordinate.
Geometrically, this rotates $x_4$ from its perpendicular
imaginary-axis orientation into the real-axis orientation, mapping
the Lorentzian metric
$ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + dx_\text{spatial}^2$ to the Euclidean metric
$ds_E^2 = c^2 d\tau^2 + dx_\text{spatial}^2$. In the McGucken
framework, this is the coordinate identification between the
integrated form $x_4 = ict$ (perpendicular, imaginary axis) and the
proper-time parameterization $\tau = x_4/c$ (real axis).

**Step 3 ($\psi$ is $i$-bearing between emission and measurement.)**
Between emission and measurement, the particle's wavefunction $\psi$
is $i$-bearing: its complex phase encodes the particle's accumulated
$x_4$-component along its worldline. The complex character of $\psi$
is the imprint of $x_4$-perpendicularity on the wavefunction's phase,
with multiplication by $\exp(i\varphi)$ implementing rotation by
angle $\varphi$ in the perpendicular $x_4$-direction
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}).

**Step 4 (Geometric meeting at $E$ rotates the worldline out of $x_4$.)**
At a measurement event $E$, the geometric meeting of the forward
$x_4$-expansion $\psi$ with the localized absorber's conjugate
$x_4$-image $\psi^*$ at $E$
(Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"}) rotates the particle's
four-velocity out of $x_4$. The geometric meeting requires both
factors to be present at $E$ — the forward expansion's amplitude AND
the conjugate image's amplitude — with the product
$\psi^*(E)\psi(E)$ the algebraic record of the bilinear coincidence
(Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}, with rank-2 forced by
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}).

**Step 5 (The product $\psi^*\psi$ is real-valued; the $i$ is
removed.)** Any complex number $z$ multiplied by its conjugate $z^*$
gives $|z|^2$, a real non-negative quantity. The squaring eliminates
the imaginary part of $\psi$, removing the $i$ that encoded the
particle's participation in $x_4$-perpendicularity. The result is a
real-valued probability density on the spatial slice at $E$.

**Step 6 (Identification of coordinate-level and amplitude-level
rotations.)** The physical content of the squaring at the amplitude
level is identical to the physical content of the Wick rotation at
the coordinate level: both remove the $i$ that is the
perpendicularity marker for $x_4$. The mathematical operation
$x_4 = ict \to ct$ (Wick rotation at the coordinate level) and the
physical operation $\psi \to |\psi|^2$ (squaring at the amplitude
level) are the same geometric operation — rotation of the $i$-bearing
perpendicular structure into the real spatial-slice structure —
performed at different levels of the chain.

**Step 7 (Post-measurement state collapsed to the corresponding
eigenstate.)** The post-measurement state is the particle localized
at $E$, with the wavefunction collapsed onto the corresponding
eigenstate
(Corollary [9.40](#cor:DvN-4){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:DvN-4"}). The particle's worldline tangent has
reoriented from the $x_4$-perpendicular direction toward the spatial
directions; it is no longer participating in the spreading
$x_4$-expansion, and its description no longer requires the $i$-marker
for $x_4$-perpendicularity.

**Step 8 (Conclusion: measurement = physical Wick rotation.)**
Therefore the measurement event at $E$ *is* the physical realization
of the Wick rotation $x_4 \to -i x_4$, with the $i$ removed at both
the coordinate-level ($x_4 \to ct$ at the rotation moment) and the
amplitude-level ($\psi \to |\psi|^2$ at the rotation moment), both
operations performed in coincidence at the geometric meeting event
$E$. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:path-integral-wick-rotation .corollary}
**Corollary 1.44.1** (The standard path-integral Wick rotation as the
formal abstraction of the physical measurement rotation;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Corollary 12.3). *The standard path-integral Wick
rotation, used as a mathematical convergence device in quantum field
theory ($t \to -i\tau$ converting oscillating phase weights
$\exp(iS/\hbar)$ into damped real weights $\exp(-S_E/\hbar)$), is
the formal abstraction of the physical measurement rotation. The
physical measurement event removes the $i$ from the particle's
amplitude with the same geometric effect: transition from the
$i$-bearing oscillatory description (active $x_4$-perpendicularity)
to the $i$-free real description (localized spatial event). The Wick
rotation has, in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, a physical referent: the
measurement event in the laboratory.*
:::

#### The universal non-closure quantum: $\hbar$ across foundational physics {#sec:universal-non-closure-quantum}

The non-closure of round-trip rotations involving $x_4$ is not
confined to the canonical commutator
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$. The McGucken framework's reading of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ with action quantum $\hbar$ per
radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation of $x_4$-advance supplies a single
physical mechanism by which **any closed loop in physics that involves
a round-trip through $x_4$ cannot close more tightly than the action
quantum $\hbar$**. This minimum-non-closure principle is the upstream
physical content of nine independently-celebrated results across
foundational physics, each treated historically as a separate
empirical fact requiring its own derivation. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework
places all nine under a single upstream principle and identifies the
universal minimum quantum $\hbar$ as the action carried by one cycle
of $x_4$-advance.

::: {#thm:universal-non-closure-quantum .theorem}
**Theorem 1.45** (Universal non-closure quantum of $x_4$-involving
rotations; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 12.11). *Let $R$ denote any
physical operation involving rotation through the perpendicular
$x_4$-direction of the McGucken constraint surface $M_{1,3}$ (a
quantum-mechanical operator action involving $x_4$-phase via the
operator $i$; a closed loop in phase space; a closed loop in
parameter space for adiabatic transport; a closed spatial loop
around a region of gauge curvature; a closed orbit traversing
classical turning points; a composition of non-parallel Lorentz
boosts; or any other process whose round-trip closure depends on the
integrated $x_4$-content along the trajectory). Then the round-trip
non-closure of $R$ is bounded below by the action quantum $\hbar$:*
$$\mathrm{non\text{-}closure}(R) \ge \hbar \times (\text{topological coefficient determined by } R\text{'s structure}),$$
*with the topological coefficient ranging from $1$ (for the
infinitesimal canonical-commutator case) down to $1/2$ (for the
Robertson uncertainty bound, the Bohr--Sommerfeld Maslov correction,
the spin-1/2 $4\pi$ closure relative to $2\pi$, and the Dirac
monopole minimum quantization), or up to large integers determined by
the topology of $R$ (winding number for Aharonov--Bohm and Dirac
monopole; Chern number for Wigner--Zee non-Abelian; etc.). The
universal lower bound across all instances is the action quantum
$h$ carried by one Compton-frequency oscillation of
$x_4$-advance ($\hbar$ per radian): any round-trip involving $x_4$ cannot resolve a phase
difference finer than this quantum because $x_4$-advance occurs in
discrete units of $\hbar$ per oscillation.*

*Specifically, the following nine canonical non-closures are all
instances of this universal principle:*

*(1) Canonical commutator
$[\hat{q}_i, \hat{p}_j] = i\hbar \delta_{ij}$
(Theorem [10.1](#thm:QMT10){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT10"}): the infinitesimal-loop non-closure of
$(\hat{q}, \hat{p})$-rotation, with non-closure quantum $\hbar$
in the perpendicular direction marked by $i$.*

*(2) Robertson uncertainty bound
$\sigma_q \sigma_p \ge \hbar/2$: the statistical version of (1),
with the $1/2$ supplied by Cauchy--Schwarz on the commutator's
$i\hbar$.*

*(3) Berry geometric phase
$\gamma_B = \oint_C A \cdot d\ell$ (Berry 1984
[@Berry1984Phase]): the global non-closure of an adiabatic loop in
parameter space; the Berry connection $A$ is geometrically the
connection on the $U(1)$ fiber bundle whose fiber is the
$x_4$-phase circle.*

*(4) Spin-1/2 $4\pi$ closure (SU(2) double cover of SO(3); Rauch et
al. 1975 [@Rauch1975Spin], Werner et al. 1975 [@Werner1975Spin]): a
spin-1/2 particle rotated by $2\pi$ picks up phase
$\exp(i\pi) = -1$; full closure requires $4\pi$. The "extra
$2\pi$" is the half-quantum of $x_4$-rotation that a spin-1/2
particle carries.*

*(5) Bohr--Sommerfeld + Maslov $\frac{1}{2}$-quantum
$\oint p\,dq = (n + \mu/4)h$ (Maslov 1965
[@Maslov1965Asymptotic]; Arnold 1967 [@Arnold1967Maslov]): each
classical turning-point traversal contributes $1/4$ to the Maslov
index $\mu$; the geometric origin is the rotation through $x_4$ at
the turning point.*

*(6) Aharonov--Bohm phase
$\exp(ie\Phi/\hbar)$ (Aharonov--Bohm 1959
[@AharonovBohm1959Phase]; Tonomura et al. 1986
[@Tonomura1986AB]): the closed-loop phase of a charged particle
around a region of confined magnetic flux $\Phi$; the $U(1)$ gauge
fiber is geometrically the $x_4$-phase circle.*

*(7) Dirac monopole quantization $eg = (n/2)\hbar c$ (Dirac 1931
[@Dirac1931Monopole]; Wu--Yang 1975 [@WuYang1975Bundle]): the minimum
monopole charge $eg = (1/2)\hbar c$ is the minimum non-closure that
the global geometry of the $x_4$-phase bundle tolerates.*

*(8) Wigner rotation from non-parallel boost composition (Wigner 1939
[@Wigner1939Rotation]; Thomas 1927 [@Thomas1927Precession]): two
non-parallel Lorentz boosts compose to a boost plus a residual
rotation because boosts are rotations involving $x_4$
(cf. Remark [19.8](#rmk:boost-measurement-x4-rotation){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:boost-measurement-x4-rotation"}).*

*(9) Universal path-integral interference $\exp(iS/\hbar)$
(Feynman 1948 [@Feynman1948Path]): the path-integral phase is the
integrated $x_4$-phase along the path, with $i$ the perpendicularity
marker for $x_4$ and $\hbar$ the action quantum per
radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation of $x_4$-advance.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (verification of each of the nine instances).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**(1) Canonical commutator.**
$[\hat{q}_i, \hat{p}_j] = i\hbar\delta_{ij}$ is
Theorem [10.1](#thm:QMT10){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT10"}. The non-closure quantum is $i\hbar$ with $i$
the perpendicularity marker for $x_4$ and $\hbar$ the action
quantum per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation. The infinitesimal-loop
non-closure is exactly the McGucken-quantum at the local operator
level.

**(2) Uncertainty bound.** $\sigma_q \sigma_p \ge \hbar/2$
follows from Robertson's inequality applied to the commutator
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ via Cauchy--Schwarz, with the
factor of $1/2$ arising from the Cauchy--Schwarz reduction of the
operator-level $i\hbar$ to the statistical-bound level $\hbar/2$.

**(3) Berry phase.** The Berry connection $A$ on the $U(1)$ fiber
bundle over parameter space has curvature whose integral over a
closed loop gives the Berry phase. The fiber is the $x_4$-phase
circle (the perpendicular direction whose advance carries the
$\hbar$ quantum at each event); adiabatic loops in any parameter
space induce $x_4$-rotations whose non-closure is the Berry phase.
The minimum resolvable phase is $\hbar$-quantized because
$x_4$-advance is $\hbar$-quantized.

**(4) Spin-1/2 $4\pi$ closure.** A spin-1/2 particle's angular
momentum is $\hbar/2$, corresponding to half-quantized $x_4$-oscillation
participation. The $2\pi$-rotation phase $\exp(i\pi) = -1$ records
the half-quantum non-closure: the particle's $x_4$-content is half
the standard quantum, so its round-trip in $2\pi$ picks up only half
the standard $2\pi\hbar$ action that would give full closure.

**(5) Bohr--Sommerfeld--Maslov.** Each classical turning-point
traversal reverses the particle's direction in $x_1 x_2 x_3$, which
requires a rotation through $x_4$. Each such rotation contributes
one quarter-quantum of action $\hbar$ to the round-trip; the
cumulative Maslov correction $\mu/4$ is the total non-closure of
all turning-point rotations along the closed orbit.

**(6) Aharonov--Bohm.** The $U(1)$ gauge fiber is geometrically the
$x_4$-phase circle; a closed spatial loop in $(x_1, x_2)$ around a
region of gauge curvature (magnetic flux $\Phi$) accumulates
$x_4$-phase that cannot be removed by deforming the loop within the
field-free region. The elementary flux quantum $h/e$ corresponds to
one full round-trip of $x_4$-phase circulation.

**(7) Dirac monopole.** The Dirac string is a singular $x_4$-phase
line; the round-trip around it accumulates phase in units of
$\frac{1}{2}\hbar$; the minimum monopole charge
$eg = \frac{1}{2}\hbar c$ is the minimum non-closure that the
global geometry of the $x_4$-phase bundle tolerates.

**(8) Wigner rotation.** Boosts are rotations involving $x_4$. Two
non-parallel boosts compose to a boost plus a residual rotation
because boost-composition in a curved (hyperbolic) velocity space
does not close (cf.
Remark [19.8](#rmk:boost-measurement-x4-rotation){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:boost-measurement-x4-rotation"} for the boost-measurement
parallel reading). The curvature of velocity space is geometrically the
same as the Berry curvature of (3) — both descend from
$x_4$-involving rotations of the four-dimensional structure.

**(9) Path-integral interference.** The path-integral phase
$\exp(iS/\hbar)$ is the integrated $x_4$-phase along the path,
with $i$ the perpendicularity marker for $x_4$ and $\hbar$ the
action quantum per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation. Every quantum
interference effect is the empirical record of integrated
$x_4$-phase non-closure between distinct paths.

The nine items therefore share their non-closure quantum $\hbar$
because all nine involve rotations of, or phase-content along,
$x_4 = ict$, and $x_4$-advance occurs in discrete quanta of $\hbar$
per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation. The universal lower bound $\hbar$
across all nine instances is the empirical content of the McGucken
Principle's action-quantization clause at every level of the chain. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:architectural-significance-universal-hbar .remark}
*Remark 1.45.A* (Architectural significance). Prior unifications had
reached subsets — gauge-theoretic via Wu--Yang--Berry--Simon--Wilczek--Zee,
symplectic-geometric via Souriau--Kostant — but no prior program
connected the canonical commutator (1) and the uncertainty bound (2)
to the geometric / topological / semiclassical / relativistic
non-closures (3)--(8) as instances of a single physical principle. The path-integral case (9) was understood by Feynman to
involve all of the others (every path interference is an
action-difference in units of $\hbar$), but the upstream physical
content of "why $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ is the universal carrier" was
never identified — Feynman's $i$ and $\hbar$ were inputs
to the formalism, not derived quantities of an upstream principle.
The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies the missing physical content: $i$ and
$\hbar$ are twin properties of one geometric flow ($\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$
with action $\hbar$ per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation), and every
non-closure that involves $x_4$ inherits the $i\hbar$ structure as
its algebraic signature.

The architectural significance is that **the empirical universality
of $\hbar$ across these nine independently-celebrated results is the
empirical content of the McGucken Principle's action-quantization
clause itself, measured nine different ways**. Every interferometer,
every monopole-search experiment, every neutron-spin rotation, every
adiabatic quantum transport, every semiclassical Bohr--Sommerfeld
orbit, every relativistic Thomas precession measurement, and every
quantum interference experiment is, in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, a
measurement of the same physical quantity — the action carried by
one cycle of $x_4$-advance — instantiated at the level of the chain
appropriate to the experimental setup. The agreement of all these
measurements on the same numerical value of $\hbar$ is therefore not
nine independent empirical coincidences but the same empirical
content measured by different probes.
:::

### Hilbert's Sixth Problem and the variability diagnostic

The variability in the postulate count of the leading
textbooks---between four (Shankar) and six (Cohen-Tannoudji), with
intermediate counts in Sakurai (five effective postulates folded into a
unified chapter), Griffiths (four to five, distributed across the early
chapters), and Weinberg (five, framed as "general principles" in Chapter
3)---is the symptom that quantum mechanics is, in the textbook
tradition, not axiomatized in the Hilbert--Sixth-Problem sense. A theory
whose axiom count varies between four and seven across its leading
expositions is a collection of empirically validated regularities being
grouped pedagogically in whatever way each author finds convenient. *The
fact that the QM postulate count is not pinned to a single integer is
the proof that, in the textbook tradition, Hilbert's Sixth Problem
remains open for quantum mechanics.*

the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$: $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) closes
it. The count of axioms is *one*. The count of derived theorems is 366
and rising. The variability disappears because the postulates were never
independent---they were the four (or five, or six, or seven) shadows
that a single geometric fact casts when projected onto different parts
of the algebraic-analytic apparatus that physicists built before
recognizing the underlying principle.

### The McGucken Dual-Channel ledger: Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel sketched side by side for QM T1--T23 {#sec:dual-channel-ledger}

Each of the 23 QM theorems QM T1--T23 proved in Part II is derived along
*two derivationally disjoint channels* from the McGucken Principle
($\mathrm{McP}$: $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$):

-   **Geometric Channel** --- the *geometric-propagation* reading of
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$: the McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ at
    every event (QB1), its $SO(3)$ spherical symmetry (QB2), the
    Compton-frequency phase rate on the Sphere (QB3), the $SU(2)$-spinor
    bundle over the Sphere (QB4), the mere integrated kinematic shadow $x_{4}= ict$ (QB5), Huygens-iterated wavefront envelopes (QB6), and the
    cross-section reading $\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ of the 4D
    $\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4)$ (QB7).

-   **Algebraic Channel** --- the *algebraic-symmetry* reading of
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$: Lorentz/translation invariance (QA1),
    Stone-theorem packaging of one-parameter unitary groups (QA2),
    compatibility-of-observables relations (QA3), Stone--von Neumann
    uniqueness on the joint observable algebra (QA4), self-adjoint
    operators as observables (QA5), Wigner classification at the
    appropriate spin/mass (QA6), and $U(1)$ phase invariance (QA7);

The two channels share only $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the final
theorem; their intermediate machinery is disjoint. The disjointness is
verified theorem-by-theorem in the audit sections of each chapter of
Part II, and it is the reason the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework
qualifies as a Hilbert--Sixth-Problem axiomatization of quantum
mechanics: the same conclusion is reached by two independent routes,
neither route privileged, both routes forced by
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

**Reading the cross-references between the two channels.** Each channel
proof closes with a characterisation step naming the machinery it used
and naming the other channel's route, in the form "no [other channel's
machinery] appears; the proof is [channel], derivationally disjoint from
the [other] route of Lemma $N$." Those references are *negative*: they
record what the proof does not use. A reader --- or an automated
dependency scan --- that counts every cross-reference inside a proof as
a dependency will therefore report the two channels as mutually
dependent, and will have the relation exactly inverted. The convention observed throughout Part II is that the only reference
from one channel's proof to the other channel's proof is the
disjointness declaration in its closing step; any positive use of the
other channel's machinery would be a failure of the audit and is
recorded as such where it occurs.

The same reading applies to *application pointers*: a proof of an
upstream result sometimes closes by naming the downstream theorem that
consumes it --- Theorem [3.2](#thm:cauchy-schwarz){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:cauchy-schwarz"} names the Heisenberg relation, and
Theorem [3.9](#thm:cauchy){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:cauchy"}
names the Born-rule derivation. Those sentences point forward from a
completed proof and carry no load in it. A dependency scan that treats
every reference inside a proof block as an edge will read both the
disjointness declarations and the application pointers backwards, and
will report cycles where the derivation order is in fact strict.

theorem statement on the left and a brief sketch of each channel's route
to that theorem in the middle and right columns. Full proofs, audits,
and disjointness verifications appear in Chapters 5--13 of Part II.

### The Projection Theorem: the Geometric Channel is foundational, the Algebraic Channel is its $T$-invariant projection {#sec:projection-theorem}

The dual-channel ledger above presents Geometric Channel and Algebraic
Channel as parallel siblings: two derivations of every QM theorem from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt} = ic$, derivationally disjoint in intermediate
machinery, converging on the same conclusion. This framing has done
useful expository work but is insufficient. The deeper
architectural fact is that the Geometric Channel is *self-sufficient* — it produces both its own $T$-anti-invariant content
and the Algebraic Channel's $T$-invariant content via the joint
chain of theorems — while the Algebraic Channel is *constructively independent
but empirically insufficient*: the Algebraic Channel's sign-blind
operator-algebraic apparatus can be built from algebraic foundations
alone but cannot pick out the $+ic$ orientation that distinguishes the
forward $x_4$-expansion from its time-reverse without importing the
Spectrum Condition or its equivalent. The projection theorem establishes
this asymmetry formally.

The three theorems of this section (Theorems 1.40, 1.41, 1.42) provide
the reading of the dual-channel architecture as a *projection
theorem*: the Algebraic Channel is the $T$-invariant projection $\Pi_A$
of the Geometric Channel, the inverse projection $\Pi_B$ does not
exist as a constructive functor, and the asymmetry between $T$-invariant
and $T$-anti-invariant content explains the empirically observed pattern
(CPT conservation while individual C, P, T are violated). The 47
dual-derivation theorems of the McGucken Duality catalog correspond to
$T$-invariant content surviving the projection; the mono-channel
theorems (strict Second Law, radiative arrow, cosmological expansion
direction, matter-antimatter asymmetry) correspond to $T$-anti-invariant
content killed by the projection. This converts the dual-channel catalog
from a contingent count into a *census*.

#### The channel projection $\Pi_A$: formal definition {#sec:channel-projection-defn}

The channel projection $\Pi_A : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ is the
forgetful functor that sends each geometric structure in the Geometric
Channel $\mathcal{B}$ to its underlying $T$-invariant algebra of
automorphisms, where $T$ is Wigner's antiunitary time-reversal operator
satisfying $T i T^{-1} = -i$ and $T M^{+}_{p}(t) = M^{-}_{p}(t)$
(the forward Sphere maps to the backward Sphere). Formally, for any
geometric structure $X \in \mathcal{B}$,
$$\Pi_A(X) := \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(X + T X T^{-1}\bigr)$$
projects onto the $T$-invariant subalgebra. Algebraic Channel content
$\mathcal{A}$ is the image of $\Pi_A$: $\mathcal{A} = \Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$.

The decomposition $+ic = (+) \cdot i \cdot c$ makes the projection's
sign-blindness explicit. The Geometric Channel content
$+ic$ carries three pieces: the orientation $(+)$, the perpendicularity
marker $i$, and the rate $c$. Under $T$: the orientation $(+)$ flips
to $(-)$, the perpendicularity marker $i$ flips to $-i$, and the rate
$c$ is preserved. The $T$-invariant content $\Pi_A(+ic) = ic - ic = 0$
when applied to the orientation alone; what survives is $i \cdot c$ as
the rate-times-perpendicularity content, with the orientation forgotten.
This is the mechanism by which the Algebraic Channel's
apparatus contains $i\hbar$ in the canonical commutator
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ — the perpendicularity marker $i$ and
the action quantum $\hbar$ survive the projection — but does not
contain the $+ic$ orientation that distinguishes the future Sphere
from the past Sphere.

::: {#thm:geometric-channel-foundational-self-sufficiency .theorem}
**Theorem 1.40** (Geometric Channel's foundational self-sufficiency;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 16.1). *The Geometric Channel
$\mathcal{B}$ is self-sufficient: it produces both its
own $T$-anti-invariant content (McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{p}(t)$, Huygens
self-replication, strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$, retarded Green's
function, Wick rotation sign $t \to -i\tau$) and the Algebraic
Channel's $T$-invariant content (operator algebra, Lorentz group,
canonical commutator $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, unitary
evolution, Dirac--von Neumann axiomatization, the chain of theorems
$\mathcal{M}_G \to M_{1,3} \to \mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{H}$)
constructively, without invoking any element of the Algebraic Channel
as input.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (eight-step constructive realisation; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] §16.4).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).
The proof is the explicit construction of the chain of theorems
from the McGucken Principle alone, with every Algebraic Channel object
reached as theorem. The eight steps are:

*Step 1: McGucken source space.* By the Space-Operator Joint derivation
Theorem
(Theorem [4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"}), the McGucken Principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt} = ic$ generates the McGucken source space
$\mathcal{M}_G = (E_4, \Phi_M, D_M, \Sigma_M)$: ambient 4D space,
constraint $\Phi_M = x_4 - ict$, source operator
$D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$, McGucken measure $\Sigma_M$.

*Step 2: Lorentzian spacetime.* The constraint surface $\Phi_M^{-1}(0)$
equipped with the induced metric from the 4D Euclidean line element
is Minkowski spacetime $M_{1,3}$ with signature $(-, +, +, +)$
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}).

*Step 3: Complex scalar field $\mathbb{C}$.* By perpendicularity selection
from one perpendicular axis
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}), the scalar field on $M_{1,3}$ is
$\mathbb{C}$.

*Step 4: Pre-Hilbert vector space.* The space of $\mathbb{C}$-valued
McGucken-Sphere wavefronts on the spatial slice, with the geometric
overlap inner product, forms a pre-Hilbert space
(Theorems [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"},
[9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}).

*Step 5: Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$.* Cauchy completion of the
pre-Hilbert space produces
$\mathcal{H} \cong L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3 x)$
(Theorem [9.17](#thm:hilbert-complete){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complete"}); the completion presupposes the
null structure of the McGucken Sphere
(Theorem [9.19A](#thm:null-structure-prerequisite){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:null-structure-prerequisite"}).

*Step 6: Canonical commutator $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$.*
Derived from the McGucken Sphere's $x_4$-perpendicularity (via $i$) and
action quantization (via $\hbar$) as the operator-level expression of
the Sphere's geometric content
(Theorem [10.1](#thm:QMT10){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT10"}).

*Step 7: Unitary evolution $U(t) = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}$.* The
McGucken-Sphere wavefront's $x_4$-flux conservation, combined with
Stone's theorem, supplies the unitary one-parameter group
(Theorem [7.1](#thm:QMT7){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT7"}).

*Step 8: Algebraic Channel's full content as theorem.* The
Lorentz group, the canonical commutator algebra, the unitary
evolution, the Dirac--von Neumann axiomatization, and the
Hilbert-Minkowski identity $\mathcal{H} \cong L^2(M_{1,3})$ are all
reached as theorems of Steps 1--7. Every Algebraic Channel
object is constructed from Geometric Channel content; no Algebraic
Channel object is invoked as input.

The construction in Steps 1--8 operates without invoking operator
algebra as primitive input. The Geometric Channel's apparatus is
self-sufficient, and the Geometric Channel's
independent construction reaches all of the Algebraic Channel's
content via the chain of theorems. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind .theorem}
**Theorem 1.41** (The Algebraic Channel's sign-blind constructive
independence and empirical insufficiency without the Spectrum
Condition; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 16.2). *The Algebraic Channel
content $\mathcal{A}$ — Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with Hermitian
operator algebra, canonical commutator $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$,
Poincaré algebra
$\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$, Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$,
variational Lagrangian--Hamiltonian formalism, Noether's first and
second theorem currents, CPT operator — is constructively independent
of the Geometric Channel: the apparatus can be built from algebraic
foundations alone without invoking the McGucken Sphere or any
Geometric Channel geometric primitive as input. The historical record
of 1925--1957 (Heisenberg-Born-Jordan, Dirac, Stone, von Neumann,
Bargmann, the first five Wightman axioms) establishes this
constructive independence empirically.*

*Stone's theorem and Stone--von Neumann uniqueness are absent from this
list by design. Per
Remark [4.36](#rmk:QA-axioms-grade1){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:QA-axioms-grade1"} they are packaging algorithms
for one-parameter unitary groups and belong to neither channel; either
channel may apply them to a unitary group it has produced by its own
route.*

*However, the Algebraic Channel's sign-blind apparatus is empirically
insufficient: it does not distinguish positive-energy from
negative-energy spectrum, does not distinguish the forward Sphere
$M^{+}_{p}(t)$ from the backward Sphere $M^{-}_{p}(t)$ as physically
realised, does not produce the strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$, does
not give the radiative arrow (retarded over advanced Green's function),
does not give the cosmological expansion direction $H_0 > 0$, and
does not produce matter dominance. Empirical adequacy of the
algebraic apparatus requires importing the **Spectrum Condition**
(Wightman 1956 sixth axiom:
$\mathrm{Spec}(P^\mu) \subset \overline{V_+}$, the closed forward
light cone in momentum space), which explicitly breaks the
$+ic \leftrightarrow -ic$ symmetry by selecting positive-energy
states. The Spectrum Condition is not a theorem of the other Algebraic
Channel axioms; it must be imposed externally as the algebraic residue
of the Geometric Channel's $+ic$ orientation surviving the projection
$\Pi_A$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). Constructive independence is established by the historical
record (citations above). Empirical insufficiency is established by
the explicit observation that the standard Wightman axioms 1--5
(invariance, vacuum uniqueness, locality, completeness, fields as
operator-valued distributions) do not entail the Spectrum Condition;
this is a fact about the algebraic apparatus, not a
contingent historical accident. The Spectrum Condition was added as
an independent axiom (Wightman 1956 axiom 6) because the first five
axioms cannot select positive-energy spectrum without it. The
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework identifies the Spectrum Condition as the algebraic
residue of the Geometric Channel's $+ic$ orientation surviving the
projection $\Pi_A$: the orientation cannot live in the sign-blind
algebra (Lemma 16.3.1 below), but it must be imported for the algebra
to be empirically adequate. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:content-asymmetry .theorem}
**Theorem 1.42** (Content asymmetry: $\Pi_A$ exists, $\Pi_B$ does
not; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 16.3). *The channel projection
$\Pi_A : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ exists as a constructive
forgetful functor (Theorem [1.40](#thm:geometric-channel-foundational-self-sufficiency){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:geometric-channel-foundational-self-sufficiency"}). The
inverse channel projection $\Pi_B : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$
does not exist: there is no constructive functor from the Algebraic
Channel's content alone to the Geometric Channel's full content. Any
candidate $\Pi_B$ requires importing either*

*(a) the Spectrum Condition or its equivalent — the $+ic$ orientation
expressed algebraically — which is not a theorem of $\mathcal{A}$
(sign-blindness obstruction); or*

*(b) a geometric-reconstruction theorem requiring additional
non-algebraic input — commutativity (Gelfand--Naimark), regional
structure (Reeh--Schlieder), Dirac operator (Connes), or
noncommutative spectral triple — to recover the McGucken Sphere
as a point-set in $M_{1,3}$ (geometry-blindness obstruction).*

*The Algebraic Channel's content equals $\Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$ (the
$T$-invariant projection of the Geometric Channel's geometric content);
the Geometric Channel's content properly contains the Algebraic
Channel's content. The $T$-anti-invariant residue
$\mathcal{B} \setminus \Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$ — the $+ic$ orientation,
the six aligned arrows of time, the strict Second Law, the
matter-dominance / baryon-asymmetry direction, the retarded-causation
direction, the Wick-rotation convergent sign, and the McGucken Sphere
as geometric point-set — exists in $\mathcal{B}$ but not in
$\mathcal{A}$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (via two independent lemmas establishing two obstructions to $\Pi_B$).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**Sign-blindness obstruction (Lemma 16.3.1 of [@MG-Hilbert-2026]).**
Let $\mathcal{A}_0 \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ be the subset of
Algebraic Channel content consisting of the Lorentzian metric
$\eta_{\mu\nu}$, the Lorentz algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, the
Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$, the canonical commutator
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, the unitary group
$U(t) = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}$, and the variational
Lagrangian-Hamiltonian apparatus with Noether currents. Each element
of $\mathcal{A}_0$ is $T$-invariant up to algebra-internal sign
conventions consistent with antiunitarity:

-   $T\eta_{\mu\nu}T^{-1} = \eta_{\mu\nu}$ (the metric depends on
    $(ic)^2 = -c^2$, sign-blind on $i$).
-   $T J^{\mu\nu}T^{-1}$ preserves the Lorentz algebra (both sides
    flip sign of $i$, structure constants flip accordingly).
-   $T[\hat{q}, \hat{p}]T^{-1} = [T\hat{q}T^{-1}, T\hat{p}T^{-1}] = -i\hbar$
    with the Wigner convention $T\hat{q}T^{-1} = \hat{q}$,
    $T\hat{p}T^{-1} = -\hat{p}$: the algebra is preserved.
-   $TU(t)T^{-1} = U(-t)^{-1}$: the one-parameter group is mapped to
    its inverse parameterization, generating an isomorphic algebra.
-   The Lagrangian $L(q, \dot{q})$ is $T$-symmetric when
    $L(q, -\dot{q}) = L(q, \dot{q})$, which holds for standard
    kinetic-plus-potential Lagrangians.

Closure of the algebra: every element of $\mathcal{A}_0$ is built
from these by polynomial composition, bracketing, and exponentiation;
each operation preserves $T$-invariance. The involution
$i \mapsto -i$ extends to an automorphism of $\mathcal{A}_0$. No
element of $\mathcal{A}_0$ distinguishes the $+ic$ from $-ic$
orientation.

Suppose for contradiction that $\Pi_B : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$
exists as a constructive functor. Then $\Pi_B$ must produce the
McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ from the Algebraic Channel's content
alone. The Sphere has definite orientation:
$TM^{+}_{p}(t) = M^{-}_{p}(t)$ with $M^{+}_{p}(t) \ne M^{-}_{p}(t)$.
To distinguish $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ from $M^{-}_{p}(t)$, $\Pi_B$ must break
the $+ic \leftrightarrow -ic$ symmetry. But every element of
$\mathcal{A}_0$ is preserved by the involution. Therefore no
algebraic structure in $\mathcal{A}$ breaks the symmetry. Any
candidate $\Pi_B$ must import the symmetry-breaking content (the
Spectrum Condition or equivalent) from outside $\mathcal{A}$. This is
the first obstruction.

**Geometry-blindness obstruction (Lemma 16.3.2 of
[@MG-Hilbert-2026]).** The Algebraic Channel operates on operator
algebras, not on point-sets. The Sphere $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ is a point-set:
a specific subset of $M_{1,3}$ identified by a metric equation.
Recovering $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ from $\mathcal{A}$ requires a reconstruction
theorem mapping algebraic data to point-set geometric data. The
historical record of algebra-to-geometry reconstruction theorems
(Gelfand-Naimark, Reeh-Schlieder, Connes' spectral triples,
noncommutative geometry) shows that each reconstruction requires
additional non-algebraic input: a commutative subalgebra (Gelfand),
a regional-structure map $O \mapsto \mathcal{R}(O)$ (Reeh-Schlieder),
a Dirac operator with accompanying axioms (Connes), or a
noncommutative spectral triple. None of these is internal to
$\mathcal{A}$; each is imposed from outside.

Even granted such additional input, the recovered manifold is at best
Minkowski space $M_{1,3}$, not the Sphere $M^{+}_{p}(t)$. The Sphere
is a specific subset of $M_{1,3}$ identified by the metric equation
$|\mathbf{x}_q - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t_q - t_p)$ with the orientation
constraint $t_q > t_p$. To identify this subset within the
reconstructed manifold requires (a) a marked event $p$, (b) an
orientation choice for $t_q - t_p > 0$, (c) the metric structure to
evaluate the equation — none of which is internal to the algebra.

**Both obstructions independently block $\Pi_B$.** The two
obstructions are independent: resolving one does not resolve the
other. Importing the Spectrum Condition resolves sign-blindness but
leaves geometry-blindness; importing a Dirac operator resolves
geometry-blindness but leaves sign-blindness. Both must be addressed
independently to construct $\Pi_B$, and each requires importing
content not present in $\mathcal{A}$.

**Conclusion.** Both obstructions independently block the existence
of a constructive $\Pi_B : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$. The
forward projection $\Pi_A$ exists; the inverse projection does not.
The Algebraic Channel is the constructive forgetful image of the
Geometric Channel under $\Pi_A$; the Geometric Channel is the source.
The relation is image-source asymmetric, not symmetric sibling-sibling.
◻
:::

::: {#rmk:projection-theorem-architectural-reading .remark}
*Remark 1.43* (Architectural reading of the projection theorem). The
projection theorem reframes the dual-channel architecture from the
"parallel siblings" expository framing into a census:

-   The catalog of dual-derivation theorems (the McGucken Duality
    catalog) is the catalog of objects $T$ such that
    $T \in \Pi_A(\mathcal{B}) \cap \mathcal{A}$ — i.e., $T$

    constructible within $\mathcal{A}$ (which is why each theorem
    has two derivations: the Geometric Channel route through the

-   The mono-channel catalog is the catalog of
    $T \in \mathcal{B} \setminus \Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$ — objects
    whose orientation content is killed by $\Pi_A$ and therefore
    have no Algebraic Channel derivation. The strict Second Law
    $dS/dt > 0$, the radiative arrow, the cosmological expansion
    direction $H_0 > 0$, the matter-antimatter asymmetry, the
    Wick-rotation convergent sign, and the McGucken Sphere as
    point-set are in this catalog.

The empirical signature of the projection-theorem structure is the
**CPT conservation with individual C, P, T violation** pattern of
contemporary particle physics (Wu 1957, Cronin-Fitch 1964,
CPLEAR 1998, BaBar 2012): CPT is $T$-invariant and dual-channel;
individual C, P, T are $T$-anti-invariant and mono-channel. The
projection theorem accounts for this empirical pattern as the
consequence of the $\Pi_A$ projection's kernel containing
the individual time-reversal content.

The diagnostic implication for orthodox programs: every
program operating purely within $\mathcal{A}$ (universal wavefunction
of Many-Worlds, AdS/CFT, ER=EPR, Page curve, holographic principle,
algebraic QFT, Wightman axiomatics without the Spectrum Condition)
fails to recover the $T$-anti-invariant content of physical reality
because the algebra it operates on is the $T$-invariant projection of
the structure. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's recovery of the
arrows of time, the strict Second Law, and matter-dominance from the
Geometric Channel's $+ic$ orientation is the mechanism by
which this content lives in the channel — not in its
projection.
:::

#### Corollary 1.44.2: Dual-derivation availability iff $T$-invariance of mathematical content {#sec:dual-derivation-iff-T-invariance}

::: {#cor:dual-derivation-iff-T-invariance .corollary}
**Corollary 1.46** (Dual-derivation availability iff $T$-invariance;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Corollary 16.4). *For any framework theorem
$T_\text{th}$:*

*(i) If $T_\text{th}$'s mathematical content is $T$-invariant
(sign-blind on $+ic$, i.e.,
$T_\text{th} = \Pi_A(T_\text{th})$), then $T_\text{th}$ has both
an Algebraic Channel derivation (using only algebraic content, never
invoking the Sphere) and a Geometric Channel derivation (using full
geometric content), and the two derivations share no intermediate
machinery (convergent overdetermination in Wimsatt 1981
[@Wimsatt1981Robust] sense).*

*(ii) If $T_\text{th}$'s mathematical content is $T$-anti-invariant
(depends on the sign of $+ic$, i.e.,
$T_\text{th} \ne \Pi_A(T_\text{th})$), then
$T_\text{th} \in \mathcal{B} \setminus \Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$ —
$T_\text{th}$ has no Algebraic Channel derivation, by the
impossibility that the sign content distinguishing
$T_\text{th}$ from $\Pi_A(T_\text{th})$ has been projected away.*

*The 47-theorem dual-channel catalog of [@MG-Symmetry-2026] is
therefore the census of $T$-invariant framework content;
the mono-channel catalog is the census of
$T$-anti-invariant framework content. The dual-derivation count is the catalog of which theorems sit in the image of
$\Pi_A$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

*(i)* Suppose $T_\text{th}$ is $T$-invariant. Then
$T_\text{th} \in \Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$ by definition of $\Pi_A$
as restriction to the $T$-invariant subalgebra. Therefore
$T_\text{th}$ has an Algebraic Channel derivation via the
sign-blind algebraic apparatus (the 1925--1957 historical record
demonstrates that the sign-blind apparatus reaches $T$-invariant
content). $T_\text{th}$ also has a Geometric Channel derivation via
the geometric apparatus (the Sphere, Huygens, chain of theorems).
The two derivations share no intermediate machinery because the
Algebraic Channel derivation never invokes the Sphere and the
Geometric Channel derivation never invokes the operator algebra as
primitive input
(Theorem [1.40](#thm:geometric-channel-foundational-self-sufficiency){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:geometric-channel-foundational-self-sufficiency"}).

*(ii)* Suppose $T_\text{th}$ is $T$-anti-invariant:
$T(T_\text{th}) \ne T_\text{th}$. Then
$\Pi_A(T_\text{th}) = \tfrac{1}{2}(T_\text{th} + T T_\text{th} T^{-1})$
either equals zero (for fully anti-invariant content) or is strictly
less than $T_\text{th}$ (for content with both $T$-invariant and
$T$-anti-invariant components). Therefore $T_\text{th}$ is
(partially) killed by $\Pi_A$, and
$T_\text{th} \notin \Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$. By
Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}, the inverse projection $\Pi_B$
does not exist; there is no Algebraic Channel construction reaching
$T_\text{th}$. ◻
:::

#### Corollary 1.44.3: Mathematical content vs. physical instantiation {#sec:mathematical-content-vs-physical-instantiation}

**Corollary 1.47** (Mathematical content vs. physical instantiation;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Corollary 16.5). *Every framework theorem
$T_\text{th}$ has two readings:*

reference="cor:dual-derivation-iff-T-invariance"}).*

*(ii) Physical instantiation: the realisation of $T_\text{th}$ in
a physical event or process in the universe. This instantiation is

expands outward, measurements happen forward in time, decoherence

Channel.*

may be $T$-invariant or $T$-anti-invariant; the physical
instantiation of any theorem (symmetric or asymmetric

runs at $+ic$.*

distinction is established by the following canonical examples,
each verifying the pattern in (i)--(ii):

content ($|\psi|^2 = \psi^* \psi$ is PT-symmetric on $i$);

$G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$:* $T$-invariant
