#### Theorem 16.6: No-go theorem for entropy-decreasing macroscopic trajectories {#sec:no-go-entropy-decreasing}

::: {#thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing .theorem}
**Theorem 1.48** (No-go theorem for entropy-decreasing macroscopic
trajectories; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 16.6). *Under the McGucken
Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = +ic$ with the McGucken-Sphere
Brownian coupling
$D_x = \varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega/(2\gamma_L^2)$, no
entropy-decreasing macroscopic trajectory in the universe's Sphere
chain exists.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Suppose, for contradiction, that there exists a
macroscopic trajectory along which $dS/dt < 0$ for some finite
interval $\Delta t > 0$. By the identification of macroscopic
entropy with $x_4$-mode-counting on Sphere horizons, a decreasing
$S$ corresponds to a decreasing $x_4$-mode count along the
trajectory. The $x_4$-mode count on any horizon is proportional to
the surface area of the corresponding McGucken Sphere, with one
Planck-area cell per mode. A decreasing mode count therefore
requires a contracting Sphere.

A contracting McGucken Sphere corresponds to
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = -ic$ at the Sphere's apex, contradicting the
McGucken Principle's $+ic$ orientation
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i) and (iii)). Since the
principle holds at every spacetime event without exception
(event-homogeneity), no event in the universe's Sphere chain can
have $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = -ic$, and therefore no contracting Sphere
exists. Therefore no entropy-decreasing macroscopic trajectory
exists. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:loschmidt-boltzmann-dissolution .remark}
*Remark 1.48.A* (The Loschmidt--Boltzmann dissolution). The strict
Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ is a forced consequence of the McGucken
Principle's $+ic$ orientation — not a separate postulate, not a
statistical assumption, not a thermodynamic limit theorem requiring
the Stosszahlansatz. The Loschmidt objection (Loschmidt 1876
[@Loschmidt1876Objection]) states that time-symmetric microdynamics
cannot derive a strict monotonic Second Law because any solution
has a time-reversed counterpart with entropy decreasing. The
orthodox response (Boltzmann's Stosszahlansatz / molecular-chaos
assumption; the Past Hypothesis of Albert 2000
[@Albert2000Time]; fluctuation theorems of Jarzynski 1997
[@Jarzynski1997Equality], Crooks 1999 [@Crooks1999Fluctuation]) has
not produced a derivation of the strict Second Law from
time-symmetric microdynamics alone; every successful derivation
imports time-asymmetric content as additional input.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reconciles both positions:

*(i)* Loschmidt was right about Algebraic Channel: it is
time-symmetric microdynamics by construction
(Theorem [1.41](#thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind"}, the sign-blind
apparatus is $T$-invariant). The 150-year debate confirms this
empirically.

*(ii)* Boltzmann was right that the Second Law is a real physical
fact: entropy increases, heat flows from hot to cold, eggs break
and do not unbreak, biological systems run irreversibly, black-hole
horizons grow monotonically.

*(iii)* The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reconciles both: Algebraic Channel
is time-symmetric (Loschmidt is right about this); Geometric
Channel carries the $+ic$ orientation that produces the strict
Second Law (Boltzmann is right about this); both hold
simultaneously because they are two readings of one principle (the
projection theorem). The Algebraic Channel cannot produce the
Second Law (Loschmidt) because the projection is sign-blind on
$+ic$; the Geometric Channel does produce the Second Law
(Boltzmann + Theorem [1.48](#thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing"}) because the orientation
is in the principle. The 150-year standoff is resolved by
recognising that both observers were correct in their respective
channels.
:::

#### Theorem 1.48.B: Positive constructive derivation of $dS/dt > 0$ from Huygens' Principle on the expanding McGucken Sphere {#sec:sphere-expansion-entropy-positive}

Theorem [1.48](#thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing"} established the *no-go*
side of the Second Law: no entropy-decreasing macroscopic trajectory
exists because a decreasing $x_4$-mode count would require a
contracting Sphere, contradicting $+ic$. Theorem 1.48.B establishes
the *positive constructive* complement: a direct four-step chain
from the McGucken Principle's $+ic$-oriented Huygens Sphere
expansion at every event to strictly positive entropy production,
with three convergent tier-level realizations. Where
Theorem [1.48](#thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing"} proves that $dS/dt < 0$
cannot occur, Theorem 1.48.B derives that $dS/dt > 0$ *does* occur,
by explicit construction on the expanding Sphere's Planck-area mode
count.

::: {#thm:sphere-expansion-entropy-positive .theorem}
**Theorem 1.48.B** (Positive constructive derivation of the strict
Second Law from expanding McGucken Sphere via Huygens' Principle
and Shannon entropy on Planck-area mode count;
McGucken, E. (Aug 25, 2025) *The Derivation of Entropy's Increase from the McGucken Principle of a Fourth Expanding Dimension dx₄/dt = ic*; elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2025/08/25/; McGucken, E. (April 15, 2026) *A Derivation of Feynman's Path Integral from the McGucken Principle of the Fourth Expanding Dimension dx₄/dt = ic*; elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/04/15/;
McGucken, E. (2026) *McGucken Thermodynamics from dx₄/dt = ic*, Theorems 9 and 15; elliotmcguckenphysics.com).

*Under the McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = +ic$ at every
event $p \in \mathcal{M}_G$, the entropy of the universe increases
monotonically in parameter time via the direct constructive chain*
$$\underbrace{\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = +ic}_{\text{McGucken Principle}}
\xrightarrow{\text{Huygens Sphere generation}}
\underbrace{A(t) = 4\pi c^2 (t - t_p)^2\ \uparrow}_{\text{Sphere surface area grows}}
\xrightarrow{\text{Planck-area quantization}}
\underbrace{N(t) = \frac{A(t)}{\ell_P^2}\ \uparrow}_{x_4\text{-mode count grows}}
\xrightarrow{S = k_B \ln W}
\underbrace{\frac{dS}{dt} > 0}_{\text{strict Second Law}}$$
*with three convergent tier-level realizations:*

*(i) **Geometric tier (Bekenstein--Hawking on the expanding Sphere):**
$S_{BH}(t) = k_B\, A(t)/(4\ell_P^2) = \pi k_B c^2 (t - t_p)^2 / \ell_P^2$
grows quadratically in $t$, with
$dS_{BH}/dt = 2\pi k_B c^2 (t - t_p)/\ell_P^2 > 0$.*

*(ii) **Matter tier (Compton diffusion on the Sphere via
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$):** For matter systems coupled to the
advancing $x_4$ via Compton frequency, isotropic diffusion on the
Sphere generates a Gaussian spatial distribution with variance
$\sigma^2(t) = 2 D_{\text{total}}\, t$, whose Shannon entropy is
$S(t) = \tfrac{3}{2}\, k_B \ln(4\pi e D_{\text{total}}\, t)$ with
$dS/dt = \tfrac{3}{2}\, k_B / t > 0$
(Theorem [22.4](#thm:compton-entropy){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:compton-entropy"}).*

*(iii) **Nonlocality tier (Second McGucken Law of Nonlocality):**
The sphere of potential entanglement grows at radius
$R(t) = c(t - t_p)$
(Theorem [1.50.2](#thm:second-mcgucken-law){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:second-mcgucken-law"}); more particles become
Sphere participants; joint entanglement-state-space volume grows;
entanglement entropy of any coarse-grained subsystem grows
monotonically.*

*All three tiers descend from the single chain via
the same four steps. The convergence is
the McGucken Entropy Identity
(Remark [1.48.B.2](#rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity"}): five orthodox entropy
formulas (Shannon, Boltzmann--Gibbs, von Neumann,
Bekenstein--Hawking, Wiener) are five readings of one quantity —
the entropy of the McGucken Sphere's $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant
Haar measure under Compton coupling.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (four-step chain, then three-tier realization).*

**Step 1: $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = +ic$ generates the per-event McGucken
Sphere via Huygens' Principle.** By
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i), (ii), (iii), and (v), at
every event $p \in \mathcal{M}_G$ the fourth dimension advances at
$+ic$ isotropically in the spatial three, with monotonic orientation.
By the McGucken-Sphere definition (paper §2.5, Definition 2.3:
$\Sigma^+(p) = \{q : |\mathbf{x}_q - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t_q - t_p),\ t_q > t_p\}$)
and the McGucken-Sphere-as-Huygens-wavefront identification (paper
Remark 7.16: *"the McGucken Sphere from any event E is, by the
canonical isotropic expansion of clause 3 of §2.4, exactly the
Huygens wavefront from that event"*), the McGucken Principle at
$p$ generates the spherically symmetric null wavefront
$\Sigma^+(p)$ expanding at velocity $c$ from $p$ into the future
light-cone, with every point on the wavefront itself the apex of a
secondary McGucken Sphere (Sphere self-replication). The Sphere is
*not* postulated separately from the McGucken Principle; it is a
direct geometric consequence of $+ic$ at every event, with Huygens'
Principle as the natural per-event mechanism of Sphere generation
[McGucken, E., *A Derivation of Feynman's Path Integral from the
McGucken Principle*, April 15, 2026, §3 Lemma 3.1;
elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/04/15/].

**Step 2: Sphere surface area grows monotonically in $t$.** At
parameter time $t > t_p$, the spatial slice cross-section of
$\Sigma^+(p)$ is a 2-sphere of radius $r(t) = c(t - t_p)$ centered
at $\mathbf{x}_p$. Its surface area is
$$A(t) = 4\pi\, r(t)^2 = 4\pi c^2 (t - t_p)^2.$$
By $+ic$-orientation
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iii), monotonicity),
$t - t_p > 0$ for all $t > t_p$ with strict monotonic increase in
$t$, so $A(t)$ grows monotonically. The area growth rate is
$dA/dt = 8\pi c^2 (t - t_p) > 0$, strictly positive at every
parameter time after the apex event. This is pure geometry with no
thermodynamic or matter input.

**Step 3: Planck-area quantization gives monotonic mode count
growth.** Decompose the Sphere's surface into cells of Planck area
$\ell_P^2 = \hbar G / c^3$. Each Planck-area cell hosts one
$x_4$-mode — one elementary oscillation of $x_4$-advance carrying
one quantum of action $\hbar$ at Planck frequency
$\omega_P = \sqrt{c^5 / \hbar G}$
(Theorem [3.1](#thm:c-hbar-twin){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:c-hbar-twin"} — the twin-constant status of $c$ and
$\hbar$ as rate and action quantum of $x_4$-advance). Total mode count on the Sphere
at parameter time $t$ is
$$N(t) = \frac{A(t)}{\ell_P^2} = \frac{4\pi c^2 (t - t_p)^2}{\ell_P^2},$$
with growth rate
$dN/dt = 8\pi c^2 (t - t_p) / \ell_P^2 > 0$. The mode count grows
quadratically in parameter time. This step uses the two McGucken
constants $c$ (rate of $x_4$-advance) and $\hbar$ (action quantum
per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation) plus Newton's $G$ to set the
Planck-area cell size. The mode-count identification is anchored
in McGucken, E. (2026) *McGucken Thermodynamics from dx₄/dt = ic*, Theorem 15; elliotmcguckenphysics.com.

**Step 4: Boltzmann's formula gives strict monotonic entropy
growth.** Let $g$ denote the microstate-count-per-mode assigned by
the counting convention in use — the number of accessible states
per Planck-area cell consistent with the macrostate constraints.
The total accessible microstate count is
$$W(t) = g^{N(t)},$$
and Boltzmann's formula gives
$$S(t) = k_B \ln W(t) = k_B\, N(t)\, \ln g.$$
Since $N(t)$ grows monotonically in $t$ (Step 3) and $\ln g > 0$
for any $g > 1$, $S(t)$ grows monotonically in $t$:
$$\frac{dS}{dt} = k_B\, \ln g \cdot \frac{dN}{dt} = \frac{8\pi k_B c^2 (t - t_p)\ln g}{\ell_P^2} > 0.$$
The strict Second Law is thereby established as a forced theorem
of the McGucken Principle, with the $+ic$ orientation clause doing
the the essential work at Step 2 (area monotonicity) and the
Planck-area-cell identification doing the mode-count work at
Step 3. **The specific numerical value of the proportionality
constant $k_B \ln g$ depends on the counting convention**: a
two-state-per-mode convention ($g = 2$) yields
$k_B \ln 2 \approx 0.693\, k_B$ per mode; the Bekenstein--Hawking
convention (see Tier 1 below) yields $k_B/4$ per mode. What Step 4
derives is monotonicity, not the specific constant — the constant
is fixed by external inputs from the counting convention appropriate
to the tier.

**Three-tier realization.**

*Tier 1 (Geometric — Bekenstein--Hawking).* The Bekenstein--Hawking
counting convention specifies entropy per Planck-area cell equal to
$k_B/4$ (Bekenstein 1973 *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333; Hawking 1975
*Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199 — the factor $1/4$ is fixed by
Hawking's near-horizon quantum-field calculation of the horizon
temperature $T_H = \hbar\kappa/(2\pi c k_B)$ together with the
Clausius relation $dS = dE/T$, not by the elementary
mode-counting of Step 4). Under this convention:
$$S_{BH}(t) = \frac{k_B\, A(t)}{4\ell_P^2} = \frac{\pi k_B c^2 (t - t_p)^2}{\ell_P^2},$$
growing quadratically with $dS_{BH}/dt = 2\pi k_B c^2 (t - t_p)/\ell_P^2 > 0$.
This is Bekenstein--Hawking horizon entropy applied at the
per-event Sphere scale rather than the black-hole-horizon scale
[McGucken, E., *The Derivation of Entropy's Increase from the
McGucken Principle*, August 25, 2025;
elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2025/08/25/].

*Tier 2 (Matter — Compton diffusion).* For matter systems Compton-
coupled at $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$, the McGucken-Sphere Brownian
coupling
(Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT22"}) generates isotropic diffusion on the spatial
slice with $\sigma^2(t) = 2 D_{\text{total}}\, t$. The Shannon
entropy of the resulting 3D Gaussian is
$S(t) = \tfrac{3}{2} k_B \ln(4\pi e D_{\text{total}}\, t)$, with
$dS/dt = \tfrac{3}{2} k_B / t > 0$
(Theorem [22.4](#thm:compton-entropy){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:compton-entropy"}). The physical mechanism: matter
particles' collision events undergo iterated isotropic displacement
on the McGucken Sphere at each collision, with the collision rate
set by the Compton coupling. The Shannon entropy of the matter
distribution grows with $\ln t$.

*Tier 3 (Nonlocality — Second McGucken Law).* By
Theorem [1.50.2](#thm:second-mcgucken-law){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:second-mcgucken-law"} (Second McGucken Law of
Nonlocality), the region of potential entanglement from apex $p$
at parameter time $t$ is the 2-sphere of radius $c(t - t_p)$,
growing at velocity $c$. Particles inside this region are potential
Sphere participants; particles outside cannot be. As the region
grows, more particles become potential participants; the joint
state-space volume of the entangled subsystem grows; the
entanglement entropy of any coarse-grained subsystem-plus-environment
partition grows monotonically. The nonlocality tier connects
McGucken to Van Raamsdonk 2010's vacuum-entanglement-entropy
picture at the tier level but with the direction of derivation
reversed (Sphere expansion → entanglement growth, not entanglement
→ spacetime).

**Convergence of the three tiers.** All three tiers instantiate the
same four-step chain (Steps 1--4) with different specifications of
the microstate count $W(t)$: Tier 1 uses horizon-mode counts on the
Sphere's Planck-area cells; Tier 2 uses matter-diffusion Gaussian
volumes; Tier 3 uses joint-entanglement state spaces. All three
grow monotonically because $A(t) = 4\pi c^2(t-t_p)^2$ grows
monotonically, which grows because $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = +ic$ at
every event. The convergence is the McGucken Entropy Identity
(Remark [1.48.B.2](#rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity"}). $\square$
:::

::: {#rmk:huygens-per-event-sphere-mechanism .remark}
*Remark 1.48.B.1* (Huygens' Principle as the per-event Sphere
generation mechanism). Step 1 of the proof invokes Huygens'
Principle as the mechanism by which $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = +ic$ at
every event generates the McGucken Sphere. This identification is
established rigorously in McGucken, E. (April 15, 2026)
*A Derivation of Feynman's Path Integral from the McGucken Principle
of the Fourth Expanding Dimension dx₄/dt = ic*, §3 Lemma 3.1
(elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/04/15/): the spherically symmetric expansion of $x_4$ at rate
$c$ from every point in 3-space *is* Huygens' construction, viewed
geometrically. Every point in 3-space acts as a source of a
spherical wavefront at parameter time $t$ because $x_4$'s expansion
at $+ic$ physically distributes every point across a 2-sphere of
radius $c(t - t_p)$. Huygens' 1690 Principle
[@Huygens1690TraiteLumiere] is therefore not a postulate about
wave propagation added to the framework — it is a derived theorem
of the McGucken Principle at the per-event Sphere-generation level.
The paper's §17.1bis Sense (iii) (Huygens caustics) establishes
this at the multi-framework-reinforcement level; Theorem 1.48.B
uses it at Step 1.
:::

::: {#rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity .remark}
*Remark 1.48.B.2* (The McGucken Entropy Identity: five orthodox
entropies as five readings of one quantity). The convergence of the
three tiers in Theorem 1.48.B is the tier-level content of the
**McGucken Entropy Identity** McGucken, E. (2026) *Companion synthesis paper* §11.5 and *McGucken Thermodynamics* §III: the five orthodox entropy formulas —

- **Shannon entropy** (Shannon 1948
  (Shannon, C. E. *Bell Syst. Tech. J.* 27, 379, 1948)): $S = -\sum_i p_i \log p_i$ on
  probability distributions.

- **Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy** (Boltzmann 1872 (Boltzmann, L. *Wiener Berichte* 66, 275, 1872);
  Gibbs 1902 (Gibbs, J. W. *Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics*, Yale University Press, 1902)): $S = k_B \ln W$ on
  phase-space microstates.

- **von Neumann entropy** (von Neumann 1932
  [@vonNeumann1932]):
  $S = -k_B\, \mathrm{Tr}(\rho \ln \rho)$ on density matrices.

- **Bekenstein--Hawking entropy** (Bekenstein 1973
  (Bekenstein, J. D. *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333, 1973); Hawking 1975 (*Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199)):
  $S = k_B A / (4 \ell_P^2)$ on horizon areas.

- **Wiener entropy** (Wiener 1948 (Wiener, N. *Cybernetics*, MIT Press, 1948)):
  $S = -\int p(x) \log p(x)\, dx$ on continuous probability
  densities.

— are five readings of *one* quantity: the entropy of the McGucken
Sphere's $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant Haar measure under Compton
coupling. The 76-year coincidence that $-\sum p_i \log p_i$ appears
identically in information theory (Shannon), statistical mechanics
(Boltzmann, Gibbs), quantum mechanics (von Neumann), and
gravitational thermodynamics (Bekenstein--Hawking) is forced by the
McGucken Duality of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$. Each formula counts $x_4$-modes on the
McGucken Sphere under a different reference structure (probability
distribution, phase-space measure, density matrix, horizon area,
continuous density), with the underlying counted quantity being
the same $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar-measure-on-Sphere structure.

Theorem 1.48.B's three-tier convergence is the physical
instantiation: Tier 1 realizes the Bekenstein--Hawking reading;
Tier 2 realizes the Shannon/Boltzmann--Gibbs/Wiener reading via
the Gaussian on the spatial slice; Tier 3 realizes the von Neumann
reading via density-matrix content on entangled subsystems. All
three tiers converge because they are three readings of the same
McGucken-Sphere-Haar-entropy content.
:::

::: {#rmk:comparison-bekenstein-1974 .remark}
*Remark 1.48.B.3* (Comparison to the Bekenstein bound). The
Bekenstein bound (Bekenstein 1974 (Bekenstein, J. D. *Phys. Rev. D* 9, 3292, 1974); Bekenstein
1981 (Bekenstein, J. D. *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 287, 1981)) states that the entropy of a system of
energy $E$ enclosed in a sphere of radius $R$ is bounded above by
$S \le 2\pi k_B\, ER / (\hbar c)$. Bekenstein's bound is an *upper*
bound on entropy in a spherical region and does not itself derive
$dS/dt > 0$. The McGucken position: Bekenstein's spherical region
is a spatial-slice section of a McGucken Sphere, with the bound's
factors of $R$ and $\hbar c$ carrying the McGucken $c$ (Sphere
radius growth rate) and $\hbar$ (Sphere action quantum) as the
two universal McGucken constants. Bekenstein correctly identified
the spherical region as the geometric locus and the two universal
constants as the central factors, but did not identify the
Sphere expansion at $+ic$ as the mechanism of monotonic entropy
production. Theorem 1.48.B supplies the mechanism; Bekenstein's
bound then supplies the compatible upper envelope on the McGucken
entropy trajectory.
:::

::: {#rmk:comparison-bekenstein-hawking-1972 .remark}
*Remark 1.48.B.4* (Comparison to Bekenstein--Hawking horizon
entropy). The Bekenstein--Hawking entropy formula
$S_{BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$ (Bekenstein 1973 (Bekenstein, J. D. *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333, 1973);
Hawking 1975 (Hawking, S. W. *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199, 1975)) applies to black-hole horizons and
gives the entropy per unit horizon area. The generalized second
law (GSL; Bekenstein 1974 (Bekenstein, J. D. *Phys. Rev. D* 9, 3292, 1974)) states that
$S_{\text{matter, outside}} + S_{BH}$ is non-decreasing during
horizon-changing processes. The McGucken position: $S_{BH}$ is
one of the five readings of the McGucken Entropy Identity
(Remark [1.48.B.2](#rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity"}), specifically the
horizon-area reading. Theorem 1.48.B applies it at the per-event
Sphere scale, not just at black-hole-horizon scale: *every* event
of $\mathcal{M}_G$ has a McGucken Sphere with its own Bekenstein-
Hawking entropy $S_{BH}(t) = k_B A(t)/(4\ell_P^2)$, growing
monotonically at rate $2\pi k_B c^2 (t - t_p)/\ell_P^2$. The GSL
is the aggregated statement across the universe's Sphere chain.
Bekenstein and Hawking correctly identified the horizon-area
entropy formula and the GSL structure; McGucken generalizes to
per-event scale via the Sphere-at-every-event postulate.
:::

::: {#rmk:comparison-bousso-covariant-1999 .remark}
*Remark 1.48.B.5* (Comparison to Bousso's Covariant Entropy Bound
— crucial distinction). Bousso's Covariant Entropy
Bound (Bousso 1999 (*JHEP* 07:004, 1999; arXiv:hep-th/9905177); Bousso 2002
[@Bousso2002HolographicPrinciple]; Bousso, Fisher, Leichenauer,
Wall 2014 (Bousso, R., Fisher, Z., Leichenauer, S., Wall, A. C., arXiv:1506.02669, 2015)) states that
the entropy on a light-sheet with **non-positive expansion**
(contracting or stationary null hypersurface) is bounded above by
$S \le A/(4\ell_P^2)$. The key feature of Bousso's
construction is that expanding null surfaces are **explicitly
excluded** from the bound: only light-sheets with $\theta \le 0$
(non-positive expansion of the null congruence) qualify.

The McGucken position on Bousso: Bousso's bound is a legitimate
holographic bound on the **contracting** null-hypersurface family
— the past light-cones and inward-focused light-sheets that Bousso's
construction requires. The McGucken Sphere is the *opposite*
family: **expanding** null wavefronts with $\theta > 0$, radiating
outward from every event. Bousso and McGucken are addressing
different halves of the four null congruences at each spacelike
2-surface: Bousso's bound covers the past-directed and inward-focused
future-directed null sheets; the McGucken Sphere is the outward-focused
future-directed null wavefront.

The two positions are therefore **complementary, not
contradictory**: Bousso bounds entropy from above on contracting
light-sheets; McGucken derives entropy production from below on
expanding light-sheets (McGucken Spheres). Together they establish
that the four null congruences at every event carry a complete
entropy structure — two contract with entropy upper-bounded (Bousso),
two expand with entropy production strictly positive (McGucken).
The orthodox tradition worked out the Bousso half in 1999--2014;
Theorem 1.48.B supplies the McGucken half at the tier level.

The reason Bousso excludes expanding null surfaces from
his bound: on an expanding null surface, entropy can grow with the
surface area (as Theorem 1.48.B derives), so an upper bound of the
form $S \le A/(4\ell_P^2)$ becomes trivially satisfied or requires
new machinery to state as a non-trivial bound. Bousso chose to work
with the contracting family where the bound is non-trivial; McGucken
works with the expanding family where the *lower bound on entropy
production* is the non-trivial statement.
:::

::: {#rmk:comparison-padmanabhan-2012 .remark}
*Remark 1.48.B.6* (Comparison to Padmanabhan's holographic
equipartition and emergent-space-through-expansion). Padmanabhan
2012 (arXiv:1206.4916, 2012) proposed that the expansion of
cosmic space is driven by the universe's tendency toward
holographic equipartition: the difference between horizon degrees
of freedom $N_{\text{sur}} = A/\ell_P^2$ and bulk degrees of
freedom $N_{\text{bulk}}$ drives the volume expansion rate
$dV/dt \propto (N_{\text{sur}} - N_{\text{bulk}})$, with the
universe reaching de Sitter equilibrium at
$N_{\text{sur}} = N_{\text{bulk}}$ (maximum horizon entropy).
Padmanabhan's Hubble-volume growth generates Bekenstein--Hawking
entropy $S_{BH} \propto A_{\text{Hubble}}$ monotonically toward
the de Sitter limit.

The McGucken position: Padmanabhan's cosmological horizon is a
Hubble-scale (10²⁶ m) McGucken Sphere; the holographic equipartition
principle is the cosmological-scale reading of the Sphere-mode-
counting content of Theorem 1.48.B Tier 1. Padmanabhan correctly
identified the horizon-area-drives-entropy structure at cosmological
scale but did not extend it to the per-event scale. The McGucken
framework generalizes: *every* event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ sources a
Sphere with its own horizon-mode content growing quadratically in
parameter time. The universe's total entropy is the aggregated
Sphere-mode content across the Sphere chain, not the single-horizon
Hubble content. Padmanabhan's law of emergence is the coarse-grained
cosmological signature of the per-event Sphere-expansion mechanism
that Theorem 1.48.B makes explicit.
:::

::: {#rmk:resolution-broadbridge-2020 .remark}
*Remark 1.48.B.7* (Resolution of the Broadbridge et al. hyperbolic-
Shannon zero-entropy-production result). Broadbridge, Kolesnik,
Leonenko, Olenko, and Omari (2020, *Entropy* 22(2), 217,
arXiv:1912.08378) established that for hyperbolic diffusion with
finite propagation speed $c$, the Shannon entropy density $s = -q^* \ln q^*$
satisfies
$$s_t + \frac{D}{c^2}\, s_{tt} = D\,\frac{q_x^{*2} - q_t^{*2}/c^2}{q^*}$$
(their Eq. 8.1). In the uni-directional limit — solutions where
the wavefront propagates at a single velocity $\pm c$ with
$q_t^* = \pm c\, q_x^*$ — the **entropy production source term
on the right-hand side vanishes identically**. Under this vanishing,
$s$ satisfies a homogeneous hyperbolic equation and, integrated
over space, the total Shannon entropy is conserved. Broadbridge et
al. interpret this as "zero entropy production" in the thermodynamic
sense. Under a naive reading, this appears to contradict
Theorem 1.48.B: if the McGucken Sphere is a uni-directional
wavefront at velocity $c$, its Shannon entropy production should
be zero.

The resolution is: **Broadbridge et al.'s Shannon
entropy and Theorem 1.48.B's Shannon entropy are entropies of
different objects.** Broadbridge et al.'s Shannon entropy is on the
*wave-amplitude distribution* $q^*(x, t)$ propagating along the
characteristic direction — the entropy is $-\int q^* \ln q^*\, dx$
of the amplitude density at each parameter time. For a wave
propagating uni-directionally at $+c$, the amplitude density
translates rigidly at velocity $c$; its entropy is
translation-invariant and therefore stationary in $t$. This is
Broadbridge's result and it is correct on its own terms.

Theorem 1.48.B's Shannon entropy is on the *Planck-area
mode-count distribution* on the expanding 2-sphere surface at
parameter time $t$. The mode count $N(t) = A(t)/\ell_P^2$ grows
quadratically because the *surface area* $A(t) = 4\pi c^2 (t-t_p)^2$
grows quadratically, not because the wave amplitude spreads. The
McGucken entropy is the entropy of the **available degrees of
freedom** on the wavefront's surface, not the entropy of the
amplitude distribution moving through space.

The two entropies are distinct in the same way that
Bekenstein--Hawking entropy $A/(4\ell_P^2)$ (horizon-area mode count)
is distinct from the Shannon entropy of a wave packet's amplitude
density. Broadbridge et al.'s result correctly says the latter is
translation-invariant for uni-directional waves; Theorem 1.48.B
correctly says the former grows quadratically with the expanding
wavefront's surface area. Both are correct; they compute different
quantities. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's entropy content — the
mode-count on the expanding Sphere — is compatible with, not
contradictory to, Broadbridge et al.'s zero-production result on
the amplitude-density Shannon entropy.

**Note.** The Broadbridge et al. finding is important
supporting evidence for the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework: it shows that in the
uni-directional wave-propagation limit *without* Sphere-area-based
mode-count content, Shannon entropy is exactly conserved. The
Sphere-area-based mode count is therefore the central feature
that generates entropy production; without it, uni-directional
propagation gives zero entropy production. This aligns with the
McGucken position that entropy production is a per-event
Sphere-area-growth phenomenon, not a wave-propagation phenomenon
in the amplitude-density sense.
:::

::: {#rmk:comparison-tozzi-peters-2019 .remark}
*Remark 1.48.B.8* (Comparison to Tozzi--Peters cosmic expansion →
entropy). Tozzi and Peters 2019 (Tozzi, A., Peters, J. F. *Entropy* 21(9), 924, 2019)
correlate cosmic expansion with the second law via the Bekenstein
bound: for a local observer enclosed in a cosmological comoving
horizon, the information density (bits per comoving volume unit)
decreases with time while thermodynamic entropy inside the horizon
increases. The mechanism is the Bekenstein bound applied to the
comoving-horizon sphere as an upper limit on horizon entropy, with
cosmic expansion increasing the horizon radius and hence the
Bekenstein-bound value.

The McGucken position: Tozzi and Peters correctly identify cosmic
expansion → increasing entropy via a spherical-region-plus-bound
mechanism. Their construction uses the Bekenstein bound at
cosmological horizon scale (∼10²⁶ m). Theorem 1.48.B generalizes
to per-event scale via the Sphere-at-every-event postulate: every
event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ has its own expanding Sphere with its own
Bekenstein-bound-compatible entropy growth. Tozzi--Peters's cosmic-
expansion argument is the coarse-grained cosmological signature of
the per-event Sphere-expansion mechanism.

**Note.** Tozzi--Peters state: *"here we start from
information, and reach the entropy, and not vice versa as generally
assumed."* This inverts the orthodox direction (which usually
derives information from entropy). The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework goes one
step further: both information (Shannon entropy of mode-count
distribution) and thermodynamic entropy
(Boltzmann--Gibbs / Bekenstein--Hawking / von Neumann) are five
readings of the *same* quantity — the McGucken-Sphere Haar entropy
(Remark [1.48.B.2](#rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity"}). Neither information
nor entropy is "prior" to the other; both descend from the
foundational $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ via the per-event Sphere.
:::

::: {#rmk:novel-content-of-theorem-1-48-B .remark}
*Remark 1.48.B.9* (Novel content of Theorem 1.48.B relative to the
prior-work catalog). Table
[1.48.B.A](#tbl:orthodox-comparison-catalog){reference-type="ref"
reference="tbl:orthodox-comparison-catalog"} catalogs 12 prior
works that relate expanding spherical elements to entropy at
various scales. Theorem 1.48.B supplies content that none of them
explicitly derives:

*(i) **Per-event scale, not cosmological or black-hole scale.**
Bekenstein--Hawking is at black-hole-horizon scale;
Padmanabhan/Bousso/Bousso--Engelhardt/Tozzi--Peters are at
cosmological-horizon scale. Theorem 1.48.B is at per-event scale:
every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ sources its own McGucken Sphere
with its own monotonically growing surface area. At the
matter-tier order of magnitude, the Compton frequency
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ gives $\sim 10^{20}$ Hz per electron and
$\sim 10^{23}$ Hz per nucleon; combined with ordinary matter
density $\sim 10^{23}$ nucleons/cm³, the Compton-coupling event
rate per unit volume is at the order of
$\sim 10^{43}\text{--}10^{46}$ events/sec/cm³ — some 20 orders
of magnitude denser than the single Hubble-horizon that
Padmanabhan/Bousso--Engelhardt/Tozzi--Peters describe.*

*(ii) **Expanding light-sheets, not contracting.** Bousso's
covariant entropy bound explicitly covers only non-expanding null
surfaces. Theorem 1.48.B covers the complementary expanding null
family, supplying entropy-production-from-below where Bousso
supplies entropy-bound-from-above.*

*(iii) **Huygens' Principle as generation mechanism.** No orthodox
prior work identifies Huygens' Principle as the mechanism of
per-event Sphere generation and hence of entropy production.
Theorem 1.48.B Step 1 makes this identification explicit via
McGucken, E. (April 15, 2026) *A Derivation of Feynman's Path Integral from the McGucken Principle*, §3 Lemma 3.1; elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/04/15/.*

*(iv) **Five-entropy convergence via Sphere-Haar identification.**
No orthodox prior work identifies Shannon, Boltzmann--Gibbs,
von Neumann, Bekenstein--Hawking, and Wiener entropies as five
readings of one Sphere-Haar quantity. The McGucken Entropy Identity
(Remark [1.48.B.2](#rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:mcgucken-entropy-identity"}) supplies this unification.*

*(v) **Three-tier convergence from a single upstream principle.**
Some orthodox works partially assemble two of the three tiers:
Jacobson 2015 [*Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 201101; arXiv:1505.04753]
relates geometric-tier Bekenstein--Hawking area entropy to
nonlocality-tier vacuum entanglement entropy on a spherical geodesic
ball, without a matter-diffusion tier. Verlinde 2010
(*JHEP* 04:029) and Padmanabhan 2010 (*Rept. Prog. Phys.* 73,
046901) partially link geometric-tier horizon entropy to
matter-tier degrees of freedom, without an independent
nonlocality tier. What no orthodox prior work does is derive
all three tiers from a **single upstream principle**
via a shared four-step chain. Theorem 1.48.B does this: the
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = +ic$ McGucken Principle at every event
generates the per-event McGucken Sphere via Huygens' Principle,
whose area growth simultaneously supports all three tier-level
entropy productions (geometric, matter-diffusion, nonlocality)
via the shared four-step chain. This is the novel content: the
single-upstream-principle assembly, not the tier-level content
individually.*

The novel content is the per-event Sphere-expansion-→-Shannon-entropy
mechanism at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$, with Huygens' Principle
as the generation mechanism and three-tier convergence as the
reason five orthodox entropies agree.
:::

#### Theorem 16.7: Dissolution of the orthodox measurement problem {#sec:measurement-problem-dissolution}

The orthodox measurement problem has been the central foundational
impasse of physics for nearly a century. The standard statement
(Bohr--Heisenberg 1927, von Neumann 1932, Wigner 1961, Bell 1990,
Schlosshauer 2007 [@Schlosshauer2007Decoherence]): the Schrödinger
equation propagates $\psi$ unitarily, but laboratory measurements
produce definite outcomes; what dynamics, mechanism, or
interpretation bridges the unitary evolution and the
definite-outcome reality? Every orthodox interpretation of quantum
mechanics is an attempt to answer this question (Copenhagen,
Many-Worlds, GRW, de Broglie--Bohm, QBism, consistent histories,
relational QM, decoherence-based readings), and Bell 1990
[@Bell1990Against] called the measurement problem "the greatest
unsolved mystery in modern physics."

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's diagnosis is that the question
is malformed. The positive content provides a dissolution as a
theorem.

::: {#thm:measurement-problem-dissolution .theorem}
**Theorem 1.49** (Dissolution of the orthodox measurement problem;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 16.7). *The orthodox measurement problem
— "how does the unitary evolution of $|\psi\rangle$ produce
definite measurement outcomes?" — is malformed.
Specifically:*

*(i) Measurement events are physical events in spacetime: head-on
McGucken Sphere collisions at $+ic$-oriented detection events
(Theorem [11.5](#thm:born-as-collision){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-as-collision"}).*

*(ii) These events are Geometric Channel content; they are not
contained in the Algebraic Channel's apparatus (Hilbert space,
wavefunction, operator algebra, unitary evolution, Born rule
equation, projection operators — none of which is a physical event
in spacetime).*

*(iii) The orthodox measurement question asks Algebraic Channel's
apparatus to produce content (definite measurement events in
spacetime) that Algebraic Channel does not contain. Asking "how
does $\psi$'s unitary evolution produce a definite outcome" is
analogous to asking "how does an actuarial table
produce a death" — the table does not produce deaths; people die
in the physical world; the table records the statistics.*

*(iv) The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies the positive Geometric
Channel mechanism: the Born rule probability density
$|\psi(q)|^2$ is the Haar-measure-weighted rate of head-on Sphere
collisions at the $+ic$-oriented detection event $q$, with the
exponent $2$ overdetermined by three independent routes (rank-2
sesquilinear metric pairing, two-Sphere collision rate, PT-symmetry
through the source event). Definite outcomes are produced at every
measurement event by the Sphere-collision mechanism in the
Geometric Channel; The Algebraic Channel reports the statistics.*

*(v) Therefore the orthodox measurement problem dissolves: the
question presupposes Algebraic Channel is the locus of
measurement-event production, when in fact Geometric Channel is
the locus and Algebraic Channel is the statistical encoding. The
dissolution is complete because Geometric Channel has
a positive physical mechanism (Sphere collision with Haar measure), which locates the outcome in a physical event.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). We establish each step.

**Step 1 (Category identification).** The two channels operate on
categorically distinct content. The Geometric Channel's content
$\mathcal{B}$ is physical-spatiotemporal: $+ic$-oriented McGucken
Spheres at every spacetime event, with the Sphere collisions, the
cosmological expansion, the arrows of time, the matter dominance as
physical entries in the universe. The Algebraic Channel's content
$\mathcal{A}$ is calculational-statistical: Hilbert spaces,
operator algebras, wavefunctions, projection operators, unitary
one-parameter groups, the Born rule equation. The categorical
distinction is that Geometric Channel's content sits in spacetime
at events (definite location, definite time, definite
physical-causal interactions with other content), while Algebraic
Channel's content does not (the Hilbert space has no spatiotemporal
location; the wavefunction is a function on configuration space,
not an event at a spacetime point; the operator algebra is a set of
mathematical relations, not a set of physical processes).

**Step 2 (Definite outcomes are Geometric Channel events).** Each
laboratory measurement event is a physical event in spacetime: at
the moment of detection, a single click occurs at a single detector
at a single time. The click is a $+ic$-oriented spacetime event $q$
at which the source's forward Sphere $\psi$ and the apparatus's
conjugate Sphere $\psi^*$ meet head-on
(Theorem [11.5](#thm:born-as-collision){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-as-collision"}). The conjugate branch is not
created by the apparatus: by
Lemma [6.6A](#lem:reception-reading){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reception-reading"} a convergent family of wavefronts
arrives at every event of $M_{G}$, and C4 forbids privileging
instrumented events over any others. What the apparatus supplies is
localisation --- a departure from the isotropic arrival distribution of
Theorem [6.6B](#thm:convergent-flux-isotropy){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:convergent-flux-isotropy"}, which is what converts the
ever-present coincidence into a registration. The cancellation of
$x_4$-momenta at the collision redeposits the cancelled
$x_4$-momenergy as 3-spatial momenergy by four-momentum
conservation; both particles localize at the collision event. The
definite outcome is the Geometric Channel physical event itself —
no further mechanism is required to "produce" a definite outcome
because the Sphere collision IS the definite outcome.

**Step 3 (Algebraic Channel reports the statistics).** The Born
rule equation $P(q) = |\psi(q)|^2$ is the Haar-measure-weighted
rate of head-on Sphere collisions at the $+ic$-oriented detection
event $q$. The exponent $2$ is overdetermined by three independent
routes (rank-2 sesquilinear metric pairing of
Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}, two-Sphere collision rate of
Theorem [11.5](#thm:born-as-collision){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-as-collision"}, PT-symmetry through the source
event). The Born rule is therefore a statement *about*
Sphere-collision rates at $+ic$-oriented detection events; it is
not itself a Sphere-collision mechanism.

**Step 4 (The orthodox question's malformation).** The orthodox
measurement problem asks Algebraic Channel's apparatus (statistical
encoding) to produce Geometric Channel content (definite spacetime
events). By
Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}, the inverse projection $\Pi_B$
does not exist; there is no constructive functor from Algebraic
Channel to Geometric Channel. The Algebraic Channel content
contains no $+ic$-oriented spacetime events as such; it contains
only statistical encodings of those events. The orthodox question
asks for content that Algebraic Channel does not have, which is why
the question has been answered by every orthodox interpretation
through a different *ad hoc* addition (Copenhagen's primitive
measurement category, MWI's branching, GRW's stochastic non-unitary
term, Bohm's hidden trajectories, QBism's epistemic refusal).

**Step 5 (The framework's positive resolution).** The framework
supplies the Geometric Channel mechanism (Sphere collision with
Haar measure) that produces definite outcomes at every measurement
event. The Algebraic Channel apparatus is then correctly understood
as the statistical encoding of those events, with the Born rule
equation reporting the statistics of the collisions. No additional
mechanism, hidden variable, branching, or stochastic term is
required. The mystery dissolves because the locus of
definite-outcome production is correctly identified as the
Geometric Channel, with the Algebraic Channel apparatus serving its
proper role of statistical bookkeeping. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:collapse-as-bayesian-bookkeeping .remark}
*Remark 1.49.A* (The collapse postulate as Bayesian-update
bookkeeping). The "collapse postulate" of orthodox quantum mechanics
— the abrupt non-unitary transition
$|\psi\rangle \to |n\rangle$ upon measurement of outcome $n$ —
is, in the framework's reading, *not a physical process needing a
physical mechanism*. It is the algebraic bookkeeping of updating the
Algebraic Channel statistical encoding when a Geometric Channel
physical event has occurred. The analog: an actuarial
table maintained by an insurance actuary records probability
distributions over outcomes (death rates by age, etc.); each
individual death is a physical event in the world; when a death is
reported, the actuary updates the table to reflect the new
information. The update is *epistemic* — the table's content now
reflects which events have occurred. The update is *not physical* —
nothing happens in the world when the actuary updates the table;
the death happened in the world, and the table records it. The
collapse postulate has the same status:
$|\psi\rangle$ is the Algebraic Channel statistical encoding of
the source's Sphere collision distribution; the head-on Sphere
collision at $q$ is the Geometric Channel physical event; the
post-measurement update to $|n\rangle$ is the Algebraic Channel
encoding accommodating new information about which Geometric
Channel event has occurred.

This dissolves the collapse-mechanism question. The orthodox
programme has searched for a physical mechanism for collapse — a
non-unitary term in the Schrödinger equation (GRW), a gravity-induced
reduction (Penrose), a consciousness-induced collapse (Wigner), a
branch-selection mechanism (MWI's preferred basis). All such
searches presuppose that collapse is a physical process needing a
physical mechanism. The framework's reading: collapse is not a
physical process at all — it is the algebraic bookkeeping of
updating the Algebraic Channel statistical encoding when a
Geometric Channel event has been registered. No physical collapse
mechanism exists or is needed; the only physical event is the
Geometric Channel Sphere collision at $q$, and the post-collision
Algebraic Channel update is the statistical-encoding accommodation
of that event's having occurred.
:::

#### Historical-constructive independence versus physical foundationality: the algebraic shadow and what Heisenberg actually built in 1925 {#sec:algebraic-shadow-heisenberg-1925}

The three projection-theorem core results above
(Theorems [1.40](#thm:geometric-channel-foundational-self-sufficiency){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:geometric-channel-foundational-self-sufficiency"},
[1.41](#thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind"},
[1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}) yield a precise
statement of the relation between Geometric and Algebraic Channels
that resolves an interpretive question the parallel-siblings framing
left ambiguous: **Historically, the Algebraic Channel is independently
constructible; physically, the Geometric Channel is foundational.**
Both claims hold simultaneously, because they answer two different
questions. The present section makes this distinction essential and identifies, with full precision, what Heisenberg
actually built in 1925.

::: {#prop:heisenberg-built-T-invariant-shadow .proposition}
**Proposition 1.49.B** (Historical-constructive independence vs.
physical foundationality of the dual-channel architecture;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] §16.16). *Two distinct questions
admit two distinct answers about the relation between
the Geometric and Algebraic Channels:*

*(i) **Historical-constructive question.** Was the Algebraic Channel
built without the Geometric Channel as input in the documented
history of physics? **Yes.** Heisenberg's matrix mechanics
[@Heisenberg1925Umdeutung] was derived from atomic spectroscopic
data, the Ritz combination principle for spectral lines, and the
correspondence principle that classical phase-space orbits become
matrix-element transitions in the quantum regime. No McGucken Sphere
appeared in the construction. Born and Jordan
[@BornJordan1925ZurQuantenmechanik] formalized the matrix mechanics
into the operator-algebraic apparatus; Dirac
[@Dirac1925Fundamental] produced an independent operator-algebraic
formulation with the Poisson-bracket-to-commutator correspondence
rule; Schrödinger [@Schrodinger1926Quantisierung] produced the
wave-mechanical formulation from de Broglie's matter waves; Stone
[@Stone1932Linear] proved the theorem on one-parameter unitary
groups from pure functional analysis; von Neumann
[@vonNeumann1932] axiomatized the Hilbert-space framework with the
spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators; Wigner
[@Wigner1939Unitary] classified the unitary irreducible
representations of the Poincaré group; Bargmann
[@Bargmann1957] completed the classification machinery; Wightman
[@Wightman1956Quantum] axiomatized QFT with the five sign-blind
axioms plus the imported Spectrum Condition. The
historical-constructive trajectory from atomic spectra to the
canonical commutator to the Wightman axioms is documented,
self-sufficient, and independent of the McGucken Sphere as primitive
input. To claim otherwise would falsify the historical record.*

*(ii) **Physical-question.** Does the Algebraic
Channel's content include the $+ic$ orientation of the physical
universe? **No.** By
Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}, the $+ic$ orientation is the
content that the projection $\Pi_A$ projects away. The Algebraic
Channel is sign-blind on $+ic$ by
Theorem [1.41](#thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind"}; its algebraic
apparatus is invariant under the $+ic \leftrightarrow -ic$
involution; its content does not include the McGucken Sphere as a
geometric primitive; its content does not include any of the
$T$-anti-invariant entries of the asymmetric census
(cosmological expansion direction, strict Second Law, matter
dominance, radiative arrow with retarded Green's functions,
quantum-measurement arrow with Wick rotation in the convergent
direction, decoherence monotonicity, black-hole horizon growth,
CMB redshift, etc.). The physical content of the universe — the
Sphere expanding outward at every event with its $+ic$ orientation
— is the Geometric Channel's content and is not contained in the
Algebraic Channel.*

*The two answers coexist because they refer to two distinct relations. Question (i) asks about **constructive
derivability** between the apparatuses; Question (ii) asks about
**content containment** between the channels. The Algebraic Channel
is constructively independent of the Geometric Channel (one can
build it without invoking the Sphere) and content-deficient with
respect to the Geometric Channel (its content is $\Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$,
the $T$-invariant subset of the Geometric Channel's content).
Constructive independence and content deficiency are different
relations; both statements can hold simultaneously without
contradiction.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.*

*(i) Constructive independence (1925--1957 historical record).* The
documented historical record establishes the constructive independence
directly. Heisenberg's 1925 derivation of matrix mechanics from
spectroscopic data is the canonical case: the Ritz combination
principle for spectral lines, the correspondence principle between
classical phase-space orbits and quantum matrix-element transitions,
and Bohr's old-quantum-theory orbital quantization are the constructive
inputs. The McGucken Sphere is not invoked; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ is not invoked; the geometric content of
$x_4$-perpendicularity is not invoked. The Born--Jordan 1925
formalization, Dirac 1925 operator-algebraic re-derivation, Schrödinger
1926 wave-mechanical formulation, von Neumann 1932 Hilbert-space
axiomatization, Wigner 1939 Poincaré-representation classification,
Bargmann 1957 supercharge correction, and Wightman 1956 QFT
axiomatization are each independently completable without recourse to
Geometric Channel primitives. The historical record is documentation
that the constructive independence is real.

*(ii) Content deficiency (projection-theorem core).* By
Theorem [1.41](#thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind"}, every step of the
Algebraic Channel's apparatus is sign-blind on the $+ic$ orientation:
the Born rule equation, the Schrödinger equation, the canonical
commutator, the Wightman axioms, the spectral theorem, Stone's
theorem, the Lorentz-group unitary representations — all are
$T$-invariant algebraic content. By
Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}, the inverse projection $\Pi_B$
does not exist: no construction in the Algebraic Channel reaches the
$T$-anti-invariant content of physical reality. Hence the
Algebraic Channel's content equals $\Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$, which is
the $T$-invariant subset of the Geometric Channel's content. The
content asymmetry is the projection-theoretic precision of the
foundational asymmetry. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:shadow-framing .remark}
*Remark 1.49.B.1* (The shadow framing). A *shadow* is a real but
content-incomplete projection of a deeper object. The shadow of a
three-dimensional figure on a two-dimensional plane is a genuine
mathematical object — internally consistent, measurable, related to
the source figure by a precise projection — but lacks the depth
content of the source. The relation between the Geometric Channel
and the Algebraic Channel has the same form. The
Algebraic Channel is the *$T$-invariant algebraic shadow* of the
McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = +ic$. The shadow is genuine
(the algebra is internally consistent, the canonical commutator
holds, Stone's theorem is provable, the Lorentz group acts
unitarily), independently constructible (the historical trajectory
established this), and empirically anchored to every $T$-invariant
measurement (atomic spectra, electron $g{-}2$, Casimir effects,
scattering cross-sections at the equation level). But the shadow
lacks the $+ic$ orientation content that distinguishes the source:
under the projection $\Pi_A$, the orientation is projected away and
only the algebra survives.
:::

::: {#rmk:what-heisenberg-built-in-1925 .remark}
*Remark 1.49.B.2* (What Heisenberg actually built in 1925). The
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's identification of what Heisenberg
constructed: **Heisenberg built the $T$-invariant algebraic shadow
of the principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = +ic$ from spectroscopic data,
without knowing it was a shadow.** The shadow is a real mathematical
object, and Heisenberg's derivation of it from atomic spectra is
correct as a mathematical construction. What Heisenberg did *not*
identify — because the framework's principle was not
available in 1925 — is that his algebraic apparatus is the
$T$-invariant projection of a deeper geometric content. The
framework identifies what he reached (the shadow) and why it has the
form it has (sign-blind on $+ic$, interior-$i$ position
forced by Hermitian-operator requirements, empirically incomplete in
the categories of physical content where $T$-anti-invariance is
essential). The 1925 derivation is correct mathematics; the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies the interpretation of what
it is mathematics *of*.
:::

::: {#rmk:three-consequences .remark}
*Remark 1.49.B.3* (Three consequences).

*First*, the framework does not claim Heisenberg was wrong, nor that
1925 matrix mechanics requires revision. The shadow is what it is.
The Algebraic Channel is constructively independent and internally
consistent. The framework adds a reading: the shadow is
the $T$-invariant projection of a deeper principle, and the deeper
principle is what the physical universe actually runs on.

*Second*, the framework's claim on the Geometric Channel's
status is *physical*, not *constructive*. The
constructive claim that one cannot build the algebra without first
having the principle is false (history disproves it); the framework
does not make this claim. The physical claim that the
$+ic$-oriented McGucken Sphere expansion at every event is the
foundational physical fact of the universe — that the orientation is
real, that the strict Second Law is forced
(Theorem [1.48](#thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing"}), that the cosmological
expansion direction is, that the matter-dominance
asymmetry is principle-derived — is the claim the framework makes.
This is a claim about *what the universe is*, not about *what can be
constructed from what*.

*Third*, the constructive independence of the Algebraic Channel is a
strength of the framework, not a weakness. The historical-constructive
trajectory from Heisenberg to Wightman demonstrates that the algebraic
shadow is buildable from $T$-invariant empirical content
(spectroscopy, scattering, group representations) without requiring
the framework's principle as primitive input. This is
exactly what the projection theorem predicts: $T$-invariant content
is reachable through the algebraic apparatus alone because
$T$-invariant content is what survives $\Pi_A$. If the algebraic
shadow had required the McGucken Sphere as primitive input, the
framework would be in tension with the 1925--1957 historical record;
instead, the framework's reading is consistent with that
record and supplies the interpretive content (the shadow's relation
to the source) that the historical-constructive derivations did not.
:::

::: {#rmk:the-slogan .remark}
*Remark 1.49.B.4* (The slogan). Historically, the Algebraic Channel
is independently constructible; physically, the Geometric Channel is
foundational. The Algebraic Channel is the algebra one can derive
from spectroscopic data without invoking a Sphere. The Geometric
Channel is the geometric-physical content of the universe with its
$+ic$ orientation. The relationship between them is that the
Algebraic Channel is the time-reversal-symmetric image of the
Geometric Channel under $\Pi_A$ — what Heisenberg built in 1925
was the $T$-invariant shadow of the principle
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = +ic$ without identifying it as such. The shadow
is genuine and self-sufficient as a mathematical object; the
principle is what the universe runs on. Both at once.
:::

#### The orthodox foundational confusion: six programs treating the algebraic shadow as foundational physical content {#sec:orthodox-foundational-confusion}

The shadow-versus-source distinction of
§[\[sec:algebraic-shadow-heisenberg-1925\]](#sec:algebraic-shadow-heisenberg-1925){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:algebraic-shadow-heisenberg-1925"} has a consequence for the interpretation of contemporary unification
programs in theoretical physics. Orthodox foundational physics has,
over the past fifty years, increasingly treated the algebraic shadow
as the physical content rather than as the $T$-invariant
projection of a deeper geometric reality. The error is the
systematic conflation of $\Pi_A(\text{physical reality})$ with
physical reality itself. The present section diagnoses the error
program by program. In each case the framework identifies the
Algebraic Channel content being treated as foundational, the
Geometric Channel content being projected away or ignored, the
diagnosis, and the observational status.

**(O1) The universal wavefunction $|\Psi\rangle$** (Everett 1957
[@Everett1957Relative], DeWitt 1973 [@DeWitt1973ManyWorlds],
Wallace 2012 [@Wallace2012Emergent]).

*Algebraic Channel content treated as foundational.* The universal
wavefunction $|\Psi(t)\rangle$ is taken as the complete physical
state of the universe, evolving unitarily under Schrödinger's
equation: $i\hbar\,\partial_t |\Psi\rangle = \hat{H}|\Psi\rangle$.
All physical content reduces to inner products and operator
expectation values on the universal Hilbert space. Branches of
$|\Psi\rangle$ proliferate via decoherence, with each branch
representing a self-consistent quasi-classical history.

*Geometric Channel content projected away.* The unitary evolution
$U(t) = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}$ is $T$-invariant
(Theorem [1.41](#thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind"}). The universal
wavefunction apparatus contains no $+ic$ orientation; both forward
and backward branchings are formally admissible. The physical fact
that decoherence is monotonic in the future direction, that
branch-splitting produces irreversible records, that measurement
events happen forward in time at the head-on Sphere collision
(Theorem [11.5](#thm:born-as-collision){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-as-collision"}) — all this is Geometric Channel
content not present in the unitary universal wavefunction.

*Diagnosis.* The universal wavefunction is a computation
in $\Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$. The orientation that picks out the forward
branching direction is imported tacitly through the Past Hypothesis
(Albert 2000 [@Albert2000Time], Loewer 2007
[@Loewer2007CounterfactualsCausalDecisionTheory]) or smuggled in via
the decoherence-basis choice, with neither move being a derivation
from the universal-wavefunction apparatus itself. The Born rule
emerges from the universal wavefunction only through additional
postulates (the branch-counting argument of Deutsch 1999
[@Deutsch1999Decision] and Wallace 2012
[@Wallace2012Emergent], or the envariance argument of Zurek 2005
[@Zurek2005Envariance]), each importing Geometric Channel content as
auxiliary input.

*Observational status.* The universal-wavefunction framework produces
no observational predictions distinguishing it from "ordinary"
quantum mechanics applied to subsystems — the multiverse branches
are by construction inaccessible to observation. The framework is
internally consistent as $\Pi_A$-content computation; it produces
zero falsifiable predictions for the asymmetric universe.

**(O2) AdS/CFT bulk-boundary duality** (Maldacena 1997
[@Maldacena1997AdSCFT], Witten 1998 [@Witten1998AntiDeSitter],
Gubser--Klebanov--Polyakov 1998
[@GubserKlebanovPolyakov1998Gauge]).

*Algebraic Channel content treated as foundational.* A bulk
gravitational theory on $(d{+}1)$-dimensional anti-de Sitter spacetime
is conjectured to be dual to a conformal field theory on the
$d$-dimensional boundary, with the duality stated at the level of
generating functionals:
$Z_\text{bulk}[\phi_0] = Z_\text{CFT}[\phi_0]$, where $\phi_0$
is a boundary value of a bulk field. The duality is
algebraic-equational and operates entirely on $T$-invariant content.

*Geometric Channel content projected away.* The physical universe is
not AdS but de Sitter — the cosmological expansion satisfies
$H_0 > 0$ with $\Lambda > 0$ in Einstein's field equations, opposite
in sign to the AdS curvature. The cosmological expansion direction
$H_0 > 0$ is asymmetric Geometric Channel content not derivable from
the algebraic apparatus. AdS/CFT works in the unphysical AdS regime
where the cosmological constant is negative and the spacetime
contracts asymptotically; the physical regime where $H_0 > 0$ has
resisted analogous formulation for the entire history of the
conjecture (1997--present).

*Diagnosis.* AdS/CFT is an exact computation of
$\Pi_A(\mathcal{B}_\text{AdS})$ — the algebraic shadow of a
hypothetical AdS Geometric Channel content — and not a computation
of $\Pi_A(\mathcal{B}_\text{de Sitter})$, the shadow of the
universe's actual Geometric Channel content. The duality's
exactness in the AdS regime reflects its operation within the
Algebraic Channel where both sides of the duality are $T$-invariant
by construction; the difficulty of extending to de Sitter reflects
the absence of $\Pi_B$
(Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}): one cannot reverse-engineer
the cosmological orientation from algebraic-shadow content.

*Observational status.* The duality has produced no observational
predictions for the de Sitter universe we inhabit. A multi-decade
program has produced a large body of internally consistent
mathematical structure with no contact with cosmological
observation.

**(O3) ER=EPR** (Maldacena--Susskind 2013 [@MaldacenaSusskind2013]).

*Algebraic Channel content treated as foundational.* An entangled
Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen (EPR) pair is conjectured to be
geometrically equivalent to a non-traversable Einstein--Rosen (ER)

sign-blind (the EPR state is $T$-symmetric up to overall phase), and
the wormhole geometry is the algebraic content of a metric tensor
that is itself $T$-invariant as a Lorentzian-metric structure.

*Geometric Channel content projected away.* The physical instantiation

$t_0$ (Geometric Channel: $+ic$-oriented source-event Sphere) and
detection events at $t > t_0$ (Geometric Channel: head-on Sphere
collisions in the future direction at each detection apparatus). The
asymmetric direction of entanglement creation followed by
spacelike-separated measurements is Geometric Channel content not
present in the ER=EPR algebraic identification.

*Diagnosis.* ER=EPR identifies two pieces of $T$-invariant
algebraic content with each other. The identification is internally
consistent but does not extend to the Geometric Channel content of
how entanglement is produced and how measurements collapse the joint
state. The identification operates at the level of
$|\Psi\rangle$-content (universal wavefunction with entanglement)
and metric-content (Lorentzian wormhole), both of which sit in
$\Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$. The framework's reading: ER=EPR is a
$\Pi_A$-internal identification, neither falsified nor confirmed by

Geometric Channel content enters the identification.

*Observational status.* The conjecture has produced no falsifiable
observational predictions for the asymmetric universe.

**(O4) The Page curve and the "island" programme** (Page 1993
[@Page1993InformationBlackHole]; Penington 2019
[@Penington2019Entanglement];
Almheiri--Engelhardt--Marolf--Maxfield 2019
[@AlmheiriEngelhardtMarolfMaxfield2019];
Penington--Shenker--Stanford--Yang 2019
[@PeningtonShenkerStanfordYang2019]).

#### Theorem 1.50: The Imaginary-Unit-Selects-Nonlocality Theorem {#sec:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality}

::: {#thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality .theorem}
**Theorem 1.50** (Imaginary-Unit-Selects-Nonlocality;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 17.1). *Given a putative principle of the form "the fourth dimension expands at velocity $c$,"
there are two distinct readings of the principle
corresponding to two choices of the algebraic character of the
fourth-dimensional coordinate:*

*Reading (I), Euclidean-local: $x_4 \in \mathbb{R}$ is a fourth
spatial dimension; $dx_4/dt = c$ with $c$ real; the wavefront from
event $p$ is the 3-sphere $S^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^4$ of Euclidean
radius $R(t) = c(t - t_p)$ centered at the spacetime position of
$p$.*

*Reading (II), Lorentzian-nonlocal: $x_4 = ict$ with $i^2 = -1$;
$dx_4/dt = ic$; the wavefront from event $p$ is the null
hypersurface $\Sigma^+(p) \subset M_{1,3}$ at apex $p$, with
every point $q \in \Sigma^+(p)$ satisfying $ds^2(p, q) = 0$ in the
Lorentzian metric.*

*The imaginary unit $i$ in $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ is what selects
(II) over (I). Without the $i$, reading (I) holds, and the wavefront
preserves normal Euclidean locality (no nonlocal correlations across
the wavefront, no Lorentzian invariance, no null cones, no path to
the empirical content of QM, GR, or thermodynamics). With the $i$,
reading (II) holds, and the wavefront is null with $ds^2 = 0$
between apex and every wavefront point (Sphere nonlocality content
from which QM, GR, and thermodynamics descend as forced theorems via
the cumulative chain of theorems).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (five-step discrimination between readings (I)
and (II)).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**Step 1: Reading (I), Euclidean-local — consequences.**
Suppose $x_4 \in \mathbb{R}$ is a fourth real spatial dimension and
$dx_4/dt = c$ with $c$ real-positive. Then $x_4 = ct$ (integrated
form), and the four-dimensional position of event $p$ is
$(\mathbf{x}_p, x_4(t_p)) = (\mathbf{x}_p, c t_p) \in \mathbb{R}^4$.
The wavefront from $p$ at parameter time $t$ is the set
$$\mathcal{W}^{(\mathrm{I})}_p(t) = \{(\mathbf{x}_q, x_4(t)) \in \mathbb{R}^4 : |\mathbf{x}_q - \mathbf{x}_p|^2 + (x_4(t) - x_4(t_p))^2 = (ct)^2_\mathrm{rel}\},$$
i.e., the 3-sphere $S^3$ of Euclidean radius $c(t - t_p)$ centered at
the four-dimensional position of $p$, where the Euclidean radius is
defined under the Euclidean metric on $\mathbb{R}^4$:
$ds^2_\mathrm{Eucl} = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2$. Two points
$q, q' \in \mathcal{W}^{(\mathrm{I})}_p(t)$ on the wavefront at
parameter time $t$ are at *positive* Euclidean distance from each
other, with equality only when $q = q'$. The wavefront preserves
Euclidean locality.

**Step 2: Reading (II), Lorentzian-nonlocal — consequences.** Suppose $x_4 = ict$ with $i^2 = -1$. Then
$(dx_4)^2 = (ic\,dt)^2 = -c^2 dt^2$. The metric on $M_{1,3}$ is
$ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + |d\mathbf{x}|^2$ with Lorentzian signature
$(-, +, +, +)$. The wavefront from event $p$ is the null hypersurface
$\Sigma^+(p) = \{q \in M_{1,3} : ds^2(p, q) = 0,\ t_q > t_p\}$,
i.e., the future light cone from $p$. Every point $q \in \Sigma^+(p)$
satisfies $|\mathbf{x}_q - \mathbf{x}_p|^2 - c^2(t_q - t_p)^2 = 0$,
equivalently $|\mathbf{x}_q - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t_q - t_p)$.

The consequence: two points
$q, q' \in \Sigma^+(p)(t)$ on the wavefront at parameter time $t$
share locality in $x_4 = ict$ with the apex $p$, sharing the
parameter time $t_q = t_{q'} = t$ on the spatial slice; both are at
$ds^2 = 0$ from $p$. The First McGucken Law of Nonlocality
(Theorem [1.50.1](#thm:first-mcgucken-law){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:first-mcgucken-law"} below) makes this precise: $q$
and $q'$ are EPR-correlated through their common apex $p$ via
co-emission, with the correlation strength bounded by the Tsirelson
bound $2\sqrt{2}$.

**Step 3: The $i$ is what distinguishes the two readings.** The
pivot between (I) and (II) is the algebraic character of
the fourth-dimensional coordinate: real in (I), purely imaginary in
(II) via the $i$. The consequence at the metric level:
$$\begin{aligned}
\text{Reading (I):} \quad & dx_4 = c\,dt \in \mathbb{R} \Rightarrow (dx_4)^2 = c^2\,dt^2 \Rightarrow \text{Euclidean signature }(+,+,+,+),\\
\text{Reading (II):} \quad & dx_4 = ic\,dt \in i\mathbb{R} \Rightarrow (dx_4)^2 = -c^2\,dt^2 \Rightarrow \text{Lorentzian signature }(-,+,+,+).
\end{aligned}$$
The $i$ in reading (II) supplies the $(-)$ sign in the signature via
$i^2 = -1$. Without it, the time-component squared is $+c^2 dt^2$
(Euclidean); with it, the time-component squared is $-c^2 dt^2$
(Lorentzian). The Lorentzian signature is what permits the existence
of null vectors, which is what permits the existence of null
hypersurfaces and null cones, which is what permits the McGucken
Sphere $\Sigma^+(p)$ to have its null wavefront character with
$ds^2 = 0$ between apex and wavefront points.

**Step 4: What reading (I) cannot produce.** Under reading (I), the
following empirically observed phenomena are inaccessible:

*(a) Bell-violation of local-hidden-variable correlations.* The
Bell--CHSH bound for local-hidden-variable theories on a Euclidean
four-manifold is $|S| \le 2$. The Tsirelson bound $|S| \le 2\sqrt{2}$
observed empirically (Aspect 1982 [@Aspect1982CHSH]; Hensen 2015
[@Hensen2015Loophole]; Giustina 2015 [@Giustina2015Loophole]; Shalm
2015 [@Shalm2015Loophole]; BIG Bell 2018 [@BIGBellTest2018]; Nobel
2022) requires nonlocal correlations between spatially separated
detectors. Reading (I) has no nonlocal-correlation content because
its wavefront preserves Euclidean locality (Step 1). Therefore
reading (I) is incompatible with observed Bell-violation.

*(b) Lorentz invariance of physical laws.* Special relativity (1905
onward) is empirically validated by every accelerator experiment,
every GPS timing measurement, every muon-decay observation, every
Hafele--Keating clock comparison. The isometry group of reading
(I)'s Euclidean four-manifold is $SO(4)$, not the Lorentz group
$SO^+(1,3)$. Therefore reading (I) is incompatible with empirical
Lorentz invariance.

*(c) Light-cone causal structure.* The empirical principle that no
information propagates faster than light, expressed via the null-cone
causal structure of Lorentzian spacetime, has no analog in Euclidean
$\mathbb{R}^4$ (which has no null vectors, hence no null cones).
Therefore reading (I) is incompatible with empirical light-cone
causality.

*(d) Wick rotation as relating QM amplitudes to thermal partition
functions.* The Feynman--Wiener correspondence
$\exp(iS/\hbar) \leftrightarrow \exp(-\beta E)$ via the analytic
continuation $\tau = it/\hbar$ (Feynman 1948
[@Feynman1948Path]; Matsubara 1955 [@Matsubara1955]) requires a
transition between Lorentzian and Euclidean signatures. Reading (I)
is already Euclidean, so no Wick rotation needs to occur — the
rotation is the transition between the two readings, and reading
(I) alone has nothing to rotate to. The empirical signature of the
Wick rotation across 78 years requires reading (II) plus the
McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ as the transition.

*(e) The Born rule's normalization
$\int |\psi|^2\,d^3 x = 1$ as a probability density.* The Born
rule is a bilinear sesquilinear pairing
$\langle\psi, \psi\rangle = \int \psi^* \psi\,d^3 x$ on the
wavefunction with $\psi$ complex-valued. The $\psi^*$ requires the
complex conjugate, which requires the complex structure of
$\mathbb{C}$, which requires the perpendicularity marker $i$ for
$x_4 = ict$
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}, anchored in Frobenius's theorem on
$\mathbb{R}$-algebras admitting a single perpendicular axis).
Without the $i$, the wavefunction would be real-valued; there would
be no $\psi^*$ structure; the Born rule's normalization could not
be formulated. Therefore reading (I) is incompatible with the
empirical structure of QM.

**Step 5: Conclusion.** The imaginary unit $i$ in
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ carries the selection. The $i$ is what
selects reading (II) — the Lorentzian-nonlocal reading — over
reading (I) — the Euclidean-local reading. Without the $i$, the
framework collapses into reading (I), which is incompatible with
five independent empirical facts (Bell-violation, Lorentz invariance,
light-cone causality, Wick rotation, Born-rule structure). With the
$i$, reading (II) holds, and the framework produces the McGucken
Sphere null wavefront with $ds^2 = 0$ nonlocality at every event,
supplying the content from which QM, GR, and
thermodynamics descend as forced theorems of the chain of theorems.

The $i$ in $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ is therefore *the indispensable feature* of the principle. The McGucken
framework's principle is precisely "$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ with the $i$ giving the wavefront its null Lorentzian structure." ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:i-as-nonlocality-marker .remark}
*Remark 1.50.A* (The McGucken Sphere as null versus Euclidean

::: {#thm:second-mcgucken-law .theorem}

::: {#thm:six-sense-nonlocality-convergence .theorem}
**Theorem 1.50.3** (Six-sense convergence for McGucken-Sphere
nonlocality; [@MG-Nonlocality-2026] §4; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] §17.1bis).
*The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^+(p)$ generated by

*(i) **Foliation-theoretic sense**: $\Sigma^+(p) \cap \Sigma_t$ is

*(ii) **Metric-level-set sense**: $\Sigma^+(p) \cap \Sigma_t$ is
