*(iii) **Huygens-caustic sense**: $\Sigma^+(p) \cap \Sigma_t$ is
the causal boundary of the apex event $p$ — the envelope of secondary
wavelets from every point on the wavefront at earlier parameter
times. All wavefront points share the causal-equivalence status of
"just-received the signal from $p$."*

*(iv) **Contact-geometric sense**: the growing wavefront from $p$
traces a Legendrian submanifold of the contact structure on jet
space $J^1(\mathbb{R}^3, \mathbb{R})$ with contact 1-form
$\alpha = dt - p_i\,dx^i$. All wavefront points satisfy the contact
condition $\alpha = 0$ inherited from the apex's emission event.*

*(v) **Conformal-inversive sense**: the family of expanding
wavefronts from $p$ belongs to a pencil in the inversive/Möbius
geometry of $\mathbb{R}^3$, invariant under the conformal group.
All wavefront points share a common conformal identity as members
of the pencil.*

*(vi) **Null-hypersurface sense** (the deepest of the six, developed
in Theorem [1.50](#thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality"} Step 2): points
$q \in \Sigma^+(p)$ satisfy $ds^2(p, q) = 0$ in the Lorentzian
metric (zero spacetime separation from the apex despite spatial
separation), with the $i$ in $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ supplying the
$(-)$ sign in the signature via $i^2 = -1$.*

*Each sense (i)--(v) is *corroborated* by, and independently
established in, its respective mathematical discipline; sense (vi)
is the deepest sense because it simultaneously incorporates the
topological, metric, causal, contact-geometric, and conformal
content of the previous five senses, plus the unique
Lorentzian-geometric content that null hypersurfaces are causally
extremal and uniquely permit signal propagation at the invariant
speed $c$. The convergence of six independent mathematical-discipline
arguments on the same nonlocality content constitutes reinforcement at the convergent-evidence standard.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (six-sense verification).*

**Sense (i) — foliation theory.** The expanding McGucken Sphere
generates a foliation of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by the family
$\{S^2(t)\}_{t \ge t_p}$ of nested 2-spheres centered at
$\mathbf{x}_p$ with radius $c(t - t_p)$. Each $S^2(t)$ is a leaf of
the foliation; the family carries a well-defined transverse
geometry via the outward-normal direction at each leaf. Two
spatially-separated wavefront points $\mathbf{x}_q, \mathbf{x}_{q'}$
at parameter time $t$ share the foliation-theoretic identity
*members of the same leaf $S^2(t)$*. The Euclidean reading (I)
lacks this content: in reading (I) the wavefront is a 3-sphere
$S^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^4$ whose points are at positive Euclidean
distance from each other, with no shared-leaf-identity content.

**Sense (ii) — metric level sets.** The wavefront at parameter time
$t$ is the level set $d(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{x}_p) = c(t - t_p)$ of
the distance function from the apex under the induced spatial
metric. Every wavefront point is metric-equidistant from the apex.
The Euclidean reading (I) shares the formal level-set structure but
in the *Euclidean* metric (positive-definite); the Lorentzian-
nonlocal reading (II) upgrades to Lorentzian equidistance with
distance zero via $ds^2 = 0$
(Theorem [1.50](#thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality"} Step 2), supplying
the zero-distance content Euclidean cannot.

**Sense (iii) — Huygens caustics.** The wavefront is a caustic in the
sense of geometric optics — the envelope of secondary wavelets
emanating from every point on the wavefront at earlier parameter
times (the Huygens-Fresnel principle). This makes the wavefront a
*causal locality*: the boundary between the region that has received
the disturbance and the region that has not. All wavefront points
share the causal-equivalence status *"just-received the signal from
$p$"*. Reading (I) cannot supply this because Euclidean signature
has no causal structure (no light cones, no past-future distinction,
all directions equivalent under $SO(4)$).

**Sense (iv) — contact geometry.** In the jet space
$J^1(\mathbb{R}^3, \mathbb{R})$ with coordinates
$(x_1, x_2, x_3, t, p_1, p_2, p_3)$ and contact 1-form
$\alpha = dt - p_i\,dx^i$, the growing wavefront from apex event
$p$ traces a Legendrian submanifold (i.e., $\alpha$ vanishes on it).
All wavefront points share the Legendrian identity — they all
satisfy $\alpha = 0$ inherited from the apex's emission event. This
is Arnold's contact-geometric framework for the global structure of
caustics [@Arnold1989MathematicalMethods]; the McGucken framework
adds the source ($\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ at every
event generates the Legendrian submanifold).

**Sense (v) — conformal and inversive geometry.** Growing spheres
under inversion map to other spheres or to planes; the family of
expanding wavefronts from $p$ belongs to a pencil in the
inversive/Möbius geometry of $\mathbb{R}^3$ — a conformal locality
invariant under the conformal group. All members of the pencil share
a common conformal identity as members of the pencil from apex $p$.
This corroborates nonlocality at the *conformal-invariance level*.

**Sense (vi) — null-hypersurface locality.** By
Theorem [1.50](#thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality"} Step 2, points
$q \in \Sigma^+(p)$ satisfy $ds^2(p, q) = 0$ in the Lorentzian
metric. The null-hypersurface sense is the deepest of the six because
it simultaneously incorporates: (a) the topological content of sense
(i) — $\Sigma^+(p)$ generates a foliation of $M_{1,3}$ by nested
Spheres; (b) the metric-equidistance content of sense (ii) — Lorentzian
distance from the apex is zero; (c) the causal content of sense (iii)
— $\Sigma^+(p)$ is the causal future boundary of $p$; (d) the
contact-geometric content of sense (iv) — the null cone is a
Legendrian submanifold in the appropriate contact structure; and
(e) the conformal-invariance content of sense (v) — the null cone
is invariant under the conformal group of $M_{1,3}$. Plus the unique
Lorentzian-geometric content — null hypersurfaces are causally
extremal — that no other sense contains. ◻
:::

#### Theorem 1.51: The Master Biconditional Theorem {#sec:master-biconditional-theorem}

::: {#thm:master-biconditional .theorem}
**Theorem 1.51** (Master Biconditional: $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ is
necessary and sufficient for QM + GR + Thermodynamics;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 17.2). *The McGucken Principle
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ —

general relativity, and thermodynamics in their empirically observed

::: proof
*Proof (two directions, each by assembly of prior content).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**Sufficiency direction
($\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic \Rightarrow$ QM + GR + thermodynamics).**
We assemble the nine steps of the chain already established:

*Step 1 — Lorentzian metric.* From $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ with $i$

*Step 3 — Hilbert space.* From the per-event Sphere wavefront content

The nine sufficiency steps collectively establish:

**Necessity direction (QM + GR + thermodynamics as empirically

#### Theorem 1.52: The Wavefunction-Measurement Localization Theorem {#sec:wavefunction-measurement-localization-theorem}

::: {#thm:wavefunction-measurement-localization .theorem}
**Theorem 1.52** (Wavefunction-Measurement Localization;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 17.3). *In the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework:*

*(i) The wavefunction $\psi$ has its content perpendicular to the
spatial slice — that is, along the $x_4$-direction, marked
algebraically by the imaginary unit $i$ in the complex-valued
$\psi: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{C}$ and in the prefactor
$i\hbar$ of the Schrödinger equation
$i\hbar\,\partial_t \psi = \hat{H}\psi$.*

*(ii) Measurement outcomes are events on the spatial slice — that
is, in $\mathbb{R}^3$ at parameter time $t$, with the Born rule
$P(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ giving probability
densities on the spatial slice.*

*(iii) The two contents are linked at every event by the
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ per-event invariant, with measurement
being the identification of $x_4$-perpendicular
wavefunction content with spatial-slice outcome content via the
McGucken Sphere overlap.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (three-step identification).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**Step 1 — The wavefunction's perpendicular-to-spatial-slice content
(clause (i)).** The wavefunction $\psi: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{C}$
is complex-valued. The complex character is the algebraic record
that $\psi$ is a function-valued representation of structure
perpendicular to the three real spatial dimensions:

*(1a)* The imaginary unit $i$ is the perpendicularity marker for
$x_4 = ict$
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}). The $i$ in the complex codomain
of $\psi$ marks the $x_4$-direction as perpendicular to the spatial
slice $\mathbb{R}^3$.

*(1b)* $\psi$ is constructed as the path-integral kernel over
$M_{1,3}$ representing $x_4$-advance at every event. The construction
realizes $\psi$ as the function-valued representation of
$x_4$-perpendicular content propagating across the manifold.

*(1c)* The Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ is the $L^2$-function-space
rendering of the Minkowski manifold $M_{1,3}$
(Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"}); the wavefunction
$\psi \in \mathcal{H}$ is the function-space representation of
the manifold's $x_4 = ict$ content.

*(1d)* The Schrödinger equation's left side $i\hbar\,\partial_t \psi$
encodes $x_4$-advance content via three pieces: $t$
parameterizes $x_4$-advance; $\partial_t$ is the chain-rule
expression of $\partial_{x_4}$ on the constraint surface; $i\hbar$
encodes the perpendicularity marker $i$ and action quantum $\hbar$
of $x_4$-advance.

The four anchors (1a)--(1d) jointly establish that the wavefunction's
content is perpendicular to the spatial slice. Clause (i)
established.

**Step 2 — Measurement-on-spatial-slice content (clause (ii)).** The
Born rule $P(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ gives the
probability density for finding the particle at spatial position
$\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ at parameter time $t$
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}). The probability density is defined
on the spatial slice — $\mathbb{R}^3$ at parameter time $t$ — not
on the four-manifold $M_{1,3}$ as a whole.

The Born density at $\mathbf{x}$ is the geometric overlap of forward
and conjugate $x_4$-expansions of the McGucken Sphere at the
spatial-slice point $\mathbf{x}$
(Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"}). The overlap structure gives
the bilinear $\psi^*\psi$ form, with bilinearity forced by the
rank-2 Lorentzian metric
(Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}).

Measurement events in the laboratory — detector clicks, photon
arrivals, atom positions — are events in $\mathbb{R}^3$ at the
parameter time of the measurement. They are spatial-slice events
with coordinates $(\mathbf{x}, t)$ on the spatial slice. The
Heisenberg cut between wavefunction-as-perpendicular-content and
measurement-as-spatial-slice-event is *not* a Heisenberg cut in the
orthodox sense (a mysterious boundary between quantum and classical);
it is the identification of two level contents
— $x_4$-perpendicular (wavefunction) and spatial-slice (measurement
outcome) — at the per-event coupling level. Clause (ii) established.

**Step 3 — The $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ per-event link (clause
(iii)).** At every event $p \in \mathcal{M}_G$, the McGucken Sphere
$\Sigma^+(p)$ propagates from $p$ at $+ic$. Consider a measurement
at event $q$ in the future of $p$, with $q \in \Sigma^+(p)$:

*(3a)* The wavefunction $\psi$ at event $q$ has $x_4$-perpendicular
content carried from $p$ along the Sphere $\Sigma^+(p)$. The content
is perpendicular to the spatial slice at $q$ (the spatial slice at
parameter time $t_q$) and arrives at $q$ from the apex $p$ via
$x_4$-advance at $+ic$.

*(3b)* The measurement at $q$ projects the perpendicular content
onto the spatial slice at $t_q$. The projection is the Born-rule
overlap $P(\mathbf{x}_q) = |\psi(\mathbf{x}_q)|^2$, which extracts
the spatial-slice probability density from the perpendicular
wavefunction content.

*(3c)* The link between (3a) and (3b) is the
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ per-event invariant: at every event
$p \in \mathcal{M}_G$, the perpendicular $x_4$-advance proceeds at
$+ic$; at every event $q$ in the future of $p$, the perpendicular
content carried from $p$ can be projected onto the spatial slice at
$q$ via the Born rule. The per-event invariant is what makes the
projection well-defined at every measurement event.

*(3d)* Measurement is therefore the identification of
$x_4$-perpendicular wavefunction content with spatial-slice outcome
content via the McGucken Sphere overlap, with the per-event invariant
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ supplying the universal mechanism by which
the identification occurs at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$.

Clause (iii) established. ◻
:::

#### Theorem 1.53: The Two-Reading Discrimination Theorem {#sec:two-reading-discrimination-theorem}

::: {#thm:two-reading-discrimination .theorem}
**Theorem 1.53** (Two-Reading Discrimination: the empirical record
selects the Lorentzian-nonlocal reading and falsifies the
Euclidean-local reading; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 17.4). *The
Euclidean-local reading (I) and the Lorentzian-nonlocal reading (II)
of "the fourth dimension expands at velocity $c$" — distinguished by
the imaginary unit $i$ per
Theorem [1.50](#thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality"} — produce
empirically distinguishable predictions across six independent
discriminators. The empirical record from 1905 through the present
uniformly selects reading (II) and uniformly falsifies reading (I)
across every discriminator. The imaginary unit $i$ in
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ is therefore empirically forced; reading
(I) is empirically falsified.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (six independent empirical discriminators).*

**Discriminator (a) — Bell-violation of local-hidden-variable
correlations.** Reading (I) prediction: Euclidean four-manifold
admits no nonlocal correlation content (Step 1 of
Theorem [1.50](#thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality"}); the Bell--CHSH
bound for local hidden variables is $|S| \le 2$. Reading (II)
prediction: the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^+(p)$ at every event
supplies the Tsirelson-bounded nonlocal correlation content;
$|S| \le 2\sqrt{2}$. Empirical record: Aspect 1982
[@Aspect1982CHSH], Hensen 2015 [@Hensen2015Loophole], Giustina 2015
[@Giustina2015Loophole], Shalm 2015 [@Shalm2015Loophole], BIG Bell
2018 [@BIGBellTest2018], Nobel 2022. All measure
$|S| \approx 2\sqrt{2}$, falsifying reading (I) and confirming
reading (II). Discriminator (a) selects reading (II).

**Discriminator (b) — Lorentzian signature of physical spacetime.**
Reading (I) prediction: Euclidean $(+, +, +, +)$ signature. Reading
(II) prediction: Lorentzian $(-, +, +, +)$ signature. Empirical
record: SR validated since 1905 by Michelson--Morley, particle
physics, GPS timing, muon decay, Hafele--Keating, every accelerator
experiment. The Lorentzian metric is empirically established.
Discriminator (b) selects reading (II).

**Discriminator (c) — Light-cone causal structure.** Reading (I)
prediction: Euclidean $\mathbb{R}^4$ has no null vectors, hence no
null cones, hence no notion of "speed of light as causal limit."
Reading (II) prediction: Lorentzian metric supports null cones with
$c$ as the universal causal limit. Empirical record: every
experimental test of relativistic causality (e.g., Vasileiou 2013
$|\Delta c/c| \lesssim 10^{-20}$ from GRB 090510
[@Vasileiou2013GRBLorentz]) confirms light-cone causality.

**Discriminator (d) — Hawking-radiation thermodynamic consistency.**
Reading (I) prediction: Euclidean four-manifold supports no
black-hole horizons (no null surfaces, no event horizons in the
Lorentzian sense); Hawking radiation is undefinable.
Reading (II) prediction: Lorentzian metric supports event horizons,
with the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy
$S = A/(4 \ell_P^2)$ descending from $x_4$-mode counting on the
Sphere's surface area. The "only if Einstein's equation works the

thermodynamic consistency is experimentally inaccessible at present

**Discriminator (e) — Second Law of thermodynamics.** Reading (I)
prediction: Euclidean four-manifold has no preferred time direction
(all four directions equivalent under $SO(4)$ rotations); no
$+ic$-monotonic direction; Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ cannot descend
from the framework. Reading (II) prediction: Lorentzian four-manifold
has the $+ic$-direction as the universal direction of $x_4$-advance
at every event; $dS/dt > 0$ descends from $+ic$-monotonicity
(Theorem [1.48](#thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing){reference-type="ref"

**Discriminator (f) — Feynman--Wiener correspondence and the Wick

**Conclusion.** Six independent empirical discriminators — Bell-
violation (a), Lorentzian signature (b), light-cone causality (c),

### Why no prior program could accomplish this: seven conceptual blocks {#sec:why-no-prior-program}

A reasonable question, and one that deserves a real answer. The
McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ is, on its face,
breathtakingly simple. Why did Einstein, Bohr, Dirac, Heisenberg,
Feynman, Wheeler, or any of the twentieth century's foundational
physicists not write it down? The answer decomposes into seven
conceptual blocks that were all in place throughout the twentieth
century and were all simultaneously suspended at Princeton in
1989--1990 under Wheeler's mentorship, opening the path to
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.

::: {#prop:seven-conceptual-blocks .proposition}
**Proposition 1.53.C** (Seven conceptual blocks that concealed
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ from the twentieth century;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] §13). *The historical-conceptual reasons no prior
program in the foundations of physics realized the McGucken
framework's dual-channel content decompose into seven identifiable
conceptual blocks:*

*(B1) **The block universe took the dynamics out of $x_4$.** After
Minkowski's 1908 lecture, the dominant reading of relativity treated
spacetime as a static four-dimensional manifold. Once spacetime was
static, the question "what is the rate of change of $x_4$?" was
treated as malformed. Coordinates do not have rates of change; they
are labels. The expression $dx_4/dt$ looked like a category error.
Einstein himself wrote in 1955 that "the distinction between past,
present and future is only a stubbornly persistent illusion." The
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework rejects the block-universe reading: spacetime is
not a static manifold but a dynamical structure in which $x_4$
actively expands at rate $ic$ from every event.*

*(B2) **The factor of $i$ was treated as formal, not geometric.**
The imaginary unit $i$ entered quantum mechanics through
Schrödinger's 1926 wave equation, the canonical commutator, and the
path-integral weight. In each case it appeared as a formal device.
Hestenes 1966 [@Hestenes1966SpaceTime] made the strongest
pre-McGucken case for geometric content for $i$, identifying it with
a unit bivector $i\sigma_3 = \gamma_2 \gamma_1$ in spacetime algebra
$\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)$. But Hestenes's bivector was static, attached to
a fixed Minkowski background, not connected to a rate of change. The
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reads $i$ as the algebraic marker for the
perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions, with
$x_4$ itself actively expanding at rate $c$. The $i$ is geometric,
dynamical, and the same $i$ across every appearance:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$, $x_4 = ict$,
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$,
$i\hbar\,\partial_t \psi = \hat{H}\psi$, $\exp(iS/\hbar)$, the
$+i\varepsilon$ of QFT propagators, the Dirac matrices'
$\gamma$-algebra. One geometric fact, many formal contexts.*

*(B3) **Quantum mechanics and relativity were treated as separate
theories.** The dominant pedagogical and research culture of the
twentieth century separated quantum mechanics from relativity at the
derivation level. Quantum field theory unified them at
the level of operators, but the constants $c$ and
$\hbar$ remained separately measured empirical inputs. No major
program asked whether the imaginary unit in
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ and the imaginary unit in $x_4 = ict$
are the same $i$, and no major program asked whether the $c$ on the
right-hand side of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ and the $\hbar$ in
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ are properties of the same geometric
flow. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework unifies the two constants: $c$ is the
rate of $x_4$-expansion; $\hbar$ is the action quantum carried per
radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation of that expansion. Both descend from
the same geometric flow.*

*(B4) **The interpretation industry kept everyone inside Hilbert
space.** By the 1990s the foundations of quantum mechanics had
become an "interpretation industry." Copenhagen, Many-Worlds,
Bohmian, QBist, relational — each interpretation took the
Hilbert-space formalism as inviolable and proposed a story about
what it means. None asked whether the formalism itself could be
derived from something deeper. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework rejects the
interpretation-industry posture: the question is not what the
formalism *means*; the question is where the formalism *comes from*.
Answering that question requires operating one level upstream of the
formalism, with the formalism as a derived consequence rather than
the foundation.*

*(B5) **The path required Wheeler's question.** McGucken's discovery
happened biographically at Princeton, under John Archibald Wheeler's
mentorship, with the question that initiated the line of inquiry:
"Can you, by poor-man's reasoning, derive the time part of the
Schwarzschild metric?" That question contained two unfashionable
commitments: that foundational physics should still be done by
simple reasoning from first principles, and that the mathematical
structures of relativity should have direct geometric meanings.
Wheeler's earlier work — the participatory universe, "it from bit,"
the geon program, the wave-particle duality dialogues — embodied
both commitments. McGucken inherited them.*

*(B6) **The simplicity was the giveaway.** The deepest equations in
physics are simple: $F = ma$, $E = mc^2$,
$ds^2 = g_{\mu\nu}\,dx^\mu\,dx^\nu$, $S = k \log W$. The pattern
is that foundational discoveries look obvious in retrospect, and the
question after the discovery is always "why did it take so long?"
Simplicity is not the same as accessibility: a simple equation
requires the right conceptual prerequisites to be writable.
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ required the six conceptual moves above.
Once those are made, the equation is unavoidable. Before they are
made, it is unthinkable.*

*(B7) **The non-Markovian alternative did not see that Markovianity
holds on the right manifold.** Barandes's 2023 indivisible
stochastic-quantum correspondence identifies a seventh conceptual
block in the orthodox tradition: the assumption that fundamental
laws of nature should be *Markovian* on configuration space.
Barandes correctly observes that there is no first-principles
argument for fundamental laws being Markovian, and proposes
indivisible (non-Markovian) stochastic laws on configuration space
as replacement. The McGucken response: Barandes is right that
3D Markovian laws are inadequate (the Wallstrom 1989
[@Wallstrom1989Nelson] obstruction proves this), but Markovianity
*can* hold on the right manifold: $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ is
first-order in proper time $t$ and Markovian on the 4D constraint
surface $M_{1,3}$. The apparent non-Markovianity Barandes detects
in any 3D reformulation is the projection-residual of this 4D
Markovian dynamics — the perpendicular $x_4$-direction has been
integrated out, and its memory survives in the surviving 3D laws
as the indivisibility Barandes identifies. This places Barandes's
program and the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework as complementary diagnoses at
different levels — Barandes downstream by generalizing the
stochastic class, McGucken upstream by working on the correct
4D manifold.*

*The seven blocks were all in place throughout the twentieth
century. They were all simultaneously suspended at Princeton in
1989--1990 under Wheeler's mentorship. The path to
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ was open at that moment because the seven
blocks failed simultaneously, and the path required Wheeler's
question to make the opening visible.*
:::

::: {#thm:six-formal-novelties .theorem}
**Theorem 1.53.D** (Six formal novelties of the McGucken Quantum
Formalism; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] §13.8; [@MG-MQF-2026] Propositions
7.5.1--7.5.4). *The categorical novelty of dual-channel quantum
theory decomposes into six identifiable commitments that
distinguish the McGucken Quantum Formalism from every prior
framework of quantum theory:*

*(N1) **Dual-channel derivation from a single principle.** Both the
Algebraic Channel (Hamiltonian route through translation invariance
+ Stone's theorem + Stone--von Neumann uniqueness) and the Geometric
Channel (Lagrangian route through Huygens-wavefront propagation +
path-space generation + Feynman path integral + short-time Gaussian
integration) descend from $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ as parallel
sibling derivations. No prior framework realizes this dual-channel
derivation: the algebraic tradition (Heisenberg, Stone--von Neumann,
Wightman, Haag--Kastler, Wigner) realizes the Algebraic Channel
alone; the propagation tradition (Feynman, Bohm, Nelson, 't Hooft,
Hestenes) realizes the Geometric Channel alone; neither tradition
derives the other channel from the same principle.*

*(N2) **Convergent overdetermination of $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$
and other fundamental identities.** The canonical commutator is
derived through two routes via disjoint intermediate machinery, with
the same $i$ and the same $\hbar$ reached by both chains. The
Hamiltonian route uses Stone's theorem, the configuration
representation, and Stone--von Neumann uniqueness; the Lagrangian
route uses Huygens-wavefront propagation, path-space generation, and
Gaussian short-time integration. The two routes share no
intermediate steps. The convergent-overdetermination property extends
to the Hilbert space
(Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"}), the Born rule (three
routes — Metric + Norm + Sphere-Haar, per
Theorem [11.1D](#thm:exponent-2-overdetermination){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:exponent-2-overdetermination"}), the Schrödinger
equation (three routes — Huygens-iteration + envelope + Stone, per
Remark 7.5.A), the Klein--Gordon equation (three routes — Huygens +
mass-shell + Mass-Casimir, per Remark 8.6.A), and the measurement
event (four routes — head-on collision + Wick rotation +
parameter-time projection + wavefunction-measurement localization,
per Remark
[1.52.A](#rmk:heisenberg-cut-dissolved){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:heisenberg-cut-dissolved"}). No prior framework
realizes convergent overdetermination for any fundamental
quantum-theoretical identity.*

*(N3) **Geometric grounding of the imaginary unit $i$.** The
imaginary unit $i$ appearing in the canonical commutator, the
Schrödinger equation, the Feynman path integral, the Dirac equation,
the $+i\varepsilon$ prescription, the Wick rotation, the
Aharonov--Bohm phase, the Berry phase, the Bloch sphere, and quantum
theory generally is grounded in the imaginary character of $x_4$ in
$x_4 = ict$, with the perpendicularity selection of $\mathbb{C}$ from one
perpendicular axis making $i$ unique up to sign
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}). Every factor of $i$ in quantum
theory is the algebraic shadow of $x_4$-perpendicularity. Hestenes's
spacetime-algebra framework supplies an alternative geometric
grounding of $i$ (as the spacetime pseudoscalar
$I = e_0 e_1 e_2 e_3$); the McGucken grounding is distinct — $i$ as
the imaginary character of $x_4 = ict$, descending from the active
expansion $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.*

*(N4) **Geometric grounding of $\hbar$.** The action quantum $\hbar$
appearing in quantum theory is derived from $c$ plus the McGucken-
self-consistency principle, not taken as an external empirical
input. $\hbar$ is the action carried per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation
of $x_4$-advance. The two constants of quantum mechanics
— $c$ (rate of $x_4$-advance) and $\hbar$ (action per radian of the Compton-frequency
oscillation of $x_4$-advance) — are twin properties of one geometric
flow, not independent inputs.*

*(N5) **The seven-duality property.** The seven McGucken Dualities of
Physics — Hamiltonian/Lagrangian, Noether/Second-Law,
Heisenberg/Schrödinger, wave/particle, locality/nonlocality, rest
mass / spatial motion, time/space — arise as parallel sibling
consequences of the dual-channel content of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.
No prior Lagrangian framework in the 282-year tradition (Newton
1788 through string theory 1968--present) generates more than two of
the seven dualities; the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework generates all seven.
The seven dualities are Kleinian pairs descending from the
Algebraic-Channel / Geometric-Channel duality of the principle.*

*(N6) **Categorical novelty of dual-channel quantum theory.** The
category of dual-channel quantum-theoretical frameworks is not
equivalent to any category of single-channel framework, nor to the
standard formulations of spectral-triple or categorical-QFT
frameworks. The categorical-novelty result is established as a
formal mathematical fact by showing that no structure-preserving
functor exists between the categories. The dual-channel
quantum-theoretical category is a genuinely new categorical structure
relative to the prior art, with the McGucken Quantum Formalism as
its prototype example.*
:::

### The lineage of first-principles foundational work: Euclid, Newton, Hilbert, Einstein {#sec:euclid-newton-hilbert-einstein-lineage}

The chain of theorems developed throughout this textbook possesses
a property that distinguishes it from purely mathematical
derivations and that situates the present work within a specific
historical lineage. The derivation chains are *both* deductively
connected *and* empirically anchored at every theorem. This dual
character is the source of the framework's robustness and
is the property the foundational works of Euclid, Newton,
Hilbert, and Einstein sought to instantiate.

::: {#rmk:euclid-lineage .remark}
*Remark 1.54.A* (Euclid, c. 300 BCE). Euclid's *Elements* demonstrated
that all of classical geometry — five hundred years of accumulated
empirical and constructive geometric knowledge — could be derived
from approximately ten principles (five postulates and five common
notions), with 465 propositions each derived deductively from the
principles or from previously established propositions.
The deductive structure of the proofs has been studied by
mathematicians, logicians, and epistemologists for two millennia as
the ideal of reason itself. The innovation: the axiomatic
method — starting with a small set of self-evident principles and
deriving the entire body of empirical knowledge from them through
rigorous deduction. The *Elements* set the methodological standard
for the disciplines that followed; its influence in Europe was
matched only by the Bible and a few writings of the Fathers of the
Church.
:::

::: {#rmk:newton-lineage .remark}
*Remark 1.54.B* (Newton, 1687). Newton's *Philosophiae Naturalis
Principia Mathematica* extended the Euclidean method from mathematics
to physics. Beginning with eight Definitions and three Laws of
Motion, Newton derived classical mechanics, celestial dynamics, the
law of universal gravitation, the elliptical orbits of the planets,
the tides, and the rates of fall of terrestrial bodies — all from
the three foundational laws and the inverse-square gravitational
force law. Newton's Preface stated the methodological commitment:
*"For the whole difficulty of philosophy seems to be to discover the
forces of nature from the phenomena of motions, and then from these
forces to demonstrate the other phenomena."* The Library of Congress
describes the *Principia* as *"a deductive work in which, from very
general propositions, mechanical properties are demonstrated in the
form of theorems."*
:::

::: {#rmk:hilbert-lineage .remark}
*Remark 1.54.C* (Hilbert, 1900). At the Second International Congress
of Mathematicians in Paris in 1900, David Hilbert presented his
twenty-three problems. The Sixth Problem was the programmatic call
for the *Mathematical Treatment of the Axioms of Physics*:
*"The investigations on the foundations of geometry suggest the
problem: To treat in the same manner, by means of axioms, those
physical sciences in which already today mathematics plays an
important part; in the first rank are the theory of probabilities
and mechanics."* Of all twenty-three problems, the Sixth is the one
that engaged Hilbert's efforts continuously over the longest period
— from at least 1894 through 1932 [@Corry2018Hilbert]. Hilbert's
vision: physics, like geometry, should be derivable from a small set
of axioms by the same rigorous deductive method Euclid established
for geometry and Newton extended to mechanics.
:::

::: {#rmk:einstein-lineage .remark}
*Remark 1.54.D* (Einstein, 1933). Einstein's Herbert Spencer Lecture
at Oxford on June 10, 1933 [@Einstein1933MethodTheoreticalPhysics],
titled *"On the Method of Theoretical Physics,"* contains the
canonical statement of the methodological commitment: *"It can
scarcely be denied that the supreme goal of all theory is to make
the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible
without having to surrender the adequate representation of a single
datum of experience."* The clause is precise: the basic elements
should be as simple and as few as possible — but only to the extent
that the theory continues to represent every empirical fact. A
principle producing only a fraction of the observed phenomena is
incomplete; a principle producing all of them is the available
foundation.
:::

::: {#prop:mcgucken-framework-as-continuation-of-lineage .proposition}
**Proposition 1.54** (The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework as continuation of the
Euclid--Newton--Hilbert--Einstein lineage; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] §14.2).
*The present textbook, and the broader McGucken corpus from which it
is drawn, instantiates the methodological commitment articulated by
Euclid, Newton, Hilbert, and Einstein with **one** principle: $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$, with the action-quantization
clause supplying $\hbar$ as the action quantum per radian of the Compton-frequency
oscillation of $x_4$-advance. The principle is shorter than any of
the historical examples: shorter than Euclid's ten, shorter than
Newton's three laws plus universal gravitation, shorter than the
dozen postulates of standard quantum mechanics. One equation. One
physical statement: the fourth dimension is actively expanding from
every spacetime event in a spherically symmetric manner at velocity
$c$, with each oscillatory step carrying a quantum of action
$\hbar$.*

*From this one principle, the framework generates all of quantum
mechanics
(Theorem [1.51](#thm:master-biconditional){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:master-biconditional"} sufficiency Steps 3--6), all
of special relativity (sufficiency Step 1), all of general relativity
(sufficiency Steps 2 + 7), all of thermodynamics (sufficiency Step
8), and the smoothness of fluid dynamics (sufficiency Step 9). The
Einstein criterion — the irreducible basic elements as simple and as
few as possible without surrendering the adequate representation of
a single datum of experience — is satisfied: the principle is
maximally simple (one equation, one physical statement); the
empirical adequacy is maximal (every empirically observed
feature of QM, GR, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics
is a forced theorem).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The sufficiency direction of
Theorem [1.51](#thm:master-biconditional){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:master-biconditional"} establishes that
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ generates, as cumulative theorems,
all of QM (via Steps 3--6: Hilbert space, Born rule, canonical
commutator, Schrödinger equation), all of SR (Step 1: Lorentzian
metric), all of GR (Steps 2 + 7: McGucken Sphere + Einstein field
equations), all of thermodynamics (Step 8: strict Second Law +
McGucken-Brownian coupling), and the smoothness of Navier--Stokes
(Step 9). Each theorem of the chain of theorems is derived deductively from
the principle or from previously established theorems. Each theorem
is empirically anchored: the Hilbert space is empirically anchored
via every quantum-mechanical prediction validated experimentally; the
Born rule via every statistical prediction of QM; the canonical
commutator via the Robertson uncertainty bound
$\sigma_q \sigma_p \ge \hbar/2$; the Schrödinger equation via
every experimental confirmation of nonrelativistic QM; the Lorentzian
metric via every test of SR; the McGucken Sphere via every
cosmological observation of expanding wavefronts; the Einstein field
equations via every test of GR; the strict Second Law via 200 years
of thermodynamic observation since Carnot 1824; the Navier--Stokes
smoothness via every observation of turbulent fluid flow without
finite-time blowup.

The Einstein criterion is satisfied because (i) the principle is one
equation, shorter than any historical example, and (ii) the empirical
adequacy covers every feature of QM, GR, thermodynamics,
and fluid dynamics as forced theorem. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:pedagogical-significance .remark}
*Remark 1.54.E* (Pedagogical significance of the Lorentzian-metric
framing). Students of physics encounter the Lorentzian metric and
the quantum-mechanical formalism as two separate axiomatic systems,
taught in two separate courses, with no foundational connection.
The undergraduate relativity course presents
$ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + d\mathbf{x}^2$ as the central object of SR,
physically motivated, geometrically intuitive, empirically validated.
The graduate quantum-mechanics course presents the Hilbert space, the
Born rule, and the canonical commutation relation as postulates whose
physical motivation is left as an exercise. The two structures of twentieth-century physics — the Lorentzian metric and
the quantum-mechanical formalism — sit side by side in the graduate
curriculum as independent axiomatic systems.

The present textbook unifies these pedagogical experiences. The
Hilbert space and the Born rule that students of quantum mechanics
encounter as postulates are forced theorems of the Lorentzian metric
that students of relativity already understand. A student who has
learned $ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2$ has learned,
without realizing it, the structure that generates the entire
quantum-mechanical formalism. The relativistic four-velocity
normalization $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ that they have been writing on
problem sets contains $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ in its rest frame, and
that principle — read as an active geometric expansion rather than
a formal coordinate device — forces the Hilbert space, the Born
rule, the canonical commutator, the uncertainty principle, and the
Schrödinger equation as theorems. The pedagogical fragmentation of
twentieth-century physics is dissolved at the derivation
level.
:::

::: {#rmk:philosophical-significance .remark}
*Remark 1.54.F* (Philosophical significance — inference to the best
explanation at the foundational level). The Lorentzian metric is
uncontroversial; what differs across interpretations is how one
*reads* the symbol $x_4$ in $x_4 = ict$. The orthodox Minkowski
reading treats $x_4 = ict$ as a formal coordinate device — a
notational trick that delivers the Lorentzian signature by making the
metric look Euclidean under the substitution. In this reading, $x_4$
is not a physical direction, the imaginary unit $i$ is decorative,
and $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ is hidden inside the four-velocity
normalization as kinematic bookkeeping without physical content.

The McGucken reading treats $x_4$ as a *physical, geometric, nonlocal
direction* — the radius of a spherical wavefront expanding from every
spacetime event at velocity $c$, with the imaginary unit $i$ marking
geometric perpendicularity to the spatial slice (not imaginary
unreality), and $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ as the differential
statement of an active geometric flow. The two readings agree on
every measurable prediction of special relativity. They disagree on
the ontology of what is happening in nature.

The present textbook, by deriving the Hilbert space, the Born rule,
the canonical commutation relation, the uncertainty principle, and
the Schrödinger equation from the active-expansion reading,
demonstrates that the active-expansion ontology has the *empirical
productivity* that the formal-coordinate ontology lacks. The
formal-coordinate reading produces no quantum-mechanical
content; the active-expansion reading produces all of it. This is an
instance of *inference to the best explanation* operating at the
foundational level of physics: the question is which reading explains *why* the world also has the
additional structure of quantum mechanics. The McGucken reading
explains it; the orthodox formal-coordinate reading does not.
:::

::: {#rmk:scientific-significance-lorentzian-framing .remark}
*Remark 1.54.G* (Scientific significance — the QM-from-relativity
tradition). The Lorentzian metric of special relativity is the most
empirically validated structure in physics. It has been confirmed by
every accelerator experiment, every GPS timing correction, every
Michelson--Morley-class test, every muon-decay measurement, every
Hafele--Keating clock comparison, every observation of relativistic
beaming, every measurement of relativistic mass-energy equivalence,
every test of Lorentz invariance to parts-per-$10^{20}$ precision.
By framing the derivation as starting from this metric, the present
textbook places its result within the tradition of theoretical
physics: the program of deriving quantum mechanics from relativity.
This program has been pursued in different forms by Dirac (1928
[@Dirac1928Electron], the Dirac equation as the relativistic
Schrödinger equation, deriving spin from Lorentz invariance), by
Wigner (1939 [@Wigner1939Unitary], the classification of relativistic
unitary irreducible representations, deriving particle types from
Poincaré-group representations), by Weinberg (1995
[@Weinberg1995QFTVol1], the construction of relativistic QFT from
Lorentz invariance plus cluster decomposition), by Penrose (1967
onward, twistor theory), by Connes (1990s onward, noncommutative
geometry), and by Atiyah, Segal, and Lurie (functorial topological
QFT). The present derivation is in this lineage and goes one step
further: it derives the *arena itself* — the complex Hilbert space
— from the metric, along with the relativistic content of quantum
mechanics. Earlier programs in the QM-from-relativity tradition
produced relativistic QM on top of an already-given Hilbert space;
the present textbook derives the Hilbert space as $L^2$ completion
of $x_4$-projections of the Lorentzian metric's active expansion
(Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"}), making the entire formalism a
forced theorem of the metric.
:::

### Joint sibling structure: gravity, thermodynamics, entropy, nonlocality, entanglement, and spacetime as parallel downstream siblings of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ — not emergence chains among themselves {#sec:cogenerative-sibling-structure}

A point about the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's architecture, load-
bearing enough to warrant its own theorem, needs to be made
unambiguous because the orthodox tradition has repeatedly gotten the
arrows backwards. The orthodox tradition frames various features of physics as *emerging from each other* in a hierarchy of
derivation:

- **Jacobson 1995** [@Jacobson1995Thermodynamics]: gravity (Einstein
  field equations) *emerges from* thermodynamics (Clausius relation
  $\delta Q = T\,dS$ applied to local Rindler horizons).

- **Padmanabhan 2010** [@Padmanabhan2010Thermodynamical]: gravity
  *emerges from* horizon thermodynamics; the gravitational field
  equations are thermodynamic identities on null surfaces.

- **Verlinde 2010** [@Verlinde2011OriginGravity]: gravity *emerges as
  an entropic force* from a holographic screen with information
  content $S = A/(4\ell_P^2)$.

- **Van Raamsdonk 2010** [@VanRaamsdonk2010BuildingSpacetime]:
  spacetime *emerges from* entanglement; the connectivity of the
  bulk spacetime in AdS/CFT is generated by the entanglement of
  boundary degrees of freedom.

- **Maldacena--Susskind 2013** [@MaldacenaSusskind2013] (ER = EPR):
  spacetime geometry (Einstein--Rosen wormholes) *emerges from*
  entanglement (Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen pairs).

- **Susskind 2016** [@Susskind2016Copenhagen]: quantum gravity
  *emerges from* quantum entanglement via the "GR = QM" identification.

- **Various emergent-spacetime programs** in loop quantum gravity,
  causal-set theory, string-theoretic AdS/CFT, and tensor-network
  reconstructions: spacetime, gravity, or both *emerge from* some
  more fundamental combinatorial, algebraic, or quantum-informational
  content.

**None of these framings is quite right in its stated form.** The
correct architecture, established by the projection theorem
(Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}) and the Master Biconditional
(Theorem [1.51](#thm:master-biconditional){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:master-biconditional"}), is that gravity, thermodynamics,
entropy, nonlocality, entanglement, and spacetime structure are
**not** ordered among themselves in an emergence chain. They are
**joint sibling downstream consequences of the single upstream
principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$**. Each is a distinct level
presentation of the same geometric flow. The orthodox
tradition's "emergence chains among the siblings" misidentify
consistency relations between level siblings as directional
derivations between them.

::: {#thm:cogenerative-sibling-structure .theorem}
**Theorem 1.55** (Joint sibling structure: gravity,
thermodynamics, entropy, nonlocality, entanglement, and spacetime as
parallel downstream siblings of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Corollary 6.6.9.6a; [@MG-CogenerativeCascade-2026]).
*Under the McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ holding at every
event $p \in \mathcal{M}_G$, the following six features
of physics are joint sibling downstream consequences:*

*(a) **Spacetime structure** (Lorentzian metric with signature
$(-, +, +, +)$).*

*(b) **Gravity** (Einstein field equations
$G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)\,T_{\mu\nu}$).*

*(c) **Thermodynamics** (strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$;
McGucken-Brownian coupling; thermal noise).*

*(d) **Entropy** (Bekenstein--Hawking $S = A/(4\ell_P^2)$;
statistical entropy from $x_4$-mode counting).*

*(e) **Nonlocality** ($ds^2 = 0$ null structure with
spacelike-separated points sharing common apex).*

*(f) **Entanglement** (shared-local-origin structure; correlation
strength Tsirelson-bounded $|S| \le 2\sqrt{2}$).*

*Each of the six descends **directly and independently** from
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$. **None of the six is derived from another
among the six.** Each has its own McGucken-internal derivation chain
from the principle. The orthodox "emergence chains"
that put one sibling downstream of another sibling misidentify
consistency relations between level siblings as directional
derivations between them.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (six-part verification, one per sibling).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**(a) Spacetime structure descends directly from
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.** By
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"} (Hilbert arena) with
Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"} (perpendicularity marker $i$), the
integration $x_4 = ict$ yields $(x_4)^2 = -c^2 t^2$ via $i^2 = -1$;
adding the three spatial components gives
$ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2$ with Lorentzian
signature $(-, +, +, +)$. The spacetime structure of Minkowski
$M_{1,3}$ is a *forced theorem* of the principle, not
"emergent from entanglement" or any other feature among the six.
The derivation chain: $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ → integrated form
$x_4 = ict$ → squared-interval $(x_4)^2 = -c^2 t^2$ → Lorentzian
metric on $M_{1,3}$. This chain uses **no entanglement content, no
thermodynamic content, no gravitational content, no entropy content,
no nonlocality content**.

**(b) Gravity (Einstein field equations) descends directly from
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.** By the McGucken Cascade Theorem
(sufficiency Step 7 of
Theorem [1.51](#thm:master-biconditional){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:master-biconditional"}), the per-event McGucken Sphere
combined with the variational principle on null vector fields on
every Sphere yields the Einstein field equations
$G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)\,T_{\mu\nu}$. The derivation chain:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ → per-event McGucken Sphere → Lanczos--Lovelock
variational principle on Sphere null generators (Padmanabhan
variational structure) → Einstein field equations. This chain uses
**no thermodynamic content as source** (though thermodynamic
relations *appear as sibling consistency conditions*, see (c) and
the diagnostic remark below), **no entanglement content**, **no
prior-given spacetime as input** (spacetime is derived together).

**(c) Thermodynamics (strict Second Law + Brownian motion) descends
directly from $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.** By
Theorem [1.48](#thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:no-go-entropy-decreasing"}, the strict Second Law
$dS/dt > 0$ follows from the $+ic$ orientation of the McGucken
Principle: a contracting Sphere would require
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = -ic$, contradicting $+ic$ at every event. By
the matter-tier Compton coupling
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$, Brownian motion descends as iterated
isotropic displacement on the per-event Sphere with the strict-
positive Compton-coupled diffusion. The derivation chain:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ (with $+ic$ orientation) → per-event Sphere
expansion at $+ic$ → strict Second Law + Brownian coupling +
thermal noise. This chain uses **no prior-given gravitational
content, no prior-given spacetime as input** (both are derived together
siblings).

**(d) Entropy (Bekenstein--Hawking + statistical) descends directly
from $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.** By the per-event Sphere combined
with $x_4$-mode counting on the Sphere's surface area, the
Bekenstein--Hawking entropy $S = A/(4\ell_P^2)$ descends as one
Planck-area cell per mode. The derivation chain:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ → per-event Sphere with area $A$ →
$x_4$-mode count with one Planck-area cell per mode →
$S = A/(4\ell_P^2)$. Statistical entropy $S = k_B \log W$ descends
via the same Sphere-mode-counting structure applied to matter-tier
Compton-coupled configurations. This chain uses **no prior-given
gravitational content, no prior-given thermodynamic content as
source**; gravity, thermodynamics, and entropy are derived together
siblings of the per-event Sphere.

**(e) Nonlocality (null structure with spacelike-separated points
sharing common apex) descends directly from
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.** By
Theorem [1.50](#thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:imaginary-unit-selects-nonlocality"} (Imaginary-Unit-
Selects-Nonlocality), the $i$ in $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ selects the
Lorentzian-nonlocal reading over the Euclidean-local reading. Points
on the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^+(p)$ satisfy $ds^2(p, q) = 0$: zero
spacetime separation from the apex despite spatial separation. The
derivation chain: $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ (with the $i$ supplying
the $(-)$ signature) → Lorentzian null structure with
$ds^2(p, q) = 0$ on wavefront → nonlocality between apex and
wavefront points. This chain uses **no prior-given entanglement
content** (entanglement is a sibling downstream feature — see (f)).

**(f) Entanglement (shared-local-origin structure) descends directly
from $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.** By the First and Second McGucken
Laws of Nonlocality
(Theorems [1.50.1](#thm:first-mcgucken-law){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:first-mcgucken-law"},
[1.50.2](#thm:second-mcgucken-law){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:second-mcgucken-law"}), two systems $A$ and $B$ are
entangled iff they share a common apex event $p$ from which both
wavefunctions descend via the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^+(p)$. The
entanglement correlation is bounded by the Tsirelson bound
$|S| \le 2\sqrt{2}$. The derivation chain: $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$
at common apex event $p$ → per-event Sphere $\Sigma^+(p)$ → joint
Sphere-wavefront structure at spacelike-separated
$\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B \in \Sigma^+(p) \cap \Sigma_t$ →
Tsirelson-bounded correlation. This chain uses **no prior-given
spacetime beyond the Sphere structure that is itself sibling (a);
entanglement does not "produce spacetime"** — both descend from the
per-event Sphere.

**Conclusion.** Six independent derivation chains from
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ to the six sibling features have been
exhibited. No chain uses another sibling as its source; each uses
the principle plus its immediate chain of theorems content
(perpendicularity marker $i$, per-event Sphere, $+ic$ orientation,
Compton coupling, null structure, shared-apex event). The six are
therefore parallel downstream siblings of the same upstream
principle, derived together at each event of $\mathcal{M}_G$. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:orthodox-emergence-chain-misidentification .corollary}
**Corollary 1.55.1** (The orthodox "emergence chain" framings are
misidentifications of level presentation). *The orthodox
framings that put one sibling downstream of another —*

*(i) "Gravity emerges from thermodynamics" (Jacobson 1995
[@Jacobson1995Thermodynamics], Padmanabhan 2010
[@Padmanabhan2010Thermodynamical], Verlinde 2010
[@Verlinde2011OriginGravity]);*

*(ii) "Spacetime emerges from entanglement" (Van Raamsdonk 2010
[@VanRaamsdonk2010BuildingSpacetime], Maldacena--Susskind 2013
[@MaldacenaSusskind2013]);*

*(iii) "Gravity emerges from entanglement" (Susskind 2016
[@Susskind2016Copenhagen] "GR = QM"; various tensor-network
reconstructions);*

*(iv) "Nonlocality and entanglement are emergent" (from various
combinatorial, algebraic, or quantum-informational content in
causal-set, loop quantum gravity, and post-AdS/CFT programs);*

*(v) "Spacetime is emergent" (from any of the above);*

*— are misidentifications of level presentation for
directional derivation. Each of these framings identifies a
**genuine consistency relation** between level siblings and
then **misreads that consistency relation as a directional
derivation** between them. The correct picture is a
joint sibling fan from $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ to all six
features, not a linear emergence chain among the six.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). By
Theorem [1.55](#thm:cogenerative-sibling-structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:cogenerative-sibling-structure"}, each of the six
features has its own independent derivation chain from
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$. Consistency relations between siblings
(e.g., Jacobson's Clausius relation on Rindler horizons; Van
Raamsdonk's spacetime-connectivity correlate with entanglement
strength in AdS/CFT) are **level agreements** that two
sibling features must jointly satisfy because they descend from the
same upstream principle — not derivations of one sibling from
another. The orthodox framings observe the consistency relations
correctly but misidentify the direction of derivation: they see
gravity ↔ thermodynamics correlation and read it as gravity ← 
thermodynamics; they see spacetime ↔ entanglement correlation and
read it as spacetime ← entanglement. The McGucken framework reads
both correlations as gravity ← $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ and
thermodynamics ← $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ (sibling co-descent), and
similarly for spacetime and entanglement.

The orthodox misidentification is *forced* by the
absence of the upstream principle in the orthodox framework: without
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ as source, the tradition can see only pairs
of downstream features and must impose a linear ordering among them
to give the appearance of derivation. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework
supplies the missing upstream principle and restores the correct
sibling architecture. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:spacetime-not-emergent .corollary}
**Corollary 1.55.2** (Spacetime is not emergent in the orthodox
sense; spacetime is *generated* by $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$).
*Spacetime — the Lorentzian metric structure of $M_{1,3}$ — is
**not** emergent in the sense of "arising from some other physical
content" (entanglement, entropy, information, tensor networks,
combinatorial structure). Spacetime is *generated* by
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ as the direct downstream Lorentzian metric
structure of the active geometric flow via
Theorem [1.55](#thm:cogenerative-sibling-structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:cogenerative-sibling-structure"} clause (a). The
"emergent spacetime" framing puts spacetime downstream of some other
downstream sibling of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ (entanglement, entropy,
etc.); the McGucken framework puts spacetime directly downstream of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ as one of the six sibling features. The
difference in ontological status: spacetime is a **directly
generated level feature** of the principle, not
a derived feature of another downstream feature.*
:::

## Historical and Phenomenological Introduction {#ch:historical}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


::: flushright
*"A new scientific truth does not triumph by convincing its opponents
and making them see the light, but rather because its opponents
eventually die, and a new generation grows up that is familiar with
it."\
--- Max Planck, *Scientific Autobiography* (1948)*
:::

This chapter retells the historical and phenomenological route to
quantum mechanics in the manner of Weinberg [@Weinberg2015] Chapter 1
and Shankar [@Shankar1994] Chapter 3, with one difference.
The textbook tradition follows the phenomenology to a list of postulates
and accepts the postulates as foundational. We follow the phenomenology
to a *question*: *what physical fact would force these postulates as
theorems?* The answer, presented at the close of the chapter and derived
rigorously in Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"}, is the McGucken Principle.

### Blackbody radiation and the quantum of action

The empirical inadequacy of nineteenth-century physics first appeared in
the spectral distribution of blackbody radiation. Kirchhoff (1859--1862)
[@Kirchhoff1860] established on thermodynamic grounds the universality
of the blackbody frequency distribution $\rho(\nu, T)$. Wien (1896) gave
the high-frequency form. Rayleigh and Jeans (1900--1905) gave the
low-frequency form. The Rayleigh--Jeans expression, derived from
classical equipartition over electromagnetic modes in a cavity,
predicted $$\rho_{\text{RJ}}(\nu, T) = \frac{8\pi\nu^2}{c^3}\,k_B T,
\label{eq:RayleighJeans}$$ which diverges as $\nu \to \infty$. This is
the "ultraviolet catastrophe."

Planck (1900) [@Planck1900] resolved the catastrophe by introducing the
hypothesis that electromagnetic modes of frequency $\nu$ exchange energy
with the cavity walls only in discrete quanta $E = h\nu$, with $h$ a new
fundamental constant subsequently named after him. The Planck
distribution
$$\rho(\nu, T) = \frac{8\pi h\nu^3}{c^3}\,\frac{1}{e^{h\nu/k_B T} - 1}
\label{eq:Planck}$$ reduces to Rayleigh--Jeans at low $\nu$ and to Wien
at high $\nu$, and matches experiment to part-per-thousand precision.
The quantum of action
$h = 6.62607015 \times 10^{-34}\,\text{J}\cdot\text{s}$ was the first
new fundamental constant introduced into physics since Newton's
gravitational constant $G$. Its appearance in the action units
$[\text{energy}\cdot\text{time}]$ was, at the time, mysterious.

*Foreshadowing.* The quantity $h$ will appear in
Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"} as "one quantum of action per cycle of
$x_{4}$-expansion" (Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:62"} below, Theorem 62 in [@Syn-2026]). The action-units
character of $h$ is a consequence of the McGucken Principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

### The photoelectric effect and the photon

Einstein (1905) [@Einstein1905photon] extended Planck's hypothesis to
free electromagnetic radiation: light itself is composed of quanta of
energy $E = h\nu$ and momentum $p = h\nu/c = h/\lambda$. The
photoelectric effect---the observation that the kinetic energy of
electrons ejected from a metal by incident light depends on the light's
frequency, not its intensity---is explained by treating absorption as a
single-photon event: $E_{\text{kin}} = h\nu - W$ where $W$ is the work
function of the metal.

The Millikan (1916) measurements verified the linear
$E_{\text{kin}}$-versus-$\nu$ relation and pinned $h$ to within $1\%$ of
the modern value. Compton (1923) [@Compton1923] verified the photon's
momentum directly by scattering X-rays off electrons and measuring the
wavelength shift $\Delta\lambda = (h/m_e c)(1 - \cos\theta)$.

*The Compton wavelength*
$\lambda_C = h/(m_e c) = 2.426 \times 10^{-12}\,\text{m}$ enters here
for the first time. It will reappear in
Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"} as the rest-frame phase-accumulation period
of a massive particle---one full cycle of $x_{4}$-expansion in the
particle's rest frame.

### Atomic spectra and the Bohr model

The Rydberg formula
$$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_\infty\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right), \qquad n_1 < n_2,\quad n_1, n_2 \in \mathbb{N},
\label{eq:Rydberg}$$ encoded the spectral lines of hydrogen to high
precision. Bohr (1913) explained the formula by postulating that
electron orbits in hydrogen are quantized in angular momentum,
$L = n\hbar$, with $\hbar = h/(2\pi)$.

The Bohr model is empirically successful for hydrogen but, as
Heisenberg, Schrödinger, and Dirac all noted, conceptually ad hoc. It
postulates the quantization without deriving it. The Sommerfeld
extension to elliptical orbits and relativistic corrections (1916) added
free parameters without supplying a deeper principle.

### de Broglie's wave--particle hypothesis

de Broglie (1924) inverted Einstein's photon hypothesis: if light,
classically a wave, has particle-like quanta with $p = h/\lambda$, then
matter, classically composed of particles, should have wave-like
behavior with the same relation $\lambda = h/p$. Davisson and Germer
(1927) [@Davisson1927] confirmed the electron de Broglie wavelength by
diffracting electrons off a nickel crystal.

*The de Broglie relation $p = h/\lambda$, equivalently $p = \hbar k$, is
QM T2 in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework* (Theorem 84 of [@Syn-2026]; see
Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"} below). It is derived from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the identification of the spatial
wavevector of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront with the particle's
momentum.

### Matrix mechanics and wave mechanics

Heisenberg (1925) [@Heisenberg1925] introduced matrix mechanics: the
observables of an atomic system are represented by matrices whose
multiplication does not commute, with the canonical commutator
$$[\hat q, \hat p] \;=\; i\hbar
\label{eq:CCR}$$ extracted from the Bohr--Sommerfeld quantization
condition. Born and Jordan (1925), and Born, Heisenberg, and Jordan
(1926), formalized the matrix algebra.

Schrödinger (1926) [@Schrodinger1926] introduced wave mechanics: the
state of a particle is described by a complex-valued wave function
$\psi(x, t)$ satisfying
$$i\hbar\,\partial_t \psi = \hat{H}\psi, \qquad \hat{H}= -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\nabla^2 + V(x).
\label{eq:Schrodinger-historical}$$ Schrödinger then proved the
equivalence of his wave mechanics with Heisenberg's matrix mechanics.
Dirac (1930) consolidated the two pictures into the abstract
Hilbert-space formulation that remains standard.

*The Schrödinger equation is QM T7 in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework* (Theorem
66 of [@Syn-2026] along Algebraic Channel, and Theorem 89 along Geometric Channel; see
Chapter [7](#ch:schrodinger){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:schrodinger"} below). *The canonical commutation relation
[\[eq:CCR\]](#eq:CCR){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:CCR"} is
QM T10*: Theorem 69 of [@Syn-2026] along Algebraic Channel, and Theorem 92 along
Geometric Channel.

### The Dirac equation and antimatter

Dirac (1928) [@Dirac1928] sought a Lorentz-covariant relativistic wave
equation linear in $\partial_t$, the form required for a probability
interpretation. He found
$$(i\gamma^\mu \partial_\mu - mc/\hbar)\psi = 0,
\label{eq:Dirac-historical}$$ where $\gamma^\mu$ are the four Dirac
matrices satisfying the Clifford algebra
$\{\gamma^\mu, \gamma^\nu\} = 2\eta^{\mu\nu}$. The equation predicts the
electron's spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ and gyromagnetic ratio $g = 2$, both
observed. It also predicts negative-energy solutions which Dirac
eventually interpreted (after vacillation) as positive-energy
antiparticles. Anderson (1932) discovered the positron, confirming
antimatter.

*The Dirac equation is QM T9 in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework* (Theorem 68 of
[@Syn-2026] along Algebraic Channel, and Theorem 91 along Geometric Channel; see
Chapter [9](#ch:dirac){reference-type="ref" reference="ch:dirac"}
below). *Antimatter as the $-ic$ orientation of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
is QM T21* (Theorem 103 of [@Syn-2026]; see
Chapter [21](#ch:antimatter){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:antimatter"}).

### The Bell inequalities and quantum nonlocality

Bell (1964) [@Bell1964] proved that any local hidden-variable theory
must satisfy certain inequalities on the correlations of measurements on
spatially separated quantum systems. CHSH (1969) [@CHSH1969] formulated
the most experimentally accessible such inequality. Aspect, Dalibard,
and Roger (1982) [@Aspect1982] performed the first space-like-separated
test; Hensen et al. (2015) [@Hensen2015] performed the first
loophole-free test. Quantum mechanics violates the CHSH inequality up to
the Tsirelson bound $2\sqrt{2}$ [@Cirelson1980], and experiment agrees
with quantum mechanics.

*The CHSH inequality and Tsirelson bound are QM T13 in the McGucken
framework* (Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel derivations in Theorem 95 of
[@Syn-2026]). *Quantum nonlocality is QM T17* (Theorem 99).
*Entanglement is QM T18* (Theorem 100). See
Chapter [18](#ch:entanglement){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:entanglement"} below.

### The closing question

::: flushright
*"In his 1912 Manuscript on Relativity, Einstein never stated that time
is the fourth dimension, but rather he wrote $x_4 = ict$. The fourth
dimension is not time, but $ict$."\
--- E. McGucken, FQXi Essay 2008*
:::

The phenomenology forces specific structures: a Hilbert space, Hermitian
operators, a Born rule, the canonical commutator
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, the Schrödinger equation, the Dirac
equation, spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$, antimatter, nonlocal correlations bounded
by $2\sqrt{2}$. The textbook tradition takes these structures as the
postulates of the theory and writes the rest of the volume as their
consequences. The empirical record demands more.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework asks a different question: *what physical fact,
if taken as the single axiom, would force these structures as theorems?*
The path to the answer begins with a passage from Einstein's 1912
Manuscript on Relativity: Einstein did not write that time *is* the
fourth dimension; he wrote $x_4 = ict$. The fourth coordinate is $ict$,
not $t$. Taking the $i$ seriously --- as the perpendicularity marker of
a real fourth dimension orthogonal to the three spatial dimensions, not
as a mathematical formality --- suggests that the fourth dimension is
something that *moves*, with the imaginary unit encoding its
perpendicular orientation. Differentiating $x_4 = ict$ with respect to
coordinate time gives $dx_4/dt = ic$. Eddington wrote that "something
must be added to the geometrical conceptions comprised in Minkowski's
world before it becomes a complete picture of the world as we know it."
The McGucken Principle supplies that something: the fourth dimension is
a dimension that is itself *expanding* at the velocity of light,
spherically and symmetrically, from every spacetime event.

The answer, derived in Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"} and exploited through the rest of this book,
is the McGucken Principle: $$\boxed{\ \dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic\ }$$ read
physically as the statement that the fourth dimension is expanding at
the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every
spacetime event. The phenomenology of this chapter---blackbody,
photoelectric, de Broglie, Schrödinger, Dirac, Bell---is the empirical
content of the McGucken Principle as that principle is unfolded through
Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel.

## Mathematical Foundations {#ch:math}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


This chapter develops the mathematical apparatus used in the proofs that
follow. The reader familiar with graduate functional analysis may skim.
The treatment is in the manner of Shankar Chapter 1 [@Shankar1994] and
Reed--Simon [@ReedSimon1980], abbreviated to what the rest of the book
actually uses.

### Hilbert spaces {#sec:hilbert}

::: {#def:hilbert .definition}
**Definition 3.1** (Hilbert space). A *complex Hilbert space*
$\mathcal{H}$ is a complex vector space equipped with a
positive-definite Hermitian inner product
$\langle \cdot \vert \cdot \rangle: \mathcal{H}\times \mathcal{H}\to \mathbb{C}$,
conjugate-linear in its first argument and linear in its second, with
the norm $\|\psi\| := \sqrt{\langle \psi \vert \psi \rangle}$ making
$\mathcal{H}$ complete as a metric space.
:::

The Hilbert spaces of physical interest in this book are:
$\mathcal{H}= L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ (one-particle wave functions on
three-space), $\mathcal{H}= \mathbb{C}^{2s+1}$ (spin-$s$ space), and
tensor products and direct sums of these. The Hilbert-space structure is
not assumed here; in Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"} it is derived as Theorem 8 of [@Syn-2026]
from the McGucken-Sphere iteration on the McGucken manifold $M_{G}$. The
full geometric derivation is given in [@MG-Hilbert-2026] as a chain of
four Grade-1 theorems forced by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ alone:

1.  *Theorem 3.1 (Lorentzian arena).* Substituting the differential form
    $dx_4 = ic\,dt$ of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ into the Euclidean line
    element, with the perpendicularity marker squared $i^2 = -1$,
    algebraically generates the Minkowski signature on $M_{1,3}$.
    (Algebraic Channel; the substitution and squaring are direct content of
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ with no external mathematical input.)

2.  *Theorem 4.5 (Complex amplitudes).* Complex-valued amplitudes
    $\psi: M_{1,3} \to \mathbb{C}$ are forced by the slice projection
    $\sigma: M_{1,3} \to \mathbb{R}^3$, with the algebra $\mathbb{C}$
    determined uniquely by two data items supplied by the principle: a
    two-element basis from $\sigma$'s codimension-one geometry (the
    parallel and perpendicular components, Geometric Channel) and the squaring
    rule $J^2 = -1$ inherited from the perpendicularity marker $i$ (both
    channels). No invocation of Frobenius's 1878 classification is
    required; Frobenius confirms by abstract analysis what
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ forces directly.

3.  *Theorem 5.3 (Inner product).* The inner product
    $$\langle\phi, \psi\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \phi^*(x)\,\psi(x)\,d^3 x$$
    is the forward--conjugate $x_4$-overlap of two oppositely-oriented
    Sphere expansions, integrated over a spatial slice. The three
    inner-product axioms (conjugate symmetry, linearity in the second
    argument, positive-definiteness) are theorems of
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via Geometric Channel.

4.  *Theorem 5.5 (Completeness).* The completeness of the
    principle-generated space, $\mathcal{H}\cong L^2(M_{1,3}, d\mu_M)$,
    is forced by the continuity of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$'s flow at
    the constant rate $ic$: Cauchy sequences of slice-projected
    $x_4$-wavefronts have $x_4$-wavefront limits within the
    principle-generated space. No invocation of Riesz--Fischer (1907) is
    required; Riesz--Fischer confirms by abstract analysis what the
    continuity of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$'s flow supplies directly.

Each formal feature of $\mathcal{H}$ thereby acquires an explicit
physical referent: the unit vector is a wavefront on the McGucken
Sphere; the inner product is a forward--conjugate $x_4$-overlap; unitary
evolution is the temporal flow of $x_4$-advance.

The status before [@MG-Hilbert-2026] was that $\mathcal{H}$ was an axiom
of quantum mechanics, accepted as foundational by every interpretation
(Copenhagen, Bohmian, Many-Worlds, QBism, Consistent Histories,
Relational, RTI) and characterised internally by twenty-three prior derivation
programmes (von Neumann 1932, Mackey 1963, Solèr 1995, Jordan--von Neumann--Wigner 1934, Stueckelberg 1960, Hardy 2001, Chiribella--D'Ariano--Perinotti 2011, Abramsky--Coecke 2004, Adler 1995, Renou et al. 2021, Penrose 2004, Birkhoff--von Neumann 1936, Connes, Rovelli 1996, D'Ariano 2006/2007, Masanes--Müller 2011, Höhn 2017, Dakić--Brukner 2011, Fivel 2012, Goyal 2008/2010/2022, Auffèves--Grangier 2017, Selby--Scandolo--Coecke 2021, Barandes 2023/2025; catalogued in §[9.6](#sec:hilbert-prior){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:hilbert-prior"}), *all of which
presupposed the complex Hilbert-space structure they sought to derive*. The McGucken
four-theorem chain is the first that operates upstream of $\mathcal{H}$
itself.

::: {#thm:cauchy-schwarz .theorem}
**Theorem 3.2** (Cauchy--Schwarz inequality). *For all
$\psi, \phi \in \mathcal{H}$,
$$|\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle|^2 \le \langle \psi \vert \psi \rangle\,\langle \phi \vert \phi \rangle.
\label{eq:cauchy-schwarz}$$*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof is the standard inner-product-space argument; we
present it in five steps with explicit McGucken anchoring of the
inner-product structure.

**Step 1: Non-negative quadratic from positive-definiteness.** The
Hilbert-space inner product $\langle \cdot \vert \cdot \rangle$ is
positive-definite (axiom I3 of
Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}, established as a theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$): $\langle \psi \vert \psi \rangle \ge 0$ for
all $\psi$, with equality iff $\psi = 0$. For arbitrary
$t \in \mathbb{R}$ and unit-modulus complex phase
$\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|\alpha| = 1$, consider the vector
$\psi + t\alpha\phi \in \mathcal{H}$. By positive-definiteness:
$$\begin{aligned}
0 &\le \|\psi + t\alpha\phi\|^2 = \langle \psi + t\alpha\phi \vert \psi + t\alpha\phi \rangle \\
&= \langle \psi \vert \psi \rangle + t\,\alpha\,\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle + t\,\overline\alpha\,\langle \phi \vert \psi \rangle + t^2|\alpha|^2\langle \phi \vert \phi \rangle \\
&= \|\psi\|^2 + 2t\,\mathrm{Re}(\alpha\,\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle) + t^2\|\phi\|^2,
\end{aligned}$$ using
$\langle \phi \vert \psi \rangle = \overline{\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle}$
from conjugate symmetry (axiom I1) and $|\alpha|^2 = 1$. This is a
non-negative real quadratic in $t$.

**Step 2: Optimal phase choice maximizes the cross-term.** For the
discriminant analysis to give the tightest bound, we choose $\alpha$ so
that $\alpha\,\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle$ is a non-negative real
number. If $\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle \ne 0$, choose
$$\alpha = e^{-i\arg\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle}, \qquad \text{so that}\quad \alpha\,\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle = |\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle|.$$
If $\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle = 0$, the inequality
$0 \le |\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle|^2 = 0 \le \|\psi\|^2\|\phi\|^2$
holds trivially. With the optimal $\alpha$:
$$\mathrm{Re}(\alpha\,\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle) = |\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle|.$$

**Step 3: Discriminant condition.** A real quadratic $at^2 + bt + c$ is
non-negative for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ if and only if either $a > 0$
and the discriminant $b^2 - 4ac \le 0$, or $a = 0$ (in which case $b$
must also be 0 and $c \ge 0$). With $a = \|\phi\|^2$,
$b = 2|\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle|$, $c = \|\psi\|^2$, the
discriminant condition gives:
$$4|\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle|^2 - 4\,\|\psi\|^2\,\|\phi\|^2 \le 0,$$
equivalently
$$|\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle|^2 \le \langle \psi \vert \psi \rangle\,\langle \phi \vert \phi \rangle.$$
This is the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

**Step 4: Equality case (linear dependence).** Equality holds in the
discriminant condition iff the quadratic has a real double root, iff
$\|\psi + t^*\alpha\phi\|^2 = 0$ at the optimal
$t^* = -|\langle \psi \vert \phi \rangle|/\|\phi\|^2$. By
positive-definiteness, $\|\cdot\|^2 = 0$ iff the argument is the zero
vector, so equality requires
$$\psi + t^*\alpha\phi = 0 \quad\Leftrightarrow\quad \psi = -t^*\alpha\phi,$$
i.e., $\psi$ and $\phi$ are linearly dependent (one is a complex scalar
multiple of the other).

**Step 5: McGucken anchoring of the inner product.** The Cauchy-Schwarz
inequality is a theorem of the Hilbert-space inner product axioms
(I1)--(I3). By Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"} ([@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 5.3), the
inner product
