(Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:62"}),
Compton-rate matching (Theorem [4.1](#thm:QMT4){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT4"}, Geometric Channel), Lorentz-covariance of four-vector
proportionality.

**Algebraic Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, time-translation invariance,
QA2 (Stone's theorem), $\hat{H}= i\hbar\,\partial_t$ as generator
(Lemma [3.3](#lem:Hhat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:Hhat-generator"}), eigenvalue calculation
(Lemma [3.4](#lem:energy-phase){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:energy-phase"}), Noether identification generator $\to$
energy.

**Intersection:** $\{(\mathrm{McP}), E = \hbar\omega\}$. Stone's theorem
does not appear in Geometric Channel; Sphere phase does not appear in Algebraic Channel.
*Disjointness verified.*

### Empirical anchor

The Planck--Einstein relation was first introduced by Planck in 1900
[@Planck1900] to resolve the blackbody ultraviolet catastrophe, and
extended by Einstein in 1905 to free electromagnetic radiation
[@Einstein1905photon]. Confirmation:

-   the photoelectric effect (Millikan 1916, confirming $E = h\nu$ for
    photons);

-   the Bohr atomic spectrum (Franck and Hertz 1914, confirming energy
    quantization);

-   the Compton effect (Compton 1923 [@Compton1923], confirming $E$ and
    $p$ of the photon simultaneously);

-   modern atomic-clock optical frequency measurements (since 2005),
    confirming $E = \hbar\omega$ for atomic transitions to fractional
    precision $\sim 10^{-18}$.

## QM T4: The Compton Coupling $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ {#ch:compton}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial
three. Throughout this chapter, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ refers to this
principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: (i) *invariance* --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the
expansion is isotropic in the spatial three, with the set of events
reachable from $p$ in proper time $\tau$ being a 2-sphere of radius
$c\tau$; (iii) *monotonicity* --- the integral curve is strictly
monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of $x_4$-advance; (iv)
*Lorentz consistency* --- the structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on
$M_{G}$; (v) *global validity* --- $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at
every event of $M_{G}$. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ (Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the central fact.

### Statement

::: {#thm:QMT4 .theorem}
**Theorem 4.1** (QM T4: Compton Coupling). *A massive particle of rest
mass $m$ exhibits an internal angular frequency of phase oscillation, in
its rest frame, equal to the Compton frequency
$$\omega_C \;=\; \frac{mc^2}{\hbar}.
\label{eq:compton-coupling}$$ This oscillation is the particle's
physical response to the $x_{4}$-expansion of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.
This is Theorem 63 (Geometric Channel) and Theorem 86 (Algebraic Channel) of
[@Syn-2026].*
:::

### Geometric Channel derivation: Sphere phase accumulation in the rest frame {#sec:QMT4-channelB}

::: {#lem:QMT4-channelB-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 4.4** (Geometric Channel proof of QM T4). *The McGucken Sphere phase
accumulates at rate $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ in the rest frame of a
massive particle.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: Rest-frame $x_{4}$-advance per proper time.** By
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i) (invariance) and (ii) (spherical
symmetry of the $x_{4}$-expansion at rate $c$), in the rest frame,
$dt = d\tau$ and $dx_4 = ic\,d\tau$. The total $x_{4}$-advance over
proper time $\tau$ is $x_{4}(\tau) - x_{4}(0) = ic\tau$, i.e.,
$|x_4(\tau) - x_4(0)| = c\tau$. This is the integrated kinematic shadow $x_{4}= ict$
(Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) restricted to the rest-frame
worldline; the dynamical principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the
central fact, $x_4 = ict$ the integrated kinematic shadow.

**Step 2: Action accumulated per proper time.** By
Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:62"}, one
quantum of action accrues per Sphere cycle, i.e., per $x_{4}$-cycle at
the appropriate matter frequency. For a particle of rest mass $m$, the
matter-specific $x_{4}$-cycling rate is the Compton frequency $\omega_C$
(the rate at which a matter wave of mass $m$ oscillates in phase per
unit proper time as it rides the $x_{4}$-expansion). The total action
over rest-frame proper time $\tau$ is
$$S(\tau) \;=\; \int_0^\tau -mc^2\,d\tau' \;=\; -mc^2\,\tau,$$ using the
standard relativistic action for a free particle $S = -mc^2\int d\tau$
(which is Proposition IV.1 of [@MG-Lagrangian-2026], a Geometric Channel /
variational theorem of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**Step 3: Phase per proper time.** The accumulated quantum-mechanical
phase is $\theta(\tau) = S(\tau)/\hbar = -mc^2\tau/\hbar$. The
instantaneous angular frequency is
$$\omega(\tau) \;=\; -\frac{d\theta}{d\tau} \;=\; \frac{mc^2}{\hbar} \;=\; \omega_C.$$
The sign convention $\psi \propto e^{-i\omega\tau}$ with positive
$\omega$ is the convention that matter has positive rest energy. The
magnitude of the rate is $\omega_C$.

**Step 4: Geometric interpretation.** The Sphere phase in the rest frame
is precisely the integrated $x_{4}$-advance: as the particle's worldline
traces forward in proper time, the $x_{4}$-coordinate advances at rate
$ic$, and the wavefront on the Sphere accumulates phase
$e^{ix_{4}/\hbar c} \cdot e^{-i\omega_C\tau} = e^{i \cdot ict/\hbar c}\cdot e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}$.
The two factors combine: the phase per unit proper time is the rate
$mc^2/\hbar = \omega_C$ at which $x_{4}$ cycles through one quantum of
action.

This is the physical content of QM T4: the particle's rest-frame
oscillation IS the principle's $x_{4}$-expansion read at the rate
$\omega_C$ that corresponds to one quantum of action per cycle. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem [4.1](#thm:QMT4){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT4"}.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The theorem asserts the Compton coupling: a
massive particle of rest mass $m$ at spatial rest has its wavefunction
oscillating at angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$. We establish
this along both channels and verify their derivational disjointness.

**Step 1: Algebraic Channel derivation
(Lemma [4.3](#lem:QMT4-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT4-channelA-proof"}).** By
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} (the four-velocity budget at
rest), a particle at spatial rest directs its entire four-velocity
budget into the $x_{4}$-direction at rate $c$, with rest-frame
four-momentum $P^\mu = (mc, \mathbf{0})$. The rest energy is
$E_0 = P^0 c = mc^2$. Applying the Planck-Einstein relation
$E = \hbar\omega$ (Theorem [3.1](#thm:QMT3){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT3"}) at the rest state:
$$\omega_C = \frac{E_0}{\hbar} = \frac{mc^2}{\hbar}.$$ The mass-Casimir
Wigner classification (QA6) confirms that $P^\mu P_\mu = -m^2 c^2$ for
the massive irreducible representation. The Algebraic Channel route:
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ $\to$ four-velocity budget $\to$ $E_0 = mc^2$
$\to$ Planck-Einstein $\to$ $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$.

**Step 2: Geometric Channel derivation
(Lemma [4.4](#lem:QMT4-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT4-channelB-proof"}).** The rest-frame McGucken-Sphere
phase accumulates at rate determined by the rest-frame action. The
relativistic action for a free particle of rest mass $m$ is
$S = -mc^2\int d\tau$ along the proper-time worldline (derived as a
theorem of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the McGucken Lagrangian,
Chapter [12](#ch:lagrangian-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:lagrangian-uniqueness"}). The phase per unit proper time
is $\omega_{\text{phase}} = (1/\hbar)\cdot dS/d\tau = -mc^2/\hbar$ (with
the negative sign tracking the matter-branch convention). The magnitude
is the Compton angular frequency:
$$|\omega_{\text{phase}}| = \omega_C = \frac{mc^2}{\hbar}.$$ By
Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:62"}, $\hbar$
is the action per Sphere cycle, fixing the Compton frequency as the
Sphere-phase rate per proper time. The Geometric Channel route:
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ $\to$ Sphere construction $\to$ relativistic
action $\to$ action-per-cycle
(Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:62"}) $\to$
Compton phase rate.

**Step 3: Derivational disjointness of the two channels.** Algebraic Channel uses
the four-velocity-budget calculation
(Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"}), the rest-energy-mass equivalence
$E_0 = mc^2$, the Planck-Einstein relation (derived along Algebraic Channel
through Stone's theorem on time-translation), and Wigner's mass-Casimir
classification. Geometric Channel uses the McGucken-Sphere phase accumulation,
the relativistic action principle along the worldline, and the
action-per-cycle quantum $\hbar$
(Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:62"}). The
intermediate machinery is disjoint:

-   Four-velocity budget and Wigner classification appear in Algebraic Channel,
    not in Geometric Channel;

-   Sphere-phase accumulation and action-per-cycle appear in Geometric Channel,
    not in Algebraic Channel.

The two channels share only $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the final
relation $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$.

**Step 4: McGucken anchoring of mass.** The rest mass $m$ enters both
channels through its identification with the four-velocity-budget
temporal component
(Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"}): at spatial rest, the
four-momentum is $P^\mu = mu^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} = (mc, \mathbf{0})$,
with the magnitude $mc$ being the temporal component of the rest-frame
four-momentum. The mass is therefore not an external parameter but the
inertia for $x_{4}$-advance: a higher-mass particle accumulates phase
more rapidly because its $x_{4}$-momentum is larger, and the Compton
frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ measures the rate of this
phase accumulation.

**Step 5: Physical content and experimental verification.** The Compton
frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is the proper-time oscillation rate of
every massive particle's wavefunction. Compton's 1923 measurement of
X-ray wavelength shift in electron scattering established the relation
empirically for the electron:
$\Delta\lambda = (h/(m_e c))(1 - \cos\theta)$ with
$\lambda_C = h/(m_e c) = 2.426$ pm. The relation has been independently
confirmed for the proton, neutron, and atomic nuclei. The cross-species
mass-independence test of clause QA1 (universal-rate clause: every
species couples to $x_{4}$-expansion at the same fundamental rate $c$,
modulated only by $m$) is a falsifiable prediction of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, tested to $\sim 10^{-20}$ at Planck-scale
$\Omega$ in the MGT (McGucken Theory) modulation framework
(Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT22"}). ◻
:::

### Algebraic Channel derivation: Four-velocity budget plus Planck--Einstein {#sec:QMT4-channelA}

::: {#lem:four-velocity-budget .lemma}
**Lemma 4.2** (Rest-frame four-velocity is entirely $x_{4}$-directed).
*For a massive particle at spatial rest ($\mathbf{p} = 0$ in the lab
frame), the four-velocity $u^\mu = dx^\mu/d\tau$ satisfies
$u^\mu = (c, \mathbf{0})$ in the rest frame, and the four-momentum is
$P^\mu = mu^\mu = (mc, \mathbf{0})$. The rest energy is
$$E_0 \;=\; P^0 c \;=\; mc^2.$$*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has six steps; every step explicitly invokes the
relevant clause of Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"},
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, or
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"} establishing $x_{4}= ict$ as the
integrated kinematic shadow of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

**Step 1: Definition of four-velocity.** The four-velocity is the
tangent vector to the worldline parameterised by proper time. With the
worldline $x^\mu(\tau) = (ct(\tau), \mathbf{x}(\tau))$ in the
McGucken-derived Minkowski arena $M_{1,3}$
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}), we have
$u^\mu = (c\,dt/d\tau, d\mathbf{x}/d\tau)$.

**Step 2: Rest frame.** At spatial rest,
$d\mathbf{x}/d\tau = \mathbf{0}$. The proper-time relation
$c^2\,d\tau^2 = c^2\,dt^2 - |d\mathbf{x}|^2$ (descending from the
Minkowski line element of
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, which itself comes from substituting
$dx_4 = ic\,dt$ from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ into the Euclidean line
element) gives $d\tau = dt$ in the rest frame. Hence
$u^\mu = (c, \mathbf{0})$ in the rest frame.

**Step 3: The four-velocity budget in McGucken language.** The norm of
the four-velocity in Minkowski signature $(-,+,+,+)$ (the standard signature
of this textbook, established in
Theorem [4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"}) is
$$u^\mu u_\mu = -(u^0)^2 + |\mathbf{u}|^2 = -c^2 + 0 = -c^2,$$ a Lorentz
invariant (preserved by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv), derived at Theorem 4.6, Lorentz consistency). In the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, this magnitude is the rate at which $x_{4}$ advances
per proper time: $|dx_4/d\tau| = c$ from the differential form
$dx_4 = ic\,dt = ic\,d\tau$ (rest frame), which is the differential
statement of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ per
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i). So at spatial rest, the entire
four-velocity budget is in the $x_{4}$-direction; the principle
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ --- read at the rest-frame worldline parameter
--- gives $|dx_4/d\tau| = c$, which is exactly $u^0 = c$. (More
precisely: in the constraint surface picture of
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"} Step 2, $u^0 = dx_0/d\tau$ where
$x_0 = ct$; and the integrated kinematic shadow $x_{4}= ict = ix_0$ per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}, so
$dx_4/d\tau = i\,dx_0/d\tau = iu^0$. Magnitude $|dx_4/d\tau| = u^0 = c$
at rest, consistent.)

**Step 4: Rest energy.** The four-momentum is
$P^\mu = mu^\mu = (mc, \mathbf{0})$. The temporal component is the
energy: $E_0/c = P^0 = mc$, so $E_0 = mc^2$. By
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i) (invariance: the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content), the parameter $c$ appearing here is the
same invariant rate for every particle species, so $E_0 = mc^2$ holds
universally.

**Step 5: Reading --- rest energy as $x_{4}$-kinetic
energy.** The result $E_0 = mc^2$ has a direct reading in the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework: the rest energy of a massive particle is the kinetic
energy of its $x_{4}$-advance at rate $c$. A particle at spatial rest is
not at rest at all --- it advances along $x_{4}$ at the full rate $c$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i)), and its energy $mc^2$ is the
kinetic energy of this advance, with $m$ playing the role of an inertia
parameter for $x_{4}$-motion. This contrasts with the textbook
interpretation of $E_0 = mc^2$ as a mysterious "rest-mass-energy
equivalence" (Einstein 1905 [@Einstein1905E], the inertia-of-energy
paper) or as a consequence of Lorentz invariance; in the McGucken
framework, the relation is and direct: at rest, the
four-velocity budget is fully $x_{4}$-directed by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(ii), and the kinetic energy of
this $x_{4}$-advance is the rest energy.

**Step 6: McGucken-anchoring summary.** The four-velocity budget at
rest, $u^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} = (c, \mathbf{0})$, is the shadow of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at the rest-frame worldline: the
principle's rate $c$ becomes the rest-frame temporal four-velocity
component, with the spatial components vanishing (since the particle is
at spatial rest). The rest energy $E_0 = mc^2$ is therefore not an
additional empirical input but the temporal four-momentum component
dictated by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i) (invariance of the rate) and (ii)
(spherical symmetry, which forces zero spatial four-velocity at rest).
The integrated kinematic shadow $x_{4}= ict$
(Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow on which the
rest-frame $x_{4}$-advance accumulates; the dynamical content that the
rest-frame four-velocity is $(c, \mathbf{0})$ sits in
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. This is the McGucken anchoring of the most
famous equation in physics. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:coordinate-time-budget .remark}
*Remark 4.2A* (The rate budget is stated per coordinate time, and why
that matters at $v = c$). The principle is
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with $t$ the coordinate time of the frame in
which the statement is made
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}). Every allocation statement in this book ---
"the entity's rate budget is divided between spatial motion and
$x_{4}$-advance" --- is a statement about rates with respect to that
same $t$, and the arithmetic closes in that parameterisation:
$$\left|\frac{dx_{4}}{dt}\right|^2 + \left|\frac{d\mathbf{x}}{dt}\right|^2
\;=\; \frac{c^2}{\gamma^2} + v^2 \;=\; c^2\!\left(1 - \frac{v^2}{c^2}\right) + v^2 \;=\; c^2 ,$$
for every $v \in [0, c]$, where $|dx_{4}/dt| = c/\gamma$ follows from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ read at the entity's own worldline parameter
together with $d\tau/dt = 1/\gamma$.

*The endpoints.* At $v = 0$ the budget is entirely in $x_{4}$:
$|dx_{4}/dt| = c$. At $v = c$ it is entirely spatial:
$|dx_{4}/dt| = c/\gamma \to 0$. The rest endpoint is the content of
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} above, and the massless endpoint is
the zero-rest-mass case used in the derivation of
Theorem [1.1](#thm:QMT1){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT1"}; the interpolation between them is continuous
through the massless limit.

*Why the proper-time parameterisation cannot carry the statement.* The
four-velocity $u^\mu = dx^\mu/d\tau$ is defined per proper time, and the
same allocation written in that parameter does not close: with
$|dx_{4}/d\tau| = c\gamma$ and $|d\mathbf{x}/d\tau| = v\gamma$,
$$\left|\frac{dx_{4}}{d\tau}\right|^2 - \left|\frac{d\mathbf{x}}{d\tau}\right|^2 \;=\; \gamma^2(c^2 - v^2) \;=\; c^2 ,$$
a difference rather than a sum, which is the Lorentzian norm
$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ of
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} and is the correct statement of
that quantity. Two distinct facts are therefore in play, and this book
uses both with the parameter named: the *norm* is Lorentzian and
invariant, stated per $\tau$; the *allocation* is Pythagorean, stated
per $t$. Reading the allocation as a Pythagorean sum of four-velocity
components conflates them, and produces a relation that holds at no
speed except $v = 0$.

*The massless case as a discriminator between the two parameterisations.*
For a photon $d\tau = 0$ along the worldline, so $u^\mu = dx^\mu/d\tau$
does not exist and no statement about a photon's four-velocity can be
made or refuted. The rate $dx_{4}/dt$ has no such difficulty: $t$ is a
coordinate, not a property of the entity, and $|dx_{4}/dt| = c/\gamma$
approaches $0$ continuously as $v \to c$. This is the reason the
principle is stated with $t$ and not with $\tau$, and it is a
substantive reason rather than a convention.

The orthodox formulation carries an exception at exactly this point. The
statement that every entity moves through spacetime at the invariant
rate $c$ is a statement about $|u^\mu|$ with $u^\mu = dx^\mu/d\tau$,
and it holds for every massive entity and for no massless one; the
massless case is handled separately with an affine parameter $\lambda$
and a null tangent $k^\mu$ satisfying $k^\mu k_\mu = 0$, whose norm is
$0$ rather than $c$. The universal statement and its exception are both
correct, and they are not one statement. Stated per coordinate time the
allocation covers $v \in [0, c]$ inclusive, with the photon as the
endpoint of the same relation that governs every massive entity rather
than as a case requiring separate machinery. What the framework claims
here is narrow and checkable: the same physical content --- null
worldline, zero rest mass, maximal spatial rate --- is expressible
without a case split, and the case split in the orthodox presentation is
an artefact of parameterising by a quantity that vanishes on the
worldline in question.

*Scope.* Nothing above disputes the standard treatment of null
geodesics. Affine parameterisation of null curves is correct and
necessary for many purposes, and the physical content of the two
descriptions agrees wherever both are defined. The claim is about which
parameterisation permits a single statement to cover the massive and
massless cases together, and the coordinate-time parameterisation does
so because the parameter belongs to the frame rather than to the entity.
:::

::: {#def:x4-share .definition}
**Definition 4.2B** (The worldline's share of the $x_{4}$-expansion, and
its accumulation). *By Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} the fourth dimension expands at rate $c$ from
every event of $M_{G}$, and the expansion is the same at every event
regardless of which worldline crosses it. A worldline crossing an event
with spatial speed $v$ divides that rate between spatial motion and
$x_{4}$-advance. Its* share *of the expansion, per unit coordinate time
$t$, is*
$$v_{x_4} \;:=\; \sqrt{c^{2} - v^{2}}, \qquad v \in [0, c],$$
*and the partition*
$$v^{2} + v_{x_4}^{2} \;=\; c^{2}$$
*holds identically on the closed interval, null worldlines included. Its*
accumulated $x_{4}$-advance *along a worldline $\Gamma$ is the functional*
$$X_{4}[\Gamma] \;:=\; \int_{\Gamma} ic \, d\tau, \qquad
dX_{4} \;=\; ic \, d\tau \;=\; i\, v_{x_4}\, dt .$$
:::

::: {#rmk:share-endpoints .remark}
*Remark 4.2C* (Why the share is written $\sqrt{c^{2}-v^{2}}$, and what
each endpoint says). On a timelike worldline the share is the standard time-dilation factor of special relativity, $$v_{x_4} \;=\; c\,\frac{d\tau}{dt} \;=\; \frac{c}{\gamma} \qquad (0 \le v < c),$$
so nothing in the standard formalism is displaced; $\tau$ appears here as
output, not as the parameter of differentiation. The defining form
$\sqrt{c^{2}-v^{2}}$ is used as primary because it evaluates at $v = c$ by
direct substitution, giving $v_{x_4} = 0$, whereas $c\,d\tau/dt$ and
$c/\gamma$ reach that value only as limits ($d\tau \to 0$ and
$\gamma \to \infty$ respectively). The massless case is therefore an
endpoint of one relation rather than a case requiring separate machinery.

At $v = 0$ the share is $v_{x_4} = c$: the entity directs the whole of the
expansion into $x_{4}$, which is the content of
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} and the source of $E_0 = mc^2$. At
$v = c$ the share is $v_{x_4} = 0$: the entity directs the whole of it into
space, $X_{4}$ does not accumulate along its worldline, and it ages not at
all. Three statements must be kept apart. The coordinate rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the principle and holds at every event of
$M_{G}$, including every event a photon crosses --- what vanishes for a
photon is its share in the expansion, never the expansion itself. The
share $v_{x_4}$ is worldline-dependent and bounded by $c$. The Lorentzian
component $dx_{4}/d\tau = ic\gamma$ is a chain-rule consequence, unbounded
as $v \to c$, and undefined on null worldlines, where the affinely
parameterised null tangent replaces it
(Remark [4.2A](#rmk:coordinate-time-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:coordinate-time-budget"}).
:::

::: {#lem:QMT4-channelA-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 4.3** (Algebraic Channel proof of QM T4). *The rest-frame angular
frequency of a massive particle's wavefunction equals
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: Rest energy from four-velocity budget.** By
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} (the four-velocity budget at
rest), a massive particle at spatial rest has its entire four-velocity
budget in the $x_{4}$-direction: $u^\mu = (c, \mathbf{0})$ with
$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ (signature $(-,+,+,+)$). The four-momentum is
$P^\mu = mu^\mu = (mc, \mathbf{0})$, with temporal component
$E_0/c = P^0 = mc$, hence $$E_0 = mc^2.$$ This is the rest-frame energy
of the particle, derived from the $x_{4}$-advance rate $c$ of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

**Step 2: Planck--Einstein at the rest state.** By
Theorem [3.1](#thm:QMT3){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT3"}
(Planck--Einstein, Algebraic Channel:
Lemmas [3.3](#lem:Hhat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:Hhat-generator"}
and [3.4](#lem:energy-phase){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:energy-phase"}), every quantum entity in a stationary
energy eigenstate has $E = \hbar\omega$ where $\omega$ is the angular
frequency of its temporal phase. The rest-frame energy eigenstate exists
because the rest-frame Hamiltonian has eigenvalue $E_0 = mc^2$ on the
rest state --- equivalently, the rest-frame wavefunction is
$\psi_{\mathrm{rest}}(\tau) = A\,e^{-iE_0\tau/\hbar}$ with proper time
$\tau$.

**Step 3: Compton frequency.** Applying the Planck--Einstein relation at
the rest state:
$$E_0 = mc^2 = \hbar\,\omega_C, \qquad \text{equivalently} \qquad \omega_C = \frac{mc^2}{\hbar}.$$
The angular frequency $\omega_C$ is the *Compton angular frequency* of
the particle, named after the empirical Compton scattering relation that
exhibited the same length scale $\lambda_C = h/(mc) = 2\pi c/\omega_C$.

**Step 4: Wigner-Casimir identifies $m$ uniquely.** By QA6 (Wigner
classification of irreducible massive Poincaré representations), the
mass-Casimir $P^\mu P_\mu = -m^2 c^2$ is the unique invariant labelling
the irreducible representation. Hence $m$ is uniquely determined by the
representation, and so is $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$. The Compton frequency
is therefore an invariant attribute of the particle, not a
frame-dependent quantity.

**Step 5: Algebraic Channel characterisation.** The derivation uses the
four-velocity budget (a kinematic theorem of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$),
Stone's theorem via Theorem [3.1](#thm:QMT3){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT3"} (QA2), and Wigner classification (QA6) --- all
algebraic-symmetry inputs. No Sphere-geometric machinery appears; the
proof is Algebraic Channel, derivationally disjoint from the Geometric Channel
Sphere-phase route of
Lemma [4.4](#lem:QMT4-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT4-channelB-proof"}. ◻
:::

### Disjointness audit

**Geometric Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, Sphere phase accumulation,
$S = -mc^2\int d\tau$ (relativistic action via Lagrangian theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), action-per-cycle
(Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:62"}).

**Algebraic Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, four-velocity budget
(Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"}), $E_0 = mc^2$, Planck--Einstein
(QM T3 Algebraic Channel), Wigner mass-Casimir (QA6).

**Intersection:** $\{(\mathrm{McP}), \omega_C = mc^2/\hbar\}$. The
four-velocity-budget calculation does not appear in Geometric Channel; the
Sphere-phase derivation does not invoke Wigner classification.
*Disjointness verified.*

### Empirical anchor

The Compton effect, measured by Compton in 1923 [@Compton1923],
established $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ for the electron via the X-ray
wavelength shift $\Delta\lambda = (h/m_e c)(1 - \cos\theta)$. The
numerical value $\lambda_C = h/(m_e c) = 2.426\,\text{pm}$ is the
Compton wavelength of the electron. Higher-mass species (proton,
neutron) have been independently confirmed. The cross-species
mass-independence test of QA1 (the universal-rate clause) --- that every
species couples to $x_{4}$-expansion with the same fundamental rate,
modulated only by $m$ --- is a falsifiable prediction of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ tested to $\sim 10^{-20}$ at Planck-scale
$\Omega$ in the MGT modulation framework
(Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT22"}).

## QM T5: The Rest-Mass Phase Factor {#ch:rest-mass-phase}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial
three. Throughout this chapter, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ refers to this
principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: (i) *invariance* --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the
expansion is isotropic in the spatial three, with the set of events
reachable from $p$ in proper time $\tau$ being a 2-sphere of radius
$c\tau$; (iii) *monotonicity* --- the integral curve is strictly
monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of $x_4$-advance; (iv)
*Lorentz consistency* --- the structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on
$M_{G}$; (v) *global validity* --- $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at
every event of $M_{G}$. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ (Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the central fact.

### Statement

::: {#thm:QMT5 .theorem}
**Theorem 5.1** (QM T5: Rest-mass phase factor). *The rest-frame matter
wavefunction of a particle of rest mass $m$ has the form
$$\psi_{\mathrm{rest}}(\tau) \;=\; A\,\exp(-imc^2\tau/\hbar),
\label{eq:rest-mass-phase}$$ where $\tau$ is the rest-frame proper time
and $A$ is a normalization constant (depending on spatial position in
the rest frame, but not on $\tau$).*

*This is Theorem 64 (Geometric Channel) and Theorem 87 (Algebraic Channel) of
[@Syn-2026]. The $i$ in the exponent traces directly to the $i$ in
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$: it is the perpendicularity marker of $x_{4}$,
propagated through the mere integrated kinematic shadow $x_{4}= ict$ of
the dynamical principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (Remark
[4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) into the rest-frame phase.*
:::

### Geometric Channel derivation: Direct integration of the Sphere phase {#sec:QMT5-channelB}

::: {#lem:QMT5-channelB-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 5.3** (Geometric Channel proof of QM T5). *Direct integration of the
McGucken Sphere phase along the rest-frame worldline gives
[\[eq:rest-mass-phase\]](#eq:rest-mass-phase){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:rest-mass-phase"}.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has six steps establishing the rest-mass
phase factor as direct integration of the McGucken-Sphere Compton phase
along the rest-frame worldline.

**Step 1: Phase accumulation rate from QMT4 Geometric Channel.** By
Theorem [4.1](#thm:QMT4){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT4"}
(Compton coupling, Geometric Channel), the rest-frame McGucken-Sphere phase
accumulates at angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ per unit proper
time. The phase rate is therefore
$$\frac{d\theta}{d\tau} = -\omega_C = -\frac{mc^2}{\hbar},$$ where the
negative sign tracks the convention $\psi \sim e^{-i\omega\tau}$ for
positive-energy matter (the opposite sign $+\omega_C$ corresponds to
antimatter, treated in QM T21).

**Step 2: Integrate along the rest-frame worldline.** Starting from
initial phase $\theta(0) = 0$ at proper time $\tau = 0$, integrate from
$0$ to $\tau$:
$$\theta(\tau) = \int_0^\tau\frac{d\theta}{d\tau'}\,d\tau' = \int_0^\tau (-\omega_C)\,d\tau' = -\omega_C\tau = -\frac{mc^2\tau}{\hbar}.$$
The accumulated phase grows linearly in proper time.

**Step 3: Form of the wavefunction.** The McGucken-Sphere wavefront
amplitude at proper time $\tau$ is the initial amplitude $A$ multiplied
by the accumulated phase factor:
$$\psi_{\mathrm{rest}}(\tau) = A\,e^{i\theta(\tau)} = A\,e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar},$$
which is
exactly [\[eq:rest-mass-phase\]](#eq:rest-mass-phase){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:rest-mass-phase"}. This is the rest-frame wavefunction of
a massive particle.

**Step 4: The $i$ traces to $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the chain-rule
mechanism.** The complex-exponential structure descends from Geometric Channel
inputs alone. The integrated kinematic shadow of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at the
rest-frame worldline is $x_{4}(\tau) = ic\tau$, so
$\tau = x_{4}/(ic) = -i\,x_{4}/c$. Substituting into
$\theta(\tau) = -\omega_C\tau$ of Step 2 expresses the phase as a function
of the advance itself:
$$\theta \;=\; -\omega_C\left(\frac{-i\,x_{4}}{c}\right) \;=\; +\,\frac{i\omega_C}{c}\,x_{4},$$
so the phase per unit $x_{4}$-advance is the matter-specific rate
$$\frac{d\theta}{dx_{4}} \;=\; \frac{i\omega_C}{c} \;=\; -\frac{\omega_C}{ic},$$
which is imaginary. Multiplying by the advance $x_{4}= ic\tau$, itself
imaginary, returns the phase angle
$$\frac{d\theta}{dx_{4}}\cdot x_{4} \;=\; \frac{i\omega_C}{c}\cdot ic\tau \;=\; i^2\,\omega_C\tau \;=\; -\omega_C\tau,$$
in agreement with Steps 1--3. The geometric reading: the rate at which
phase accumulates per unit $x_{4}$ is imaginary because the advance it
is measured against is the perpendicular one that the marker $i$ of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ picks out (C2); the product of the two
imaginary factors is the real, negative phase angle carried by
$e^{-i\omega_C\tau}$. The single $i$ of the principle enters twice --- once
in the rate and once in the coordinate --- and the exponential records
their product.

**Step 5: Theorem 42 classification.** The $i$ in the rest-mass phase
factor is mechanism (a) of
Theorem [9.21](#thm:twelve-i){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:twelve-i"}: the chain-rule-mechanism image of the
McGucken-Principle $i$. Theorem 42 of [@MG-Ontic-2026] catalogues twelve
canonical insertions of $i$ in quantum theory and proves that all twelve
are the suppression-map image of the single $i$ in
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via three mechanisms (chain-rule,
signature-change, contour-integration). The rest-mass phase factor is
the chain-rule case.

**Step 6: Geometric Channel characterisation.** The derivation uses only
McGucken-Sphere construction (QB1), Compton-phase accumulation
(Theorem [4.1](#thm:QMT4){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT4"}
Geometric Channel), and direct worldline integration. No Stone's theorem, no
Wigner classification, no abstract algebraic-representation machinery is
invoked; the entire structure is the geometric reading of Sphere-phase
accumulation along the rest-frame worldline. The proof is Geometric Channel,
derivationally disjoint from the Algebraic Channel route
(Lemma [5.2](#lem:QMT5-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT5-channelA-proof"}) which derives the same equation
via Stone's theorem applied to time-translation invariance and the
rest-frame energy eigenvalue $mc^2$. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem [5.1](#thm:QMT5){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT5"}.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The theorem asserts the rest-mass phase factor:
a massive particle at spatial rest has wavefunction
$\psi_{\mathrm{rest}}(\tau) = A\,e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}$. We establish

**Step 2: Geometric Channel derivation

**Step 3: Derivational disjointness of the two channels.** Algebraic Channel uses

for relativistic Dirac particles. ◻

### Algebraic Channel derivation: Stone's theorem applied to the rest-frame Hamiltonian {#sec:QMT5-channelA}

::: {#lem:QMT5-channelA-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 5.2** (Algebraic Channel proof of QM T5). *The rest-frame wavefunction
[\[eq:rest-mass-phase\]](#eq:rest-mass-phase){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:rest-mass-phase"} satisfies the time-evolution equation
$i\hbar\,\partial_\tau\psi_{\mathrm{rest}} = E_0\,\psi_{\mathrm{rest}} = mc^2\,\psi_{\mathrm{rest}}$,
and is the unique stationary energy eigenstate of the rest-frame
Hamiltonian.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: Apply Stone's theorem.** By
Lemma [3.3](#lem:Hhat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:Hhat-generator"} (Stone applied to time translation), the
time-evolution operator in the rest frame is
$$\hat{U}(\tau) \;=\; \exp\!\left(-\frac{i\tau\hat{H}}{\hbar}\right),$$
with $\hat{H}$ self-adjoint on a dense domain. (In the rest frame, the
worldline parameter is proper time $\tau$; in the lab frame, it is lab
time $t$; here we work in the rest frame so $t = \tau$.)

**Step 2: Energy eigenstate at rest.** By
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} (rest-frame four-velocity budget),
the rest energy is $E_0 = mc^2$. The rest-frame Hamiltonian's eigenstate
corresponding to this eigenvalue, $\hat{H}\phi_0 = mc^2\,\phi_0$, when
propagated by $\hat{U}(\tau)$, evolves as
$$\psi_0(\tau) \;=\; \hat{U}(\tau)\phi_0 \;=\; e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}\,\phi_0.$$
Setting $A := \phi_0$ (the rest-frame spatial profile), we obtain
$\psi_{\mathrm{rest}}(\tau) = A\,e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}$, which is
[\[eq:rest-mass-phase\]](#eq:rest-mass-phase){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:rest-mass-phase"}.

**Step 3: Uniqueness up to phase / normalization.** The energy
eigenstate at eigenvalue $mc^2$ in the rest frame is unique up to
overall scale, by QA6 (the massive irreducible representation of the
Poincaré group at the mass $m$ has a unique rest-frame ground state). So
[\[eq:rest-mass-phase\]](#eq:rest-mass-phase){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:rest-mass-phase"} is unique up to the overall $A$.

**Step 4: The $i$ in the exponent is the perpendicularity marker.** The
$i$ in $e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}$ comes from the $-i\tau\hat{H}/\hbar$ in
$\hat{U}(\tau)$, which in turn comes from Stone's theorem requirement
that the generator be self-adjoint (real eigenvalues) while the
exponentiation be unitary (norm-preserving). The factor $i$ converts a
real generator (energy operator) to a phase (complex exponent), and the
appearance of $i$ here is, via
Lemma [3.3](#lem:Hhat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:Hhat-generator"} Step 3, the same $i$ as in
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. Carrying the chain rule through explicitly:
the principle gives $\partial_t = ic\,\partial_{x_{4}}$, so the generator
expressed in $x_{4}$ is
$$\hat{H} \;=\; i\hbar\,\partial_t \;=\; i\hbar\,(ic\,\partial_{x_{4}}) \;=\; -\hbar c\,\partial_{x_{4}},$$
and the evolution operator is
$$\hat{U}(\tau) \;=\; \exp\!\left(-\frac{i\tau\hat{H}}{\hbar}\right) \;=\; \exp\!\left(+\,ic\tau\,\partial_{x_{4}}\right),$$
which acts as $\psi(x_{4}) \mapsto \psi(x_{4} + ic\tau)$: a translation of
the fourth coordinate by $ic\tau$.

That translation is the integrated principle itself, since
$x_{4}(t + \tau) - x_{4}(t) = ic\tau$
(Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}). Time evolution over $\tau$ and
$x_{4}$-advance over $\tau$ are therefore the same operation written in
two coordinates, and the $i$ appearing in the exponent is the $i$ of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ rather than a feature of either chart: it is
present in both readings, and the change of coordinate moves it between
the generator and the shift without removing it. The perpendicularity
marker of C2 is what makes the shift imaginary, and it is what makes the
evolution a phase rotation rather than a real translation.

This is case (a) of Theorem 42 of [@MG-Ontic-2026]: the
$\sigma$-chain-rule mechanism that transports $i$ from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ into the time-evolution exponent. ◻
:::

### The role of $i$ as perpendicularity marker

::: remark
*Remark 5.4* (Frobenius-free identification of $i$). The complex unit
$i$ in
[\[eq:rest-mass-phase\]](#eq:rest-mass-phase){reference-type="eqref"

reference="lem:algebra-is-C"}), without invocation of Frobenius's 1878

perpendicularity marker of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, transported to the
wavefunction via Stone's theorem (Algebraic Channel) or via direct Sphere-phase

Theorem 42 of [@MG-Ontic-2026] catalogues twelve canonical insertions of

**Geometric Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, Sphere construction,

### Empirical anchor

The rest-mass phase factor is the foundation of all matter-wave phase
interferometry. Direct confirmation:

-   Cesium-atom interferometry (Müller, Peters & Chu 2010, *Nature*
    **463**, 926) reports a gravitational phase shift read as
    Compton-frequency cycling of cesium atoms at
    $\omega_C^{Cs} = m_{Cs}c^2/\hbar$. The interpretation is contested:
    Wolf, Blanchet, Bordé, Reynaud, Salomon & Cohen-Tannoudji (2010,
    *Nature* **467**, E1) argue that the measurement is sensitive to
    photon recoil rather than to the gravitational redshift, with a
    reply from Müller, Peters & Chu in the same issue. The experiment is
    cited here as the most directly relevant measurement rather than as
    settled confirmation; the uncontested support for the rest-mass
    phase factor is carried by the two interferometry results below;

-   Neutron interferometry (Werner et al. 1979) confirms the
    gravitational and inertial phase shifts via the same Compton-phase
    mechanism;

-   Molecular interferometry up to $\sim 25\,\text{kDa}$ (Fein et
    al. 2019 [@Fein2019]) confirms the cross-species $m$-scaling of the
    rest-mass phase.

The cross-species mass-independence is the falsifiable prediction of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$'s universal-rate clause (QA1): the same
$(\varepsilon, \Omega)$ modulation in the McGucken--Compton framework
must apply to all matter species. Current bounds:
$\varepsilon \lesssim 10^{-20}$ at Planck-scale $\Omega$.

### Conceptual elevation: rest-mass phase as physical oscillation, not gauge freedom {#sec:rest-mass-physical-vs-gauge}

::: {#rmk:rest-mass-physical-oscillation .remark}
*Remark 5.5* (The rest-mass phase as physical oscillation:
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reading vs. standard QFT gauge reading;
[@MG-Compton-2026] §2). A sharp conceptual distinction separates the
standard quantum-field-theory reading of the rest-mass phase factor
$e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}$ from its McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reading.

*Standard QFT (quantum field theory) reading.* The global phase
$e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}$ multiplying every wavefunction component is a
$U(1)$ gauge freedom with no direct physical significance. Observable
predictions depend only on relative phases between wavefunction
components or on phase differences accumulated between distinct paths
(as in interference experiments). The absolute global phase, including
its rest-mass-Compton-rate winding, can be redefined freely by an
arbitrary $U(1)$ rotation $\psi \to e^{i\alpha}\psi$, and all
measurement outcomes are invariant. In this reading, the Compton
frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is a calculational artefact of the
proper-time exponential, not a physically oscillating quantity.

*McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reading.* The global phase $e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}$ is
elevated to a physical oscillation driven by the advancing $x_{4}$. By
Theorem [5.1](#thm:QMT5){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT5"}, the
phase advance at rate $\omega_C$ is the direct Geometric Channel reading of the
integrated kinematic shadow $x_{4}= ic\tau$ of the McGucken Principle: the
particle's worldline is carried by $x_{4}$-expansion at rate $c$, and
the rest-frame phase records the angular progression of $x_{4}$ along
the worldline. The phase is therefore not gauge but a real geometric
oscillation of the matter wavefront on the McGucken Sphere, with its
rate set by the species' rest mass and the universal McGucken constants
$c$ and $\hbar$.

This conceptual elevation has three consequences:

1.  *Compton coupling becomes natural.* If the rest-mass phase is a
    physical oscillation rather than gauge, then matter naturally
    couples to any modulation of $x_{4}$-expansion through this
    oscillation. The Compton coupling proposal of [@MG-Compton-2026]
    (formalised as Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT22"}) is the simplest realisation: a small
    modulation $\varepsilon\cos(\Omega\tau)$ of $x_{4}$'s monotonic
    advance produces a matter response proportional to
    $\varepsilon\cdot mc^2$ at frequency $\Omega$ in the rest frame.

2.  *Compton-frequency decoherence becomes a mechanism.* If
    every massive particle physically oscillates at its Compton
    frequency, then environmental interactions at this frequency produce
    decoherence of superpositions of distinct mass states or distinct
    spatial configurations. This is the mechanism underlying
    Proposition [10.36](#prop:preferred-basis-compton){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:preferred-basis-compton"}: the preferred basis of
    macroscopic observers is selected by Compton-frequency coupling to
    the environment, with decoherence rate
    $\Gamma_{\mathrm{dec}} \sim \sum_i \omega_{C,i}\,g_{S,i}^2/\hbar$
    (Step 3 of that proof).

3.  *Mass-energy equivalence becomes geometric.* If the rest-mass phase
    rate $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is a real physical oscillation, then
    the rest energy $E_0 = \hbar\omega_C = mc^2$ is the geometric
    content of the McGucken-Sphere cycling rate. Einstein's $E = mc^2$
    is, in this reading, the statement that mass-energy is the rate at
    which the McGucken-Sphere wavefront cycles at rest, transported
    through Planck's relation $E = \hbar\omega$ --- itself a theorem of
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
    (Theorem [3.1](#thm:QMT3){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT3"}).

The conceptual elevation has the role of a unifying
commitment: the three downstream consequences listed above (Compton
coupling, Compton-frequency decoherence, geometric mass-energy
equivalence) become mutually consistent and grounded in a single
physical oscillation common to all matter species, with the role of a
purely interpretive choice replaced by the role of the foundation underlying the Compton coupling
Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT22"},
the preferred-basis
Proposition [10.36](#prop:preferred-basis-compton){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:preferred-basis-compton"}, and the arrow-of-time
Theorem [12.18](#thm:five-arrows-of-time){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:five-arrows-of-time"}.
:::

::: {#rmk:physical-vs-gauge-commitment .remark}
*Remark 5.6* (The choice of physical vs gauge as a theoretical
commitment). The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reading of the rest-mass phase as
physical is a *theoretical commitment of the McGucken framework*, not a
forced consequence of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ alone. Standard QFT,
treating the phase as gauge, is internally consistent and reproduces
every observable prediction of conventional quantum mechanics. The
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework departs from this reading by elevating the phase to a
physical oscillation, and the empirical content of this departure is
precisely the Compton coupling
Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT22"}
and its three experimental tests
(Section [22.7](#sec:compton-experimental-tests){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:compton-experimental-tests"}): zero-temperature residual
diffusion, cross-species mass-independence, and Compton-frequency
spectroscopic sidebands. A successful detection of these signatures
would establish the physical reading; a confirmed null result at
improved precision would either rule out the specific Compton-coupling
ansatz or, at sufficient precision, rule out the physical reading
altogether (forcing return to the gauge interpretation). The McGucken
framework is therefore experimentally distinguishable from standard QFT
at the level of the rest-mass-phase status.
:::

## QM T6: Wave--Particle Duality {#ch:wave-particle}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial
three. Throughout this chapter, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ refers to this
principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: (i) *invariance* --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the
expansion is isotropic in the spatial three, with the set of events
reachable from $p$ in proper time $\tau$ being a 2-sphere of radius
$c\tau$; (iii) *monotonicity* --- the integral curve is strictly
monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of $x_4$-advance; (iv)
*Lorentz consistency* --- the structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on
$M_{G}$; (v) *global validity* --- $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at
every event of $M_{G}$. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ (Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the central fact.

The textbook tradition presents wave--particle duality as an
interpretive puzzle ("how can it be both?"). Bohr's complementarity
principle treats the two as mutually exclusive descriptions invoked in
different measurement contexts. In the McGucken framework, the duality
has the reading of a theorem of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$: the
same McGucken Sphere $S_p$ has two readings (apex/source
and wavefront/extended), and the Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel derivation
chains read it twice. The duality has the role of a derived fact at the McGucken-Sphere level, with the role of an interpretive
paradox replaced by the role of a theorem with full proof.

### Statement

::: {#thm:QMT6 .theorem}
**Theorem 6.1** (QM T6: Wave--Particle Duality). *A quantum entity
has two simultaneously valid readings of the underlying
McGucken Sphere $S_p$:*

1.  **Wave reading.* The wavefunction $\psi$ on the 3-spatial slice
    $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ at lab time $t > t_p$ is an extended amplitude
    distribution on a 2-sphere of radius $c(t - t_p)$.*

2.  **Particle reading.* The Sphere apex at the source event $p$ is a
    sharply-localised spacetime point; measurement projection onto a
    single spatial location at $t > t_p$ produces a localised detection
    event.*

*The two readings are the position-representation expansion
$\psi = \int \psi(\mathbf{x})\lvert \mathbf{x} \rangle d^3x$ and the
momentum-representation expansion
$\psi = \int \tilde\psi(\mathbf{k})\lvert \mathbf{k} \rangle d^3k$ of
the same Hilbert-space vector. They are Fourier-conjugate, and both
descend from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. This is Theorem 65 (Algebraic Channel)
and Theorem 88 (Geometric Channel) of [@Syn-2026].*
:::

::: {#rmk:electron-as-sphere .remark}
*Remark 6.A* (The electron as McGucken Sphere expansion: the
ontological identification under the dual-channel architecture). *The
wave-particle structure of Theorem
[6.1](#thm:QMT6){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT6"} has a
sharpened ontological reading. The electron, considered as a physical
entity in spacetime sourced at an emission event $p = (\mathbf{x}_p,
t_p)$, has the role of the $+ic$-oriented McGucken Sphere
$\Sphere_p^+(t)$ expanding from $p$ at the rate $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$,
with definite radius $c(t-t_p)$, definite area $4\pi c^2(t-t_p)^2$, and
intrinsic Compton phase content $\omega_C \cdot (t - t_p)$ with
$\omega_C = m_e c^2/\hbar \approx 7.76 \times 10^{20}\,\mathrm{rad/s}$.
The Sphere is a real geometric object on the four-manifold $M_G$: a
2-sphere at every coordinate time $t > t_p$, with the Sphere surface
carrying the Compton-phase content from $p$ uniformly across all
spatial directions by the $SO(3)$-symmetry of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ at the source event.*

*The wave-character of the electron in Theorem
[6.1](#thm:QMT6){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT6"} has the
role of the Sphere's wavefront content: the extended
amplitude distribution on the 2-sphere at each $t > t_p$ is the
Geometric Channel description of the Sphere expanding outward in real space.
The particle-character has the role of the head-on
$x_4$-collision event at a definite spacetime point: when the Sphere
wavefront reaches a detector configuration, the head-on $x_4$-collision
between the propagating Sphere and the detector atom's Sphere
3-localizes the interaction at that event (Theorem
[\[thm:born-as-collision\]](#thm:born-as-collision){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-as-collision"} of
Chapter [\[ch:born\]](#ch:born){reference-type="ref" reference="ch:born"}),
producing the localised detection outcome that Algebraic Channel reports as a
position-eigenvalue registration. Both characters --- wave and particle
--- are simultaneously real readings of the underlying Sphere: the wave
character is the Sphere's expansion through real space, and the
particle character is the localisation event at head-on Sphere
collisions. The orthodox wave-particle "paradox" --- the question of
how the electron can be both a wave and a particle --- dissolves under
this identification: the electron is always the $+ic$-oriented McGucken
Sphere; the wave aspect is the Sphere's wavefront expansion in real
space; the particle aspect is the head-on-collision localisation at
detection events.*

*This identification is the framework's foundational ontological claim
about matter, and it is a substantive physical claim with empirical
content beyond a reinterpretation of formalism: the Sphere has
definite radius, definite area, definite Compton frequency, and
definite $+ic$ orientation at every retarded time $t - t_p$ from the
source event, propagating outward through spacetime as a real
geometric structure. The orthodox 'particle' reading of the electron
as a classical point-particle with deterministic worldline is the
short-wavelength limit of this geometry, recovered in the eikonal
limit $\lambda_C/L \to 0$ where $L$ is the characteristic geometric
scale; the orthodox 'wave' reading of the wavefunction $\psi$ as a
calculational amplitude on configuration space is the
operator-algebraic encoding through the suppression map $\sigma$ of
the same Sphere. Both readings hold simultaneously because both are
genuine readings of the same geometric object, and the McGucken
framework supplies the framework in which both are derivations from
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$.*
:::

### Geometric Channel derivation: Apex and wavefront as two readings of the McGucken Sphere {#sec:QMT6-channelB}

::: {#lem:sphere-apex-wavefront .lemma}
**Lemma 6.6** (The McGucken Sphere admits a apex/wavefront
duality). *For every source event $p \in M_{G}$, the McGucken Sphere
$S_p$ has two simultaneous geometric readings:*

1.  *The **apex** at the source event $p = (\mathbf{x}_p, t_p)$, a
    sharply-localised spacetime point in $M_{G}$;*

2.  *The **wavefront**
    $M^{+}_{p}(t) = \{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t - t_p)\}$
    at lab time $t > t_p$, a 2-sphere of finite radius in
    $\mathbb{R}^3$.*

*Both readings are determined uniquely by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at
the source event: the apex by the source-event location, the wavefront
by the principle's clause that $x_{4}$ expands at rate $c$ from $p$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* **Step 1: The Sphere is the locus of forward $x_{4}$-advance
from a single event.** By the construction in
§[9.2](#sec:hilbert-mp-and-sigma){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:hilbert-mp-and-sigma"} (the McGucken Sphere as the
spatial trace of the principle's spherical $x_{4}$-expansion sourced at
$p$), the Sphere $S_p$ contains exactly two distinguished geometric
features:

\(a\) The *source event* $p$ at which $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is
activated. This is a single point in $M_{G}$ with definite coordinates
$(\mathbf{x}_p, t_p)$. The source event is sharply localised --- it has
no spatial extent in $\mathbb{R}^3$ at lab time $t_p$ (where the
wavefront has zero radius and reduces to the single point
$\mathbf{x}_p$).

\(b\) The *wavefront* at $t > t_p$, a 2-sphere of radius $c(t - t_p)$,
an extended object in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The wavefront has spatial extent
$c(t-t_p)$ --- explicitly, $4\pi c^2 (t-t_p)^2$ surface area.

**Step 2: Both readings are forced by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.** The
principle $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at the event $p$ states that $x_{4}$
expands radially from $p$ at rate $c$. This single statement encodes (a)
the location of the source event (where the expansion begins) and (b)
the geometry of the wavefront (where the expansion has reached at any
later time). Neither reading is more fundamental than the other; they
are the two components of one principle application at one
event.

**Step 3: Reading (P) corresponds to the particle reading.** A
measurement projecting the wavefunction onto a single spatial location
at lab time $t$ is a measurement of the source-apex reading --- the
sharply-localised registration event corresponds to the source event of
a Sphere about to be sourced. Mathematically, this is the
position-representation reading of
Lemma [6.2](#lem:position-localized){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:position-localized"}.

**Step 4: Reading (W) corresponds to the wave reading.** The
wavefunction $\psi$ on $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ has amplitude defined over the
extended 2-sphere; its Fourier transform decomposes into spatial plane
waves of definite wavevector
(Lemma [2.5](#lem:plane-wave-limit){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:plane-wave-limit"}). Interference and diffraction effects
appear in any computation involving multiple wavefront cross-sections
(multiple slits, multiple measurement events). This is the wave reading
of Lemma [6.3](#lem:momentum-planewave){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:momentum-planewave"}.

**Step 5: Simultaneity.** The two readings (P) and (W) coexist in the
same Sphere $S_p$. They have the reading of two
simultaneously-present geometric slices of one underlying object
generated by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with the role of two distinct
objects replaced by the role of two projections of one
McGucken Sphere onto the apex-event and wavefront-locus respectively. ◻
:::


### The reception reading: the convergent conjugate flux at every event {#sec:convergent-flux}

Lemma [6.6](#lem:sphere-apex-wavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:sphere-apex-wavefront"} reads one Sphere at its apex and
at its wavefront. The present section reads one *event* against all the
Spheres that reach it. Both readings descend from the same clause: C5
generates a Sphere at every event, so an event is a source in one
reading and a reception point in the other, with no additional
postulate. Everything in this section is a consequence of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}; no result of
Chapter [9](#ch:hilbert-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:hilbert-theorem"} or later is used.

::: {#lem:reception-reading .lemma}
**Lemma 6.6A** (Reception reading: every event receives wavefronts from
every event of its past at rate $c$). *Let $E = (\mathbf{x}_E, t_E) \in
M_{G}$. For every event $p = (\mathbf{x}_p, t_p) \in M_{G}$ with
$t_p < t_E$ and $|\mathbf{x}_E - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t_E - t_p)$, the
event $E$ lies on the wavefront $M^{+}_{p}(t_E)$ of the McGucken Sphere
sourced at $p$. The set of such $p$ is the $2$-sphere of radius
$c(t_E - t_p)$ about $\mathbf{x}_E$ at each earlier time $t_p$, and the
wavefront through $E$ from each such $p$ arrives at $E$ with radial
speed $c$ directed inward toward $\mathbf{x}_E$. Consequently $E$ is
simultaneously the apex of its own Sphere, expanding outward at $+ic$,
and a reception point of a convergent family of wavefronts arriving at
$c$ from every spatial direction.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* **Step 1: Sphere generation at every event.** By C5 with
clause (v) of Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} (global validity), every event $p \in M_{G}$
sources a McGucken Sphere $S_p$, and by
Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:sphere"} its wavefront at lab time $t$ is
$M^{+}_{p}(t) = \{\mathbf{x} : |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t - t_p)\}$.
Generation is unconditional: it does not depend on what occupies $p$, by
clause (i) (invariance of the rate, independent of matter content).

**Step 2: Membership condition.** The event $E$ lies on
$M^{+}_{p}(t_E)$ exactly when $|\mathbf{x}_E - \mathbf{x}_p| =
c(t_E - t_p)$, which is the stated condition. For each fixed $t_p <
t_E$ the solution set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is the $2$-sphere of radius
$c(t_E - t_p)$ centred at $\mathbf{x}_E$. Every spatial direction
$\hat{u} \in S^2$ is represented on that $2$-sphere, and the family is
non-empty for every $t_p < t_E$.

**Step 3: Direction of arrival.** Along the ray from $\mathbf{x}_p$ to
$\mathbf{x}_E$, the wavefront radius grows as $c(t - t_p)$, so at $E$
the wavefront crosses $\mathbf{x}_E$ moving outward from $\mathbf{x}_p$
--- equivalently, moving toward $\mathbf{x}_E$ along the direction
$-\hat{u}$ where $\hat{u}$ points from $\mathbf{x}_E$ to
$\mathbf{x}_p$. Ranging over the $2$-sphere of Step 2, the arrival
directions at $E$ exhaust $S^2$.

**Step 4: Coexistence of the two readings.** By
Lemma [6.6](#lem:sphere-apex-wavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:sphere-apex-wavefront"} Step 5 the apex and wavefront
readings of a single Sphere coexist. Applying that lemma at $E$ to
$S_E$ gives the outward reading; applying it at $E$ to each $S_p$ of
Step 2 gives the inward readings. Both hold at $E$ at once. $\square$ ◻
:::

**McGucken-internal source of Lemma 6.6A**: C5 (Sphere generation at
every event); clause (i) (rate invariance, so generation does not
require matter at $p$); clause (ii) (spherical symmetry, so every
arrival direction occurs); clause (v) (global validity, so the family
is non-empty at every earlier time); C1 (rate $c$).

::: {#thm:convergent-flux-isotropy .theorem}
**Theorem 6.6B** (The convergent flux is isotropic and transfers no net
three-momentum). *Let $E \in M_{G}$ and let the convergent family of
Lemma [6.6A](#lem:reception-reading){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reception-reading"} arrive at $E$. The distribution of
arrival directions on $S^2$ is $SO(3)$-invariant about $\mathbf{x}_E$,
and the net three-momentum deposited at $E$ by the family vanishes.
Registration at $E$ therefore requires a breaking of that isotropy
rather than the mere presence of the flux.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: $SO(3)$-invariance of the arrival distribution.** By
clause (ii) of Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} the $x_{4}$-expansion at each source event
$p$ is isotropic, so the wavefront $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ carries no
distinguished direction. By C4 the same holds at every $p$ with the
same rate. For fixed $t_p$, the set of sources reaching $E$ is by
Lemma 6.6A the $2$-sphere of radius $c(t_E - t_p)$ centred at
$\mathbf{x}_E$, which is carried to itself by every rotation about
$\mathbf{x}_E$. The induced distribution of arrival directions on $S^2$
is therefore invariant under $SO(3)$ acting about $\mathbf{x}_E$.

**Step 2: Uniqueness of the invariant distribution.** The rotation group
$SO(3)$ acts transitively on $S^2$, and by Haar uniqueness on the
compact group $SO(3)$ the invariant probability measure on $S^2$ is
unique. The arrival distribution of Step 1 is therefore the uniform
measure $d\Omega/4\pi$.

**Step 3: Vanishing of the net three-momentum.** The momentum deposited
by an arrival from direction $\hat{u}$ is $-p(\hat{u})\,\hat{u}$ for a
scalar magnitude $p$ that is direction-independent by Step 1. The net
deposit is therefore proportional to
$$\int_{S^2} \hat{u}\;\frac{d\Omega}{4\pi} \;=\; \mathbf{0},$$
the vanishing following from the same $SO(3)$-invariance argument used
for the cross terms $g_{i4}$ in
Theorem [4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"} Step 2: the defining
three-dimensional representation of $SO(3)$ is irreducible and contains
no non-zero invariant vector. Hence the convergent flux transfers no net
three-momentum at $E$.

**Step 4: What a registration requires.** A non-zero deposit at $E$
requires the arrival distribution to depart from the uniform measure of
Step 2 --- that is, one incoming amplitude meeting the outward
expansion of $S_E$ head-on with weight exceeding the isotropic
background. The flux alone produces nothing; the coincidence does.
$\square$ ◻
:::

**McGucken-internal source of Theorem 6.6B**: clause (ii) (spherical
symmetry, giving the invariance); C4 (per-event universality, extending
it to every source); C5 (the family itself); Haar uniqueness on $SO(3)$
and Schur irreducibility as supporting machinery.

::: {#lem:reception-amplitude-falloff .lemma}
**Lemma 6.6C** (Amplitude falloff and finiteness of the received
amplitude). *The amplitude carried by the wavefront $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ at
radius $r = c(t - t_p)$ from its source scales as $r^{-1}$, so the
density carried scales as $r^{-2}$. The convergent family of
Lemma [6.6A](#lem:reception-reading){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reception-reading"} therefore deposits a finite density
at $E$ from each spherical shell of sources, and the inverse-square law
is the same statement.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: Area growth of the wavefront.** By clause (ii) the
expansion is isotropic, so the wavefront at parameter time $t$ is the
$2$-sphere of radius $r = c(t - t_p)$, of area $4\pi r^2$.

**Step 2: Conservation of the wavefront's total weight.** By
Theorem [6.6B](#thm:convergent-flux-isotropy){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:convergent-flux-isotropy"} Step 2 the wavefront carries
the $SO(3)$-invariant measure of total mass $1$, and by C1 the rate of
advance is the same at every event, so no weight is created or
destroyed as the wavefront expands. The weight per unit area is
therefore $\propto r^{-2}$.

**Step 3: Amplitude from density.** The density is the
forward--conjugate pairing of the amplitude with itself, which is
quadratic in the amplitude
(Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"} supplies the rank-$2$ character; the
present step uses only that the pairing is quadratic, which is visible
already from the two orientations $\pm ic$ of one advance). A density
scaling as $r^{-2}$ therefore comes from an amplitude scaling as
$r^{-1}$.

**Step 4: Finiteness at the reception point.** Sources at
$r \in [r, r + dr]$ from $\mathbf{x}_E$ occupy a shell of volume
$4\pi r^2\,dr$ and each contributes density $\propto r^{-2}$, so each
shell contributes a finite amount $\propto dr$ and the received density
is finite on any bounded interval of source distance. The $r^{-2}$
falloff of the density is the inverse-square law, obtained here from
clause (ii) and C1 rather than assumed. $\square$ ◻
:::

**McGucken-internal source of Lemma 6.6C**: clause (ii) (isotropy,
giving the $4\pi r^2$ area); C1 (rate invariance, giving weight
conservation along the advance); C5 (the wavefront whose weight is
conserved).

::: {#rmk:reception-is-psi-star .remark}
*Remark 6.6D* (The convergent family is the conjugate branch, and it is
present at every event). Chapter [9](#ch:hilbert-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:hilbert-theorem"} introduces the conjugate amplitude
$\psi^*$ as the same wavefront read at the opposite $x_{4}$-orientation
(Lemma [9.12](#lem:forward-conjugate){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:forward-conjugate"}), and the measurement chapter reads
a registration as the head-on meeting of a forward Sphere $\psi$ with a
conjugate Sphere $\psi^*$. Lemma 6.6A identifies what carries $\psi^*$
at a general event: the convergent family arriving at that event. Three
consequences follow, each a consequence of C4 rather than of any
laboratory arrangement.

First, $\psi^*$ is present at *every* event of $M_{G}$, not only where
an apparatus has been prepared. C4 states that the advance is the same
at every event with none privileged; a conjugate amplitude that existed
only at instrumented events would privilege those events, which C4
forbids. An apparatus selects and localises the coincidence; it does not
create the conjugate branch.

Second, the outward and inward readings coexist at every event without
any oscillation of the orientation in time. The entity's own advance
remains $+ic$ (C1 directional), and the inward arrivals are the
conjugate branch of other events' advances. No clause of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is weakened, so every result that descends from
the forward orientation --- the Spectrum Condition
(Theorem W.6), the strict Second Law, retarded over advanced
propagation, matter dominance --- stands unchanged.

Third, the bilinear form of the registration density has a two-sided
geometric reading at every event rather than only at detectors: the
outward factor is supplied by the event's own Sphere and the inward
factor by the convergent family, so $\psi^*\psi$ records a coincidence
of two Spheres that C5 puts at every event of $M_{G}$.
:::

::: {#lem:QMT6-channelB-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 6.7** (Geometric Channel proof of QM T6). *A quantum entity, modeled as
the matter wavefunction on a McGucken Sphere generated by
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, simultaneously has the wave reading and the
particle reading of that Sphere.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* **Step 1: Sphere has dual readings.** By
Lemma [6.6](#lem:sphere-apex-wavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:sphere-apex-wavefront"}, the McGucken Sphere $S_p$ admits
the apex/wavefront duality:

-   \(P\) The apex at source event $p = (\mathbf{x}_p, t_p)$ --- a
    sharply localised point in $M_{G}$;

-   \(W\) The wavefront $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ at lab time $t > t_p$ --- a
    2-sphere of finite radius $c(t-t_p)$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

Both readings are simultaneously present in the same geometric object
$S_p$.

**Step 2: Matter wavefunction inherits the duality.** The matter
wavefunction $\psi: M_{G}\to \mathbb{C}$ associated with $S_p$ encodes:
(i) the source-event location $p$ (the apex of the Sphere), via the
position-representation $\psi(\mathbf{x}_p, t_p)$ being sharply
localised at $\mathbf{x}_p$ at parameter time $t_p$; (ii) the wavefront
amplitude on $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ for $t > t_p$, an extended-amplitude
function on a 2-sphere of finite radius. The wavefunction itself is not
the carrier of the duality --- the underlying Sphere $S_p$ is. The
wavefunction inherits the duality from the geometric object on which it
is defined.

**Step 3: Particle reading (P) via apex.** A measurement projecting
$\psi$ onto a single spatial location at parameter time $t$ is
mathematically the position-representation reading: the wavefunction
value at a sharp spatial point. Geometrically, this is the apex reading
of the Sphere --- the source event of a Sphere about to be (re-)sourced
upon registration.
Lemma [19.4](#lem:QMT19-3D-projection){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT19-3D-projection"} confirms this identification: the
registration event is the 3D-projection of the 4D Sphere onto a single
point.

**Step 4: Wave reading (W) via wavefront.** A measurement involving
multiple wavefront cross-sections --- multiple slits, multiple
detectors, interference patterns --- is the wave-reading: the
wavefunction value over the extended wavefront $M^{+}_{p}(t)$.
Interference and diffraction effects arise from amplitude superposition
across the wavefront, exactly as in the classical Huygens treatment of
wave optics.

**Step 5: Simultaneity is.** The two readings (P) and (W)
coexist in the same Sphere $S_p$ and have the reading of two
simultaneously-present geometric slices of one underlying object
generated by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The role of two distinct objects
and the role of two alternative ontological categories are both replaced
by the role of two projections of the same McGucken Sphere
--- the apex-event reading (P) and the wavefront-locus reading (W) ---
both forced by clauses (i)+(ii) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} at the source event $p$. The textbook framing
of wave--particle duality as a paradox ("how can the electron be both a
wave and a particle?") misclassifies (P) and (W) as alternative
descriptions of disjoint phenomena; in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, the
readings are forced to coexist by the geometry of $S_p$, and the paradox
dissolves.

**Step 6: Geometric Channel characterisation.** The derivation uses only the
McGucken Sphere construction (QB1) and the apex/wavefront geometric
reading (QB2). No Stone's theorem, no Fourier transform, no Plancherel
theorem appears; this is Geometric Channel, derivationally disjoint from the
Algebraic Channel Fourier-conjugacy route of
Lemma [6.5](#lem:QMT6-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT6-channelA-proof"}. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem [6.1](#thm:QMT6){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT6"}.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The theorem asserts wave-particle duality: a quantum entity carries simultaneously a wave reading and a particle reading of its wavefunction. We establish this along both channels.

**Step 1: Algebraic Channel derivation
(Lemma [6.5](#lem:QMT6-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT6-channelA-proof"}).** The wave reading and the
particle reading have the reading of two Fourier-conjugate
decompositions of a single Hilbert-space vector
$\psi \in \mathcal{H}= L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. By
Lemma [6.2](#lem:position-localized){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:position-localized"}, the position eigenstates
$\{\lvert \mathbf{x} \rangle\}$ form an improper basis whose elements
are sharply localised events (P reading). By
Lemma [6.3](#lem:momentum-planewave){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:momentum-planewave"}, the momentum eigenstates
$\{\lvert \mathbf{p} \rangle\}$ form an improper basis whose elements
are extended plane waves (W reading). By
Lemma [6.4](#lem:fourier-conjugate){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:fourier-conjugate"}, both are complete bases for the same
Hilbert space, related by the unitary Fourier transform. Every
$\psi \in \mathcal{H}$ is expressible as both a P-expansion
($\psi = \int d^3\mathbf{x}\,\psi(\mathbf{x})\lvert \mathbf{x} \rangle$)
and a W-expansion
($\psi = \int d^3\mathbf{p}\,\tilde\psi(\mathbf{p})\lvert \mathbf{p} \rangle$).
The two readings have the role of two complete decompositions of the
same Hilbert-space object, with the role of alternative descriptions of
disjoint phenomena replaced by the role of representation-choices on one
underlying state.

**Step 2: Geometric Channel derivation
(Lemma [6.7](#lem:QMT6-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT6-channelB-proof"}).** The McGucken Sphere $S_p$ at
source event $p$ has two simultaneous geometric readings: the apex at
$p$ (sharply-localised source event in $M_{G}$) and the wavefront
$M^{+}_{p}(t)$ at lab time $t$ (extended 2-sphere of radius $c(t - t_p)$
in $\mathbb{R}^3$). Both readings are determined uniquely by
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at the source event: the apex by the
source-event location, the wavefront by the principle's clause that
$x_{4}$ expands at rate $c$ from $p$. The two readings are geometrically
inevitable, not interpretively chosen: a McGucken Sphere has both an
apex and a wavefront simultaneously.

**Step 3: Derivational disjointness of the two channels.** Algebraic Channel uses
Hilbert-space tensor structure (QA4), the spectral theorem on $\hat{q}$
and $\hat{p}$, the Plancherel theorem for Fourier completeness, and the
unitarity of the Fourier transform --- all algebraic-symmetry machinery.
Geometric Channel uses the McGucken-Sphere construction (QB1), the
apex/wavefront geometric reading (QB2), and the fact that a
