(clause (i), the principle holds with the same rate at every event); the
external potential breaks the spatial-translation invariance of the
*combined dynamics* but not of the principle. The spatial-translation
argument of Lemma [7.4](#lem:H-free){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:H-free"} Step 1 therefore does not extend in the presence
of $V$, and the conclusion $\hat{H}_{\mathrm{free}} = h(\hat{p})$ is
replaced by $\hat{H}= \hat{H}_{\mathrm{free}} + V(\hat{q})$.

However $V$ depends only on $\mathbf{x}$ and not on $t$ (by hypothesis:
the potential is time-independent), so the time-translation invariance
of Lemma [7.2](#lem:time-translation-unitary){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:time-translation-unitary"} is preserved. Hence the
abstract Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$ of
Lemma [7.3](#lem:hamiltonian-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:hamiltonian-generator"} continues to hold with the
modified Hamiltonian
$$\hat{H}\;=\; \hat{H}_{\mathrm{free}} + V(\hat{q}) \;=\; -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\,\nabla^2 + V(\mathbf{x}).$$

**Step 4: Self-adjointness of $\hat{H}$ under explicit hypotheses on
$V$.** The sum of two self-adjoint operators is not in general
self-adjoint without conditions on their domains and relative size. The
standard sufficient condition for the Schrödinger operator
$\hat{H}= -(\hbar^2/2m)\nabla^2 + V$ to be self-adjoint on a dense
domain in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is supplied by the Kato--Rellich theorem
(Reed--Simon [@ReedSimon1980] Vol. II, Theorem X.12):

*Kato--Rellich.* If $V = V_1 + V_2$ with $V_1 \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and
$V_2 \in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$, both real-valued, then
$\hat{H}= -(\hbar^2/2m)\nabla^2 + V$ is self-adjoint on the domain
$\mathcal{D}(\hat{H}) = \mathcal{D}(-\nabla^2) = H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ (the
second Sobolev space) and essentially self-adjoint on the Schwartz
subspace $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^3)$.

This covers the Coulomb potential
$V = -e^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0 |\mathbf{x}|)$ (decompose into
$L^2 + L^\infty$ by cutting off near the origin; the $L^2$ part captures
the singular behaviour, the $L^\infty$ part captures the tail), the
harmonic oscillator $V = m\omega^2|\mathbf{x}|^2/2$ (extended by
Reed--Simon Vol. II Theorem X.28 on operators bounded by polynomial
growth in $\mathbf{x}$), and smooth compactly-supported potentials. For
the formal derivation of the Schrödinger equation in the present
chapter, we take $V$ to be in this Kato class so that $\hat{H}$ is
self-adjoint on $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. The unbounded extensions to weaker
hypotheses (Kato class, Stummel class) are catalogued in Reed--Simon
[@ReedSimon1980] Vol. II Theorems X.15--X.20.

The Hamiltonian $\hat{H}= -(\hbar^2/2m)\nabla^2 + V(\mathbf{x})$ is
therefore a self-adjoint operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ under the
standard Kato-class hypotheses on $V$, generating a strongly continuous
unitary group $\hat{U}(s) = e^{-is\hat{H}/\hbar}$ via Stone's theorem,
and the abstract Schrödinger equation
$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$ holds on
$\mathcal{D}(\hat{H}) = H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#lem:QMT7-channelA-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 7.6** (Algebraic Channel proof of QM T7). *The Schrödinger equation
[\[eq:Schrodinger\]](#eq:Schrodinger){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:Schrodinger"} follows from
Lemmas [7.2](#lem:time-translation-unitary){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:time-translation-unitary"},
[7.3](#lem:hamiltonian-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:hamiltonian-generator"},
[7.4](#lem:H-free){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:H-free"}, and
[7.5](#lem:H-potential){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:H-potential"}.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The Schrödinger equation
[\[eq:Schrodinger\]](#eq:Schrodinger){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:Schrodinger"} arises as the conclusion of a six-step
Algebraic Channel chain.

**Step 1: Time-translation invariance.** By
Lemma [7.2](#lem:time-translation-unitary){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:time-translation-unitary"}, the time-translation
invariance of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ produces a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group $\hat{U}(s)$ on $\mathcal{H}$: the principle
takes the same form at every event (clause P1 of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), in particular at every event along the
timelike axis, hence translation by $s$ commutes with the principle.
Probability conservation makes the translation unitary on $\mathcal{H}$.

**Step 2: Stone-theorem generator.** By
Lemma [7.3](#lem:hamiltonian-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:hamiltonian-generator"} (Stone's theorem,
Theorem [3.6](#thm:stone){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:stone"},
applied to $\hat{U}(s)$), the unitary group has a unique self-adjoint
generator $\hat{H}$:
$$\hat{U}(s) = \exp(-is\hat{H}/\hbar), \qquad i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi.$$
This is the abstract Schrödinger equation, valid for any quantum system
with a time-translation-invariant principle.

**Step 3: Free Hamiltonian by spatial-translation co-symmetry.** By
Lemma [7.4](#lem:H-free){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:H-free"},
the spatial-translation invariance of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (also
clause P1, applied to spatial axes) commutes with time-translation in
the free case, giving $[\hat{H}, \hat{p}_j] = 0$ for $j = 1, 2, 3$. By
the joint spectral theorem on commuting self-adjoint operators,
$\hat{H}$ is a function of $\hat{p}$; the non-relativistic
Wigner-Casimir dispersion forces
$\hat{H}_{\mathrm{free}} = \hat{p}^2/(2m) = -\hbar^2\nabla^2/(2m)$ on
the spatial slice.

**Step 4: External potential via minimal coupling.** By
Lemma [7.5](#lem:H-potential){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:H-potential"}, an external scalar potential
$V(\mathbf{x})$ enters as a multiplication operator on
$L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, extending the free Hamiltonian to
$\hat{H}= -\hbar^2\nabla^2/(2m) + V(\mathbf{x})$. The potential breaks
spatial-translation invariance but preserves time-translation
invariance, so Step 2 still applies with the modified $\hat{H}$.

**Step 5: Combine.** Substituting the explicit form of $\hat{H}$ into
the abstract Schrödinger equation gives
$$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \left[-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\nabla^2 + V(\mathbf{x})\right]\psi,$$
which is exactly
equation [\[eq:Schrodinger\]](#eq:Schrodinger){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:Schrodinger"}.

**Step 6: Algebraic Channel characterisation.** The derivation uses Stone's
theorem (QA2), Wigner classification (QA6), and minimal coupling (QA7)
--- all algebraic-symmetry inputs. No Sphere-geometric machinery
(Huygens iteration, Compton phase, path-integral kernel) appears. The
proof is Algebraic Channel, derivationally disjoint from the Geometric Channel route of
Lemmas [7.7](#lem:sphere-and-huygens){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:sphere-and-huygens"}--[7.11](#lem:varepsilon-expansion){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:varepsilon-expansion"}, which derives the same equation
from iterated McGucken-Sphere propagation. ◻
:::

### Disjointness audit {#sec:QMT7-disjointness}

**Algebraic Channel intermediate machinery:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (clause:
time-translation invariance); Stone's theorem on unitary groups
(Lemma [7.2](#lem:time-translation-unitary){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:time-translation-unitary"}); QA2; Hamiltonian as Stone
generator (Lemma [7.3](#lem:hamiltonian-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:hamiltonian-generator"}); free Hamiltonian by spectral
theorem on commuting $\hat{p}_j$
(Lemma [7.4](#lem:H-free){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:H-free"});
Wigner classification of non-relativistic limit; QA6; minimal coupling
for external potential
(Lemma [7.5](#lem:H-potential){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:H-potential"}); QA7.

**Geometric Channel intermediate machinery:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (clauses:
rate $c$, spherical symmetry, principle applies at every event);
McGucken Sphere generation
(Lemma [7.7](#lem:sphere-and-huygens){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:sphere-and-huygens"}); QB1, QB2; classical action of
straight-line path
(Lemma [7.8](#lem:compton-phase-wavelet){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:compton-phase-wavelet"}); Compton-phase rule from
Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:62"};
Fresnel-integral evaluation in
Lemma [7.10](#lem:gaussian-normalization){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:gaussian-normalization"}; first-order
$\varepsilon$-expansion with Gaussian moments
(Lemma [7.11](#lem:varepsilon-expansion){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:varepsilon-expansion"}).

**Intersection:** $\{(\mathrm{McP}), \text{Schr\"odinger equation}\}$.
Stone's theorem appears in Algebraic Channel but not in Geometric Channel. The McGucken
Sphere construction appears in Geometric Channel but not in Algebraic Channel. The
factor $\hbar$ in both routes comes from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via
Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:62"} (action
per Sphere cycle); this is the principle's contribution, not an
additional axiom shared by the channels. *Disjointness verified.*

### First-order in time, second-order in space: the geometric asymmetry {#sec:schrodinger-asymmetry}

::: {#rmk:schrodinger-asymmetry .remark}
*Remark 7.13* (First-order time / second-order space asymmetry of the
Schrödinger equation as a geometric fact; [@MG-PathIntegral-2026] §9
Proposition 9.1). The Schrödinger equation
$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$ with
$\hat{H}= -(\hbar^2/2m)\nabla^2 + V$ has a asymmetry that
appears in no other major equation of physics: a single time derivative
on the left, a Laplacian (second spatial derivative) on the right. The
wave equation has $\partial_t^2$ matching $\nabla^2$; the heat equation
has $\partial_t$ matching $\nabla^2$ but is real and dissipative; the
Dirac equation has matched first-order $\partial_\mu$ in all four
coordinates. The Schrödinger equation alone has the mismatch
first/second between time and space, with the additional feature of an
$i$ on the time-derivative side. The textbook tradition (Schrödinger
1926, Dirac 1930 *Principles*) presents this asymmetry as a consequence
of taking the non-relativistic limit of the Klein--Gordon equation under
the substitution $\psi = \tilde\psi e^{-imc^2 t/\hbar}$ and dropping a
second-derivative term that is negligible at $|\mathbf{v}| \ll c$. The
asymmetry is therefore correct but not, in the textbook reading,
illuminating.

In the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, the asymmetry has a direct geometric reading.
The McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ specifies (clauses
(i)--(iii) of Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}) a *single, uniform, directional advance* of
$x_4$ at rate $c$ at every event of $M_{G}$: one temporal step per
coordinate-time tick, with no preferred spatial direction. The
3D-spatial *consequence* of this single uniform advance is *diffusive
spherical spreading* on the McGucken Sphere (the $SO(3)$-Haar measure on
the wavefront, Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}): each point on the wavefront has equal
amplitude, and the wavefront grows spherically. The two orders of derivative reflect this asymmetry directly:

1.  *First derivative in time.* The temporal direction carries one
    uniform $x_4$-advance per tick. The amplitude evolution per unit
    coordinate time is therefore first-order: $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi$
    measures the rate of $x_4$-phase accumulation, which by
    Theorem [4.1](#thm:QMT4){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT4"}
    (Compton coupling, Geometric Channel) is $\hbar\omega_C\psi = E\psi$ for
    energy eigenstates. The first-order time derivative is the direct
    geometric expression of the uniform $x_4$-advance rate.

2.  *Second derivative in space (Laplacian).* The spatial direction
    carries diffusive spreading of the wavefront across the 2-sphere
    (Lemma [1.5](#lem:spherical-wave-kinematics){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:spherical-wave-kinematics"}: the spherical wave
    $\psi \propto e^{i(kr - \omega t)}/r$ satisfies $\Box\psi = 0$). The
    spatial spreading scale is quadratic --- the wavefront's area grows
    as $r^2 = (ct)^2$, so the spatial-amplitude derivative that captures
    this growth is the Laplacian $\nabla^2$, a second-order operator
    with the standard Cartesian form
    $\nabla^2 = \partial_{x_1}^2 + \partial_{x_2}^2 + \partial_{x_3}^2$.
    The Laplacian is the local operator whose eigenvalue on a plane wave
    $e^{i\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x}}$ is $-|\mathbf{k}|^2$, dimensionally
    $1/L^2$ --- the quadratic-in-spatial-displacement scaling
    appropriate to a diffusive spherical-wavefront construction.

The asymmetry first/second is therefore the mathematical expression of a
single underlying geometric fact: *one uniform expansion (first-order in
the expanding dimension $t$) produces diffusive spreading (second-order
in the spatial dimensions $\mathbf{x}$ it expands into)*. The $i$
accompanying the time derivative is the perpendicularity marker of
$x_4 = ict$ --- the same $i$ as in the McGucken Principle, in the
path-integral phase $e^{iS/\hbar}$, in the canonical commutation
relation $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, and in the four-momentum
operator $\hat p^\mu = i\hbar\,\partial/\partial x_\mu$
(Theorem [9.21](#thm:twelve-i){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:twelve-i"}, case 1: chain-rule mechanism image of the
McGucken-Principle $i$). The Schrödinger equation's mismatched
derivative orders are the direct algebraic signature of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$'s asymmetric coupling between the single
$x_4$-direction (first-order) and the three spatial directions it
expands into (second-order, Laplacian).
:::

### Empirical anchor

-   the hydrogen-atom spectrum (Sommerfeld--Schrödinger 1926, confirming
    Bohr's energy levels with relativistic corrections);

-   the harmonic-oscillator spectrum (vibrational molecular spectra);

-   the tunneling rate in $\alpha$-decay (Gamow--Condon--Gurney 1928),
    confirming the wave-mechanical penetration of classically forbidden
    barriers;

-   the entirety of quantum chemistry (Pauling, Slater, Mulliken from
    the 1930s onward), which is computational Schrödinger;

-   the matter-wave interferometry of Fein et al. [@Fein2019],
    confirming the Schrödinger phase up to $25\,\text{kDa}$ mass.

## QM T8: The Klein--Gordon Equation {#ch:klein-gordon}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial
three. Throughout this chapter, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ refers to this
principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: (i) *invariance* --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the
expansion is isotropic in the spatial three, with the set of events
reachable from $p$ in proper time $\tau$ being a 2-sphere of radius
$c\tau$; (iii) *monotonicity* --- the integral curve is strictly
monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of $x_4$-advance; (iv)
*Lorentz consistency* --- the structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on
$M_{G}$; (v) *global validity* --- $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at
every event of $M_{G}$. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ (Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the central fact.

The Klein--Gordon equation is the relativistic generalisation of the
Schrödinger equation for spin-$0$ massive particles. In the textbook
tradition it appears as the simplest relativistic wave equation
(Bjorken--Drell 1964; Itzykson--Zuber 1980; Peskin--Schroeder
[@PeskinSchroeder1995]), and is sometimes derived by "squaring" the
Dirac operator or by writing the operator form of the relativistic
energy-momentum dispersion. In the McGucken framework, it is a theorem
of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ along two derivationally disjoint routes.

### Statement

::: {#thm:QMT8 .theorem}
**Theorem 8.1** (QM T8: Klein--Gordon Equation). *The matter
wavefunction $\psi : M_{G}\to \mathbb{C}$ of a spin-$0$ massive particle
of rest mass $m$, in the absence of external interactions, satisfies
$$\left(\Box \;-\; \frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2}\right)\psi(\mathbf{x}, t) \;=\; 0,
\label{eq:Klein--Gordon}$$ where $\Box = -c^{-2}\partial_t^2 + \nabla^2$
is the d'Alembertian on $M_{G}$. This is Theorem 67 (Algebraic Channel) and
Theorem 90 (Geometric Channel) of [@Syn-2026].*
:::

### Geometric Channel derivation: Sphere wavefront with Compton-phase mass term {#sec:QMT8-channelB}

::: {#lem:massless-channelB .lemma}
**Lemma 8.5** (Massless wavefront satisfies $\Box\psi = 0$). *The
McGucken-Sphere wavefront amplitude $\psi$ for a massless particle
satisfies $\Box\psi = 0$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof proceeds in five steps. Step 1 establishes the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront kinematics from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.
Step 2 derives the wave equation $\Box\psi = 0$ as the second-order
characteristic equation of rate-$c$ propagation at every event of the
wavefront, with the eikonal-like argument completed in Step 3. Step 4
verifies the result explicitly on the canonical spherical-wave and
plane-wave solutions. Step 5 closes by linearity for general
superpositions.

**Step 1: McGucken-Sphere wavefront kinematics.** By
Theorem [1.1](#thm:QMT1){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT1"}
(Geometric Channel derivation of the wave equation,
Chapter [1](#ch:wave-equation){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:wave-equation"}), the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at
source event $p$ is the locus of $x_{4}$-advance at rate $ic$ from $p$
in time $t - t_p$; its spatial wavefront at lab-time $t$ is the 2-sphere
$|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t - t_p)$, propagating outward at rate
$c$. By construction QB1 (every event sources a McGucken Sphere) and QB2
(Huygens iteration: every wavefront point is itself a source of a new
Sphere), the global wavefront amplitude $\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ is a
function on $M_{G}$ whose iso-surfaces $\{\psi = \mathrm{const}\}$ are
propagated outward at rate $c$ at every event.

**Step 2: Wave equation as second-order characteristic of rate-$c$
propagation.** A massless wavefront on the Lorentz arena $M_{G}$
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}) propagates along null worldlines, i.e.,
worldlines whose tangent vector $u^\mu = dx^\mu/d\lambda$ (with
$\lambda$ any affine parameter) satisfies $u^\mu u_\mu = 0$. In
components, with $u^\mu = (c, \mathbf{v})$ where $|\mathbf{v}| = c$ for
null propagation:
$$u^\mu u_\mu \;=\; \eta_{\mu\nu}u^\mu u^\nu \;=\; -c^2 + |\mathbf{v}|^2 \;=\; -c^2 + c^2 \;=\; 0,$$
in signature $(-, +, +, +)$. The wavefront amplitude $\psi$ is constant
along these null worldlines: differentiating $\psi$ along the null
tangent gives the first-order characteristic equation
$$u^\mu\,\partial_\mu\,\psi \;=\; 0$$ along every null direction at
every event. Repeating this along a different null direction at the same
event (since the null cone has a one-parameter family of null directions
through every event, indexed by $\mathbf{v}/c \in S^2$):
$$v^\mu\,\partial_\mu\,(u^\nu\,\partial_\nu\,\psi) \;=\; 0.$$ Averaging
over the null cone with the McGucken-Sphere-induced $SO(3)$-invariant
measure on the spatial directions $\hat{\mathbf{v}} \in S^2$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii): spherical symmetry of the
$x_{4}$-expansion supplies the isotropic measure on the wavefront
sphere) gives the second-order Lorentz-invariant characteristic
equation. Explicitly:
$$\int_{S^2}\frac{d\Omega}{4\pi}\,(c, c\hat{\mathbf{v}})^\mu\,(c, c\hat{\mathbf{v}})^\nu\,\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\,\psi \;=\; 0,$$
where the average over $\hat{\mathbf{v}} \in S^2$ uses
$\int_{S^2}(d\Omega/4\pi)\,v^j v^k = \tfrac{1}{3}c^2\delta^{jk}$ for
spatial components and $\int_{S^2}(d\Omega/4\pi)\,v^j = 0$ for the mixed
time-space term:
$$c^2\,\partial_0^2\,\psi + c^2\cdot\tfrac{1}{3}\delta^{jk}\,\partial_j\partial_k\,\psi \;=\; c^2\,\partial_0^2\,\psi + \tfrac{c^2}{3}\,\nabla^2\,\psi \;=\; 0.$$
This gives $\partial_0^2\psi = -\tfrac{1}{3}\nabla^2\psi$ as the
angular-averaged characteristic equation, which is not the d'Alembert
equation directly. The angular average loses geometric information about
which directional null cone the wavefront is propagating along.

A cleaner derivation comes from the second-order operator that
annihilates every plane-wave solution of the form
$\psi \sim e^{i(\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x} - \omega t)}$ with the
massless dispersion $\omega = c|\mathbf{k}|$ (the Fourier-decomposition
signature of null propagation). On such a plane wave:
$$\partial_t^2\psi \;=\; -\omega^2\,\psi, \qquad \nabla^2\psi \;=\; -|\mathbf{k}|^2\,\psi,$$
and the massless dispersion $\omega^2 = c^2|\mathbf{k}|^2$ gives
$$-c^{-2}\partial_t^2\psi + \nabla^2\psi \;=\; -c^{-2}(-\omega^2)\psi + (-|\mathbf{k}|^2)\psi \;=\; \bigl(\omega^2/c^2 - |\mathbf{k}|^2\bigr)\psi \;=\; 0.$$
The d'Alembert operator $\Box = -c^{-2}\partial_t^2 + \nabla^2$
annihilates every plane wave whose dispersion satisfies
$\omega = c|\mathbf{k}|$, i.e., every massless plane wave on $M_{G}$.

**Step 3: $\Box\psi = 0$ as the unique covariant second-order equation
enforcing rate-$c$ propagation.** The d'Alembert operator
$\Box = \eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ is the unique (up to
scalar multiple) Lorentz-invariant second-order partial differential
operator on $M_{G}$ whose Fourier symbol $-\eta^{\mu\nu}k_\mu k_\nu$
vanishes on the null cone $\{k^\mu : k^\mu k_\mu = 0\}$. (Any
second-order constant-coefficient operator on $\mathbb{R}^{1,3}$ has the
form $a^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ for some symmetric
$a^{\mu\nu}$; Lorentz invariance forces
$a^{\mu\nu} = \lambda\,\eta^{\mu\nu}$ for some scalar $\lambda$, and the
symbol vanishing on the null cone is equivalent to $\lambda$ being the
d'Alembertian coefficient.) The McGucken-derived metric of
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"} is the essential input: it supplies
the null cone whose Fourier symbol $\Box$ vanishes on. Therefore
$\Box\psi = 0$ is the unique covariant second-order wave equation
expressing the rate-$c$ propagation of a massless wavefront on $M_{G}$.

**Step 4: Explicit verification on the canonical solutions.** We verify
$\Box\psi = 0$ explicitly on two classes of solutions, both massless
wavefronts derived from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ Geometric Channel kinematics.

*Sub-step 4a: Spherical wave $\psi = f(r - ct)/r$.* For a point source
at the origin, the McGucken-Sphere wavefront amplitude is
$$\psi(\mathbf{x}, t) \;=\; \frac{f(r - ct)}{r}, \qquad r := |\mathbf{x}|,$$
for some smooth profile $f$
(Lemma [1.5](#lem:spherical-wave-kinematics){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:spherical-wave-kinematics"}, derived in
Chapter [1](#ch:wave-equation){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:wave-equation"}; the argument $r - ct$ encodes outward
propagation at rate $c$). Compute:
$$\partial_t\psi \;=\; -\frac{c\,f'(r - ct)}{r}, \qquad \partial_t^2\psi \;=\; \frac{c^2\,f''(r - ct)}{r},$$
and
$$\nabla^2\psi \;=\; \nabla^2\Bigl(\frac{f(r-ct)}{r}\Bigr) \;=\; \frac{f''(r - ct)}{r},$$
using the standard identity $\nabla^2(g(r)/r) = g''(r)/r$ for
spherically symmetric profiles, valid for $r > 0$. Therefore
$$\Box\psi \;=\; -c^{-2}\partial_t^2\psi + \nabla^2\psi \;=\; -c^{-2}\cdot\frac{c^2 f''}{r} + \frac{f''}{r} \;=\; -\frac{f''}{r} + \frac{f''}{r} \;=\; 0.$$
The spherical-wave amplitude satisfies $\Box\psi = 0$ at every point
$r > 0$ (off the source locus).

*Sub-step 4b: Massless plane wave
$\psi = e^{i(\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x} - \omega t)}$ with
$\omega = c|\mathbf{k}|$.* Computed in Step 2:
$\Box\psi = (\omega^2/c^2 - |\mathbf{k}|^2)\psi = 0$ when
$\omega = c|\mathbf{k}|$.

**Step 5: Extension to general massless wavefronts by linearity.** A
general massless wavefront amplitude on $M_{G}$ is a superposition of
the canonical solutions: spherical waves sourced at various events
$p_\alpha$ with various profile functions $f_\alpha$, and massless plane
waves with various wavevectors $\mathbf{k}_\beta$:
$$\psi(\mathbf{x}, t) \;=\; \sum_\alpha \frac{f_\alpha(|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_{p_\alpha}| - c(t - t_{p_\alpha}))}{|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_{p_\alpha}|} \,+\, \sum_\beta A_\beta\,e^{i(\mathbf{k}_\beta\cdot\mathbf{x} - c|\mathbf{k}_\beta|t)}.$$
By linearity of $\Box$ (the d'Alembertian is a constant-coefficient
differential operator) and Step 4, $\Box\psi = 0$ for any such
superposition (off the source loci for the spherical-wave terms). By
Fourier completeness on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$
(Lemma [6.4](#lem:fourier-conjugate){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:fourier-conjugate"} of
Chapter [2](#ch:de-broglie){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:de-broglie"}), every massless wavefront has a
representation of this form. The McGucken-Sphere wavefront amplitude,
propagating at the McGucken-Principle rate $c$ at every event
(clause (i) of Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, with QB1 supplying source events and QB2
supplying Huygens iteration), is a function of this form, hence
satisfies $\Box\psi = 0$. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#lem:compton-dispersion .lemma}
**Lemma 8.6** (Mass term adds a Compton-frequency contribution to the
dispersion). *For a massive particle of rest mass $m$, the rest-frame
Sphere phase advances at Compton angular frequency
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$. In four-momentum form, this contributes
$\omega_C^2 = m^2 c^4/\hbar^2$ to the squared energy, giving
$$\frac{\omega^2}{c^2} = k^2 + \frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2}$$ for plane-wave
modes $\psi \sim e^{i(\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x} - \omega t)}$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has six steps, deriving the relativistic
dispersion $\omega^2/c^2 = k^2 + m^2c^2/\hbar^2$ along a Geometric-Channel-pure
chain (rest-frame Compton oscillation + Lorentz invariance of the
McGucken-derived Minkowski metric), with no invocation of Wigner
classification or Casimir analysis.

**Step 1: Rest-frame phase from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.** By
Theorem [5.1](#thm:QMT5){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT5"}
(Geometric Channel), the rest-frame wavefunction of a massive particle of rest
mass $m$ is
$$\psi_{\mathrm{rest}}(\tau) \;=\; A\,e^{-i\,m c^2\,\tau/\hbar} \;=\; A\,e^{-i\,\omega_C\,\tau}, \qquad \omega_C \;:=\; \frac{mc^2}{\hbar},$$
advancing in proper time $\tau$ at the Compton angular frequency
$\omega_C$. The derivation: by
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"}, a particle at rest directs its
entire four-velocity budget into the $x_{4}$-direction at rate $c$
(forced by Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii), spherical symmetry of
$x_{4}$-expansion); by Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:62"}, the action quantum $\hbar$ accumulates per Sphere
cycle, giving the phase-accumulation rate $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ at the
rest-frame Compton oscillation.

**Step 2: Lorentz boost to the moving frame.** The Minkowski arena
$M_{G}$ supports the Lorentz group $SO^+(1,3)$ acting on four-vectors
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv);
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}). Under a Lorentz boost $\Lambda$ from
the rest frame to a frame where the particle has four-momentum
$P^\mu = (E/c, \mathbf{p})$ with $E = \gamma mc^2$ and
$\mathbf{p} = \gamma m\mathbf{v}$ (the standard relativistic
four-momentum components in signature $(-, +, +, +)$, with
$\gamma = (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$), the proper time $\tau$ of the particle
relates to the moving-frame spacetime coordinates by the Lorentz
invariance of the line element
$-c^2 d\tau^2 = ds^2 = \eta_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu dx^\nu$, evaluated along the
worldline. Solving for $\tau$ in terms of $(t, \mathbf{x})$ along the
worldline:
$$\tau \;=\; \frac{E\,t - \mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{x}}{m c^2} \;=\; \frac{P^\mu x_\mu}{(-)\,m c^2},$$
using $P^\mu x_\mu = -Et + \mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{x}$ in signature
$(-, +, +, +)$. (More carefully:
$P^\mu x_\mu = \eta_{\mu\nu}P^\mu x^\nu = -P^0 x^0 + \mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{x} = -(E/c)(ct) + \mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{x} = -Et + \mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{x}$.)

Substituting into the rest-frame phase:
$$-\omega_C\,\tau \;=\; -\frac{m c^2\,\tau}{\hbar} \;=\; -\frac{m c^2}{\hbar}\cdot\frac{E t - \mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{x}}{m c^2} \;=\; -\frac{E t - \mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{x}}{\hbar} \;=\; \frac{P^\mu x_\mu}{\hbar}.$$
The moving-frame wavefunction is the Lorentz-covariant lift of the
rest-frame oscillation:
$$\psi(\mathbf{x}, t) \;=\; A\,e^{i\,P^\mu x_\mu/\hbar} \;=\; A\,e^{-i(E t - \mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{x})/\hbar} \;=\; A\,e^{i(\mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{x}/\hbar - E t/\hbar)}.$$
The phase $P^\mu x_\mu/\hbar$ is a Lorentz scalar (four-vector
contraction divided by the Lorentz-invariant action quantum), as
required for a covariant scalar wavefunction.

**Step 3: Plane-wave form.** Writing the wavefunction in the moving
frame as a plane wave with wavevector $\mathbf{k}$ and angular frequency
$\omega$:
$$\psi(\mathbf{x}, t) \;=\; A\,e^{i(\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x} - \omega t)}, \qquad \mathbf{k} \;:=\; \frac{\mathbf{p}}{\hbar}, \quad \omega \;:=\; \frac{E}{\hbar}.$$
The wavevector and angular frequency are related to the four-momentum by
the de Broglie and Planck--Einstein relations
(Theorems [2.1](#thm:QMT2){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT2"}
and [3.1](#thm:QMT3){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT3"}, both
Geometric Channel derivations from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**Step 4: Relativistic dispersion from the rest-frame norm and Lorentz
invariance.** The squared four-momentum $P^\mu P_\mu$ is a Lorentz
invariant on $M_{G}$ (Step 3 of
Lemma [8.3](#lem:massive-rep-eigenvalue){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:massive-rep-eigenvalue"}: the Minkowski metric is
$SO^+(1,3)$-invariant, hence the four-vector contraction $P^\mu P_\mu$
equals its rest-frame value in every Lorentz frame). At rest,
$P^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} = (mc, 0, 0, 0)$ gives
$$P^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}}\,P^{\mathrm{rest}}_\mu \;=\; \eta_{00}(mc)^2 \;=\; -m^2c^2.$$
Lorentz invariance extends this to the moving frame:
$$P^\mu P_\mu \;=\; -m^2c^2 \qquad \text{in every Lorentz frame on $M_{G}$}.$$
Expanding the moving-frame contraction in components:
$$P^\mu P_\mu \;=\; \eta_{00}(E/c)^2 + \delta_{jk}p^j p^k \;=\; -\frac{E^2}{c^2} + |\mathbf{p}|^2,$$
so $-E^2/c^2 + |\mathbf{p}|^2 = -m^2c^2$, equivalently
$$E^2 \;=\; |\mathbf{p}|^2\,c^2 + m^2\,c^4.$$ This is the relativistic
energy-momentum dispersion, derived along a Geometric-Channel-pure chain from
the rest-frame Compton oscillation (Step 1) and Lorentz invariance of
the McGucken-derived Minkowski metric (Step 3 above), with no input from
Wigner classification or representation-theoretic Casimirs.

Substituting $E = \hbar\omega$ and $\mathbf{p} = \hbar\mathbf{k}$ from
Step 3:
$$\hbar^2\,\omega^2 \;=\; \hbar^2\,c^2\,k^2 + m^2\,c^4, \qquad \text{where } k \;:=\; |\mathbf{k}|.$$
Dividing by $\hbar^2 c^2$:
$$\frac{\omega^2}{c^2} \;=\; k^2 + \frac{m^2\,c^2}{\hbar^2}.$$ This is
the relativistic dispersion relation for plane-wave modes of a massive
matter wavefunction.

**Step 5: Klein-Gordon equation in plane-wave form.** On plane-wave
modes $\psi \sim e^{i(\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x} - \omega t)}$, the
partial derivatives act as
$$\partial_t\psi = -i\omega\,\psi, \quad \partial_t^2\psi = -\omega^2\,\psi, \quad \nabla\psi = i\mathbf{k}\,\psi, \quad \nabla^2\psi = -k^2\,\psi.$$
The d'Alembertian $\Box = -c^{-2}\partial_t^2 + \nabla^2$ in the
convention of
equation [\[eq:Klein\--Gordon\]](#eq:Klein--Gordon){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:Klein--Gordon"} acts as
$$\Box\psi \;=\; -\frac{1}{c^2}(-\omega^2)\psi + (-k^2)\psi \;=\; \Bigl(\frac{\omega^2}{c^2} - k^2\Bigr)\psi.$$
Using the dispersion relation from Step 4,
$\omega^2/c^2 = k^2 + m^2 c^2/\hbar^2$:
$$\Box\psi \;=\; \Bigl(k^2 + \frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2} - k^2\Bigr)\psi \;=\; +\frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2}\,\psi.$$
Rearranging: $(\Box - m^2 c^2/\hbar^2)\psi = 0$ --- the Klein-Gordon
equation in plane-wave form, exactly
equation [\[eq:Klein\--Gordon\]](#eq:Klein--Gordon){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:Klein--Gordon"}. Extension to general wavefunctions by
Fourier completeness is handled in
Lemma [8.7](#lem:QMT8-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT8-channelB-proof"} below.

**Step 6: McGucken anchoring.** The Compton angular frequency
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ in the dispersion relation is the rest-frame
phase-accumulation rate at which the matter wavefunction's $x_{4}$-phase
advances (Theorem [5.1](#thm:QMT5){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT5"}, derived from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at the
source event via the rest-frame four-velocity budget and the action
quantum per Sphere cycle, Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:62"}). The mass term $m^2c^2/\hbar^2$ in the Klein-Gordon
equation traces to this rest-frame phase rate: it is the
squared Compton angular frequency divided by $c^2$, i.e., the squared
rest-frame $x_{4}$-phase rate in spatial-wavevector units. The $i$ in
the plane-wave phase $e^{-i\omega t}$ traces through
Theorem [9.21](#thm:twelve-i){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:twelve-i"} case 2 (chain-rule mechanism (a) image of the
McGucken-Principle $i$) to the perpendicularity marker $i$ in
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. Both algebraic ingredients of the mass term
descend from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#lem:QMT8-channelB-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 8.7** (Geometric Channel proof of QM T8). *The wavefunction of a massive
spin-$0$ particle, modeled as the McGucken-Sphere wavefront with a
Compton-frequency rest-mass oscillation, satisfies
$(\Box - m^2 c^2/\hbar^2)\psi = 0$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof builds the Klein--Gordon equation along a Geometric Channel
chain in six steps, with the mass shell
$P^\mu P_\mu = -m^2 c^2$ identified as a consequence of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (Theorem 4.6, Lemma 4.2) via
Lemma [4.7](#lem:reverse-reading-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reverse-reading-equivalence"}. The construction follows
the structure of [@MG-Pointwise-2026] §9.1.5: the Klein--Gordon equation
falls out as the differential expression of the mass-shell constraint,
with no canonical-quantization step performed at any point in the chain.

**Step 1: Mass shell from the McGucken Principle in four-vector form.**
By Lemma [4.7](#lem:reverse-reading-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reverse-reading-equivalence"} (the rest-frame reading of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), the rest-frame four-velocity normalization
$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ is a consequence of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Theorem 4.6, Lemma 4.2); it carries no Sphere, no orientation and no
measure, and it holds at every spacetime point in the rest frame of any
massive particle at that point.
Multiplying both sides by the squared rest mass $m^2$ and using the
definition $P^\mu := m u^\mu$:
$$P^\mu\,P_\mu \;=\; m^2\,u^\mu\,u_\mu \;=\; m^2\,(-c^2) \;=\; -m^2\,c^2.$$
This is the mass shell --- the geometric locus in four-momentum space
where the McGucken-Sphere wavefront is consistent with rest mass $m$.
The mass-shell condition is Lorentz-invariant: by Lorentz invariance of
the McGucken-derived Minkowski metric
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, descending from
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv), derived at Theorem 4.6), the relation
$P^\mu P_\mu = -m^2 c^2$ holds in every Lorentz frame on $M_{G}$. The
mass shell is a consequence of the McGucken Principle:
$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ follows from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (Theorem 4.6,
Lemma 4.2), and multiplying by $m^2$ promotes it to the four-momentum mass
shell.

**Step 2: Compton frequency from action quantization of the wavefront.**
By the physical content of the principle
(Remark [4.2](#rmk:substantive-content-of-principle){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:substantive-content-of-principle"} of
Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"}), the $x_4$-wavefront carries action $\hbar$
per oscillatory cycle at the Planck frequency. For a particle of rest
mass $m$, the rest-frame wavefunction oscillates at the Compton angular
frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ along proper time
(Theorem [5.1](#thm:QMT5){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT5"},
derived from the rest-frame four-velocity budget of
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} combined with the action quantum
per Sphere cycle of Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:62"}). The four-wavevector $k^\mu := P^\mu/\hbar$ carries
the mass shell into wavevector-frequency form:
$$k^\mu\,k_\mu \;=\; \frac{P^\mu P_\mu}{\hbar^2} \;=\; -\,\frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2},$$
holding in every Lorentz frame on $M_{G}$. The constants $c$ and $\hbar$
appearing in this relation are the twin properties of one wavefront
advance (Theorem [9.35](#thm:c-hbar-twin){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:c-hbar-twin"}): $c$ is the rate of $x_4$-advance and
$\hbar$ is the action per oscillatory cycle at the Planck frequency,
with both reading off the physical content of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

**Step 3: Plane-wave wavefunction as elementary mode of the
McGucken-Sphere expansion at four-wavevector on the mass shell.** On
$M_{G}$, an elementary mode of the McGucken-Sphere expansion at
four-wavevector $k^\mu$ is the plane-wave
$$\psi_k(x^\mu) \;=\; \exp\!\bigl(i\,k^\nu x_\nu\bigr) \;=\; \exp\!\bigl(i\,S[\gamma]/\hbar\bigr),$$
where the second equality identifies the four-wavevector phase
$k^\nu x_\nu$ with the classical action $S[\gamma] = P^\nu x_\nu$ along
the straight worldline $\gamma$ at four-wavevector $k^\mu$, divided by
the action quantum $\hbar$. The plane-wave mode $\psi_k$ satisfies the
mass-shell constraint of Step 2 by construction:
$k^\mu k_\mu = -m^2 c^2/\hbar^2$ is the Lorentz-invariant statement that
$\psi_k$ propagates on the McGucken-Sphere expansion of a particle of
rest mass $m$.

**Step 4: d'Alembertian applied --- Klein--Gordon as the differential
expression of the mass-shell constraint.** The d'Alembertian
$\Box = \eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ acts on the plane-wave
mode $\psi_k(x^\mu) = \exp(ik^\nu x_\nu)$ by direct differentiation:
$$\Box\,\psi_k \;=\; \eta^{\mu\nu}(ik_\mu)(ik_\nu)\,\psi_k \;=\; -\,k^\mu k_\mu\,\psi_k \;=\; +\,\frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2}\,\psi_k,$$
using the mass-shell relation $k^\mu k_\mu = -m^2 c^2/\hbar^2$ of Step 2
in the last equality. Rearranging:
$$\Bigl(\Box - \frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2}\Bigr)\,\psi_k \;=\; 0,$$ the
Klein--Gordon equation in plane-wave form, exactly
equation [\[eq:Klein\--Gordon\]](#eq:Klein--Gordon){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:Klein--Gordon"}. Extension to general wavefunctions
follows by Fourier completeness: the Klein--Gordon operator
$\Box - m^2c^2/\hbar^2$ is linear, so every superposition
$\psi(x) = \int d^3\mathbf{k}\,\tilde\psi(\mathbf{k})\,\psi_k(x)$ over
plane-wave modes on the mass shell satisfies the same equation. Since
plane-wave modes are dense in the matter-wavefunction space
$L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3\mathbf{x})$ by Fourier completeness
(Lemma [6.4](#lem:fourier-conjugate){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:fourier-conjugate"} of
Chapter [2](#ch:de-broglie){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:de-broglie"}), the Klein--Gordon equation
$(\Box - m^2c^2/\hbar^2)\psi = 0$ holds for every massive spin-$0$
matter wavefunction.

*No canonical-quantization step has been performed.* The Geometric Channel chain
reads off the Klein--Gordon equation as the differential expression of
the mass-shell constraint, with the d'Alembertian acting on plane-wave
modes producing the mass-shell eigenvalue
$-k^\mu k_\mu = m^2c^2/\hbar^2$ by direct evaluation of
$\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu \exp(ik^\nu x_\nu)$. The Algebraic
Channel quantization rule $\hat P^\mu = -i\hbar\,\partial^\mu$ (Stone's
theorem applied to spacetime-translation invariance,
Lemma [8.4](#lem:QMT8-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT8-channelA-proof"}) does not appear in Geometric Channel: the
role of mapping classical four-momentum to operator action that Algebraic
Channel executes through Stone-quantization is replaced in Geometric Channel by the
role of reading off the differential action of $\Box$ on McGucken-Sphere
plane-wave kernels through direct evaluation. The two channels arrive at
the same Klein--Gordon equation through derivationally disjoint chains.

**Step 5: Huygens--Fresnel--Kirchhoff integral form of the same
content.** The differential form $(\Box - m^2c^2/\hbar^2)\psi = 0$ has a
corresponding integral form: the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
$M^{+}_{p}(t)$ from each Cauchy-surface event $p$ is the elementary
secondary wavefront, with rest-frame Compton-phase content
$\exp(-i\omega_C \tau)$ along proper time
(Lemma [7.8](#lem:compton-phase-wavelet){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:compton-phase-wavelet"}), and the Klein--Gordon equation
is the self-consistency condition on the superposition of secondary
wavefronts. This is the massive-case generalization of Huygens's
principle (Theorem [1.1](#thm:QMT1){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT1"}, QM T1): each McGucken Sphere from a
Cauchy-surface point carries its rest-frame Compton-phase content
forward, and the Kirchhoff diffraction integral over the Cauchy surface
reproduces the wavefunction at any subsequent event on $M_{G}$. The
differential form (Klein--Gordon) and the integral form
(Huygens--Fresnel--Kirchhoff superposition over McGucken Spheres) are
two expressions of the same dynamical content of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, related by Stokes' theorem on the spacetime
slab between successive Cauchy surfaces. The massless case ($m = 0$,
$\omega_C = 0$) recovers the standard Huygens construction of QM T1
Geometric Channel; the massive case adds the Compton-phase content to each
secondary wavefront.

**Step 6: Massless limit and Geometric Channel characterisation.** In the
massless limit $m \to 0$, the mass shell collapses to the null cone
$k^\mu k_\mu = 0$ at every event of $M_{G}$, and the Klein--Gordon
equation reduces to the massless wave equation $\Box\psi = 0$
(Lemma [8.5](#lem:massless-channelB){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:massless-channelB"}, QM T1 Geometric Channel). Photons and other
massless particles propagate on the null cone with no Compton frequency:
the rest-frame phase oscillation has rate zero
($\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar = 0$ when $m = 0$), the rest-frame wavefunction
degenerates to a constant phase, and the wavefront's $x_4$-advance has
no associated rest-mass cycling. The massless limit recovers the
spherical-wavefront content of QM T1 Geometric Channel as a consistent special
case of the massive Klein--Gordon equation.

The Geometric Channel chain uses (i) the four-velocity normalization
that follows from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via
Lemma [4.7](#lem:reverse-reading-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reverse-reading-equivalence"} giving the mass shell
directly; (ii) the action quantization clause of the physical content
(Remark [4.2](#rmk:substantive-content-of-principle){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:substantive-content-of-principle"}, the action $\hbar$
per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation of the $x_4$-wavefront) giving the
Compton frequency; (iii) direct evaluation of $\Box$ on McGucken-Sphere
plane-wave kernels giving the differential form. No Wigner
classification, mass-Casimir analysis, or canonical-quantization rule
appears in the chain; the proof is Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation),
derivationally disjoint from the Algebraic Channel mass-Casimir +
Stone-quantization route of
Lemma [8.4](#lem:QMT8-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT8-channelA-proof"}. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:kg-wavefront-essential-inputs .remark}
*Remark 8.8* (The wavefront kinematics are the essential inputs; the
dynamics are in the premise). The four wavefront properties named in the
physical content of the principle
(Remark [4.2](#rmk:substantive-content-of-principle){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:substantive-content-of-principle"} of
Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"}) appear as the essential derivational
inputs of the Geometric Channel chain above:

-   *Wavelength.* The Compton wavelength $\lambda_C = \hbar/(mc)$
    appears in Step 2 as the rest-frame wavelength of the matter
    wavefront, with the mass-shell relation
    $k^\mu k_\mu = -m^2 c^2/\hbar^2$ giving
    $|k|_{\mathrm{rest}} = 1/\lambda_C$ in the rest frame.

-   *Frequency.* The Compton angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$
    appears in Step 2 as the rest-frame phase-accumulation rate, the
    origin of the Klein--Gordon mass term.

-   *Phase.* The four-wavevector phase $k^\nu x_\nu$ appears in Step 3
    as the plane-wave phase, equivalent to the classical action
    $S[\gamma] = P^\nu x_\nu$ along the straight worldline divided by
    the action quantum $\hbar$.

-   *Action.* The action quantum $\hbar$ appears in Step 2 as the
    Compton-frequency oscillation quantum and in Step 3 as the
    action-normalization scale of the plane-wave phase.

The Geometric Channel derivation reads off the Klein--Gordon equation from the
physical content of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ as a spherically-symmetric
wavefront with wavelength, frequency, phase, and action: the mass-shell
constraint $P^\mu P_\mu = -m^2 c^2$ is a consequence of the
principle (Theorem 4.6, Lemma 4.2); the Compton-frequency rest-mass phase is the wavefront's
frequency content at the particle's rest mass; the plane-wave kernel
$\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$ is the McGucken-Sphere expansion at
four-wavevector on the mass shell; and the d'Alembertian acting on these
kernels gives the Klein--Gordon equation as the differential form of the
mass-shell constraint. The dynamics of the relativistic spin-$0$
wavefunction were in the premise: every algebraic ingredient of the
Klein--Gordon equation traces directly to the wavefront content of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with no canonical-quantization step performed.

A plane-wave kernel $\psi_k(x^\mu) = \exp(ik^\nu x_\nu)$ from an
emission event $E$ on the mass shell satisfies the PT-symmetry through
$E$ exactly
(Theorem [11.10](#thm:born-as-pt-symmetry-through-source){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-as-pt-symmetry-through-source"} clause (ii)):
$\psi_k(\mathrm{PT}_E\cdot\text{event}) = \psi_k^*(\text{event})$
holding identically on $M_{G}$. The Klein--Gordon retarded and advanced
Green's functions on $M_{G}$ are the PT-conjugate pair on the forward
and past light cones of the source event, with their relation being the
geometric realization of the Wigner antiunitary $T$ at the kernel level.
The wavefunction's complex-conjugation symmetry --- and therefore the
bilinearity of the Born density in $(\psi, \psi^*)$ for Klein--Gordon
plane-wave solutions --- has its geometric source in the McGucken
Sphere's PT-symmetry through the source event.
:::

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem [8.1](#thm:QMT8){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT8"}.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The theorem asserts the Klein-Gordon equation
$(\Box - m^2 c^2/\hbar^2)\psi = 0$ for the wavefunction of a spin-0
massive particle. We establish this along both channels and verify their
derivational disjointness.

**Step 1: Algebraic Channel derivation
(Lemma [8.4](#lem:QMT8-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT8-channelA-proof"}).** By the rest-frame four-velocity
budget of Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} (the rest particle directs its
entire four-velocity into the $x_{4}$-direction at rate $c$, forced by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i), (ii)) together with the Lorentz
invariance of the McGucken-derived Minkowski metric
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"},
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv)), the rest-frame four-momentum
$P^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} = (mc, 0, 0, 0)$ has the Lorentz-invariant
squared norm
$$P^\mu P_\mu \;=\; -m^2c^2 \qquad \text{in every Lorentz frame on $M_{G}$}$$
(Lemma [8.3](#lem:massive-rep-eigenvalue){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:massive-rep-eigenvalue"} Steps 1--3, with Wigner
classification appearing as a corroborating external result in Step 5).
The operator-level statement is
$\hat P^\mu\hat P_\mu\,\psi = -m^2 c^2\,\psi$ on the massive irreducible
representation. By the quantisation rule
$\hat P^\mu = -i\hbar\,\partial^\mu$ (Stone's theorem applied to
spacetime translation invariance of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), the
Casimir operator equals $\hat P^\mu\hat P_\mu = -\hbar^2\,\Box$
(Lemma [8.2](#lem:mass-casimir-operator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:mass-casimir-operator"}). Equating the two operator
actions: $-\hbar^2\,\Box\,\psi = -m^2c^2\,\psi$, hence
$$\Bigl(\Box - \frac{m^2c^2}{\hbar^2}\Bigr)\,\psi \;=\; 0.$$ The Algebraic
Channel route: $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ $\to$ rest-frame four-velocity
budget + Lorentz invariance
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}) $\to$ rest-frame Minkowski norm
$P^\mu P_\mu = -m^2c^2$ extended Lorentz-invariantly $\to$
operator-quantization rule from Stone $\to$ Klein-Gordon equation.

**Step 2: Geometric Channel derivation
(Lemma [8.7](#lem:QMT8-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT8-channelB-proof"}).** The McGucken-Sphere wavefront
satisfies $\Box\psi = 0$ in the massless case
(Lemma [8.5](#lem:massless-channelB){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:massless-channelB"}: explicit verification on the
canonical spherical-wave and plane-wave solutions, with rate-$c$
propagation at every event as the input). For a massive
particle, the rest-frame matter wavefunction accumulates phase at the
Compton angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ per proper time
(Theorem [5.1](#thm:QMT5){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT5"},
Geometric Channel; the rest-frame phase rate descends from
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the rest-frame four-velocity budget of
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} and the action quantum per Sphere
cycle of Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:62"}). Lorentz-boosting to the moving frame on $M_{G}$
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, McGucken-derived Minkowski metric)
produces the relativistic dispersion
$$\frac{\omega^2}{c^2} \;=\; k^2 + \frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2}$$
(Lemma [8.6](#lem:compton-dispersion){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:compton-dispersion"} Step 4, derived along a
Geometric-Channel-pure chain via rest-frame norm
$P^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}}P^{\mathrm{rest}}_\mu = -m^2c^2$ extended by
Lorentz invariance). On plane-wave modes
$\psi \sim e^{i(\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x} - \omega t)}$ with
$\Box = -c^{-2}\partial_t^2 + \nabla^2$:
$$\Box\psi \;=\; -\frac{1}{c^2}(-\omega^2)\psi + (-k^2)\psi \;=\; \Bigl(\frac{\omega^2}{c^2} - k^2\Bigr)\psi \;=\; +\frac{m^2c^2}{\hbar^2}\,\psi,$$
using the relativistic dispersion in the last equality. Rearranging
gives $(\Box - m^2c^2/\hbar^2)\psi = 0$, extended to general
wavefunctions by Fourier completeness
(Lemma [8.7](#lem:QMT8-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT8-channelB-proof"} Step 4). The Geometric Channel route:
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ $\to$ McGucken-Sphere construction $\to$
massless backbone $\Box\psi = 0$ $\to$ rest-frame Compton oscillation at
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ $\to$ Lorentz-covariant relativistic dispersion
$\to$ Klein-Gordon equation.

**Step 3: Derivational disjointness of the two channels.** Algebraic Channel uses
Wigner classification, mass-Casimir analysis, the quantisation rule for
the four-momentum operator, and Lorentz-invariant operator
identification. Geometric Channel uses the McGucken-Sphere construction, the
explicit spherical-wave kinematics for the massless backbone, the
Compton-phase per Sphere cycle for the rest-mass contribution, and
plane-wave dispersion analysis. The intermediate machinery is disjoint:

-   Wigner classification and mass-Casimir appear in Algebraic Channel, not in
    Geometric Channel;

-   Sphere wavefront and Compton-phase appear in Geometric Channel, not in
    Algebraic Channel.

The two channels share only $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the final
Klein-Gordon equation.

**Step 4: McGucken anchoring of mass term.** The mass term
$m^2c^2/\hbar^2$ in the Klein-Gordon equation is, in Geometric Channel, the
shadow of the McGucken-Sphere's rest-frame Compton-phase
accumulation at angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$. In Algebraic Channel,
it is the mass-Casimir eigenvalue of the irreducible Poincaré
representation. Both readings descend from the same fact: at
rest, a massive particle has four-velocity entirely in the
$x_{4}$-direction at rate $c$, with rest energy $mc^2$. The Klein-Gordon
mass term is therefore the squared $x_{4}$-velocity component of the
rest particle, divided by $\hbar^2$.

**Step 5: Spin-0 specialisation.** The Klein-Gordon equation as written
holds for any massive irreducible representation (the mass-Casimir is
spin-independent). The spin-0 specification appears when we ask for the
irreducible representation with trivial intrinsic angular momentum ---
the smallest representation of $\hat P^\mu\hat P_\mu = -m^2 c^2$, acting
on scalar wavefunctions $\psi: M_{G}\to \mathbb{C}$. For spin-$1/2$
matter, the Dirac equation
(Theorem [9.1](#thm:QMT9){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT9"})
supplements Klein-Gordon with the Clifford-algebra factorisation; for
spin-$1$, the Proca equation; for higher spins, the Pauli-Fierz /
Rarita-Schwinger equations. Klein-Gordon is the spin-independent core;
higher-spin equations add structure beyond.

**Step 6: Physical and historical content.** The Klein-Gordon equation,
introduced independently by Klein and Gordon in 1926 as the relativistic
generalisation of Schrödinger's equation, has historically been treated
as a postulate of relativistic quantum mechanics. The
McGucken framework derives it as a theorem of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ along both algebraic and geometric channels.
Klein-Gordon is the basic dynamical equation for the Higgs scalar,
neutral and charged pions in the low-energy limit, and any spin-0
quantum field; its empirical relevance spans particle physics,
condensed-matter Bose-Einstein condensates, and cosmological scalar
fields (inflaton, dark matter scalars). ◻
:::

### Geometric Channel derivation, second route: mass shell from $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ plus Compton frequency from action quantization {#sec:QMT8-channelB-mass-shell}

The Geometric Channel derivation above
(§[\[sec:QMT8-channelB\]](#sec:QMT8-channelB){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:QMT8-channelB"}) proceeded via Huygens iteration on
null worldlines, eikonal characteristics, and spherical-wave / plane-wave
verification. A second, distinct Geometric Channel
derivation reaches the Klein--Gordon equation through a different chain:
the mass-shell constraint $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ (the four-vector form
of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt} = ic$) supplies the wavevector magnitude, the
Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ supplies the rest-frame
oscillation rate, and the d'Alembertian on the Lorentzian metric
expresses the mass-shell constraint differentially on the wavefunction.
The two Geometric Channel routes share no intermediate machinery beyond
the McGucken Principle itself: the present route uses Compton
frequency + dispersion relation + d'Alembertian; the earlier route used
Huygens iteration + null characteristics + eikonal averaging. The
convergence supplies a second McGucken-internal route to the
Klein--Gordon equation, sharpening the convergent-overdetermination
property of the dual-channel architecture.

::: {#thm:KG-mass-shell-route .theorem}
**Theorem 8.6** (Klein--Gordon equation via mass shell and Compton
frequency, Geometric Channel second route; [@MG-Hilbert-2026]
Theorem 9.0). *Let particle $A$ of rest mass $m$ at event
$p_0 \in M_{1,3}$ propagate its McGucken-expansion wavefront outward
according to the McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}) with action $\hbar$ per radian of the Compton-frequency
oscillation. The wavefunction $\psi$ on $M_{1,3}$ representing this
McGucken-expansion wavefront satisfies the Klein--Gordon equation*
$$(\Box - m^2 c^2/\hbar^2)\,\psi = 0,$$
*where $\Box = -(1/c^2)\,\partial_t^2 + \nabla^2$ is the
d'Alembertian on $M_{1,3}$, $m$ is the particle's rest mass, $c$ is
the rate of $x_4$-advance, and $\hbar$ is the action quantum per
radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation of $x_4$-advance.*

*The derivation uses only the wavefront geometry: the spherical
symmetry of the McGucken Sphere at every event, the Lorentz-invariant
magnitude $c$ of the four-velocity (equivalent to
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt} = ic$), and the Compton-frequency oscillation of
the rest-frame wavefront. No quantization of
$E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4$ is invoked; no canonical-commutator operator
substitution is required.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has six steps.

**Step 1: McGucken-Sphere expansion forces the mass-shell constraint.**
By Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)--(v) and the spherical symmetry
of the wavefront, the particle's four-velocity satisfies
$$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2,$$
equivalently $dx_4/d\tau = ic$ in the rest frame
(Lemma [4.7](#lem:reverse-reading-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reverse-reading-equivalence"}). Multiplying by $m^2$
gives the four-momentum norm
$$p^\mu p_\mu = m^2 u^\mu u_\mu = -m^2 c^2,$$
the mass-shell constraint on the wavefront: the four-momentum of any
massive particle propagating according to $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$
lies on the timelike hyperboloid
$\{p^\mu : p^\mu p_\mu = -m^2 c^2\}$. The constraint is purely
geometric: it states that the four-velocity has magnitude $c$, a
consequence of the McGucken Principle (Theorem 4.6, Lemma 4.2).

**Step 2: Compton-frequency oscillation supplies the four-wavevector.**
For a particle of rest mass $m$, the intrinsic rest-frame oscillation
of the McGucken-expansion wavefront has Compton frequency
$$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar, \qquad \nu_C = mc^2/h, \qquad \lambda_C = \hbar/(mc),$$
supplied by the McGucken Principle's action-quantization clause via
Theorem [4.1](#thm:QMT4){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT4"}. The rest-frame four-wavevector is
$$k^\mu_\text{rest} = (\omega_C/c,\, \mathbf{0}) = (mc/\hbar,\, \mathbf{0}),$$
with Lorentz-invariant magnitude
$$k^\mu_\text{rest}\, k_{\text{rest},\mu} = -(mc/\hbar)^2 = -m^2 c^2/\hbar^2.$$
By Lorentz covariance under the $SO^+(1,3)$ isometry group of the
Lorentzian metric, the four-wavevector in any inertial frame satisfies
$$k^\mu k_\mu = -m^2 c^2/\hbar^2$$
— the mass-shell constraint in wavevector form.

**Step 3: Plane-wave wavefunction on the wavefront.** The wavefunction
$\psi$ representing the McGucken-expansion wavefront in a general
inertial frame is the plane wave
$$\psi(x^\mu) = \exp(i k^\nu x_\nu) = \exp\bigl(i(\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x} - \omega t)\bigr)$$
with $\mathbf{k} = \mathbf{p}/\hbar$, $\omega = E/\hbar$. The
phase $k^\nu x_\nu$ is the path-integral $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ phase
evaluated on the straight worldline from the source event to $x^\mu$.
The Fourier mode is the natural elementary mode of the
McGucken-Sphere expansion at four-wavevector $k^\mu$ on the mass
shell of Step 2.

**Step 4: Differential expression of the mass shell = Klein--Gordon
equation.** Apply $\Box = -(1/c^2)\,\partial_t^2 + \nabla^2$ to the
plane wave of Step 3:
$$\partial_t \psi = -i\omega\psi, \quad \partial_t^2 \psi = -\omega^2 \psi, \quad \nabla\psi = i\mathbf{k}\psi, \quad \nabla^2\psi = -|\mathbf{k}|^2 \psi,$$
hence
$$\Box\psi = (\omega^2/c^2 - |\mathbf{k}|^2)\psi.$$
In four-vector form with $k^\mu = (\omega/c, \mathbf{k})$ and
$\eta_{\mu\nu}$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$:
$$k^\mu k_\mu = -(\omega/c)^2 + |\mathbf{k}|^2 = -(\omega^2/c^2 - |\mathbf{k}|^2),$$
so $\Box\psi = -k^\mu k_\mu\cdot\psi$. By Step 2 the mass-shell
forces $k^\mu k_\mu = -m^2 c^2/\hbar^2$, hence
$$\Box\psi = (m^2 c^2/\hbar^2)\psi,$$
i.e. $(\Box - m^2 c^2/\hbar^2)\psi = 0$. This is the Klein--Gordon
equation, derived as the differential expression of the McGucken
Principle's mass-shell constraint $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ on the
wavefront. No quantization of $E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4$ has been
invoked; no canonical-quantization operator substitution has been
performed. The Klein--Gordon equation is the wavefront geometry
expressed differentially.

**Step 5: Self-consistency via Huygens--Fresnel--Kirchhoff on the
McGucken Sphere.** The plane-wave solutions of Step 3 are the
elementary modes of the McGucken-Sphere expansion at four-wavevector
$k^\mu$. General wavefronts are spectral superpositions
$$\psi(x^\mu) = \int d^4 k\,\delta(k^\mu k_\mu + m^2 c^2/\hbar^2)\,\tilde\psi(k)\,\exp(i k_\nu x^\nu),$$
with the delta supporting the integral on the mass shell of Step 2.
Every such superposition satisfies the Klein--Gordon equation; by the
spectral theorem applied to $\Box$, every solution admits this
Fourier representation. The solution space of the Klein--Gordon
equation is exactly the space of McGucken-expansion wavefronts
consistent with rest mass $m$.

**Step 6: Massless limit (photons).** For $m = 0$, the mass shell
collapses to the null cone $k^\mu k_\mu = 0$, and Klein--Gordon
reduces to $\Box\psi = 0$. Photons propagate along the null cone of
every source event with no rest-frame oscillation
($\omega_C = 0$ when $m = 0$). The McGucken Sphere of the photon is
the null cone itself; the massless case is the null-cone boundary of
the massive Klein--Gordon equation, recovered as the $m\to 0$ limit.
◻
:::

::: {#rmk:KG-two-geometric-routes .remark}
*Remark 8.6.A* (Two Geometric Channel routes to the Klein--Gordon
equation). The textbook now contains two distinct
Geometric Channel derivations of the Klein--Gordon equation:

-   *Huygens-iteration route*
    (Lemma [8.5](#lem:massless-channelB){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:massless-channelB"} and surrounding material in
    §[\[sec:QMT8-channelB\]](#sec:QMT8-channelB){reference-type="ref"
    reference="sec:QMT8-channelB"}): null propagation $\to$ Huygens
    iteration via eikonal characteristics $\to$ spherical/plane-wave
    verification of $\Box\psi = 0$, with the mass term obtained by
    Compton-phase modulation.

-   *Mass-shell + Compton-frequency route*
    (Theorem [8.6](#thm:KG-mass-shell-route){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:KG-mass-shell-route"}): mass shell from
    $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ $\to$ Compton frequency
    $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ from action quantization $\to$
    plane-wave $\exp(i k^\nu x_\nu)$ on the mass shell $\to$
    d'Alembertian yields Klein--Gordon directly.

Both routes start from the McGucken Principle; both reach
$(\Box - m^2 c^2/\hbar^2)\psi = 0$ through derivationally disjoint
chains. Both Geometric-Channel routes are independent of the
Algebraic-Channel mass-Casimir route of
§[\[sec:QMT8-channelA\]](#sec:QMT8-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:QMT8-channelA"}. The Klein--Gordon equation is
therefore *triply* overdetermined by McGucken machinery — two
Geometric-Channel routes and one Algebraic-Channel route — all
descending from $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.
:::

### Algebraic Channel derivation: Mass-Casimir of the Poincaré representation {#sec:QMT8-channelA}

::: {#lem:mass-casimir-operator .lemma}
**Lemma 8.2** (Mass-Casimir is $-\hbar^2\Box$ in operator form). *The
four-momentum operator
$\hat{P}^\mu = -i\hbar\,\partial^\mu = -i\hbar\,\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu$
on $\mathcal{H}$ satisfies
$$\hat{P}^\mu \hat{P}_\mu = -\hbar^2\,\Box.$$*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Convention.** We work in the standard high-energy signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ with timelike coordinate $x^0 = ct$, equivalently
$\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1,+1,+1,+1)$ on the four spacetime
indices $\mu = 0, 1, 2, 3$. This is the textbook's standard signature,
established (with the same sign convention) in
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"} (with $x_4 = ict$ as the integrated
kinematic shadow per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}; both index conventions agree on
the metric being diag$(-1,+1,+1,+1)$ in the $(ct,x,y,z)$ basis, with
the McGucken-Principle squaring rule $dx_4^2 = -c^2 dt^2$ supplying the
timelike negative sign).
The d'Alembertian in
the present convention is
$\Box = \eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu = -c^{-2}\partial_t^2 + \nabla^2$,
matching the theorem
statement [\[eq:Klein\--Gordon\]](#eq:Klein--Gordon){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:Klein--Gordon"}.

**Step 1: Covariant form of $\hat P^\mu$.** By
Lemma [2.2](#lem:phat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:phat-generator"} of
Chapter [2](#ch:de-broglie){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:de-broglie"} (spatial component, derived from Stone's
theorem applied to spatial-translation invariance of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$) and
Lemma [7.3](#lem:hamiltonian-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:hamiltonian-generator"} of
Chapter [7](#ch:schrodinger){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:schrodinger"} (time component, derived from Stone's
theorem applied to time-translation invariance of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), the covariant four-momentum operator is
$$\hat P_\mu \;=\; -i\hbar\,\partial_\mu, \qquad \mu = 0, 1, 2, 3,$$
with $\partial_0 = c^{-1}\partial_t$ and
$\partial_j = \partial/\partial x^j$ for $j = 1, 2, 3$. The
contravariant form follows by raising the index with $\eta^{\mu\nu}$:
$$\hat P^\mu \;=\; \eta^{\mu\nu}\,\hat P_\nu \;=\; -i\hbar\,\eta^{\mu\nu}\,\partial_\nu \;=\; -i\hbar\,\partial^\mu.$$
In components:
$\hat P^0 = \eta^{00}\hat P_0 = (-1)\cdot(-i\hbar)\partial_0 = +i\hbar/c\cdot\partial_t$.
The energy operator $\hat H := c\hat P^0 = i\hbar\partial_t$ matches
Lemma [7.3](#lem:hamiltonian-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:hamiltonian-generator"}. For spatial indices
$j = 1, 2, 3$:
$\hat P^j = \eta^{jj}\hat P_j = (+1)\cdot(-i\hbar)\partial_j = -i\hbar\partial_j$,
matching $\hat p_j$ from
Lemma [2.2](#lem:phat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:phat-generator"}.

**Step 2: Square the four-momentum operator.** The Lorentz scalar formed
by contracting $\hat P^\mu$ with $\hat P_\mu$ is
$$\hat P^\mu\,\hat P_\mu \;=\; (-i\hbar\,\partial^\mu)\,(-i\hbar\,\partial_\mu) \;=\; (-i\hbar)^2\,\partial^\mu\partial_\mu \;=\; (-i)^2\,\hbar^2\,\partial^\mu\partial_\mu \;=\; -\hbar^2\,\partial^\mu\partial_\mu,$$
using the elementary identity $(-i)^2 = i^2 = -1$. The minus sign at the
end traces to the McGucken-Principle squaring $i^2 = -1$
(equivalent algebraic content as $dx_4 = ic\,dt$ giving
$dx_4^2 = -c^2\,dt^2$ in
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}).

**Step 3: Identify $\partial^\mu\partial_\mu$ with the d'Alembertian
$\Box$.** By definition of the d'Alembertian as the metric contraction
of two partial derivatives:
$$\Box \;:=\; \eta^{\mu\nu}\,\partial_\mu\partial_\nu.$$ By raising one
index ($\partial^\nu := \eta^{\nu\mu}\partial_\mu$), this is
equivalently
$$\Box \;=\; \eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu \;=\; \partial^\nu\partial_\nu \;=\; \partial^\mu\partial_\mu,$$
where the last two expressions are identical up to the dummy summation
index. Expanding component-by-component in signature $(-,+,+,+)$:
$$\Box \;=\; \eta^{00}\partial_0\partial_0 + \sum_{j=1}^{3}\eta^{jj}\partial_j\partial_j \;=\; (-1)(c^{-1}\partial_t)^2 + \sum_{j=1}^3 (+1)\partial_j^2 \;=\; -c^{-2}\partial_t^2 + \nabla^2,$$
matching the theorem-statement convention. Substituting into Step 2:
$$\hat P^\mu\,\hat P_\mu \;=\; -\hbar^2\,\Box.$$

**Step 4: McGucken anchoring of the factor $-\hbar^2$.** The factor
$-\hbar^2$ in $\hat P^\mu\hat P_\mu = -\hbar^2\Box$ decomposes into two
pieces, each McGucken-anchored:

-   The minus sign comes from the squaring of the perpendicularity
    marker $i$: $(-i)^2 = i^2 = -1$, with the $i$ tracing through
    Theorem [9.21](#thm:twelve-i){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:twelve-i"} case 1 (chain-rule mechanism) to the
    perpendicularity marker of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in
    Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}.

-   The factor $\hbar^2$ comes from the action quantum $\hbar$ per
    Sphere cycle appearing twice in the squared four-momentum
    (Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:62"},
    derived from the rest-frame Compton oscillation at angular frequency
    $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ generated by $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at the
    source event).

Both factors trace directly to $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ through named
theorems.

Combined with the mass-Casimir eigenvalue
$\hat P^\mu\hat P_\mu\,\psi = -m^2 c^2\,\psi$ on the massive irreducible
Poincaré representation
(Lemma [8.3](#lem:massive-rep-eigenvalue){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:massive-rep-eigenvalue"} below), Step 3 yields the
operator equation $-\hbar^2\Box\,\psi = -m^2c^2\,\psi$, equivalently
$$\Bigl(\Box - \frac{m^2c^2}{\hbar^2}\Bigr)\,\psi \;=\; 0,$$ the
Klein--Gordon equation in the book's signature. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#lem:massive-rep-eigenvalue .lemma}
**Lemma 8.3** (Massive irreducible representation satisfies
$\hat{P}^\mu \hat{P}_\mu = -m^2 c^2$). *By QA6 (Wigner classification of
irreducible unitary representations of the Poincaré group), the massive
irreducible representation labelled by rest mass $m > 0$ has the
four-momentum Casimir invariant
$$\hat{P}^\mu \hat{P}_\mu\,\psi \;=\; -m^2 c^2\,\psi.$$*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has six steps. The McGucken-derived core
(Steps 1--3) derives $\hat P^\mu\hat P_\mu = -m^2c^2$ directly from the
rest-frame four-velocity budget of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the
Lorentz invariance of the McGucken-derived Minkowski metric, with no
input from external representation-theoretic classifications. Steps 4--5
corroborate the result with the standard Wigner-classification framing.
Step 6 records the interpretation of the mass parameter $m$
within the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework.

**Step 1: Rest-frame four-velocity budget on $M_{G}$.** By
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} of
Chapter [4](#ch:compton){reference-type="ref" reference="ch:compton"}
(derived from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at the source event via
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i), (ii): the principle holds at
every event with magnitude $c$, and spherical symmetry of the
$x_{4}$-expansion guarantees that a particle at spatial rest directs no
four-velocity into the spatial three), the rest-frame four-velocity of a
massive particle is entirely in the $x_{4}$-direction:
$$u^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} \;=\; (c, 0, 0, 0) \qquad \text{in signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with $x^0 = ct$},$$
equivalently $u^4_{\mathrm{rest}} = ic$ in the McGucken-derived
$(+,+,+,-)$ convention with $x^4 = ict$. The norm is computed from the
McGucken-derived Minkowski metric
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"},
$\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1,+1,+1,+1)$):
$$u^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}}\,u^{\mathrm{rest}}_\mu \;=\; \eta_{\mu\nu}u^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}}u^\nu_{\mathrm{rest}} \;=\; \eta_{00}\,c^2 + 0 \;=\; -c^2.$$
This is the rest-frame value of the Lorentz scalar $u^\mu u_\mu$.

**Step 2: Rest-frame four-momentum and the mass parameter.** The
four-momentum of a particle of rest mass $m > 0$ is $P^\mu := m u^\mu$,
by direct definition (rest mass times four-velocity). At rest:
$$P^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} \;=\; m u^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} \;=\; (mc, 0, 0, 0),$$
with temporal component $mc$ and spatial components zero. The rest
energy is $E_0 = c P^0_{\mathrm{rest}} = mc^2$ (the standard
relativistic rest-energy formula), and the rest-frame four-momentum has
Minkowski-norm
$$P^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}}\,P^{\mathrm{rest}}_\mu \;=\; m^2\,u^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}}\,u^{\mathrm{rest}}_\mu \;=\; m^2\,(-c^2) \;=\; -m^2 c^2.$$
This direct calculation in the rest frame establishes the rest-frame
value of the squared four-momentum.

**Step 3: Extension to every Lorentz frame by McGucken-derived Lorentz
invariance.** The Minkowski metric on $M_{G}$ is Lorentz-invariant:
under any $\Lambda \in SO^+(1,3)$, the line element
$ds^2 = \eta_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu dx^\nu$ is preserved
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv): the $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
structure on $M_{G}$ is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant, with the Minkowski metric
itself the integrated kinematic shadow). The four-momentum $P^\mu$
transforms as a four-vector under $\Lambda$:
$$P^\mu \;\xrightarrow{\Lambda}\; P^{\prime\mu} \;=\; \Lambda^\mu{}_\nu\,P^\nu,$$
preserving the Minkowski norm:
$$P^{\prime\mu}\,P^\prime_\mu \;=\; \eta_{\mu\nu}P^{\prime\mu}P^{\prime\nu} \;=\; \eta_{\mu\nu}\Lambda^\mu{}_\alpha\Lambda^\nu{}_\beta\,P^\alpha P^\beta \;=\; \eta_{\alpha\beta}\,P^\alpha P^\beta \;=\; P^\alpha P_\alpha,$$
using the Lorentz-invariance identity
$\eta_{\mu\nu}\Lambda^\mu{}_\alpha\Lambda^\nu{}_\beta = \eta_{\alpha\beta}$
(the defining property of $SO^+(1,3)$). Therefore $P^\mu P_\mu$ has the
same value in every Lorentz frame, equal to the rest-frame value
computed in Step 2:
$$P^\mu P_\mu \;=\; -m^2 c^2 \qquad \text{in every Lorentz frame on $M_{G}$}.$$
This is the relativistic energy-momentum dispersion in covariant form,
derived from McGucken machinery alone (rest-frame four-velocity budget +
Lorentz invariance of the McGucken-derived metric); no external
representation-theoretic input is invoked.

**Step 4: Operator quantization.** The four-momentum operator
$\hat P^\mu = -i\hbar\,\partial^\mu$ is the generator of spacetime
translation (Lemma [2.2](#lem:phat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:phat-generator"} for the spatial component,
Lemma [7.3](#lem:hamiltonian-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:hamiltonian-generator"} for the temporal component, both
descending from Stone's theorem applied to translation invariance of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ per
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(v)). On a wavefunction $\psi$ of
a particle of rest mass $m$, the operator action of the squared
four-momentum produces the eigenvalue identified in Step 3:
$$\hat P^\mu\,\hat P_\mu\,\psi \;=\; -m^2 c^2\,\psi.$$ The wavefunction
$\psi$ is the simultaneous eigenfunction of all Casimir operators of the
Poincaré group with eigenvalues labelled by $(m, s)$; the mass-Casimir
eigenvalue $-m^2c^2$ is the content derived above.

**Step 5: Corroboration by Wigner classification.** The result of Step 4
is the operator-level statement of Wigner's classification theorem
(Wigner 1939; Weinberg [@Weinberg1995] Ch. 2) for the massive
irreducible unitary representations of the Poincaré group
$\mathrm{Poin}^+ = \mathbb{R}^{1,3} \rtimes SO^+(1,3)$. The two
independent Casimir operators of the Poincaré Lie algebra are

-   $C_1 = P^\mu P_\mu$ --- squared four-momentum (Lorentz scalar);

-   $C_2 = W^\mu W_\mu$ --- squared Pauli-Lubanski vector
    $W^\mu := -\tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}J_{\nu\rho}P_\sigma$
    (related to spin).

The irreducible unitary representations are labelled by the eigenvalues
of $C_1, C_2$:

-   *Massive* ($C_1 < 0$): $C_1 = -m^2 c^2$,
    $C_2 = -m^2 c^2 s(s+1)\hbar^2$ with mass $m > 0$ and spin
    $s \in \{0, 1/2, 1, 3/2, \ldots\}$;

-   *Massless* ($C_1 = 0$): $C_2 = 0$ with helicity
    $\lambda \in \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}$;

-   *Tachyonic* ($C_1 > 0$): unphysical; excluded by
    Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iii) (monotonicity of
    $x_{4}$-advance fixes the forward causal direction, ruling out
    spacelike-momentum representations);

-   *Vacuum* ($C_1 = 0$, $P^\mu = 0$): trivial representation.

The massive representation labelled by rest mass $m$ has
$C_1$-eigenvalue $-m^2c^2$, matching the McGucken-anchored derivation of
Steps 1--3.

**Step 6: Reading of the mass parameter $m$.** Within the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, the rest mass $m$ has direct content: it
is the inertial parameter that, multiplied by the McGucken-Principle
rate $c$ via $P^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} = mu^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}}$, gives the
magnitude of the rest-frame $x_{4}$-momentum. The Compton angular
frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar = E_0/\hbar$
(Theorem [4.1](#thm:QMT4){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT4"}) is
the phase rate of the rest-frame $x_{4}$-advance: the rest-frame
wavefunction $\psi_{\mathrm{rest}}(\tau) = A e^{-i\omega_C \tau}$
oscillates at $\omega_C$ along proper time. The mass-Casimir $-m^2c^2$
is therefore the squared norm of the rest-frame four-momentum
$P^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} = (mc, 0, 0, 0)$ computed using the
McGucken-derived Minkowski metric. Within the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, the
mass parameter has the reading of the inertial coefficient in
the four-momentum $P^\mu = mu^\mu$ on $M_{G}$; the integrated kinematic shadow
