via the RGC (Relational Geometric Constructor)${}_6$ procedure
(Theorem [13.8](#thm:rgc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:rgc-six"}), and is itself recovered from any other
element of $\mathcal{F}_M$ via the MCC (Matter--Channel
Categorical)${}_6$ extraction
(Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"}). Self-generation at the Sphere level is the
geometric face of the categorical self-generation of $\mathrm{McG}_6$. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:mutual-containment .theorem}
**Theorem 17.18** (Theorem A: Mutual Containment (MCC);
[@MG-Hilbert6-2026] §13.3). *Each member of the McGucken source-pair
$(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ contains the McGucken Axiom
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in full. The McGucken Space $\mathcal{M}_G$, as
the four-tuple $(E_4, \Phi_M, D_M, \Sigma_M)$, contains the Axiom
*twice*: once as its operator constituent
$D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$, and once as the integrated
constraint $\Phi_M = x_4 - ict = 0$. The McGucken Operator $D_M$
contains the Axiom as the ratio of its own coefficients ($ic$ to $1$).
The founding law is present, in full, inside both members of the pair.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). This is the pair-level specialisation of MCC${}_6$
(Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"}) to the dynamical pair
$(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M) \subset \mathcal{F}_M$. We establish the three
containments in six steps.

**Step 1: $\mathcal{M}_G$ contains the axiom via level-set
differentiation (first containment).** Apply the extraction
$\Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}$ from the proof of
Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"} (Case $X = \mathcal{M}_G$). The McGucken Space
$\mathcal{M}_G$ is the four-tuple $(E_4, \Phi_M, D_M, \Sigma_M)$, where
$\Phi_M: E_4 \to \mathbb{C}$ is the constraint function
$$\Phi_M(\mathbf{x}, t) = x_4 - ict.$$ The McGucken-Space is precisely
the level set $\Phi_M = 0$, equivalently the relation $$x_4 = ict.$$
Differentiating both sides with respect to $t$:
$$\frac{dx_4}{dt} = ic.$$ This is the McGucken Axiom in differential
form. The constraint function $\Phi_M$ --- itself a component of
$\mathcal{M}_G$ --- extracted via level-set differentiation recovers the
axiom. This is the first containment.

**Step 2: $\mathcal{M}_G$ contains the axiom via its operator component
(second containment).** The four-tuple
$\mathcal{M}_G = (E_4, \Phi_M, D_M, \Sigma_M)$ includes the McGucken
Operator $D_M$ as one of its components. Applying $\Pi_{D_M}$ (Case
$X = D_M$) to the operator $$D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$$
reads the ratio of coefficients: the coefficient of $\partial_{x_4}$ is
$ic$, the coefficient of $\partial_t$ is $1$, and their ratio recovers
$dx_4/dt = ic/1 = ic$. The same axiom is therefore extractable from
$\mathcal{M}_G$ via a second, distinct operation:
coefficient-reading on the operator-component.

**Step 3: $\mathcal{M}_G$ contains the axiom *twice* --- significance.** Steps 1 and 2 establish that $\mathcal{M}_G$ contains
the axiom via two distinct extraction procedures:

-   Level-set differentiation of $\Phi_M$ (Step 1);

-   Coefficient-reading on $D_M$ (Step 2).

The McGucken-Space has the reading of a redundant container
of the axiom: $\mathcal{M}_G$ contains $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ both
implicitly (in the dynamical-arena role) and explicitly (in the
constraint reading on $D_M$ of Step 2). This redundancy makes the
framework robust: extracting the axiom from $\mathcal{M}_G$ proceeds via
either reading without requiring a choice between them; both succeed.

**Step 4: $D_M$ contains the axiom (third containment).** Apply
$\Pi_{D_M}$ to $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$. Two equivalent
extractions:

-   *Coefficient ratio:* the $x_4$-coefficient is $ic$, the
    $t$-coefficient is $1$; their ratio $ic/1 = ic$ recovers
    $dx_4/dt = ic$;

-   *Kernel computation:* setting $D_M\Phi = 0$ for
    $\Phi(\mathbf{x}, t) = x_4 - f(t)$ gives $-f'(t) + ic\cdot 1 = 0$,
    i.e., $f'(t) = ic$, which is the axiom along the kernel-curve.

Both extractions read the axiom directly from the structure of $D_M$.

**Step 5: Standard catalogue of operations.** All three containment
proofs (Steps 1, 2, 4) use only operations in the standard mathematical
catalogue:

-   Level-set extraction (Step 1);

-   Differentiation (Step 1);

-   Coefficient reading (Steps 2, 4);

-   Kernel-of-operator computation (Step 4).

No specialised or post-hoc machinery is required, as required by the MCC
theorem (Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"}). The containments are mathematically
elementary.

**Step 6: Significance --- founding law is present in both
members.** The Mutual Containment Theorem establishes that the founding
law $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is present, in full, inside both members of
the McGucken source-pair $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$. The axiom has the
role of an object contained within the
framework's own constituents, rather than the role of an external
parameter or input to the framework. This is the categorical content of
the McGucken Principle's centrality: the axiom is the object through
which every other object of $\mathcal{F}_M$ is generated
(Theorem [13.8](#thm:rgc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:rgc-six"}), and is recoverable from any object via the
corresponding extraction
(Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"}). The pair-level statement above is the
dynamical specialisation of this general categorical structure. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:reciprocal-generation .theorem}
**Theorem 17.19** (Theorem B: Reciprocal Generation (RGC);
[@MG-Hilbert6-2026] §13.3). *Each member of $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$
generates the other by an explicit constructive procedure, with the two
procedures mutually inverse. Specifically, there exist procedures
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}}: D_M \mapsto \mathcal{M}_G$ and
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}}: \mathcal{M}_G \mapsto D_M$
satisfying
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}} \circ \Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{M}_G}, \qquad \Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}} \circ \Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}} = \mathrm{id}_{D_M}.$$
The procedures use only elementary differential calculus, with no
external input in either direction. Each member of the pair produces the
other.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). This is the pair-level specialisation of RGC${}_6$
(Theorem [13.8](#thm:rgc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:rgc-six"}) to the ordered pair $(D_M, \mathcal{M}_G)$. We
construct
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}} := C_{\mathcal{M}_G} \circ \Pi_{D_M}$
and
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}} := C_{D_M} \circ \Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}$,
using the canonical extraction and construction rules of
§[13.3](#sec:three-theorems-six-objects){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:three-theorems-six-objects"}.

**Step 1: Construct $\Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}}$.** Apply
$\Pi_{D_M}$ to extract $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (Case $X = D_M$ of
Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"}: read ratio of coefficients of $D_M$). Apply
$C_{\mathcal{M}_G}$ (Part 1 of proof of
Theorem [13.8](#thm:rgc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:rgc-six"}): form carrier
$E_4 = \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{C}$; impose constraint
$\Phi_M = x_4 - ict$; attach $D_M$ and $\Sigma_M$. The composition
$C_{\mathcal{M}_G} \circ \Pi_{D_M}$ takes $D_M$ to $\mathcal{M}_G$.

**Step 2: Construct $\Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}}$.** Apply
$\Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}$ (Case $X = \mathcal{M}_G$: level-set extraction +
differentiation) to extract $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. Apply $C_{D_M}$:
form the chain-rule operator $\partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$. The
composition takes $\mathcal{M}_G$ to $D_M$.

**Step 3: Verify
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}} \circ \Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{M}_G}$.**
Compute:
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}} \circ \Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}} = (C_{\mathcal{M}_G} \circ \Pi_{D_M}) \circ (C_{D_M} \circ \Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}) = C_{\mathcal{M}_G} \circ (\Pi_{D_M} \circ C_{D_M}) \circ \Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}.$$
By Lemma [13.9](#lem:round-trip-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:round-trip-identity"} (Round-Trip Identity),
$\Pi_{D_M} \circ C_{D_M} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}}$. Therefore
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}} \circ \Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}} = C_{\mathcal{M}_G} \circ \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}} \circ \Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G} = C_{\mathcal{M}_G} \circ \Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}.$$
By the dual of the Round-Trip Identity (the round-trip on
$\mathcal{M}_G$-content),
$C_{\mathcal{M}_G} \circ \Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{M}_G}$
up to canonical isomorphism.

**Step 4: Verify
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}} \circ \Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}} = \mathrm{id}_{D_M}$.**
Symmetric to Step 3, with the roles of $D_M$ and $\mathcal{M}_G$
exchanged. Both procedures use only the operations of the standard
mathematical catalogue (differentiation, level-set extraction,
coefficient reading, chain-rule operator construction); no external
input is required. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:containment-generation-equivalence .theorem}
**Theorem 17.20** (Theorem C: Containment-Generation Equivalence (CGE
(Cosmic Geometric Engine)); [@MG-Hilbert6-2026] §13.3).
*Theorems [17.18](#thm:mutual-containment){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mutual-containment"} (MCC)
and [17.19](#thm:reciprocal-generation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:reciprocal-generation"} (RGC) are equivalent for the
source-pair $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$. Taken together, they identify the
source-pair as *a single mathematical object* --- the structure exalted
by the McGucken Axiom --- written in two notational conventions, rather
than two correlated structures generated together.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has two steps establishing the
biconditional. This is the pair-level specialisation of CGE${}_6$
(Theorem [13.10](#thm:cge-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:cge-six"}) restricted to the dynamical pair
$(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$. The result descends from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, the physical, geometric fact that the fourth
dimension expands at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric
manner): both $\mathcal{M}_G$ (the McGucken Space, generated by the
integrated kinematic shadow $x_4 = ict$ of
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) and $D_M$ (the McGucken Operator
$\partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$) descend canonically from the same
axiom, with the round-trip identity
(Lemma [13.9](#lem:round-trip-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:round-trip-identity"}) supplying the mutual-inverse
property.

**Step 1: $(\Rightarrow)$ Containment forces generation.** Suppose MCC
holds: $\mathcal{M}_G$ contains $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in full (i.e.,
$\Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}$ exists) and $D_M$ contains the axiom in full
(i.e., $\Pi_{D_M}$ exists). By the construction rules of
§[13.3](#sec:three-theorems-six-objects){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:three-theorems-six-objects"}, $C_{D_M}$ and
$C_{\mathcal{M}_G}$ exist. Define
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}} = C_{\mathcal{M}_G} \circ \Pi_{D_M}$
and
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}} = C_{D_M} \circ \Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}$,
exactly as in the proof of
Theorem [17.19](#thm:reciprocal-generation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:reciprocal-generation"}. These are well-defined
morphisms; the Round-Trip Identity
(Lemma [13.9](#lem:round-trip-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:round-trip-identity"}) guarantees their mutual-inverse
property. RGC holds.

**Step 2: $(\Leftarrow)$ Generation forces containment.** Suppose RGC
holds: the two mutually inverse procedures
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}}$,
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{arena}\to\mathrm{op}}$ exist. By
Lemma [13.11](#lem:three-step-factorisation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:three-step-factorisation"} (Universal Three-Step
Factorisation, applied to each procedure), each $\Gamma$ factors
uniquely through the axiom:
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{arena}} = C_{\mathcal{M}_G} \circ \Pi_{D_M}$,
requiring the existence of $\Pi_{D_M}$. Similarly $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}$
exists. Therefore both members of the pair contain the axiom in full;
MCC holds. The biconditional MCC $\Leftrightarrow$ RGC holds at the pair
level, exactly as it holds at the six-object level
(Theorem [13.10](#thm:cge-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:cge-six"}).

**Step 3: Single-object synthesis.** As a consequence of
Steps 1 and 2 jointly, the source-pair $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ has the
role of a *single mathematical object*: the structure exalted by
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}), manifested in two notational conventions
(operator and arena) related by the mutually inverse procedures
$\Gamma$. The two notational conventions are the operator notation
(Algebraic Channel, $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$) and the arena

Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} via differentiation and integration, with the
role of two independent structures replaced by the role of two
notational windows onto a single underlying object. The identity is the categorical content of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at every event of
$M_{G}$ (clauses (i)+(v)) is the primitive from which both

(Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"

##### Category McG and the six descent functors {#category-mcg-and-the-six-descent-functors .unnumbered}

[@MG-Hilbert6-2026] §13.4 develops Category McG built on the source-pair
as a fully grounded categorical primitive. The construction supplies
*six descent functors*, each specified explicitly on objects and proved
functorial (preserving identity and composition):

1.  $F_{\mathrm{spacetime}}: \mathrm{McG} \to \mathrm{LorMfd}$ --- produces
    Lorentzian spacetime via the pullback metric construction.

2.  $F_{\mathrm{Hilbert}}: \mathrm{McG} \to \mathrm{Hilb}$ --- produces
    the Hilbert space of quantum mechanics.

3.  $F_{\mathrm{Clifford}}: \mathrm{McG} \to \mathrm{Cliff}$ --- produces
    the Clifford algebra and Dirac spinor bundle.

4.  $F_{\mathrm{gauge}}^G: \mathrm{McG} \to \mathrm{PrinBun}_G$ --- produces
    principal $G$-bundles for any compact Lie group $G$.

5.  $F_{\mathrm{algebra}}: \mathrm{McG} \to C^*\mathrm{Alg}$ --- produces
    the operator algebras $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$.

6.  $F_{\mathrm{Klein}}: \mathrm{McG} \to \mathrm{KleinPair}$ --- produces
    the Klein pair $(\mathrm{ISO}(1,3), \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3))$.

The collection is *jointly faithful*: distinct morphisms in McG produce
distinct morphisms in at least one downstream category. This
faithfulness, combined with the Foundational Maximality Theorem (Theorem
20 of [@MG-Hilbert6-2026]) and the Minimal Primitive-Law Complexity
result $C(\mathcal{M}_G) = 1$ (Theorem 22), establishes the following.

::: {#thm:initial-object-physfound .theorem}
**Theorem 17.23** ($(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ as initial object in
PhysFound; [@MG-Hilbert6-2026] §13.4). *The McGucken source-pair
$(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ is an *initial object* in the category
$\mathrm{PhysFound}$ of foundational physical-mathematical arenas: for
every object in $\mathrm{PhysFound}$, there exists a unique
derivation-preserving morphism from $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$. Initial
objects are unique up to natural isomorphism. The McGucken source-pair
therefore occupies a position --- the source position of the
category of foundational arenas of mathematical physics --- that no
prior framework has occupied.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). We prove the initial-object property by exhibiting a unique
morphism from $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ to every object of
$\mathrm{PhysFound}$, then argue uniqueness up to natural isomorphism.

**Step 1: Existence of the morphism.** Let
$\mathcal{O} \in \mathrm{PhysFound}$ be any object --- a candidate
arena, characterised by (i) an arena (manifold, Hilbert
space, $C^*$-algebra, etc.), (ii) a dynamical content (operator,
differential, or constraint), and (iii) a axiom relating (i)
and (ii). The six descent functors (D1)--(D6) of Category McG (listed in
this chapter) supply, for any such $\mathcal{O}$, a
derivation-preserving morphism
$F_\mathcal{O}: (\mathcal{M}_G, D_M) \to \mathcal{O}$ constructed as
follows:

-   If $\mathcal{O}$ is a Lorentzian manifold, use
    $F_{\mathrm{spacetime}}$ (D1).

-   If $\mathcal{O}$ is a Hilbert space with self-adjoint dynamics, use
    $F_{\mathrm{Hilbert}}$ (D2).

-   If $\mathcal{O}$ is a Clifford algebra with Dirac spinor bundle, use
    $F_{\mathrm{Clifford}}$ (D3).

-   If $\mathcal{O}$ is a principal $G$-bundle for some compact Lie
    group $G$, use $F_{\mathrm{gauge}}^G$ (D4).

-   If $\mathcal{O}$ is a $C^*$-algebra of observables, use
    $F_{\mathrm{algebra}}$ (D5).

-   If $\mathcal{O}$ is a Klein pair $(G, X)$, use $F_{\mathrm{Klein}}$
    (D6).

For an $\mathcal{O}$ that combines multiple structures (e.g., the QFT
(quantum field theory) package consisting of a manifold $+$ Hilbert
space $+$ algebra), the morphism is the joint application of the
relevant descent functors. The Foundational Maximality Theorem of
[@MG-Hilbert6-2026] (Theorem 20) guarantees that every object of
$\mathrm{PhysFound}$ is reached by some composition of the six descent
functors.

**Step 2: Uniqueness of the morphism.** The Minimal Primitive-Law
Complexity Theorem of [@MG-Hilbert6-2026] (Theorem 22) establishes
$C(\mathcal{M}_G) = 1$: the source-pair has primitive-law complexity 1
(one principle, $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). Any derivation-preserving
morphism from $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ to $\mathcal{O}$ must transport
this primitive law into $\mathcal{O}$; by
Lemma [13.11](#lem:three-step-factorisation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:three-step-factorisation"} (Universal Three-Step
Factorisation) of the McG${}_6$ chapter, the morphism factors uniquely
as $C_\mathcal{O} \circ \Pi$ for the construction rule $C_\mathcal{O}$
specific to $\mathcal{O}$. Uniqueness of the factorisation forces
uniqueness of the morphism. (The joint-faithfulness of the descent
collection (D1)--(D6), established in [@MG-Hilbert6-2026] §13.4,
guarantees that distinct morphisms on the McG side produce distinct
images on the $\mathcal{O}$ side, so no two morphisms can collapse to a
single image.)

**Step 3: Uniqueness up to natural isomorphism.** If
$(\mathcal{M}_G', D_M')$ is any other initial object of
$\mathrm{PhysFound}$, then by initiality each maps uniquely to the
other: there exist morphisms
$f: (\mathcal{M}_G, D_M) \to (\mathcal{M}_G', D_M')$ and
$g: (\mathcal{M}_G', D_M') \to (\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$. The composition
$g \circ f$ is a morphism
$(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M) \to (\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$; by uniqueness of
morphisms out of an initial object,
$g \circ f = \mathrm{id}_{(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)}$. Similarly
$f \circ g = \mathrm{id}_{(\mathcal{M}_G', D_M')}$. Hence $f$ and $g$
are mutually inverse natural isomorphisms; the initial object is unique
up to natural isomorphism, a standard categorical fact.

**Step 4: Significance.** The Dual-Failure Historical Novelty
Theorem of [@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] (Theorem 8.5) tests ten
candidate arena-operator pairs from the 2,300-year arc
(Euclid, Newton, Cauchy--Riemann, Riemannian Laplace--Beltrami, Cartan
exterior derivative, Atiyah--Singer, Heisenberg--Schrödinger,
Lagrangian--Hamiltonian, Stone--von Neumann, Connes' spectral triple)
and establishes that each fails the MCC/RGC/CGE triple --- none is
initial in $\mathrm{PhysFound}$ in the sense of Step 1. The McGucken
source-pair, by contrast, satisfies all three
(Theorems [17.18](#thm:mutual-containment){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mutual-containment"},
[17.19](#thm:reciprocal-generation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:reciprocal-generation"},
[17.20](#thm:containment-generation-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:containment-generation-equivalence"}) and is therefore
initial. This is the novelty content of the McGucken
framework. ◻
:::

##### The double completion of Klein's Erlangen Programme {#the-double-completion-of-kleins-erlangen-programme .unnumbered}

[@MG-Hilbert6-2026] §13.2 establishes that the McGucken source-pair
completes Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme along *two independent routes*, both descending from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

::: {#rmk:erlangen-completion .remark}
*Remark 17.25* (The two-route Erlangen completion; [@MG-Hilbert6-2026]
§13.2). **Route 1 (group-theoretic).** The McGucken Principle supplies
the missing physical generator that selects the relativistic Klein pair
$(\mathrm{ISO}(1,3), \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3))$ from within Klein's
group-invariant architecture. Klein's 1872 Programme classified
geometries by their symmetry groups but did not pre-specify which group
should be selected for the physical world; the McGucken Axiom supplies
the physical generator that makes the selection, completing Klein's
programme on its own terms.

**Route 2 (category-theoretic).** The McGucken Principle goes *beneath*
Klein's primitive group-space pair $(G, X)$ and replaces it with the
deeper source-pair $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ derived together by
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The Klein architecture itself is recovered as
the descent image of the source-pair under the functor
$F_{\mathrm{Klein}}$ of (D6) above.

The two routes terminate in different categorical fields (group theory
and category theory, separate research traditions for over a century)
yet both completions descend from the same single physical equation,
unifying the two mathematical traditions through one principle. A single physical equation $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
simultaneously supplies what Klein's group-theoretic programme lacked
(the physical generator selecting the Klein pair, Route 1), and replaces
Klein's primitive with a deeper categorical primitive (the source-pair
$(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$, Route 2).
:::

::: {#rmk:why-erlangen-matters .remark}
*Remark 17.26* (Why the Erlangen completion matters for the textbook).
The two-route Erlangen completion has a direct bearing on the
architecture of this textbook. Route 1 (group-theoretic) supplies the
reason why the Lorentz group, the gauge groups of the
Standard Model, and the diffeomorphism group of general relativity are
the right symmetry groups --- not by empirical fit but as the consequence of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$'s selection of
$(\mathrm{ISO}(1,3), \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3))$. Route 2 (category-theoretic)
supplies the reason why the Hilbert space, Clifford algebra,
principal bundles, and $C^*$-algebras of mathematical physics are the
right algebraic objects to host the dynamics: they are
downstream-functor images of the source-pair under (D1)--(D6). The
textbook's Part II (QM T1--T23) and Part III (Hilbert-space
applications) supply the physical content within these algebraic
objects; the content explaining *why these are the right
objects* is supplied by Category McG and the source-pair, via
[@MG-Hilbert6-2026].
:::

construction). The punchline is: *the McGucken source-pair

#### From geometric nonlocality to quantum probability {#from-geometric-nonlocality-to-quantum-probability .unnumbered}

The six-fold identity is the geometric foundation; the connection to
quantum probability is the corresponding ontic content.

::: {#thm:geometric-to-quantum-probability .theorem}
**Theorem 17.28** (From geometric nonlocality to quantum probability;
[@MG-NonlocalityPrinciple-2026] §4.8). *The same geometric identity that
produces nonlocality
(Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}) also produces the Born rule
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}). Because the expansion of $x_4$ is
spherically symmetric, the rotation group $SO(3)$ acts transitively on
the expanding sphere $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$. By the uniqueness of the Haar
measure on the compact group $SO(3)$, the only probability measure on
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ invariant under $SO(3)$ is the uniform measure. A
photon surfing the expanding wavefront inhabits the entire sphere of
nonlocality with equal geometric weight --- there is no geometric
structure that distinguishes one point from another --- until a
measurement event localizes it in three spatial dimensions.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* **Step 1: Spherical symmetry of the $x_{4}$-expansion.** By
clause (P2) of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, the $x_{4}$-expansion at rate
$ic$ from event $p_0$ is spherically symmetric in the three spatial
dimensions. The McGucken Sphere wavefront $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ at parameter
time $t$ is the locus
$$M^{+}_{p_0}(t) = \{x \in \Sigma_t : |x - x(p_0)| = ct\},$$ which is
$SO(3)$-invariant about the spatial location $x(p_0)$.

**Step 2: $SO(3)$ acts transitively on $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$.** The 2-sphere
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ is a homogeneous space under the $SO(3)$ action: any
two points on the wavefront are related by some rotation about $x(p_0)$.
Formally, $M^{+}_{p_0}(t) \cong SO(3)/SO(2)$ as a homogeneous space,
where $SO(2)$ is the stabiliser of any chosen wavefront point (the
subgroup of rotations about the axis through $x(p_0)$ and that point).

**Step 3: Uniqueness of the Haar measure on compact groups.** The Haar
uniqueness theorem (a standard result in harmonic analysis on compact
Lie groups; modern textbook treatment in Folland--Sitaram
[@FollandSitaram1997] and standard harmonic-analysis references) states
that on any compact group $G$, there is a unique (up to normalisation)
probability measure invariant under the group action. For $G = SO(3)$
acting on the homogeneous space $SO(3)/SO(2) \cong S^2$, the unique
$SO(3)$-invariant probability measure projects to the standard
rotation-invariant probability measure on $S^2$, given in standard
spherical coordinates by
$d\mu(\theta, \varphi) = \frac{1}{4\pi}\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$.

**Step 4: Geometric weight of the wavefront.** A photon (or matter
wavefront) inhabiting the McGucken Sphere $S_{p_0}$ at parameter time
$t$ has its support on the entire 2-sphere $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$. The only
$SO(3)$-invariant probability measure assigning weight to wavefront
points is the uniform measure of Step 3. There is no geometric structure
on the bare wavefront that distinguishes one point from another ---
until a measurement event localises the wavefunction at a specific
point.

**Step 5: Born density on the wavefront.** Modulating the uniform Haar
measure by the wavefunction's amplitude $|\psi|^2$ produces the
Born-rule probability density
$$d\Pr(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2\,d\mu(\mathbf{x}),$$ which is
the unique geometric measure compatible with the $SO(3)$-symmetry of the
expansion and the amplitude profile of the wavefront. The Born rule has
the reading of a unique geometric calibration of probability
to wavefront intensity forced by spherical symmetry of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with the role of an additional postulate
replaced by the role of a derived consequence of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii) (spherical symmetry of the
$x_{4}$-expansion) combined with the Haar-uniqueness theorem on the
compact group $SO(3)$.

**Step 6: Two-faces statement.**
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"} establishes that the McGucken Sphere
is simultaneously (i) a Huygens caustic, (ii) the boundary of
nonlocality, (iii) a null hypersurface cross-section, etc. The
probabilistic Born-rule reading and the nonlocal-correlation reading
both descend from the same $SO(3)$-symmetric wavefront: probability is
the wavefront's $SO(3)$-invariant intensity calibration; nonlocality is
the wavefront's $SO(3)$-invariant identity calibration. Both arise from
the same source --- the expanding $x_{4}$ --- and are quantitatively
linked by the McGucken No-Signaling Theorem
(Theorem [17.32](#thm:mcgucken-no-signaling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcgucken-no-signaling"}). ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:nonlocality-probability-one-source .remark}
*Remark 17.29* (The punchline). Quantum probability has the
reading of a direct geometric consequence of the wavefront's
nonlocal identity: the photon has equal probability of being found at
any point on $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ because all points share the same
geometric identity in all six senses of
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}, with the role of an additional
postulate replaced by the role of a derived consequence of the
wavefront's $SO(3)$-invariant geometry. *Nonlocality and probability
arise from the same source --- the expanding fourth dimension --- and
the McGucken Nonlocality Principle and the Born rule are two faces of
one geometric fact.* The McGucken No-Signaling Theorem of
§[17.5](#sec:no-signaling){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:no-signaling"} below makes this two-faces statement
quantitative: nonlocality saturates Tsirelson at $2\sqrt 2$ from the
wavefront identity, probability gives $SO(3)$-flat marginals from the
wavefront intensity, and the joint exactness is forced by the single
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$-symmetry.
:::

#### The New York--Los Angeles falsifiability test {#the-new-yorklos-angeles-falsifiability-test .unnumbered}

The McGucken Nonlocality Principle makes a concrete, falsifiable
prediction.

::: {#rmk:NY-LA-challenge .remark}
*Remark 17.30* (The New York--Los Angeles Challenge;
[@MG-NonlocalityPrinciple-2026] §3). Consider two electrons: electron
$A$ in a laboratory in New York, electron $B$ in a laboratory in Los
Angeles. Both positions, spins, and momenta are continuously measured.
The experimentalists determine that no correlation between the
measurements obtains; they conclude $A$ and $B$ are not entangled. The
McGucken Nonlocality Principle predicts: *it is impossible to entangle
$A$ and $B$ without some form of local contact, either directly or
through a locally originated intermediary.*

To falsify the principle, one would need to demonstrate a method
satisfying *all* of the following:

1.  the electrons are never brought into direct local contact;

2.  no intermediary particle or system that has shared a local origin is
    used to mediate the entanglement;

3.  the entanglement is established faster than the velocity of light,
    i.e., without waiting for any signal or system to travel from one
    laboratory to the other.

If such a method can be demonstrated, the principle is falsified. If no
such method can be found --- either experimentally or in any thought
experiment consistent with known physics --- then the principle stands.
Every known method for entangling distant particles (entanglement
swapping in particular) requires a locally originated intermediary; the
principle is therefore consistent with the entire empirical record of
quantum information, and it makes a sharp prediction --- that the
empirical record will continue to require such intermediaries --- that
is in principle falsifiable.
:::

::: {#rmk:double-slit-eraser-delayed .remark}
*Remark 17.31* (Double-slit, quantum eraser, delayed-choice as
McGucken-Sphere phenomena). A consequence of
Theorems [17.4](#thm:first-law-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:first-law-nonlocality"}--[17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}: the double-slit experiment, the
quantum-eraser experiment, and Wheeler's delayed-choice experiment all
take place within the confines of a single McGucken Sphere (or a network
of intersecting Spheres). In each case, the apparent paradox dissolves
once the full four-dimensional geometry of the expanding $x_4$ is
recognized: *within a McGucken Sphere, no $x_{4}$-advance accumulates between any two events on the wavefront --- a frame-independent consequence of the photon's vanishing share $v_{x_4} = 0$.* What a three-dimensional observer
describes as "the past" (the slit crossing) is separated from the detection by zero accumulated $x_{4}$-advance; what is described as "a future detection
setting choice" (the delayed-choice eraser) is simultaneous with the
slit crossing on the same wavefront. The paradoxes of these experiments
are artefacts of the three-dimensional projection; the geometry of the
McGucken Sphere is paradox-free.
:::

### The McGucken No-Signaling Theorem: probability cloaks nonlocality {#sec:no-signaling}

The textbook no-signaling theorem (Ghirardi--Rimini--Weber 1980
[@GhirardiRimini1980]; Eberhard 1978 [@Eberhard1978]; Bussey 1982
[@Bussey1982]) states that the maximal Bell-CHSH violation $2\sqrt{2}$
exhibited by entangled pairs cannot be used to transmit a message faster
than light. Its standard derivation is purely algebraic: the marginal
$P(a \mid x) = \sum_b P(a, b \mid x, y)$ at Alice's detector is
independent of Bob's setting $y$ by the trace-preserving property of
completely positive maps applied to the partial trace over Bob's
subsystem. The derivation works equally well in any flat-space algebraic
formalism with no metric, no light cone, and no specific spacetime
structure. This is why no-signaling has historically appeared as an
unmotivated coexistence between nonlocality (which requires
faster-than-light correlations) and relativistic causality (which
forbids faster-than-light signaling): the two are reconciled
algebraically but not physically. Shimony called this the puzzle of
*peaceful coexistence*.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reformulates the no-signaling theorem as a
property of the physical apparatus itself rather than of the algebraic
formalism. The result, with its corollaries, is the canonical resolution
of the peaceful-coexistence puzzle; the source paper is
[@MG-NonlocalityProb-2026] §6.4.

::: {#thm:mcgucken-no-signaling .theorem}
**Theorem 17.32** (McGucken No-Signaling Theorem: probability cloaks
nonlocality; building on [@MG-NonlocalityProb-2026] §5.5). *Let $A$ and
$B$ be two subsystems on a shared McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$, with
joint state $\rho_{AB}$ inherited from the wavefront identity at the
common source event $p_0$. Let $\{\hat{M}_a^{A,x}\}_a$ and
$\{\hat{M}_b^{B,y}\}_b$ be Alice's and Bob's local measurement settings
(POVMs) at detection events $p_A, p_B$ on the wavefront. Then:*

1.  **(Geometric nonlocality.)* The joint statistics
    $$P(a, b \mid x, y) = \operatorname{tr}\!\left[\bigl(\hat{M}_a^{A,x} \otimes \hat{M}_b^{B,y}\bigr)\,\rho_{AB}\right]$$
    exhibit the full Tsirelson-bound violation of CHSH, with singlet
    correlation $E(a, b) = -\hat{a}\cdot\hat{b}$ saturating
    $|\langle CHSH\rangle| = 2\sqrt{2}$, as a direct geometric
    consequence of shared null-hypersurface origin at $p_0$.*

2.  **(Marginal flatness.)* For each detector, the marginal probability
    $$P(a \mid x) = \sum_b P(a, b \mid x, y) = |\psi_A^x|^2$$ is
    independent of the distant setting $y$, by the $SO(3)$-symmetry of
    $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ and the Born rule applied separately to each
    subsystem (Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}); and similarly
    $P(b \mid y) = |\psi_B^y|^2$.*

3.  **(No-signaling as cloaking.)* The geometric nonlocal channel of (i)
    carries no usable information. The statistics that saturate the
    Tsirelson bound in (i) are the very same statistics that render the
    marginals flat in (ii); a single $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$-induced
    geometric fact enforces both. This is the no-signaling theorem
    stated as a property of the physical apparatus
    $(M_{G}, \mathcal{F}_M)$, not of the algebraic formalism.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has four steps establishing each part (i),
(ii), (iii) of the theorem and synthesising the no-signaling cloak. The
theorem descends from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, the physical, geometric fact that the fourth
dimension expands at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric
manner): the shared McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ at common source
event $p_0$ is generated by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i) invariance and (ii) spherical
symmetry, with $x_4 = ict$ the integrated kinematic shadow per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}.

**Step 1: Part (i) --- Tsirelson saturation from $SO(3)$-Haar on the
shared wavefront.** The shared-wavefront content of
[@MG-NonlocalityProb-2026] §5.5 applied to the singlet wavefront on
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ gives the singlet correlation
$E(a, b) = -\hat{a}\cdot\hat{b} = -\cos\theta_{ab}$ as the $SO(3)$-Haar
inner product on the wavefront 2-sphere --- the unique $SO(3)$-invariant
antisymmetric correlation on the shared null-hypersurface cross-section
(Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}).
Theorem [13.1](#thm:QMT13){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT13"}
(Geometric Channel, Step B-2 of Tsirelson) showed that with the optimal settings
$\hat{a} = \hat{z}, \hat{a}' = \hat{x}, \hat{b} = (\hat{z}+\hat{x})/\sqrt{2}, \hat{b}' = (\hat{z}-\hat{x})/\sqrt{2}$,
the four singlet correlations combine to
$\langle CHSH\rangle = -2\sqrt{2}$. The geometric source of the
saturation is the shared null-hypersurface origin at $p_0$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i) invariance, with the same Sphere
generated at $p_0$ propagating to both Alice's and Bob's detection
events).

**Step 2: Part (ii) --- marginal flatness from POVM resolution of
identity and $SO(3)$-symmetry.** For a single-side operation
$\hat{M}_b^{B,y}$ acting on Bob's subsystem, the marginal at Alice is
$$P(a \mid x) = \sum_b \operatorname{tr}\!\left[\bigl(\hat{M}_a^{A,x} \otimes \hat{M}_b^{B,y}\bigr)\,\rho_{AB}\right] = \operatorname{tr}\!\left[\hat{M}_a^{A,x}\,\operatorname{tr}_B\bigl(\hat{\mathbb{1}}_B^y\,\rho_{AB}\bigr)\right]$$
where $\hat{\mathbb{1}}_B^y = \sum_b \hat{M}_b^{B,y}$ is the resolution
of identity on Bob's outcome space (a defining property of any POVM,
$\sum_b \hat{M}_b^{B,y} = \mathbb{1}_B$). Hence the marginal reduces to
$$P(a \mid x) = \operatorname{tr}_A\!\left[\hat{M}_a^{A,x}\,\rho_A\right], \qquad \rho_A := \operatorname{tr}_B \rho_{AB},$$
which is manifestly independent of $y$. The Geometric Channel reading of this
algebraic identity: the reduced state $\rho_A$ is the slice projection
$\sigma$ (Lemma [9.1](#lem:suppression-map){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:suppression-map"}) of the wavefront $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ onto
Alice's spatial region $\Sigma_A$; this projection is invariant under
any operation applied to Bob's spatial region $\Sigma_B$ because the
Sphere is $SO(3)$-homogeneous about $p_0$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii) spherical symmetry) and the
foliation of $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ into Alice's and Bob's regions is itself
$SO(3)$-invariant. The flatness of the marginal is the geometric
statement of the $SO(3)$-Haar measure's invariance under any single-side
group action.

**Step 3: Part (iii) --- no-signaling as cloaking, synthesis of (i) and
(ii).** Combining (i) and (ii): the same $SO(3)$-Haar structure on
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ (forced by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii) spherical symmetry of the
$x_{4}$-expansion) that produces the singlet correlation
$-\hat{a}\cdot\hat{b}$ saturating Tsirelson (Step 1) also produces the
rotationally invariant marginal $|\psi_A^x|^2$ at each detector (Step
2). A single geometric fact --- the $SO(3)$ symmetry of the McGucken
Sphere generated by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at $p_0$ --- simultaneously
calibrates the maximally nonlocal joint correlations and the marginal
flatness that hides them from observers.

**Step 4: Cloaking forced by geometry, not algebra.** The two phenomena
of Steps 1 and 2 have the reading of two readings of one
geometric object (the McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$,
Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:sphere"}), rather than the role of two separate algebraic
facts requiring separate reconciliation. Hence no message is
transmissible through the nonlocal channel: probability cloaks
nonlocality, with the cloak forced by the same expansion that creates
the channel. The cancellation between nonlocality and
signaling sits at the level of the geometry of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$,
with the cancellation reading as a geometric consequence of the single
$SO(3)$-Haar structure on $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ rather than as an
algebraic-axiom-level identity: there is no parameter in the McGucken
framework that could be tuned to introduce a small no-signaling
violation, because the $SO(3)$-Haar measure is canonical (unique by
Haar's theorem on compact Lie groups) and the wavefront geometry is
fixed by Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}. The result is exact at every separation
(Hensen et al. [@Hensen2015], loophole-free Bell test confirming
no-signaling exactness to within experimental precision across 1.3 km).
$\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#cor:no-signaling-exact .corollary}
**Corollary 17.33** (Exactness of the no-signaling cancellation at the
geometric level). *The no-signaling theorem is exact at the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework level, with the role of an approximate or low-energy
effective statement replaced by the role of a geometric identity. The
reason: the wavefront $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ is the one and only
object on which both nonlocality and probability live. Any deformation
of one is a deformation of the other; the cancellation sits at the level
of the geometry, with the cancellation reading as a geometric
consequence rather than as an algebraic identity. This is also the
reason for the exact saturation of
$|\langle CHSH\rangle| = 2\sqrt{2}$ across forty years of Bell
experiments at separations from millimetres to 1200 km [@Hensen2015]:
the saturation and the no-signaling are two consequences of one
geometric fact.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: No approximation in the parent theorem.** The
exactness follows from inspection of the proof of
Theorem [17.32](#thm:mcgucken-no-signaling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcgucken-no-signaling"}. Part (i) (Tsirelson saturation
by the singlet) descends from the exact $SO(3)$-invariance of the
spin-correlation function on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$: the singlet two-point correlation
$E(\hat a, \hat b) = \langle\Psi^-, (\vec\sigma_A\cdot\hat a)\otimes(\vec\sigma_B\cdot\hat b)\,\Psi^-\rangle = -\hat a\cdot\hat b$
is the unique $SO(3)$-invariant antisymmetric two-point correlation on
the shared wavefront, with the spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ representation of
$\mathrm{Spin}(1,3) = SL(2,\mathbb{C})$
(Lemma [9.4](#lem:spin-double-cover){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:spin-double-cover"}) supplying both the antisymmetry
(from the singlet's total spin $S = 0$ rotational character) and the
unit-strength normalisation (from
$2\,\vec\sigma_A\cdot\vec\sigma_B = (\vec\sigma_A+\vec\sigma_B)^2 - \vec\sigma_A^2 - \vec\sigma_B^2 = 4S(S+1)\,\mathbf{1} - 6\,\mathbf{1}$,
evaluating to $-6\,\mathbf{1}$ on the singlet's $S = 0$ subspace).
The explicit closed-form computation appears in
Theorem [13.1](#thm:QMT13){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT13"} Step 4 (Geometric Channel Step B-2 of the Tsirelson
proof), a closed-form algebraic identity with no approximation.
Part (ii) (marginal flatness at each detector) is the POVM
resolution-of-identity $\sum_b \hat{M}_b^{B,y} = \mathbf{1}_B$
combined with the $SO(3)$-homogeneity of $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ about $p_0$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii)); both factors are exact. The
combined no-signaling statement is therefore exact at every step of the
derivation.

**Step 2: Reason for exactness.** The wavefront
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ is the one and only object on which both nonlocality
(its identity across spatial separation) and probability (its $|\psi|^2$
intensity) live. Any deformation of one face of the wavefront is
necessarily a deformation of the other; the cancellation sits at the
level of the geometry, with the cancellation reading as a geometric
consequence of the wavefront's $SO(3)$-Haar structure rather than as an
algebraic-axiom-level identity. There is no parameter in the McGucken
framework that could be tuned to introduce a small no-signaling
violation: the $SO(3)$-Haar measure is canonical (unique by Haar's
theorem on compact Lie groups), and the wavefront geometry is fixed by
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

**Step 3: Empirical signature.** The forty-year empirical record of
exact no-signaling and exact Tsirelson saturation across thirteen orders
of magnitude in detector separation (millimetres for early Aspect
experiments [@Aspect1982] to 1200 km for the Hensen et al. 2015
loophole-free test [@Hensen2015], with the Cosmic Bell Test reaching
$\sim 10^{12}$ km via stellar correlations) is the empirical signature
of this exactness. Any approximation that gave
$|\langle CHSH\rangle| = 2\sqrt{2} + \epsilon$ for $\epsilon \neq 0$
would manifest experimentally; no such deviation has been observed. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:two-faces .corollary}
**Corollary 17.34** (Two faces of one expansion;
[@MG-NonlocalityProb-2026] §5 and [@MG-NonlocalityPrinciple-2026] §4.8
jointly). *The two "strange features" of quantum mechanics historically
taken as independent --- instantaneous nonlocal correlation
(Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen 1935 [@EPR1935]; Bell 1964 [@Bell1964];
Aspect 1982 [@Aspect1982]) and irreducible probability (Born 1926
[@Born1926]; Heisenberg 1927 [@Heisenberg1927]) --- have the reading of two faces of a single geometric primitive. Each face has the
role of a projection of the single expansion $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$:
*nonlocality is the wavefront's identity*; *probability is the
wavefront's intensity*; and the relation between them is precisely the
no-signaling theorem stated geometrically
(Theorem [17.32](#thm:mcgucken-no-signaling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcgucken-no-signaling"}). The Born rule
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}) gives the intensity; the Tsirelson
saturation (Theorem [13.1](#thm:QMT13){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT13"}) gives the identity; the no-signaling theorem
above gives their mutual calibration.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The corollary identifies two faces of one McGucken-Sphere
wavefront. We argue in three steps.

**Step 1: Nonlocality is the wavefront's identity.** By
Theorem [17.7](#thm:intersecting-spheres-transfer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:intersecting-spheres-transfer"} (Intersecting-Sphere
transfer of entanglement) and
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"} clauses (F4) and (F6), the singlet
wavefront from a common source event $p_0$ is a single McGucken Sphere
whose identity at each spatial cross-section $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ is
preserved across spatial separation. The EPR-Bell correlation
$E(\hat a, \hat b) = -\cos\theta_{ab}$ is the inner product of two
arrays measured on the same wavefront --- the wavefront's spatial
identity manifested as correlation. The Tsirelson saturation at
$|E_{\mathrm{singlet}}| = 2\sqrt{2}$
(Theorem [13.1](#thm:QMT13){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT13"})
is the geometric saturation of this identity at the maximum allowed by
the spherical $SO(3)$-symmetric structure (cf. §4.5 of
[@MG-NonlocalityPrinciple-2026]).

**Step 2: Probability is the wavefront's intensity.** The Born rule
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}, derived along Geometric Channel via
Theorem [17.28](#thm:geometric-to-quantum-probability){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:geometric-to-quantum-probability"}) gives
$P(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ as the registration probability
at spatial point $\mathbf{x}$ on the wavefront. This is the
intensity-distribution face of the same Sphere: amplitude squared per
Planck-area cell of $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$, weighted by the $SO(3)$-Haar
measure on the Sphere's spherical symmetry. The probability density is
the intensity of the wavefront, not an independent stochastic
ingredient.

**Step 3: No-signaling is the geometric calibration.** The McGucken
No-Signaling
Theorem [17.32](#thm:mcgucken-no-signaling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcgucken-no-signaling"} establishes that the wavefront's
identity (Step 1) and its intensity (Step 2) are calibrated exactly so
that no marginal-probability difference can be transmitted between two
spatial regions of the wavefront --- even though the wavefront's spatial
identity is single. The exact cancellation between marginal-probability
variation and conditional-correlation strength is the no-signaling
content, derived geometrically rather than algebraically.

Combining Steps 1--3: nonlocality (the identity face) and probability
(the intensity face) have the reading of two aspects of one
wavefront $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ sourced by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at $p_0$,
calibrated by no-signaling. The two have the role of one geometric
structure read in two ways, with the role of two independent
quantum-theoretic features replaced by the role of two projections of
one $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$-generated object. $\square$ ◻
:::

#### The reciprocal identity: relativity is $x_{4}$'s nonlocality, and $x_{4}$'s nonlocality is relativity's null structure {#the-reciprocal-identity-relativity-is-x_4s-nonlocality-and-x_4s-nonlocality-is-relativitys-null-structure .unnumbered}

The Two-Faces corollary above identifies the two features of
quantum mechanics (nonlocality + probability) as two faces of one
wavefront. A sharper identification, developed in
[@MG-Forcing-2026] (May 21, 2026; posted May 30, 2026) along three
independent proof routes, completes the unification by making
the channel-readings of *relativity* and of *nonlocality* reciprocal:
each is the other read through the alternate channel.

::: {#thm:reciprocal-identity-relativity-nonlocality .theorem}
**Theorem 17.35** (Reciprocal identity of relativity and quantum
nonlocality; [@MG-Forcing-2026] §1 Step 3.5, §12.3, and §14). *Under the
McGucken Principle $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}), the null structure of relativity and the
quantum nonlocality of the McGucken Sphere stand in a *reciprocal
Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel identity*:*

1.  **Algebraic Channel reading.* Relativity has the reading of
    $x_{4}$'s nonlocality. The Lorentz-invariant null structure of
    spacetime --- the future light cone of an event $p$, on which the
    radii from $p$ to each cone-point are null vectors of zero spacetime
    length --- is the algebraic-symmetry shadow of the spherical
    $x_{4}$-expansion from $p$ at rate $ic$, read by Algebraic Channel through
    Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-arena"} (Lorentzian arena) and
    Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:six-fold-identity"} clause (F6) (null-hypersurface
    cross-section).*

2.  **Geometric Channel reading.* $x_{4}$'s nonlocality has the reading of relativity's null structure. The Tsirelson saturation
    $|\langle CHSH\rangle| = 2\sqrt{2}$ and the spatial-cross-section
    nonlocality of $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ are the geometric-propagation shadow
    of the same null-cone configuration, read by Geometric Channel through
    Theorem [17.7](#thm:intersecting-spheres-transfer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:intersecting-spheres-transfer"} (Intersecting-Sphere
    transfer of entanglement) and
    Theorem [13.1](#thm:QMT13){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT13"} (Tsirelson saturation on the wavefront).*

3.  **Equivalence of (R1) and (R2).* The two readings produce
    theorem-by-theorem-equivalent empirical content through derivationally
    disjoint intermediate machinery. In particular, breaking the
    null-cone structure (any single Lorentz violation, e.g. Mode D of
    [@MG-Uniqueness-2026]) breaks Tsirelson saturation simultaneously,
    and breaking Tsirelson saturation (any single failure of the
    wavefront's $x_{4}$-coherent identity, Modes A--C of
    [@MG-Uniqueness-2026]) breaks the null-cone structure
    simultaneously. The two are co-failed by any perturbation of
    sphere-surface $x_{4}$-locality
    (Theorem [11.10](#thm:uniqueness-mcgucken-sphere){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:uniqueness-mcgucken-sphere"}).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has six steps establishing the reciprocal
Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel reading of relativity and nonlocality.

**Step 1: Null-vector geometry of the McGucken Sphere (the bridge
fact).** By Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:sphere"} and
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"} clause (F6), every point
$q \in M^{+}_{p}(t)$ is connected to the apex $p$ by a worldline along
which the Minkowski spacetime separation vanishes:
$\Delta s^2 = -c^2(t - t_p)^2 + |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p|^2 = 0$,
because the spatial separation
$|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t - t_p)$ is set by the sphere's
radius. The radii from $p$ to each $q \in M^{+}_{p}(t)$ have the
role of *null vectors of zero spacetime length*, in the
precise Minkowski-metric sense established by Minkowski (1908) and
standardised across special relativity. The word "null" has the role of
recording this zero-spacetime-length property explicitly: the events $p$
and $q$ are at zero spacetime distance from each other in the Lorentzian
metric, even though they are spatially separated by $c(t - t_p)$ in the
spatial three. Every pair of points $q_1, q_2 \in M^{+}_{p}(t)$ on the sphere is joined to the source by a null radius of zero spacetime length. The *radius* of the McGucken Sphere is a null vector; the *chord* between two points on it is not. For two points separated by angle $\theta$ on the wavefront at coordinate time $t$, $$s^{2}(q_1, q_2) \;=\; 2c^{2}(t-t_p)^{2}\bigl(1 - \cos\theta\bigr),$$ which vanishes at $\theta = 0$ (two points on one null generator, where the relation is transitive along the ray) and is maximal at $\theta = \pi$, the diameter: $s^{2} = 4c^{2}(t-t_p)^{2}$, the back-to-back emission of an entangled pair. The chord is therefore *spacelike*, $s^2(q_1, q_2) > 0$, and this is the content of the phenomenon rather than an obstacle to it: correlated outcomes registered at null-separated events would be ordinary signal propagation, and what makes entanglement remarkable is that the outcomes agree across a separation no signal crosses. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies the object that carries the correlation across it. Both registrations lie on one McGucken Sphere --- the single physically expanding wavefront generated at the emission event $p$ by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, carrying one $SO(3)$-Haar measure and one quantum of action. In the fourth dimension the two registrations are not separated at all: each photon travels a null worldline, so $d\tau = 0$ pointwise and the accumulated $x_{4}$-advance is $X_{4}(q_1) = X_{4}(q_2) = X_{4}(p) = 0$. The separation between the two detections is purely spatial --- $2c(t-t_p)$ for a back-to-back pair, $2400$ km in the Yin 2017 Micius configuration --- with zero separation in $x_{4}$. One expanding front, two spacelike-separated registrations on it: the correlation is carried by the shared front, and no interval between the detection events is invoked. This is the
bridge fact on which Steps 2--3 below depend.

**Step 2: Algebraic Channel reading --- Lorentz null structure as $x_{4}$'s
nonlocality (clause R1).** The Lorentz-invariant null hypersurface ---
the future light cone of $p$ --- is generated by
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at $p$ via
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}: the Lorentzian arena $M_{1,3}$ is
generated by $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ from the Euclidean manifold $M_E$
via the embedding $\iota: (t, \mathbf{x}) \mapsto (\mathbf{x}, ict)$,
with the imaginary unit $i$ in $x_{4}= ict$ flipping the sign of the
$x_{4}$-diagonal of the metric under pullback to produce the Lorentzian
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ from the Euclidean signature $(+,+,+,+)$ on the
complexified embedding. The null hypersurface is the locus on which the
resulting Lorentzian line element $ds^2 = -c^2\,dt^2 + |d\mathbf{x}|^2$
vanishes, which by Step 1 is the surface of zero spacetime distance from
$p$. Read in Algebraic Channel's algebraic-symmetry language, this surface has
the reading of $x_{4}$'s nonlocality: the set of events that
share zero spacetime distance from $p$ through the $x_{4}$-expansion is
the geometric expression of the principle that $x_{4}$ advances
perpendicular to all three spatial directions equally (clause (ii) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, spherical symmetry) and at the universal
rate $ic$ (clauses (i) and (v) jointly). The Lorentz invariance of the
speed of light $c$ across all frames is the algebraic-symmetry shadow of
the same $x_{4}$-rate $ic$ being preserved by the proper orthochronous
Lorentz group $SO^+(1,3)$ acting on the embedding
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, Step 6). This establishes clause (R1):
relativity has the role of $x_{4}$'s nonlocality read along
Algebraic Channel.

**Step 3: Geometric Channel reading --- $x_{4}$'s nonlocality as null cone
structure (clause R2).** The Tsirelson saturation
$|\langle CHSH\rangle| = 2\sqrt{2}$ and the spatial-cross-section
nonlocality of the McGucken Sphere are produced by Geometric Channel as the
geometric-propagation shadow of the same null-cone configuration. By
Theorem [17.7](#thm:intersecting-spheres-transfer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:intersecting-spheres-transfer"} (Intersecting-Sphere
transfer of entanglement), an entangled pair produced at a common source
event $p_0$ shares the same McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ at every
$t > t_0$; the two-particle wavefunction restricted to detector
positions on $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ has the role of the unique
singlet state on the shared wavefront. By
Theorem [13.1](#thm:QMT13){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT13"}
(CHSH/Tsirelson), the singlet correlation
$E(\hat a, \hat b) = -\cos\theta_{ab}$ saturates the Tsirelson bound on
the wavefront's $SO(3)$-Haar structure. Read in Geometric Channel's
geometric-propagation language, the wavefront's $x_{4}$-coherent
identity has the reading of the same null surface that
Algebraic Channel produced as the light cone: the two detector points
$q_1, q_2 \in M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ are at zero spacetime distance from each
other through the source (by Step 1), and the Bell-test correlation at
the Tsirelson bound is the empirical signature of this
zero-spacetime-distance reading. The 1200 km spatial separation in the
Yin 2017 Micius satellite Bell test [@Yin2017] is therefore the
spatial-three-projection of a zero spacetime separation in the
four-dimensional manifold --- exactly the identification that
Step 3.5 of [@MG-Forcing-2026] establishes. This establishes clause
(R2): $x_{4}$'s nonlocality has the role of relativity's null
structure read along Geometric Channel.

**Step 4: Theorem-by-theorem equivalence via the Signature-Bridging
Theorem (clause R3, first half).** By the Signature-Bridging Theorem
(Theorem 106 of [@Syn-2026], imported from the three-channel paper), the
Algebraic Channel reading of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the Geometric Channel reading
produce theorem-by-theorem-equivalent empirical content through
derivationally disjoint intermediate machinery. In the present context:
Algebraic Channel delivers the Lorentzian metric
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}) and the Lorentz invariance of $c$ (§6 of
Chapter [9](#ch:hilbert-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:hilbert-theorem"}, the algebraic-symmetry route via

$E(\hat a, \hat b) = -\cos\theta_{ab}$

Theorem [13.1](#thm:QMT13){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT13"}),

**Step 5: Co-failure under perturbation (clause R3, second half).** The

**Step 6: McGucken anchoring and conclusion.** The reciprocal

nonlocality have the role of two channel-readings of a single

::: {#rmk:null-vector-formalism-was-recording .remark}
*Remark 17.36* (The null-vector formalism was always recording this).
The null-vector formalism that Minkowski wrote down in 1908 has been the
standard mathematical structure of special relativity for over a
century. The word "null" was chosen to record that null vectors have
zero spacetime length under the Lorentzian inner product, even though
they are non-zero as vectors in the four-dimensional manifold. The radii
from $p$ to every point on the future light cone of $p$ are null vectors
by the Minkowski metric:
$\Delta s^2 = -c^2(t-t_p)^2 + |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p|^2 = 0$ on the
cone. What the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework recognises ([@MG-Forcing-2026] §1 Step
3.5) is the physical content of this metric fact that the standard
reading had left unconnected. If every event on the McGucken Sphere is at zero spacetime distance from the source $p$ along a null radius, so that all of them belong to one Sphere generated at one event and all sit at the same $x_{4}$-advance $X_{4} = 0$, then in the spatial-three projection where we observe these
events to be widely separated --- 1200 km in the Yin 2017 Micius
experiment, of order $10^7$ to $10^9$ m in upcoming lunar-distance Bell
tests, and cosmological scales in delayed-choice experiments through
gravitational lenses --- the zero spacetime separation manifests as the
empirical phenomenon called *nonlocality*. The Tsirelson saturation at
$|\langle CHSH\rangle| = 2\sqrt{2}$ is the empirical signature of zero
spacetime distance through the source. Einstein's "spooky action at a
distance" has the reading of no action at a distance in the
spacetime metric: the distance was always zero in the Lorentzian metric,
with the spatial three only being the slice on which the zero is
projected as the appearance of separation. The reciprocal identity of
Theorem [17.35](#thm:reciprocal-identity-relativity-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:reciprocal-identity-relativity-nonlocality"} is therefore
the recognition of what the null-vector formalism has been recording
since 1908.
:::

::: {#rmk:three-independent-proofs-converge .remark}
*Remark 17.37* (Three independent proofs converging on the same
reciprocal identity). The reciprocal Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel identity is
independently forced by three and empirically disjoint
routes [@MG-Forcing-2026]: (i) the commonsense Bell-test proof, via the
null-vector geometry of Step 1 of
Theorem [17.35](#thm:reciprocal-identity-relativity-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:reciprocal-identity-relativity-nonlocality"} and the
Tsirelson saturation across the four-decade Bell-test record; (ii) the
GPS Forcing Theorem, via the non-reciprocal time-dilation of the GPS
constellation, with the seven-alternative case-exhaustion ($H_1$--$H_7$
of [@MG-Forcing-2026] §2 Lemma 3) leaving $H_7 = \dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
as the unique survivor; (iii) the Axiomatic Foundational Proof,
deductive from four Minkowski-geometry axioms plus
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ stated ontologically, with five lemmas closing
the chain. The three proofs use disjoint inputs (no quantum-mechanical
input in (ii) or (iii); no GPS input in (i) or (iii); no axiomatic
deductive content in (i) or (ii)), and meet at $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
because $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the unique principle they have in
common. This three-fold convergence has the role of an empirical
signature of a true physical principle, with the role of three
independent confirmations of one fact replaced by the role of three
channel-readings of the single $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$-generated
geometric primitive that underlies relativity's null structure and
quantum mechanics' nonlocality jointly.
:::

::: {#rmk:why-standard-no-signaling-insufficient .remark}
*Remark 17.38* (Why the standard no-signaling derivation cannot supply
the geometric content). The Ghirardi--Rimini--Weber
[@GhirardiRimini1980], Eberhard [@Eberhard1978], and Bussey
[@Bussey1982] derivations of no-signaling proceed entirely within the
algebraic formalism: linearity of QM, completely positive
trace-preserving maps, partial trace reducing to the same density matrix
regardless of distant operations. None of these ingredients carries any
geometric information about *why* the nonlocal correlation should
exactly cancel against the marginal flatness in the way required for
no-signaling. The standard derivation works --- it produces the correct
conclusion algebraically --- but it does not explain why the calibration
is exact rather than approximate, nor why the nonlocal correlation
saturates at $2\sqrt{2}$ rather than at some other value below the
no-signaling bound of $4$ (the Popescu--Rohrlich bound, achieved by
hypothetical PR-boxes which are not realized in nature). Both exactness
and the specific saturation value are calibrated by the geometry of the
McGucken Sphere; the standard algebraic derivation lacks the geometric
content and cannot supply the reason for either. The McGucken
No-Signaling Theorem above is the Geometric Channel reading; the standard
algebraic theorem is the Algebraic Channel reading; both are projections of the
same fact $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ acting at $p_0$ with full $SO(3)$
symmetry on the resulting wavefront.
:::

::: remark
*Remark 17.39* (Resolution of Shimony's "peaceful coexistence" puzzle).
The historical puzzle is that QM is genuinely nonlocal yet relativity is
preserved. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework explains the coexistence as a single
geometric fact: nonlocality and no-signaling have the role of two
readings of the same Sphere wavefront, with the wavefront *identity*
carrying the nonlocal correlation and the wavefront *intensity* carrying
the marginal probability statistics; the calibration between them is
forced by the $SO(3)$ symmetry of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ acting at the
source event $p_0$. The coexistence has the reading of a
peaceful coexistence because both features have the role of projections
of one object; the textbook formalism reads them as two algebraic facts
to be independently reconciled, while the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework reads them
as one fact viewed through two channels.
:::

## QM T18: Quantum Entanglement {#ch:entanglement}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial
three. Throughout this chapter, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ refers to this
principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: (i) *invariance* --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the
expansion is isotropic in the spatial three, with the set of events
reachable from $p$ in proper time $\tau$ being a 2-sphere of radius
$c\tau$; (iii) *monotonicity* --- the integral curve is strictly
monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of $x_4$-advance; (iv)
*Lorentz consistency* --- the structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on
$M_{G}$; (v) *global validity* --- $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at
every event of $M_{G}$. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ (Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the central fact.

### Statement

::: {#thm:QMT18 .theorem}
**Theorem 18.1** (QM T18: Entanglement, = Theorem 77 (Algebraic Channel) and
Theorem 100 (Geometric Channel) of [@Syn-2026]). *For two subsystems $A, B$ with
state
$\lvert \Psi \rangle_{AB} \in \mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$, the
Schmidt decomposition
$$\lvert \Psi \rangle_{AB} = \sum_n \sqrt{\lambda_n}\,\lvert a_n \rangle_A \otimes \lvert b_n \rangle_B$$
exists with orthonormal $\{\lvert a_n \rangle\}$,
$\{\lvert b_n \rangle\}$ and Schmidt coefficients $\lambda_n \ge 0$,
$\sum_n\lambda_n = 1$. The state is *entangled* iff more than one
$\lambda_n$ is nonzero. The von Neumann entanglement entropy
$$S_{\text{ent}}(\Psi) = -\sum_n \lambda_n \log\lambda_n$$ measures the
degree of entanglement, with $S_{\text{ent}} = 0$ for product states and
$S_{\text{ent}} = \log\dim\mathcal{H}_A$ for maximally entangled states
(when $\dim\mathcal{H}_A \le \dim\mathcal{H}_B$).*
:::

### Geometric Channel derivation: Non-factorisable joint Sphere wavefront

::: {#lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront .lemma}
**Lemma 18.5** (Joint wavefront from common source event is
single-valued, not factorisable). *When two particles $A$ and $B$ are
emitted from a common source event $p_0 \in M_{G}$ (e.g., singlet
creation in $\eta_c \to \gamma\gamma$ or atomic two-photon cascade), the
joint McGucken-Sphere wavefront is a single object $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ on
$M_{G}$, not the product of two independent wavefronts.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has six steps establishing the joint
wavefront from a common source as a single non-factorisable Sphere
object on the McGucken arena $M_{G}$.

**Step 1: Single source event sources a single Sphere.** By
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(v) (invariance and global
validity of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), every event $p \in M_{G}$ sources
a single McGucken Sphere $S_p$ via the $x_{4}$-expansion at rate $ic$,
and by clause (ii) (spherical symmetry), this Sphere is the unique
2-sphere of radius $c(t - t_p)$ centred on the spatial projection of $p$
(Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:sphere"}). The Sphere has a unique apex at $p$ and a
unique expanding wavefront $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ at every lab time $t > t_p$.
If two particles are emitted from the *same* source event $p_0$ (e.g.,
the singlet-creation point in $\eta_c \to \gamma\gamma$ or the
parametric down-conversion crystal in spontaneous parametric
down-conversion (SPDC)), they share the same Sphere: one source-apex at
$p_0$, one wavefront-locus $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$, one $x_{4}$-expansion
sourced at $p_0$. The two particles are not on separate Spheres --- they
ride the same Sphere from $p_0$, with the joint wavefront identity
established by the content of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (the
principle of joint-wavefront origin from a single source event is the
First Law of Nonlocality,
Theorem [17.4](#thm:first-law-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:first-law-nonlocality"}).

**Step 2: Joint wavefunction lives on the joint configuration space.**
The joint wavefunction $\Psi(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B, t)$ assigns an
amplitude to the pair of spatial locations
$(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B) \in \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}^3$ at
time $t$ for the two particles. The configuration space is the Cartesian
product $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}^3 = \mathbb{R}^6$, not two
independent copies of $\mathbb{R}^3$. By
Lemma [10.4](#lem:stone-vonNeumann-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:stone-vonNeumann-uniqueness"} (Stone--von Neumann
uniqueness QA4), the joint Hilbert space is the tensor product
$\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B = L^2(\mathbb{R}^3) \otimes L^2(\mathbb{R}^3) \cong L^2(\mathbb{R}^6)$.
This is a feature of multi-particle quantum mechanics: the
joint state lives in a higher-dimensional configuration space, not in
physical 3D space.

**Step 3: Non-factorisability --- product states are special.** A
product state
$\Psi(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B) = \psi_A(\mathbf{x}_A)\psi_B(\mathbf{x}_B)$
would correspond to two independent particles each on its own Sphere.
But Step 1 forces both particles onto the same Sphere from $p_0$. For
generic singlet emission, the joint wavefunction is non-factorisable: it
cannot be written as a product of single-particle wavefunctions on
$\mathbb{R}^3$ for $A$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ for $B$. The non-factorisable
subspace of $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ contains the entangled
states; the factorisable (product) states are a measure-zero subset
under the natural measure on the unit sphere of the joint Hilbert space.

**Step 4: Source-event symmetries impose correlations.** Conservation
laws at the source event $p_0$ impose correlations between $A$-branch
and $B$-branch properties (Noether's theorem applied to the source-event
symmetries; the Noether-McGucken machinery is established in
Lemma [16.2](#lem:QMT16-noether){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT16-noether"} as the Algebraic Channel reading of conservation
laws as theorems of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$):

-   Angular-momentum conservation ($J = 0$ for $\eta_c$-singlet
    emission) forces $\vec J_A + \vec J_B = 0$, hence the polarisation
    singlet
    $\lvert \Psi^- \rangle = (\lvert HV \rangle - \lvert VH \rangle)/\sqrt 2$;

-   Momentum conservation forces $\vec p_A + \vec p_B = \vec p_{p_0}$;

-   Energy conservation forces $E_A + E_B = E_{p_0}$.

These constraints cannot be separated into independent factors: the
polarisation singlet is non-factorisable; the momentum-momentum
correlation is non-factorisable; the energy-energy correlation is
non-factorisable.

**Step 5: Geometric content of entanglement.** The non-factorisability
is the geometric content of entanglement at the McGucken-Sphere level:
the joint Sphere wavefront from $p_0$ carries correlations between its
two propagating branches (the $A$-branch and the $B$-branch) that cannot
be decomposed into independent single-particle Spheres. The Sphere is a
single geometric object on $M_{G}$, not a tensor product of two Spheres.
The joint wavefunction $\Psi(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B, t)$ on the
joint configuration space encodes the correlation structure of this
single Sphere wavefront. By
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}, this same Sphere is simultaneously a
foliation leaf, a null-hypersurface cross-section of the future light
cone, a Huygens caustic, a Legendrian submanifold, a conformal-pencil
member, and an entropy-bearing wavefront --- six readings of
one geometric object.

**Step 6: McGucken anchoring and consequences.** The
joint-wavefront non-factorisability traces directly to the fact that a single source event sources a single Sphere (from
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i), (ii), (v) per Step 1, with the
integrated kinematic shadow $x_{4}= ict$ of
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"} supplying the coordinate label on the
wavefront). This is the geometric origin of:

-   EPR correlations (joint Sphere wavefront from a common source
    event);

-   Bell inequality violations (the joint Sphere's correlation structure
    is richer than any classical joint-distribution model --- Tsirelson
    saturation at $2\sqrt 2$, derived independently in
    Theorem [13.1](#thm:QMT13){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT13"});

-   Quantum nonlocality (the joint Sphere is a single 4D object, not two
    independent 3D wavefronts; correlations between distant detection
    events trace to the shared Sphere structure on $M_{G}$ ---
    formalised in the First and Second Laws of Nonlocality,
    Theorems [17.4](#thm:first-law-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:first-law-nonlocality"}
    and [17.5](#thm:second-law-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:second-law-nonlocality"}).

Entanglement has the reading of the geometric fact that
pair-emission from a common source event produces a single Sphere
wavefront, with the role of a mysterious correlation between separate
quantum systems replaced by the role of a derived consequence of
single-source $x_{4}$-expansion. The 3D-cross-section reading of this
single Sphere at separated detector locations registers correlated
outcomes (Theorem [19.1](#thm:QMT19){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT19"}). The Geometric Channel reading of QM T18 (Schmidt
decomposition,
Lemma [18.6](#lem:QMT18-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-channelB-proof"}) builds on this geometric
foundation. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#lem:QMT18-channelB-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 18.6** (Geometric Channel proof of QM T18). *The Schmidt decomposition
has a Geometric Channel reading as the spectral decomposition of the joint
Sphere wavefront's correlation kernel into orthogonal Sphere-mode
pairs.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has six steps. The Schmidt decomposition
has, in addition to its Algebraic Channel reading
(Lemma [18.2](#lem:QMT18-schmidt){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-schmidt"}, the algebraic SVD on the tensor product
$\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$), a Geometric Channel reading as the
spectral decomposition of the joint McGucken-Sphere wavefront's
correlation kernel (Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(ii)+(v) jointly: invariance,
spherical symmetry, and global validity applied to a common source event
$p_0$, with $x_4 = ict$ the integrated kinematic shadow per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}). The Geometric Channel route exhibits
entanglement as a geometric fact about the joint wavefront, with the
role of an algebraic-only feature of the tensor product replaced by the
role of a derived geometric consequence of single-source
$x_{4}$-expansion at $p_0$.

**Step 1: Joint wavefront as non-factorisable object.** By
Lemma [18.5](#lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront"}, when two particles $A, B$ are
