emitted from a common source event $p_0$ (e.g., singlet creation in
$\eta_c \to \gamma\gamma$, atomic two-photon cascade, or parametric
down-conversion), the joint McGucken-Sphere wavefront is a single object
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ on $M_{G}$
(Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:sphere"}, the McGucken Sphere generated at $p_0$ by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii) spherical symmetry of the
$x_{4}$-expansion), not the tensor product of two independent
wavefronts. The joint wavefunction $\Psi(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B, t)$
lives on the joint configuration space
$\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}^3$ and carries correlations between the
$A$-branch and the $B$-branch of the wavefront.

**Step 2: Correlation kernel from the joint wavefront.** Define the
correlation kernel of the joint wavefront at time $t$ as the operator
$K_t: \mathcal{H}_B \to \mathcal{H}_A$ with kernel
$$K_t(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B) := \Psi(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B, t).$$
The kernel encodes the geometric correlation structure of the joint
Sphere wavefront: $K_t$ tells us how the $A$-branch amplitude at
$\mathbf{x}_A$ couples to the $B$-branch amplitude at $\mathbf{x}_B$ on
the shared wavefront.

**Step 3: Spectral decomposition of the correlation kernel.** The
correlation operator $K_t$ is a Hilbert--Schmidt operator
(square-integrable kernel by joint-wavefunction normalisation
$\int|\Psi|^2 d^3\mathbf{x}_A\,d^3\mathbf{x}_B = 1$). Apply
singular-value decomposition to $K_t$:
$$K_t = \sum_n \sqrt{\lambda_n}\,\lvert a_n \rangle_A \otimes \langle b_n \rvert_B^*,$$
where $\{\lvert a_n \rangle_A\}$ and $\{\lvert b_n \rangle_B\}$ are
orthonormal eigenbases of $K_t K_t^\dagger$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$ and
$K_t^\dagger K_t$ on $\mathcal{H}_B$ respectively, and
$\sqrt{\lambda_n}$ are the singular values (Schmidt coefficients) with
$\sum_n\lambda_n = 1$.

**Step 4: Schmidt decomposition is geometric.** Pulling the spectral
decomposition of $K_t$ back to the joint wavefunction:
$$\Psi(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B, t) = \sum_n\sqrt{\lambda_n}\,a_n(\mathbf{x}_A)\,b_n(\mathbf{x}_B),$$
which is exactly the Schmidt decomposition of
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle\in \mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$. Each
Schmidt mode pair $(\lvert a_n \rangle_A, \lvert b_n \rangle_B)$
corresponds to a correlation channel of the joint Sphere wavefront: the
$A$-branch mode $\lvert a_n \rangle_A$ is paired with the $B$-branch
mode $\lvert b_n \rangle_B$ at the geometric level. The weights
$\sqrt{\lambda_n}$ measure the spectral weight of each correlation
channel.

**Step 5: Entanglement entropy as channel-spectrum dimension.** The von
Neumann entropy of the reduced density matrix
$\rho_A = \mathrm{tr}_B|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi| = K_t K_t^\dagger$ is
$$S_{\mathrm{ent}} = -\sum_n\lambda_n\log\lambda_n,$$ which is the
Shannon entropy of the channel-spectrum $\{\lambda_n\}$. Geometrically,
this measures the effective dimension of the joint Sphere wavefront's
correlation structure:

-   $S_{\mathrm{ent}} = 0$: single correlation channel ($\lambda_1 = 1$,
    all other $\lambda_n = 0$) --- product state, no entanglement;

-   $S_{\mathrm{ent}} = \log 2$: two equally-weighted channels (Bell
    state) --- qubit-level entanglement;

-   $S_{\mathrm{ent}} = \log d$: $d$ equally-weighted channels
    (maximally entangled in $\mathbb{C}^d \otimes \mathbb{C}^d$) ---
    full-rank entanglement.

**Step 6: Geometric Channel characterisation.** The derivation uses (i) the
McGucken Sphere construction at a common source event (QB1), (ii) the
non-factorisability of the joint Sphere wavefront
(Lemma [18.5](#lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront"}, geometric fact about the
wavefront's correlation structure), (iii) the spectral decomposition of
the correlation kernel (a Hilbert--Schmidt-operator theorem on the joint
wavefront). No Stone--von Neumann uniqueness, no abstract tensor-product
axiom, no singular-value decomposition of an abstract coefficient matrix
appears; the entire structure is the geometric reading of the joint
Sphere wavefront. The proof is Geometric Channel, derivationally disjoint from the
Algebraic Channel route of
Lemma [18.4](#lem:QMT18-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-channelA-proof"}.

**McGucken anchoring.** The Schmidt decomposition has the reading of the spectral analysis of a joint geometric object --- the
non-factorisable McGucken-Sphere wavefront sourced at a common event ---
in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, complementing its Algebraic Channel reading as a
linear-algebraic decomposition on the tensor product. Entanglement has
the reading of a geometric fact about the wavefront, with the
role of an algebraic-only feature of the Hilbert-space tensor product
replaced by the role of a derived consequence of the joint Sphere's
non-factorisable correlation structure at the McGucken-Sphere level.
This is the Geometric Channel view that complements the Algebraic Channel view of
Lemma [18.4](#lem:QMT18-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-channelA-proof"}. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem [18.1](#thm:QMT18){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT18"}.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The theorem asserts the Schmidt decomposition
and entanglement-entropy structure of bipartite pure states: every
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle\in \mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ admits a
canonical decomposition
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle= \sum_n\sqrt{\lambda_n}\lvert a_n \rangle_A \otimes \lvert b_n \rangle_B$
with entanglement entropy
$S_{\mathrm{ent}} = -\sum_n\lambda_n\log\lambda_n$. We establish this
along both channels and verify their derivational disjointness.

**Step 1: Algebraic Channel derivation
(Lemma [18.4](#lem:QMT18-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-channelA-proof"}).** The joint Hilbert space of
subsystems $A, B$ is the tensor product
$\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ (QA4: Stone-von Neumann uniqueness
extended to composite systems). Any
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle\in \mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ has a
coefficient matrix $C_{ij} = \langle i, j \vert \Psi \rangle$ in product
bases. Applying singular-value decomposition (SVD) to $C$:
$C = U\Sigma V^\dagger$ with $\Sigma$ diagonal, $U, V$ unitary. Defining
$\lvert a_n \rangle_A := \sum_i U_{in}\lvert i \rangle_A$ and
$\lvert b_n \rangle_B := \sum_j V^*_{jn}\lvert j \rangle_B$ yields the
Schmidt decomposition
(Lemma [18.2](#lem:QMT18-schmidt){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-schmidt"}). The reduced density matrix
$\rho_A = \mathrm{tr}_B\lvert \Psi \rangle\langle \Psi \rvert$ is
diagonal in the Schmidt basis with eigenvalues $\lambda_n = \sigma_n^2$,
and the von Neumann entropy $S(\rho_A) = -\sum_n\lambda_n\log\lambda_n$
is the Shannon entropy of the Schmidt distribution
(Lemma [18.3](#lem:QMT18-entropy){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-entropy"}). The Algebraic Channel route:
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ $\to$ Hilbert-space tensor structure $\to$ SVD
of coefficient matrix $\to$ Schmidt decomposition $\to$ reduced density
matrix $\to$ entanglement entropy.

**Step 2: Geometric Channel derivation
(Lemma [18.6](#lem:QMT18-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-channelB-proof"}).** When two particles $A, B$ are
emitted from a common source event $p_0 \in M_{G}$, they share a single
McGucken-Sphere wavefront
(Lemma [18.5](#lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront"}: joint Sphere from common past,
non-factorisable for generic singlet emission). The joint wavefunction
$\Psi(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B, t)$ defines a correlation kernel
$K_t(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B) := \Psi(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B, t)$
as a Hilbert-Schmidt operator $\mathcal{H}_B \to \mathcal{H}_A$.
Spectral decomposition of $K_t$ produces orthogonal Sphere-mode pairs
$\{\lvert a_n \rangle_A, \lvert b_n \rangle_B\}$ with weights
$\sqrt{\lambda_n}$:
$$\Psi(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B, t) = \sum_n\sqrt{\lambda_n}\,a_n(\mathbf{x}_A)\,b_n(\mathbf{x}_B).$$
This is the Geometric Channel Schmidt decomposition. Each Schmidt mode pair
corresponds to a correlation channel of the joint Sphere wavefront; the
spectral weights $\lambda_n$ measure the spectral complexity of the
correlation structure. Entanglement entropy is the Shannon entropy of
the channel spectrum. The Geometric Channel route: $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
$\to$ joint Sphere from common source $\to$ non-factorisable correlation
kernel $\to$ spectral decomposition of correlation kernel $\to$ Schmidt
decomposition.

**Step 3: Derivational disjointness of the two channels.** Algebraic Channel uses
the tensor-product Hilbert space (from Stone-von Neumann uniqueness on
composite systems), the SVD theorem for $\mathbb{C}^{m \times n}$
matrices, the reduced density matrix via partial trace, and the Shannon
entropy of the Schmidt distribution. Geometric Channel uses the McGucken-Sphere
construction at a common source event, the non-factorisability of the
joint Sphere wavefront, and the spectral decomposition of the
correlation kernel as a Hilbert-Schmidt operator. The intermediate
machinery is disjoint:

-   Tensor-product Hilbert space and SVD of abstract coefficient matrix
    appear in Algebraic Channel, not in Geometric Channel;

-   Joint Sphere wavefront and correlation-kernel spectral decomposition
    appear in Geometric Channel, not in Algebraic Channel.

The two channels share only $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the final
Schmidt decomposition with entanglement entropy.

**Step 4: McGucken anchoring of entanglement.** In the McGucken
framework, entanglement has the reading of the geometric fact
that pair-emission from a common source event produces a single Sphere
wavefront, with the role of a mysterious correlation between separate
quantum systems replaced by the role of a derived consequence of
single-source $x_{4}$-expansion. The Schmidt coefficients
$\sqrt{\lambda_n}$ are the spectral weights of correlation channels in
this joint Sphere wavefront. The entanglement entropy measures the
effective dimension of the wavefront's correlation structure:
$S_{\mathrm{ent}} = 0$ for product states (single channel), $\log 2$ for
Bell states (two equally-weighted channels), $\log d$ for maximally
entangled $\mathbb{C}^d \otimes \mathbb{C}^d$ states ($d$
equally-weighted channels). The geometric origin in clause QB1 of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (every event sources a single Sphere) explains
why entanglement is generic for pair-creation processes.

**Step 5: Physical and empirical content.** The Schmidt decomposition is
the foundational tool of quantum information theory: it characterises
entangled pure states, determines the Schmidt rank (= effective
dimension of correlation), and provides the entanglement entropy as a
quantitative measure of entanglement. Empirical verification: Bell-state
tomography in atomic systems, polarisation entanglement in spontaneous
parametric down-conversion (SPDC), and the Pan-group 2017 satellite Bell
test (Yin et al. [@Yin2017]) measuring $|CHSH| > 2.4$ at 1200-km
detector separation. The non-factorisability of the joint Sphere
wavefront --- and hence the Schmidt-decomposition structure --- descends
directly from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via clause QB1, with no
additional postulate required. ◻
:::

### Algebraic Channel derivation: Singular-value decomposition of $\Psi$ as $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$-tensor

::: {#lem:QMT18-schmidt .lemma}
**Lemma 18.2** (Schmidt decomposition exists for any bipartite pure
state). *Let $\mathcal{H}_A, \mathcal{H}_B$ be separable Hilbert spaces
with countable orthonormal bases. Any normalised pure state
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle\in \mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ admits a
unique (up to ordering and degeneracies) Schmidt decomposition
$$\lvert \Psi  \rangle= \sum_n \sqrt{\lambda_n}\,\lvert a_n \rangle_A \otimes \lvert b_n \rangle_B,$$
with orthonormal $\{\lvert a_n \rangle\} \subset \mathcal{H}_A$,
$\{\lvert b_n \rangle\} \subset \mathcal{H}_B$ and Schmidt coefficients
$\lambda_n \ge 0$, $\sum_n\lambda_n = 1$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has four steps. The Schmidt decomposition
is a theorem on the tensor product
$\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ of two Hilbert spaces
(Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"}, where each factor $\mathcal{H}$ is
itself a theorem of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} and the integrated $x_4 = ict$ per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}). The tensor product is the
McGucken-anchored structure for joint subsystems
(Lemma [18.5](#lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront"}), and the Schmidt decomposition
is the existence theorem for canonical bipartite-state decomposition on
this tensor product.

**Step 1: $\lvert \Psi \rangle$ as a linear map.** Fix bases
$\{\lvert e_i \rangle_A\}$ and $\{\lvert f_j \rangle_B\}$ of
$\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\mathcal{H}_B$, and expand
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle= \sum_{ij} \Psi_{ij}\,\lvert e_i \rangle_A \otimes \lvert f_j \rangle_B$.
The coefficient array $\Psi_{ij} \in \mathbb{C}$ is a (potentially
infinite-dimensional) matrix. The pure state $\lvert \Psi \rangle$ is
equivalent to a linear operator
$\Psi: \mathcal{H}_B^* \to \mathcal{H}_A$ via
$\langle f \rvert\lvert \Psi \rangle \in \mathcal{H}_A$ for any
$\langle f \rvert \in \mathcal{H}_B^*$. Concretely,
$\Psi(\langle f_j \rvert) = \sum_i \Psi_{ij}\,\lvert e_i \rangle_A$. The
complex-valued coefficient array $\Psi_{ij}$ inherits its complex
character from the perpendicularity marker $i$ in
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}, the complex structure of $\mathcal{H}$
as a theorem of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**Step 2: Singular value decomposition.** The Hilbert--Schmidt operator
$\Psi$ has a singular-value decomposition (the infinite-dimensional
generalisation of the SVD for matrices; see Reed--Simon [@ReedSimon1980]
Theorem VI.17 for the compact-operator case, and noting that any pure
state with $\sum_{ij}|\Psi_{ij}|^2 = 1$ corresponds to a
Hilbert--Schmidt operator):
$$\Psi = \sum_n \sigma_n \lvert a_n \rangle_A\langle b_n \rvert_B,$$
where $\sigma_n \ge 0$ are the singular values (eigenvalues of
$\sqrt{\Psi^\dagger\Psi}$), $\{\lvert a_n \rangle\}$ are the left
singular vectors (orthonormal in $\mathcal{H}_A$), and
$\{\lvert b_n \rangle\}$ are the right singular vectors (orthonormal in
$\mathcal{H}_B$). The normalisation $\sum|\Psi_{ij}|^2 = 1$ comes from
the Born rule (Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}) on the joint state.

**Step 3: Rewrite as Schmidt form.** The operator $\Psi$ corresponds to
the state
$$\lvert \Psi  \rangle= \sum_n \sigma_n\,\lvert a_n \rangle_A \otimes \lvert b_n \rangle_B.$$
Setting $\lambda_n := \sigma_n^2 \ge 0$ gives the Schmidt form
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle= \sum_n \sqrt{\lambda_n}\,\lvert a_n \rangle_A \otimes \lvert b_n \rangle_B$.
Normalisation $\langle\Psi|\Psi\rangle = 1$ implies
$\sum_n \sigma_n^2 = 1$, i.e., $\sum_n \lambda_n = 1$, which is the
Born-rule normalisation
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}) restricted to the Schmidt coefficients.

**Step 4: Uniqueness.** The Schmidt coefficients $\sqrt{\lambda_n}$ are
the singular values of $\Psi$, which are uniquely determined by $\Psi$
(the spectrum of $\sqrt{\Psi^\dagger\Psi}$, a self-adjoint compact
operator with discrete spectrum by the spectral theorem, Reed--Simon
[@ReedSimon1980] Theorem VI.16). The bases $\{\lvert a_n \rangle\}$ and
$\{\lvert b_n \rangle\}$ are unique up to the eigenspace-degeneracy
freedom (within an eigenspace of $\Psi^\dagger\Psi$, any orthonormal
basis works). The Schmidt decomposition is therefore a theorem on bipartite tensor-product states, valid for any
$\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ arising from McGucken-derived
single-particle Hilbert spaces
(Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"}) joined by the tensor-product
construction
(Lemma [18.5](#lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront"}, with the joint structure
descended from Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(v) applied jointly to subsystems
$A$ and $B$). $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#lem:QMT18-entropy .lemma}
**Lemma 18.3** (Entanglement entropy from Schmidt coefficients). *The
von Neumann entanglement entropy of $\lvert \Psi \rangle$ equals the
Shannon entropy of the Schmidt-coefficient distribution:
$S_{\mathrm{ent}}(\Psi) = -\sum_n \lambda_n \log\lambda_n$. The state is
entangled iff more than one $\lambda_n$ is nonzero.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has six steps establishing the
entanglement entropy as the Shannon entropy of the Schmidt-coefficient
distribution. The entropy is a geometric quantity measuring the spectral
complexity of the joint McGucken-Sphere wavefront sourced at a common
event (Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(ii)+(v) jointly: invariance,
spherical symmetry, and global validity at every event of $M_{G}$, with
$x_4 = ict$ the integrated kinematic shadow per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}).

**Step 1: Compute the reduced density matrix.** The reduced density
matrix on $\mathcal{H}_A$ is obtained by tracing the pure-state
projector $\lvert \Psi \rangle\langle \Psi \rvert$ over the
$B$-subsystem (with the partial-trace operation defined on the tensor
product $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ established as a theorem
of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in
Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"}):
$$\rho_A := \mathrm{tr}_B(\lvert \Psi \rangle\langle \Psi \rvert) = \sum_m\langle b_m \rvert_B\lvert \Psi \rangle\langle \Psi \rvert\lvert b_m \rangle_B.$$
Using the Schmidt decomposition
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle= \sum_n\sqrt{\lambda_n}\lvert a_n \rangle_A\otimes\lvert b_n \rangle_B$
from Lemma [18.2](#lem:QMT18-schmidt){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-schmidt"}: $$\begin{aligned}
\rho_A &= \sum_m\langle b_m \rvert_B\bigl(\sum_n\sqrt{\lambda_n}\lvert a_n \rangle_A\otimes\lvert b_n \rangle_B\bigr)\bigl(\sum_p\sqrt{\lambda_p}\langle a_p \rvert_A\otimes\langle b_p \rvert_B\bigr)\lvert b_m \rangle_B \\
&= \sum_m\sum_{n,p}\sqrt{\lambda_n\lambda_p}\,\delta_{nm}\delta_{pm}\,\lvert a_n \rangle_A\langle a_p \rvert_A \\
&= \sum_n\lambda_n\,\lvert a_n \rangle_A\langle a_n \rvert_A.
\end{aligned}$$ The reduced density matrix is diagonal in the Schmidt
basis with eigenvalues $\{\lambda_n\}$.

**Step 2: Von Neumann entropy of a diagonal $\rho_A$.** The von Neumann
entropy is defined as $$S(\rho_A) := -\mathrm{tr}(\rho_A \log\rho_A).$$
For a diagonal density matrix
$\rho_A = \sum_n\lambda_n\lvert a_n \rangle\langle a_n \rvert$ with
eigenvalues $\{\lambda_n\}$, the function $-x\log x$ acts diagonally:
$$\rho_A\log\rho_A = \sum_n\lambda_n\log\lambda_n\,\lvert a_n \rangle\langle a_n \rvert.$$
Taking the trace: $$S(\rho_A) = -\sum_n\lambda_n\log\lambda_n.$$ This is
the Shannon entropy of the discrete probability distribution
$\{\lambda_n\}$ (the Schmidt-coefficient distribution).

**Step 3: Entanglement-entropy identification.** The entanglement
entropy of the pure state $\lvert \Psi \rangle$ is, by definition, the
von Neumann entropy of either reduced density matrix:
$$S_{\mathrm{ent}}(\Psi) := S(\rho_A) = S(\rho_B) = -\sum_n\lambda_n\log\lambda_n.$$
The equality $S(\rho_A) = S(\rho_B)$ for pure states follows from the
symmetry of the Schmidt decomposition between $A$ and $B$ (both reduced
density matrices have the same spectrum $\{\lambda_n\}$).

**Step 4: Entanglement criterion (product states have zero entropy).**
If exactly one $\lambda_n = 1$ and all others vanish, then
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle= \lvert a_1 \rangle_A\otimes\lvert b_1 \rangle_B$
is a product state (Schmidt rank 1, not entangled). Computing:
$$S_{\mathrm{ent}} = -1\cdot\log 1 - 0\cdot\log 0 = 0,$$ using the
convention $0\cdot\log 0 = 0$ (limit as $\lambda \to 0^+$). The entropy
is zero exactly when the state is a product, i.e., not entangled.

**Step 5: Maximal entanglement.** The maximum of the Shannon entropy
$-\sum\lambda_n\log\lambda_n$ subject to $\sum\lambda_n = 1$ is attained
on the uniform distribution $\lambda_n = 1/d$ for $n = 1, \ldots, d$
(where $d = \min(\dim\mathcal{H}_A, \dim\mathcal{H}_B)$). The maximum
value is
$$S_{\mathrm{ent}}^{\max} = -\sum_{n=1}^d\frac{1}{d}\log\frac{1}{d} = \log d.$$
States achieving this maximum are called maximally entangled: examples
include the Bell state
$\lvert \Psi^- \rangle = (\lvert HV \rangle - \lvert VH \rangle)/\sqrt 2$
in $\mathbb{C}^2\otimes\mathbb{C}^2$ (with $S_{\mathrm{ent}} = \log 2$).

**Step 6: McGucken anchoring --- entropy as channel-spectrum
dimension.** In the McGucken-Sphere framework
(cf. Lemma [18.6](#lem:QMT18-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-channelB-proof"}, Geometric Channel), the Schmidt
coefficients $\{\lambda_n\}$ are the spectral weights of correlation
channels in the joint Sphere wavefront from a common source event
(Lemma [18.5](#lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront"}). The entanglement entropy
$S_{\mathrm{ent}} = -\sum\lambda_n\log\lambda_n$ is therefore the
effective dimension of the joint Sphere wavefront's correlation
structure:

-   $S_{\mathrm{ent}} = 0$: single correlation channel (product state);

-   $S_{\mathrm{ent}} = \log 2$: two equally-weighted channels (Bell
    state);

-   $S_{\mathrm{ent}} = \log d$: $d$ equally-weighted channels
    (maximally entangled state on $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$).

Entanglement entropy has the reading of a geometric quantity
measuring the spectral complexity of the joint McGucken-Sphere wavefront
--- with the role of an abstract information-theoretic quantity replaced
by the role of a forced geometric consequence of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ applied at a common source event, expressed
through the spectral weights of correlation channels in the joint Sphere
wavefront via Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i), (ii), (v) jointly. ◻
:::

::: {#lem:QMT18-channelA-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 18.4** (Algebraic Channel proof of QM T18). *The Schmidt decomposition
and entanglement entropy follow from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the
Hilbert-space tensor structure (QA4) and singular-value decomposition.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: Hilbert-space tensor structure for composite
systems.** By
Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"} (the Hilbert space as a theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), each subsystem $A$ and $B$ has its own
Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\mathcal{H}_B$. By QA4 (Stone--von
Neumann uniqueness extended to composite systems, equivalently the
Wigner classification on the joint Poincaré representation), the joint
state space of the composite system is the tensor product
$\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$. This is the standard construction
for two-particle quantum mechanics; the tensor structure is forced by
the requirement that observables on $A$ commute with observables on $B$
when both are measured on the joint system.

**Step 2: Schmidt decomposition for pure states.** By
Lemma [18.2](#lem:QMT18-schmidt){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-schmidt"} (four-step proof: write
$\lvert \Psi \rangle$ in product basis as
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle= \sum_{ij}C_{ij}\lvert i \rangle_A\otimes\lvert j \rangle_B$,
perform singular-value decomposition $C = U\Sigma V^\dagger$ on the
coefficient matrix, define orthonormal bases
$\lvert a_n \rangle_A := \sum_i U_{in}\lvert i \rangle_A$ and
$\lvert b_n \rangle_B := \sum_j V^*_{jn}\lvert j \rangle_B$, conclude
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle= \sum_n\sqrt{\lambda_n}\lvert a_n \rangle_A\otimes\lvert b_n \rangle_B$),
every pure state
$\lvert \Psi  \rangle\in \mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ admits a
canonical decomposition
$$\lvert \Psi  \rangle= \sum_n\sqrt{\lambda_n}\,\lvert a_n \rangle_A \otimes \lvert b_n \rangle_B,$$
with $\lambda_n \ge 0$ summing to 1, and
$\{\lvert a_n \rangle_A\}, \{\lvert b_n \rangle_B\}$ orthonormal bases
of (subspaces of) $\mathcal{H}_A, \mathcal{H}_B$.

**Step 3: Reduced density matrix and entanglement entropy.** The reduced
density matrix on $A$, obtained by tracing over $B$, is diagonal in the
Schmidt basis:
$\rho_A = \sum_n\lambda_n\,\lvert a_n \rangle_A\langle a_n \rvert_A$. By
Lemma [18.3](#lem:QMT18-entropy){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-entropy"} (three-step proof: identify $\rho_A$ as
diagonal in the Schmidt basis with eigenvalues $\{\lambda_n\}$, compute
$-\mathrm{tr}(\rho_A\log\rho_A) = -\sum\lambda_n\log\lambda_n$, identify
with the Shannon entropy of the Schmidt distribution), the von Neumann
entropy of $\rho_A$ is
$$S_{\mathrm{ent}}(\Psi) = -\sum_n\lambda_n\log\lambda_n.$$

**Step 4: Entanglement criterion and Algebraic Channel characterisation.** The
entropy $S_{\mathrm{ent}}(\Psi) > 0$ iff more than one $\lambda_n > 0$
iff $\lvert \Psi \rangle$ is not a tensor-product state. This
characterises entangled pure states algebraically: a pure state is
entangled iff its Schmidt rank exceeds 1. The derivation uses only
Hilbert-space tensor structure (Algebraic Channel: QA4), singular-value
decomposition (linear-algebraic theorem on $\mathbb{C}^{m\times n}$),
and the Shannon-entropy formula on the Schmidt distribution. No
Sphere-geometric machinery appears; the proof is Algebraic Channel, derivationally
disjoint from the Geometric Channel Sphere-wavefront route (joint Sphere from a
single source event,
Lemma [18.5](#lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT18-joint-wavefront"} below). ◻
:::

### Disjointness audit {#disjointness-audit-15}

**Geometric Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, joint McGucken-Sphere
wavefront, non-factorisability of joint wavefront, Sphere-mode
correlation structure.

**Algebraic Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, tensor-product Hilbert space,
singular-value decomposition, reduced density matrix, von Neumann
entropy.

**Intersection:**
$\{(\mathrm{McP}), \text{Schmidt decomposition and } S_{\text{ent}}\}$.
*Disjointness verified.*

### Empirical anchor

-   Bell-state generation in parametric down-conversion (Kwiat et
    al. 1995): produces polarization-entangled photon pairs satisfying
    $S_{\text{ent}} = \log 2$ for maximally entangled Bell states.

-   Quantum teleportation (Bouwmeester et al. 1997): uses entanglement
    as the channel for transferring quantum states.

-   Quantum key distribution: BB84, E91 protocols use entanglement-based
    key generation.

-   GHZ-state experiments (Pan, Bouwmeester, Zeilinger 1998):
    three-particle entanglement, testing locality without inequalities.

### The McGucken Equivalence Principle (three components)

::: {#rmk:mcgucken-equivalence-principle-qm .remark}
*Remark 18.7* (McGucken Equivalence Principle in QM). The synthesis
paper [@Syn-2026] identifies a quantum-mechanical analogue of the GR
(general relativity) equivalence principle, with three components:

1.  *Wave--particle equivalence:* the two readings (wave and particle)
    are equivalent descriptions of $S_p$;

2.  *Position--momentum equivalence:* the two readings (spatial and
    Fourier) are equivalent descriptions of the wavefront;

3.  *Matter--antimatter equivalence:* the two readings ($+ic$ and $-ic$)
    are equivalent descriptions of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, related by
    CPT (charge--parity--time-reversal).

Each pair has the reading of an equivalence between two
channel-readings of the same underlying McGucken Sphere, with the role
of a competing dual structure replaced by the role of two
channel-projections of one $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$-generated object.
:::

## QM T19: The Measurement Problem and the Copenhagen Interpretation {#ch:measurement}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial
three. Throughout this chapter, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ refers to this
principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: (i) *invariance* --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the
expansion is isotropic in the spatial three, with the set of events
reachable from $p$ in proper time $\tau$ being a 2-sphere of radius
$c\tau$; (iii) *monotonicity* --- the integral curve is strictly
monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of $x_4$-advance; (iv)
*Lorentz consistency* --- the structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on
$M_{G}$; (v) *global validity* --- $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at
every event of $M_{G}$. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ (Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the central fact.

::: flushright
*"It is wrong to think that the task of physics is to find out how
nature *is*. Physics concerns what we can *say* about nature."\
--- Niels Bohr (attrib. Petersen, 1963)*
:::

::: flushright
*"No phenomenon is a phenomenon until it is an observed phenomenon."\
--- John Archibald Wheeler, on the delayed-choice experiment*
:::

This is the chapter where the advantage of the McGucken
framework is most consequential. The textbook tradition treats
measurement as an independent postulate (Cohen-Tannoudji's projection
postulate, Sakurai's collapse rule, the corresponding postulates in
Shankar and Weinberg) and accumulates "interpretations" (Copenhagen,
many-worlds, Bohmian, decoherence-only) to explain why this postulate is
consistent with unitarity. In the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, the projection
postulate is a theorem; there is no separate collapse postulate; the
"measurement problem" as classically formulated does not arise.

Wheeler's call from his 1989 "It from Bit" essay
[@FQXi-5-Honor-2013] --- that every *it* ultimately derives its
existence from a binary observational *bit* --- and Bohr's insistence
that physics concerns what we can *say* about nature, not how nature
*is*, both point to the operational status of measurement that the
McGucken dual-channel architecture makes precise: the unitary Algebraic Channel
reading governs the 4D Sphere wavefront; the projective Geometric Channel
reading governs its 3D-projection at the registration event. Neither is
fundamental in isolation; together they exhaust the content
of the measurement act.

### Statement

::: {#thm:QMT19 .theorem}
**Theorem 19.1** (QM T19: Measurement, = Theorem 78 (Algebraic Channel) and
Theorem 101 (Geometric Channel) of [@Syn-2026]). *A measurement of an observable
$\hat{O}$ on a state $\lvert \psi \rangle$ proceeds by coupling the
quantum entity to a classical pointer (device) via a self-adjoint
coupling Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_{\text{int}}$. The outcome is the
registration of an eigenvalue $o_n$ of $\hat{O}$, with probability
$P(o_n) = \|\hat{P}_n\lvert \psi \rangle\|^2 = |\langle o_n \vert \psi \rangle|^2$
(the Born rule, Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}), at a 3D spatial location determined by
the device's coupling extent. The post-measurement state of the quantum
entity is
$\hat{P}_n\lvert \psi \rangle/\|\hat{P}_n\lvert \psi \rangle\|$ (the
projection postulate).*
:::

### Geometric Channel derivation: 3D-projection of the 4D McGucken Sphere

::: {#lem:QMT19-3D-projection .lemma}
**Lemma 19.4** (The wavefront at lab time $t$ is the 3D-projection of
the 4D Sphere). *By QB1, a matter entity is a McGucken Sphere $S_p$ on
the four-dimensional manifold $M_{G}$. At any lab time $t$, the
wavefront $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ is a 2-sphere on the 3D spatial slice
$\mathbb{R}^3 \subset M_{G}$ at coordinate time $t$ --- a projection of
the 4D Sphere onto the 3D slice via the suppression map $\sigma$ of
Chapter [9](#ch:hilbert-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:hilbert-theorem"}.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* **Step 1: Sphere ambient space.** By
Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:sphere"} of
Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"}, the McGucken Sphere $S_p$ at source event
$p$ is the locus reached by $x_{4}$-advance at rate $ic$ from $p$, lying
in the four-dimensional Euclidean ambient manifold $\mathbb{R}^4$ with
coordinates $(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$. The Sphere itself satisfies
$(x_1 - x_{p,1})^2 + (x_2 - x_{p,2})^2 + (x_3 - x_{p,3})^2 + x_4^2 = 0$
on the integrated principle $x_4 = ict$.

**Step 2: Spatial slice and parameter time.** The suppression map
$\sigma: M_{G}\to \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ projects the
four-dimensional manifold onto the three-spatial-dimensions slice plus
the integration-parameter time $t$
(Lemma [9.1](#lem:suppression-map){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:suppression-map"}). At a fixed parameter time $t$, the
slice $\Sigma_t = \{(\mathbf{x}, t) : \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3\}$
corresponds to the fixed value $x_4 = ict$ in the original
four-dimensional ambient space.

**Step 3: Sphere intersected with spatial slice.** The intersection
$S_p \cap \Sigma_t$ in the ambient $\mathbb{R}^4$, with $x_4 = ict$
substituted, becomes
$$|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p|^2 + (ict)^2 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p|^2 = c^2 t^2 \;\Rightarrow\; |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p| = ct.$$
This is exactly the 2-sphere
$M^{+}_{p}(t) = \{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p| = ct\}$
--- the wavefront at parameter time $t$.

**Step 4: Wavefunction restriction.** The matter wavefunction
$\psi: M_{G}\to \mathbb{C}$, evaluated on the spatial slice $\Sigma_t$,
becomes the conventional spatial wavefunction
$\psi(\mathbf{x}, t) := \psi(\mathbf{x}, ict)$ on
$\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$. The Sphere wavefunction $\psi|_{S_p}$
restricted to $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ is the spatial wavefunction's value on the
2-sphere of radius $ct$ centred at $\mathbf{x}_p$.

**Step 5: 3D projection identification.** Combining Steps 1--4, the
wavefront at lab time $t$ is exactly the 3D-projection (via $\sigma$) of
the 4D Sphere $S_p$ intersected with the slice $\Sigma_t$. The
2-dimensional wavefront $M^{+}_{p}(t) \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ at parameter
time $t$ is the lab-time cross-section of the 4D Sphere.

**Step 6: Geometric Channel characterisation.** The derivation uses only the
McGucken-Sphere construction (QB1), the suppression-map projection (a
kinematic theorem of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), and the principle's
$x_4 = ict$ constraint. No Hilbert-space operators, no Stone's theorem
appear; the proof is Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation). $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#lem:QMT19-channelB-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 19.5** (Geometric Channel proof of QM T19). *Registration of a
measurement is the 3D-projection of the 4D McGucken Sphere onto a single
spatial point at the registration event. The Born rule arises from the
$SO(3)$-Haar measure on the Sphere weighted by wavefunction amplitude;
the projection postulate is the irreversible registration of the
4D-to-3D collapse.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: Registration is a 3D-event.** When a measurement
device registers a particle at spatial position $\mathbf{x}$ at lab time
$t$, the registration is an event on the 3D slice: a single point
$(\mathbf{x}, t) \in \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$. The 4D Sphere
$S_p$ has full extent on $M_{G}$, but registration occurs at one spatial
point.

**Step 2: Born-rule probability from amplitude on the wavefront.** By
Lemma [19.4](#lem:QMT19-3D-projection){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT19-3D-projection"}, the wavefront is the 2-sphere
$M^{+}_{p}(t)$, sitting on the 3D spatial slice $\Sigma_t$ as the
spatial cross-section of the 4D Sphere $S_p$. The matter wavefunction
$\psi: \Sigma_t \to \mathbb{C}$ assigns a complex amplitude
$\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ to each spatial point. By the Born rule
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}, established as a theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), the registration probability density at
spatial point $\mathbf{x}$ at lab time $t$ is
$$\rho(\mathbf{x}, t) \;=\; |\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)|^2,$$ with the total
probability normalised by
$\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|\psi(\mathbf{x},t)|^2\,d^3\mathbf{x} = 1$. The
$SO(3)$-isotropy of the wavefront
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii): spherical symmetry of
$x_{4}$-expansion) is the feature that supplies the wavefront
geometry on which the Born-rule weighting is defined: for a spatially
symmetric wavefunction ($\psi$ depending only on
$|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p|$), the registration probability is uniform
over the wavefront $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ by $SO(3)$-Haar symmetry; for a
general wavefunction, the Born-rule density $|\psi(\mathbf{x},t)|^2$
weights the rotational measure according to the local amplitude.

**Step 3: Post-measurement state.** Registration projects the 4D Sphere
wavefunction onto its support at the registered event $(\mathbf{x}, t)$:
the new initial condition for subsequent evolution is the wavefunction
concentrated at $(\mathbf{x}, t)$ (or, more precisely, in the
spatial-resolution width of the device's coupling). Subsequent unitary
evolution proceeds from this projected state; the projection itself has
the geometric reading of the 4D-to-3D suppression of $S_p$ at the
registration moment.

**Step 4: Irreversibility from macroscopic information transfer.** On
the 4D side of $M_{G}$, evolution remains unitary (governed by
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ acting at every event). On the 3D side, the
registration is irreversible because information has been transferred to
the device's macroscopic pointer (an entropy-bearing $\sim 10^{20}$-DOF
object whose time-reversal would require coherent reassembly of all its
degrees of freedom --- exponentially suppressed by the Second Law
derived along Geometric Channel in [@Syn-2026]). The "collapse" has the
reading of the 3D-projection of the 4D Sphere at the
registration event, with the irreversibility supplied by the
entropy-bearing macroscopic state of the device. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem [19.1](#thm:QMT19){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT19"}.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). By
Lemmas [19.3](#lem:QMT19-channelA-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT19-channelA-proof"}
and [19.5](#lem:QMT19-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT19-channelB-proof"}, the measurement scheme of
Theorem [19.1](#thm:QMT19){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT19"}
follows from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ along both Algebraic Channel
(Stone-theorem coupling + Born rule + von Neumann projection) and
Geometric Channel (4D-to-3D Sphere projection + $SO(3)$-Haar + macroscopic
irreversibility). The projection postulate has the reading of
a theorem of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ rather than an independent
postulate: in Algebraic Channel it has the reading of an operational
consequence of Stone-theorem coupling; in Geometric Channel it has the geometric
reading of the 3D-projection of the 4D Sphere at the registration event.
The two channels descend through derivationally disjoint intermediate
machinery to the same Born-probability outcomes and post-measurement
state. $\square$ ◻
:::

### Algebraic Channel derivation: Stone-theorem coupling and Born-rule registration

::: {#lem:QMT19-coupling .lemma}
**Lemma 19.2** (Device-coupling Hamiltonian generates the projection).
*A measurement of an observable $\hat O = \sum_n o_n\hat P_n$ on a state
$\lvert \psi \rangle$ proceeds via a device-coupling Hamiltonian
$\hat H_{\mathrm{int}}$ that entangles the quantum entity with a
macroscopic pointer. The Stone-theorem evolution
$U_{\mathrm{int}}(\tau) = \exp(-i\tau \hat H_{\mathrm{int}}/\hbar)$
drives the joint state $\lvert \psi  \rangle\otimes \lvert D_0 \rangle$
(system + ready-state device) to a superposition
$\sum_n c_n \lvert o_n \rangle_{\mathrm{sys}}\otimes\lvert D_n \rangle_{\mathrm{dev}}$
with $c_n = \langle o_n \vert \psi \rangle$ and $\lvert D_n \rangle$
distinct macroscopic pointer states.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has six steps. The measurement scheme of
Theorem [19.1](#thm:QMT19){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT19"}
is built from McGucken-derived machinery: the Stone-theorem coupling
(descended from Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i) invariance via time-translation
symmetry, with $x_4 = ict$ the integrated kinematic shadow per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) entangles the system with the
device, and the Born rule
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}, itself a theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$) supplies the outcome probabilities.

**Step 1: Coupling Hamiltonian.** A standard von Neumann measurement
model uses a coupling
$\hat H_{\mathrm{int}} = g\,\hat O \otimes \hat p_{\mathrm{dev}}$ where
$g$ is a coupling constant, $\hat O$ is the system observable, and
$\hat p_{\mathrm{dev}}$ is the pointer-momentum operator on the device's
Hilbert space (with $\hat p = -i\hbar\nabla$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$
established as a theorem of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in
Lemma [2.2](#lem:phat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:phat-generator"}). The coupling is on for a brief
interval $\tau$ then off; during the coupling, the device pointer shifts
by an amount proportional to $\hat O$'s eigenvalue. The interaction
Hamiltonian is self-adjoint by construction
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i), forcing real-valued energy
eigenvalues via Stone's theorem applied to the joint time-translation
group).

**Step 2: Apply Stone's theorem.** The time evolution generated by
$\hat H_{\mathrm{int}}$ (a self-adjoint operator on
$\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sys}} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dev}}$) is
$U_{\mathrm{int}}(\tau) = \exp(-i\tau g\,\hat O \otimes \hat p_{\mathrm{dev}}/\hbar)$.
On the initial state $\lvert \psi  \rangle\otimes \lvert D_0 \rangle$
with $\lvert \psi  \rangle= \sum_n c_n\lvert o_n \rangle$ (expansion in
$\hat O$-eigenbasis):
$$U_{\mathrm{int}}(\tau)(\lvert \psi  \rangle\otimes \lvert D_0 \rangle) \;=\; \sum_n c_n\,\lvert o_n \rangle\otimes U_{\mathrm{shift}}(g\tau o_n)\lvert D_0 \rangle,$$
where
$U_{\mathrm{shift}}(\alpha) = \exp(-i\alpha\hat p_{\mathrm{dev}}/\hbar)$
shifts the device pointer by $\alpha$ (by the standard
$\exp(-i\alpha\hat p/\hbar)\lvert D_0 \rangle = \lvert D_0 + \alpha \rangle$
identity in the pointer-position representation, since $\hat p$
generates spatial translation per
Lemma [2.2](#lem:phat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:phat-generator"}). Define
$\lvert D_n \rangle := U_{\mathrm{shift}}(g\tau o_n)\lvert D_0 \rangle$;
for sufficiently distinct $o_n$, the $\lvert D_n \rangle$ are
macroscopically distinguishable.

**Step 3: Born-rule probabilities.** The final state is
$\sum_n c_n\lvert o_n \rangle\otimes\lvert D_n \rangle$. The probability
of registering the device in pointer-state $\lvert D_n \rangle$ is
$|c_n|^2 = |\langle o_n \vert \psi \rangle|^2 = \|\hat P_n\lvert \psi \rangle\|^2$
(Born rule, Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}). This is the standard von Neumann
measurement scheme; the projection
$\hat P_n = \lvert o_n \rangle\langle o_n \rvert$ appears via the
orthogonality of distinct $\lvert D_n \rangle$ in the macroscopic limit.

**Step 4: Macroscopic distinguishability of pointer states.** For the
measurement to register definite outcomes, the pointer states
$\{\lvert D_n \rangle\}$ must be macroscopically distinguishable:
$\langle D_n \vert D_m \rangle \approx \delta_{nm}$ in the macroscopic
limit. The Stone-theorem unitary $U_{\mathrm{shift}}(g\tau o_n)$ shifts
the device pointer by amount $g\tau o_n$. Modelling the ready-state
pointer as a Gaussian wavepacket of position-spread $\sigma$ centred at
$D_0 = 0$,
$$\langle D | D_0\rangle \;=\; (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-1/4}\,\exp\!\left(-\frac{D^2}{4\sigma^2}\right),$$
the shifted pointer state $\lvert D_n \rangle$ has wavefunction
$\langle D | D_n\rangle = (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-1/4}\exp(-(D - g\tau o_n)^2/(4\sigma^2))$.
The overlap of two distinct shifted pointers is the standard
Gaussian-overlap integral:
$$\langle D_m \vert D_n \rangle \;=\; \int dD\,\langle D_m|D\rangle\langle D|D_n\rangle \;=\; \exp\!\left(-\frac{(g\tau(o_m - o_n))^2}{8\sigma^2}\right),$$
by direct evaluation of the Gaussian integral
$\int dD\,\exp[-(D-\mu_m)^2/(4\sigma^2) - (D-\mu_n)^2/(4\sigma^2)]/(2\pi\sigma^2)^{1/2}$
with $\mu_n = g\tau o_n$ via completing the square and integrating the
resulting unit-normalized Gaussian. The overlap is suppressed
exponentially as $(g\tau)^2(o_m - o_n)^2/\sigma^2$ grows. For the
macroscopic limit $g\tau|o_m - o_n| \gg \sigma$ (large signal compared
to pointer width), the overlap satisfies
$|\langle D_m \vert D_n \rangle| \to 0$, giving
$\langle D_m \vert D_n \rangle \approx \delta_{mn}$. This is the
macroscopic-limit requirement of the von Neumann measurement scheme.

**Step 5: McGucken anchoring of the coupling structure.** The factor of
$i$ in $U_{\mathrm{int}}(\tau) = e^{-i\tau\hat H_{\mathrm{int}}/\hbar}$
is the chain-rule case
(Theorem [9.21](#thm:twelve-i){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:twelve-i"} case 1): the McGucken-Principle
perpendicularity marker transmitted through Stone's theorem applied to
the time-translation generated by the coupling Hamiltonian. The factor
of $\hbar$ is the action quantum per Sphere cycle
(Theorem [3.2](#thm:62){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:62"}). Both
constants have the reading of consequences of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$: the $i$ from the perpendicularity marker, the
$\hbar$ from the Sphere action quantum, with both descending from the
same principle through the chain
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} $\to$ Stone's theorem on time-translation
invariance $\to$ time-evolution operator $U_{\mathrm{int}}$ of the
coupled system.

**Step 6: Projection postulate emerges from tracing over the device.**
Tracing the joint state
$\sum_n c_n\lvert o_n \rangle\otimes\lvert D_n \rangle$ over the
device's macroscopic degrees of freedom (or conditioning on observation
of a specific pointer state $\lvert D_n \rangle$) leaves the system in
the projected state
$\hat P_n\lvert \psi \rangle/\|\hat P_n\lvert \psi \rangle\|$ with
probability $|c_n|^2$. Concretely: the reduced density matrix of the
system after the coupling is
$$\rho_{\mathrm{sys}} \;=\; \mathrm{Tr}_{\mathrm{dev}}\!\left[\sum_{m,n} c_m c_n^*\,\lvert o_m \rangle\langle o_n \rvert\otimes\lvert D_m \rangle\langle D_n \rvert\right] \;=\; \sum_{m,n} c_m c_n^*\,\langle D_n \vert D_m \rangle\,\lvert o_m \rangle\langle o_n \rvert.$$
In the macroscopic limit of Step 4 where
$\langle D_n \vert D_m \rangle \to \delta_{mn}$, the off-diagonal terms
vanish and
$$\rho_{\mathrm{sys}} \;\to\; \sum_n |c_n|^2\,\lvert o_n \rangle\langle o_n \rvert \;=\; \sum_n |c_n|^2\,\hat P_n,$$
the mixed state in the $\hat O$-eigenbasis with weights $|c_n|^2$.
Conditioning on the specific pointer outcome $\lvert D_n \rangle$
further reduces $\rho_{\mathrm{sys}}$ to the pure projected state
$\hat P_n\lvert \psi \rangle/\|\hat P_n\lvert \psi \rangle\|$. The
projection postulate has the reading of an operational
consequence of three ingredients, all derived from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$: Stone-theorem-generated entanglement between
system and device (Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i) via time-translation invariance);
macroscopic distinguishability of pointer states (Step 4
Gaussian-overlap argument); and the observer's restricted access to a
single 3D-cross-section reading at the registration event (the
spatial-slice projection of the McGucken-Sphere geometry). At the
McGucken-Principle level, the projection postulate has the role of a
derived consequence rather than an additional dynamical input.
$\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#lem:QMT19-channelA-proof .lemma}
**Lemma 19.3** (Algebraic Channel proof of QM T19). *The measurement scheme of
Theorem [19.1](#thm:QMT19){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT19"}
follows from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ along Algebraic Channel via Stone-theorem
coupling and the Born rule.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has six steps, building the Algebraic-Channel
measurement scheme entirely from McGucken-derived machinery.

**Step 1: Device coupling via Stone-theorem unitarity.** By
Lemma [19.2](#lem:QMT19-coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT19-coupling"}, the measurement is implemented by a
coupling Hamiltonian
$\hat H_{\mathrm{int}} = g\,\hat O \otimes \hat p_{\mathrm{dev}}$
entangling the quantum entity with a macroscopic pointer. Stone's
theorem (QA2, applied to the self-adjoint coupling Hamiltonian)
generates the unitary evolution
$U_{\mathrm{int}}(\tau) = e^{-i\tau\hat H_{\mathrm{int}}/\hbar}$, which
acts on the joint state $\lvert \psi  \rangle\otimes \lvert D_0 \rangle$
in a finite time interval $\tau$ producing the entangled superposition
$\sum_n c_n\lvert o_n \rangle_{\mathrm{sys}}\otimes\lvert D_n \rangle_{\mathrm{dev}}$.

**Step 2: Born-rule probability.** The Born rule
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}) assigns to the registration of
device-pointer state $\lvert D_n \rangle$ the probability
$$P(o_n) = |c_n|^2 = |\langle o_n \vert \psi \rangle|^2 = \|\hat P_n\lvert \psi \rangle\|^2,$$
where $\hat P_n = \lvert o_n \rangle\langle o_n \rvert$ is the spectral
projector onto the eigenspace of $\hat O$ with eigenvalue $o_n$. The
Born rule itself is a theorem of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ vian Algebraic Channel
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}, derived from the $SO(3)$-Haar measure
on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront) rather than an independent postulate.

**Step 3: 3D spatial locus of registration.** The registration event
occurs at the spatial location determined by the device's coupling
extent --- formally, the spatial support of $\hat H_{\mathrm{int}}$
restricted to a finite region. In the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, this is the
3D-slice projection of the 4D measurement interaction at the
registration event.

**Step 4: Projection postulate from tracing out the device.** The
post-measurement state of the quantum entity (after tracing over the
device's degrees of freedom or, equivalently, conditioning on the
registered pointer-state $\lvert D_n \rangle$) is the projected state
$$\frac{\hat P_n\lvert \psi \rangle}{\|\hat P_n\lvert \psi \rangle\|}.$$
This is the projection-postulate state. At the McGucken-Principle level,
the projection postulate has the reading of an operational
consequence of three derived ingredients:

-   Stone-theorem-generated unitary evolution (Step 1: device-system
    coupling drives entangled superposition);

-   Macroscopic distinguishability of pointer states (the
    $\lvert D_n \rangle$ are orthogonal in the macroscopic limit, by
    environment-induced decoherence on timescales much shorter than
    experimental times; see
    Lemma [19.2](#lem:QMT19-coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:QMT19-coupling"} Step 4 for the explicit
    Gaussian-overlap computation);

-   Conditioning on observed pointer state (the observer registers a
    specific $\lvert D_n \rangle$, restricting attention to the
    corresponding system branch).

The projection postulate therefore has the role of a theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ rather than an independent dynamical input:
each of the three operational ingredients descends from the principle
through derived machinery (Stone's theorem from time-translation
invariance via Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i); macroscopic distinguishability
from the spatial-translation structure of $\hat p_{\mathrm{dev}}$ via
Lemma [2.2](#lem:phat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:phat-generator"}; spatial-slice conditioning from the
suppression-map projection of the 4D Sphere to the 3D registration
slice).

**Step 5: McGucken anchoring of measurement.** At the level,
the measurement act has the geometric reading of the moment at which the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront $S_{\mathrm{sys}}$ of the system intersects
the wavefront $S_{\mathrm{dev}}$ of the device. The intersection of two
Spheres
(Theorem [17.7](#thm:intersecting-spheres-transfer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:intersecting-spheres-transfer"}) transfers entanglement
from the system to the device, creating the joint system-device
wavefront whose 3D-projection at the registration event yields a single
outcome. The projection postulate has the reading of the
algebraic-symmetry-channel shadow of this geometric intersection
process: Algebraic Channel reads the coupling Hamiltonian and Stone-theorem
evolution at the operator level; Geometric Channel reads the same process as the
geometric intersection of two McGucken Spheres at the registration event
(the Geometric Channel reading is developed in
Lemma [19.5](#lem:QMT19-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT19-channelB-proof"}).

**Step 6: Algebraic Channel characterisation.** The derivation uses Stone's
theorem (QA2, applied to the joint time-translation symmetry on
$\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sys}} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dev}}$); the
Stone--von Neumann uniqueness theorem (QA4, supplying the irreducible
Heisenberg representation of the joint operator algebra); the Wigner
classification (QA6, for the spectral decomposition
$\hat O = \sum_n o_n\hat P_n$ into eigenprojectors); and the Born rule
from Algebraic Channel (Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}, derived from the four requirements R1--R4 descending from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ through the
Cauchy functional equation, with the exponent 2 supplied by the rank-2
character of the Minkowski metric induced by $x_{4}= ict$). No
Sphere-geometric Huygens machinery is invoked at the algebraic level;
the proof is Algebraic Channel, derivationally disjoint from the Geometric Channel
3D-projection route of
Lemma [19.5](#lem:QMT19-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT19-channelB-proof"}. $\square$ ◻
:::

### Resolution of the textbook "measurement problem"

::: {#rmk:no-measurement-problem .remark}
*Remark 19.6* (Resolution of the textbook measurement problem in the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework). The textbook measurement problem has two
components:

*Problem 1: The Schrödinger--von Neumann tension.* Unitary evolution
under $i\hbar\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$ is reversible; the projection
postulate is irreversible. How can the same theory contain both?

*Problem 2: The Heisenberg cut.* Where does the quantum system end and
the classical device begin? At what scale does the projection postulate
apply?

*Resolution in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework.* Problem 1 is dissolved by the
dual-channel architecture: unitary evolution has the Algebraic Channel reading
of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ on the 4D manifold; projection has the
Geometric Channel reading of the 4D-to-3D Sphere projection at registration. The
two readings have the role of complementary descriptions of
the same underlying event --- unitarity describes the 4D Sphere
evolution between events; projection describes the 3D registration at a
single event --- with the dual-channel disjointness (Disjointness audit
below) establishing that both descend from the same principle through
derivationally disjoint intermediate machinery.

Problem 2 is dissolved by the operational specification of the device's
coupling extent: the projection postulate applies at the spatial scale
of the device's coupling Hamiltonian, which is determined experimentally
for each device. The Heisenberg cut has the operational role of the
device-specific spatial scale at which $\hat H_{\mathrm{int}}$ is
supported, with the device-system distinction reading as an operational
specification rather than a fundamental ontological boundary.

The §VIII.4 no-signaling theorem and the Appendix B Dirac--von Neumann
postulate cross-walk in the synthesis paper formalize this resolution.
The textbook "interpretations" (Copenhagen, many-worlds, Bohmian,
decoherence-only, GRW (Ghirardi--Rimini--Weber spontaneous-collapse
model), QBism) have the role, in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, of
different verbal accounts of the same dual-channel structure: each
interpretation captures part of the structure but presents it as the
whole. The Copenhagen interpretation captures the projection (Geometric Channel
at registration); the many-worlds interpretation captures the unitarity
(Algebraic Channel); the Bohmian interpretation captures the trajectory reading
(Geometric Channel path); decoherence captures the device coupling. In the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, all four are correct readings of the same underlying
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.
:::

::: {#rmk:measurement-as-channel-b-event .remark}
*Remark 19.7* (Measurement events as Geometric Channel physical events). The
dual-channel resolution of Problem 1 sharpens into an explicit
identification of where measurement happens. Every measurement event
--- the detector click, the photographic emulsion grain blackening, the
photomultiplier chain of theorems, the CCD pixel charge, the Stern--Gerlach
beam-deflection, the bubble-chamber track --- has the role
of a head-on $x_4$-collision of two McGucken Spheres at a definite
spacetime event, with the $+ic$-oriented Sphere from the source meeting
the $+ic$-oriented Sphere from the detector atom and 3-localizing the
interaction at that event
(Theorem [\[thm:born-as-collision\]](#thm:born-as-collision){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-as-collision"} of
Chapter [\[ch:born\]](#ch:born){reference-type="ref" reference="ch:born"}). The
collision has definite spatiotemporal coordinates, definite
energy-momentum transfer, and definite interaction content
(electromagnetic, strong, or weak depending on the species involved).
The measurement is the Geometric Channel head-on collision; the mathematical
apparatus of Algebraic Channel --- Hilbert spaces, eigenvalue spectra, density
matrices, projection operators --- has the role of encoding
the statistics of such collision events when aggregated over many
preparations of the source and detector configurations. The
Algebraic Channel apparatus has no separate measurement events of its own; the
events are Geometric Channel events, and Algebraic Channel reports their statistics.
This identification removes the residual mystery of where measurement
happens that survives in every orthodox interpretation: measurement
happens at definite spacetime events, in the form of head-on Sphere
collisions, with the Algebraic Channel apparatus tracking the statistics of
where the collisions occur.
:::

::: {#rmk:no-foundational-psi-collapse .remark}
*Remark 19.8* (No foundational $|\psi\rangle$ collapses). The textbook
collapse postulate --- the irreversible projection
$|\psi\rangle \mapsto \hat{P}_n|\psi\rangle / \|\hat{P}_n|\psi\rangle\|$
following a measurement registering eigenvalue $o_n$ --- has been the
central interpretive impasse of orthodox quantum mechanics for ninety
years. Every Algebraic Channel-only resolution attempts to either preserve
unitarity by branching the wavefunction (Everett many-worlds), add a
stochastic non-unitary term to the dynamics (Ghirardi--Rimini--Weber,
continuous spontaneous localization), supplement the wavefunction with
hidden variables governed by a guidance equation (de Broglie--Bohm), or
deny ontological status to $|\psi\rangle$ entirely (QBism). Each
approach treats $|\psi\rangle$ as the primitive whose collapse
or non-collapse must be explained.

The dual-channel diagnosis dissolves the question at the level of the
primitive. The wavefunction $|\psi\rangle$ has the role of the Algebraic Channel operator-algebraic encoding of the Geometric Channel
Sphere wavefront's measurement statistics; it is not the foundational
spatiotemporal entity but the algebraic image of one through the
suppression map $\sigma$ of
Definition [\[def:suppression-map\]](#def:suppression-map){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:suppression-map"}. The "collapse" has the role of the algebraic update of the Algebraic Channel encoding consequent on a
Geometric Channel head-on collision having occurred at a definite spacetime
event. The update has the same role as a Bayesian posterior
update reflecting new evidence: the agent's probabilistic encoding is
revised in light of the new information that the Geometric Channel event has
occurred. The wavefunction does not undergo a physical collapse,
because the wavefunction is not the physical entity that would have to
collapse; the physical entity is the McGucken Sphere wavefront, and
the wavefront undergoes no collapse --- it propagates continuously and
unitarily on $M_G$, with the registration event being a head-on
collision that 3-localizes the interaction at a definite spacetime
event without ending the wavefront's propagation in any sense. The collapse postulate is therefore not a separate dynamical
postulate but the algebraic shadow on the operator-algebraic side of
the Geometric Channel registration event.

The orthodox measurement problem dissolves at the level of the
primitive: there is no foundational $|\psi\rangle$ to
collapse, because $|\psi\rangle$ is the Algebraic Channel encoding of statistics
whose Geometric Channel physical events occur at definite spacetime
coordinates. The question of how unitary evolution produces definite
outcomes has the form of asking how an actuarial table
produces a death: it does not, because the actuarial table is the
statistical encoding and the deaths are events that occur in the
physical world. The Algebraic Channel apparatus encodes; the Geometric Channel events
occur; the dual-channel architecture supplies both readings as
derivations from $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$.
:::

::: {#rmk:orthodox-interpretations-diagnostic .remark}
*Remark 19.9* (Diagnostic of the orthodox interpretations under the
dual-channel architecture). Remark
[1.13](#rmk:no-measurement-problem){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:no-measurement-problem"} above stated the mapping of the
seven major orthodox interpretations of quantum mechanics onto partial
readings of the dual-channel structure. The diagnostic sharpens here
into an account of why each interpretation has the explanatory range it
has and where it falls short of the full structure.

Copenhagen (Bohr, Heisenberg) captures the Geometric Channel registration event
correctly as the moment at which a definite outcome is produced;
Bohr's "phenomenon" is the head-on $x_4$-collision at the detector.
Copenhagen falls short of the full structure by denying foundational
ontological status to what propagates between source and detector, and
by treating the projection postulate as a primitive of the framework
rather than as a theorem of a deeper geometric principle.

Many-worlds (Everett, DeWitt, Deutsch) captures Algebraic Channel's unitarity
correctly as the framework's universal dynamical rule; the universal
wavefunction $|\Psi\rangle$ evolves unitarily without exception.
Many-worlds falls short by reading $|\Psi\rangle$ as the cosmological
ontology --- the Algebraic Channel encoding mistaken for the encoded ---
producing branches as Algebraic Channel-internal substitutes for the missing
Geometric Channel physical events. The branching structure is the operator-algebraic
shadow of the Geometric Channel propagation, with the absence of definite
outcomes within any single branch reflecting Algebraic Channel's inability to localize an outcome without a Geometric Channel head-on collision
event.

de Broglie--Bohm pilot-wave theory captures the Geometric Channel trajectory
reading correctly as the spatiotemporal worldline of the registered
configuration; the trajectory is the head-on-collision sequence of
the Sphere along its detection history. Bohmian mechanics falls short
by coupling the trajectory to an Algebraic Channel guidance equation defined on
configuration space, treating the wavefunction as a separate
entity (the pilot wave) rather than as the Algebraic Channel
operator-algebraic encoding of the same Geometric Channel Sphere whose
trajectory the theory tracks.

GRW and continuous spontaneous localization (Ghirardi, Rimini, Weber;
Pearle; Bassi) capture the registration-event localization correctly
as a physical fact about the configuration of detected matter, but
locate the localization mechanism in a stochastic non-unitary term
added to the dynamics rather than in the Geometric Channel head-on Sphere
collision. The localization happens, but its mechanism in the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is the geometric collision, not a stochastic
non-unitary modification of Algebraic Channel's unitary evolution.

QBism (Caves, Fuchs, Schack) captures the agent-subjective character
of probability assignments correctly as the personal-Bayesian content
of the Algebraic Channel apparatus; quantum states encode the agent's
expectations about future Geometric Channel events. QBism falls short by
declining to commit to the existence of Geometric Channel physical events as
the substrate the agent is encoding; the framework supplies the
substrate as the McGucken Sphere expansion at every event.

Consistent histories (Griffiths, Omnès, Gell-Mann--Hartle) and
relational quantum mechanics (Rovelli) capture the framework
relativity correctly --- which propositions can be jointly asserted,
which agents have which records --- but treat the consistent-histories
or relational structure as the foundational level, without supplying
the Geometric Channel geometric content that produces the histories or the
relations.

The diagnostic conclusion: each orthodox interpretation captures part
of the dual-channel structure correctly and falls short of the full
structure at exactly the point where it would require the Geometric Channel
geometric apparatus. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies the Geometric Channel
geometric apparatus --- the Sphere expansion at $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$
at every event, with the suppression map $\sigma$ projecting the
$+ic$-oriented expansion into the operator-algebraic encoding of
Algebraic Channel. Once both channels are available, each orthodox
interpretation reads as a partial account of one half of the
dual-channel architecture, and the seventy-year impasse over
interpretations dissolves into a integration in which each
contributing tradition retains its correct partial reading and gains
the corresponding Geometric Channel geometric referent.
:::

::: {#rmk:universal-wavefunction-diagnosis .remark}
*Remark 19.10* (The universal wavefunction $|\Psi\rangle$ and the
fifty-year stall of orthodox unification). The orthodox reading of
$|\Psi\rangle$ as the wavefunction of the universe --- the primitive of Many-Worlds, the bulk content of the AdS/CFT correspondence,
the universal-Hilbert-space content of Susskind's black-hole
information-preservation arguments --- has the role of a
Algebraic Channel operator-algebraic object treated as the ontological
substrate of the universe. The dual-channel diagnosis: this is a
category-level reading of the encoding as the encoded, and the
fifty-year stall of orthodox unification work centered on
$|\Psi\rangle$ has a source in this misidentification.

The universal Hilbert-space vector $|\Psi\rangle$ has the role of the operator-algebraic encoding of the universe's Geometric Channel
content --- the totality of $+ic$-oriented McGucken Sphere expansions
at every event of $M_G$. The encoded entity is not $|\Psi\rangle$ but
the underlying spatiotemporal field of Sphere expansions; $|\Psi\rangle$
is the algebraic shadow of that field under the suppression map
$\sigma$. The features that distinguish the universe at large scale ---
the strict Second Law of thermodynamics with its unambiguous
time-direction, the cosmological expansion with its unambiguous spatial
direction outward from the origin, the matter dominance over
antimatter, the arrow of time across nineteen distinct physical
phenomena (Chapter [\[ch:antimatter\]](#ch:antimatter){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:antimatter"}, Theorem 21.4) --- are carried by
the $+ic$ orientation that distinguishes forward Sphere expansion from
time-reversed contraction. The orientation has the role of a
geometric fact about $M_G$ that the Algebraic Channel operator-algebraic
apparatus encodes through the $i$ in every operator equation but does
not carry as a primitive of the wavefunction $|\Psi\rangle$ itself.

The empirical content of this diagnosis is sharp. Fifty years of
orthodox unification programs --- Many-Worlds at the cosmological
scale, AdS/CFT bulk reconstruction, Susskind's universal-Hilbert-space
arguments, the Page-curve calculation, ER=EPR, replica wormholes ---
have produced no observable new-physics predictions in the empirical
record. The reason is that the primitive on which
these programs are built, the universal Hilbert-space vector
$|\Psi\rangle$, does not carry the $+ic$-oriented directional content
that the observable universe requires. The strict Second Law cannot be
derived from $|\Psi\rangle$ alone, because the unitary evolution of
$|\Psi\rangle$ is time-reversal symmetric; the cosmological expansion
direction cannot be derived from $|\Psi\rangle$ alone, because the
Hilbert-space structure has no preferred spatial direction; the matter
dominance cannot be derived from $|\Psi\rangle$ alone, because
$|\Psi\rangle$ is symmetric under charge conjugation absent additional
input. The features that the universe displays as definite directional
asymmetries are supplied, in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, by the $+ic$
orientation of Geometric Channel's Sphere expansion at every event; they are
not present in Algebraic Channel's $|\Psi\rangle$ as encoding without that
geometric input.

The framework's prediction is that orthodox unification
work centered on $|\Psi\rangle$ as foundational cannot produce the
observable directional asymmetries of the universe because the
primitive lacks the required directional content. Either
the directional content is added externally (initial conditions,
boundary conditions, environmental selection), in which case it is
not a derived consequence of the foundational framework, or it must
be inferred from a deeper geometric principle that supplies it ---
which the McGucken Principle does. The fifty-year stall has the
form of a programme attempting to derive directional
asymmetries from a non-directional primitive, and the
dual-channel architecture diagnoses the obstruction explicitly.
:::


### Disjointness audit {#disjointness-audit-16}

**Geometric Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, McGucken Sphere on 4D,
3D-projection-of-4D-Sphere at registration, Sphere Haar measure, Born
rule (Geometric Channel).

**Algebraic Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, QA5 projection-valued
measurement, Stone-theorem coupling, Born rule (Algebraic Channel).

**Intersection:**
$\{(\mathrm{McP}), \text{projection postulate as theorem}\}$.
*Disjointness verified.*

### Empirical anchor

The measurement framework is operationally tested in every
quantum-mechanical experiment. The Born rule's empirical anchor
(Chapter [11](#ch:born){reference-type="ref" reference="ch:born"})
extends here, supplemented by:

-   Weak measurements (Aharonov, Albert, Vaidman 1988): demonstrate the
    existence of a measurement protocol intermediate between projective
    and trivial, confirming that the projection postulate is the
    strong-coupling limit of a continuous family of measurements.

-   Decoherence experiments (Brune, Haroche et al. 1996): trace out the
    device's environmental degrees of freedom and observe the
    disappearance of interference between distinct pointer states,
    confirming the Heisenberg-cut explanation as operational
    scale-dependence.

-   Quantum non-demolition measurements (Braginsky, Vorontsov, Thorne
    1980): demonstrate that the projection acts only on the measured
    observable's conjugate, preserving the measured observable for
    repeated measurement.

## QM T20: Pauli Exclusion and the Spin--Statistics Theorem {#ch:identical}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial
three. Throughout this chapter, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ refers to this
principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: (i) *invariance* --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the
expansion is isotropic in the spatial three, with the set of events
reachable from $p$ in proper time $\tau$ being a 2-sphere of radius
$c\tau$; (iii) *monotonicity* --- the integral curve is strictly
monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of $x_4$-advance; (iv)
*Lorentz consistency* --- the structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on
$M_{G}$; (v) *global validity* --- $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at
every event of $M_{G}$. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ (Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the central fact.

### Statement

::: {#thm:QMT20 .theorem}
**Theorem 20.1** (QM T20: Pauli exclusion, = Theorem 79 (Algebraic Channel) and
Theorem 102 (Geometric Channel) of [@Syn-2026]). *The wavefunction of $N$
identical particles satisfies one of two symmetry properties under
exchange of any two particles:*

-   *Symmetric
    ($\Psi(\ldots, x_i, \ldots, x_j, \ldots) = +\Psi(\ldots, x_j, \ldots, x_i, \ldots)$)
    for integer-spin particles (*bosons*);*

-   *Antisymmetric
    ($\Psi(\ldots, x_i, \ldots, x_j, \ldots) = -\Psi(\ldots, x_j, \ldots, x_i, \ldots)$)
    for half-integer-spin particles (*fermions*).*

*The antisymmetry of fermions forces the Pauli exclusion principle: no
two identical fermions can occupy the same single-particle state, since
the antisymmetric wavefunction vanishes when two arguments coincide.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We prove the spin-statistics dichotomy along Algebraic Channel (Wigner
classification + spin-statistics theorem) and Geometric Channel (geometric
exchange on the McGucken Sphere spinor bundle), in six explicit steps.
Both channels descend from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}) via the Minkowski metric structure
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}) and the spinor representations on the
McGucken Sphere
(Lemma [9.14](#lem:sphere-double-cover){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:sphere-double-cover"}).

**Step 1 (Algebraic Channel): Wigner classification fixes spin labels.** By QA6
(Wigner classification of irreducible unitary representations of the
Poincaré group), particle species are labelled by spin
$s \in \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ (and mass $m$, for the massive
irreducible representations) --- integer $s$ for bosons, half-integer
$s$ for fermions. The Lorentz invariance underlying the classification
descends from Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv), derived at Theorem 4.6 (Lorentz consistency: the
structure built on $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is invariant under
$SO^+(1,3)$) and the Minkowski metric on $M_{G}$ established in
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}.

**Step 2 (Algebraic Channel): Spin-statistics theorem assumptions verified from
McGucken structure.** The Pauli spin-statistics theorem (Pauli 1940
[@Pauli1940]; rigorous proof via analytic-continuation argument in
Weinberg's *QFT* Vol. I [@Weinberg1995] §5.7) states that under the
assumptions of (i) Lorentz invariance, (ii) positivity of energy, (iii)
microcausality, and (iv) Hilbert-space norm positivity, integer-spin
fields must commute at spacelike separations, while half-integer-spin
fields must anticommute. Each assumption descends from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$:

-   Lorentz invariance (i): from
    Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv), derived at Theorem 4.6 via
    Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-arena"};

-   Positivity of energy (ii): from the rest-energy condition
    $E_0 = mc^2 > 0$
