    (Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"}) with $c$ being the rate of
    $x_{4}$-advance in
    Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i);

-   Microcausality (iii): from the spacelike/timelike causal-cone
    structure of $M_{G}$ established by the Lorentzian signature
    $(-,+,+,+)$ of
    Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, with McGucken Spheres at
    spacelike-separated events being disjoint as causal-future cones
    (Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii) spherical symmetry sets the
    expansion rate to $c$);

-   Hilbert-space norm positivity (iv): from the inner-product
    construction of
    Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}.

All four assumptions hold in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework.

**Step 3 (Algebraic Channel): $4\pi$-periodicity forces the exchange sign.** For
half-integer spin, a $2\pi$ rotation acts as
$-\mathbf{1}_{\mathbb{C}^4}$ on the Dirac spinor
(Lemma [9.4](#lem:spin-double-cover){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:spin-double-cover"}). Exchanging two particles in a joint
two-particle configuration space corresponds to a homotopy class of
paths that, for half-integer spin, transports the spinor through a
$2\pi$ rotation, picking up the $-\mathbf{1}$ sign. The joint
wavefunction therefore satisfies $\Psi(x_2, x_1) = -\Psi(x_1, x_2)$ ---
antisymmetric. For integer spin, the analogous $2\pi$ rotation acts as
$+\mathbf{1}$, giving the symmetric exchange. Algebraic Channel delivers the
spin-statistics dichotomy.

**Step 4 (Geometric Channel): Exchange path on joint configuration space.** By
the McGucken Sphere construction (QB1,
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (v) at every event) and the
$SU(2) \to SO(3)$ double cover of the sphere isometry group
(Lemma [9.14](#lem:sphere-double-cover){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:sphere-double-cover"}), the spinor bundle over the
spatial 2-sphere $S^2$ carries the $\mathbb{C}^2$ defining
representation of $SU(2)$. For two identical fermions, the joint
configuration space is
$(\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \text{diagonal})/\mathbb{Z}_2$
(Leinaas--Myrheim 1977 [@LeinaasMyrheim1977]). The fundamental group of
this space (for $D = 3$ spatial dimensions) is $\mathbb{Z}_2$; the
non-trivial generator is the exchange path, which when lifted to the
universal cover transports the spinor through a $2\pi$ rotation.

**Step 5 (Geometric Channel): $-\mathbf{1}$ sign from spinor lift on the
McGucken Sphere.** By
Lemma [9.14](#lem:sphere-double-cover){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:sphere-double-cover"}, this $2\pi$ rotation acts as
$-\mathbf{1}$ on the spinor frame. The joint wavefunction therefore
satisfies $\Psi(x_2, x_1) = -\Psi(x_1, x_2)$ for fermions, $+\Psi$ for
bosons. The exchange sign is fixed by the topology of the spinor bundle
on $S_p$ generated by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at every event
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (ii)+(v)).

**Step 6 (Geometric Channel): Exclusion as wavefront non-coincidence +
disjointness verification.** Setting $x_1 = x_2 = x$:
$\Psi(x, x) = -\Psi(x, x) = 0$. No two identical fermions can have their
wavefronts coincide at the same spatial point with the same spin
orientation; this is the Pauli exclusion principle geometrically. The
McGucken Sphere wavefront of one fermion cannot occupy the same Sphere
mode (spatial location $\times$ spinor orientation) as another identical
fermion. *Both channels deliver the same conclusion* (integer spin $\to$
symmetric $\to$ bosons; half-integer spin $\to$ antisymmetric $\to$
fermions $\to$ Pauli exclusion). The two derivations are disjoint: Algebraic Channel uses Wigner classification + spin-statistics
theorem + analytic continuation; Geometric Channel uses Sphere spinor bundle +
$SU(2) \to SO(3)$ double cover + configuration-space fundamental group.
The shared content is $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the final exchange
sign. $\square$ ◻
:::

### Geometric Channel derivation (QB1 + $4\pi$-periodicity of spinor frames on Sphere)

::: channelb
*Geometric Channel Derivation 20.3* (Pauli exclusion from $4\pi$-periodicity of
spinor frames on McGucken Sphere). By QB1, every fermion is a McGucken
Sphere with spinor orientation in $\mathbb{C}^2$ (Geometric Channel of
Theorem [9.1](#thm:QMT9){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT9"}).
The spinor structure is the section of the double cover
$SU(2) \to SO(3)$ over the spatial 2-sphere $S^2$.

Exchange of two identical fermions corresponds to a $2\pi$ rotation in
the joint two-particle configuration space (a homotopy class of the
exchange path; see Leinaas--Myrheim 1977 [@LeinaasMyrheim1977]). On the
spinor frame, this $2\pi$ rotation acts as $-\mathbb{1}$ (Geometric Channel of
Theorem [9.1](#thm:QMT9){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT9"}).
The joint wavefunction therefore picks up a sign under exchange, i.e.,
is antisymmetric.

*Geometric interpretation of exclusion.* The wavefront of the McGucken
Sphere of one fermion cannot occupy the same Sphere mode as another
identical fermion: the antisymmetry of the joint wavefunction means the
joint amplitude vanishes when the two Sphere modes coincide. Pauli
exclusion is therefore the geometric impossibility of two identical
fermion wavefronts occupying the same Sphere mode---the
spatial-orientation realization of the spinor sign flip. ◻
:::

### Algebraic Channel derivation (QA6 --- Wigner classification plus spin-statistics)

::: channela
*Algebraic Channel Derivation 20.2* (Spin-statistics from Wigner classification
plus second-quantization anticommutation). By QA6 (Wigner
classification), particle states are labeled by spin
$s \in \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, integer $s$ for bosons and
half-integer $s$ for fermions.

The Pauli spin-statistics theorem (Pauli 1940 [@Pauli1940]; rigorous
proof via the analytic-continuation argument in Weinberg *Quantum Theory
of Fields* Vol. I [@Weinberg1995] §5.7) states that, under the
assumptions of Lorentz invariance, positivity of energy, microcausality,
and Hilbert-space norm-positivity, integer-spin fields must be quantized
with commutation relations $[\hat\phi(x), \hat\phi(y)] = 0$ for
spacelike separations and half-integer-spin fields must be quantized
with anticommutation relations $\{\hat\psi(x), \hat\psi(y)\} = 0$ for
spacelike separations. The anticommutation forces antisymmetric
multi-fermion states.

The lemma underneath the spin-statistics theorem is that, for
half-integer spin, a $2\pi$ rotation acts as $-\mathbb{1}$ on the spinor
(Theorem [9.1](#thm:QMT9){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT9"},
$4\pi$-periodicity); this sign flip propagates into the exchange
operation via the standard Lorentz-covariance argument and forces the
antisymmetric combination. ◻
:::

### Disjointness audit {#disjointness-audit-17}

**Geometric Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, McGucken Sphere spinor
orientation, $4\pi$-periodicity of spinor frames on $S^2$, joint

**Algebraic Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, Wigner classification,

**Intersection:**
$\{(\mathrm{McP}), \text{antisymmetric fermion wavefunction}\}$.
*Disjointness verified.*

-   Atomic shell structure (Mendeleev periodic table; quantum-mechanical

-   White dwarf stability (Chandrasekhar 1931): electron degeneracy

-   Neutron-star structure: neutron degeneracy pressure from exclusion.

-   Direct test of two-fermion-in-same-state suppression in cold-atom

## QM T21: Matter and Antimatter as the $\pm ic$ Orientation of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ {#ch:antimatter}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial
three. Throughout this chapter, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ refers to this
principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: (i) *invariance* --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the
expansion is isotropic in the spatial three, with the set of events
reachable from $p$ in proper time $\tau$ being a 2-sphere of radius
$c\tau$; (iii) *monotonicity* --- the integral curve is strictly
monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of $x_4$-advance; (iv)
*Lorentz consistency* --- the structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on
$M_{G}$; (v) *global validity* --- $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at
every event of $M_{G}$. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ (Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the central fact.

This chapter establishes the origin of antimatter in the
McGucken framework. The $\pm i$ sign ambiguity in
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$---the principle is
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= \pm ic$, with the sign chosen by
orientation---generates the matter / antimatter dichotomy.

### Statement

::: {#thm:QMT21 .theorem}
**Theorem 21.1** (QM T21: Matter--Antimatter, = Theorem 80 (Algebraic Channel)
and Theorem 103 (Geometric Channel) of [@Syn-2026]). *The matter / antimatter
distinction is the choice of sign in
$$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= +ic \qquad\text{(matter)}, \qquad \dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= -ic \qquad\text{(antimatter)}.$$
The two branches are related by CPT (charge-parity-time inversion), and
antimatter has all the same physical properties as matter except for the
sign-reversal of CPT-odd quantum numbers (charge, lepton number, baryon
number, etc.).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). We prove the matter-antimatter dichotomy along Algebraic Channel (CPT
theorem applied to Wigner classification) and Geometric Channel (geometric
$\pm ic$ orientation of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), in six explicit
steps. Both channels descend from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}): Algebraic Channel via the Minkowski metric of
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"} and the Wigner classification on its
Poincaré group; Geometric Channel via the binary orientation choice in the
perpendicularity marker $\pm i$ of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ itself.

**Step 1 (Algebraic Channel): Dirac's hole theory and modern second-quantisation
interpretation.** By QA1+QA6, the irreducible unitary representations of
the connected Poincaré group include the positive-energy ($E > 0$) and
negative-energy ($E < 0$) branches. The Lorentz invariance underlying
this classification descends from
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv), derived at Theorem 4.6 via the Minkowski metric of
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}. Dirac's original interpretation
[@Dirac1928] treated negative-energy solutions as filled-sea "holes,"
with a hole being an antiparticle of reversed charge. The modern
interpretation via second quantisation is equivalent: positive-energy
creation operators $\hat a^\dagger$ create particles; positive-energy
creation operators in the conjugate representation $\hat b^\dagger$
create antiparticles. The negative-energy mode of the original
wavefunction is reinterpreted as the positive-energy creation of a
conjugate-representation antiparticle.

**Step 2 (Algebraic Channel): CPT theorem assumptions verified from McGucken
structure.** The CPT theorem (Lüders, Pauli, Schwinger 1954--1957;
rigorous proof in Weinberg *QFT* Vol. I [@Weinberg1995] §5.8) states
that, under (i) Lorentz invariance, (ii) microcausality, (iii)
Hermiticity of the Hamiltonian, every relativistic QFT is invariant
under the combined operation
$\Theta_{\mathrm{CPT}} = \mathcal{C} \cdot \mathcal{P} \cdot \mathcal{T}$.
Each of the three assumptions descends from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$:

-   Lorentz invariance:
    Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv), derived at Theorem 4.6 via
    Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-arena"};

-   Microcausality: spacelike-disjoint McGucken Spheres at
    spacelike-separated events, with the causal-cone structure of
    Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii);

-   Hermiticity of $\hat{H}$:
    Lemma [7.3](#lem:hamiltonian-generator){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:hamiltonian-generator"}, descending from Stone's
    theorem applied to time-translation invariance of
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

Therefore CPT is a theorem of the McGucken framework. The transformation
reads
$$\Theta_{\mathrm{CPT}}\,\lvert \text{particle}, \mathbf{p}, s, q \rangle = \lvert \text{antiparticle}, \mathbf{p}, s, -q \rangle,$$
with $q$ all CPT-odd quantum numbers.

**Step 3 (Algebraic Channel): CPT-conjugate states have identical mass and
spin.** Two states related by $\Theta_{\mathrm{CPT}}$ are in the same
Poincaré representation (same mass-Casimir $m^2 c^2$ and same
Pauli--Lubanski-Casimir $s(s+1)$). All non-CPT-odd quantum numbers are
preserved; only the CPT-odd ones flip sign (electric charge, lepton
number, baryon number, magnetic moment, etc.). This is the source of the empirical observation that particles and antiparticles
have identical mass and spin to within experimental precision (CPT tests
on $K_0/\bar K_0$ and $e^+/e^-$ mass equality at the $\sim 10^{-19}$
level).

**Step 4 (Geometric Channel): Two orientations of the McGucken Sphere from
$\pm i$ in $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.** By QB1
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (v) at every event),
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ generates an iterated McGucken Sphere at every
event. The perpendicularity marker $i$ in $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ has
an intrinsic binary sign ambiguity: $\sqrt{-1}$ admits two values
$\pm i$. The two orientations generate two distinct sphere structures on
$M_{G}$:

-   $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= +ic$: the Sphere expands in the
    $+x_{4}$-direction (matter orientation, selected by
    Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iii) monotonicity for the matter
    sector);

-   $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= -ic$: the Sphere expands in the
    $-x_{4}$-direction (antimatter orientation, the time-reversed
    branch).

Under the identification $x_{4}= ict$ from
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"} (kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), the two orientations are mirror images under
reflection of $x_{4}$, which corresponds to $t \to -t$ (time reversal)
combined with $i \to -i$ (perpendicularity-marker complex conjugation).

**Step 5 (Geometric Channel): CPT as the orientation-flip symmetry of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.** Under the matter $\to$ antimatter
orientation flip $+ic \to -ic$, complex conjugation acts on
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ as $i \to -i$, which is the combined effect of:

-   Time reversal $\mathcal{T}$ (flipping the sign of $t$-evolution in
    $x_{4}= ict$, the kinematic shadow);

-   Parity $\mathcal{P}$ (flipping the spatial orientation of the
    Sphere, $\mathbf{x} \to -\mathbf{x}$);

-   Charge conjugation $\mathcal{C}$ (flipping the sign of CPT-odd
    quantum numbers, equivalently swapping representations under the
    $\pm i$ inequivalence).

The combined operation
$\Theta_{\mathrm{CPT}} = \mathcal{C} \cdot \mathcal{P} \cdot \mathcal{T}$
is the orientation-flip symmetry of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, mapping
matter to antimatter. This is the geometric content of CPT in the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework: CPT has the reading of a forced
consequence of the $\pm ic$ orientation freedom of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with the role of an emergent symmetry to be
tested experimentally replaced by the role of a derived theorem at the
McGucken-Principle level.

**Step 6 (Synthesis): Feynman's reading and dual-channel agreement.**
Feynman's interpretation of antimatter as "particles moving backwards in
time" (Feynman 1949 [@Feynman1949]) is the geometric content of the
$-ic$ orientation: the antimatter Sphere expands in the negative
$x_{4}$-direction, which from the matter frame's perspective is
"backwards in time" (since $x_{4}= ict$ and matter has $x_{4}$
increasing with $t$). Both channels reach: matter and antimatter are
CPT-conjugates, with identical mass/spin and opposite CPT-odd quantum
numbers, related by the $\pm i$ orientation of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.
The two derivations are derivationally disjoint: Algebraic Channel invokes Wigner
classification + Lüders--Pauli--Schwinger CPT theorem +
analytic-continuation machinery; Geometric Channel invokes the binary
orientation of the perpendicularity marker $\pm i$ in
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ itself. The shared content is
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the final CPT-conjugation relation.
$\square$ ◻
:::

### Geometric Channel derivation (QB1 with $\pm i$ orientation of the McGucken Sphere)

::: channelb
*Geometric Channel Derivation 21.3* (Antimatter from two iterated-Sphere
orientations of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). By QB1,
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ generates an iterated McGucken Sphere at every
event. The sign of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}$ is a binary choice---$+ic$ or
$-ic$---selected by orientation. The two orientations generate two
distinct sphere structures on $M_{G}$:

-   $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= +ic$: the Sphere expands in the
    $+x_{4}$-direction (matter orientation);

-   $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= -ic$: the Sphere expands in the
    $-x_{4}$-direction (antimatter orientation).

The two orientations are mirror images of each other under time
reversal, which (combined with parity inversion and charge conjugation,
by the CPT theorem) implements the matter--antimatter exchange.

Feynman's interpretation of antimatter as "particles moving backwards in
time" (Feynman 1949 [@Feynman1949]) is, in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework,
exactly the geometric content of the $-ic$ orientation of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$: the antimatter Sphere expands in the negative
$x_{4}$-direction, which from the matter frame's perspective is
"backwards in time." ◻
:::

### Algebraic Channel derivation (QA1+QA6 --- CPT theorem + Dirac negative-energy)

::: channela
*Algebraic Channel Derivation 21.2* (Antimatter from CPT theorem applied to
Wigner classification). By QA1 (Lorentz invariance) + QA6 (Wigner
classification), the Poincaré group's representations include the
positive-energy ($E > 0$) and negative-energy ($E < 0$) branches. The
negative-energy branch was originally interpreted (Dirac 1928
[@Dirac1928]) as antimatter via the hole-theoretic argument: the
negative-energy "sea" is filled, and a hole in the sea is an
antiparticle with reversed quantum numbers.

The modern interpretation, via second quantization, is the same physical
content: positive-energy creation operators $\hat{a}^\dagger$ create
particles; positive-energy creation operators in the conjugate
representation $\hat{b}^\dagger$ create antiparticles. The relation
between particles and antiparticles is CPT:
$$\Theta_{\text{CPT}}\,\lvert \text{particle}, p, s, q \rangle = \lvert \text{antiparticle}, p, s, -q \rangle,$$
where $\Theta_{\text{CPT}}$ is the antiunitary CPT operator and $q$
stands for all CPT-odd quantum numbers. ◻
:::

### QED (quantum electrodynamics) vertex factor from $U(1)$ minimal coupling

::: remark
*Remark 21.4*. The QED vertex factor $-ig\gamma^\mu$ (for an
electron--photon interaction) follows from $U(1)$ minimal coupling
(Theorem [16.1](#thm:QMT16){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT16"})
applied to the Dirac field
(Theorem [9.1](#thm:QMT9){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT9"}).
The CKM (Cabibbo--Kobayashi--Maskawa)-matrix structure
(Cabibbo--Kobayashi--Maskawa quark-flavor mixing) and the small but
nonzero CP-violation parameter $\eta_{CP} \approx 3 \times 10^{-3}$ are
not in conflict with CPT (which is exact); CP-violation is a feature of
the weak interaction's vertex structure, not a violation of CPT.
:::

### Disjointness audit {#disjointness-audit-18}

**Geometric Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, McGucken Sphere $\pm i$
orientation, time-reversal of Sphere expansion, Feynman
backwards-in-time reading.

**Algebraic Channel:** $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, Wigner classification,
positive-and negative-energy branches, CPT theorem, second-quantized
creation operators for particles and antiparticles.

**Intersection:**
$\{(\mathrm{McP}), \text{antimatter and matter as branches of }(\mathrm{McP})\}$.
*Disjointness verified.*

### Empirical anchor

-   Positron discovery (Anderson 1932): cloud-chamber observation of
    positively charged tracks with electron mass.

-   Antiproton discovery (Chamberlain, Segrè 1955): observed at the
    Bevatron at Berkeley.

-   Antihydrogen production (CERN ATHENA and ATRAP collaborations,
    2002): direct synthesis of antimatter atoms.

-   CPT tests (Hughes, Kinoshita, others): the muon $g$-factor and the
    proton/antiproton charge-to-mass ratio agree to $\sim 10^{-9}$
    between matter and antimatter, confirming CPT.

> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial

principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"

$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the

--- [@MG-Compton-2026] §1*
:::

### The Compton coupling as the matter--$x_4$ interaction proposal of the McGucken framework {#sec:compton-status}

The 22 theorems QM T1--T21 and QM T23 of the textbook are forced
consequences of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$: each follows from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ alone, or from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
together with an explicitly labelled assumption (such as
Wigner classification of Poincaré representations). The result of this
chapter --- a specific predicted Compton-frequency modulation of matter
coupling at characteristic frequency $\Omega$ with amplitude
$\varepsilon$ --- occupies a different position: the April
18, 2026 paper [@MG-Compton-2026] *proposes* this specific matter--$x_4$
interaction to complete the postulate, and the present
chapter develops the proposal and its falsifiable consequences.

### Statement

::: {#thm:QMT22 .theorem}
**Theorem 22.1** (QM T22: Compton Diffusion Coefficient;
[@MG-Compton-2026] §2--6). *A particle of mass $m$, at rest in the three
spatial dimensions, directs its entire four-velocity budget into advance
along $x_4$ at rate $ic$, and its rest-frame quantum phase accumulates
at the Compton angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ as the standard
free-particle wavefunction $\psi \sim e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}$. The Compton
coupling proposal of [@MG-Compton-2026] extends this baseline by
elevating the rest-mass phase from a global gauge freedom to a physical
oscillation driven by the advancing $x_4$:
$$\psi(\tau) \;\sim\; e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}\,\bigl[1 + \varepsilon\cos(\Omega\tau)\bigr],
\label{eq:compton-coupling-wavefunction}$$ with universal dimensionless
coupling $\varepsilon$ and modulation frequency $\Omega$ (both
species-independent properties: $\varepsilon$ and $\Omega$ are intrinsic
characteristics of the $x_4$-advance under
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, the same for every matter species coupling
to the advancing $x_4$, with the role of matter-species-dependent
parameters replaced by the role of universal $x_4$-advance parameters).
Equivalently, the coupling contributes an effective rest-frame
Hamiltonian
$$H_{\mathrm{mod}}(\tau) \;=\; \varepsilon\,mc^2 \cos(\Omega\tau).
\label{eq:H-mod}$$ Under standard environmental coupling with damping
rate $\gamma$, the coupling produces:*

1.  **momentum diffusion* with constant
    $D_p = \varepsilon^2 m^2 c^2 \Omega/2$;*

2.  **spatial diffusion* with constant
    $$\boxed{\ D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} \;=\; \frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega}{2\gamma^2}\ }
    \label{eq:Dx-mass-independent}$$ that is **mass-independent** ($m$
    cancels between coupling strength and mobility);*

3.  **total diffusion*
    $D_{\mathrm{total}} = kT/(m\gamma) + \varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega/(2\gamma^2)$,
    the second term persisting at $T = 0$ as a sharp experimental
    signature;*

4.  **entropy growth*
    $S(t) = (3/2)k_B \ln(4\pi e\, D_{\mathrm{total}}\,t)$, with the
    direction of increase tied to the direction of $x_4$-expansion
    (linking the thermodynamic arrow of time to the geometric arrow of
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).*

*The current empirical bound is
$\varepsilon^2\Omega \lesssim 2D_0^{\mathrm{exp}}\gamma^2/c^2$ from
atomic-clock and cold-atom diffusion experiments; at Planck-scale
$\Omega \sim c/\ell_P$, this gives $\varepsilon \lesssim 10^{-20}$.*
:::

### Derivation of the momentum diffusion (Floquet--Magnus--Lindblad) {#sec:compton-floquet-magnus-lindblad}

We reconstruct the explicit derivation chain of [@MG-Compton-2026] §3.

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT22"}, umbrella structure.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The theorem makes four
distinct claims (i)--(iv); each is established by a separate technical
proof block below. We give the overview here, anchored in
McGucken machinery descending from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

**Step 1: Motivation for the Compton coupling from the
four-velocity-budget structure.** By
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} (the four-velocity budget at
rest), a particle of mass $m$ at spatial rest directs its entire
four-velocity budget into $x_{4}$-advance at rate $c$, with rest-frame
phase accumulation at angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$
(Theorem [4.1](#thm:QMT4){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT4"}).
The standard free-particle wavefunction $\psi \sim e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}$
captures this baseline. The Compton coupling proposal extends the
baseline by promoting the rest-mass phase from a global gauge freedom to
a physical oscillation driven by the advancing $x_{4}$:
equation [\[eq:compton-coupling-wavefunction\]](#eq:compton-coupling-wavefunction){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:compton-coupling-wavefunction"}. This promotion is
consistent with $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ but not forced by it;
[@MG-Compton-2026] §9 explicitly identifies the form as "one proposal
among possible choices," and the present chapter develops its
falsifiable consequences without claiming uniqueness. The
four-velocity-budget structure of
Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"} establishes that *some*
matter--$x_{4}$ coupling is permitted, with
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ as its natural angular-frequency scale; the
specific bilinear-amplitude form $[1 + \varepsilon\cos(\Omega\tau)]$ is
the proposal's particular realisation, to be tested against alternative
coupling structures
(cf. Remark [22.6](#rmk:compton-status-correction){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:compton-status-correction"}).

**Step 2: Clause (i) --- momentum diffusion (Heuristic + Formal proofs
below).** The effective rest-frame Hamiltonian
$H_{\mathrm{mod}}(\tau) = \varepsilon mc^2\cos(\Omega\tau)$ has zero
first-order time-average, so no net coherent force results. The
second-order stochastic momentum kicks accumulate as a random walk under
weak environmental decoherence, giving momentum-diffusion constant
$D_p = \varepsilon^2 m^2 c^2\Omega/2$. The Heuristic-derivation proof
block gives the order-of-magnitude argument; the Formal-derivation proof
block establishes the result rigorously through Floquet analysis, Magnus
expansion, and Lindblad reduction.

**Step 3: Clause (ii) --- mass-independent spatial diffusion
(Langevin/Ornstein--Uhlenbeck proof below).** The momentum-diffusion
result of Step 2 combines with the Einstein--Smoluchowski mobility
relation $\mu = 1/(m\gamma)$ via standard Langevin/Ornstein--Uhlenbeck
analysis to give spatial diffusion
$D_x = D_p/(m\gamma)^2 = \varepsilon^2 c^2\Omega/(2\gamma^2)$. The
mass-factor $m$ cancels exactly: the Compton coupling has strength
$\propto m$ in the Hamiltonian, but the mobility $\propto 1/m$, and
these compensate in the diffusion constant. This mass-independence is
the sharp experimental signature distinguishing the McGucken Compton
coupling from any mass-dependent diffusion mechanism. The detailed
derivation is in the Langevin/Ornstein--Uhlenbeck proof block below.

**Step 4: Clause (iii) --- total diffusion has a $T = 0$ residue.** The
total diffusion is the sum of independent thermal Brownian contribution
$D_{\mathrm{thermal}} = kT/(m\gamma)$ and the McGucken Compton-coupling
contribution $D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})}$. At $T = 0$, the thermal term
vanishes but the McGucken contribution persists: this is the falsifiable
signature. The additivity follows from independence of the noise sources
(thermal noise from a bath; Compton noise from $x_{4}$-coupling,
independently established by
Theorem [17.5](#thm:second-law-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:second-law-nonlocality"} as a separate physical
mechanism).

**Step 5: Clause (iv) --- entropy growth tied to $x_{4}$-arrow.** The
entropy of a Gaussian wave packet of variance
$\sigma^2(t) = D_{\mathrm{total}}t$ in three dimensions is
$S(t) = \frac{3}{2}k_B\ln(4\pi e\,D_{\mathrm{total}}\,t)$. The growth
$dS/dt > 0$ tracks the direction of $x_{4}$-advance: the diffusion is
sourced by the $x_{4}$-coupling, which advances at rate $+ic$ (forward
orientation). The thermodynamic arrow of time is therefore tied to the
geometric arrow of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. This is the
McGucken-anchored unification of the second-law arrow with the
spacetime-expansion arrow
(cf. Theorem [12.18](#thm:five-arrows-of-time){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:five-arrows-of-time"} of
Chapter [12](#ch:lagrangian-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:lagrangian-uniqueness"}).

**Step 6: Empirical bound.** Atomic-clock and cold-atom diffusion
experiments give the current bound
$\varepsilon^2\Omega \lesssim 2 D_0^{\mathrm{exp}}\gamma^2/c^2$; at
Planck-scale $\Omega \sim c/\ell_P$, this implies
$\varepsilon \lesssim 10^{-20}$. The proposal is therefore consistent
with current data but predicts a sharp, falsifiable diffusion residue at
$T = 0$.

The technical proof blocks that follow establish the individual clauses
formally. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Heuristic derivation; [@MG-Compton-2026] §3.1.* For $\Omega$ large
compared to inverse timescales of spatial motion, the first-order
time-average of $H_{\mathrm{mod}}$ vanishes:
$\langle\varepsilon mc^2 \cos(\Omega\tau)\rangle_\tau = 0$, so the
particle experiences no net coherent force. The second-order effect is a
stochastic momentum kick. Each modulation cycle of period
$\sim 1/\Omega$ produces a momentum impulse of order
$\Delta p \sim \varepsilon mc$. Over time $t$ there are $\sim \Omega t$
cycles, and in the presence of weak environmental coupling that breaks
coherence between cycles, their contributions add as a random walk
rather than a coherent displacement:
$$\langle(\Delta p)^2\rangle \sim \varepsilon^2 m^2 c^2 \Omega t.$$ This
gives momentum-space diffusion with constant
$D_p = \varepsilon^2 m^2 c^2 \Omega / 2$. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Formal derivation; [@MG-Compton-2026] §3.2.* The heuristic result is
obtained rigorously through Floquet analysis of the time-periodic
Hamiltonian $H_0 + H_{\mathrm{mod}}(\tau)$, followed by Magnus / van
Vleck expansion in $\varepsilon$:

1.  *Floquet decomposition.* The Hamiltonian
    $H_0 + H_{\mathrm{mod}}(\tau)$ is $T$-periodic with
    $T = 2\pi/\Omega$; Floquet's theorem gives a quasi-energy spectrum
    and a unitary $U(\tau) = e^{-iK\tau}P(\tau)$ with
    $P(\tau + T) = P(\tau)$.

2.  *Magnus/van Vleck expansion.* The effective time-averaged
    Hamiltonian $K = K_0 + \varepsilon K_1 + \varepsilon^2 K_2 + \ldots$
    has $K_1 = \langle H_{\mathrm{mod}}\rangle_\tau = 0$ (no first-order
    shift); $K_2$ is the second-order rotating-frame correction.

3.  *Lindblad reduction.* When the particle is coupled weakly to an
    environment (residual gas, thermal bath, engineered dissipation),
    the reduced density matrix obeys a Lindblad equation with a
    momentum-diffusion term of the form
    $D_p \sim \varepsilon^2 m^2 c^2 \Omega / 2$ up to an $O(1)$ constant
    depending on the environmental coupling structure. This step is
    standard in the theory of periodically driven open quantum systems
    and is adopted from there in [@MG-Compton-2026].

The resulting momentum-diffusion constant is the result stated in clause
(i) of Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT22"}. ◻
:::

### Derivation of the mass-independent spatial diffusion {#sec:compton-spatial-diffusion}

::: proof
*Spatial diffusion via Langevin/Ornstein--Uhlenbeck; [@MG-Compton-2026]
§4.* For a particle in an environment providing damping with rate
$\gamma$ (residual gas collisions, trap-induced cooling, engineered
dissipation), the reduced dynamics is described by the Langevin /
Ornstein--Uhlenbeck equation
$$\frac{dp}{dt} = -\gamma p + \eta(t), \qquad \langle\eta(t)\eta(t')\rangle = 2D_p \delta(t - t').$$
At long times compared to $1/\gamma$, this produces spatial diffusion
with constant $$D_x = \frac{D_p}{(m\gamma)^2}.$$ Substituting the
Compton-coupling result $D_p = \varepsilon^2 m^2 c^2 \Omega / 2$ from
Section [22.3](#sec:compton-floquet-magnus-lindblad){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:compton-floquet-magnus-lindblad"}:
$$D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} \;=\; \frac{\varepsilon^2 m^2 c^2 \Omega}{2 m^2 \gamma^2} \;=\; \frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega}{2\gamma^2}.$$
The mass dependence has cancelled. The coupling strength is proportional
to $m$ (through the rest energy $mc^2$ in $H_{\mathrm{mod}}$); the
mobility $1/(m\gamma)$ is inversely proportional to $m$. The two cancel
exactly. The result is a sharp prediction of the specific coupling form
proposed by [@MG-Compton-2026]. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:mass-independence-essential .remark}
*Remark 22.2* (Why mass-independence is the essential-input test). The
mass-independence of $D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})}$ is the single feature that
distinguishes the Compton coupling proposal from any thermal mechanism
(where $D_x \propto 1/m$ via the Einstein relation), from gravitational
decoherence proposals (where the coupling scales as $m^2$), and from
continuous spontaneous-localisation models (where it scales as $m$).
*Cross-species comparison of residual diffusion at $T \to 0$ is
therefore the direct test of the Compton coupling form.* A
mass-dependent residual would rule out this specific ansatz and point
toward a different coupling structure within the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework.
:::

### Total diffusion and the zero-temperature signature {#sec:compton-total-diffusion}

::: {#thm:compton-zero-T-signature .theorem}
**Theorem 22.3** (Zero-temperature signature; [@MG-Compton-2026] §5).
*Adding the Compton-coupling contribution to ordinary thermal diffusion
from the Einstein relation gives
$$D_{\mathrm{total}}(T) \;=\; \frac{kT}{m\gamma} + \frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega}{2\gamma^2}.
\label{eq:D-total}$$ The first term is standard thermal diffusion and
vanishes as $T \to 0$. The second term is temperature-independent and
persists at $T = 0$. A gas cooled toward absolute zero retains a nonzero
diffusion constant sourced by its coupling to $x_4$'s expansion, after
all known thermal and technical noise channels are minimised.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: Standard thermal diffusion via Einstein relation.**
For a Brownian particle in equilibrium with a thermal bath at
temperature $T$, the Einstein--Sutherland--Smoluchowski relation
(Einstein 1905; [@Einstein1905SR]) gives the spatial diffusion constant
$$D_x^{(\mathrm{thermal})} = \mu k_B T,$$ where $\mu = 1/(m\gamma)$ is
the mobility ($\gamma$ the damping rate, $m$ the particle mass).
Substituting: $$D_x^{(\mathrm{thermal})} = \frac{k_B T}{m\gamma}.$$ This
is the standard thermal contribution to spatial diffusion; it vanishes
as $T \to 0$.

**Step 2: McGucken-Compton contribution.** By
Section [22.4](#sec:compton-spatial-diffusion){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:compton-spatial-diffusion"}
(Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT22"},
clause (ii)), the spatial diffusion sourced by the Compton coupling at
all temperatures is
$$D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} = \frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega}{2\gamma^2}.$$
This expression contains *no temperature dependence*:
$\varepsilon, c, \Omega, \gamma$ are all temperature-independent (with
$\gamma$ understood as the asymptotic-low-$T$ damping rate, which may
itself have weak $T$-dependence but does not vanish at $T = 0$). The
McGucken-Compton contribution is therefore temperature-independent.

**Step 3: Additivity of diffusion contributions.** The two diffusion
mechanisms (thermal Brownian motion and Compton coupling to
$x_4$-expansion) are statistically independent stochastic processes: the
thermal noise has bath origin, the Compton noise has $x_4$-coupling
origin (by Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT22"}). For independent additive noise sources, the
variance of position grows linearly in $t$ with rate equal to the sum of
the individual diffusion constants (a standard fact about sums of
independent Gaussian processes:
$\mathrm{Var}(X_1 + X_2) = \mathrm{Var}(X_1) + \mathrm{Var}(X_2)$ for
independent $X_1, X_2$). Hence
$$D_{\mathrm{total}}(T) = D_x^{(\mathrm{thermal})}(T) + D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} = \frac{k_B T}{m\gamma} + \frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega}{2\gamma^2}.$$

**Step 4: Zero-temperature limit.** As $T \to 0$, the first term
vanishes ($k_B T/(m\gamma) \to 0$), but the second term remains
$\varepsilon^2 c^2\Omega/(2\gamma^2) > 0$ (provided
$\varepsilon \neq 0$, i.e., the Compton coupling is non-trivial).
Therefore
$$\lim_{T \to 0}D_{\mathrm{total}}(T) = \frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2\Omega}{2\gamma^2} \neq 0.$$
A gas cooled toward absolute zero retains a temperature-independent
residual diffusion constant of magnitude
$\varepsilon^2 c^2\Omega/(2\gamma^2)$, sourced not by thermal
fluctuations but by the universal coupling to $x_4$-expansion of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. ◻
:::

The signature is analogous to how quantum zero-point motion leaves
residual fluctuations where classical theory predicts none, but the
source here is explicit: coupling to the advancing fourth dimension
rather than zero-point field fluctuations of the standard kinds. This is
the empirical handle by which the Compton coupling proposal of
[@MG-Compton-2026] is distinguished from standard QM at the level of
experiment.

### Entropy evolution and the arrow of time {#sec:compton-entropy}

::: {#thm:compton-entropy .theorem}
**Theorem 22.4** (Entropy growth from $x_4$-coupling; [@MG-Compton-2026]
§6). *A gas of $N$ particles initially sharply localised evolves under
$D_{\mathrm{total}}$ into a three-dimensional Gaussian distribution
$$p(x, t) = \frac{1}{(2\pi\sigma^2(t))^{3/2}} \exp\bigl(-|x|^2/(2\sigma^2(t))\bigr),$$
with variance $\sigma^2(t) = 2D_{\mathrm{total}}\,t$. The Shannon
entropy of the spatial distribution is
$$\boxed{\ S(t) \;=\; -k_B \int d^3x\, p(x, t) \ln p(x, t) \;=\; \tfrac{3}{2} k_B \ln(4\pi e D_{\mathrm{total}}\,t)\ }
\label{eq:compton-entropy}$$ up to an additive constant depending on
units and initial conditions. The entropy grows monotonically and
logarithmically in time. At $T = 0$ the thermal contribution vanishes
but $D_{\mathrm{total}} = D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} > 0$, so **entropy still
grows**: the McGucken mechanism produces entropy increase even in the
zero-temperature limit.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has four steps. The entropy growth is a
direct consequence of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, the physical, geometric fact that the fourth
dimension expands at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric
manner): the $x_{4}$-coupling diffusion coefficient
$D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})}$ is generated by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii) (spherical symmetry of the
$x_{4}$-expansion, producing isotropic diffusion in 3-space) and clause
(iii) (monotonicity, fixing the arrow of $x_{4}$-advance and hence the
direction of entropy increase), with $x_4 = ict$ the integrated
kinematic shadow per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}.

**Step 1: Gaussian-spreading from diffusion equation.** The diffusion
equation $\partial_t p = D_{\mathrm{total}}\,\nabla^2 p$ with initial
condition $p(x, 0) = \delta^3(x)$ (sharply localised) has the well-known
fundamental solution (heat kernel)
$$p(x, t) = \frac{1}{(4\pi D_{\mathrm{total}}\,t)^{3/2}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{|x|^2}{4 D_{\mathrm{total}}\,t}\right).$$
Identifying with the Gaussian form
$p(x, t) = (2\pi\sigma^2(t))^{-3/2}\exp(-|x|^2/(2\sigma^2))$ gives
$\sigma^2(t) = 2 D_{\mathrm{total}}\,t$. The Gaussian Green's function
is the standard heat-kernel formula (Reed--Simon [@ReedSimon1980] §X.1,
the heat-equation propagator on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$).

**Step 2: Shannon/Boltzmann entropy of a 3D Gaussian.** For an isotropic
Gaussian $p(x) = (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-3/2}\exp(-|x|^2/(2\sigma^2))$, the
differential Shannon entropy is computed directly: $$\begin{aligned}
S/k_B &= -\int d^3 x\,p(x)\ln p(x) \\
&= -\int d^3 x\,p(x)\left[-\tfrac{3}{2}\ln(2\pi\sigma^2) - \frac{|x|^2}{2\sigma^2}\right] \\
&= \tfrac{3}{2}\ln(2\pi\sigma^2) + \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\int d^3 x\,|x|^2\,p(x).
\end{aligned}$$ The second-moment integral for the 3D isotropic
Gaussian: $\int d^3 x\,|x|^2\,p(x) = 3\sigma^2$ (one factor of
$\sigma^2$ from each spatial dimension, times the variance integral
$\int (x^i)^2 p(x) dx^i = \sigma^2$ for each $i = 1, 2, 3$). Hence
$$S/k_B = \tfrac{3}{2}\ln(2\pi\sigma^2) + \tfrac{3}{2} = \tfrac{3}{2}\ln(2\pi e\sigma^2),$$
where we used $\ln e = 1$ to absorb the additive $3/2$ into the log.

**Step 3: Substitute $\sigma^2(t) = 2D_{\mathrm{total}}\,t$.**
$$S(t)/k_B = \tfrac{3}{2}\ln(2\pi e \cdot 2D_{\mathrm{total}}\,t) = \tfrac{3}{2}\ln(4\pi e D_{\mathrm{total}}\,t).$$
This is
[\[eq:compton-entropy\]](#eq:compton-entropy){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:compton-entropy"}.

**Step 4: Monotonicity and zero-temperature persistence.**
Differentiating: $$\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{3 k_B}{2 t} > 0,$$ so entropy
is strictly increasing for all $t > 0$. At $T = 0$, by
Theorem [22.3](#thm:compton-zero-T-signature){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:compton-zero-T-signature"},
$D_{\mathrm{total}}(T = 0) = \varepsilon^2 c^2\Omega/(2\gamma^2) > 0$
(provided the Compton coupling is non-trivial), so $S(t)$ continues to
grow even at absolute zero. The McGucken-Compton mechanism produces
entropy increase from $x_{4}$-coupling alone, independent of any thermal
reservoir. The direction of entropy increase tracks the direction of
$x_{4}$-advance, both fixed by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iii) (monotonicity: the integral
curve is strictly monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of
$x_{4}$-advance and hence the thermodynamic arrow of time). The
zero-temperature persistence is the signature of the McGucken mechanism
distinguishing it from purely thermal diffusion: at $T = 0$ all thermal
contributions vanish, but the $x_{4}$-coupling continues to drive
Gaussian spreading at rate $D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} > 0$ supplied by the
universal $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at every event of $M_{G}$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(v)). $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:arrow-of-time .remark}
*Remark 22.5* (The arrow of time as the arrow of $x_4$-expansion). The
direction of entropy increase under
Theorem [22.4](#thm:compton-entropy){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:compton-entropy"} follows the direction of $x_4$'s
expansion. Because $x_4$ advances monotonically in one direction and
does not retreat (this is the integrated kinematic shadow of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ being irreversible), the diffusion it induces
is forward-directed, and the entropy increase is forward-directed in the
same sense. *The arrow of time in this gas is the same arrow as $x_4$'s
expansion.* The thermodynamic arrow of time, in the McGucken-Compton
picture, has the reading of a derived feature of the
universal $x_4$-coupling, with the role of a fundamental separate
postulate replaced by the role of a derived consequence of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iii) (monotonicity of the
$x_4$-advance): time goes forward because $x_4$ goes forward, and
entropy increases because $x_4$ expands.
:::


::: {#rmk:compton-entropy-orientation-iff .remark}
*Remark 22.5.A* (The Compton-entropy/orientation iff and its

### Three experimental tests of the $(\varepsilon, \Omega)$ parameter space {#sec:compton-experimental-tests}

The Compton coupling proposal of [@MG-Compton-2026] §7 supplies three
falsification routes.

#### Test 1: Zero-temperature residual diffusion {#test-1-zero-temperature-residual-diffusion .unnumbered}

Cold-atom experiments in optical lattices, magneto-optical traps, and
ion traps can measure diffusion constants at ultra-low temperatures. At
the lowest accessible temperatures, the thermal contribution
$kT/(m\gamma)$ is strongly suppressed. Fitting
$D_{\mathrm{meas}}(T) \approx kT/(m\gamma) + D_0$, the intercept $D_0$
at $T \to 0$ is identified with $D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})}$ if all other
noise sources are accounted for. This gives the direct constraint
$$\varepsilon^2 \Omega \;\lesssim\; \frac{2 D_0^{\mathrm{exp}} \gamma^2}{c^2}.$$
For Planck-scale $\Omega \sim c/\ell_P \approx 1.85 \times 10^{43}$ Hz,
current atomic-clock bounds on anomalous low-temperature diffusion
constrain $\varepsilon \lesssim 10^{-20}$. Lower values of $\Omega$
relax the bound as $\varepsilon \propto \sqrt{D_0/\Omega}$.

#### Test 2: Cross-species mass-independence {#test-2-cross-species-mass-independence .unnumbered}

Because $D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})}$ is mass-independent
(Section [22.4](#sec:compton-spatial-diffusion){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:compton-spatial-diffusion"}), two species $A$ and $B$
with similar damping rates should show residual-diffusion ratios
$$\frac{D_{0, A}}{D_{0, B}} \;\approx\; \left(\frac{\gamma_B}{\gamma_A}\right)^2 \qquad \text{independent of the mass ratio } m_A/m_B.$$
This contrasts sharply with thermal diffusion, where the ratio scales as
$m_B/m_A$. Comparing residual diffusion across electrons in solids, ions
in traps, and neutral atoms in optical lattices (with $\gamma$
controlled or measured) provides the cleanest single test of the Compton
coupling form.

#### Test 3: Spectroscopic sidebands at $\pm\Omega$ {#test-3-spectroscopic-sidebands-at-pmomega .unnumbered}

The coupling modulates the rest energy at frequency $\Omega$.
Transitions tied to the rest-mass frequency would carry sidebands at
offsets of $\pm\Omega$. For Planck-scale $\Omega$ these are far above
accessible spectroscopic resolution; for lower $\Omega$ they fall within
range of optical clocks and trapped-ion interferometry, which reach
fractional frequency precisions of $\sim 10^{-18}$ to $10^{-19}$.

### Audit and scope {#sec:compton-audit}

::: {#rmk:compton-status-correction .remark}
*Remark 22.6* (Status correction: the Compton coupling is proposed, not
forced). The original prior-iteration draft of this textbook (and prior
turns of the build pipeline) labelled this chapter as the "most directly
falsifiable prediction of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ beyond the standard
QM phenomenology" in a manner that left ambiguous whether the prediction
was *forced* by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ or merely *consistent* with it.
The full reading of [@MG-Compton-2026] now in hand clarifies the status:
the coupling is a proposed matter interaction, explicitly described by
the paper as "one specific proposal to be tested" (§1) and "one proposal
among possible choices" (§9). $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ admits other
matter couplings that would yield different diffusion predictions and
different experimental signatures. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is therefore
falsifiable in two distinct senses: (a) the 22 forced
theorems QM T1--T21 and T23 are falsifiable through any experimental
contradiction of standard QM phenomenology; (b) the present chapter is
falsifiable through any experimental contradiction of the specific
$(\varepsilon, \Omega)$ Compton coupling, which would rule out this
particular matter-coupling proposal while leaving the postulate
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ intact.

This status is also why the present chapter carries a single derivation
rather than the paired Algebraic and Geometric Channel derivations of QM
T1--T21 and T23. Derivational disjointness is a property of two routes
from the principle to one forced result; where a result rests on the
principle together with a proposed coupling, a second route through the
other channel would inherit the same proposal and the audit would record
that proposal in both columns. The dual-channel structure resumes at QM
T23.
:::

::: {#rmk:compton-wigner .remark}
*Remark 22.7* (On the relation to Wigner classification). A prior draft
of this textbook indicated that [@MG-Compton-2026], once read in full,
would eliminate the dependency on Wigner classification in the
Schrödinger Algebraic Channel derivation of
Chapter [7](#ch:schrodinger){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:schrodinger"}. *The full reading of the paper does not
support that claim.* The paper supplies a Compton-coupling
matter-interaction proposal --- specifically, the coupling form
$\psi \sim e^{-imc^2\tau/\hbar}[1 + \varepsilon\cos(\Omega\tau)]$ and
its diffusion consequences --- not a derivation of the relativistic
dispersion relation $E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4$ from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ alone. The relativistic dispersion remains in
the Schrödinger Algebraic Channel audit traceable to the assumption
(labelled A6 in Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"}) about the Wigner classification of the
Poincaré representations, and the present chapter does not change that
status. The Geometric Channel derivation of Schrödinger via Klein--Gordon
non-relativistic limit ([@MG-NonlocalityProb-2026] §6.6a) remains the
cleanest route; it relies only on the assumption A6.
:::

### Empirical anchor and falsifiability {#sec:compton-empirical}

The Compton coupling proposal is the most directly testable extension of
standard QM phenomenology in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework. The three
experimental routes of
Section [22.7](#sec:compton-experimental-tests){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:compton-experimental-tests"} together delimit the
$(\varepsilon, \Omega)$ parameter space across decades of $\Omega$, with
the current cumulative bound from atomic-clock and cold-atom diffusion
experiments giving $\varepsilon \lesssim 10^{-20}$ at Planck-scale
$\Omega$. Looser values of $\Omega$ produce looser bounds on
$\varepsilon$ according to $\varepsilon \propto \sqrt{D_0/\Omega}$.

A successful detection of zero-temperature residual diffusion with the
predicted mass-independence and sidebands would confirm the specific
Compton coupling form; a failed detection at improved precision would
rule it out and motivate one of the alternative coupling structures
admitted by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. Either outcome leaves the
postulate $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ intact and the forced
theorems QM T1--T21 and T23 unaffected; this chapter is the
empirical-signature chapter of the textbook, and its falsifiability is
the testable handle the framework supplies.

## QM T23: Feynman Diagrams as 4D-$x_{4}$-Trajectories {#ch:feynman-diagrams}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial
three. Throughout this chapter, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ refers to this
principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: (i) *invariance* --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the
expansion is isotropic in the spatial three, with the set of events
reachable from $p$ in proper time $\tau$ being a 2-sphere of radius
$c\tau$; (iii) *monotonicity* --- the integral curve is strictly
monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of $x_4$-advance; (iv)
*Lorentz consistency* --- the structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on
$M_{G}$; (v) *global validity* --- $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at
every event of $M_{G}$. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ (Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the central fact.

### Statement

::: {#thm:QMT23 .theorem}
**Theorem 23.1** (QM T23: Feynman diagrams, = Theorem 82 (Algebraic Channel) and
Theorem 105 (Geometric Channel) of [@Syn-2026]). *The Feynman-diagram apparatus
of perturbative quantum field theory---propagators, vertex factors, the
$+i\varepsilon$ prescription, Dyson expansion, Wick's theorem, loop
integrals, Wick rotation to Euclidean signature---is the perturbative
expansion of the path integral
(Theorem [15.1](#thm:QMT15){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT15"})
in powers of the coupling, with the diagrammatic elements as the
geometric structure of 4D $x_{4}$-trajectories on $M_{G}$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We prove the Feynman-diagram structure along Algebraic Channel
(Dyson--Wick expansion of $S$-matrix) and Geometric Channel ($x_{4}$-trajectory
configurations on $M_{G}$), in six explicit steps. Both channels descend
from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}): Algebraic Channel via Stone's theorem and the path
integral of Theorem [15.1](#thm:QMT15){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT15"}, Geometric Channel via the McGucken Sphere structure of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (ii)+(v).

**Step 1 (Algebraic Channel): Dyson series from time-translation invariance.**
By QA2 (Stone's theorem applied via
Lemma [3.3](#lem:Hhat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:Hhat-generator"}, descending from time-translation
invariance of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ per
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i)), the time-evolution operator is
$\hat{U}(t) = \exp(-it\hat{H}/\hbar)$. Splitting
$\hat{H}= \hat{H}_0 + \hat{H}_{\mathrm{int}}$ (free + interaction), and
moving to the interaction picture, the $S$-matrix
$\hat S = \hat{U}^\dagger_0(\infty)\hat{U}(\infty)$ has the Dyson series
[@Dyson1949]:
$$\hat S = T\exp\!\left(-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int dt\,\hat H_{\mathrm{int}}(t)\right) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-i)^n}{n!\hbar^n}\int dt_1\cdots dt_n\,T[\hat H_{\mathrm{int}}(t_1)\cdots\hat H_{\mathrm{int}}(t_n)],$$
with $T$ the time-ordering. This is the perturbative expansion in powers
of $\hat H_{\mathrm{int}}$.

**Step 2 (Algebraic Channel): Wick's theorem and contractions.** For a free
scalar field $\hat\phi$ on the McGucken Hilbert space
(Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"}), Wick's theorem (Wick 1950
[@Wick1950]) reduces a time-ordered product to a sum over normal-ordered
products with contractions:
$$T[\hat\phi(x_1)\cdots\hat\phi(x_n)] = \sum_{\text{contractions}} (\text{product of two-point contractions})\cdot(\text{normal-ordered remainder}).$$
Each two-point contraction $\langle T[\hat\phi(x)\hat\phi(y)]\rangle$ is
the Feynman propagator. This decomposition into propagators with
vertices gives the Feynman-rule structure.

**Step 3 (Algebraic Channel): Feynman rules and the $+i\varepsilon$ prescription
from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.** The standard Feynman rules
(Peskin--Schroeder [@PeskinSchroeder1995] Ch. 4) emerge:

-   Propagator:
    $\langle T[\hat\phi(x)\hat\phi(y)]\rangle = i\hbar/(p^2 - m^2 + i\varepsilon)$
    in momentum space, with the $+i\varepsilon$ prescription enforcing
    the causal-retarded propagator. The sign $+i\varepsilon$ (not
    $-i\varepsilon$) is fixed by the forward $+ic$ direction of
    $x_{4}$-advance from
    Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iii) (monotonicity); this is
    Theorem [9.21](#thm:twelve-i){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:twelve-i"} case 7 (the $i\varepsilon$-prescription
    perpendicularity-marker case);

-   Vertex: $-ig\gamma^\mu$ for QED electron--photon, supplied by
    minimal coupling from
    Theorem [16.1](#thm:QMT16){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT16"} (gauge invariance derived from
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$);

-   Loop integral: $\int d^4 k/(2\pi)^4$ over each loop's four-momentum,
    with appropriate regularization (dimensional regularization,
    Pauli--Villars, etc.).

The full set of Feynman rules is therefore the algebraic encoding of the
Dyson--Wick expansion of the $S$-matrix.

**Step 4 (Geometric Channel): Path-integral perturbative expansion.** By
Theorem [15.1](#thm:QMT15){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT15"},
the propagator
$K(x_B, t_B; x_A, t_A) = \int\mathcal{D}[\gamma]\,e^{iS[\gamma]/\hbar}$
sums over continuous paths $\gamma$ on $M_{G}$, with each path generated
by iterated McGucken-Sphere Huygens construction from
Proposition [4.11](#prop:iter){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:iter"}. With interactions, the action splits as
$S = S_0 + S_{\mathrm{int}}$, and the exponential expands as
$$e^{iS/\hbar} = e^{iS_0/\hbar}\sum_n \frac{1}{n!}\left(\frac{iS_{\mathrm{int}}}{\hbar}\right)^n.$$
Each power of $S_{\mathrm{int}}$ corresponds to an interaction vertex in
the diagrammatic expansion.

**Step 5 (Geometric Channel): Diagrams as $x_{4}$-trajectory configurations on
$M_{G}$.** Each Feynman diagram corresponds to a specific configuration
of $x_{4}$-trajectories on $M_{G}$: particle worldlines (propagators),
interaction events (vertices), and loop closures (no external
endpoints). By
Proposition [23.4](#prop:propagator-rides-sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:propagator-rides-sphere"} (propagator rides the McGucken
Sphere), each propagator is the sphere-wavefront between two events; by
Proposition [23.6](#prop:vertex-sphere-intersection){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:vertex-sphere-intersection"} (vertex as
sphere-intersection event), each vertex is a sphere-intersection event
on $M_{G}$.

**Step 6 (Geometric Channel): Seven elements + disjointness.** The
seven Geometric Channel elements of the Feynman-diagram apparatus are:

1.  *Propagator*: the McGucken-Sphere wavefront between two events, with
    amplitude determined by the action accumulated along the connecting
    trajectory
    (Proposition [23.4](#prop:propagator-rides-sphere){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:propagator-rides-sphere"});

2.  *$+i\varepsilon$ prescription*: causal-retarded structure --- only
    $+x_{4}$-going trajectories contribute to the matter propagator;
    this is the Sphere-orientation selection $+ic$ from
    Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iii) (monotonicity), equivalently
    Theorem [21.1](#thm:QMT21){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT21"};

3.  *Vertex factor*: minimal-coupling junction
    (Theorem [16.1](#thm:QMT16){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT16"}) where matter and gauge $x_{4}$-trajectories
    meet, with the sphere-intersection structure of
    Proposition [23.6](#prop:vertex-sphere-intersection){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:vertex-sphere-intersection"};

4.  *Dyson expansion*: time-ordering of $x_{4}$-trajectories on $M_{G}$,
    equivalently
    Proposition [23.8](#prop:dyson-chain-of-spheres){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:dyson-chain-of-spheres"} (chain of spheres);

5.  *Wick contractions*: pairing of $x_{4}$-trajectory endpoints to form
    propagators
    (Proposition [23.4](#prop:propagator-rides-sphere){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:propagator-rides-sphere"});

6.  *Loop integral*: integration over closed $x_{4}$-trajectories (no
    external endpoints),
    Proposition [23.9](#prop:loops-closed-sphere-chains){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:loops-closed-sphere-chains"};

7.  *Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$*: McGucken--Wick rotation, the
    analytic continuation of $x_{4}= ict$ to $x_{4}= c\tau$ --- both
    forms being readings of the same underlying $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
    axis (Theorem 106 of [@Syn-2026], the Signature-Bridging Theorem,
    with $x_{4}= ict$ as integrated kinematic shadow of
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ per
    Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
    reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}).

Each diagram is a 4D $x_{4}$-trajectory configuration on $M_{G}$, with
the algebraic Feynman rules being the algebraic shadows of the geometric
structures. The two channels are derivationally disjoint: Algebraic Channel
invokes Dyson--Wick algebraic machinery on the operator product; Geometric
Channel invokes $x_{4}$-trajectory geometry on $M_{G}$ with no operator
algebra. The shared content is $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the final
Feynman amplitude. $\square$ ◻
:::

### Geometric Channel derivation (QB3 --- diagrams as 4D-$x_{4}$-trajectory configurations)

::: channelb
*Geometric Channel Derivation 23.3* (Feynman diagrams as geometric
$x_{4}$-trajectory configurations on $M_{G}$). The path integral
(Theorem [15.1](#thm:QMT15){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT15"})
is the sum over continuous paths on $M_{G}$ with action-weighted phases.
Perturbative expansion in the coupling generates a sum over
$x_{4}$-trajectory configurations: each diagram is a configuration of
particle worldlines on $M_{G}$, with vertices corresponding to coupling
events.

The seven Geometric Channel elements of the Feynman-diagram apparatus (each a
Geometric Channel reading of a standard Feynman rule):

1.  *Propagator*: the McGucken-Sphere wavefront between two events, with
    amplitude determined by the action accumulated along the connecting
    trajectory.

2.  *$+i\varepsilon$ prescription*: causal-retarded structure: only
    $+x_{4}$-going trajectories contribute to the matter propagator;
    this is the Sphere-orientation selection of $+ic$
    (Theorem [21.1](#thm:QMT21){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT21"}).

3.  *Vertex factor*: minimal-coupling junction
    (Theorem [16.1](#thm:QMT16){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT16"}) where matter and gauge $x_{4}$-trajectories
    meet.

4.  *Dyson expansion*: time-ordering of $x_{4}$-trajectories on $M_{G}$.

5.  *Wick contractions*: pairing of $x_{4}$-trajectory endpoints to form
    propagators.

6.  *Loop integral*: integration over closed $x_{4}$-trajectories (no
    external endpoints).

7.  *Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$*: McGucken--Wick rotation, the
    analytic continuation of $x_{4}= ict$ to $x_{4}= c\tau$ (Theorem 106
    of [@Syn-2026], the Signature-Bridging Theorem of \[3CH\]).

Each diagram is a 4D $x_{4}$-trajectory configuration on $M_{G}$, with
the algebraic Feynman rules being the algebraic shadows of the geometric
structures. ◻
:::

### Algebraic Channel derivation (QA1, QA7 --- Dyson-Wick-propagator algebra)

::: channela
*Algebraic Channel Derivation 23.2* (Feynman diagrams from Dyson--Wick
expansion). The Dyson expansion of the $S$-matrix (Dyson 1949) is
$$S = T\exp(-i\int dt\,\hat{H}_{\text{int}}/\hbar) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-i)^n}{n!\hbar^n}\,T(\hat{H}_{\text{int}}(t_1)\cdots\hat{H}_{\text{int}}(t_n)),$$
with $T$ time ordering and $\hat{H}_{\text{int}}$ the interaction
Hamiltonian. Wick's theorem (Wick 1950 [@Wick1950]) reduces the
time-ordered product to a sum over contractions, with each contraction
yielding a propagator $\langle T(\hat{\phi}\hat{\phi})\rangle$. Standard
Feynman rules (Peskin--Schroeder [@PeskinSchroeder1995]):

-   Propagator:
    $\langle T(\hat{\phi}(x)\hat{\phi}(y))\rangle = i\hbar/[(p^2 - m^2 + i\varepsilon)]$,
    the $+i\varepsilon$ prescription enforcing the causal-retarded
    propagator.

-   Vertex: $-ig\gamma^\mu$ for QED electron--photon, supplied by
    minimal coupling (Theorem [16.1](#thm:QMT16){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT16"}).

-   Loop integral: $\int d^4 k/(2\pi)^4$ over each loop's four-momentum,
    with appropriate regularization.

◻
:::

### The McGucken-Sphere geometric substrate of Feynman diagrams {#sec:mcgucken-sphere-substrate-feynman}

The Geometric Channel reading just established identifies Feynman diagrams as
4D-$x_{4}$-trajectory configurations on $M_{G}$. The April 23, 2026
Feynman-diagrams paper [@MG-FeynmanDiagrams-2026] sharpens this
identification by specifying the geometric substrate on which each
diagrammatic element lives. The four propositions of this section
establish that propagators ride McGucken Spheres, vertices are Sphere
intersections, the Dyson expansion is a chain of intersecting Spheres,
and loops are closed chains of intersecting Spheres. The diagrammatic
apparatus is then visible as the geometry of intersecting expanding
wavefronts on $M_{G}$.

::: {#prop:propagator-rides-sphere .proposition}
**Proposition 23.4** (Each propagator rides a McGucken Sphere;
[@MG-FeynmanDiagrams-2026] Proposition VI.1). *The Feynman propagator
$G(x - y)$ from event $y$ to event $x$ has its geometric support on and
inside the future McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{y}(t_x - t_y)$ of radius
$c(t_x - t_y)$ centred on $y$. The $+i\varepsilon$ prescription selects
the forward-$x_{4}$ branch of the Sphere's expansion.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has three steps establishing the propagator's
geometric support and the forward-direction selection by
$+i\varepsilon$.

**Step 1: Momentum-space form and real-space inverse Fourier
transform.** The Feynman propagator's momentum-space form
$1/(p^2 - m^2 + i\varepsilon)$ has the real-space inverse Fourier
transform
$$G(x - y) \;=\; \int\frac{d^4 p}{(2\pi)^4}\,\frac{i}{p^2 - m^2 + i\varepsilon}\,e^{-ip\cdot(x - y)},$$
which is supported on and inside the future light cone of $y$, with the
support precisely on the null hypersurface vanishing for $m > 0$ and
nonvanishing for $m = 0$. The null hypersurface emanating from $y$ is
the future light cone
$|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}|^2 - c^2(t_x - t_y)^2 = 0$, $t_x \ge t_y$.

**Step 2: Null hypersurface = McGucken Sphere.** By clause (F6) of
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}
(Chapter [16](#ch:gauge){reference-type="ref" reference="ch:gauge"}),
the null hypersurface emanating from $y$ intersected with the spacelike
slice $\Sigma_{t_x}$ is precisely the McGucken Sphere
$M^{+}_{y}(t_x - t_y)$ of radius $c(t_x - t_y)$ centred on $y$. The
propagator's geometric support is therefore on and inside this McGucken
Sphere. The six independent senses of geometric locality of
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"} (F1: foliation leaf; F2: metric level
set; F3: Huygens caustic; F4: Legendrian submanifold; F5: conformal
pencil member; F6: null-hypersurface cross-section) apply simultaneously
to this Sphere, so the propagator propagates between events that are
six-fold local on the same geometric object.

**Step 3: $+i\varepsilon$ selects the forward branch.** The
$+i\varepsilon$ prescription, by
Proposition [16.7](#prop:vector-coupling-from-M){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:vector-coupling-from-M"} and the discussion of
Theorem [16.1](#thm:QMT16){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT16"}
in Chapter [16](#ch:gauge){reference-type="ref" reference="ch:gauge"},
is the infinitesimal Wick rotation in the $+x_{4}$ direction inherited
from the forward direction $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= +ic$ of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}. It selects the forward-in-time branch of the
Sphere's expansion: the future light cone, not the past light cone. The
propagator's dominant contribution is therefore on the forward McGucken
Sphere $M^{+}_{y}(t_x - t_y)$ (future light cone), not on the backward
light cone of $y$ that would correspond to the opposite $-i\varepsilon$
prescription. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#cor:internal-line-sphere-shadow .corollary}
**Corollary 23.5** (Internal lines as McGucken-Sphere shadows). *Every
internal line in a Feynman diagram is a one-dimensional projection of a
four-dimensional McGucken Sphere carrying $x_{4}$-flux of a virtual
quantum from one interaction event to the next. The standard graphical
conventions (wavy for photon, straight for fermion, spring for gluon)
are graphical projections of the underlying McGucken-Sphere geometry
onto the diagram's drawing plane.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* By
Proposition [23.4](#prop:propagator-rides-sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:propagator-rides-sphere"}, the Feynman propagator from
source event $y$ to sink event $x$ has its geometric support on and
inside the future McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{y}(t_x - t_y)$, a
four-dimensional object (a 3-sphere of spatial radius $c(t_x - t_y)$ in
the spacelike slice $\Sigma_{t_x}$, parametrised by the lab time
$t_x - t_y$ between source and sink, giving a one-parameter family of
3-spheres swept out as $t_x$ varies). An internal line in a Feynman
diagram represents exactly such a propagator: it connects two
interaction events $y$ and $x$, carrying the virtual-quantum
$x_{4}$-flux of the field species labelling the line.

The diagrammatic convention represents this 4D object as a 1D line
segment in the drawing plane by projecting along the trajectory's
principal $x_{4}$-direction $y \to x$, collapsing the transverse
(spatial) Sphere structure to the line's graphical body. The shape
conventions (wavy/straight/spring) carry the field species'
McGucken-derived signature data --- wavy denoting the massless
transverse-polarisation photon Sphere of
Theorem [16.1](#thm:QMT16){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT16"},
straight denoting the massive Dirac Sphere of
Theorem [9.1](#thm:QMT9){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT9"}
(Chapter [9](#ch:dirac){reference-type="ref" reference="ch:dirac"}, via
Lemmas [9.2](#lem:clifford-existence){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:clifford-existence"}--[9.15](#lem:QMT9-channelB-proof){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QMT9-channelB-proof"}), spring denoting the non-Abelian
Yang--Mills Sphere structure --- but the underlying geometric content is
in every case the McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{y}(t_x - t_y)$ of the
propagator. The line is therefore the projection-shadow of the Sphere,
not an independent object. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#prop:vertex-sphere-intersection .proposition}
**Proposition 23.6** (Each vertex is a McGucken-Sphere intersection;
[@MG-FeynmanDiagrams-2026] Proposition VI.3). *A Feynman vertex at
spacetime point $v$, with incoming lines of types $\{A_1, \ldots, A_n\}$
and outgoing lines of types $\{B_1, \ldots, B_m\}$, is the geometric
intersection at $v$ of $n$ incoming McGucken Spheres (one for each
$A_i$, centred on the $A_i$'s source event) together with the emission
of $m$ outgoing McGucken Spheres (one for each $B_j$, centred on $v$).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has four steps establishing the vertex as a geometric
Sphere intersection rather than an abstract point of field interaction.

**Step 1: Each incoming field rides a McGucken Sphere.** By
Proposition [23.4](#prop:propagator-rides-sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:propagator-rides-sphere"}, each field $A_i$ arriving at
$v$ is the $x_{4}$-flux carried along the McGucken Sphere of its source
event $y_i$. For an internal line connecting $y_i$ to $v$, the field's
geometric carrier is the McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{y_i}(t_v - t_{y_i})$,
which contains $v$ on its boundary (the null hypersurface of $y_i$).

**Step 2: Multiple incoming fields meet at $v$ via Sphere
intersection.** For $n$ fields $A_1, \ldots, A_n$ to be simultaneously
present at $v$, the $n$ McGucken Spheres
$M^{+}_{y_1}(t_v - t_{y_1}), \ldots, M^{+}_{y_n}(t_v - t_{y_n})$ must
all contain $v$ on their respective wavefronts. The vertex $v$ is then a
common geometric intersection point of these $n$ Spheres in the
four-dimensional arena $M_{G}$. This is the geometric content of "the
fields meet at $v$".

**Step 3: Outgoing fields launch fresh Spheres from $v$.** For each
outgoing field $B_j$, the wavefront emanating from $v$ at the moment of
interaction is the McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{v}(t - t_v)$ for $t > t_v$.
Each outgoing line is therefore the future-light-cone $x_{4}$-flux
launched from the intersection event $v$. The vertex is, geometrically,
both an intersection (incoming) and an emission (outgoing) of McGucken
Spheres.

**Step 4: The vertex factor as phase-exchange marker.** The vertex
factor (the $-ie\gamma^\mu$ in QED from
Proposition [16.7](#prop:vector-coupling-from-M){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:vector-coupling-from-M"}; the $-ig f^{abc} \gamma^\mu$
in non-Abelian gauge theories; the $-i$ factor common to all) is the
algebraic shadow of the geometric $x_{4}$-phase exchange at the Sphere
intersection. The $i$ marks the perpendicularity of $x_{4}$ to the three
spatial dimensions (Theorem [9.21](#thm:twelve-i){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:twelve-i"}), and the phase-exchange records the moment at
which two separately-propagating $x_{4}$-trajectories share a common
coherent phase structure at the Sphere intersection. The vertex is
therefore not a structureless interaction point; it is a geometric
Sphere-intersection event with the vertex factor encoding the
$x_{4}$-perpendicular phase exchange. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:vertex-entanglement-swapping .remark}
*Remark 23.7* (Parallel to entanglement swapping;
[@MG-FeynmanDiagrams-2026] Remark VI.1). The
intersecting-McGucken-Spheres structure of
Proposition [23.6](#prop:vertex-sphere-intersection){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:vertex-sphere-intersection"} parallels the
entanglement-swapping protocol developed in the McGucken Nonlocality
Principle paper [@MG-NonlocalityPrinciple-2026] §5: in entanglement
swapping, three McGucken Spheres ($\Sigma_{CD}$, $\Sigma_{DE}$,
$\Sigma_{EF}$) intersect pairwise at local Bell-measurement events to
transfer the nonlocal correlation from the $CD$ and $EF$ pairs to the
far-separated $A$ and $B$ particles. In a Feynman diagram, the same
pairwise-intersection structure appears at each interaction vertex:
incoming McGucken Spheres meet at $v$, and outgoing ones are launched
from $v$, forming a chain of intersecting Spheres whose net structure is
the full graph. The entanglement-swapping protocol and the
Feynman-vertex apparatus are two physical realizations of the same
geometric pattern (chains of intersecting McGucken Spheres) descending
from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. Every interaction in QFT occurs at a
definite local spacetime vertex, just as every entanglement-swap step
occurs at a definite local Bell-measurement event; the apparent
nonlocalities of QFT (the nonlocal correlations carried by individual
propagators, the nonlocal spread of scattering amplitudes) are chains of
locally-originated McGucken-Sphere intersections, in conformity with the
First Law of Nonlocality.
:::

::: {#prop:dyson-chain-of-spheres .proposition}
**Proposition 23.8** (The Dyson expansion as a chain of intersecting
McGucken Spheres; [@MG-FeynmanDiagrams-2026] Proposition VI.5). *The
$n$th-order term in the Dyson expansion of the $S$-matrix evolution
operator is the sum over all topologically distinct chains of $n$
intersecting McGucken Spheres connecting the asymptotic incoming state's
outgoing Spheres to the asymptotic outgoing state's incoming Spheres,
with each intersection corresponding to a vertex of the interaction
Hamiltonian.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has four steps establishing the geometric content of
the Dyson expansion.

**Step 1: Dyson expansion form.** The $S$-matrix evolution operator has
the Dyson expansion
$$S(t, t_0) \;=\; T\exp\!\left(-i\int_{t_0}^t\,dt'\,H_I(t')\right) \;=\; \sum_n \frac{(-i)^n}{n!}\int dt_1\cdots dt_n\,T[H_I(t_1)\cdots H_I(t_n)]$$
where $H_I$ is the interaction Hamiltonian and $T$ denotes
time-ordering. The $n$th term contains $n$ insertions of $H_I$ at times
$t_1, \ldots, t_n$.

**Step 2: Each $H_I(t_i)$ is a vertex = Sphere intersection.** Each
$H_I(t_i)$ insertion at time $t_i$ corresponds (by
Proposition [23.6](#prop:vertex-sphere-intersection){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:vertex-sphere-intersection"}) to an interaction vertex
at some spacetime event $v_i = (t_i, \mathbf{x}_i)$, which is
geometrically a McGucken-Sphere intersection event. The integration
$\int dt_i\,d^3\mathbf{x}_i$ over the vertex's spacetime location is the
integration over the possible placements of this intersection on the
boundary hypersurface where the $x_{4}$-trajectory can have an
interaction.

**Step 3: Time-ordering as forward-$x_{4}$ ordering.** The time-ordering
$T[H_I(t_1)\cdots H_I(t_n)]$ orders the vertices by their coordinate
times, which is the same as ordering by their $x_{4}$-coordinates
$x_4 = ict$. The forward direction $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= +ic$ of
