with no appeal to the $U(1)$-bundle result of Chapter 16.

By C2 the marker $i$ makes $x_4$ the axis perpendicular to the spatial
slice, and by
Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"} the amplitude takes values in the
algebra $\mathbb{C}$ that this one perpendicular axis selects. The phase
$\arg\psi$ is therefore the angular position of the entity in its
$x_{4}$-advance: the coordinate of where it stands in the cycle that
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ drives in the plane $i$ marks.

By C4 the advance is the same at every event of $M_{G}$, with no event
privileged over any other. There is therefore no privileged event at
which to set $\arg\psi = 0$: the zero of the $x_{4}$-phase is a choice
of origin rather than a fact about the entity. A global rotation
$\psi \mapsto e^{i\alpha}\psi$ re-zeroes that origin and changes nothing
about the advance it describes, so no registration density may depend
on $\alpha$. (Chapter 16 later organises this same freedom as a
$U(1)$-bundle structure on the Sphere; the present step supplies the
invariance and does not draw on it.)

The replacement takes $\psi(B) \mapsto e^{i\alpha}\psi(B)$ and
$\psi^*(B) \mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\psi^*(B)$. Substituting into the ansatz:

-   $\psi\psi^*$ term: invariant (the phases cancel);

-   $\psi^2$ term: picks up phase $e^{2i\alpha}$;

-   $\psi^{*2}$ term: picks up phase $e^{-2i\alpha}$;

-   Linear $\psi$ term: picks up phase $e^{i\alpha}$;

-   Linear $\psi^*$ term: picks up phase $e^{-i\alpha}$;

-   Constant: invariant.

For $\rho(B)$ to be invariant under all $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, the
non-invariant terms must vanish: $c_2 = c_3 = c_4 = c_5 = 0$. Combined
with the requirement that $\rho \equiv 0$ when $\psi \equiv 0$: by C5 the
registration density on the slice is carried by the Sphere wavefront,
so where there is no wavefront amplitude there is nothing to register.
Hence $c_6 = 0$.

**Step 5: Non-negativity constraint (B2).** The remaining form is
$\rho(B) = c_1|\psi(B)|^2$ with $c_1 \in \mathbb{R}$. Non-negativity
$\rho(B) \ge 0$ for all $\psi$ requires $c_1 \ge 0$.

**Step 6: Normalization and unique result.** The scale $c_1$ is fixed by
the Sphere, with no appeal to the completed space of Theorem 9.17. By C5
with clause (ii) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, the wavefront $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ generated at
$p$ carries an $SO(3)$-invariant measure, unique up to scale by Haar
uniqueness on the compact group $SO(3)$, and normalised to total mass
$1$ by the requirement that the entity is somewhere on its own
wavefront. The registration density on the spatial slice is that measure
modulated by the $x_{4}$-overlap of Step 1, so
$\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\rho(B)\,d^3x = 1$ for a wavefront-normalised
$\psi$, which fixes $c_1 = 1$. (The same normalisation is adopted as the
convention on $\mathcal{H}= L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ in Theorem 9.17 below;
the present step supplies that
normalisation and does not draw on it.) Therefore:
$$\rho(B) = \psi^*(B)\psi(B) = |\psi(B)|^2.$$

**Step 7: McGucken anchoring of the squared form.** The squared-modulus
structure $|\psi|^2$ is the unique form compatible with the four
conditions (B1)--(B4), all of which descend from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$:

-   (B1) Reality of probabilities --- forced by physical requirement of
    real-valued frequencies, with $\rho \in \mathbb{R}$ following from
    the bilinear $\psi^*\psi$ pairing of forward and conjugate
    $x_{4}$-branches (Step 1);

-   (B2) Non-negativity --- forced by physical requirement of
    probability $\ge 0$, with $\psi^*\psi = |\psi|^2 \ge 0$ pointwise
    from the algebra of $\mathbb{C}$ selected by C2 (the modulus of a
    complex number is non-negative), so the forward--conjugate pairing
    of Step 1 is non-negative before any inner-product structure is in
    place;

-   (B3) Global-phase invariance --- from C2 and C4 directly (Step 4):
    C2 makes the phase the angular position of the $x_{4}$-advance in
    the plane the marker $i$ picks out, and C4 leaves no privileged
    event at which to zero it, so the origin of the phase is a choice.
    The marker itself is case 5 of
    Theorem [9.21](#thm:twelve-i){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:twelve-i"} ($U(1)$ phase as the gauge content of the
    perpendicularity marker); Chapter 16 organises the same freedom as
    a bundle without being used here;

-   (B4) Bilinearity in forward/conjugate components --- the duality of the McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{p}(t)$ (forward $+ic$ branch)
    with its time-reversed image $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= -ic$ (conjugate
    branch), per
    Lemma [9.12](#lem:forward-conjugate){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:forward-conjugate"} and
    Theorem [9.1](#thm:QMT9){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT9"}
    on the $\pm ic$ matter--antimatter branch structure.

The squared-modulus Born density is therefore not an external postulate
but the unique geometric overlap of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront with
its conjugate at the measurement event --- a forced consequence of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the conditions above. The
integrated kinematic shadow $x_{4}= ict$
(Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ that supports the wavefront construction; the
dynamical content forcing the squared form sits in
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ itself. $\square$ ◻
:::

#### The inner product as off-diagonal forward--conjugate overlap

::: {#thm:hilbert-inner .theorem}
**Theorem 9.15** (Inner product; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 5.3). *The
bilinear pairing
$$\langle\varphi, \psi\rangle \;:=\; \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\varphi^*(\mathbf{x}, t)\,\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)\,d^3x, \qquad \varphi, \psi \in \mathcal{V}_2,$$
where
$\mathcal{V}_2 := \{\psi \in \mathcal{V} : \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|\psi|^2\,d^3x < \infty\}$,
is the off-diagonal extension of the Born density. The three
inner-product axioms hold as theorems:*

::: description
*Conjugate symmetry:
$\langle\psi, \varphi\rangle = \langle\varphi, \psi\rangle^*$;*

*Sesquilinearity:
$\langle\varphi, a\psi_1 + b\psi_2\rangle = a\langle\varphi, \psi_1\rangle + b\langle\varphi, \psi_2\rangle$
and
$\langle a\varphi_1 + b\varphi_2, \psi\rangle = a^*\langle\varphi_1, \psi\rangle + b^*\langle\varphi_2, \psi\rangle$;*

*Positive-definiteness:
$\langle\psi, \psi\rangle = \int|\psi|^2\,d^3x \geq 0$, with equality
iff $\psi = 0$ a.e.*
:::

*All three axioms (I1)--(I3) are forced by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
alone, with no external mathematical postulate essential.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has seven steps establishing the three
inner-product axioms as theorems of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront structure
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, with $x_4 = ict$ the integrated kinematic
shadow per Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}). The forward and conjugate
$x_{4}$-advances at rates $+ic$ and $-ic$ supply the geometric overlap
that becomes the bilinear pairing; the spatial-slice integration via the
suppression map $\sigma$
(Lemma [9.1](#lem:suppression-map){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:suppression-map"}) aggregates the pointwise overlap into
the inner product.

**Step 1: Geometric content --- forward-conjugate $x_{4}$-overlap.** By
Lemma [9.12](#lem:forward-conjugate){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:forward-conjugate"}, the wavefunction $\varphi$ carries
the forward $x_{4}$-advance at rate $+ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(iii), invariance and
monotonicity of the matter branch), and its complex conjugate
$\varphi^*$ carries the conjugate $x_{4}$-advance at rate $-ic$ (the
time-reversed branch of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). At a point
$(\mathbf{x}, t)$ on the spatial slice, the pointwise product
$\varphi^*(\mathbf{x}, t)\,\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ is the geometric overlap
of $\varphi$'s conjugate wavefront with $\psi$'s forward wavefront at
that point. Integration over $\mathbb{R}^3$ aggregates these pointwise
overlaps into the total overlap on the spatial slice --- the meaning of the inner product (Reed--Simon [@ReedSimon1980] Vol. I,
§II.2, the standard $L^2$-inner-product construction supplied here with
McGucken-anchored geometric meaning).

**Step 2: Verification of (I1) --- Conjugate symmetry.** Using complex
conjugation under the integral (allowed by absolute convergence of the
integrand for $\varphi, \psi \in \mathcal{V}_2$ via Cauchy-Schwarz):
$$\begin{aligned}
\langle\psi, \varphi\rangle^* &= \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\psi^*(\mathbf{x}, t)\,\varphi(\mathbf{x}, t)\,d^3x\right)^* \\
&= \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\bigl(\psi^*(\mathbf{x}, t)\,\varphi(\mathbf{x}, t)\bigr)^*\,d^3x \\
&= \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)\,\varphi^*(\mathbf{x}, t)\,d^3x \\
&= \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\varphi^*(\mathbf{x}, t)\,\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)\,d^3x = \langle\varphi, \psi\rangle.
\end{aligned}$$ The conjugate symmetry axiom (I1) holds.

**Step 3: Verification of (I2) --- Sesquilinearity (linear in second
slot).** For $a, b \in \mathbb{C}$, by additivity of integration and
bilinearity of pointwise multiplication in $\mathbb{C}$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\langle\varphi, a\psi_1 + b\psi_2\rangle &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\varphi^*\bigl(a\psi_1 + b\psi_2\bigr)\,d^3x \\
&= a\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\varphi^*\psi_1\,d^3x + b\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\varphi^*\psi_2\,d^3x \\
&= a\langle\varphi, \psi_1\rangle + b\langle\varphi, \psi_2\rangle.
\end{aligned}$$ Linearity in the second slot is verified.

**Step 4: Verification of (I2) --- Conjugate-linearity in first slot.**
By (I1) and Step 3: $$\begin{aligned}
\langle a\varphi_1 + b\varphi_2, \psi\rangle &= \langle\psi, a\varphi_1 + b\varphi_2\rangle^* \\
&= \bigl(a\langle\psi, \varphi_1\rangle + b\langle\psi, \varphi_2\rangle\bigr)^* \\
&= a^*\langle\varphi_1, \psi\rangle + b^*\langle\varphi_2, \psi\rangle.
\end{aligned}$$ Conjugate-linearity in the first slot is verified. The
geometric reading: $\varphi^*$ carries the conjugate orientation, so
scaling $\varphi$ by $a$ scales $\varphi^*$ by $a^*$.

**Step 5: Verification of (I3) --- Positive-definiteness.** By
Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"}, the diagonal value
$\varphi^*(\mathbf{x}, t)\,\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ with $\varphi = \psi$
gives the Born density $|\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)|^2 \ge 0$ pointwise.
Integrating:
$$\langle\psi, \psi\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)|^2\,d^3x \ge 0.$$
Equality $\langle\psi, \psi\rangle = 0$ requires $\int|\psi|^2 = 0$.
Since the integrand $|\psi|^2$ is non-negative and integrable, the zero
integral forces $|\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)|^2 = 0$ almost everywhere, hence
$\psi = 0$ a.e. This is positive-definiteness modulo the null subspace
$\mathcal{N}$ --- the quotient $\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$ inherits
strict positive-definiteness.

**Step 6: McGucken anchoring of the inner product.** Every step of the
proof is forced by the McGucken Principle:

-   The forward and conjugate orientations are the $\pm ic$ orientations
    of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (clause P3 of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$:
    matter advances forward at $+ic$, antimatter advances backward at
    $-ic$);

-   The pointwise product is the algebra of $\mathbb{C}$, itself a
    theorem of the perpendicularity-marker structure of
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
    (Lemma [9.6](#lem:algebra-is-C){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:algebra-is-C"});

-   The integration over $\mathbb{R}^3$ is the principle's spatial-slice
    projection $\sigma$, summing pointwise wavefront contributions
    across the McGucken constraint locus $x_4 = ict$.

The inner product is therefore not an external mathematical structure
but the off-diagonal extension of the Born density
(Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"}), with both built from the same
forward/conjugate $x_{4}$-advance wavefront structure.

**Step 7: Conservation of $x_{4}$-flux.** The unit-norm condition
$\langle\psi, \psi\rangle = 1$ has a transparent geometric meaning: the
total $x_{4}$-flux through the spatial slice equals 1. Conservation of
probability under unitary evolution is therefore conservation of
$x_{4}$-flux through advancing spatial slices --- a consequence of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$'s uniform-rate $x_{4}$-advance
at $ic$, not an external postulate. This is the geometric content of the
Hilbert-space inner-product structure, forced by the principle alone:
all three axioms (I1)--(I3) are derived from the principle's wavefront
kinematics with no external mathematical postulate essential. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 9.16* (Conservation of $x_{4}$-flux). The unit-norm condition
$\langle\psi, \psi\rangle = 1$ has a transparent geometric meaning: the
total $x_{4}$-flux through the spatial slice equals 1. Conservation of
probability is conservation of $x_{4}$-flux.
:::

### Step 4: Completeness of the principle-derived inner-product space {#sec:hilbert-step4}

::: {#thm:hilbert-complete .theorem}
**Theorem 9.17** (Hilbert space; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 5.5). *Let
$\mathcal{V}_2$ be the square-integrable subspace with inner product
$\langle\cdot, \cdot\rangle$, and let
$\mathcal{N} := \{\psi \in \mathcal{V}_2 : \psi = 0\ \text{a.e.}\}$.
Then $\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$ is complete in the norm
$\|\psi\| = \sqrt{\langle\psi, \psi\rangle}$, and
$$\mathcal{H}\;:=\; \mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N} \;\cong\; L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x).$$
The pre-Hilbert structure on $\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$ (inner product,
norm, $\sigma$-finite measure) is forced by the McGucken Principle via
Theorems [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}--[9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}; completeness of that structure under its
principle-derived norm follows by the standard Lebesgue $L^p$
Cauchy-completeness theorem (Reed--Simon [@ReedSimon1980] Vol. I,
Theorem II.10) applied to the principle-derived inner-product space.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The space $\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$ inherits its inner
product, norm, and Cauchy structure from the McGucken-derived
forward--conjugate $x_{4}$-overlap of
Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}, which in turn is forced by
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the integrated shadow $x_{4}= ict$.
Completeness of this principle-derived space follows by applying the
standard Lebesgue $L^p$ Cauchy-completeness theorem (Reed--Simon
[@ReedSimon1980] Vol. I, Theorem II.10) to the McGucken-derived
inner-product space. The McGucken content is the *object being
completed* (the slice-projected $x_{4}$-wavefronts with their geometric
forward-conjugate overlap as inner product, all forced by
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$); the completion machinery is standard real
analysis applied to that derived object. We give the construction in
five steps, with the McGucken provenance traced at each step and the
application of Reed--Simon II.10 made explicit.

**Step 1: The pre-Hilbert structure is derived from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.** By
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, the spatial slice $\mathbb{R}^3$ at each
fixed $t$ is the spatial slice of $M_{1,3}$. By
Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}, the wavefunction space
$\mathcal{V} = \{\psi : M_{1,3} \to \mathbb{C}\,:\, \psi\ \text{smooth}\}$
takes values in $\mathbb{C}$, with the complex structure forced by the
perpendicularity-marker $i$ of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. By
Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}, the inner product
$$\langle\varphi, \psi\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \varphi^*(\mathbf{x}, t)\,\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)\,d^3x$$
on the square-integrable subspace $\mathcal{V}_2$ is the
forward-conjugate $x_{4}$-overlap on the spatial slice, with both the
integrand structure (pointwise product $\varphi^*\psi$) and the
integration domain ($\mathbb{R}^3$, the spatial slice of $M_{1,3}$)
derived from the principle. The norm
$\|\psi\| := \sqrt{\langle\psi, \psi\rangle}$ on
$\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$ is the principle-derived norm. The Cauchy
condition $\|\psi_n - \psi_m\| \to 0$ is a condition on this
principle-derived norm.

**Step 2: The McGucken-derived inner-product space coincides as a normed
space with $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$.** The set
$\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$ consists of equivalence classes (modulo null
sets) of square-integrable smooth $\mathbb{C}$-valued functions on
$\mathbb{R}^3$. The norm
$\|\psi\|^2 = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |\psi|^2 d^3x$ matches the standard
$L^2$-norm. The smoothness restriction can be relaxed without changing
the completion: by density of smooth compactly-supported functions
$C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ (Reed--Simon
[@ReedSimon1980] Vol. I, Theorem II.6), the closure of the smooth
$L^2$-subspace under the $L^2$-norm is exactly
$L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$. As normed spaces, $\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$
and $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ have the same norm and the same underlying
set (modulo the density-completion identification).

**Step 3: Apply Reed--Simon Theorem II.10 to the McGucken-derived
norm.** Reed--Simon [@ReedSimon1980] Vol. I, Theorem II.10 (the Lebesgue
$L^p$ Cauchy-completeness theorem) states: for any $\sigma$-finite
measure space $(X, \mathcal{F}, \mu)$ and any $p \in [1, \infty]$, the
space $L^p(X, \mu)$ is complete in the $L^p$-norm. Applying this theorem
to $X = \mathbb{R}^3$, $\mu = d^3x$ (Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^3$,
$\sigma$-finite), $p = 2$: the space $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ is
complete in the $L^2$-norm. By Step 2, $\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$
coincides with $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ as a normed space. Therefore
$\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$ is complete in its norm.

**Step 4: Explicit Cauchy-limit construction.** For concreteness and to
make the completion mechanism transparent, we give the explicit
construction of the Cauchy limit (the proof of Reed--Simon II.10
specialised to our setting). Let
$(\psi_n) \subset \mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$ satisfy
$\|\psi_n - \psi_m\| \to 0$. Choose a subsequence $(\psi_{n_k})$ with
$\|\psi_{n_{k+1}} - \psi_{n_k}\| < 2^{-k}$. Define
$$g_K(\mathbf{x}) \;:=\; \sum_{k=1}^K |\psi_{n_{k+1}}(\mathbf{x}, t) - \psi_{n_k}(\mathbf{x}, t)|.$$
By the Minkowski inequality for $L^2$ (valid by positive-definiteness of
the inner product from
Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"} (I3)):
$$\|g_K\| \;\leq\; \sum_{k=1}^K \|\psi_{n_{k+1}} - \psi_{n_k}\| \;<\; \sum_{k=1}^K 2^{-k} \;<\; 1.$$
The sequence $g_K$ is monotone non-decreasing pointwise; let
$g := \lim_K g_K \in [0, +\infty]$ pointwise. By the monotone
convergence theorem (Reed--Simon [@ReedSimon1980] Vol. I, Theorem I.7)
applied to $g_K^2$ (non-negative, non-decreasing, with
$\int g_K^2 = \|g_K\|^2 \leq 1$):
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} g(\mathbf{x})^2\,d^3x \;=\; \lim_K \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} g_K(\mathbf{x})^2\,d^3x \;\leq\; 1,$$
so $g \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ and in particular
$g(\mathbf{x}) < +\infty$ for almost every
$\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$. At every such $\mathbf{x}$, the partial
sums of the absolute series converge, so $(\psi_{n_k}(\mathbf{x}, t))$
is a Cauchy sequence in $\mathbb{C}$ (by completeness of $\mathbb{C}$ as
$\mathbb{R}^2$ under the Euclidean norm) and converges in $\mathbb{C}$.
Define
$$\psi_\infty(\mathbf{x}, t) := \lim_{k \to \infty} \psi_{n_k}(\mathbf{x}, t)$$
at every point of pointwise-a.e. convergence, and $\psi_\infty := 0$ on
the null exceptional set.

**Step 5: $\psi_\infty \in \mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$ and norm
convergence.** A Cauchy sequence is bounded:
$\|\psi_n\| \leq C < \infty$ for all $n$. By Fatou's lemma (Reed--Simon
[@ReedSimon1980] Vol. I, Theorem I.8) applied to $|\psi_{n_k}|^2$:
$$\|\psi_\infty\|^2 \;=\; \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |\psi_\infty|^2\,d^3x \;\leq\; \liminf_{k \to \infty} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |\psi_{n_k}|^2\,d^3x \;=\; \liminf_{k \to \infty} \|\psi_{n_k}\|^2 \;\leq\; C^2,$$
so $\psi_\infty \in \mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$. For norm convergence,
fix $\varepsilon > 0$. By the Cauchy condition, there exists $N$ with
$\|\psi_n - \psi_m\| < \varepsilon$ for all $n, m \geq N$. Apply Fatou's
lemma to $|\psi_n - \psi_{n_k}|^2$ with $n \geq N$ and $n_k \to \infty$:
$$\|\psi_n - \psi_\infty\|^2 \;\leq\; \liminf_{k \to \infty} \|\psi_n - \psi_{n_k}\|^2 \;\leq\; \varepsilon^2.$$
Hence $\|\psi_n - \psi_\infty\| \leq \varepsilon$ for $n \geq N$, so
$\psi_n \to \psi_\infty$ in norm. The space $\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$
is complete; the identification
$\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N} \cong L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ is
established.

**Provenance.** Every ingredient is traced explicitly:

-   The arena $\mathbb{R}^3$ (spatial slice) is derived from
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via
    Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-arena"};

-   The $\mathbb{C}$-valued wavefunction space $\mathcal{V}$ is derived
    from the perpendicularity marker $i$ of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via
    Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-complex"};

-   The inner product
    $\langle\varphi, \psi\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \varphi^*\psi\,d^3x$
    is derived as the forward-conjugate $x_{4}$-overlap via
    Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-inner"};

-   The Lebesgue measure $d^3x$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the completion
    machinery (Reed--Simon II.10, II.6, I.7, I.8) are standard
    real-analysis tools applied to the principle-derived inner-product
    space.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies the structured object being completed: a
pre-Hilbert space whose every feature traces to
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The Lebesgue/Reed--Simon machinery supplies
the standard completion procedure for inner-product spaces over
$\sigma$-finite measure spaces. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 9.18* (The principle's continuity supplies the smooth-flow
regularity). The McGucken Principle states $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at
every event with $c$ constant: the rate is uniformly continuous (in fact
Lipschitz with constant $c$) along every worldline. This regularity is
direct content of Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i) (invariance) together with
clause (v) (global validity), not an external assumption. It supplies
the smoothness of the $x_{4}$-flow that makes the slice projection
$\sigma_*$ of
Lemma [9.5](#lem:two-component-projection){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:two-component-projection"} well-defined as a linear
operator on real-analytic functions. The Cauchy completeness of the
principle-derived inner-product space, by contrast, is established by
applying standard Lebesgue machinery (Reed--Simon Theorem II.10) to that
inner-product space; the smooth-flow regularity is the upstream input,
the Lebesgue machinery is the standard completion procedure.
:::

::: remark
*Remark 9.19* (The object completed is geometric; the completion
machinery is standard). The Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ of standard
treatments is obtained by abstract Cauchy completion of a pre-Hilbert
space, with elements as equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences. The
pre-Hilbert space being completed is treated as an input.
The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies the explicit pre-Hilbert structure:
$\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$ is the space of slice-projected
$x_{4}$-wavefronts with inner product equal to the forward-conjugate
$x_{4}$-overlap on the spatial slice, all derived from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via
Theorems [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}--[9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}. Standard Lebesgue machinery (Reed--Simon
Theorem II.10) then completes this principle-derived space. The McGucken
contribution is the geometric content of the object being completed; the
completion procedure itself is the standard one of real analysis applied
to that geometric object. Theorem
[9.19A](#thm:null-structure-prerequisite){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:null-structure-prerequisite"} below establishes the
sharper statement: the completion *presupposes* the null structure of the McGucken Sphere at the derivation level, with no Hilbert space of QM derivable
without it.
:::

### The null-structure prerequisite: Cauchy completeness presupposes the McGucken Sphere {#sec:null-structure-prerequisite}

The standard derivation of $\mathcal{H} = L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ via
abstract Cauchy completion (Reed--Simon Theorem II.10 applied to a
pre-Hilbert space) is agnostic about what kind of object
is being completed. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies the sharpening: the pre-Hilbert space being completed is specifically the space of McGucken-Sphere wavefront superpositions, and *every step of the construction depends
on the Lorentzian null structure of the McGucken Sphere being present
as upstream input*. The completion requires the null structure as
upstream input: it must already be present in the pre-Hilbert
space being completed, and it is supplied by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
via the Sphere's identification with the future null hypersurface
(clause F6 of
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}).

#### Disambiguating "null vectors" {#sec:null-disambiguation}

The term "null vector" has two distinct meanings that must be separated
before the analysis begins:

*(i) Linear-algebra sense.* The zero vector $\mathbf{0}$, the identity
element of vector addition. Every vector space, including every Hilbert
space, must contain $\mathbf{0}$ by axiom. This is the trivial reading
and not the subject of this section.

*(ii) Lorentzian sense.* Non-zero vectors $v$ in a Lorentzian
inner-product space satisfying $\langle v, v\rangle = 0$ --- that is,
vectors on the light cone. The McGucken Sphere
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t) = \{p : ds^2(p_0, p) = 0,\, x_4(p) - x_4(p_0) = ict\}$
**is** the null surface: the locus of points at null separation from
the source event $p_0$ at parameter time $t$, by clause F6 of
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"} (the spatial cross-section of the
future null hypersurface at $\Sigma_{t}$). The Sphere is the null cone
intersected with the constant-$x_4$ hypersurface; equivalently the null
cone is the Sphere.

In what follows "null vectors" means the Lorentzian-sense reading
throughout, since this is the interesting case. The
question is: *can the physical QM Hilbert space be Cauchy
complete without the Lorentzian null structure?*

::: {#thm:null-structure-prerequisite .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19A** (Null-structure prerequisite for the McGucken Hilbert
space; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] §6.6.6). *The Geometric Channel construction
of $\mathcal{H} = L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ as the Cauchy completion of
finite McGucken-Sphere wavefront superpositions has the Lorentzian null
structure of the McGucken Sphere as a prerequisite at every
step. Specifically, each of the following six construction steps fails
categorically if the null structure is stripped:*

1.  **Primitive vectors:* the Sphere wavefronts $\psi_{p_0}$ are
    sourced on the null hypersurface $\{p : ds^2(p_0, p) = 0\}$
    (Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
    reference="def:sphere"}). No null structure $\Rightarrow$ no Sphere
    $\Rightarrow$ no primitive vectors.*

2.  **Linear combinations:* finite superpositions
    $\sum_{p_0} c_{p_0}\psi_{p_0}$ are sums of Sphere-wavefront
    contributions on null cones. No null structure $\Rightarrow$ no
    Sphere wavefronts to superpose $\Rightarrow$ linearity vacuous.*

3.  **Inner product:* the pairing
    $\langle\varphi, \psi\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\varphi^*\psi\,d^3x$
    is the pointwise overlap of two Sphere wavefronts at each
    spatial-slice point. The overlap at point $\mathbf{x}$ is the
    simultaneous presence of two null-cone wavefronts at $\mathbf{x}$.
    No null structure $\Rightarrow$ no Sphere wavefronts to overlap
    $\Rightarrow$ no inner product.*

4.  **Pre-Hilbert axioms:* each of sesquilinearity (rank-2 character
    of $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ from $(ic)^2 = -c^2$,
    Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}), conjugate symmetry (PT-symmetry of
    the Sphere through the source event,
    Lemma [9.12](#lem:forward-conjugate){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:forward-conjugate"}), and positive-definiteness
    (Born density as Sphere overlap with PT-conjugate,
    Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"}) traces to a Sphere-geometric
    theorem that depends on the null structure. Strip the null
    structure $\Rightarrow$ no Sphere $\Rightarrow$ no Lorentzian
    signature $\Rightarrow$ no rank-2 character $\Rightarrow$ no
    sesquilinearity.*

5.  **Density (Hermite basis):* the Hermite functions
    $h_n(\mathbf{x}) = H_n(\mathbf{x})\exp(-|\mathbf{x}|^2/2)$ are
    obtained from Gaussian source-event distributions on the McGucken
    Sphere; the free-evolution operator requires the Sphere mass-shell
    and Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$
    (Theorem [4.1](#thm:QMT4){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT4"}); the position operator $\hat{x}$ requires a
    spacelike slice; the momentum operator $\hat{p}$ requires a
    Lorentzian metric for its Stone-generator construction
    (Lemma [2.2](#lem:phat-generator){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:phat-generator"}). Each input depends on the null
    structure.*

6.  **Cauchy completion:* the completion produces $L^2$ from finite
    Sphere-wavefront combinations. The completion is *of* finite linear
    combinations of Sphere wavefronts. **The completion does not
    manufacture the null structure; the null structure must already be
    present in the pre-Hilbert space being completed.***

*Consequence: any Hilbert space of QM derivable as a Cauchy completion
of physically meaningful primitives has the Sphere null structure as
upstream input, supplied in the McGucken framework by
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the Sphere's identification with the
future null hypersurface (clause F6 of
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}). The completion machinery
(Reed--Simon Theorem II.10) is downstream of, not upstream of, the null
structure.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof verifies each of clauses (1)--(6) by tracing the
dependence of the corresponding step in the Geometric
Channel Hilbert-space construction.

**Clause (1) — Primitive vectors.** By
Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:sphere"}, the McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ is the
locus of points at null separation from the source event $p_0$ at
parameter time $t$. By clause F6 of
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}, this locus is the spatial
cross-section of the future null hypersurface emanating from $p_0$.
The Sphere wavefronts $\psi_{p_0}$ are sourced on this null
hypersurface; without the null structure, the locus
$\{p : ds^2(p_0, p) = 0\}$ is empty and the Sphere is undefined.

**Clause (2) — Linear combinations.** Each summand $c_{p_0}\psi_{p_0}$
in a finite superposition $\sum_{p_0} c_{p_0}\psi_{p_0}$ is a Sphere
wavefront from a specific source event $p_0$. The wavefront's support
on the null cone of $p_0$ is what makes it a wavefront at all (clause
F3 of Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}, the Huygens envelope-caustic
reading). Without null vectors, there is no Sphere on which the
wavefront can ride; the linearity-from-universality argument has no
vectors to apply to.

**Clause (3) — Inner product.** By
Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}, the inner product
$\langle\varphi, \psi\rangle = \int\varphi^*\psi\,d^3x$ is the
forward-conjugate $x_4$-overlap on the spatial slice. The integrand
$\varphi^*(\mathbf{x})\psi(\mathbf{x})$ at each spatial point
$\mathbf{x}$ is the simultaneous presence at $\mathbf{x}$ of two
Sphere wavefronts (one forward $+ic$, one conjugate $-ic$). Both are
null-cone-supported by clause (1). The overlap is a null-structure
statement: $\mathbf{x}$ is a point where the null cones of two source
events meet on the spatial slice.

**Clause (4) — Pre-Hilbert axioms.** Each axiom traces to a
Sphere-geometric theorem depending on the null structure:

-   *Sesquilinearity*
    (Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}): the rank-2 character of
    $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ comes from $(ic\,dt)^2 = -c^2\,dt^2$
    (Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-arena"} Step 3), which is the squared form
    of the McGucken Principle producing the Lorentzian signature.
    Without the null structure $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ would not be
    Lorentzian and the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing would not be the
    natural pairing on amplitudes.

-   *Conjugate symmetry*
    (Lemma [9.12](#lem:forward-conjugate){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:forward-conjugate"}): the Sphere's PT-symmetry
    through the source event is the symmetry of the null cone under
    simultaneous spatial inversion and time reversal through $p_0$.
    The forward $+ic$ and conjugate $-ic$ branches are the two
    PT-related orientations on the same null hypersurface. Strip the
    null structure $\Rightarrow$ no Sphere $\Rightarrow$ no
    PT-symmetry $\Rightarrow$ no conjugate symmetry of the inner
    product.

-   *Positive-definiteness*
    (Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"}): the integrand $|\psi|^2$ is
    positive because it is a real non-negative function of the
    Sphere's null-cone amplitude. Strip the Sphere $\Rightarrow$
    nothing to integrate.

**Clause (5) — Density (Hermite basis).** The Hermite functions $h_n$
that span a countable dense subspace of
$L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ are obtained from Gaussian source-event
distributions on the McGucken Sphere together with the free-evolution
operator generated by the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$.
Each input depends on the null structure: Gaussian source distributions
have no surface to live on without the Sphere; the free-evolution
operator requires the Sphere mass-shell; $\omega_C$ requires the
four-velocity normalization $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, a
consequence of the McGucken Principle
(Lemma [4.7](#lem:reverse-reading-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reverse-reading-equivalence"}). The position operator
$\hat{x}$ requires the spacelike slice $\Sigma_t$, which is the
constant-$x_4$ slice through the Sphere foliation; the momentum
operator $\hat{p} = -i\hbar\nabla$ requires the Lorentzian metric for
its Stone-generator construction
(Lemma [2.2](#lem:phat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:phat-generator"}).

**Clause (6) — Cauchy completion.** The metric completion of finite
Sphere-wavefront combinations under the norm
$\|\psi\| = \sqrt{\langle\psi, \psi\rangle}$ produces
$L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$. The completion takes finite Sphere
combinations as input; by clauses (1)--(5), every component of this
input depends on the null structure. The completion machinery
(Reed--Simon Theorem II.10) operates on a $\sigma$-finite measure
space and produces a complete metric space; it does not manufacture any
of the geometric input it operates on. The null structure must already
be present in the pre-Hilbert space being completed.

**Closure.** Each of clauses (1)--(6) verifies that the corresponding
construction step depends on the null structure of the
McGucken Sphere. Stripping the null structure causes the construction
to fail at clause (1) and chain of theorems through clauses (2)--(6). The
completion machinery is downstream of the null structure, not upstream
of it. ◻
:::

**Table 9.19A: Sphere null structure as prerequisite at each step of
the Geometric Channel Hilbert-space construction.**

| Construction step | What it produces | Sphere/null prerequisite | Consequence of stripping the null structure |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1) Primitive vectors | Sphere wavefronts $\psi_{p_0}$ | Sphere $M^{+}_{p_0}(t) = \{p : ds^2(p_0, p) = 0\}$ as null surface | No primitive vectors |
| (2) Linear combinations | $\sum_{p_0} c_{p_0}\psi_{p_0}$ | Sphere wavefronts to superpose; universality of McP | Linearity vacuous |
| (3) Inner product | $\langle\varphi, \psi\rangle = \int\varphi^*\psi\,d^3x$ | Sphere overlap as forward-conjugate $x_4$-meeting | No inner product |
| (4) Pre-Hilbert axioms | Sesquilinearity / conjugate symmetry / positive-definiteness | Rank-2 metric; PT-symmetry through source; Born-density Sphere overlap | No pre-Hilbert structure |
| (5) Density (Hermite basis) | Countable dense $\{h_n\} \subset L^2$ | Gaussian source distributions; Compton-frequency free evolution; spatial slice; Stone-generator momentum | No basis; no separability |
| (6) Cauchy completion | $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ | All of (1)--(5) as upstream input | No object to complete |

::: {#rmk:null-structure-architectural .remark}
*Remark 9.19B* (Architectural reading of the null-structure
prerequisite). The content of
Theorem [9.19A](#thm:null-structure-prerequisite){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:null-structure-prerequisite"} is that no derivation of
the physical QM Hilbert space can avoid the Lorentzian null structure
of the McGucken Sphere; what differs across prior derivation programs
catalogued in §[9.7](#sec:hilbert-prior){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:hilbert-prior"} (von Neumann, Mackey, Solèr, Hardy,
Chiribella--D'Ariano--Perinotti, etc.) is the depth at which the null
structure enters and whether it is input or downstream
coupling. The McGucken Geometric Channel is distinguished from all
prior programs by having the null structure as the input
--- the McGucken Sphere is the null surface generated directly from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via clause F6 of
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"} --- rather than as a downstream
feature added when the abstract Hilbert space is coupled to spacetime.
Stripping the null structure from prior axiomatizations forces them
either to fail (Cauchy completeness has no object to complete) or to
silently re-import the null structure under a different name (e.g.,
Hardy's "continuity axiom" is the operational shadow of the Sphere's
continuous null-cone expansion).
:::

### The probability-nonlocality chain of theorems: Born rule requires nonlocality requires null vectors {#sec:probability-nonlocality-chain}

Theorem [9.19A](#thm:null-structure-prerequisite){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:null-structure-prerequisite"} established that the
Cauchy completion producing $\mathcal{H} = L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3 x)$
presupposes the Lorentzian null structure of the McGucken Sphere. The
present section extends that result by establishing a sharper chain of
formal implications, each a theorem with proof:
$$\text{Born rule} \Longleftarrow \text{nonlocality} \Longleftarrow \text{null vectors} \Longleftarrow \dfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic.$$
The orthodox tradition treats the Hilbert space, the Born rule, and
quantum nonlocality (entanglement, Bell violation, no-signaling) as
three separate features requiring three separate postulates or three
separate puzzles. The chain of theorems below establishes them as three
level presentations of the same Sphere-geometric content
rooted in $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$. The Born-rule postulate, the
measurement problem, the EPR "spookiness," and the Lorentz-invariance-of-collapse
tension all dissolve simultaneously as artifacts of treating the
algebraic projection $\Pi_A$ (Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}) as the source instead of the
McGucken Sphere.

::: {#thm:hilbert-spacelike-support .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19C** (Hilbert space carries spacelike-separated support;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 6.6.7.1). *Let $M_{1,3}$ be Minkowski
spacetime generated by $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}), and let
$\Sigma_t = \{p \in M_{1,3} : x_4(p) = ict\}$ be the spatial slice
at parameter time $t$. For any wavefunction
$\psi \in L^2(\Sigma_t)$ with $\psi \not\equiv 0$ a.e., the
support
$\operatorname{supp}(\psi) = \{\mathbf{x} \in \Sigma_t : \psi(\mathbf{x}) \ne 0\}$
has positive Lebesgue measure, contains the continuum cardinality of
points, and contains uncountably many pairs of distinct spatial points
each pair being spacelike separated in $M_{1,3}$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). Suppose $\psi \in L^2(\Sigma_t)$ and $\psi \not\equiv 0$
a.e. Then
$\|\psi\|^2 = \int_{\Sigma_t} |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2 d^3 x > 0$.
The integrand $|\psi|^2 \ge 0$; the integral is positive iff the set
$\{\mathbf{x} : |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2 > 0\}$ has positive Lebesgue
measure. Hence $\operatorname{supp}(\psi)$ has positive Lebesgue
measure on $\Sigma_t \cong \mathbb{R}^3$. By standard measure
theory, every set of positive Lebesgue measure in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has
cardinality of the continuum.

For the spacelike-separation claim: by
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, $M_{1,3}$ carries the Lorentzian
metric $ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2$, generated by the
McGucken Principle via $(ict)^2 = -c^2 t^2$. The spatial slice
$\Sigma_t$ at fixed parameter time $t$ is the constraint surface
$\{x_4 = ict\}$. For any two distinct points
$\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B \in \Sigma_t$, the spacetime interval
is
$$ds^2(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B) = -c^2(t - t)^2 + |\mathbf{x}_A - \mathbf{x}_B|^2 = |\mathbf{x}_A - \mathbf{x}_B|^2 > 0$$
since $\mathbf{x}_A \ne \mathbf{x}_B$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$. By the
standard definition of spacelike separation in Lorentzian signature,
$ds^2 > 0$ means spacelike separated. Hence any two distinct points
on $\Sigma_t$ are spacelike separated in $M_{1,3}$.

Since $\operatorname{supp}(\psi)$ contains continuum-many points,
it contains continuum-many pairs of distinct points, each pair being
spacelike separated. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:trivial-state-characterization .corollary}
*Corollary 9.19C.1* (Trivial-state characterization). *The only
$\psi \in L^2(\Sigma_t)$ whose support fails to contain
spacelike-separated pairs is the trivial wavefunction
$\psi \equiv 0$. Hence every physically nontrivial quantum state
has nonlocal spatial support.*
:::

::: {#thm:inner-product-nonlocal-coupling .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19D** (Inner product carries nonlocal coupling;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 6.6.7.2). *For any wavefunctions
$\varphi, \psi \in L^2(\Sigma_t)$ whose supports are disjoint open
regions $U_A = \operatorname{supp}(\varphi)$,
$U_B = \operatorname{supp}(\psi)$ with $U_A \cap U_B = \emptyset$,
any pair of points $\mathbf{x}_A \in U_A$, $\mathbf{x}_B \in U_B$
is spacelike separated in $M_{1,3}$. For wavefunctions
$\varphi', \psi'$ with support overlapping both $U_A$ and $U_B$,
the inner product
$\langle \varphi' | \psi' \rangle = \int_{\Sigma_t} \varphi'^* \psi'\, d^3 x$
couples amplitude contributions at these
spacelike-separated regions; the Born-rule probability
$|\langle \varphi' | \psi' \rangle|^2$ depends on the relative
phases of contributions from $U_A$ and $U_B$, the operational
signature of quantum interference between spacelike-separated
amplitude support.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). By Theorem
[9.19C](#thm:hilbert-spacelike-support){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-spacelike-support"}, any two distinct points on
$\Sigma_t$ are spacelike separated. Hence for disjoint supports
$U_A, U_B \subset \Sigma_t$, every $\mathbf{x}_A \in U_A$ and
$\mathbf{x}_B \in U_B$ are spacelike separated. The inner product
integrates the pointwise pairing $\varphi'^*(\mathbf{x})\psi'(\mathbf{x})$
over $\Sigma_t$, summing contributions from every spacelike-separated
region in the support of $\varphi'$ and $\psi'$. The Born-rule
probability
$|\langle \varphi' | \psi' \rangle|^2$ depends on the relative
phases of $\varphi'$ and $\psi'$ at all points of overlap, including
points in spacelike-separated regions; varying the relative phase at
points in $U_B$ alters the value of the inner product without
altering the modulus pointwise. This is the operational content of
quantum interference between spacelike-separated amplitude support.
◻
:::

::: {#thm:nonlocality-requires-null-structure .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19E** (Quantum nonlocality requires the Lorentzian null
structure; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 6.6.7.3). *Quantum nonlocality
in its operationally meaningful sense — Bell-inequality violation
between spacelike-separated measurements — is unstateable without the Lorentzian null structure. The terms "Bell
inequality," "spacelike-separated measurements," and "violation by
quantum correlations" each presuppose the null-cone structure of
$M_{1,3}$ that distinguishes spacelike from timelike separation.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The Bell inequality
$|S(\hat{a}, \hat{a}', \hat{b}, \hat{b}')| \le 2$ is a statement
about correlations $E(\hat{a}, \hat{b}) = \langle A B \rangle$
between measurement outcomes $A, B$ obtained at *spacelike-separated*
events $E_A, E_B$. The spacelike-separation condition
$ds^2(E_A, E_B) > 0$ is meaningful only if the metric $ds^2$ admits
non-zero null vectors (the boundary between timelike and spacelike).
By Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, the metric is Lorentzian iff it
admits null vectors; the null cone is the locus
$\{p : ds^2 = 0\} \ne \emptyset$. Strip the null structure → no
distinction between timelike and spacelike → "spacelike separation"
is undefined → "Bell-inequality violation between spacelike-separated
measurements" is unstateable.

Quantum nonlocality in the operationally meaningful sense is the
empirical fact (Aspect 1982 [@Aspect1982CHSH], Hensen 2015
[@Hensen2015Loophole], Big Bell Test 2018 [@BIGBellTest2018]) that
Bell-type correlations $|S| = 2\sqrt{2}$ are observed between
spacelike-separated measurements. Without the null structure, this
empirical fact cannot even be formulated. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:born-rule-presupposes-nonlocal-coupling .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19F** (Born rule presupposes nonlocal coupling;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 6.6.7.4). *The Born rule
$P(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$, in its physical content —
pointwise probability density, normalization
$\int P\,d^3 x = 1$, interference, applicability across
spacelike-separated regions — presupposes the nonlocal
inner-product coupling of
Theorem [9.19D](#thm:inner-product-nonlocal-coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:inner-product-nonlocal-coupling"}.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The Born rule's physical content has four ingredients, each
requiring the inner-product coupling at spacelike-separated points:

*(a) Probability density.* $P(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$
is computed pointwise from $\psi$ at $\mathbf{x}$. But the meaning
of "$\psi$ at $\mathbf{x}$" requires $\psi$ to be an element of
$L^2(\Sigma_t)$, hence a function defined on the entire slice with
support of positive measure
(Theorem [9.19C](#thm:hilbert-spacelike-support){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-spacelike-support"}). The value
$\psi(\mathbf{x})$ at a single point requires the wavefunction's
extension across spacelike-separated regions to be defined.

*(b) Normalization.* $\int_{\Sigma_t} |\psi|^2 d^3 x = 1$ is a
sum over the entire spatial slice, hence couples $|\psi|^2$ at every
pair of spacelike-separated points to the global normalization
constraint.

*(c) Interference.* For superposition states $\psi = \alpha\varphi_1 + \beta\varphi_2$
with $\varphi_1, \varphi_2$ having overlapping spatial supports,
$|\psi|^2 = |\alpha|^2|\varphi_1|^2 + |\beta|^2|\varphi_2|^2 + 2\text{Re}(\alpha^* \beta \varphi_1^* \varphi_2)$.
The interference term $\varphi_1^* \varphi_2$ couples amplitudes at
every point of overlap, including points in spacelike-separated
regions.

*(d) Applicability to spacelike-separated regions.* The probability
that a measurement at $\mathbf{x}_A$ yields a specific outcome
depends on $|\psi|^2$ evaluated at $\mathbf{x}_A$, computed from
$\psi$ whose support includes points spacelike separated from
$\mathbf{x}_A$.

Each ingredient requires the inner-product coupling of values at
spacelike-separated points. Hence the Born rule, in its physical
content, presupposes the nonlocal inner-product coupling of
Theorem [9.19D](#thm:inner-product-nonlocal-coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:inner-product-nonlocal-coupling"}. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:born-rule-requires-null-vectors .corollary}
*Corollary 9.19G* (Born rule requires Lorentzian null structure;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Corollary 6.6.7.5). *Combining
Theorems [9.19C](#thm:hilbert-spacelike-support){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-spacelike-support"},
[9.19D](#thm:inner-product-nonlocal-coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:inner-product-nonlocal-coupling"},
[9.19E](#thm:nonlocality-requires-null-structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:nonlocality-requires-null-structure"}, and
[9.19F](#thm:born-rule-presupposes-nonlocal-coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-rule-presupposes-nonlocal-coupling"}, the Born
rule $P(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ in its physical
content requires the Lorentzian null structure of the underlying
spacetime. The full chain to the principle is:*
$$\text{Born rule} \Longleftarrow \text{nonlocal coupling} \Longleftarrow \text{spacelike separation} \Longleftarrow \text{Lorentzian null structure} \Longleftarrow \dfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic.$$
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). By
Theorem [9.19F](#thm:born-rule-presupposes-nonlocal-coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-rule-presupposes-nonlocal-coupling"}, Born
$\Rightarrow$ nonlocal coupling. By
Theorem [9.19D](#thm:inner-product-nonlocal-coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:inner-product-nonlocal-coupling"}, nonlocal coupling
$\Rightarrow$ spacelike separation. By
Theorem [9.19E](#thm:nonlocality-requires-null-structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:nonlocality-requires-null-structure"}, spacelike
separation $\Rightarrow$ Lorentzian null structure. By
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, the Lorentzian null structure is
generated by $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$. The full chain follows. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:four-chain-equivalence .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19H** (Four-level equivalence: Sphere → Hilbert →
Born → nonlocality; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 6.6.7.6). *The McGucken
Sphere $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ generated by $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ at each
event $p_0 \in M_{1,3}$ simultaneously generates four level
presentations of the same Sphere-geometric content:*

*(i) **Geometric level**: the null cone at $p_0$, the
spacelike-vs-timelike-vs-null distinction, the causal structure of
$M_{1,3}$.*

*(ii) **Function-space level**: the Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H} \cong L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3 x)$ via
Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"}, with Sphere wavefronts
$\psi_{p_0}$ as primitive vectors and inner product as Sphere
overlap.*

*(iii) **Probabilistic level**: the Born rule
$P(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ as Sphere overlap at the
spatial slice
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}).*

*(iv) **Correlational level**: quantum nonlocality — entanglement
structure, Bell-violating correlations, no-signaling — as
Sphere-wavefront overlap at spacelike-separated regions on
$\Sigma_t$.*

*Each of the four levels is derivable from the McGucken Sphere via
established theorems; all four levels collapse simultaneously upon
stripping the null structure (Theorem
[9.19A](#thm:null-structure-prerequisite){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:null-structure-prerequisite"}).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). Each derivation chain is established individually.

**(i) Geometric level.** By
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ generates
the Lorentzian metric $ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + dx^2$ via
$(ict)^2 = -c^2 t^2$. The light cone at $p_0$ is
$\mathcal{N}_{p_0} = \{p : ds^2(p_0, p) = 0\}$, and the McGucken
Sphere is the constant-parameter-time intersection
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t) = \mathcal{N}_{p_0}^+ \cap \{x_4 = x_4(p_0) + ict\}$
where $\mathcal{N}_{p_0}^+$ is the future light cone. The causal
structure of $M_{1,3}$ — past light cone, future light cone,
elsewhere region — is fully specified by the family of light cones at
all events, equivalently by the family of Spheres at all events and
parameter times.

**(ii) Function-space level.** By
Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"}, $\mathcal{H}$ is the Cauchy
completion of finite linear combinations of Sphere wavefronts
$\sum_{p_0} c_{p_0} \psi_{p_0}$ under the inner-product norm. The
Sphere wavefronts are the primitive vectors of the construction. The
inner product
$\langle \varphi | \psi \rangle = \int \varphi^*\psi\,d^3 x$
at parameter time $t$ is the pointwise Sphere overlap at the spatial
slice $\Sigma_t$.

**(iii) Probabilistic level.** By
Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"}, the Born density
$P(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ is the geometric overlap of
the Sphere wavefront $\psi$ with the position-eigenstate Sphere at
$\mathbf{x}$, integrated against the rank-2 metric on the Sphere
wavefront (Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}). The total probability
$\int |\psi|^2 d^3 x = 1$ is conserved under parameter-time
evolution (Theorem [7.1](#thm:QMT7){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT7"} via $x_4$-flux conservation).

**(iv) Correlational level.** Consider a two-particle entangled state
$\Psi(\mathbf{x}_1, \mathbf{x}_2, t)$ on the joint spatial slice
$\Sigma_t \times \Sigma_t$. In the Sphere geometry, $\Psi$
encodes the joint Sphere-wavefront structure of two particle
amplitudes originating from a common interaction event $p_I$ in
their common past. The single-particle Sphere wavefronts
$\psi^{(1)}(\mathbf{x}_1, t) = \psi_{p_I}^{(1)}(\mathbf{x}_1, t)$
and
$\psi^{(2)}(\mathbf{x}_2, t) = \psi_{p_I}^{(2)}(\mathbf{x}_2, t)$
share the common source $p_I$, hence are correlated at
spacelike-separated points $\mathbf{x}_1, \mathbf{x}_2 \in \Sigma_t$
via the common source. The Bell-CHSH correlations
$E(\hat{a}, \hat{b})$ between spacelike-separated measurements are
computed via the joint Born rule
$P(a, b\,|\,\hat{a}, \hat{b}) = |\langle a, b\,|\,\Psi\rangle|^2$,
which by Sphere-overlap content extends Born to multiparticle states
via the tensor product
$L^2(\Sigma_t \times \Sigma_t) \cong L^2(\Sigma_t) \otimes L^2(\Sigma_t)$.
The Tsirelson bound $|S| \le 2\sqrt{2}$ is a consequence
of the Sphere geometry constraining the joint correlation structure
within the rank-2 inner-product space.

All four levels derive from the McGucken Sphere via established
theorems. The simultaneous collapse upon stripping the null structure
is established by
Theorem [9.19A](#thm:null-structure-prerequisite){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:null-structure-prerequisite"}: stripping the Sphere
collapses primitive vectors (level ii), inner product (level ii),
Born density (level iii), and spacelike-separated overlap (level iv)
all at once. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:same-object-four-presentations .corollary}
*Corollary 9.19H.1* (Same object, four presentations;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Corollary 6.6.7.6a). *The Sphere $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$,
the Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, the Born rule $P(\mathbf{x})$,
and the entanglement / Bell-violation correlations are four level presentations of the same Sphere-geometric
content generated by $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.*
:::

::: {#cor:dissolution-of-four-postulates .corollary}
*Corollary 9.19H.2* (Dissolution of the "four separate postulates"
framework; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Corollary 6.6.7.6b). *The orthodox
tradition's framework treats (a) the Hilbert-space postulate,
(b) the Born-rule postulate, (c) the unitary-evolution postulate, and
(d) the projection (collapse) postulate as a set of axiomatic
independent postulates. The level equivalence dissolves this
multiplicity: all postulates are downstream theorems of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ via the Sphere geometry. The orthodox
postulational structure is replaced by a single principle with derived theorems.*
:::

::: {#thm:no-signaling-from-null-propagation .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19I** (No-signaling from Sphere null propagation;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 6.6.7.7). *In the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework,
Bell-violating correlations between measurements at
spacelike-separated events $E_1, E_2$ do not permit superluminal
signaling because the correlations are present in the Sphere
wavefront structure from the common source event $p_I$ onward, with
the Sphere wavefront propagating at null on the light cone
$\mathcal{N}_{p_I}^+$ from $p_I$ to both $E_1$ and $E_2$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). Let $p_I \in M_{1,3}$ be the common source / interaction
event producing an entangled two-particle state. Let
$E_1, E_2 \in M_{1,3}$ be spacelike-separated measurement events
with $p_I$ in the common past of both:
$ds^2(p_I, E_1) \le 0$, $ds^2(p_I, E_2) \le 0$, and
$ds^2(E_1, E_2) > 0$.

The entangled wavefunction $\Psi(\mathbf{x}_1, \mathbf{x}_2, t)$
at parameter time $t$ is the Sphere-wavefront joint structure
originating from $p_I$. Each constituent wavefront
$\psi_{p_I}^{(i)}(\mathbf{x}_i, t)$ propagates from $p_I$ at null
(on $\mathcal{N}_{p_I}^+$) by the relativistic Sphere-wavefront
structure of
Theorem [4.1](#thm:QMT4){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT4"} (Compton coupling, with the rest-frame Sphere
expanding at $+ic$ along the null cone). The correlations between
$\psi^{(1)}$ and $\psi^{(2)}$ are encoded in the joint structure
of $\Psi$ from $p_I$ onward, *before* any measurement at $E_1$ or
$E_2$.

When a measurement is performed at $E_1$ (Alice's measurement), the
outcome is determined by the Sphere overlap with the
position-eigenstate Sphere at
$\mathbf{x}_1 = \mathbf{x}(E_1)$ via
Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"}. The measurement at $E_2$
(Bob's measurement) is independently determined by the Sphere
overlap with the position-eigenstate Sphere at
$\mathbf{x}_2 = \mathbf{x}(E_2)$. The Bell-violating correlations
between Alice's and Bob's outcomes are **not** generated by a
faster-than-light influence between $E_1$ and $E_2$; they are
**revealed** at $E_1, E_2$, having been encoded in the joint
Sphere-wavefront structure from $p_I$ onward.

*Formal no-signaling computation.* Let Alice's measurement settings
be $\hat{a}, \hat{a}'$ with outcomes $\pm 1$, and Bob's settings
$\hat{b}, \hat{b}'$ with outcomes $\pm 1$. The marginal probability
for Alice's outcome $A = +1$ given setting $\hat{a}$ is
$P_A(A = +1\,|\,\hat{a}) = \sum_{B \in \{+1, -1\}} P(A = +1, B\,|\,\hat{a}, \hat{b})$,
which by direct computation from the joint Born rule yields a value
independent of Bob's setting $\hat{b}$:
$P_A(A = +1\,|\,\hat{a}) = P_A(A = +1\,|\,\hat{a}, \hat{b}) = P_A(A = +1\,|\,\hat{a}, \hat{b}')$.
The standard quantum no-signaling theorem follows; the McGucken Sphere
geometry makes the derivation automatic via the
common-source Sphere wavefront structure rather than via abstract
tensor-product manipulation.

Since the Sphere wavefront from $p_I$ propagates at null, no signal
exceeds light speed. Bob's measurement choice does not propagate to
Alice's location faster than the Sphere wavefront from $p_I$.
Therefore Bell-violating correlations in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework do
not permit superluminal signaling. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:epr-spookiness-dissolution .corollary}
*Corollary 9.19I.1* (Resolution of the EPR "spookiness" puzzle;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Corollary 6.6.7.7a). *The orthodox puzzle of how
spacelike-separated measurements yield Bell-violating correlations
without superluminal signaling — Einstein's "spukhafte Fernwirkung"
/ "spooky action at a distance" — dissolves: the correlations are
part of the joint Sphere-wavefront structure from the common source
event $p_I$, they propagate at null from $p_I$ to both $E_1$ and
$E_2$, and measurement at spacelike-separated events reveals them.
There is no measurement-event-to-measurement-event influence to
puzzle over; both measurement events are downstream of $p_I$ via
null Sphere propagation.*
:::

::: {#cor:cosmological-bell-correlations .corollary}
*Corollary 9.19I.2* (Cosmological-scale Bell correlations;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Corollary 6.6.7.7b). *Experimental verification
of Bell-violating correlations between events separated by
cosmological distances (Handsteiner et al. 2017
[@Handsteiner2017CosmicBell] using starlight from distant quasars as
random-setting source; Rauch et al. 2018 [@Rauch2018CosmicBell] cosmic
Bell test) is consistent with the McGucken Sphere
reading: the entangled photon pair's source event $p_I$ is in the
common past of all measurement events, and the Sphere wavefront from
$p_I$ propagates at null to all measurement locations, including
cosmologically distant ones. No tension with relativistic causality
arises.*
:::

### The Bidirectional Identity and Dual-Cloaking Theorems {#sec:bidirectional-identity-and-dual-cloaking}

The probability-nonlocality chain of theorems above established the directional
implication
$\text{Born rule} \Longleftarrow \text{nonlocality} \Longleftarrow \text{null vectors} \Longleftarrow \tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.
The present section establishes the *biconditional* strengthening of
this chain of theorems, together with the Dual-Cloaking Theorem unifying
Lorentz invariance and the no-signaling theorem as two readings of
one fact about the McGucken Principle. The bidirectional
content closes the identity: relativity and quantum
nonlocality are two readings of the same null-separated structure generated by $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.

::: {#thm:bidirectional-identity .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19J** (Bidirectional Identity;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 6.6.8.1). *The following four
biconditional claims hold on the McGucken manifold
$\mathcal{M}_G$ of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$:*

*(1) Existence of null vectors $\Leftrightarrow$ existence of the
McGucken Sphere as null-separated surface.*

*(2) Existence of the Lorentzian signature $\Leftrightarrow$
existence of null vectors.*

*(3) Frame-invariance of $c$ $\Leftrightarrow$ universality of
$|dx_4/dt| = c$ across worldlines.*

*(4) Lorentz invariance of the Minkowski line element
$\Leftrightarrow$ existence of the null cone.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Each direction is established.

*(1) Forward.* If non-zero $\xi^\mu$ with
$\xi^\mu \xi_\mu = 0$ exists, then for any event $p$, the locus
$\{q : ds^2(p, q) = 0\}$ is non-empty (it contains the
$\xi$-translate of $p$). This locus is the light cone at $p$;
intersected with the constant-parameter-time hypersurface
$\{x_4 = x_4(p) + ict\}$, it is the McGucken Sphere
$M^{+}_p(t)$. *Reverse.* If $M^{+}_p(t)$ exists as a non-trivial
surface, then $|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p|^2 = c^2(t - t_p)^2$ for
points on it, hence
$ds^2 = |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p|^2 - c^2(t - t_p)^2 = 0$ with
non-zero displacement vector — a null vector.

*(2) Forward.* A real symmetric non-degenerate bilinear form $g$ on
$\mathbb{R}^4$ admits non-zero null vectors iff $g$ has indefinite
signature $(p, q)$ with $p, q \ge 1$ (a definite form has
$g(\xi, \xi) \ne 0$ for all $\xi \ne 0$). The Lorentzian
signature $(-, +, +, +)$ is the indefinite signature distinguished by
having exactly one negative direction. *Reverse.* If $g$ is
Lorentzian, the null cone $\{g(\xi, \xi) = 0\}$ is a non-trivial
cone in $\mathbb{R}^4$, non-empty by direct computation.

*(3) Forward.* By the rest-frame collapse argument
(Lemma [4.7](#lem:reverse-reading-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reverse-reading-equivalence"}), if photons have
$|d\mathbf{x}/dt| = c$ universally on null worldlines, then in any
inertial frame the photon's speed is $c$ by Lorentz transformation
of the null worldline. *Reverse.* If $c$ is frame-invariant, the
Lorentzian metric is preserved by Lorentz transformations, and the
null cone (locus $|d\mathbf{x}/dt| = c$) is preserved as a
geometric object across all frames, hence $|dx_4/dt| = c$ holds
universally.

*(4) Forward.* The Lorentz transformations are defined as the linear
transformations preserving $ds^2$; they automatically preserve the
locus $ds^2 = 0$, the null cone. *Reverse.* If the null cone is
preserved, then by Alexandrov's theorem [@Alexandrov1950Causality],
the only causality-preserving transformations of Minkowski spacetime
that preserve the null cone are Lorentz transformations (up to
conformal scaling), hence the full Lorentzian metric is preserved.
◻
:::

::: {#rmk:bidirectional-identity-architectural .remark}
*Remark 9.19J.1* (Architectural reading of the Bidirectional
Identity). The bidirectional content closes the identity
between relativity's ingredients (Minkowski metric,
Lorentzian signature, Lorentz group, frame-invariance of $c$, light
cone) and the McGucken Sphere generated by $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.
The forward direction of the chain of theorems
(Theorems [9.19C](#thm:hilbert-spacelike-support){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-spacelike-support"}--[9.19I](#thm:no-signaling-from-null-propagation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:no-signaling-from-null-propagation"}) showed that QM
requires the null structure; the reverse direction
(Theorem 9.19J) shows that the null structure requires the McGucken
Sphere. Together they establish that relativity and quantum
nonlocality are two readings of the same null-separated structure.
:::

::: {#thm:dual-cloaking .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19K** (Dual-Cloaking: Lorentz invariance and no-signaling
as two readings of one fact;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 6.6.8.2). *Let $\Pi$ denote the McGucken
Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$. Lorentz invariance of $c$
(the relativistic content) and the quantum no-signaling theorem
(the quantum-content) are the same theorem in two
languages: both express the dual-channel reading of "no
signal-encoding can be faster than the McGucken Sphere wavefront's
expansion at $c$." The Algebraic Channel reading yields Lorentz
invariance; the Geometric Channel reading yields no-signaling. The
no-signaling theorem does **not** deny the causal connection between
entangled subsystems; it only denies the signal-extractability of
the connection. Bell-violation correlations at
$|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt{2}$ are the empirical signature of a
real causal connection through the shared McGucken Sphere of the
common source event; what is cloaked is the hijacking of the connection for controlled classical information,
not the connection itself.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We establish each cloaking and identify the common causal
root.

*(1) Relativistic cloaking.* Consider an observer on a worldline
$\gamma \subset M_{1,3}$ with measurement apparatus calibrated
against photon propagation: a clock $C$ (BIPM 1967 cesium-hyperfine
definition of the second, calibrated by photon emission/absorption
events whose frequency is determined by the McGucken-Sphere structure
of atomic energy levels) and a ruler $R$ (BIPM 1983 definition of the
metre as the distance traversed by light in
$1/299{,}792{,}458$ seconds). Both $C$ and $R$ are constructed from
photon propagation on the McGucken Sphere generated by
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$. Attempting to measure the speed of a
photon emitted by source $S$ in $\gamma$'s frame:
$v_\text{photon} = (R\text{-measured distance}) / (C\text{-measured time}) = L / (L/c) = c$
tautologically, in $\gamma$'s frame and in any other inertial frame.
The frame-invariance of $c$ is therefore not an independent postulate
but a tautological consequence of measurement being mediated by the
same dynamical process the measurement is meant to characterise.
Einstein's 1905 second postulate is a derived theorem of $\Pi$ once
measurement is taken into account.

*(2) Quantum cloaking.* Let
$|\psi\rangle = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|0\rangle_A |1\rangle_B - |1\rangle_A |0\rangle_B)$
be the singlet state of two qubits $A, B$ emitted from a common
source event $p_0$ and propagated on
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ to detectors at spatial locations
$\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B$. By
Theorem [9.19J](#thm:bidirectional-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:bidirectional-identity"} clause (1), $A$ and $B$ are
null-separated from $p_0$ and null-connected to each other through
the Sphere. Bob's marginal probability distribution
$p_B(\pm 1 | \hat{b}) = 1/2$ is independent of Alice's basis choice
(by direct computation:
$\rho_B^\text{reduced} = \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{1}_2$ regardless of
Alice's basis). Bob sees random $50/50$ outcomes regardless of
Alice's choice; no bit $s$ is encoded in Bob's marginal; no signal is
extracted. The correlation $E(\hat{a}, \hat{b}) = -\cos\theta_{ab}$
exists and is the empirical content of the Tsirelson bound, but it
manifests only when Alice's and Bob's records are brought into causal
contact (at sub-$c$ velocity) and compared.

The geometric interpretation: the nonlocal correlation is a real
feature of $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$, expressing that $A$ and $B$ are at
zero spacetime distance from each other *through the null surface*.
The correlation is encoded in the joint probabilities
$P(A_i, B_j | \hat{a}, \hat{b})$, not in the marginals. The
probabilistic marginals are the cloak: $50/50$ randomness at each
detector hides the joint correlation until the records are brought
together.

*(3) Common causal root.* Both cloakings are corollaries of the same
fact: no signal-encoding pattern can propagate faster than
$M^{+}_p(t)$ itself expands at $c$. The Algebraic Channel reading:
the photon worldline is at $|d\mathbf{x}/dt| = c$ by the
massless-lightspeed equivalence; no observer measures a speed faster
than $c$ for light, because all measurement is calibrated against
photon propagation. The Geometric Channel reading: the entanglement
correlation is a real causal connection through a shared null
structure — both subsystems lie on $M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ of their common
emission event $p_0$, null-separated from $p_0$ along separate null
legs. The direct spacelike interval
$ds^2(\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B) > 0$ between $A$ and $B$ is
*not* the channel through which the correlation propagates; the
correlation propagates through the shared null structure of the
common source. No signal-encoding degree of freedom can be carried on
the null legs (each null leg has zero proper-time parameter for
encoding); the direct spacelike interval supports no sub-$c$ causal
influence either. The empirical correlation is therefore real and
causal (through the shared Sphere), but signal-extractability
requires sub-$c$ communication of the local outcome records.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework dissolves the apparent tension between "QM is
nonlocal / causally connected" (Bell theorem, Tsirelson saturation)
and "no information travels faster than light" (no-signaling
theorem). The first statement is true and geometrically explicit:
$M^{+}_{p_0}(t)$ is a null surface, and entangled subsystems share
locality in $x_4$ by lying on the same Sphere of their common
emission event. The second statement is also true and follows from
the first: the connection is through the null surface, which has
zero proper-time parameter and therefore zero encoding bandwidth for
controlled classical information. Both statements are corollaries of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$; neither is in tension with the other. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:dual-cloaking-architectural .remark}
*Remark 9.19K.1* (Architectural reading of the Dual-Cloaking
Theorem). The Dual-Cloaking Theorem resolves the seventy-year
apparent tension between Bell-violating correlations and special
relativity by identifying both as readings of one fact:
no signal-encoding can be faster than the Sphere wavefront's
expansion at $c$. The relativistic and quantum no-superluminal-signaling
phenomena are the same fact in two languages. The tension was always
an artefact of reading the null cone passively (as a causal boundary
that nothing crosses) instead of actively (as the wavefront on which
entangled subsystems share locality in $x_4$).
:::

the same inseparability holds in relativity, because the measurement

is recognised as upstream, the relativistic measurement-inseparability
and the quantum measurement-inseparability are two readings of one

spherically-symmetric expansion of $x_4$ at $c$, all measurement is
