:::

#### The gauge-symmetry reading: relativistic gauge = quantum gauge {#sec:dual-cloaking-gauge-symmetry}

A further reading clarifies the dual cloak as a gauge
symmetry of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$. In relativity, the absolute
four-velocity component $|dx_4/d\tau|$ is the gauge degree of
freedom — unmeasurable, varying along the orbit of Lorentz boosts
that mix $t$ and $\mathbf{x}$ — while the proper-time interval
$\Delta\tau$ is the gauge-invariant degree of freedom — measurable,
preserved by all Lorentz transformations. In quantum mechanics, the
global phase of $|\psi\rangle$ is the gauge degree of freedom —
unmeasurable, varying along the orbit of $U(1)$ phase rotations —
while the relative phases (interference fringes, expectation values)
are gauge-invariant — measurable.

The Dual-Cloaking Theorem identifies the relativistic gauge and the
quantum gauge as readings of the same gauge: the rotation of the
four-velocity vector in the $(x_4, \mathbf{x})$ plane, which is a
Lorentz boost in the Algebraic Channel reading and a complex-phase
rotation $e^{i\theta}$ on the Sphere's spinor structure in the
Geometric Channel reading. The identification is through the Sphere angle $$\theta = \arcsin\!\left(\frac{v}{c}\right), \qquad \cos\theta = \frac{v_{x_4}}{c} = \frac{1}{\gamma},$$ the circular projection angle of the rate partition, related to the hyperbolic rapidity $\varphi$ by the Gudermannian $\theta = \operatorname{gd}(\varphi)$, so that $\cos\theta = \operatorname{sech}\varphi$; statements about the $1/\gamma$ factor as a projection are statements about $\theta$, and statements about components growing without bound as $v \to c$ are statements about $\varphi$,
verified through the McGucken-Invariance Lemma under the explicit
angle correspondence. The unmeasurability of the absolute $x_4$-frame
in both theories is therefore a single gauge symmetry of the
underlying $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$, expressed differently in the two
channels:

- **Algebraic Channel.** The gauge is the Lorentz boost; the cloaking
  is the tautological closure of $c$ under measurement.

- **Geometric Channel.** The gauge is the global phase; the cloaking
  is the probabilistic marginal of the entanglement correlation.

In both cases the gauge symmetry is what protects the theory from
inconsistency: in the Algebraic Channel, it prevents observers from
disagreeing about absolute rest in $x_4$ (which would generate
paradoxes); in the Geometric Channel, it prevents observers from
hijacking the real causal connection through the McGucken Sphere for
controlled-information transmission (which would allow superluminal
classical communication and produce paradoxes of a different kind).
The gauge symmetry is the same symmetry, viewed from the two
channels. *The protection is against superluminal signaling, not
against the causal connection itself, which is the empirical content
of Tsirelson saturation and is real.*

### Measurement as Sphere-overlap projection and Lorentz invariance of Born probabilities {#sec:measurement-sphere-overlap-and-lorentz-invariance}

The probability-nonlocality chain of theorems above
(§[\[sec:probability-nonlocality-chain\]](#sec:probability-nonlocality-chain){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:probability-nonlocality-chain"}) established that the
Born rule requires nonlocal coupling, that nonlocal coupling requires
spacelike separation, and that spacelike separation requires the
Lorentzian null structure. The Bidirectional Identity and Dual-Cloaking
theorems above established the biconditional and dual-channel-reading
content. Two further theorems complete the chain of theorems's picture: Theorem 9.19L identifies measurement as a Sphere-overlap
projection at the measurement event (dissolving the measurement
problem along a route distinct from the head-on Sphere-collision
mechanism of
Theorem [11.5](#thm:born-as-collision){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-as-collision"} and the physical-Wick-rotation
mechanism of
Theorem [1.44](#thm:measurement-as-physical-wick-rotation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:measurement-as-physical-wick-rotation"}); Theorem 9.19M
establishes the Lorentz invariance of Born probabilities despite the
parameter-time foliation being a presentation choice.

::: {#thm:measurement-as-sphere-overlap-projection .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19L** (Measurement as Sphere-wavefront projection onto
the position-eigenstate Sphere at the measurement event;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 6.6.7.8). *Let $E_M \in M_{1,3}$ be a
measurement event at spatial point $\mathbf{x}_M$ and parameter
time $t_M$. The measurement outcome at $E_M$ is the projection of
the Sphere wavefront $\psi(\cdot, t_M)$ at parameter time $t_M$
onto the position-eigenstate Sphere $|\mathbf{x}_M\rangle$ at
$E_M$, with the projection probability given by the Born rule as
Sphere overlap:*
$$P(\mathbf{x}_M) = |\langle \mathbf{x}_M\,|\,\psi(\cdot, t_M)\rangle|^2 = |\psi(\mathbf{x}_M, t_M)|^2.$$
*The "wavefunction collapse" of the orthodox tradition is identified
as this parameter-time-slicing projection — not a separate dynamical
process requiring its own postulate, but a consequence of
the Sphere wavefront's overlap with the position-eigenstate Sphere
at the measurement event.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The position-eigenstate $|\mathbf{x}_M\rangle$ is the
limit of Gaussian wavepackets $g_\sigma$ centered at
$\mathbf{x}_M$ as $\sigma \to 0$ (Gaussian wavepackets from
Gaussian Sphere distributions). In the Sphere geometry, this limit
corresponds to a degenerate Sphere of zero radius centered at the
event $E_M = (\mathbf{x}_M, t_M)$ on the parameter-time slice
$\Sigma_{t_M}$ — a "point Sphere" representing complete localization
at $E_M$. The point-Sphere is a limit of physical Sphere wavefronts
and inherits the null-cone content of the Sphere geometry: the
position eigenstate at $E_M$ is the event $E_M$ itself viewed at the
function-space level of the chain.

The Sphere wavefront $\psi$ at parameter time $t_M$ is a function
$\psi(\cdot, t_M) : \Sigma_{t_M} \to \mathbb{C}$, with the
complex character forced by
Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"} (perpendicularity selection on
$x_4$-perpendicularity). The inner product
$$\langle \mathbf{x}_M\,|\,\psi(\cdot, t_M)\rangle = \int_{\Sigma_{t_M}} \delta^3(\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_M)\,\psi(\mathbf{x}, t_M)\,d^3 x = \psi(\mathbf{x}_M, t_M)$$
is the pointwise evaluation of $\psi$ at $\mathbf{x}_M$ at
parameter time $t_M$ — equivalently the overlap of the Sphere
wavefront with the point-Sphere at $E_M$.

By
Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"}, the Born density at
$\mathbf{x}_M$ is $P(\mathbf{x}_M) = |\psi(\mathbf{x}_M, t_M)|^2$,
with the interpretation as Sphere overlap. The measurement outcome
at $E_M$ is therefore the projection of the Sphere wavefront onto
the position-eigenstate Sphere at the measurement event, with
probability the squared overlap.

The post-measurement state — the "collapsed" wavefunction — is the
renormalized projection
$|\psi_\text{post}\rangle = |\mathbf{x}_M\rangle$ for ideal
von Neumann measurement. The projection operator
$\hat\Pi_{\mathbf{x}_M} = |\mathbf{x}_M\rangle\langle\mathbf{x}_M|$
is the localization-to-$E_M$ projection at parameter time $t_M$,
satisfying $\hat\Pi_{\mathbf{x}_M}^2 = \hat\Pi_{\mathbf{x}_M}$
(genuine projection). This projection is **not** a separate
dynamical process requiring its own postulate; it is the
parameter-time-slicing structure of the Sphere wavefront's overlap
with the position-eigenstate Sphere at $E_M$.

The orthodox tradition's "measurement problem" — what causes the
wavefunction to collapse, and what distinguishes the collapse
dynamics from unitary Schrödinger evolution — dissolves into Sphere
geometry along the parameter-time-projection route: unitary
evolution
(Theorem [7.1](#thm:QMT7){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT7"}) governs the Sphere wavefront's propagation
between measurement events; the Born rule
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}) governs the projection at each
measurement event. Both are aspects of the same Sphere-geometric
content; no separate "collapse postulate" is required. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:measurement-problem-three-route-dissolution .corollary}
*Corollary 9.19L.1* (Three-route dissolution of the measurement
problem). The orthodox measurement problem is now dissolved along
three distinct McGucken-internal routes:

-   *Head-on Sphere-collision route* (Theorem
    [1.49](#thm:measurement-problem-dissolution){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:measurement-problem-dissolution"}, descending
    from Theorem
    [11.5](#thm:born-as-collision){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:born-as-collision"}): the head-on collision of
    the source's forward Sphere $\psi$ and the apparatus's
    conjugate Sphere $\psi^*$ at the detection event produces the
    definite outcome via four-momentum conservation, with both
    particles localized at the collision event.

-   *Physical-Wick-rotation route* (Theorem
    [1.44](#thm:measurement-as-physical-wick-rotation){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:measurement-as-physical-wick-rotation"}): the
    measurement event physically realizes the Wick rotation
    $x_4 \to -ix_4 = ct$, with the $i$ removed at both coordinate
    and amplitude levels in coincidence at the geometric meeting
    event.

-   *Parameter-time-projection route* (Theorem
    [9.19L](#thm:measurement-as-sphere-overlap-projection){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:measurement-as-sphere-overlap-projection"}): the
    Sphere wavefront $\psi(\cdot, t_M)$ on
    $\Sigma_{t_M}$ projects onto the position-eigenstate point
    Sphere $|\mathbf{x}_M\rangle$ at $E_M$, with the projection
    operator
    $\hat\Pi_{\mathbf{x}_M} = |\mathbf{x}_M\rangle\langle\mathbf{x}_M|$
    being the localization-to-$E_M$ structure at parameter time
    $t_M$.

All three routes start from $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$; all three
identify a geometric mechanism for definite-outcome production at
the measurement event without invoking a separate collapse
dynamics. The measurement event is therefore *triply* explicated by
McGucken machinery, sharpening the robustness property
of the dissolution.
:::

::: {#thm:lorentz-invariance-of-born-probabilities .theorem}
**Theorem 9.19M** (Lorentz invariance of Born probabilities despite
parameter-time foliation; [@MG-Hilbert-2026] Theorem 6.6.7.9). *The
probabilities $P(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ computed via
Sphere overlap
(Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"}) are Lorentz invariant, even
though the parameter-time foliation $\{\Sigma_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$
used in the inner-product computation is a presentation choice. The
probabilities are intrinsic to the Sphere geometry, not artefacts of
the foliation.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The McGucken Sphere
$M^{+}_E(t) = \{p : ds^2(E, p) = 0,\ x_4(p) - x_4(E) = ict\}$
is defined via the light cone of $E$ and the parameter-time
constraint. The light cone $\{p : ds^2(E, p) = 0\}$ is Lorentz
invariant: the metric $ds^2$ is preserved under Lorentz
transformations of $M_{1,3}$
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}), and the null condition $ds^2 = 0$
is preserved as a geometric locus. The constraint
$x_4(p) - x_4(E) = ict$ at parameter time $t$ corresponds to a
particular choice of parameter-time foliation, which is *not*
Lorentz invariant on its own (different inertial observers slice
spacetime differently). However, by the McGucken Principle's
universality clause
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (v)), the assignment
$p \mapsto M^{+}_p$ is translation-invariant, with the Sphere
wavefront content foliation-independent at the geometric level.

The Born density
$P(\mathbf{x}) = |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ is computed as Sphere
overlap — the integrand at point $\mathbf{x}$ on the spatial slice
is the contribution of Sphere wavefronts from source events whose
null cones pass through $\mathbf{x}$ at parameter time $t$. The
Sphere overlap is intrinsic to the Sphere geometry,
foliation-independent: a Lorentz-boosted observer using a different
parameter-time foliation $\{\tilde\Sigma_{\tilde t}\}$ computes
the same Sphere overlap at each spacetime event, since the Sphere
wavefronts are intrinsic to the events $E$, not to the foliation.

The total probability $\int_{\Sigma_t} P\,d^3 x = 1$ is conserved
under Lorentz transformations because the Sphere wavefront's $L^2$
norm is conserved
(Theorem [7.1](#thm:QMT7){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT7"} via $x_4$-flux conservation), and the $L^2$
norm is the integral of $|\psi|^2$ over any spacelike slice —
including slices generated by Lorentz-boosted observers'
parameter-time foliations.

The probability for a measurement outcome at a specific spacetime
event $E_M$ — $P(E_M) = |\psi(E_M)|^2\,d^3 x_\Sigma$, where
$d^3 x_\Sigma$ is the proper-volume element on the spatial slice
through $E_M$ — is Lorentz invariant when computed in any inertial
frame, because the Sphere overlap at $E_M$ is a frame-independent
geometric quantity. Different inertial observers compute the same
$P(E_M)$. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:lorentz-invariance-architectural .remark}
*Remark 9.19M.1* (Architectural reading: the foliation is
presentation, the Sphere is intrinsic). Theorem 9.19M dissolves the
seventy-year "Lorentz-invariance-of-collapse tension" of the orthodox
tradition. The orthodox puzzle: if wavefunction collapse occurs at a
measurement event $E_M$, and collapse is supposed to happen
"instantaneously" across the entire spatial slice $\Sigma_{t_M}$,
then different inertial observers with different simultaneity
hypersurfaces will disagree about *when* the collapse happens — does
the wavefunction's distant amplitude vanish at one observer's time
$t_M^{(1)}$ or another's $t_M^{(2)}$? The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework
dissolves this puzzle: the Sphere wavefront's overlap with the
position-eigenstate Sphere at $E_M$ is intrinsic to $E_M$ as a
geometric event, foliation-independent; different inertial observers
compute the same Born probability at $E_M$ using their own foliation,
without any observer-dependent collapse. The collapse-tension was an
artefact of treating the foliation as physical rather than as a
presentation choice on top of the foliation-independent Sphere
geometry.
:::

### The four-theorem chain as a single result {#sec:hilbert-chain}

::: {#thm:hilbert-as-theorem .theorem}
**Theorem 9.20** (The Hilbert space of quantum mechanics as a theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). *The complex separable Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H}$ of non-relativistic quantum mechanics is a theorem of the
McGucken Principle $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, derived as the composition
of Theorems [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"},
[9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"},
[9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"},
and [9.17](#thm:hilbert-complete){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complete"}, with no external mathematical
postulate essential in any step.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). We compose the four constituent theorems explicitly, exhibiting
the chain $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic \Rightarrow \mathcal{H}$.

**Step 1: Arena (Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}).** The Minkowski arena $M_{1,3}$ is
generated from the Euclidean four-manifold $M_E = \mathbb{R}^4$ with
Euclidean line element $d\ell^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2$ by
substituting $dx_4 = ic\,dt$ from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$:
$$dx_4^2 = (ic\,dt)^2 = -c^2\,dt^2 \;\Rightarrow\; ds^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2\,dt^2.$$
The Lorentzian arena $M_{1,3}$ is thus a derived geometric object of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, not a postulated input.

**Step 2: Complex amplitude algebra
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}).** The space of wavefunctions
$\mathcal{V} = \{\psi: M_{1,3} \to \mathbb{C}\}$ on $M_{1,3}$ takes
values in $\mathbb{C}$. The complex structure of the target comes from
the perpendicularity-marker $i$ of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$: the
squaring rule $i^2 = -1$ on the perpendicular $x_{4}$-axis is the source
of the algebraic structure of $\mathbb{C}$ (Theorem 42 of
[@MG-Ontic-2026], case (b) signature-change mechanism). Without the $i$
in the principle, the wavefunctions would be real-valued, and quantum
mechanics would lack interference; with it, complex wavefunctions are
forced.

**Step 3: Inner product
(Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}).** The inner product
$\langle\phi, \psi\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\phi^*\psi\,d^3x$ on
$\mathcal{V}_2 = \{\psi \in \mathcal{V} : \int|\psi|^2 < \infty\}$ is
the forward--conjugate $x_{4}$-overlap of wavefunctions on the spatial
slice (Lemma [9.12](#lem:forward-conjugate){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:forward-conjugate"}): the conjugate $\phi^*$ corresponds
to the backward $-ic$ branch of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at the slice
level, and the product $\phi^*\psi$ integrated over $\mathbb{R}^3$ gives
the overlap of forward-propagating $\psi$ and backward-propagating
$\phi$. The standard inner-product axioms (linearity, conjugate
symmetry, positive-definiteness) follow from the algebraic structure of
complex multiplication on the wavefunctions.

**Step 4: Completeness
(Theorem [9.17](#thm:hilbert-complete){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complete"}).** The space $\mathcal{V}_2$ modulo
equivalence by sets of measure zero ($\mathcal{V}_2/\mathcal{N}$) is the
Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}= L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$. The pre-Hilbert
structure (the inner-product space being completed) is McGucken-derived
by Steps 1--3: the arena $\mathbb{R}^3$, the $\mathbb{C}$-valued
amplitude space, and the forward-conjugate $x_{4}$-overlap inner product
all descend from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. Completeness of this
principle-derived inner-product space under its principle-derived norm
follows by the standard Lebesgue $L^p$ Cauchy-completeness theorem
(Reed--Simon Theorem II.10) applied to the principle-derived structure.

**Step 5: Composition.** Combining Steps 1--4:
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic \Rightarrow M_{1,3} \Rightarrow \mathcal{V} \Rightarrow (\mathcal{V}_2, \langle\cdot, \cdot\rangle) \Rightarrow \mathcal{H}$.
Steps 1--3 are forced by the principle alone; Step 4 applies standard
Lebesgue $L^p$ completion machinery to the principle-derived
inner-product space of Step 3. The composition is the standard complex
separable Hilbert space of non-relativistic quantum mechanics, derived
constructively from a single physical principle, with the inner-product
structure McGucken-derived and the Cauchy completion of that structure
carried out by standard real-analysis machinery.

**Status.** Before this chain, $\mathcal{H}$ was an axiom of
quantum mechanics, postulated at the foundation of every textbook
(Sakurai [@Sakurai2020], Shankar [@Shankar1994], Cohen-Tannoudji
[@CT2019], Griffiths [@Griffiths2018], Weinberg [@Weinberg2015]) with no
derivation from physical principles. The four-theorem chain establishes
that the Hilbert-space structure is a forced consequence of the McGucken
Principle, not an independent input. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:hilbert-feature-by-feature .remark}
*Remark 9.20A* (Feature-by-feature derivation of every Hilbert-space
property from $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$;
[@MG-Hilbert-2026] §6.0). The four-theorem chain composes
Theorems [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"},
[9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"},
[9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}, and
[9.17](#thm:hilbert-complete){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complete"} into the single result
that $\mathcal{H}$ is a theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$. The significance is sharpened by
the following feature-by-feature reading: *every* defining feature of
a Hilbert space — not just the inner product or the complex character
or the completeness in isolation — is the wavefront-level expression
of one geometric statement: $x_4$ is actively expanding at rate $c$,
perpendicular to $x_1 x_2 x_3$, with action $\hbar$ per
radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation. Each feature traces to a specific
clause of the McGucken Principle:

**(F1) Complex scalar field $\mathbb{C}$.** A Hilbert space needs
scalars. The McGucken Principle specifies *one* axis $x_4$
perpendicular to $x_1 x_2 x_3$ — exactly one. Frobenius 1877
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}) then forces $\mathbb{C}$: zero
perpendicular axes give $\mathbb{R}$, three give $\mathbb{H}$, one
gives $\mathbb{C}$. The number system is counted off the geometric
statement of one perpendicular axis. The single $i$ in
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ is the same $i$ that appears as a scalar in
every quantum amplitude.

**(F2) Complex vector-space structure.** A Hilbert space needs
linearity. The Huygens–Fresnel–Kirchhoff principle on the McGucken
Sphere (clause F3 of
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}) supplies this: every point on a
wavefront is the center of a new spherical secondary wavefront, and
total amplitudes at any later event are linear superpositions of
these secondaries. The McGucken Sphere is built to superpose, because
spherical wavefronts from independent source events overlap on the
spatial slice without interacting — they pass through each other and
their amplitudes add. Linearity is the wavefront's natural propagation
law.

**(F3) Inner product.** A Hilbert space needs a pairing
$\langle \varphi, \psi \rangle$. The geometric overlap of two
McGucken Spheres at a spatial-slice point — the simultaneous presence
of two wavefronts at the same $\mathbf{x}$ — supplies it as
$\varphi^*(\mathbf{x})\psi(\mathbf{x})$, integrated over the
slice (Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}). The pairing exists because spherical
wavefronts from different source events can be present at the same
spatial point at the same parameter time. *"Two wavefronts meeting"
has geometric content; that content is the inner product.*

**(F4) Sesquilinearity.** Forced by the rank-2 character of the
Minkowski metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$
(Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}). The metric is rank 2 because
$(ic\,dt)^2$ gives one factor of $c^2 dt^2$ in the line element —
second-degree in the time coordinate, no higher. A rank-2 tensor
admits exactly one natural bilinear pairing on vector pairs. The Born
rule's exponent 2 and the inner product's bilinearity are both
signatures of this single rank count.

**(F5) Conjugate symmetry.** Supplied by the McGucken Sphere's
PT-symmetry through the source event
(Lemma [9.12](#lem:forward-conjugate){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:forward-conjugate"}). Under PT-reflection through the
source event $p_0$, the wavefunction transforms as
$\psi \mapsto \psi^*$ — equivalently the $+ic$ branch becomes the
$-ic$ branch. Conjugate symmetry of
$\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is the wavefront-level statement
of this PT-symmetry. *The wavefront's reflection symmetry through its
source event is what complex conjugation means in QM.*

**(F6) Positive-definiteness.** Supplied by
Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"} (Born density as Sphere overlap):
$\langle \psi, \psi \rangle = \int |\psi|^2 d^3 x \ge 0$
because $|\psi|^2$ is the geometric overlap of a wavefront with its
own PT-reflected conjugate, which is non-negative by construction (a
wavefront cannot overlap with itself negatively).
Positive-definiteness is the Born density's non-negativity at the
inner-product level.

**(F7) Completeness.** A Hilbert space needs Cauchy sequences to
converge (Theorem [9.17](#thm:hilbert-complete){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complete"};
Theorem [9.19A](#thm:null-structure-prerequisite){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:null-structure-prerequisite"} establishes that this
completion presupposes the Sphere's null structure). This is the
physical limit of finer and finer Huygens superpositions: continuous
distributions of source events, continuous-spectrum wavepackets, limits
of finitely-many-source wavefronts. The space of finite McGucken-Sphere
superpositions is dense; its closure is $L^2$. Completeness is the
statement that the limit of "more source events with smaller weights"
produces a wavefront still in the McGucken-Sphere wavefront space.

**(F8) Separability.** A Hilbert space needs a countable dense
basis. The Hermite functions
$h_n(\mathbf{x}) = H_n(\mathbf{x})\exp(-|\mathbf{x}|^2/2)$ are
obtained from Gaussian source-event distributions on the McGucken
Sphere; they span a countable dense subspace of
$L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. Separability is the statement that countably
many source-distribution choices suffice to approximate any wavefront
arbitrarily well.

**(F9) Self-adjoint operators with continuous spectra.** Quantum
mechanics needs observables — Hermitian operators with real spectra.
The McGucken Principle supplies the canonical commutator
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$
(Theorem [10.1](#thm:QMT10){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT10"}, with $i$ from $x_4$-perpendicularity and
$\hbar$ from action quantization). The Wielandt–Wintner theorem then
forces $\hat{q}, \hat{p}$ to be unbounded; Stone–von Neumann
uniqueness forces their spectra to be continuous,
$\sigma(\hat{q}_i) = \sigma(\hat{p}_i) = \mathbb{R}$. Real
spectra are the algebraic shadow of the spatial slice's signature
$(+, +, +)$ — three real spatial directions. Continuous spectra are
the geometric continuity of the spatial slice and momentum space.

**(F10) Unitary time evolution.** Hilbert-space dynamics must
preserve norms. The McGucken-derived Schrödinger generator
$i\hbar\,\partial_t \psi = \hat{H}\psi$
(Theorem [7.1](#thm:QMT7){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT7"}) has Hermitian $\hat{H}$; Stone's theorem then
forces the dynamics to be a strongly continuous unitary group. Norm
preservation is $x_4$-flux conservation; unitarity is the statement
that total wavefront content on the spatial slice is preserved as
$x_4$ advances — none lost, none created.

**(F11) Dimension.** A Hilbert space has dimension equal to the
cardinality of the position-eigenstate basis. The position basis is
in canonical bijection with the spatial-slice points of $M_{1,3}$,
which has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. The Hilbert-space dimension is
therefore continuum-cardinality, equal to the perpendicular
$x_4$-radii count over all events of $M_{1,3}$.
*"Infinite-dimensional" means "as many dimensions as there are
perpendicular $x_4$-directions at all events of spacetime."*

**Joint principle-feature mapping (F1)–(F11).** The Hilbert space's
two essential features — complex linearity (F1–F2) and $L^2$-norm
conservation (F4–F7, F10) — correspond to the two clauses of the
McGucken Principle:

- *Complex linearity* $\leftrightarrow$ $c$ (the rate clause,
  supplying $i$ via perpendicularity $\to$ Frobenius $\to$
  $\mathbb{C}$ $\to$ linear superposition).

- *$L^2$-norm conservation* $\leftrightarrow$ $\hbar$ (the
  action-quantization clause, supplying the conserved phase
  $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ whose modulus squared is the conserved
  probability density).

The two features of the McGucken Principle that make it a
*two-constant* statement about one geometric flow are the two features
that make a Hilbert space a *complex $L^2$-normed* space — neither
real (no perpendicular axis) nor quaternionic (no three axes), neither
$L^1$ (no rank-2 metric) nor $L^4$ (rank-4 metric). The Hilbert space
is the unique function space compatible with one perpendicular axis
carrying action quantum $\hbar$ at rate $c$.

Every defining feature of a Hilbert space — its scalar field, its
vector-space structure, its inner product with all three pre-Hilbert
axioms, its completeness, its separability, its operator algebra, its
unitary dynamics, its dimension — is the wavefront-level expression of
one geometric statement: $x_4$ is actively expanding at rate $c$,
perpendicular to $x_1 x_2 x_3$, with action $\hbar$ per
radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation.
:::

### Diagnosis of twenty-three prior derivation programmes {#sec:hilbert-prior}

[@MG-Hilbert-2026] §6 catalogues twenty-three prior derivation programmes for
$\mathcal{H}$. Each falls short of the McGucken construction at a
identifiable point.

1.  *von Neumann (1932) and Dirac (1958)*: postulate $\mathcal{H}$.
    Opacity left as empirical adequacy.

2.  *Mackey (1963)*: lattice-theoretic axiomatisation; conjectured (did
    not prove) the isomorphism to closed subspaces of a Hilbert space.

3.  *Solèr (1995)*: proved Mackey's conjecture under additional axioms;
    leaves choice among $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{H}$ open.

4.  *Jordan--von Neumann--Wigner (1934)*: classified finite-dimensional
    formally real Jordan algebras; presents $\mathbb{C}$ as one option
    among several.

5.  *Stueckelberg (1960)*: real-quantum-mechanical equivalence via
    doubling; settled empirically against by Renou et al. 2021.

6.  *Hardy (2001)*: operational reconstruction from five axioms; derives
    $\mathcal{H}$ within an already-quantum-like operational framework.

7.  *Chiribella--D'Ariano--Perinotti (2011)*: information-theoretic
    reconstruction from six axioms; same diagnosis.

8.  *Abramsky--Coecke (2004)*: categorical characterisation as a
    dagger-compact category; classifies without deriving.

9.  *Adler (1995)*: quaternionic quantum mechanics; loses Born rule and
    requires extra structure to recover.

10. *Renou et al. (2021)*: experimental falsification of
    real-Hilbert-space quantum mechanics; negative result, not a
    derivation.

11. *Penrose (twistor programme, 2004)*: geometric reading via spinors
    and twistors; presupposes the Lorentzian structure.

12. *Birkhoff--von Neumann (1936)*: lattice of quantum logic founding
    the quantum-logic program; observed that quantum observable
    propositions form an orthomodular lattice rather than a Boolean
    algebra. Did not derive the Hilbert space; framed the
    lattice-theoretic question without identifying the upstream
    geometric content. The lattice is the algebraic shadow of the
    rank-2 sesquilinear pairing on the McGucken-derived $\mathcal{H}$
    with the metric content abstracted away — three levels downstream
    in the chain of theorems. Blind to all four features of
    $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$.

13. *Connes (1980s--present, noncommutative geometry)*: spectral-triple
    $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{H}, D)$ as foundational data; recovers
    Riemannian geometry, Standard Model, Einstein--Hilbert action from
    operator algebras on Hilbert space. Magnificent downstream results,
    but $\mathcal{H}$ is taken as primitive in the same way as in
    von Neumann. Connes is the strongest demonstration of the price
    the prior tradition paid for taking $\mathcal{H}$ as primitive:
    with Hilbert space as foundation, one can derive enormous content
    (NCG Standard Model, Yukawa structure, Higgs mechanism), but one
    cannot derive $\mathcal{H}$ itself. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework
    inverts: $\mathcal{H}$ is the *first* derived structure
    (Theorem [9.20](#thm:hilbert-as-theorem){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-as-theorem"}), and the spectral-triple
    program runs *inside* the McGucken-derived $\mathcal{H}$ rather
    than starting from it.

14. *Rovelli (1996, relational quantum mechanics)*: framed the right
    question — derive the formalism from physical postulates — and
    drew the Einsteinian analogy (replace observer-independent state
    with relational state). Proposed two informational postulates
    (finite information for compact phase space; new information can
    be acquired) as a seed for further work. Reconstruction not
    completed in 1996; influenced QBism and the subsequent operational
    reconstructions. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework completes the Einsteinian
    analogy: where Einstein replaced observer-independent time with
    observer-relative time via the physical principle of light's
    invariant velocity (rate of $x_4$-advance at $c$), the McGucken
    framework replaces observer-independent quantum state with
    observer-relative quantum state via the *same* physical principle
    ($\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$). Rovelli's relationality is the
    operational shadow of the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's geometric content;
    blind to the dynamism feature.

15. *D'Ariano (2006, 2007, GNS-construction operational
    reconstruction)*: five operational postulates (local observability,
    informational completeness, symmetric faithful state, etc.) yield
    a real Hilbert-space structure via Mackey--Kakutani / GNS
    construction; finite-dimensional case recovers Hermitian operators
    over an underlying complex Hilbert space. Cleanest
    finite-dimensional reconstruction in the operational tradition.
    Local observability is the operational shadow of $M_{1,3}$'s being
    composed of spacelike-separated events at each of which
    $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ holds; informational completeness is the
    operational shadow of the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing's
    non-degeneracy; the symmetric faithful state is the operational
    shadow of the universality of $x_4$-expansion from every event.
    Blind to the geometric content of his own operational axioms.

16. *Masanes--Müller (2011) and subsequent (2013, 2014, 2016, 2019)*:
    reconstructions of finite-dimensional QM from physical
    requirements about state-space dimension and reversible
    transformations; the 2019 Masanes--Galley--Müller result that the
    measurement postulates are operationally redundant. The
    three-dimensionality of the Bloch ball
    (Masanes--Müller--Augusiak--Pérez-García 2014) is the algebraic
    shadow of the three-dimensionality of $x_1 x_2 x_3$ perpendicular
    to $x_4$ — qubit states live in a complex two-dimensional Hilbert
    space whose projective space (modulo phase) is the 2-sphere with
    $SO(3)$ symmetry because the McGucken Sphere $M^{+}_p(t)$ has
    spherical symmetry on the spatial slice
    (Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii)). Blind to the McGucken
    Sphere as the geometric ground of the Bloch ball's
    three-dimensionality.

17. *Höhn (2017) and Höhn--Wever (2017, reconstruction from rules on
    information acquisition)*: question-and-answer framework with
    quantum theory emerging as the unique theory satisfying certain
    natural constraints. Most operational of the surveyed
    reconstructions. The McGucken diagnostic: information acquisition
    is a downstream consequence of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ — an
    "observer" is a localized worldline in $M_{1,3}$, "questions" are
    spatial-slice projections of $x_4$-advance at the observer's
    location, and "answers" are geometric incidences of forward and
    conjugate expansions on the observer's detection apparatus. The
    Höhn framework operates two levels downstream from the geometric
    principle; blind to the dynamism of $x_4$.

18. *Dakić--Brukner (2011, "Quantum Theory and Beyond")*: three-axiom
    reconstruction of finite-dimensional quantum theory (information
    content per system, continuous symmetries, pairwise interactions).
    The continuity axiom is the operational shadow of $x_4$'s
    continuous expansion at rate $c$; the information-content axiom is
    the operational shadow of the rank-2 metric's encoding
    finite-dimensional information per spatial-slice projection; the
    pairwise-interaction axiom is the operational shadow of two-body
    events on $M_{1,3}$. Mathematically clean but physically silent on
    why nature obeys these three axioms. Blind to the geometric
    content of all three axioms.

19. *Fivel (2012, five information-theoretic axioms)*: reconstruction
    with the complex Hilbert space and the Born rule from five axioms
    about probability distributions. Axiom V (a property of qubit
    measurements) singles out complex QM among $\{\mathbb{R},
    \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}\}$. In the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, this
    property is the algebraic shadow of one perpendicular axis (the
    perpendicularity selection of
    Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}). Fivel had the right output but
    the wrong route: rather than identifying perpendicular
    dimensionality as the upstream physical fact, he had to discover
    an operational consequence of perpendicularity at the level of
    qubit measurements and use it as an axiom. Blind to the
    perpendicularity-marker reading of $i$.

20. *Goyal (2008, 2010, 2022, information-geometric reconstruction)*:
    derives quantum theory from postulates about probabilistic
    measurements on classical systems combined with a complex-amplitude
    reformulation. Hilbert space, Born rule, and Schrödinger equation
    emerge from a small common axiomatic base. Comes closer to a
    unified derivation than most. The McGucken diagnostic: Goyal's
    complex amplitudes are introduced as a representational choice
    rather than as a forced consequence of physical perpendicularity.
    The complex structure is added by hand to give the right
    interference behavior, with no upstream physical justification for
    the $i$. Blind to the perpendicularity-marker reading of $i$;
    blind to action quantization as the calibration of complex
    phases.

21. *Auffèves--Grangier (2017, contextual objectivity)*: reconstruction
    from the thesis that physical properties are objective but always
    defined within a context. Born's rule and unitary transformations
    are derived; the Hilbert space follows. The "contextual
    objectivity" thesis is the operational shadow of the McGucken
    framework's geometric reading: a "context" is a worldline in
    $M_{1,3}$ at which $x_4$-advance is being projected onto a spatial
    slice; an "objective property" is the geometric incidence of
    forward and conjugate expansions at the context's spatial
    location. Saw the operational structure of contextuality but not
    its geometric ground; blind to the McGucken Sphere as the
    geometric mechanism of contextual measurement.

22. *Selby--Scandolo--Coecke (2021, diagrammatic / categorical
    reconstruction)*: reconstructs finite-dimensional quantum theory
    entirely in diagrammatic/categorical terms with a new
    symmetric-purification postulate doing the central derivational
    work. Most abstract of the surveyed programs: physical reality
    enters only through the diagrammatic structure of processes.
    Diagrammatic composition is the operational shadow of the McGucken
    chain of theorems's composition
    ($\mathcal{M}_G \to M_{1,3} \to \mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{H}
    \to$ operators $\to$ dynamics), and symmetric purification is
    the operational shadow of the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing's
    symmetry under $(\psi, \psi^*) \leftrightarrow (\psi^*, \psi)$.
    Blind to all four features of
    $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ by methodological choice.

23. *Barandes (2023, 2025, indivisible stochastic-quantum
    correspondence)*: establishes an exact correspondence between a
    class of non-Markovian "indivisible" stochastic processes on
    configuration space and the standard Hilbert-space formulation of
    quantum mechanics. The wavefunction is demoted "from a primary
    ontological ingredient to a secondary mathematical tool." Diagnoses
    four of the five problems with the Dirac--von Neumann formalism
    correctly. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework solves the same problems by
    going upstream rather than reformulating downstream: Barandes's
    indivisibility is the projection-residual of a 4D Markovian
    dynamics (the McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ is
    first-order in proper time $t$ and Markovian on the 4D constraint
    surface $M_{1,3}$; projection onto a 3D spatial slice integrates
    out the perpendicular $x_4$-direction and produces apparent
    non-Markovianity). Barandes correctly rejects 3D Markovianity but
    does not consider that Markovianity could hold *on the right
    manifold* ($M_{1,3}$). Blind to perpendicularity as the physical
    source of $i$ in the unistochastic-quantum correspondence.

The McGucken Principle operates upstream of all twenty-three: the Lorentzian
arena (Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}), the complex amplitude space
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}), the inner product
(Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}), and the completeness of the resulting
space (Theorem [9.17](#thm:hilbert-complete){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complete"}) are all theorems of the single
physical principle.

### The four twentieth-century commitments that blocked prior derivations

[@MG-Hilbert-2026] §7 identifies four commitments shared across the
prior programmes:

1.  *The block-universe reading of Minkowski spacetime.* Reading
    $x_{4}= ict$ as a static coordinate identification rather than the
    integral of a physical motion $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

2.  *The formalist reading of $i$.* Treating the imaginary unit as a
    calculational device rather than the principle's perpendicularity
    marker.

3.  *The separation of quantum mechanics from relativity.* Treating
    $\mathcal{H}$ and $M_{1,3}$ as independent postulates rather than as
    joint consequences of a single principle.

4.  *The inviolability of $\mathcal{H}$ as an axiom.* Reading
    $\mathcal{H}$ as the starting point rather than the destination.

The McGucken framework rejects all four commitments. The principle
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is dynamical (not block-universe); $i$ is the
perpendicularity marker (not formalist); $\mathcal{H}$ and $M_{1,3}$ are
joint consequences of a single principle (not separate axioms); and
$\mathcal{H}$ is a theorem (not an axiom).

### The universal $i$ across twelve canonical insertions {#sec:twelve-i}

The four-theorem chain establishes that the complex amplitude algebra
$\mathbb{C}$ enters quantum mechanics via the perpendicularity marker of
$x_{4}$ in $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. A natural question is whether the
imaginary unit appearing in the various other contexts of quantum
theory --- canonical quantization, Schrödinger evolution, the path
integral, the Wick rotation, the Feynman propagator's $+i\varepsilon$
prescription, and so on --- is the same $i$ or twelve different $i$'s
that happen to share the algebraic property $i^2 = -1$. The May 8 ontic
paper [@MG-Ontic-2026] establishes the unification:

::: {#thm:twelve-i .theorem}
**Theorem 9.21** (Twelve canonical $i$-insertions unified; Theorem 42 of
[@MG-Ontic-2026]). *The twelve canonical insertions of $i$ in
non-relativistic and relativistic quantum mechanics are images, through
the suppression map $\sigma$
(Lemma [9.1](#lem:suppression-map){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:suppression-map"}), of the single generator $i$ of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. They are classified by exactly three
mechanisms:*

-   *$\sigma$-chain-rule factor: the identity
    $\partial/\partial t = ic\,\partial/\partial x_{4}$ transports $i$
    from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ into time derivatives on the spatial
    slice.*

-   *$\sigma$-signature-change factor: the signature change from
    Euclidean $M$ to Lorentzian $M_{1,3}$ across the constraint surface
    introduces $i$ via $i^2 = -1$ on the timelike direction.*

-   *$\sigma$-image of integration-contour structure:
    contour-deformation prescriptions in spectral and stationary-phase
    analysis inherit $i$ from the orientation of the $+ic$ versus $-ic$
    branches of the principle.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof proceeds in three steps: (1) define the suppression
map $\sigma$ and its action on the principle's $i$; (2) classify the
twelve insertions of $i$ across non-relativistic and relativistic QM
into the three mechanisms (a), (b), (c); (3) verify each case
explicitly.

**Step 1: The suppression map $\sigma$ as the conduit.** By
Lemma [9.1](#lem:suppression-map){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:suppression-map"}, the suppression map $\sigma$ projects
the four-coordinate Euclidean line element
$d\ell^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2$ onto the three-spatial
slice by substituting $dx_4 = ic\,dt$, giving the Lorentzian Minkowski
metric $ds^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2\,dt^2$ via the algebraic
identity $(ic\,dt)^2 = -c^2\,dt^2$. The single generator $i$ of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the perpendicularity marker of $x_{4}$
relative to the three spatial dimensions. Every appearance of $i$ in
derived structures of QM traces back to this single perpendicularity
marker through one of three suppression-map mechanisms.

**Step 2: Three-mechanism classification.** The three mechanisms (a),
(b), (c) exhaust the pathways by which $\sigma$ can transport
$i$ from the principle into a derived QM quantity:

*Mechanism (a) chain-rule factor.* The chain-rule identity
$\partial/\partial t = ic\,\partial/\partial x_{4}$ on the constraint
surface $x_{4}= ict$ transports $i$ from the principle's coefficient
into any expression containing $\partial/\partial t$. This is the most
common pathway: it occurs whenever the spatial-slice formulation
involves a time-derivative, since the time-derivative is the $ic$-weighted $x_{4}$-derivative pulled back through $\sigma$.

*Mechanism (b) signature-change factor.* The signature flip from
Euclidean to Lorentzian across the constraint surface introduces $i$ via
the relation $i^2 = -1$ acting on the timelike direction. This is the
pathway for $i$'s that appear in Lorentz-covariant expressions where the
$\eta_{00}$-component contributes opposite-signed.

*Mechanism (c) contour-integration factor.* Spectral analysis (Cauchy
contour deformations), stationary-phase asymptotics (Fresnel-integral
square roots), and convergence prescriptions ($+i\varepsilon$
pole-shifts) inherit $i$ from the orientation of the principle's
$\pm ic$ branches. The forward $+ic$ branch corresponds to retarded
propagation; the backward $-ic$ branch to advanced propagation; the
$i\varepsilon$ prescription selects one branch.

**Step 3: Case-by-case verification.** We catalogue and classify the
twelve insertions;
the table below gives the explicit mechanism for each.

*Insertions 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12 (mechanism (a)):* The canonical
momentum operator $\hat{p}= -i\hbar\,\partial_x$ inherits its $i$ from
the chain-rule identity
$\partial/\partial t = ic\,\partial/\partial x_{4}$ pulled back to the
spatial slice (Lemma [2.2](#lem:phat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:phat-generator"}). The Schrödinger equation
$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$ inherits its $i$ from the same
time-derivative pull-back
(Lemma [3.3](#lem:Hhat-generator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:Hhat-generator"}). The canonical commutator
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ inherits its $i$ from $\hat{p}$'s
definition. The path-integral phase $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ inherits its $i$
from the rest-mass-phase chain-rule application
(Lemma [7.8](#lem:compton-phase-wavelet){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:compton-phase-wavelet"}). The Wick substitution
$t \to -i\tau$ inherits its $i$ from the principle's coordinate identity
$x_{4}= ict$ rewritten as $\tau = -ix_4/c$. The $U(1)$ gauge phase
$e^{i\theta}$ inherits its $i$ from the internal-fibre projection of the
spatial-slice chain rule. The spinor $4\pi$-periodicity factor
$e^{i\theta/2}$ inherits its $i$ from the double-cover structure of
$SL(2,\mathbb{C}) \to SO^+(1,3)$, where the cover's defining $i$ traces
to the metric's $i$. The KMS (Kubo--Martin--Schwinger) thermal-state
factor $e^{-\beta\hat{H}}$ with $\beta = it/\hbar$ is the chain-rule +
Wick-substitution composite.

*Insertion 4 (mechanism (b)):* The Dirac equation
$(i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu - mc/\hbar)\psi = 0$ inherits its $i$ from the
Clifford algebra $\{\gamma^\mu, \gamma^\nu\} = 2\eta^{\mu\nu}\mathbf{1}$
of the Minkowski metric, where the metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$ involves
$\eta_{00} = -1$ --- the signature-change factor. The $i$ in the Dirac
operator is the signature-change image of the principle's $i$.

*Insertions 6, 8 (mechanism (c)):* The Feynman propagator's
$+i\varepsilon$ prescription selects the retarded ($+ic$) branch from
the principle's $\pm ic$ orientation degree of freedom. The Fresnel
integral $\int e^{i\alpha y^2}dy = \sqrt{i\pi/\alpha}$ has its $i$ from
the contour-deformation of the stationary-phase asymptotic; this $i$ is
the contour-image of the principle's perpendicularity marker.

*Insertion 9 (mechanism (a)+(b) composite):* The Minkowski--Euclidean
bridge $iS_M = -S_E$ (the Wick-rotated action identity) inherits its $i$
from both the chain-rule pull-back ($iS_M$) and the signature-change
factor ($-S_E$); the equality is the algebraic statement that these two
mechanisms produce consistent results on the action functional.

The twelve cases exhaust the catalogue (verified by enumeration in
[@MG-Ontic-2026] §10). Each case is an image, through one of the three
suppression-map mechanisms, of the single $i$ in
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. There is no thirteenth canonical insertion of
$i$ in non-relativistic or relativistic quantum mechanics that fails to
be classified. ◻
:::

The import: the appearance of $i$ in twelve apparently
independent places throughout quantum theory is a single geometric fact
projected through three distinct mechanisms. Every $i$ in
non-relativistic and relativistic quantum mechanics traces to the
perpendicularity marker of the fourth dimension's expansion in
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

### The chain of theorems and the architectural inversion of Dirac--von Neumann {#sec:cogenerative-chain}

::: flushright
*"The Hilbert space and the Born rule are not parent and child but
siblings derived together from a common parent --- the rank-2 sesquilinear
pairing on complex amplitudes over $M_{1,3}$ --- which is itself
derived together from $M_{1,3}$, itself derived together from $\mathcal{M}_G$,
itself derived together from $dx_4/dt = ic$."\
--- from the joint derivation paper [@MG-Cogeneration-2026], the closing
statement*
:::

The four-theorem chain of
§§[9.3](#sec:hilbert-step1){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:hilbert-step1"}--[9.6](#sec:hilbert-step4){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:hilbert-step4"} derives the Hilbert space of quantum
mechanics from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ through the chain of theorems
$\mathcal{M}_G \to M_{1,3} \to \mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{H}$. This
section establishes the deeper architectural reading of that chain of theorems
[@MG-Cogeneration-2026]: the chain of theorems is a *chain of theorems* in which (i) the principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is pointwise constitutive at every event of
every derived structure rather than merely upstream ancestry, (ii)
sibling structures at the same level of the chain of theorems (the Hilbert space
and the Born rule, the canonical commutator and the uncertainty
principle) are derived together from a common parent rather than being
parent and child, and (iii) the principle is mutually recoverable from
every derived structure as the common waypoint of the joint derivation
architecture. The architectural inversion: the Dirac--von Neumann axioms
of standard quantum mechanics [@vonNeumann1932], treated since 1932 as
the postulates of the theory, are themselves chain of theorems
outputs, appearing as *corollaries* of upstream theorems in the chain of theorems
rather than as theorems on equal footing with the chain of theorems results.

#### The four-level chain of theorems {#ssec:four-level-chain}

::: {#def:cogenerative-chain .definition}
**Definition 9.22** (Chain of theorems). The *chain of theorems*
is the four-level architectural chain
$$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic \;\longrightarrow\; \mathcal{M}_G \;\longrightarrow\; M_{1,3} \;\longrightarrow\; \mathcal{V} \;\longrightarrow\; \mathcal{H},$$
in which each arrow denotes *joint derivation* rather than ordinary
derivation: the downstream level is forced by the upstream level (as in
derivation), and additionally (a) the upstream principle is locally
instantiated at every point of the downstream structure, (b) the
downstream structure is mutually recoverable from the upstream structure
through the principle as common waypoint, and (c) sibling downstream
structures at the same level are derived together from a common parent at
the next-upstream level rather than being parent-and-child. The four
levels of the chain of theorems are: *Level 0*: the physical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. *Level 1*: the moving four-manifold
$\mathcal{M}_G$ on which $x_4$ expands at the velocity of light from
every event. *Level 2*: the Lorentzian arena $M_{1,3}$ with metric
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ generated by squaring $dx_4 = ic\,dt$ into the
four-dimensional Euclidean line element
(§[9.3](#sec:hilbert-step1){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:hilbert-step1"}, Lemma Lemma 2.5 of
[@MG-Cogeneration-2026]). *Level 3*: the complex amplitude space
$\mathcal{V}$ of slice-projected wavefunctions
$\psi: M_{1,3} \to \mathbb{C}$, with the algebra $\mathbb{C}$ forced by
the perpendicularity selection given a single perpendicular axis
(§[9.4](#sec:hilbert-step2){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:hilbert-step2"},
Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}). *Level 4*: the complex separable
Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}\cong L^2(M_{1,3}, d\mu_M)$ with the inner
product induced as the forward--conjugate $x_4$-overlap on a spatial
slice (§§[9.5](#sec:hilbert-step3){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:hilbert-step3"}--[9.6](#sec:hilbert-step4){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:hilbert-step4"},
Theorems [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}--[9.17](#thm:hilbert-complete){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complete"}).

*Notation at Level 4.* Two renderings of Level 4 appear in this book and
denote the same object at two stages of the same construction. The
four-dimensional rendering $\mathcal{H}\cong L^2(M_{1,3}, d\mu_M)$ ---
equivalently $L^2(M_{1,3}, \eta_{\mu\nu})$ --- is the $L^2$ space of the
Lorentzian arena itself, and is the form used wherever the discussion is
covariant. The spatial-slice rendering
$\mathcal{H}\cong L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ of the boxed chain and of
Theorem [9.17](#thm:hilbert-complete){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complete"} is that same space restricted to the
slice at fixed parameter time $t$ with measure $d^3x$, and is the form
used wherever the discussion is the Schrödinger picture. The two are
reconciled at
Theorem [9.31](#thm:hilbert-minkowski-one-object){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-minkowski-one-object"} Step 1: applying the $L^2$
construction to $(M_{1,3}, \eta_{\mu\nu})$ supplies the four-dimensional
space, and restricting to the spatial slice yields exactly the space
constructed in Theorem 9.17. No third object is intended.
:::

::: {#rmk:cogeneration-vs-derivation .remark}
*Remark 9.23* (Joint derivation versus ordinary derivation). Ordinary
derivation produces a downstream structure from an upstream foundation
in a one-way fashion: the upstream is presupposed; the downstream is
constructed; the upstream is then forgotten in the formal handling of
the downstream. Joint derivation is stronger: the upstream is not forgotten
because it is pointwise instantiated at every event of the downstream.
The Lorentzian arena $M_{1,3}$, viewed as jointly derived, is the locus on which $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event, and
the metric content of $M_{1,3}$ (the signature $(-,+,+,+)$) is the local
algebraic content of the principle at each event. The complex amplitude
space $\mathcal{V}$, viewed as jointly derived, is the projection of $x_4$-advance from every source event onto the
spatial slice, with the complex structure of $\mathbb{C}$ being the
local algebraic content of the perpendicularity of $x_4$ at each event.
The Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, viewed as jointly derived, is the global integration of the forward--conjugate $x_4$-overlap on
a spatial slice, with the principle pointwise instantiated at every
event in the integration domain.
:::

#### Joint derivation in the strict sense: the principle pointwise instantiated {#ssec:cogeneration-strict}

::: {#thm:pointwise-constitutivity .theorem}
**Theorem 9.24** (Pointwise constitutivity of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
at every event of every level of the chain). *The McGucken Principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is pointwise constitutive at every event of
every level of the chain of theorems of
Definition [9.22](#def:cogenerative-chain){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:cogenerative-chain"}: at every event
$p \in \mathcal{M}_G$, at every event $p \in M_{1,3}$, at every
wavefunction $\psi \in \mathcal{V}$ evaluated at every event
$p \in M_{1,3}$, and at every Hilbert-space element
$\lvert \psi \rangle \in \mathcal{H}$ in its spatial-slice cross-section
at every event, the principle is the algebraic content of the local
structure. The four levels of the chain of theorems are therefore not four
separate structures connected by upstream arrows but four readings of
one principle at four levels of organisation, with the principle being
the constitutive content at each level.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). We verify the pointwise constitutivity at each of the four
levels.

**Level 1 ($\mathcal{M}_G$).** The moving four-manifold $\mathcal{M}_G$
is defined as the locus on which $x_4$ expands at the velocity of light
from every event by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The principle is therefore
the defining property of the manifold: $p \in \mathcal{M}_G$ if and only
if $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at $p$. Pointwise constitutivity is by
construction.

**Level 2 ($M_{1,3}$).** The Lorentzian arena $M_{1,3}$ has metric
$\eta_{\mu\nu}$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ generated from
$dx_4 = ic\,dt$ by squaring:
$ds^2 = (dx_1)^2 + (dx_2)^2 + (dx_3)^2 + (dx_4)^2 = (dx_1)^2 + (dx_2)^2 + (dx_3)^2 + (ic\,dt)^2 = (dx_1)^2 + (dx_2)^2 + (dx_3)^2 - c^2(dt)^2$
(Lemma Lemma 2.5 of [@MG-Cogeneration-2026]). At every event
$p \in M_{1,3}$, the local metric content $\eta_{\mu\nu}|_p$ is the
algebraic shadow of $dx_4 = ic\,dt$ at $p$: the time-like sign comes
from squaring $(ic)^2 = -c^2$, and this squaring is the local content of
the principle at $p$. Pointwise constitutivity follows.

**Level 3 ($\mathcal{V}$).** The complex amplitude
$\psi(p) \in \mathbb{C}$ at event $p \in M_{1,3}$ is the slice
projection of $x_4$-advance at $p$ onto the spatial three ( of
§[9.4](#sec:hilbert-step2){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:hilbert-step2"}). The two real components of $\psi(p)$
(real part $a$ and imaginary part $b$) are the spatial-parallel and
spatial-perpendicular contents of the $x_4$-advance at $p$, with the
algebra of $\mathbb{C}$ (multiplication law $i^2 = -1$) forced by the
perpendicularity selection on the one-dimensional perpendicular axis
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}). At every event $p \in M_{1,3}$, the
complex amplitude $\psi(p)$ carries the principle as its constitutive
content: the real and imaginary parts are the local projections of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at $p$. Pointwise constitutivity follows.

**Level 4 ($\mathcal{H}$).** The Hilbert-space element
$\lvert \psi \rangle \in \mathcal{H}$ is represented in its
spatial-slice cross-section by the function
$\psi: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{C}$, with
$\psi(\mathbf{x}) = \int_{M_{1,3}} \ldots\,$ as the integrated
forward--conjugate $x_4$-overlap content at spatial point $\mathbf{x}$
on the slice (Theorem [9.15](#thm:hilbert-inner){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-inner"}). At every spatial point $\mathbf{x}$ on
the slice, the value $\psi(\mathbf{x})$ is the integrated content of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ from all source events that contribute to
$\mathbf{x}$. The Hilbert-space inner product
$\langle\phi|\psi\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \phi^*\psi\,d^3x$ is the
integration of the pointwise content over the slice. Pointwise
constitutivity at every event of every spatial slice of $\mathcal{H}$
follows.

The four-level verification establishes that $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is
the constitutive content at every event of every level of the chain of theorems, present at every level rather than an upstream foundation left behind. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:four-sense-pointwise-instantiation .theorem}
**Theorem 9.25** (Four-sense classification of pointwise instantiation;
[@MG-Pointwise-2026] Theorem 10.5). *The pointwise constitutivity of
Theorem [9.24](#thm:pointwise-constitutivity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:pointwise-constitutivity"} admits a sharper classification: in every structure derived in the chain of theorems
from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, the principle is locally instantiated at
every point/element/value/term of the structure in one of four
distinct senses, corresponding to the four types of
mathematical structure the chain of theorems generates (manifold, function space,
scalar density, operator equation):*

1.  **Literal pointwise satisfaction --- geometric manifold $M_{1,3}$.*
    At every spacetime point $p \in M_{1,3}$, the principle
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds in the rest frame of any massive
    particle at $p$
    (Lemma [4.7](#lem:reverse-reading-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:reverse-reading-equivalence"}). Equivalently,
    $M_{1,3}$ is the constraint surface $\Phi_M^{-1}(0)$ where
    $\Phi_M = x_{4}- ict$ (the mere integrated kinematic shadow of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ per Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref" reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}), so every point of $M_{1,3}$ satisfies
    $\Phi_M = 0$ by definition of being on the constraint surface
    (Theorem [4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"}).*

2.  **Constructive pointwise constitution --- function space
    $\mathcal{H}$.* Every element $\psi \in \mathcal{H}$ of the
    McGucken-derived Hilbert space contains $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in
    four senses simultaneously: *algebraically* (the
    imaginary unit $i$ in $\psi$'s $\mathbb{C}$-valued structure is the
    perpendicularity marker for $x_{4}$ from $x_{4}= ict$, by
    Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}); *constructively* (every McGucken
    wavefunction is built as a path-integral kernel over paths on
    $M_{1,3}$, with the principle holding at every point per clause
    (L));  (the inner product
    $\langle\phi, \psi\rangle = \int\phi^*\psi\,d^3x$ is the rank-2
    metric pairing of
    Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}, inherited from $(ic)^2 = -c^2$
    of Theorem [4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"}); and *at the completion level*
    (the parallelogram identity holds by direct two-line algebra from
    rank-2 sesquilinearity, fixing the $L^2$-norm structure on
    $\mathcal{H}$,
    Theorem [9.17](#thm:hilbert-complete){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-complete"}).*

3.  **Evaluative pointwise constitution --- scalar density
    $P = |\psi|^2$.* At every spatial point $x \in \mathbb{R}^3$ at
    every parameter time $t$, the Born density
    $P(x, t) = \psi^*(x, t)\psi(x, t)$ is the geometric overlap of the
    forward $x_{4}$-expansion $\psi$ (carrying phase from $x_{4}= ict$)
    with the conjugate $x_{4}$-expansion $\psi^*$ (carrying phase from
    $x_{4}^* = -ict$) at $(x, t)$
    (Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"} and
    Theorem [11.5](#thm:born-as-collision){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:born-as-collision"}). Every evaluation of $P$ records
    the principle as the meeting of the forward and conjugate
    $x_{4}$-expansions. The exponent 2 in $P = |\psi|^2$ is
    overdetermined by two derivationally disjoint McGucken-internal
    routes: forced by the rank-2 character of the Minkowski metric
    (Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}, the metric route) and reinforced by the
    McGucken-internal parallelogram identity that follows from rank-2
    sesquilinearity (the parallelogram route). Both routes descend from
    $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the Jordan--von Neumann (1935)
    parallelogram identity is the historical functional-analytic
    correlate (downstream consistency check), not an upstream input.*

4.  **Operatorial pointwise constitution --- operator equation
    $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$.* Every term of the
    Schrödinger equation carries the principle. The factor $i$ on the
    LHS is the perpendicularity marker for $x_{4}$
    (Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}). The factor $\hbar$ on the LHS is
    the action quantum per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation of
    $x_{4}$-advance
    (Theorem [9.35](#thm:c-hbar-twin){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:c-hbar-twin"}). The time derivative $\partial_t$ is
    related to $\partial/\partial x_{4}$ by the chain-rule identity
    $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial/\partial x_{4}$ on the constraint
    surface where $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every point ---
    equivalently, the principle is the chain rule relating $\partial_t$
    and $\partial/\partial x_{4}$ expressed in operator form. The
    wavefunction $\psi$ on both sides contains the principle by clause
    (C). The Hamiltonian $\hat{H}$ acts on $\psi$ which contains the
    principle.*

*The four senses (literal, constructive, evaluative, operatorial)
correspond to the four types of mathematical structure the chain of theorems
generates (manifold, function space, scalar density, operator equation).
The principle is locally instantiated in each, with the role of an
upstream-derivational ancestor that produces the structures and then
withdraws replaced by the role of a recurring fact at every
level of the descendant structures. The principle is irreversibly
constitutive of every derived structure (stripping it destroys the
structure) and recoverable from any derived structure (the principle is
locally readable at every point).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). We verify each clause.

**Clause (L) --- literal pointwise satisfaction on $M_{1,3}$.** By
Theorem [4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"}, the Lorentzian spacetime $M_{1,3}$
is generated from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ by integration, squaring, and
substitution; equivalently, $M_{1,3}$ is the constraint surface
$\Phi_M^{-1}(0)$ where $\Phi_M(p) = x_{4}(p) - ict(p)$ vanishes at every
$p \in M_{1,3}$. By
Lemma [4.7](#lem:reverse-reading-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reverse-reading-equivalence"}, at every $p \in M_{1,3}$,
in the rest frame of any massive particle at $p$, the rest-frame
Lorentzian four-velocity normalization $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ expressed in
the Minkowski coordinate $x_{4}= ict$ reads $dx_4/dt = ic$. The
principle is therefore literally satisfied at every point of $M_{1,3}$:
$M_{1,3}$ is defined as the locus where the principle holds, with
Lemma [4.7](#lem:reverse-reading-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reverse-reading-equivalence"} providing the equivalent
rest-frame interpretation in terms of the four-velocity normalization.
Stripping any point $p$ from $M_{1,3}$ that does not satisfy the
principle would by definition place that point outside $M_{1,3}$; the
principle's pointwise satisfaction is therefore not a property of
$M_{1,3}$ but its very definition. ✓

**Clause (C) --- constructive pointwise constitution of $\mathcal{H}$.**
Every element $\psi \in \mathcal{H}\cong L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ is
constituted by the principle at four levels. *Algebraic
level.* By Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}, every McGucken wavefunction $\psi$ is
$\mathbb{C}$-valued, with the imaginary unit $i$ in its algebraic
structure being the perpendicularity marker for $x_{4}$'s orthogonality
to $x_1 x_2 x_3$ --- the integrated kinematic shadow of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via
Theorem [4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"}. The perpendicularity selection (§4.1 of
[@MG-Pointwise-2026]) makes $\mathbb{C}$ the unique field choice given
one perpendicular axis; replacing $\mathbb{C}$ with $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{H}$ would either erase the perpendicularity ($\mathbb{R}$: zero
imaginary units) or replace it with a three-perpendicular-axis structure
($\mathbb{H}$: three imaginary units), in both cases destroying the
principle's content. *Constructive level.* Every McGucken wavefunction
is constructed as the path-integral kernel
$\psi(B) = \sum_\gamma \exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$, where $\gamma$ ranges
over paths from a source event $E$ to $B \in M^{+}_{E}(t)$. The paths
$\gamma$ and their endpoints all lie on $M_{1,3}$; by clause (L), the
principle holds at every point of $M_{1,3}$ that any $\gamma$ traverses.
The action-quantization scale $\hbar$ in $\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$ is the
action quantum per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation of $x_{4}$-advance
(Theorem [9.35](#thm:c-hbar-twin){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:c-hbar-twin"}). The phase factor $i$ is the
perpendicularity marker (algebraic level). *Level.* The inner
product on $\mathcal{H}$ is
$\langle\phi, \psi\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \phi^*(x, t)\psi(x, t)\,d^3x$.
By Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}, this inner product is the rank-2
metric pairing on $(\phi, \psi)$ inherited from the rank-2 character of
the Minkowski metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ on $M_{1,3}$; the rank-2 character
itself comes from $(ic)^2 = -c^2 t^2$ in
Theorem [4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"}, which is the squared form of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. *Completion level.* By
Theorem [9.17](#thm:hilbert-complete){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complete"}, the McGucken-derived Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H}$ is the Cauchy completion of the pre-Hilbert space of
wavefunctions under the inner-product-induced norm; the parallelogram
identity follows by direct two-line algebra from the rank-2 sesquilinear
character of the inner product. Stripping any one of these four
levels destroys $\psi$ as a McGucken wavefunction. ✓

**Clause (E) --- evaluative pointwise constitution of $P = |\psi|^2$.**
By Lemma [9.14](#lem:born-as-x4-overlap){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:born-as-x4-overlap"} (and
Theorem [11.5](#thm:born-as-collision){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:born-as-collision"} of
Chapter [11](#ch:born){reference-type="ref" reference="ch:born"}), the
Born density $P(x, t) = \psi^*(x, t)\psi(x, t)$ at any event $(x, t)$ is
the geometric overlap of the forward $x_{4}$-expansion (carrying phase
from $x_{4}= ict$) and the conjugate $x_{4}$-expansion (carrying phase
from $x_{4}^* = -ict$) at $(x, t)$. The forward expansion $\psi$
contains the principle by clause (C) at four levels. The
conjugate expansion $\psi^*$ contains the principle by
orientation-reversal of $x_{4}$: the $-i$ in $\psi^*$'s phase factor is
the orientation-reversed perpendicularity marker; the conjugate kernel
$\psi^*(B) = \sum_\gamma \exp(-iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$ is the same path-sum
with $x_{4}$'s orientation reversed. The product structure $\psi^*\psi$
at $(x, t)$ is the rank-2 metric pairing of forward and conjugate
$x_{4}$-expansions
(Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}); the rank-2 character is from
$(ic)^2 = -c^2 t^2$ of
Theorem [4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"}. The exponent 2 in $P = |\psi|^2$ is
overdetermined by two derivationally disjoint routes that both descend
from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (rank-2 metric forcing the bilinear
pairing, and McGucken-internal parallelogram identity reinforcing the
$L^2$-norm structure). Both routes converge on the exponent 2; both
share no intermediate machinery between the principle and the
conclusion; both start from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The principle is
locally readable at every value of $P$ at every spatial point at every
parameter time. ✓

**Clause (O) --- operatorial pointwise constitution of
$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$.** Every term of the Schrödinger
equation carries the principle. *The factor $i$ on the LHS.* The
canonical-quantization rule
$\hat{p}_\mu = -i\hbar\,\partial/\partial x^\mu$ places the
perpendicularity marker $i$ in $\hat{p}_\mu$
(Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}). In Minkowski's coordinate
$x_{4}= ict$, differentiating along $x_{4}$ is differentiating along the
imaginary axis:
$\partial/\partial x_{4}= (1/ic)\partial/\partial t = -(i/c)\partial_t$,
and this $i$ propagates through the operator structure into the energy
operator $\hat E = i\hbar\,\partial_t$. *The factor $\hbar$ on the LHS.*
The Principle's McGucken Sphere wavelength sets the action $h$
(Theorem [9.35](#thm:c-hbar-twin){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:c-hbar-twin"}): $\hbar$ is the action per
radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation of $x_{4}$-advance. This is the same
$\hbar$ that appears in $\exp(iS/\hbar)$, in
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, in $\sigma_x\sigma_p \geq \hbar/2$, and
in $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$ --- all four are the same
$\hbar$ tracing to the same source. *The time derivative $\partial_t$.*
On the constraint surface $M_{1,3}$ where $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds
at every point (clause (L)), the chain rule along worldlines gives
$$(d/dt)|_\gamma \Psi \;=\; \partial_t\Psi + \frac{dx_4}{dt}\,\frac{\partial\Psi}{\partial x_{4}} \;=\; \partial_t\Psi + ic\,\frac{\partial\Psi}{\partial x_{4}} \;=\; D_M\Psi,$$
so $\partial_t$ and $ic\,\partial/\partial x_{4}$ are related by the
chain rule on $M_{1,3}$. The time derivative $\partial_t$ in the
Schrödinger equation *is* the principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
expressed in operator form, with
$\partial_t = (d/dt)|_\gamma - ic\,\partial/\partial x_{4}$ on the
constraint surface. The chain-rule identity that produces $\partial_t$
in the Schrödinger equation is the principle itself in its operator
instantiation: $\partial_t$ has the role of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ expressed in operator form on the constraint
surface, with the role of an upstream-derivational consequence replaced
by the role of a direct operator-level instantiation of the principle.
*The combination $i\hbar\,\partial_t$ on the LHS.* The LHS
$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi$ is the conjunction of three principle-derived
factors operating on $\psi$ (which itself contains the principle by
clause (C)): the perpendicularity-marker $i$, the action-quantum
$\hbar$, and the time derivative $\partial_t$ which is the chain-rule
operator form of the principle on $M_{1,3}$. The full LHS is therefore
four-fold constituted by the principle. *The Hamiltonian*
$\hat{H}= -(\hbar^2/2m)\nabla^2 + V$ on the RHS contains $\hbar^2$ as
the squared action-quantum, $\nabla^2$ acting on $\psi$ (which contains
the principle), $V$ as multiplication by the real-valued potential
(acting on $\psi$ which contains the principle), and $1/(2m)$ as the
non-relativistic kinematic factor from the rest-mass-phase factorization
(which itself depends on the Klein--Gordon equation derived from the
master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, a consequence of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). Every constant, every operator, every
variable, every term of the Schrödinger equation either *is* the
principle expressed in operator form ($\partial_t$ as the chain-rule
operator identity on $M_{1,3}$, $i$ as the perpendicularity marker,
$\hbar$ as the action quantum, master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ as
a consequence of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$) or *acts on* something
that contains the principle. ✓

All four clauses verified. The McGucken Principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is pointwise instantiated in every derived
structure of the chain of theorems --- literally in the geometric
manifold $M_{1,3}$, constructively at four levels in the
function space $\mathcal{H}$, evaluatively in the scalar density
$P = |\psi|^2$ (with the exponent 2 overdetermined by two routes), and
operatorially in the operator equation
$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat{H}\psi$ (with the time derivative being
the principle in operator form). The four senses correspond to the four
types of mathematical structure the chain of theorems generates: manifold
(literal), function space (constructive), scalar density (evaluative),
operator equation (operatorial). $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:four-sense-architectural .remark}
*Remark 9.26* (Architectural significance of the four-sense
classification). The four-sense classification is a observation about the kind of principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is. A typical upstream axiom (e.g., a postulate
of classical mechanics, or one of the Dirac--von Neumann axioms)
produces downstream theorems but does not appear "in" those theorems as
a local content --- the postulate operates as an upstream ancestor and
then withdraws. The McGucken Principle has the role of a recurring fact at every level of its descendant structures: at the
manifold level it is the constraint defining $M_{1,3}$; at the
function-space level it is the algebraic, constructive, and
completion-level content of every $\psi \in \mathcal{H}$; at the
scalar-density level it is the geometric overlap producing $|\psi|^2$ at
every spatial point; at the operator-equation level it is the chain-rule
operator identity that produces $\partial_t$ in the Schrödinger
equation. No prior program for quantum mechanics has this
pointwise-instantiation property; the Dirac--von Neumann axioms and
every other prior axiomatization (von Neumann 1932, Mackey 1963,
