(Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow on which the
Compton phase accumulates; the dynamical content selecting the preferred
basis sits in $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:cross-species-prediction .remark}
*Remark 10.37* (The cross-species empirical signature).
Proposition [10.36](#prop:preferred-basis-compton){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:preferred-basis-compton"} makes a sharp empirical
prediction ([@MG-Measurement-2026] §VII.2, last paragraph;
cf. Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT22"}): the cross-species ratio of decoherence times
for different masses is
$$\frac{T_{\mathrm{dec},A}}{T_{\mathrm{dec},B}} \;=\; \left(\frac{m_B}{m_A}\right)^2 \;=\; \left(\frac{\omega_{C,B}}{\omega_{C,A}}\right)^2.$$
No other interpretation of quantum mechanics --- Copenhagen,
Many-Worlds, Bohmian, GRW, decoherence-plus-environmental-selection,
RQM, QBism --- predicts this specific cross-species scaling. The
prediction is testable in cross-species interferometry (atoms
vs. molecules vs. nanocrystals at the same temperature), and if
confirmed, the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is the unique theory among the named
interpretations to have predicted the scaling from a single principle.
:::

::: {#rmk:gamma-dec-anchored-to-QMT22 .remark}
*Remark 10.38* (Quantitative anchoring of $\Gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ to the
Compton coupling diffusion). The decoherence rate
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ that selects the preferred basis
(Proposition [10.36](#prop:preferred-basis-compton){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:preferred-basis-compton"}, Step 3) is tied
to the Compton-coupling spatial diffusion constant of
Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT22"},
clause (ii):
$$D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} \;=\; \frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega}{2\gamma^2}.$$
The link is the following. The off-diagonal phase factors
$\exp(i\omega_{C,i}\,g_{S,i}^2 t/\hbar)$ accumulated by the system's
reduced density matrix (Step 2 of the preferred-basis proof) are the
operational expression of the same Compton-frequency coupling that
produces the momentum kicks
$\langle(\Delta p)^2\rangle \sim \varepsilon^2 m^2 c^2 \Omega t$ in
Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT22"},
clause (i). Both expressions descend from a single physical mechanism:
the matter species' Compton-frequency oscillation responding to
environmental coupling at frequencies near $\Omega$.

Quantitatively, for a system $S$ in spatial superposition with
separation $\Delta x$ between branches, the off-diagonal element of
$\rho_S$ decays as
$\exp(-(\Delta x)^2 \Gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}^{(\mathrm{spatial})}/D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})})$,
with the McGucken-Compton contribution to the spatial decoherence rate
being
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}^{(\mathrm{spatial}, \mathrm{McG})}(\Delta x) \;\sim\; \frac{(\Delta x)^2}{4 D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})}}\cdot\frac{1}{T_{\mathrm{coh}}} \;\sim\; \frac{\gamma^2 (\Delta x)^2}{2\varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega\,T_{\mathrm{coh}}}.$$
This is the same quantitative scale as the
cross-species-mass-independent diffusion: the same parameters
$(\varepsilon, \Omega, \gamma)$ that bound the QM T22 diffusion residue
also bound the McGucken-Compton contribution to spatial-superposition
decoherence. The empirical bounds $\varepsilon \lesssim 10^{-20}$ at
Planck-scale $\Omega$ translate directly to bounds on the
McGucken-Compton decoherence rate in spatial superposition experiments
--- providing an independent experimental handle on the same coupling
parameters.

The preferred-basis selection mechanism of
Proposition [10.36](#prop:preferred-basis-compton){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:preferred-basis-compton"} and the Compton diffusion of
Theorem [22.1](#thm:QMT22){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT22"}
are therefore two empirical readings of one underlying physical
mechanism: matter's Compton-frequency oscillation responding to
environmental coupling with the universal $x_{4}$-expansion modulation
parameters $(\varepsilon, \Omega)$. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework prediction is
internally consistent: the same coupling that produces zero-temperature
residual diffusion also selects the preferred basis of macroscopic
observers.
:::

### Proposition IX.1: The absence of a separate $(R)$ law as a theorem {#sec:absence-of-R-law}

::: {#prop:no-separate-R .proposition}
**Proposition 10.39** (The absence of a separate $(R)$ law is a theorem,
not an interpretive choice; [@MG-Measurement-2026] Proposition IX.1).
*In the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, the apparent reduction $(R)$ at measurement
is the cumulative geometric content of four propositions:
Proposition [10.13](#prop:born-rule-geometric){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:born-rule-geometric"} (Born rule from squared-amplitude
geometry),
Proposition [10.15](#prop:superposition-geometric){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:superposition-geometric"} (superposition as geometric
overlap of McGucken-Sphere wavefronts),
Proposition [10.19](#prop:apparent-collapse){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:apparent-collapse"} (apparent collapse as 3D
cross-section reading), and
Proposition [10.35](#prop:measurement-irreversibility){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:measurement-irreversibility"} (irreversibility from
$x_4$-monotonicity). Together, these reduce $(R)$ to a consequence of $(U)$ plus $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. No separate $(R)$
postulate is required, and the standard "$(U) + (R)$" axiomatic
structure of quantum mechanics is replaced by
"$(U) + \dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$" with $(R)$ emerging as a derived
appearance.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof; from [@MG-Measurement-2026] §IX.1.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). We establish the six-step
chain showing that $(R)$ is derived rather than postulated.

**Step 1: Superposition principle as theorem.** By
Proposition [10.15](#prop:superposition-geometric){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:superposition-geometric"}, the linear superposition
principle $(SP)$ --- that any complex linear combination
$\alpha\lvert \psi  \rangle+ \beta\lvert \phi \rangle$ of normalised
states is itself a physically realisable state --- is a theorem of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The origin: multiple
McGucken-Sphere wavefronts can coexist at a common field point because
$x_{4}$'s uniform advance does not preferentially select between sources
(clause P1 of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The combination operator
$\oplus$ on coexistent wavefronts is uniquely fixed to be complex linear
addition by the four conditions D1--D4 (associativity,
commutativity, scaling, distributivity-with-phase). $(SP)$ is therefore
not an independent postulate but a derived consequence of the principle.

**Step 2: Born probability as theorem.** By
Proposition [10.13](#prop:born-rule-geometric){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:born-rule-geometric"}, the Born rule $P(k) = |c_k|^2$ is
a theorem of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The origin: the
$SO(3)$-Haar measure on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront is the unique
probability measure invariant under the spherical-symmetry clause (P2)
of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The squared-amplitude form $|c_k|^2$ is
forced uniquely by four conditions (positivity, normalisation,
superposition-respecting interference, Lorentz-covariance of the
four-current); no other exponent works. Born is therefore not an
independent postulate but a derived consequence of $SO(3)$-Haar on the
McGucken-Sphere structure.

**Step 3: Apparent collapse as theorem.** By
Proposition [10.19](#prop:apparent-collapse){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:apparent-collapse"}, the apparent collapse at
measurement is the operational manifestation of the observer's
restricted access to a single 3D cross-section
$\pi_{\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{obs}}}\lvert \Psi(t) \rangle$ of the unitarily
evolved 4D state. The origin: the suppression map $\sigma$
(Lemma [9.1](#lem:suppression-map){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:suppression-map"}) projects the 4D wavefunction onto the
spatial slice at the McGucken-constraint locus $x_4 = ict$, with each
observer accessing one such slice. The \"collapse\" is therefore the
cross-section reading, not a separate dynamical process --- the 4D
wavefunction $\Psi$ retains its full superposition while the 3D-slice
reading registers a single outcome.

**Step 4: Measurement irreversibility as theorem.** By
Proposition [10.35](#prop:measurement-irreversibility){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:measurement-irreversibility"}, the apparent
irreversibility of measurement (the inability to reverse a registered
outcome) is the same $x_{4}$-monotonicity that grounds the second law of
thermodynamics. The origin: $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ asserts
that $x_{4}$ advances monotonically at rate $ic$ forward in coordinate
time, with no backward-advance branch in the principle's
forward-orientation convention. The thermodynamic arrow of time (entropy
increase) and the measurement-irreversibility arrow (registered outcome
persistence) both descend from this $x_{4}$-monotonicity.

**Step 5: Six sub-problems addressed by propositions.** The
six sub-problems of the measurement problem (P0)--(P5) are each
addressed by a distinct proposition, all derived from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$: $$\begin{aligned}
(P0)\ \text{Superposition} &\;\Leftarrow\; \text{Proposition~\ref{prop:superposition-geometric}}, \\
(P1)\ \text{Probability} &\;\Leftarrow\; \text{Proposition~\ref{prop:born-rule-geometric}}, \\
(P2)\ \text{Collapse} &\;\Leftarrow\; \text{Proposition~\ref{prop:apparent-collapse}}, \\
(P3)\ \text{Preferred basis} &\;\Leftarrow\; \text{Proposition~\ref{prop:preferred-basis-compton}}, \\
(P4)\ \text{Irreversibility} &\;\Leftarrow\; \text{Proposition~\ref{prop:measurement-irreversibility}}, \\
(P5)\ \text{Nonlocality} &\;\Leftarrow\; \text{Theorems~\ref{thm:first-law-nonlocality} and~\ref{thm:second-law-nonlocality}}.
\end{aligned}$$ Each row represents a derived theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, not an independent postulate.

**Step 6: Axiomatic burden reduction.** The standard "$(U) + (R)$"
axiomatic structure of quantum mechanics requires two dynamical laws:
unitary evolution $(U)$ and reduction-on-measurement $(R)$. The McGucken
framework replaces this with "$(U) + \dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$" --- one
dynamical law (unitary evolution) and one geometric principle (the
McGucken Principle). $(R)$ is no longer a postulate but emerges as a
derived appearance: the combined geometric content of Propositions
[10.15](#prop:superposition-geometric){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:superposition-geometric"},
[10.13](#prop:born-rule-geometric){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:born-rule-geometric"},
[10.19](#prop:apparent-collapse){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:apparent-collapse"},
[10.35](#prop:measurement-irreversibility){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:measurement-irreversibility"}, and
[10.36](#prop:preferred-basis-compton){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:preferred-basis-compton"}. The advantage is
the elimination of $(R)$ as an independent postulate, replacing the
dual-law $(U) + (R)$ structure with the single-principle
$(U) + (\mathrm{McP})$ structure where measurement is fully accounted
for as a consequence of geometric kinematics. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:punchline .remark}
*Remark 10.40* (The punchline: $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ both derived
from one principle). [@MG-Measurement-2026] §XI identifies the
punchline: the two postulates of the Dirac--von
Neumann axiomatisation are $(Q_1)$ linear superposition (Hilbert space)
and $(Q_3)$ Born rule. The remaining postulates $(Q_2)$ self-adjoint
operators, $(Q_4)$ Schrödinger evolution, $(Q_5)$ canonical commutation,
$(Q_6)$ tensor product structure are derivable from $(Q_1)$ and $(Q_3)$
given standard commitments. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework derives
*both* $(Q_1)$ and $(Q_3)$ as theorems of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$:

-   $(Q_1)$ is forced by
    Proposition [10.15](#prop:superposition-geometric){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:superposition-geometric"} (superposition as
    geometric overlap of McGucken-Sphere wavefronts);

-   $(Q_3)$ is forced by
    Proposition [10.13](#prop:born-rule-geometric){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:born-rule-geometric"} (Born rule as
    squared-amplitude geometry of $x_4$-wavefront cross-sections).

No prior framework --- Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, Bohmian mechanics, GRW,
decoherence-plus-environmental-selection, RQM, QBism, or any
combination --- derives both $(Q_1)$ and $(Q_3)$ from a single
underlying principle. Each takes both as postulates, or takes one as
primitive and derives the other from auxiliary assumptions, or modifies
the dynamics. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is the unique exception.
:::

### The interpretations as partial readings

The dual-channel resolution accommodates the prior interpretations as
partial readings, not as competitors to be refuted:

-   *Copenhagen* captures Geometric Channel at registration (the 3D-projection
    of the 4D Sphere). It is correct as far as it goes; it just does not
    articulate the 4D structure underneath.

-   *Many-worlds* captures Algebraic Channel (unitary evolution on $M_{G}$). The
    "many worlds" are the different branches of the 4D wavefunction on
    different 3D slices; each branch is a different 3D-projection. The
    McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework agrees that the 4D structure is unitary and that
    3D-projections at different events give different outcomes; what
    many-worlds calls "branching" is the operational manifestation of
    the 4D-to-3D projection.

-   *Bohmian mechanics* captures Geometric Channel's path-integral reading: each
    particle has a definite trajectory through the Sphere wavefront. The
    Bohmian guiding equation $\dot{x} = \nabla S/m$ (with $S$ the phase
    of the wavefunction) is the gradient of the path-integral phase,
    which is the McGucken Sphere's phase-cycling gradient. The McGucken
    framework and Bohmian mechanics agree on the existence of a
    physically real wave with definite particle trajectories but differ
    on five specific points ([@MG-deBroglie-2026] §VI.4):
    **(B1) Configuration-space vs. physical-space wave.** Bohmian
    mechanics places the pilot wave on $3N$-dimensional configuration
    space (one function on the space of all possible positions of $N$
    particles simultaneously) to handle entanglement. The McGucken
    framework places the wave on physical 3D space: the McGucken Sphere
    is a physical 3D object (the spatial cross-section of $x_{4}$'s
    expansion at rate $c$,
    Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)--(iii)), and multi-particle
    entanglement is handled via the shared null-geodesic identity of
    spheres emitted from common creation events
    (Theorem [18.1](#thm:QMT18){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT18"}), not via a wave on higher-dimensional
    configuration space. The McGucken wave is ontologically simpler (one
    3D sphere per entity rather than one function on $3N$-dimensional
    space) and lives on the space of physical experience rather than on
    a mathematical construct. **(B2) No quantum potential.** Bohmian
    mechanics introduces the quantum potential
    $Q = -(\hbar^2/2m)(\nabla^2 R/R)$ where $R = |\psi|$ as the
    representation of how quantum effects modify classical trajectories
    --- a new field with no classical analog. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework
    introduces no analogous new field; the wave's geometric expansion at
    $c$ produces interference, diffraction, and tunneling directly
    through the amplitude structure on the McGucken Sphere
    (Theorems [6.8](#thm:three-part-ontology){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:three-part-ontology"}--[6.9](#thm:duality-dissolved){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:duality-dissolved"} of
    Chapter [6](#ch:wave-particle){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ch:wave-particle"}), without any auxiliary potential.
    **(B3) No preferred-foliation problem.** Bohmian mechanics requires
    a preferred foliation of spacetime for its guiding equation to be
    well-defined in the many-particle case --- a choice of simultaneity
    structure that has no analog in Lorentz-invariant physics (the
    Maudlin 1996 objection: the preferred foliation is either additional
    absolute structure in tension with Lorentz invariance, or
    covariantly derived in ways that have not achieved consensus
    acceptance). The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework has no preferred-foliation
    problem: its foliation is the canonical observer-time foliation of
    Minkowski spacetime derived from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ itself
    (clauses (i)--(iv) of
    Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
    reference="postulate:mcp"}), not introduced as extra structure.
    **(B4) No empty waves.** In Bohmian mechanics, the pilot wave has
    non-zero amplitude in every branch of the multi-particle wave
    function, including branches where no particle is located --- "empty
    waves" or "zombie worlds" --- which are real physical structures
    with no observable consequences. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework has no
    analog: an MQF quantum entity has one McGucken Sphere with one
    amplitude distribution, not a guiding wave plus particle that can be
    in separate branches. **(B5) Derivation vs. inheritance of the de
    Broglie relation.** Bohmian mechanics preserves the de Broglie
    relation $p = \hbar k$ as a kinematic identity of the guiding
    equation: for a plane wave $\psi = e^{i(kx - \omega t)}$, the
    guidance velocity $v = \nabla S/m = \hbar k/m$ is equivalent to
    $p = \hbar k$. But Bohmian mechanics *inherits* this from the
    Schrödinger equation that the pilot wave is assumed to satisfy; it
    does not *derive* it from a geometric principle. The McGucken
    framework derives $p = \hbar k$
    (Theorem [2.1](#thm:QMT2){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QMT2"}) by derivationally disjoint Geometric Channel and
    Algebraic Channel routes from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with the wave nature
    itself (the McGucken Sphere) and the specific relation $p = \hbar k$
    as theorems of the geometric principle rather than as consequences
    of postulated Schrödinger dynamics.

-   *Decoherence* (Zurek, Joos, Zeh) captures the operational
    scale-dependence of the Heisenberg cut. [@MG-Measurement-2026]
    §VII.2 makes the mechanism precise: the environmental coupling that
    diagonalises $\rho_S$ in the pointer basis is the Compton-frequency
    coupling of environmental constituents to $x_4$'s expansion
    (Proposition [10.36](#prop:preferred-basis-compton){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:preferred-basis-compton"}). Standard decoherence
    shifts the preferred-basis problem to specifying the environmental
    coupling; the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies the coupling from first
    principles.

-   *GRW* (Ghirardi--Rimini--Weber) adds spontaneous-collapse terms to
    the Schrödinger equation with phenomenological parameters. The
    McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework requires no additional dynamics; the projection
    is the 4D-to-3D shadow of unitary evolution.

-   *QBism* reads probabilities as personal credences. This is
    consistent with the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework (the Born probabilities are
    objective frequencies of the 3D-projection events) but the McGucken
    framework is more committed: the probabilities are derived from
    $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, not chosen as subjective credences.

-   *Relational Quantum Mechanics* (Rovelli) reads $\psi$ as
    observer-relative. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework agrees that the
    3D-projection is observer-relative
    (Proposition [10.19](#prop:apparent-collapse){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:apparent-collapse"}) but maintains that the
    underlying 4D structure $\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4)$ is
    observer-independent.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework subsumes all seven interpretations as partial
readings of the dual-channel structure. Each interpretation captures one
channel or one operational aspect; the dual-channel architecture
captures both channels and their derivational disjointness.

### MQF as Copenhagen's foundational completion: the thesis {#sec:mqf-copenhagen-foundational-completion}

The April 20, 2026 Bohmian-comparison paper [@MG-CopenhagenBohmian-2026]
sharpens the relationship of MQF to Copenhagen into a thesis
with three preservation claims and three mechanism additions. The thesis
is that MQF is *not* a rival to Copenhagen --- it is Copenhagen's
*completion*. This stands in contrast to Bohmian mechanics,
whose relationship to Copenhagen is adversarial: Bohmian mechanics
denies Copenhagen's wave-function completeness (by adding particle
positions), rejects Copenhagen's fundamental status of measurement (by
treating it as effective decoherence), and substitutes an alternative
ontology. MQF does none of this. MQF preserves Copenhagen's ontology and
supplies the physical mechanisms Copenhagen was missing.

::: {#prop:mqf-copenhagen-completion .proposition}
**Proposition 10.41** (MQF as Copenhagen's completion;
[@MG-CopenhagenBohmian-2026] §VII). *The McGucken Quantum Formalism
stands to the Copenhagen Interpretation in a complementary
relation, not an adversarial one. Specifically, MQF satisfies three
preservation claims (P1)--(P3) and three mechanism-addition claims
(M1)--(M3):*

-   **Wave-function completeness preserved.* The wavefunction $\psi$
    remains a complete description of the quantum entity; no hidden
    variables or supplementary ontological posits (particle positions,
    beables) are introduced.*

-   **Fundamental status of measurement outcomes preserved.* Measurement
    outcomes are real geometric events (the 3D-localization at apparatus
    intersection with the McGucken Sphere), not effective phenomena
    emerging from a deeper deterministic dynamics.*

-   **Individual-measurement indeterminism preserved.* The outcome of an
    individual measurement remains probabilistic, governed by the Born
    rule, with the deterministic content of MQF residing at the level of
    the geometric postulate $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ rather than at the
    level of individual outcomes.*

-   **Mechanism for the projection postulate.* The non-unitary collapse
    $\lvert \psi \rangle \to \hat{P}_n\lvert \psi \rangle/\|\hat{P}_n\lvert \psi \rangle\|$
    at measurement is the geometric localization of the sphere-wide
    amplitude at the spatial intersection of the McGucken Sphere with
    the measurement apparatus --- a 3D geometric event, not a
    non-dynamical postulate.*

-   **Mechanism for the Heisenberg cut.* The boundary between quantum
    system and classical apparatus is the spatial scale at which
    environmental coupling (Compton-frequency coupling to $x_4$'s
    expansion,
    Proposition [10.36](#prop:preferred-basis-compton){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:preferred-basis-compton"}) renders the localization
    effectively irreversible --- a continuous decoherence-strength
    feature, not a sharp ontological boundary.*

-   **Mechanism for wave-particle complementarity.* The wave-like
    behavior is the pre-localization sphere-wide amplitude distribution;
    the particle-like behavior is the post-localization 3D event; both
    are aspects of one geometric process ($x_4$'s expansion and its
    sphere cross-sections), with the apparent dichotomy depending only
    on whether a measurement apparatus is present at the relevant
    event.*

*The thesis is then: MQF $=$ (P1) $+$ (P2) $+$ (P3) $+$ (M1)
$+$ (M2) $+$ (M3). Bohmian mechanics is adversarial to
Copenhagen: it violates (P1) (adds particle positions), violates (P2)
(treats measurement as effective), and *accepts* all three of
Copenhagen's open problems as resolvable only by replacing the ontology.
MQF resolves all three open problems while preserving the ontology.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof establishes the six claims (P1)--(P3) and (M1)--(M3)
by reference to the established theorems of the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework,
organized in six steps.

**Step 1: (P1) Wave-function completeness preserved.** By
Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"} (Hilbert space arena) and
Theorem [6.1](#thm:QMT6){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT6"}
(wave-particle duality), the quantum entity in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is
the McGucken Sphere wavefront with amplitude distribution
$\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ across the sphere. No supplementary particle
positions exist; the entity is exactly the wave on the sphere. The
Bohmian addition of particle positions as supplementary ontological
variables is therefore explicitly absent in MQF: $\psi$ is complete
because nothing else is needed. Wave-function completeness is preserved
by structure, not stipulation.

**Step 2: (P2) Fundamental status of measurement outcomes preserved.**
By Theorem [19.1](#thm:QMT19){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT19"} (measurement and the Copenhagen interpretation),
a measurement is the 3D-projection of the 4D McGucken Sphere at the
apparatus-intersection event, with the outcome being a real geometric
event on the 3D spatial slice. Outcomes are fundamental geometric events, not effective phenomena emerging from underlying deterministic Bohmian trajectories. The Copenhagen claim that measurement
outcomes are real, definite, and ontologically primary is preserved by
MQF without addition or subtraction.

**Step 3: (P3) Individual-measurement indeterminism preserved.** The
Born rule (Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}) governs the probability of each
possible measurement outcome; an individual measurement's outcome is not
determined by any deterministic underlying dynamics. The McGucken
framework's determinism is at the level of the geometric postulate
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the unitary evolution of the 4D
wavefunction $\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4)$; the indeterminism of individual
measurement outcomes is preserved as the 4D-to-3D projection's
branch-selection step
(cf. Proposition [10.19](#prop:apparent-collapse){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:apparent-collapse"}). Copenhagen's indeterminism is
preserved at the individual-outcome level; MQF's determinism lives one
layer deeper, at the geometric-postulate level, without contradicting
individual-outcome indeterminism.

**Step 4: (M1) Mechanism for the projection postulate.** By the Geometric
Channel reading of Theorem [19.1](#thm:QMT19){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT19"}, projection is the 3D-localization of the
sphere-wide amplitude at the apparatus-intersection point. The
non-unitarity of the projection postulate
$\lvert \psi \rangle \to \hat{P}_n\lvert \psi \rangle/\|\hat{P}_n\lvert \psi \rangle\|$
is the kinematic shadow of this 3D-localization on the spatial slice:
the full 4D state remains in unitary evolution, but the observer's
3D-cross-section access registers only the localized branch. This is a
real geometric mechanism in 3D physical space, not a non-dynamical
postulate. The mechanism is supplied by the 4D-geometric structure of
the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, without adding any new ontological commitments
beyond $x_4$'s physical reality (already implicit in
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}).

**Step 5: (M2) Mechanism for the Heisenberg cut.** By
Proposition [10.36](#prop:preferred-basis-compton){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:preferred-basis-compton"}, the environmental coupling
that fixes the preferred basis and drives effective irreversibility is
the Compton-frequency coupling of environmental constituents to $x_4$'s
expansion. The Heisenberg cut is the spatial scale at which this
coupling is strong enough to render the 3D-localization effectively
permanent --- equivalently, the scale at which decoherence (Zurek, Joos,
Zeh) becomes operationally irreversible. The cut is a continuous feature
(varying with apparatus size, temperature, and coupling strength), not a
sharp ontological boundary, and it is supplied by MQF's first-principle
account of environmental coupling rather than as a pragmatic separate
postulate.

**Step 6: (M3) Mechanism for wave-particle complementarity.** By
Theorem [6.8](#thm:three-part-ontology){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:three-part-ontology"} (three-part ontology) and the
surrounding Theorems [6.9](#thm:duality-dissolved){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:duality-dissolved"} of
Chapter [6](#ch:wave-particle){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:wave-particle"}, the wave-like behavior is the
pre-localization sphere-wide amplitude distribution on the McGucken
Sphere, and the particle-like behavior is the post-localization 3D event
at apparatus intersection. Both behaviors are aspects of the same
geometric process ($x_4$'s expansion and its sphere cross-sections); the
apparent dichotomy depends only on whether a measurement apparatus is
present at the relevant event. Complementarity is the fact
that one geometric process has two operational aspects, the difference
being the presence or absence of localization.

**Synthesis: MQF as completion.** The six steps establish
(P1)--(P3) and (M1)--(M3). Copenhagen's formalism is preserved entirely
(wave-function completeness; measurement-outcome primacy;
individual-outcome indeterminism); the physical mechanisms Copenhagen
acknowledged as absent (projection mechanism; Heisenberg cut mechanism;
complementarity mechanism) are supplied by the underlying
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ geometry. The relationship is
therefore complementary: MQF underpins Copenhagen with the physical
content Copenhagen formal-without. Bohmian mechanics, by contrast,
satisfies neither (P1) (adds particles) nor (P2) (makes measurement
effective) and accepts Copenhagen's open problems only by replacing the
ontology --- the adversarial relationship that distinguishes it from
MQF. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:full-copenhagen-mechanism-catalog .remark}

[@MG-CopenhagenBohmian-2026] §VII.5).
Proposition [10.41](#prop:mqf-copenhagen-completion){reference-type="ref"

Every element Copenhagen acknowledged as lacking mechanism is supplied
with one by MQF. Bohmian mechanics supplies mechanisms for several of
these (effective collapse via conditional wavefunction;
configuration-space guidance for nonlocality; equivariance for the Born
rule) but at the cost of replacing Copenhagen's ontology with the
Bohmian ontology (particles plus configuration-space wavefunction). MQF
provides the mechanisms without replacing the ontology: $\psi$ remains
the physical wave, no particles exist beyond the localization events,
and no configuration-space realism is required. This is the distinctive
feature that distinguishes MQF from every other
interpretation: Copenhagen's formalism is preserved wholesale, and the
missing mechanisms are supplied by the 4D-geometric structure
underneath.
:::

### Maudlin-immunity formalized: scope and methodological response {#sec:maudlin-immunity-formalized}

The five-point Bohmian contrast in the previous section established
(B3): MQF has no preferred-foliation problem because its foliation is
the canonical observer-time foliation of Minkowski spacetime derived
from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ itself, not introduced as extra structure.
The April 20, 2026 paper [@MG-CopenhagenBohmian-2026] §V sharpens this
into a formal scope statement and supplies a methodological response to
the standard reflexive objection against MQF's ontology.

::: {#rmk:maudlin-immunity-scope .remark}
*Remark 10.43* (Scope of MQF's immunity to Maudlin's 1996 critique;
[@MG-CopenhagenBohmian-2026] §V.5). The immunity of MQF to Maudlin's
preferred-foliation critique [@Maudlin1996] is a *advantage*,
not a decisive argument that MQF is the correct theory of quantum
mechanics. Specifically:

**What it establishes.** Maudlin's critique is constructively built
around the Bohmian structure: it requires a theory with (i)
instantaneous configurations of definite particle positions, (ii) a
guidance equation that depends on configuration-space structures, and
(iii) a notion of simultaneity to make (i) and (ii) work. A theory with
none of these features --- MQF has none of them --- cannot be criticized
on Maudlin's grounds. The critique is specific to
Bohmian-type theories and does not generalize to theories that build
quantum mechanics on a different foundation.

**What it does not establish.** Maudlin's critique does not show Bohmian
mechanics to be false; it identifies a serious foundational tension that
the Bohmian program has not resolved to consensus satisfaction in thirty
years. The four Bohmian responses (Dürr--Goldstein--Münch-Berndl--Zanghì
extra absolute structure; Nikolić covariantly-determined foliation;
Galvan all-foliations union; Struyve--Tumulka degenerate foliations)
each have technical and conceptual difficulties; none has achieved
consensus acceptance. MQF's advantage on this axis is: the
tension does not arise in MQF because the architecture is
different (4D-geometric postulate rather than configuration-space
guidance). Whether MQF is correct depends on empirical tests (the
Compton coupling diffusion signature of [@MG-Compton-2026]) and the
success of the derivational program; immunity to the Maudlin critique is
a necessary but not sufficient condition for foundational adequacy.

**Alignment with Maudlin's broader program.** Maudlin's broader work in
*Quantum Non-Locality and Relativity* [@Maudlin1996] argues
programmatically that the deepest resolution of the
quantum-nonlocality/relativity tension would be a theory in which
quantum correlations are explained by the structure of Minkowski
spacetime itself, not by additional faster-than-light processes or
preferred foliations. MQF is precisely such a theory: nonlocality arises
from the shared null-geodesic identity of points on the McGucken Sphere
(Theorem [17.1](#thm:QMT17){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT17"}), which is a null-hypersurface cross-section of
Minkowski spacetime (the sixth of the six independent senses of
geometric locality in
Theorem [17.12](#thm:six-fold-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:six-fold-identity"}). MQF is in substantial
methodological alignment with Maudlin's program even as it is immune to
the specific critique Maudlin mounted against Bohmian mechanics.
:::

::: {#rmk:dynamical-geometry-already-accepted .remark}
*Remark 10.44* (Dynamical-geometry-already-accepted methodological
response; [@MG-CopenhagenBohmian-2026] §VI.4.1). The standard reflexive
objection to the McGucken Principle $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ --- that
dimensions, being coordinate labels, cannot do anything (cannot expand,
contract, oscillate, or otherwise evolve) --- presupposes a
pre-relativistic picture of spacetime as an inert background container.
That picture was abandoned by physics itself more than a century ago, in
independent and reinforcing waves of theoretical and experimental
development:

-   *General relativity (1915).* Einstein's field equations
    $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$ make spacetime geometry itself
    the fundamental dynamical variable of gravitation. The metric
    $g_{\mu\nu}$ is a field that evolves according to an equation of
    motion sourced by the stress-energy tensor. Every solution to the
    field equations describes a geometry that is changing in time,
    space, or both.

-   *Inflationary cosmology (1980).* Guth's inflationary scenario
    requires spacetime to expand exponentially during the inflationary
    epoch, with the Hubble parameter $H$ taking values roughly 40 orders
    of magnitude larger during inflation than today. The expansion rate
    itself varies dynamically across cosmological eras.

-   *LIGO/Virgo gravitational-wave detection (2015).* The direct
    observation of compact-binary coalescences confirmed that spacetime
    geometry oscillates as a wave: spatial distances rhythmically
    stretch and compress as a gravitational wave passes through a
    detector. The amplitude is tiny (strain $\sim 10^{-21}$) but
    unambiguous.

-   *The FLRW scale factor $a(t)$.* Every cosmological model built on
    the Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker metric treats $a(t)$ as
    an ordinary dynamical variable satisfying the Friedmann equations.
    "The universe is expanding" means literally that $a(t)$ is an
    increasing function of time.

Against this unanimous century-long consensus --- with the metric
evolving under field equations (GR), expanding exponentially during
specific epochs (inflation), oscillating as waves (LIGO), and scaling in
time (FLRW cosmology) --- $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the natural
simplification. It is a first-order equation with a single parameter
(the measured velocity $c$), specifying evolution in the single most
natural direction (perpendicular to the spatial triple), describing the
simplest possible geometric dynamics: uniform expansion along the fourth
axis at the invariant speed. Compared to the second-order coupled tensor
field equations of general relativity, the inflaton-potential dynamics
of inflation, or the quadrupolar oscillations of a gravitational wave,
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is radically simpler --- arguably the simplest
nontrivial dynamical-geometry proposal one could write down.

The force of this observation: any physicist who accepts general
relativity, inflationary cosmology, and gravitational-wave detection has
already committed to dynamical geometry as a real feature of nature. The
ontological step of saying "geometry moves, evolves, expands, and
oscillates" was taken in 1915 and reinforced by every major development
in gravitational physics since. MQF does not take a new ontological
step; it takes the simplest possible instantiation of a step already
taken. A philosopher who accepts the expansion of the universe, the
oscillations of gravitational waves, and the dynamical metric of general
relativity cannot consistently reject $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ on the
grounds that "dimensions are static" --- the static-dimension picture is
the one modern physics has discarded, not the one it defends. The
remaining question is empirical (whether the specific dynamical geometry
proposed delivers the explanatory and predictive content claimed for
it), not ontological.
:::

### The Born rule deeper than Bohmian on five grounds {#sec:born-rule-deeper-than-bohmian}

The April 20, 2026 paper [@MG-CopenhagenBohmian-2026] §VIII establishes
a five-point comparison between the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework
derivation of the Born rule and the Bohmian account
(Dürr--Goldstein--Zanghì typicality plus Valentini--Westerman
relaxation). The Bohmian account is sophisticated, but the $|\psi|^2$
functional form is built into the equivariant-measure framework through
the specific functional form of the guidance equation; it is not derived
from a prior physical fact. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework derivation is
deeper on five distinct grounds.

::: {#prop:born-rule-deeper-than-bohmian .proposition}
**Proposition 10.45** (Born rule deeper than Bohmian on
five grounds; [@MG-CopenhagenBohmian-2026] §VIII.6). *The
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework derivation of the Born rule
(Theorem [11.1](#thm:QMT11-channelA){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"}; the SO(3)-Haar measure on the McGucken
Sphere combined with the complex character of $\psi$ from the
perpendicularity of $x_4$) is deeper than the Bohmian
account (Dürr--Goldstein--Zanghì typicality plus Valentini--Westerman
relaxation) on five distinct grounds:*

-   **Derivation of the quadratic exponent from prior geometry.* The
    McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework derives the $|\psi|^2$ exponent from the prior
    geometric fact that the $i$ in $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the
    perpendicularity marker of $x_4$ relative to the three spatial
    dimensions, forcing $\psi$ to be complex when viewed from within the
    3D slice, after which $|\psi|^2 = \psi^*\psi$ is the unique real,
    non-negative, phase-invariant scalar. Bohmian mechanics derives the
    quadratic from the equivariance of the guiding equation, but the
    equivariance was constructed to preserve $|\psi|^2$.*

-   **Derivation of the complex structure of $\psi$.* The McGucken
    framework derives the complex character of $\psi$ from the
    perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions (a prior
    geometric fact about spacetime), independent of quantum-mechanical
    machinery. Bohmian mechanics accepts the complex character of $\psi$
    as inherited from standard QM; it does not derive it from a deeper
    physical fact.*

-   **The Born rule is part of a fifteen-derivation unity.* The Born
    rule in the McGucken framework is one consequence of
    $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the same principle produces Huygens'
    principle, the Feynman path integral, the Schrödinger equation,
    least action, Noether's theorem, the canonical commutation relation,
    quantum nonlocality, wave-function collapse, the five arrows of
    time, the second law, the invariance of $c$, liberation from the
    block universe, the $+i\varepsilon$ prescription, and (via the
    oscillatory form of the principle) the numerical values of both $c$
    and $\hbar$ themselves. Bohmian mechanics' Born-rule account is
    specific to the Bohmian framework and does not participate in any
    comparable unification.*

-   **No configuration-space realism.* The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework places all
    physical waves on 3D physical space (as McGucken-Sphere
    cross-sections) or in 4D spacetime (as $x_4$-expansion). Bohmian
    mechanics requires the wavefunction on $3N$-dimensional
    configuration space to be physically real, which has generated a
    substantial philosophical literature on what kind of entity such a
    wave is.*

-   **Forward-causal substrate.* The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's nonlocal
    correlations arise from the null structure of Minkowski spacetime,
    with nothing travelling faster than $c$ at the substrate level.
    Bohmian mechanics has explicit faster-than-light influences through
    configuration-space guidance, in tension with the spirit of Lorentz
    invariance.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has five steps establishing each of
(D1)--(D5).

**Step 1: (D1) Derivation of the quadratic from prior geometry.** By
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} and the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework derivation of
complex-amplitude $\psi$ in Step 1 of the present chapter (and
Theorem [9.10](#thm:hilbert-complex){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-complex"}), $\psi$ is complex because $x_4$
extends perpendicular to the three spatial dimensions and the $i$ in
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the algebraic marker of this orthogonality.
Once $\psi$ is complex, the requirements that the probability density be
(a) real-valued, (b) non-negative, and (c) invariant under the global
phase rotation $\psi \to e^{i\theta}\psi$ together force the quadratic
form $|\psi|^2 = \psi^*\psi$ uniquely: $|\psi|^1$ fails non-negativity
for complex $\psi$ without a separate modulus; $|\psi|^3$ fails the
linear-superposition scaling required by the Born rule;
$\mathrm{Re}(\psi)$ and $\mathrm{Im}(\psi)$ each fail phase invariance.
The squaring is therefore derived from the prior physical fact that
$\psi$ is complex, which is itself derived from the prior physical fact
that $x_4$ is perpendicular to 3-space. Both facts are prior to the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's quantum-mechanical machinery and are geometric, not
quantum-mechanical. In Bohmian mechanics, by contrast, the squaring is
built into the equivariance structure of the guidance equation, which
was constructed to preserve the $|\psi|^2$ measure --- the explanation
is internal to the Bohmian framework and does not trace to a prior
physical fact.

**Step 2: (D2) Derivation of complex $\psi$.** The complex character of
$\psi$ in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is, by

reference="thm:hilbert-complex"} and the perpendicularity reading of $i$
in $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, a geometric consequence of $x_4$'s
orthogonality to the spatial three. A wave that propagates along an axis
perpendicular to our 3D slice carries complex amplitude when projected
into the slice: the real part is the component aligned with the slice,

precise algebraic expression: with the $i$ present (genuine

**Step 3: (D3) Part of fifteen-derivation unity.** The Born rule in the

reference="thm:QMT11-channelA"} by the same principle

**Step 4: (D4) No configuration-space realism.** The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework

**Synthesis.** Together (D1)--(D5) establish that the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework
