### The three pair equivalences of McG${}_6$ {#sec:pair-adjunctions}

Among the 15 unordered pairs of the six objects of McG${}_6$, exactly
three are *direct equivalences* (in fact isomorphisms of categories with
identity unit and counit), each forced by the ingredient that
the pair shares. We give the full four-part proof for each.

::: {#thm:adj-geometric .theorem}
**Theorem 13.1** (Atom/global equivalence; [@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026]
Theorem 3.1). *The assembly and localisation functors between
$\Sigma_M$-bundles and Moving-Dimension-Manifold tuples constitute an
*equivalence of categories*
$$\mathrm{Asm}: \mathbf{SphBdl} \;\xrightarrow{\;\simeq\;}\; \mathbf{MovDimMfd} \;:\; \mathrm{Loc},$$
with $\mathrm{Loc} \circ \mathrm{Asm} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{SphBdl}}$
and $\mathrm{Asm} \circ \mathrm{Loc} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{MovDimMfd}}$
(the two composites equal the identity functors, with the equality holding on the nose). The pair $(\mathrm{Asm}, \mathrm{Loc})$
is therefore an adjoint equivalence with identity unit and identity
counit --- in fact an isomorphism of categories. Writing the equivalence
at the level of generating objects, the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M$ and
the Moving-Dimension Manifold tuple $\mathcal{G}_M$ are equivalent in
McG${}_6$: $\Sigma_M \simeq \mathcal{G}_M$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has four parts: (1) define the two functors, (2)
construct the unit $\eta$ and observe it is the identity, (3) construct
the counit $\varepsilon$ and observe it is the identity, (4) record the
consequence that the pair is an isomorphism of categories (hence in
particular an equivalence). The structure is forced by
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, the physical, geometric fact that the fourth
dimension expands at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric
manner): the McGucken Sphere assignment $p \mapsto \Sigma_M^+(p)$ at
each event $p \in M^{1,3}$ is generated by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii) (spherical symmetry of the
$x_{4}$-expansion), and the foliation by $x_{4}$-flow leaves is
generated by clause (iii) (monotonicity of the integral curve), with
$x_4 = ict$ the integrated kinematic shadow per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}.

**Step 1: Functors.** Let $\mathbf{SphBdl}$ denote the category of
$\Sigma_M$-bundles over the event-set $M^{1,3}$: objects are assignments
$p \mapsto \Sigma_M^+(p)$ of a McGucken Sphere to each event
(Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:sphere"}, the McGucken Sphere as a primitive
descending from Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(ii)); morphisms are
$\Sigma_M$-bundle maps. Let $\mathbf{MovDimMfd}$ denote the category of
Moving-Dimension-Manifold objects
$\mathcal{G}_M = (M, \mathcal{F}, V, \Sigma_M)$ (with foliation
$\mathcal{F}$, privileged vector field $V$, Sphere-bundle $\Sigma_M$);
morphisms are smooth maps preserving the foliation, vector field, and
Sphere assignment.

*Asm:* Given a $\Sigma_M$-bundle $B$ with fibres $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at each
event $p$, set $\mathrm{Asm}(B) := (M, \mathcal{F}_B, V_B, B)$, where
$\mathcal{F}_B$ is the natural foliation of $M$ by $x_4$-flow leaves
(the foliation generated by translating each event along the integrated
axiom $x_4 = ict$), and $V_B$ is the privileged vector field with
$dx_4(V_B)/dt = ic$ at every event (forced by $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
at every event; $V_B$ is the McGucken Axiom's vector field).

*Loc:* Given $\mathcal{G}_M = (M, \mathcal{F}, V, \Sigma)$, set
$\mathrm{Loc}(\mathcal{G}_M) :=$ the $\Sigma$-bundle, i.e., the
assignment $p \mapsto \Sigma^+(p)$, with bundle-structure inherited from
$\mathcal{G}_M$.

**Step 2: The unit $\eta$ is the identity.** For any $\Sigma_M$-bundle
$B$, the composite $\mathrm{Loc} \circ \mathrm{Asm}$ acts by
$$\mathrm{Loc}(\mathrm{Asm}(B)) \;=\; \mathrm{Loc}(M, \mathcal{F}_B, V_B, B) \;=\; B,$$
since the bundle-component of the tuple $\mathrm{Asm}(B)$ is exactly $B$
by construction. Therefore
$\mathrm{Loc} \circ \mathrm{Asm} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{SphBdl}}$ as a
functor, and the unit
$\eta = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Loc} \circ \mathrm{Asm}}$ is the identity
natural transformation.

**Step 3: The counit $\varepsilon$ is the identity.** For any
$\mathcal{G}_M = (M, \mathcal{F}, V, \Sigma)$, the composite
$\mathrm{Asm} \circ \mathrm{Loc}$ acts by
$$\mathrm{Asm}(\mathrm{Loc}(\mathcal{G}_M)) \;=\; \mathrm{Asm}(\Sigma) \;=\; (M, \mathcal{F}_\Sigma, V_\Sigma, \Sigma).$$
We show this equals $(M, \mathcal{F}, V, \Sigma)$ canonically. The
bundle-component is $\Sigma$ in both. The foliation $\mathcal{F}_\Sigma$
is generated by the $x_4$-flow at rate $ic$ from each event of $M$; the
foliation $\mathcal{F}$ of $\mathcal{G}_M$ is by definition the
foliation generated by $V$ flowing at rate $ic$ along $x_4$. The
McGucken Axiom forces both $\mathcal{F}_\Sigma$ and $\mathcal{F}$ to be
the same foliation: the unique foliation of $M$ with leaves tangent to
$V$, where $V$ has $x_4$-rate $ic$. Similarly $V_\Sigma = V$ by the same
uniqueness. Therefore
$\mathrm{Asm} \circ \mathrm{Loc} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{MovDimMfd}}$ as
a functor, and the counit
$\varepsilon = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Asm} \circ \mathrm{Loc}}$ is the
identity natural transformation.

**Step 4: Isomorphism of categories.** Steps 2 and 3 establish that
$\mathrm{Loc} \circ \mathrm{Asm} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{SphBdl}}$ and
$\mathrm{Asm} \circ \mathrm{Loc} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{MovDimMfd}}$ on the nose, as an equality of functors. The pair
$(\mathrm{Asm}, \mathrm{Loc})$ is therefore an *isomorphism of
categories* (Mac Lane [@MacLane1971] §IV.4): a strictly stronger
relation than equivalence, which itself is strictly stronger than
adjunction. The triangle identities for the corresponding adjoint
equivalence are trivially satisfied, since they reduce to compositions
of identity natural transformations. Stating the result at the level of
generating objects, the McGucken Sphere structure $\Sigma_M$ and the
Moving-Dimension-Manifold tuple $\mathcal{G}_M$ are the same object viewed through two functorial windows. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:identity-adjunction .remark}
*Remark 13.2* (Why the unit and counit are identities). The composites
$\mathrm{Loc} \circ \mathrm{Asm}$ and $\mathrm{Asm} \circ \mathrm{Loc}$
are equal to the identity functors on the nose because the McGucken
Axiom $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ uniquely determines the
assembly-localisation pair: there is no freedom in the foliation, vector
field, or fibre assignment, all fixed by the axiom acting at every
event. This rigidity is the categorical-coherence content of MCC${}_6$
(Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"} below) specialised to the geometric pair, and
is responsible for promoting the adjunction to an isomorphism of
categories (Mac Lane [@MacLane1971] §IV.4).
:::

::: {#thm:adj-dynamical .theorem}
**Theorem 13.3** (Operator/space equivalence;
[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Theorem 3.2). *The operator-construction
and carrier-extraction functors between McGucken Operators and McGucken
Spaces constitute an *equivalence of categories*
$$\mathrm{OpCons}: \mathbf{Op} \;\xrightarrow{\;\simeq\;}\; \mathbf{StrSp} \;:\; \mathrm{CarExt},$$
with $\mathrm{CarExt} \circ \mathrm{OpCons} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{Op}}$
and
$\mathrm{OpCons} \circ \mathrm{CarExt} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{StrSp}}$.
The pair $(\mathrm{OpCons}, \mathrm{CarExt})$ is therefore an adjoint
equivalence with identity unit and identity counit --- in fact an
isomorphism of categories. At the level of generating objects, the
McGucken Operator $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$ and the
McGucken Space $\mathcal{M}_G$ are equivalent in McG${}_6$:
$D_M \simeq \mathcal{M}_G$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Following the four-step structure of
Theorem [13.1](#thm:adj-geometric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:adj-geometric"}. The equivalence is forced by
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, the physical, geometric fact that the fourth
dimension expands at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric
manner): the McGucken Operator $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$
and the McGucken Space $\mathcal{M}_G$ (with constraint
$\Phi_M = x_4 - ict$) are simultaneous outputs of the axiom via
differentiation and integration respectively, with $x_4 = ict$ the
integrated kinematic shadow per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}.

**Step 1: Functors.** Let $\mathbf{Op}$ denote the category whose
objects are McGucken Operators $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$
on a generic carrier (morphisms preserve the chain-rule structure); let
$\mathbf{StrSp}$ denote the category of McGucken Spaces
$\mathcal{M}_G = (E_4, \Phi_M, D_M, \Sigma_M)$ (morphisms preserve
carrier, constraint, operator, and Sphere-bundle).

*OpCons:* Given $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$, define
$$\mathrm{OpCons}(D_M) := (E_4, \Phi_M, D_M, \Sigma_M),$$ by attaching:
(a) the minimal carrier $E_4 = \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{C}$ (the
smallest space on which $\partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$ acts
naturally, with $x_4 \in \mathbb{C}$ tracking the imaginary expansion);
(b) the constraint $\Phi_M: E_4 \to \mathbb{C}$ defined by
$\Phi_M(\mathbf{x}, t) = x_4 - ict$, whose $t$-derivative is
$dx_4/dt - ic = 0$ (the mere integrated kinematic shadow of the dynamical principle per Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref" reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}); (c) the
$\Sigma_M$-bundle assembled at each event.

*CarExt:* Given $\mathcal{M}_G$, define
$\mathrm{CarExt}(\mathcal{M}_G) := D_M$ (the operator component of the
tuple).

**Step 2: The unit $\eta$ is the identity.** For any
$D_M \in \mathbf{Op}$, the composite
$\mathrm{CarExt} \circ \mathrm{OpCons}$ acts by
$\mathrm{CarExt}(\mathrm{OpCons}(D_M)) = D_M$, since
$\mathrm{OpCons}(D_M)$ has $D_M$ as its operator component by
construction. Therefore
$\mathrm{CarExt} \circ \mathrm{OpCons} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{Op}}$ as a
functor, and
$\eta = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{CarExt} \circ \mathrm{OpCons}}$ is the
identity natural transformation.

**Step 3: The counit $\varepsilon$ is the identity.** For any
$\mathcal{M}_G$, compute $\mathrm{CarExt}(\mathcal{M}_G) = D_M$, so
$\mathrm{OpCons}(\mathrm{CarExt}(\mathcal{M}_G)) = \mathrm{OpCons}(D_M) = (E_4', \Phi_M', D_M, \Sigma_M')$.
We verify $E_4' = E_4$, $\Phi_M' = \Phi_M$, $\Sigma_M' = \Sigma_M$:

-   $E_4' = E_4$ by definition: the carrier of $\mathcal{M}_G$ is
    $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{C}$ (same as $E_4'$).

-   $\Phi_M' = \Phi_M$: the choice $\Phi_M = x_4 - ict$ is forced up to
    additive constant by the requirement $D_M\,\Phi_M = 0$ along
    axiom-curves (kernel computation:
    $(\partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4})(x_4 - ict) = -ic + ic = 0$).

-   $\Sigma_M' = \Sigma_M$: the Sphere-bundle is uniquely determined by
    the McGucken Axiom and depends only on $D_M$ via its coefficient
    $ic$.

Hence
$\mathrm{OpCons} \circ \mathrm{CarExt} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{StrSp}}$
as a functor, and
$\varepsilon = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{OpCons} \circ \mathrm{CarExt}}$ is
the identity natural transformation.

**Step 4: Isomorphism of categories.** Steps 2 and 3 establish that
$\mathrm{CarExt} \circ \mathrm{OpCons} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{Op}}$ and
$\mathrm{OpCons} \circ \mathrm{CarExt} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{StrSp}}$
on the nose. By the argument of
Theorem [13.1](#thm:adj-geometric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:adj-geometric"} Step 4, the pair
$(\mathrm{OpCons}, \mathrm{CarExt})$ is an isomorphism of categories,
hence in particular an equivalence with identity unit and identity
counit. The triangle identities are trivially satisfied. The McGucken
Operator $D_M$ and the McGucken Space $\mathcal{M}_G$ are the same
object viewed through two functorial windows. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:co-generation .remark}
*Remark 13.4* (Joint derivation Theorem from the operator/space
equivalence). The identity-equivalence $D_M \simeq \mathcal{M}_G$ has
the deeper content that $\mathcal{M}_G$ and $D_M$ are
simultaneous outputs of the McGucken Axiom: integration with convention
$\kappa$ produces the constraint surface, and differentiation along the
integral flow produces the derivation operator. This is the feature that distinguishes the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework from every prior
axiomatic foundation of mathematical physics (Hilbert's Grundlagen,
Stone--von Neumann, Connes' spectral triple, the Wightman axioms), each
of which takes arena and operator as independent inputs.
:::

::: {#thm:adj-principle .theorem}
**Theorem 13.5** (Invariance/dynamics Noether equivalence;
[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Theorem 3.3). *The symmetry-to-action and
action-to-symmetry functors between McGucken Symmetry packages and
McGucken Action functionals constitute an *equivalence of categories*
$$\mathrm{SymToAct}: \mathbf{SymGrp} \;\xrightarrow{\;\simeq\;}\; \mathbf{ActFn} \;:\; \mathrm{ActToSym},$$
with
$\mathrm{ActToSym} \circ \mathrm{SymToAct} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{SymGrp}}$
and
$\mathrm{SymToAct} \circ \mathrm{ActToSym} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{ActFn}}$,
where the equalities follow from the four-fold uniqueness theorem
(Theorem [12.2](#thm:four-fold-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:four-fold-uniqueness"}, the unique
$\mathcal{S}_M$-invariant Lagrangian). The pair
$(\mathrm{SymToAct}, \mathrm{ActToSym})$ is therefore an adjoint
equivalence with identity unit and identity counit. At the level of
generating objects, the McGucken Symmetry package $\mathcal{S}_M$ and
the McGucken Action functional $\mathcal{A}_M$ are equivalent in
McG${}_6$: $\mathcal{S}_M \simeq \mathcal{A}_M$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The functors rely on the four-fold uniqueness theorem
(Theorem [12.2](#thm:four-fold-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:four-fold-uniqueness"} of
Chapter [12](#ch:lagrangian-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:lagrangian-uniqueness"}; [@MG-Lagrangian-2026]) and
Noether's theorem. The equivalence is the categorical statement of the
bijective correspondence between symmetry groups and their unique
invariant actions, in the present case strict (identity unit and counit)
because each $\mathcal{S}_M$ has a unique invariant $\mathcal{A}_M$ and
each $\mathcal{A}_M$ has a unique maximal Noether symmetry.

**Step 1: Functors.** Let $\mathbf{SymGrp}$ denote the category whose
objects are McGucken Symmetry packages $\mathcal{S}_M$ (the
McGucken-Klein pair $(\mathrm{ISO}(1,3), \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3))$ together
with internal-gauge lifts $U(1) \times SU(2)_L \times SU(3)_c$); let
$\mathbf{ActFn}$ denote the category of McGucken Action functionals
$\mathcal{A}_M = \int \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McG}}\,d^4x$.

*SymToAct:* Given $\mathcal{S}_M$, construct the unique
$\mathcal{S}_M$-invariant Lagrangian density
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McG}} = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{kin}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Dirac}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{YM}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{EH (Einstein--Hilbert)}}$
up to total derivative (the four-fold uniqueness theorem establishes
existence and uniqueness, see [@MG-Lagrangian-2026] §19.3). Integrate to
obtain $\mathrm{SymToAct}(\mathcal{S}_M) := \mathcal{A}_M$.

*ActToSym:* Given $\mathcal{A}_M$, extract the maximal symmetry group
leaving $\mathcal{A}_M$ invariant up to total derivative (the Noether
symmetry). For $\mathcal{A}_M$ with the four-sector structure, this
maximal group is exactly the McGucken-Klein pair extended by the
Standard-Model internal-gauge group, i.e., $\mathcal{S}_M$ itself.

**Step 2: The unit $\eta$ is the identity.** For any
$\mathcal{S}_M \in \mathbf{SymGrp}$, compute
$\mathrm{SymToAct}(\mathcal{S}_M) = \mathcal{A}_M$ (the unique
$\mathcal{S}_M$-invariant action, by the four-fold uniqueness theorem),
and $\mathrm{ActToSym}(\mathcal{A}_M)$ is the maximal Noether symmetry
of this action. By the four-fold uniqueness theorem, this maximal
symmetry is exactly $\mathcal{S}_M$: any larger group would generate a
Lagrangian invariant under a strictly larger group, contradicting
uniqueness. Hence
$\mathrm{ActToSym} \circ \mathrm{SymToAct} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{SymGrp}}$
as a functor, and
$\eta = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{ActToSym} \circ \mathrm{SymToAct}}$ is the
identity natural transformation.

**Step 3: The counit $\varepsilon$ is the identity.** For any
$\mathcal{A}_M \in \mathbf{ActFn}$, compute
$\mathrm{ActToSym}(\mathcal{A}_M) = \mathcal{S}_M$ (the maximal Noether
symmetry), then $\mathrm{SymToAct}(\mathcal{S}_M) =$ the unique
$\mathcal{S}_M$-invariant action $= \mathcal{A}_M$ (the four-fold
uniqueness theorem applied in the reverse direction). Hence
$\mathrm{SymToAct} \circ \mathrm{ActToSym} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{ActFn}}$
as a functor, and
$\varepsilon = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{SymToAct} \circ \mathrm{ActToSym}}$
is the identity natural transformation.

**Step 4: Isomorphism of categories.** Steps 2 and 3 establish that
$\mathrm{ActToSym} \circ \mathrm{SymToAct} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{SymGrp}}$
and
$\mathrm{SymToAct} \circ \mathrm{ActToSym} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{ActFn}}$
on the nose. By the argument of
Theorem [13.1](#thm:adj-geometric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:adj-geometric"} Step 4, the pair
$(\mathrm{SymToAct}, \mathrm{ActToSym})$ is an isomorphism of
categories, hence in particular an equivalence with identity unit and
identity counit. The McGucken Symmetry package $\mathcal{S}_M$ and the
McGucken Action functional $\mathcal{A}_M$ are the same object viewed through two functorial windows --- the categorical
statement of the Noether duality between symmetries and dynamics. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:three-ingredients .remark}
*Remark 13.6* (The three equivalences match the three ingredients of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The three distinguished
equivalences of McG${}_6$ correspond exactly to the three ingredients of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$:

-   $\Sigma_M \dashv \mathcal{G}_M$ (geometric pair): atom/global on the
    *coordinate-pair* ingredient $I_1$.

-   $D_M \dashv \mathcal{M}_G$ (dynamical pair): operator/space on the
    *differential* ingredient $I_2$.

-   $\mathcal{S}_M \dashv \mathcal{A}_M$ (principle pair):
    symmetry/action on the *content/invariant* ingredient $I_3$.

The other twelve pair-relations among the 15 unordered pairs (e.g.,
$\Sigma_M \leftrightarrow D_M$,
$\Sigma_M \leftrightarrow \mathcal{S}_M$) factor through the
source-axiom point. The number of distinguished equivalences --- three
--- is therefore forced by the number of ingredients of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.
:::

### The three categorical theorems characterising McG${}_6$: MCC${}_6$, RGC${}_6$, CGE${}_6$ {#sec:three-theorems-six-objects}

The three categorical theorems generalise the pair-level theorems MCC,
RGC, CGE of Ch. [17](#ch:nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:nonlocality"} to all six objects of the Source-Tuple. We
give the full proofs (transcribed from [@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] §4,
which itself imports the technical core from [@MG-Hilbert6-2026] §5).

::: {#thm:mcc-six .theorem}
**Theorem 13.7** (MCC${}_6$ --- Generalised Mutual Containment;
[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Theorem 4.1). *For every object
$X \in \mathcal{F}_M$, there exists a canonical extraction procedure
$$\Pi_X: X \longrightarrow (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)$$ that recovers the
McGucken Axiom in full from $X$ alone, using only standard mathematical
operations (differentiation, integration, level-set extraction, kernel
computation, group-invariance identification, ratio extraction,
action-stationarity).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We construct $\Pi_X$ for each of the six objects of
$\mathcal{F}_M$.

**Case $X = \Sigma_M$.** Let $p \in M^{1,3}$ be any event,
$\Sigma_M^+(p)$ the McGucken Sphere at $p$. The wavefront radius is
$r(t) = c(t - t_p)$; the perpendicular $x_4$-displacement is
$x_4(t) - x_4(t_p) = ic(t - t_p)$ (since $x_4$ evolves at rate $ic$,
with $i$ marking perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial
dimensions). Define
$$\Pi_{\Sigma_M}: \Sigma_M^+(p) \mapsto \lim_{t \to t_p^+}\frac{x_4(t) - x_4(t_p)}{t - t_p} = ic.$$
This extraction uses standard differentiation, is well-defined at every
event by translation-equivariance, and recovers
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

**Case $X = \mathcal{G}_M$.** The Moving-Dimension Manifold
$\mathcal{G}_M = (M, \mathcal{F}, V, \Sigma_M)$ carries a privileged
vector field $V$ flowing at rate $ic$ along $x_4$ at every leaf of the
foliation. Define
$$\Pi_{\mathcal{G}_M}: \mathcal{G}_M \mapsto (\text{rate of $V$-flow projected onto } x_4) = ic.$$
Equivalently, apply $\Pi_{\Sigma_M}$ pointwise on the $\Sigma_M$-bundle
and obtain the same result at every event. Either route uses standard
vector-field-evaluation operations and recovers
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

**Case $X = \mathcal{M}_G$.** The McGucken Space carries the constraint
$\Phi_M: E_4 \to \mathbb{C}$, $\Phi_M(\mathbf{x}, t) = x_4 - ict$. The
level set $\Phi_M = 0$ is the relation $x_4 = ict$. Define
$$\Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}: \mathcal{M}_G \mapsto (\text{level set } \Phi_M = 0) \mapsto \frac{d}{dt}(x_4 = ict) \mapsto (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic).$$
The extraction uses standard level-set extraction followed by
differentiation.

**Case $X = D_M$.** The McGucken Operator
$D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$ is determined by its
coefficients. Define
$$\Pi_{D_M}: D_M \mapsto (\text{ratio of $x_4$-coefficient to $t$-coefficient}) = ic/1 = ic.$$
Equivalently, setting $D_M\Phi = 0$ along an axiom-curve gives
$\partial_t\Phi + ic\,\partial_{x_4}\Phi = 0$; chain-rule expansion
gives $dx_4/dt \cdot \partial_{x_4}\Phi = -\partial_t\Phi$, hence
$dx_4/dt = ic$ is identified as the rate along which $\Phi$ is constant.
Standard coefficient extraction and kernel computation.

**Case $X = \mathcal{S}_M$.** The McGucken Symmetry $\mathcal{S}_M$ is
the assertion $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ treated as a commitment, together with its descent-package: the Lorentzian metric
signature generated via $i^2 = -1$, and the Klein pair
$(\mathrm{ISO}(1,3), \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3))$ as canonical invariance group.
By [@MG-Lagrangian-2026] Lemma 7, $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ combined with
the Euclidean form $d\ell^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2$ yields
$$dx_4^2 = (ic\,dt)^2 = -c^2\,dt^2, \quad \text{hence} \quad ds^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2\,dt^2,$$
which is the Minkowski interval. The invariance group of this interval
on flat four-manifold is the Poincaré group $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$ with
Lorentz stabiliser $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ ([@MG-Lagrangian-2026] Lemma 8).
The extraction
$\Pi_{\mathcal{S}_M}: \mathcal{S}_M \mapsto (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)$
reads the defining condition off the commitment of
$\mathcal{S}_M$: any $g \in \mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$ preserves the Minkowski
interval iff it preserves the relation $dx_4 = ic\,dt$ (since the
interval is generated from $d\ell^2$ by this substitution). Standard
group-invariance identification. By [@MG-Lagrangian-2026] Theorem 26
(uniqueness), $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the unique minimal physical
postulate whose Kleinian invariance package is $\mathcal{S}_M$.

**Case $X = \mathcal{A}_M$.** The McGucken Action
$\mathcal{A}_M = \int_M \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McG}}\,d^4x$ has
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ containing the kinetic sector
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{kin}} = \tfrac{1}{2}(D_M\Psi)^*(D_M\Psi)$. We
extract $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ from $\mathcal{A}_M$ via two routes
that agree by the universal three-step factorisation
(Lemma [13.11](#lem:three-step-factorisation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:three-step-factorisation"} below).

*Route 1 (Euler--Lagrange descent).* The stationarity condition
$\delta\mathcal{A}_M = 0$ in the kinetic sector yields the
Euler--Lagrange equation $D_M^*(D_M\Psi) = 0$ along free trajectories.
This factors through $D_M\Psi = 0$ and hence through
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ by Case $X = D_M$.

*Route 2 (Noether descent).* By Noether's first theorem
([@MG-Lagrangian-2026] Lemma 11), every continuous symmetry of
$\mathcal{A}_M$ generates a conserved current. The Poincaré-invariance
of $\mathcal{A}_M$ (forced by $\mathcal{S}_M$-invariance, Case
$X = \mathcal{S}_M$) produces the stress-energy tensor $T^{\mu\nu}$ for
spacetime translations and the angular-momentum tensor for spatial
rotations and Lorentz boosts. The translation invariance along the
$x_4$-direction produces a conserved current whose $\mu = 4$ component
encodes $dx_4/dt = ic$.

Define
$$\Pi_{\mathcal{A}_M}: \mathcal{A}_M \mapsto (\text{kinetic stationarity}) \mapsto (D_M\Psi = 0) \mapsto (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic).$$
By Lemma [13.11](#lem:three-step-factorisation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:three-step-factorisation"}, the two routes agree on the
axiom-content. By the four-fold uniqueness theorem of
[@MG-Lagrangian-2026] §19.3, $\mathcal{A}_M$ with kinetic sector
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{kin}} = \tfrac{1}{2}(D_M\Psi)^*(D_M\Psi)$ is the
unique $\mathcal{S}_M$-invariant action on $\mathcal{M}_G$ (up to total
derivative). The extraction is canonical.

In each of the six cases, $\Pi_X$ uses only operations from the standard
mathematical catalogue and recovers $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in full.
Therefore MCC${}_6$ holds. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:rgc-six .theorem}
**Theorem 13.8** (RGC${}_6$ --- Reciprocal Generation Capability;
[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Theorem 4.2). *For every ordered pair
$(X, Y) \in \mathcal{F}_M \times \mathcal{F}_M$ with $X \neq Y$, there
exists a canonical generation procedure
$$\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_Y \circ \Pi_X: X \longrightarrow Y,$$ where
$\Pi_X$ is the extraction of
Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"} and $C_Y$ is the construction rule for $Y$. The
30 such procedures form a codiscrete groupoid on the six objects of
$\mathcal{F}_M$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). We proceed in four parts: (1) existence of $\Gamma_{X \to Y}$,
(2) Round-Trip Lemma, (3) verification of groupoid axioms, (4)
Path-Independence.

**Step 1: Existence.** Fix an ordered pair $(X, Y)$ with $X \neq Y$. By
Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"}, $\Pi_X: X \to (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)$
exists. The construction rule $C_Y: (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic) \to Y$
exists for every $Y \in \mathcal{F}_M$ with the six explicit
constructions:

-   $C_{\Sigma_M}$: integrate $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ forward from each
    event $p$ to form $\Sigma_M^+(p)$.

-   $C_{\mathcal{G}_M}$: assemble the $\Sigma_M$-bundle over all events;
    attach $V$ with $dx_4(V)/dt = ic$; equip with foliation
    $\mathcal{F}$; obtain $\mathcal{G}_M$.

-   $C_{\mathcal{M}_G}$: form carrier
    $E_4 = \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{C}$; impose constraint
    $\Phi_M = x_4 - ict$; attach $D_M$ and $\Sigma_M$.

-   $C_{D_M}$: form the chain-rule operator
    $\partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$ along axiom-curves.

-   $C_{\mathcal{S}_M}$: form $\mathrm{Inv}(\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)$,
    the group of transformations preserving the axiom.

-   $C_{\mathcal{A}_M}$: form the unique $\mathcal{S}_M$-invariant
    Lagrangian and integrate.

The composition $\Gamma_{X \to Y} := C_Y \circ \Pi_X$ is a well-defined
morphism. There are $6 \times 5 = 30$ ordered pairs with $X \neq Y$,
hence 30 generation procedures.

**Step 2: Round-Trip Lemma.** The technical fact underlying the groupoid
structure is Lemma [13.9](#lem:round-trip-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:round-trip-identity"} below:
$\Pi_Y \circ C_Y = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}}$ for every $Y$.

**Step 3: Groupoid axioms.** We verify the four axioms of a groupoid for
$\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{F}_M) = (\mathcal{F}_M, \{\Gamma_{X \to Y}\})$.

*(i) Identity.* For each $X \in \mathcal{F}_M$, set
$\Gamma_{X \to X} := \mathrm{id}_X$.

*(ii) Composition (closure).* For $X, Y, Z \in \mathcal{F}_M$:
$$\Gamma_{Y \to Z} \circ \Gamma_{X \to Y} = (C_Z \circ \Pi_Y) \circ (C_Y \circ \Pi_X) = C_Z \circ (\Pi_Y \circ C_Y) \circ \Pi_X.$$
By Lemma [13.9](#lem:round-trip-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:round-trip-identity"},
$\Pi_Y \circ C_Y = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}}$. Therefore
$$\Gamma_{Y \to Z} \circ \Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_Z \circ \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}} \circ \Pi_X = C_Z \circ \Pi_X = \Gamma_{X \to Z}.$$
The composition lies in $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{F}_M)$.

*(iii) Associativity.*
$(\Gamma_{Z \to W} \circ \Gamma_{Y \to Z}) \circ \Gamma_{X \to Y} = \Gamma_{Z \to W} \circ (\Gamma_{Y \to Z} \circ \Gamma_{X \to Y})$
follows from associativity of function composition applied to the
sextuple composition
$C_W \circ \Pi_Z \circ C_Z \circ \Pi_Y \circ C_Y \circ \Pi_X$.

*(iv) Inverses.* For each $(X, Y)$ with $X \neq Y$, define
$\Gamma_{X \to Y}^{-1} := \Gamma_{Y \to X} = C_X \circ \Pi_Y$. Then
$$\Gamma_{Y \to X} \circ \Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_X \circ \Pi_Y \circ C_Y \circ \Pi_X = C_X \circ \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}} \circ \Pi_X = C_X \circ \Pi_X.$$
By the dual of
Lemma [13.9](#lem:round-trip-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:round-trip-identity"} (which holds symmetrically),
$C_X \circ \Pi_X = \mathrm{id}_X$ up to canonical isomorphism. Therefore
$\Gamma_{Y \to X} \circ \Gamma_{X \to Y} = \mathrm{id}_X$; symmetrically
$\Gamma_{X \to Y} \circ \Gamma_{Y \to X} = \mathrm{id}_Y$. Inverses
exist.

The four axioms hold; $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{F}_M)$ is a groupoid.
Codiscreteness: the morphism $\Gamma_{X \to Y}$ is unique between any
two objects (canonical $\Pi_X$ and canonical $C_Y$). Therefore
$\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{F}_M)$ is codiscrete.

**Step 4: Path-Independence.** For any $X, Y, Z \in \mathcal{F}_M$
distinct, Part 3(ii) gave
$\Gamma_{Y \to Z} \circ \Gamma_{X \to Y} = \Gamma_{X \to Z}$. The direct
route $X \to Z$ and the indirect route $X \to Y \to Z$ coincide on the
axiom-content. By repeated application, any sequence of intermediate
objects collapses to the direct route $C_Z \circ \Pi_X$. ◻
:::

::: {#lem:round-trip-identity .lemma}
**Lemma 13.9** (Round-Trip Identity; [@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Lemma
4.2.1). *For every $Y \in \mathcal{F}_M$, the composition
$\Pi_Y \circ C_Y: (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic) \to (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)$
is the identity on the axiom-content.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We verify $\Pi_Y \circ C_Y = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}}$ for
each $Y \in \mathcal{F}_M$ by direct computation, in six steps. In every case, the round trip recovers the axiom-content
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ --- the physical, geometric fact that the
fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light $c$ in a
spherically symmetric manner
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}). The integrated kinematic shadow $x_4 = ict$
(Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is recovered as the kinematic shadow
of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in the cases where the construction passes
through an integrated formulation.

**Step 1: $Y = \Sigma_M$ (the McGucken Sphere) round trip.**
$C_{\Sigma_M}(\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)$ integrates the axiom from
$p \in M_{G}$, producing $\Sigma_M^+(p) = M^{+}_{p}(t)$ with
$x_{4}$-displacement $x_{4}(t) - x_{4}(t_p) = ic(t - t_p)$ (the mere integrated kinematic shadow per Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}). $\Pi_{\Sigma_M}$ differentiates
with respect to $t$:
$\lim_{t \to t_p^+}[x_{4}(t) - x_{4}(t_p)]/(t - t_p) = ic$. The
composition recovers $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. ✓

**Step 2: $Y = \mathcal{G}_M$ (the moving-dimension manifold) round
trip.** $C_{\mathcal{G}_M}$ attaches at every event $p \in M_{G}$ a
tangent vector $V$ with $dx_{4}(V)/dt = ic$, satisfying
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (v) (global validity).
$\Pi_{\mathcal{G}_M}$ evaluates $V$'s $x_{4}$-rate at any event: $ic$.
The composition recovers $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. ✓

**Step 3: $Y = \mathcal{M}_G$ (the McGucken Space) round trip.**
$C_{\mathcal{M}_G}$ imposes the constraint
$\Phi_M(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_{4}, t) = x_{4}- ict = 0$ on the auxiliary
Euclidean five-tuple space
(cf. Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"} Step 2 construction of $\Sigma$).
$\Pi_{\mathcal{M}_G}$ extracts the level set $\Phi_M = 0$ (i.e.,
$x_{4}= ict$) and differentiates: $dx_{4}/dt = ic$. The composition
recovers $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. ✓ Note: the integrated kinematic shadow
$x_{4}= ict$ is here serving as the constraint-surface encoding of the
underlying dynamical principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.

**Step 4: $Y = D_M$ (the McGucken Operator) round trip.** $C_{D_M}$
writes the McGucken differential operator
$D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_{4}}$ on the McGucken Space,
encoding the axiom in the coefficient. $\Pi_{D_M}$ reads the coefficient
of $\partial_{x_{4}}$: $ic$. The composition recovers
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. ✓

**Step 5: $Y = \mathcal{S}_M$ (the McGucken Symmetry) round trip.**
$C_{\mathcal{S}_M}$ forms $\mathrm{Inv}(\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)$, the
invariance group of the axiom (the proper orthochronous Lorentz group
$SO^+(1,3)$ from Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv), derived at Theorem 4.6, Lorentz consistency).
$\Pi_{\mathcal{S}_M}$ reads the defining invariance condition off any
element of the group: $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The composition is
exactly the identity on the axiom-content. ✓

**Step 6: $Y = \mathcal{A}_M$ (the McGucken Action) round trip.**
$C_{\mathcal{A}_M}$ builds the McGucken Lagrangian
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ with kinetic sector
$\tfrac{1}{2}(D_M\Psi)^*(D_M\Psi)$, then forms the action
$\mathcal{A}_M = \int \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McG}}\,d^4x$ on $M_{G}$.
$\Pi_{\mathcal{A}_M}$ applies action stationarity
($\delta\mathcal{A}_M = 0$), yielding the Euler--Lagrange equation
$D_M^*(D_M\Psi) = 0$, which factors through $D_M\Psi = 0$ along free
trajectories (the McGucken-Klein--Gordon equation, by
Theorem [8.1](#thm:QMT8){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT8"} of
[@MG-Lagrangian-2026]); applying $\Pi_{D_M}$ to $D_M\Psi = 0$ then
recovers $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The composition recovers the axiom
through the action--Euler-Lagrange--operator chain. ✓

**Closure: identity on axiom-content across all six categories.** In
each of the six cases, the construction-extraction round trip yields
back exactly the axiom-content $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The dynamical
content of the principle (the active expansion of the fourth dimension
at rate $c$ in a spherically symmetric manner, per
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)--(ii)) is preserved by every
$C_Y$ and recovered by every $\Pi_Y$. Therefore
$\Pi_Y \circ C_Y = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}}$ for all
$Y \in \mathcal{F}_M$. The integrated kinematic shadow $x_4 = ict$ appears in Steps
1 and 3 as the kinematic shadow of the dynamical principle, recovered
upon differentiation back to $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#thm:cge-six .theorem}
**Theorem 13.10** (CGE${}_6$ --- Containment-Generation Equivalence;
[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Theorem 4.3). *For every
$X \in \mathcal{F}_M$,
$$X\ \text{contains}\ (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)\ \text{in full} \;\iff\; X\ \text{generates every other}\ Y \in \mathcal{F}_M.$$*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We prove the biconditional in both directions, then unpack its
meaning.

**($\Rightarrow$) Containment forces generation.** Suppose $X$ contains
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in full, i.e., the extraction
$\Pi_X: X \to (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)$ exists by
Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"} (MCC${}_6$). Fix any $Y \in \mathcal{F}_M$ with
$Y \neq X$. By the construction rules of Part 1 of the proof of
Theorem [13.8](#thm:rgc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:rgc-six"}, the morphism
$C_Y: (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic) \to Y$ exists explicitly:

-   $C_{\Sigma_M}$: construct the McGucken Sphere from the axiom by
    spherical $x_{4}$-expansion at rate $ic$;

-   $C_{\mathcal{G}_M}$: construct the moving-dimension manifold by
    integrating the principle at every spacetime point;

-   $C_{\mathcal{M}_G}$: construct the McGucken Space by imposing the
    constraint $x_4 = ict$ on $E_4$;

-   $C_{D_M}$: construct the McGucken Operator
    $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$ directly;

-   $C_{\mathcal{S}_M}$: construct the McGucken Symmetry as the
    invariance group of the axiom;

-   $C_{\mathcal{A}_M}$: construct the McGucken Action as the
    four-volume integral of the McGucken Lagrangian.

Define the canonical generation procedure
$$\Gamma_{X \to Y} := C_Y \circ \Pi_X: X \to (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic) \to Y.$$
This is a well-defined morphism in the categorical structure of
$\mathrm{McG}_6$. Since $Y$ was arbitrary, $X$ generates every other
member of $\mathcal{F}_M$, establishing the forward direction.

**($\Leftarrow$) Generation forces containment.** Suppose $X$ generates
every other $Y \in \mathcal{F}_M$, i.e., canonical procedures
$\Gamma_{X \to Y}: X \to Y$ exist for each $Y \neq X$. By
Lemma [13.11](#lem:three-step-factorisation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:three-step-factorisation"} (Universal Three-Step
Factorisation), each $\Gamma_{X \to Y}$ factors uniquely as
$$\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_Y \circ \Pi_X,$$ through the axiom
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The factorisation requires the existence of
$\Pi_X: X \to (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)$ as the unique intermediary.
Therefore $\Pi_X$ exists, and by
Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"} (MCC${}_6$), $X$ contains
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in full. This establishes the reverse
direction.

**Step 3: The biconditional applies to every $X$.** The argument is
independent of which $X \in \mathcal{F}_M$ is chosen: the construction
rules $C_Y$ from the axiom are universal, and the factorisation Lemma
applies to every source $X$. Therefore the biconditional holds for every
$X \in \mathcal{F}_M$ --- containment-of-axiom and generation-of-others
are the same property in two articulations.

**Step 4: Meaning --- CGE${}_6$ as the keystone.**
Theorem [13.10](#thm:cge-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:cge-six"} establishes that MCC${}_6$ and RGC${}_6$ are
not two independent characterisations of $\mathrm{McG}_6$ but two
articulations of the same fact: the McGucken Axiom is the
obligatory intermediary through which every relation between members of
$\mathcal{F}_M$ passes. The unary property (containment-of-axiom,
MCC${}_6$) and the binary property (generation-of-others, RGC${}_6$) are
equivalent precisely because every generation factors through the
axiom-extraction step
(Lemma [13.11](#lem:three-step-factorisation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:three-step-factorisation"}).

**Step 5: The "=" as "$\Leftrightarrow$".** CGE${}_6$ can be summarised
in a one-line categorical identity: the "$=$" of the axiom
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ acts categorically as the "$\Leftrightarrow$"
of MCC${}_6$ $\Leftrightarrow$ RGC${}_6$. The framework cannot be
weakened on one side without weakening the other: any failure of
containment at $X$ would force a failure of generation from $X$ (via the
missing intermediary), and conversely. The rigidity of
$\mathrm{McG}_6$ is the operational content of the axiom's centrality.

**Step 6: Categorical no-weakening principle.** As a corollary,
CGE${}_6$ implies the no-weakening principle: any attempt to add a new
object to $\mathcal{F}_M$ that contains the axiom but does not generate
the existing members (or vice versa) is impossible. The
Source-Tuple
$\mathcal{F}_M = (\Sigma_M, \mathcal{G}_M, \mathcal{M}_G, D_M, \mathcal{S}_M, \mathcal{A}_M)$
is closed under the biconditional; no seventh object can be added
without violating either MCC${}_6$ or RGC${}_6$. This is the categorical
foundation of the no-seventh-primitive theorem
(cf. Chapter [12](#ch:lagrangian-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:lagrangian-uniqueness"}). ◻
:::

::: {#lem:three-step-factorisation .lemma}
**Lemma 13.11** (Universal Three-Step Factorisation;
[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Lemma 4.3.1). *Every canonical generation
procedure $\Gamma_{X \to Y}$ between members of $\mathcal{F}_M$ factors
uniquely as $$\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_Y \circ \Pi_X.$$*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: Recall the round-trip identity.** By
Lemma [13.9](#lem:round-trip-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:round-trip-identity"}, the construction rule $C_Y$ is a
section of the extraction $\Pi_Y$ in the categorical sense
$$\Pi_Y \circ C_Y = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}},$$ where
$\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}}$ is the identity morphism on the axiom
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (the principle as a fixed object in the
categorical structure). Equivalently, constructing $Y$ from the axiom
and then extracting the axiom back recovers the axiom unchanged.

**Step 2: Existence --- every generation procedure factors through the
axiom.** Suppose $\Gamma_{X \to Y}: X \to Y$ is a canonical generation
procedure between members $X, Y \in \mathcal{F}_M$. By the universal
property of construction-from-axiom (the defining property of the
construction rules $C_Y$: every morphism into $Y$ from any
source-bearing object factors through the axiom via $C_Y$), there exists
a unique morphism
$$\alpha: (\text{source-content of } X) \to (\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic)$$
such that $\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_Y \circ \alpha$. By the universal
property of axiom-extraction (the defining property of the extraction
$\Pi_X$: every morphism from $X$ to the axiom factors through $\Pi_X$),
the unique such $\alpha$ is $\Pi_X$. Therefore the canonical generation
procedure factors as $$\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_Y \circ \Pi_X,$$ the
composition extract-axiom-then-construct-target.

**Step 3: Uniqueness --- the factorisation is unique.** Suppose
$\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_Y \circ \Pi'_X = C_Y \circ \Pi_X$ for two
extractions $\Pi'_X, \Pi_X$. Apply $\Pi_Y$ from the left to both sides:
$$\Pi_Y \circ C_Y \circ \Pi'_X = \Pi_Y \circ C_Y \circ \Pi_X.$$ By the
round-trip identity (Step 1),
$\Pi_Y \circ C_Y = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}}$, so
$$\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}} \circ \Pi'_X = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{axiom}} \circ \Pi_X,$$
equivalently $\Pi'_X = \Pi_X$. The factorisation is unique.

**Step 4: Meaning.** The factorisation Lemma states that
every canonical generation procedure between members of $\mathcal{F}_M$
is a three-step process:

-   Step (a): extract the McGucken Axiom from the source $X$ via
    $\Pi_X$;

-   Step (b): the axiom $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the obligatory
    intermediary;

-   Step (c): construct the target $Y$ from the axiom via $C_Y$.

The axiom is therefore the obligatory intermediary through which every
generation between members of $\mathcal{F}_M$ must pass. The principle's
centrality is the meaning of the factorisation.

**Step 5: Categorical statement.** In categorical language,
Lemma [13.11](#lem:three-step-factorisation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:three-step-factorisation"} states that the McGucken Axiom
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is an absorbing object in the category of
canonical generations on $\mathcal{F}_M$: every morphism
$\Gamma_{X \to Y}$ in this category factors through the axiom (as an
intermediate object), and the factorisation is unique. This is the
categorical content of the priority of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ over the six objects of the Source-Tuple.

**Step 6: Connection to CGE${}_6$.** The factorisation Lemma is the
technical underpinning of CGE${}_6$
(Theorem [13.10](#thm:cge-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:cge-six"}): mutual containment (MCC${}_6$: every $X$
contains the axiom via $\Pi_X$) and reciprocal generation (RGC${}_6$:
every $X$ generates every $Y$ via $\Gamma_{X \to Y}$) are equivalent
precisely because every generation factors through the axiom-extraction
step. The "$=$" of $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ acts categorically as the
"$\Leftrightarrow$" of CGE${}_6$. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:cge-keystone .remark}
*Remark 13.12* (CGE${}_6$ is the keystone). CGE${}_6$ asserts that
MCC${}_6$ and RGC${}_6$ are the same property in two articulations. The
unary property (containment-of-axiom) and the binary
property (generation-of-others) are equivalent. The framework
cannot be weakened on one side without weakening the other: any failure
of containment at $X$ would force a failure of generation from $X$, and
conversely. The $``="$ of the axiom $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ and the
$``\Leftrightarrow"$ of MCC${}_6$ $\Leftrightarrow$ RGC${}_6$ are the
same identity, written at two levels of organisation.
:::

### The $\Sigma_M$-descent: from the foundational atom to the amplituhedron {#sec:sigma-descent}

By RGC${}_6$ (Theorem [13.8](#thm:rgc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:rgc-six"}), each object of $\mathcal{F}_M$ supports a
descent to a sector of mathematical physics. The descent from $\Sigma_M$
reaches the entire positive-geometry programme: Penrose twistor space,
momentum twistors, McGucken-positive external data, the positive
Grassmannian, BCFW bridges, positroid cells, the amplituhedron map and
canonical form, the loop amplituhedron, Yangian invariance, algebraic
microcausality, and a McGucken-informed gravitational twistor string.
The descent is a 31-theorem constructive chain
([@MG-McGuckenSphereAmplituhedron-2026]); we give the first foundational
stage explicitly as Theorem [13.13](#thm:sigma-cp3){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:sigma-cp3"} below, then summarise the chain.

::: {#thm:sigma-cp3 .theorem}
**Theorem 13.13** (Penrose incidence from $\Sigma_M$;
[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Theorem 6.2). *For each spacetime point
$x \in M^{1,3}$, the null directions of the McGucken Sphere
$\Sigma_M^+(x)$ define a $\mathbb{CP}^1$ line in projective twistor
space; the union of these incidence lines over all $x \in M^{1,3}$
generates $\mathbb{CP}^3$ (with the usual treatment of conformal
infinity).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has four parts: (1) spinor decomposition of spacetime
points, (2) the McGucken Sphere's null-direction structure, (3) Penrose
incidence as a forced consequence of the perpendicularity-marker $i$,
(4) surjectivity onto $\mathbb{CP}^3$.

**Step 1: Spinor decomposition of $x \in M^{1,3}$.** A point $x$ with
coordinates $(t, x_1, x_2, x_3)$ is represented as a $2 \times 2$
Hermitian matrix in spinor notation:
$$x^{AA'} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\begin{pmatrix} ct + x_3 & x_1 - ix_2 \\ x_1 + ix_2 & ct - x_3 \end{pmatrix},$$
with capital indices $A \in \{0, 1\}$ (undotted, left-handed) and
$A' \in \{0', 1'\}$ (dotted, right-handed). The determinant
$\det(x^{AA'}) = \tfrac{1}{2}[(ct)^2 - x_1^2 - x_2^2 - x_3^2] = -\tfrac{1}{2}\eta_{\mu\nu}x^\mu x^\nu$
gives the Lorentzian inner product up to a factor. Null vectors
correspond to $\det(x^{AA'}) = 0$, i.e., rank-1 matrices factorisable as
$x^{AA'} = \pi^A\bar\pi^{A'}$ (Penrose--Rindler [@PenroseRindler1984]
Ch. 3).

**Step 2: Null directions of $\Sigma_M^+(x)$.** By the construction in
Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"}, $\Sigma_M^+(x)$ is the future null cone at
$x$. Its null directions are rays emanating from $x$ along null vectors
$v^{AA'}$ with $\det v^{AA'} = 0$, i.e., $v^{AA'} = \pi^A\bar\pi^{A'}$
for some primed spinor $\bar\pi^{A'}$ (and its conjugate $\pi^A$). The
null directions are parametrised by the projectivised primed spinor
$[\pi_{A'}] \in \mathbb{CP}^1$. The space of such projective primed
spinors is the complex projective line $\mathbb{CP}^1$.

**Step 3: Penrose incidence from the perpendicularity-marker $i$.**
Consider a null ray emanating from $x$ in the direction $\pi_{A'}$. The
twistor $Z^\alpha$ associated with this null ray has components
$(\omega^A, \pi_{A'})$, where $\omega^A$ is the spinor encoding the
ray's spatial offset from the origin of $M^{1,3}$. The Penrose incidence
relation determines $\omega^A$ in terms of $x^{AA'}$ and $\pi_{A'}$:
$$\omega^A = i\,x^{AA'}\,\pi_{A'}.$$

We derive this relation from the McGucken Principle. The axiom
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at $x$ asserts that the perpendicular
$x_4$-coordinate evolves at rate $ic$, with $i$ marking perpendicularity
of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ embeds the time-dimension as the imaginary perpendicular
axis. A null direction at $x$ picks out a generator of $\Sigma_M^+(x)$;
the spinor representation $\omega^A$ of this generator is the
spatial-spinor image of $x$ under the perpendicular-projection
$x \mapsto ix$ (where the $i$ is precisely the McGucken-Axiom $i$).
Composing with $\pi_{A'}$ gives $$\omega^A = i\,x^{AA'}\,\pi_{A'}.$$
*The factor of $i$ on the right-hand side is therefore not an external
convention of twistor theory: it is the $i$ in $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$,
propagated through the spinor decomposition into the twistor incidence
structure.*

Define the twistor
$$Z^\alpha := (\omega^A, \pi_{A'}) = (i\,x^{AA'}\,\pi_{A'},\,\pi_{A'}) \in \mathbb{C}^4 \setminus \{0\}.$$
Under projective rescaling $\pi_{A'} \mapsto r\,\pi_{A'}$
($r \in \mathbb{C}^*$), the twistor scales homogeneously:
$Z^\alpha \mapsto rZ^\alpha$. The projective twistor
$[Z^\alpha] \in \mathbb{CP}^3$ is independent of the choice of
representative. Hence each null direction at $x$ defines a unique point
$[Z^\alpha] \in \mathbb{CP}^3$, and the set of all such points for fixed
$x$ is a projective line $\mathbb{CP}^1$ in $\mathbb{CP}^3$ parametrised
by $[\pi_{A'}] \in \mathbb{CP}^1$.

**Step 4: Surjectivity --- varying $x$ sweeps out $\mathbb{CP}^3$.** Let
$[Z^\alpha] = [(\omega^A, \pi_{A'})] \in \mathbb{CP}^3$ be an arbitrary
twistor with $\pi_{A'} \neq 0$. We solve
$\omega^A = i\,x^{AA'}\,\pi_{A'}$ for $x^{AA'}$ given
$(\omega^A, \pi_{A'})$. For $\pi_{A'} \neq 0$, this linear system has a
2-real-parameter family of solutions $x^{AA'}$ after enforcing the
Hermiticity reality condition from real spacetime points
(Penrose--Rindler [@PenroseRindler1984] Vol. 2, Ch. 6). Therefore the
twistor $[Z^\alpha]$ with $\pi_{A'} \neq 0$ lies on at least one
$\mathbb{CP}^1$ line over some $x \in M^{1,3}_\mathbb{C}$ (or in
$M^{1,3}$ for real Lorentzian twistors satisfying
$Z^\alpha \bar Z_\alpha = 0$).

The boundary case $\pi_{A'} = 0$ corresponds to twistors at conformal
infinity --- the projective line at infinity in $\mathbb{CP}^3$,
representing the conformal compactification of spacetime.

Therefore the union of $\mathbb{CP}^1$ lines over $x \in M^{1,3}$
generates $\mathbb{CP}^3$. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:mcgucken-anchoring-twistor .remark}
*Remark 13.14* (The McGucken anchoring of Penrose's $i$). The factor of
$i$ in the Penrose incidence relation $\omega^A = i\,x^{AA'}\,\pi_{A'}$
has historically been taken as an unmotivated convention of twistor
theory. Theorem [13.13](#thm:sigma-cp3){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:sigma-cp3"} identifies this $i$ as the same $i$ as in
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ --- the perpendicularity marker of $x_4$
relative to the three spatial dimensions, propagated through the spinor
decomposition of Lorentz vectors. The Penrose incidence relation is
therefore not an arbitrary choice but a forced consequence of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the null-cone-projectivisation
construction.

This identification --- case (l) of Theorem 42 of [@MG-Ontic-2026], the
twelve canonical $i$-insertions --- adds the twistor $i$ to the
catalogue of $i$-instances all descending from the single $i$ in
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via the suppression map $\sigma$.
:::

::: {#thm:sigma-descent-chain .theorem}
**Theorem 13.15** (The 31-theorem $\Sigma_M$-descent chain;
[@MG-McGuckenSphereAmplituhedron-2026]). *The $\Sigma_M$-descent from
the McGucken Sphere to the amplituhedron canonical form is a 31-theorem
chain in which each stage is a morphism $C_Y \circ \Pi_X$ in McG${}_6$.
The chain proceeds: $$\boxed{\;
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic \;&\Rightarrow\; \Sigma_M \;\Rightarrow\; \mathbb{CP}^3\ \text{(Penrose twistor space)} \\
&\Rightarrow\; \text{momentum twistors } Z_a \;\Rightarrow\; \text{positive external data}\ M_+(k+4, n) \\
&\Rightarrow\; \text{positive Grassmannian}\ G_+(k, n) \;\Rightarrow\; \text{BCFW bridges, positroid cells} \\
&\Rightarrow\; \text{amplituhedron map}\ Y = CZ \;\Rightarrow\; \text{canonical } d\log \text{ form } \Omega \\
&\Rightarrow\; \text{loop amplituhedron / Yangian invariance / algebraic microcausality} \\
&\Rightarrow\; \text{McGucken-informed gravitational twistor string}.
\end{aligned}\,}$$ The endpoints are: tree-level amplituhedron
[@ArkaniHamedTrnka2014], loop amplituhedron, Yangian invariance,
algebraic microcausality. Every stage is rigorously proved in
[@MG-McGuckenSphereAmplituhedron-2026].*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The construction of
Theorem [13.13](#thm:sigma-cp3){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:sigma-cp3"} is the first stage. Each subsequent stage is
established constructively in [@MG-McGuckenSphereAmplituhedron-2026]; we
summarise the key constructions, with each being a morphism
$C_Y \circ \Pi_X$ in $\mathrm{McG}_6$ between successive intermediate
categories.

**Step 2: (Theorems 8--10 of [@MG-McGuckenSphereAmplituhedron-2026]):
Momentum twistors.** For planar null polygons with ordered vertices
$x_1, \ldots, x_n$, the momentum twistor at vertex $a$ is
$Z_a = (\lambda_a, x_a\lambda_a)$, where $\lambda_a$ is the spinor of
the null edge incident to $a$. These are the natural projective
coordinates for planar arrangements of McGucken Spheres.

**Step 3: (Theorems 11--13): McGucken-positive external configuration
and positive Grassmannian.** The McGucken-positive external
configuration $M_+(k+4, n) \subset G(k+4, n)$ consists of configurations
$Z = (Z_1, \ldots, Z_n)$ for which all consecutive Plücker minors
$(Z_i Z_{i+1} \ldots Z_{i+k+3})$ are positive. Ordered $x_4$-phase
across the external configuration gives McGucken-positive external data.
The positive Grassmannian $G_+(k, n)$ is the image of $M_+(k+4, n)$
under the natural projection.

**Step 4 (Theorems 14--24): BCFW bridges, positroid cells, amplituhedron
map and canonical form.** The Britto--Cachazo--Feng--Witten (BCFW)
recursion is a sequence of factorisations of $G_+(k, n)$ into positroid
cells, each indexed by a permutation of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. The
amplituhedron map
$Y = CZ: G_+(k, n) \times M_+(k+4, n) \to \mathrm{Amp}(n, k)$ assembles
the tree-level amplituhedron. The canonical form $\Omega$ is the unique
$d\log$ top-form on $\mathrm{Amp}(n, k)$ with logarithmic singularities
on its boundary, giving the tree-level $\mathcal{N} = 4$
super-Yang--Mills scattering amplitude as $\Omega$ evaluated on the
boundary configuration.

**Step 5 (Theorems 25--31): Loop amplituhedron, Yangian invariance,
algebraic microcausality, gravitational twistor string.** The loop
amplituhedron generalises the tree-level construction to all-loop
integrands. Yangian invariance is the symmetry inherited from
$\Sigma_M$'s spherical symmetry. Algebraic microcausality is the
Costello--Gwilliam factorisation algebra obtained by sheafifying the
$\Sigma_M$-bundle. The McGucken-informed gravitational twistor string is
the natural extension to $\mathcal{N} = 8$ supergravity. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:amplituhedron-one-descent .remark}
*Remark 13.16* (The amplituhedron is one descent from one object). The
Arkani-Hamed--Trnka 2014 amplituhedron [@ArkaniHamedTrnka2014] is the

By RGC${}_6$, all six descents from $\mathcal{F}_M$ are categorically
equivalent expressions of the same source-axiom. The other five descents
reach where the amplituhedron does not:

-   **The $\mathcal{G}_M$-descent** reaches the Lorentzian four-manifold
    structure, the Schwarzschild metric, the Einstein field equations
    (via the four-sector Lagrangian Euler--Lagrange descent of
    Ch. [12](#ch:lagrangian-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ch:lagrangian-uniqueness"}), the equivalence principle,
    Newton's law of gravity, and cosmological expansion as cosmic
    $x_4$-expansion.

-   **The $\mathcal{M}_G$-descent** reaches the Hilbert space
    $\mathcal{H}$ as $L^2$-completion of $E_4$ under the constraint
    $\Phi_M = 0$, the Born rule from spacetime geometry, the spectral
    theory of self-adjoint operators, and the von Neumann formalism ---
    recovering Ch. [9](#ch:hilbert-theorem){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ch:hilbert-theorem"}.

-   **The $D_M$-descent** reaches the Schrödinger equation
    $i\hbar\,\partial_t\Psi = H\Psi$, the Dirac equation

    $D_M$'s coefficient), the Compton coupling $\omega = mc^2/\hbar$,

    reference="ch:wave-equation"}--[10](#ch:ccr){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ch:ccr"} of Part II.

-   **The $\mathcal{S}_M$-descent** reaches the Klein pair
    $(\mathrm{ISO}(1,3), \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3))$, the gauge symmetries of
    the Standard Model, and the Erlangen Double-Completion.

-   **The $\mathcal{A}_M$-descent** reaches the four-sector Lagrangian
    $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McG}} = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{kin}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Dirac}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{YM}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{EH}}$
    and its Euler--Lagrange field equations --- recovering
    Ch. [12](#ch:lagrangian-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ch:lagrangian-uniqueness"}.

::: {#thm:six-descents-equivalent .theorem}
**Theorem 13.17** (All six descents are categorically equivalent;
[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Theorem 7.27). *By CGE${}_6$
(Theorem [13.10](#thm:cge-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:cge-six"}), all six descents from members of
$\mathcal{F}_M$ are categorically equivalent expressions of the same
source-axiom $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). **Step 1: Apply CGE${}_6$.** By
Theorem [13.10](#thm:cge-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:cge-six"} (CGE${}_6$), for each object
$X \in \mathcal{F}_M$, $X$ contains $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ in full
$\Leftrightarrow$ $X$ generates every other $Y \in \mathcal{F}_M$. Both
directions of the biconditional hold by MCC${}_6$
(Theorem [13.7](#thm:mcc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcc-six"}, which establishes containment for every $X$)
and RGC${}_6$ (Theorem [13.8](#thm:rgc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:rgc-six"}, which establishes generation for every $X$).

**Step 2: Existence of six descents.** For each
$X \in \mathcal{F}_M = \{\Sigma_M, \mathcal{G}_M, \mathcal{M}_G, D_M, \mathcal{S}_M, \mathcal{A}_M\}$,
the canonical generation procedure $\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_Y \circ \Pi_X$
exists for every $Y \neq X$ (Part 1 of the proof of
Theorem [13.8](#thm:rgc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:rgc-six"}, supplying the six explicit construction rules
$C_Y$). Composing through downstream constructions (Hilbert space,
Schrödinger equation, Lorentzian metric, etc.), each $X$ sources a
complete chain reaching the corresponding sector of mathematical
physics.

**Step 3: Path-independence makes the descents equivalent.** By Part 4
of the proof of Theorem [13.8](#thm:rgc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:rgc-six"} (Path-Independence), for any pair of objects
$X, Y \in \mathcal{F}_M$ and any sequence of intermediate objects
$Z_1, Z_2, \ldots, Z_n$ connecting $X$ to $Y$, the iterated generation
procedure $\Gamma_{Z_n \to Y} \circ \cdots \circ \Gamma_{X \to Z_1}$
collapses by the Round-Trip Identity
(Lemma [13.9](#lem:round-trip-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:round-trip-identity"}) to the direct route
$C_Y \circ \Pi_X = \Gamma_{X \to Y}$. The downstream content reached
from $X$ is therefore independent of which intermediate routes through
$\mathcal{F}_M$ are taken.

**Step 4: Categorical equivalence of the six descents.** The six
descents from $\mathcal{F}_M$ produce six categorically equivalent
expressions of the same source-axiom: any sector of mathematical physics
reached by one descent is also reachable by every other descent through
the path-independent generation network. The Hilbert-space formalism
(the $\mathcal{M}_G$-descent), the operator formalism (the
$D_M$-descent), the symmetry-group formalism (the
$\mathcal{S}_M$-descent), the action-principle formalism (the
$\mathcal{A}_M$-descent), the geometric-wavefront formalism (the
$\Sigma_M$-descent), and the spacetime-manifold formalism (the
$\mathcal{G}_M$-descent) are six articulations of one categorical
primitive --- the McGucken Source-Tuple $\mathcal{F}_M$ generated by the
single axiom $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. ◻
:::

### The McGucken Duality $\mathfrak{P} = \mathfrak{P}_A \boxtimes \mathfrak{P}_B$ {#sec:mcgucken-duality}

The textbook's dual-channel architecture is supplied by
[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] §14.17 with its formal categorical
foundation: the McGucken Duality.

::: {#def:mcgucken-duality .definition}
**Definition 13.18** (The McGucken Duality). The McGucken Duality
$\mathfrak{P} = \mathfrak{P}_A \boxtimes \mathfrak{P}_B$ (equivalently,
the $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ Duality, or the McGucken
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ Duality) is the parallel-sibling derivation of a
geometric-propagation channel ($\mathfrak{P}_B$, the
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ **Geometric Channel**, more foundational) and an
algebraic-symmetry channel ($\mathfrak{P}_A$, the
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ **Algebraic Channel**) from the single physical
principle $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ through derivationally disjoint
intermediate machinery:

-   **$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ Geometric Channel** ($\mathfrak{P}_B$,
    group-generates-geometry direction): generates the iterated
    Huygens--McGucken-Sphere propagation, the Feynman path integral,
    the Schrödinger equation in the short-time limit, the strict Second
    Law $dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0$ via the Compton-coupling Brownian
    mechanism, and the entire geometric-propagation content. Henceforth
    abbreviated as the *Geometric Channel*.

-   **$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}=ic$ Algebraic Channel** ($\mathfrak{P}_A$,
    geometry-generates-group direction): generates the Hilbert space
    $\mathcal{H}$, the canonical commutator
    $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, Stone--von Neumann uniqueness, and
    the entire algebraic-symmetry content of quantum mechanics.
    Henceforth abbreviated as the *Algebraic Channel*.

The Duality is the bidirectional Klein-correspondence reading of the
source-pair $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$. The naming convention is fixed throughout this textbook: the Geometric Channel is always introduced first, with the Algebraic Channel as its operator-algebraic shadow under the suppression map $\sigma$
(Definition [\[def:suppression-map\]](#def:suppression-map){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:suppression-map"}).
:::

::: {#thm:source-pair-equals-duality .theorem}
**Theorem 13.19** (Source-pair and Duality as the same object; [@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Theorem 14.17.3). *The source-pair
$(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ and the McGucken Duality
$\mathfrak{P} = \mathfrak{P}_A \boxtimes \mathfrak{P}_B$ are the same
object viewed at two organisational scales:*

-   *The source-pair is the categorical primitive --- *the object*.*

-   *The McGucken Duality is the bidirectional Klein-correspondence
    reading of the categorical primitive --- *the structure of the
    object*.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has three steps. The identity is forced
jointly by three mechanisms operating at distinct levels of
the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, all descending from
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, the physical,
geometric fact that the fourth dimension expands at the velocity of
light in a spherically symmetric manner, with $x_4 = ict$ the integrated
kinematic shadow per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}).

**Step 1: Reciprocal Generation (RGC${}_6$).** By
Theorem [13.8](#thm:rgc-six){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:rgc-six"} (RGC${}_6$), every object of $\mathcal{F}_M$
generates every other, supplying the bidirectional content. In
particular, $D_M$ generates $\mathcal{M}_G$ (Algebraic Channel direction:
operator generates space) and $\mathcal{M}_G$ generates $D_M$ (Geometric Channel
direction: space generates operator), with both generations canonical
and unique.

**Step 2: Operator-to-Space equivalence
(Theorem [13.3](#thm:adj-dynamical){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:adj-dynamical"}).** The dynamical-pair equivalence
$D_M \simeq \mathcal{M}_G$ has identity unit and counit, reflecting the
fact that $D_M$ and $\mathcal{M}_G$ are simultaneous outputs of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via integration with convention $\kappa$
(producing $\mathcal{M}_G$'s constraint, the integrated kinematic shadow $x_4 = ict$
of Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) and differentiation along the
integral flow (producing $D_M$). The equivalence provides the mechanism by which the operator reconstructs the space and vice versa.

**Step 3: Bidirectional Klein Correspondence.** Klein's 1872 Erlangen
Programme established the geometry-generates-group /
group-generates-geometry correspondence between geometric arenas and
their isometry groups. Applied at the source-pair level, this gives:

-   $\mathrm{Klein\text{-}corresp}(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ direction
    (geometry $\to$ group): the McGucken Space $\mathcal{M}_G$ supplies
    the geometric arena from which the algebraic-symmetry content of
    $D_M$ (Algebraic Channel) is read.

-   $\mathrm{Klein\text{-}corresp}(D_M, \mathcal{M}_G)$ direction (group
    $\to$ geometry): the McGucken Operator $D_M$ supplies the
    algebraic-symmetry content from which the geometric-propagation
    structure of $\mathcal{M}_G$ (Geometric Channel) is read.

The bidirectional reading produces the two-channel structure of the
McGucken Duality as the content of the source-pair when read
through the Klein correspondence. By Steps 1, 2, 3 jointly, the
source-pair and the Duality are the same object at two
organisational scales: the object itself (the categorical primitive of
the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, generated by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}) and the structure of the object (the
bidirectional reading via the Klein correspondence). $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:why-dual-channel-works .remark}
*Remark 13.20* (Why the textbook's dual-channel architecture works). The
textbook organises every QM theorem T1--T23 of Part II by dual-channel
proof.
Theorem [13.19](#thm:source-pair-equals-duality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:source-pair-equals-duality"} above is the reason: the dual-channel architecture is the content of the
source-pair $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ read through the bidirectional Klein
correspondence. Every theorem of physics has both an algebraic-symmetry
derivation and a geometric-propagation derivation because the
source-pair, which is the categorical primitive of physics, has both
readings simultaneously.

The empirical-historical record exhibits this: Heisenberg's 1925 matrix
mechanics derived the operator algebra from empirical spectroscopic
geometry, adjoining the Hilbert space arena retroactively (Klein
direction: geometry $\to$ group); Schrödinger's 1926 wave mechanics
derived the wave equation from the de Broglie algebraic-analytic
hypothesis, adjoining the configuration-space arena (Klein direction:
group $\to$ geometry); the Stone--von Neumann equivalence proved both
readings of the same source-pair ([@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] Theorem
14.17.5).
:::

### Huygens = Holography {#sec:huygens-equals-holography}

[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] §12 establishes a identity
connecting the entire chapter to the textbook's Huygens-of-Nonlocality
content of Ch. [17](#ch:nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:nonlocality"}.

::: {#thm:huygens-equals-holography .theorem}
**Theorem 13.21** (Huygens = Holography; [@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026]
Theorem 12.1). *Under the McGucken Principle $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$,
Huygens' Principle and the holographic principle are two formulations of
the same geometric fact: the physics of the three-dimensional bulk
region enclosed by a McGucken Sphere at parameter time $t + dt$ is fully
determined by source data on the two-dimensional surface of the McGucken
Sphere at parameter time $t$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has three steps establishing the H-Hol
clauses (H-Hol 1, H-Hol 2, H-Hol 3) that jointly express the identity.
The theorem descends from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, the physical, geometric fact that the fourth
dimension expands at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric
manner): the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at every event $p$ is
generated by clauses (i)+(ii), and the Huygens-iteration that sources
bulk wavefronts from surface modes is the geometric content of clause
(ii) spherical symmetry combined with the integrated $x_4 = ict$ per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}.

**Step 1: Surface mode count (Clause H-Hol 1).** The two-dimensional
surface of the McGucken Sphere at radius $R = c(t - t_0)$ from event
$p_0$ has area $$A(t) = 4\pi c^2 (t - t_0)^2.$$ This carries
$N_{\mathrm{modes}}$ independent $x_4$-advance modes, one per
Planck-area cell: $$N_{\mathrm{modes}}(t) = A(t)/\ell_P^2,$$ where
$\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ is the Planck length. The Planck-area cell
is the minimal coherence cell on the McGucken Sphere; at sub-Planck
areas, the spherical-symmetry assumption of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii)) breaks down due to
quantum-gravitational fluctuations of $x_{4}$.

**Step 2: Surface-to-bulk Huygens sourcing (Clause H-Hol 2).** Each
surface mode at parameter time $t$ acts as a Huygens secondary-wavelet
source for the bulk wavefront propagation in the next infinitesimal
interval $dt$, by axiom QB2 of
Chapter [4](#ch:foundations){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:foundations"} (Huygens iteration applied to
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with Huygens' Principle itself a theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ as in
Theorem [1.1](#thm:QMT1){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT1"}
Geometric Channel). The bulk wavefront at $t + dt$ is the envelope of secondary
Spheres sourced at every surface mode at time $t$. This is the canonical
Huygens-secondary-wavelet construction (Huygens 1690 [@Huygens1690])
applied to the McGucken Sphere wavefront.

**Step 3: Bekenstein bound as theorem (Clause H-Hol 3) and synthesis.**
The information-theoretic content of the bulk region at parameter time
$t + dt$ is bounded by the count of Huygens sources on the surface at
$t$:
$$N_{\mathrm{bulk}}(t + dt) \;\leq\; N_{\mathrm{modes}}(t) = A(t)/\ell_P^2.$$
This is the Bekenstein bound, holding universally at every spacetime
event $p$ whose McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ serves as a holographic
screen --- not specifically at black-hole horizons or AdS asymptotic
boundaries, but at every event of $\mathcal{G}_M$, by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (v) (global validity:
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event of $M_{G}$). The three clauses jointly express the identity Huygens = Holography: Step 1 supplies the surface-mode count;
Step 2 supplies the surface-to-bulk sourcing mechanism (Huygens'
Principle applied to $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$); Step 3 supplies the
Bekenstein-bound information-theoretic statement. The holographic
principle is the surface-sourcing of bulk wavefronts by Huygens
secondary wavelets emitted from the surface of the McGucken Sphere. The
universal applicability --- at every event, not just at horizons or AdS
boundaries --- follows because every event is the apex of a McGucken
Sphere (Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:sphere"}, generated by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(ii)+(v)) and every McGucken
Sphere is a holographic screen. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#rmk:holography-special-cases .remark}
*Remark 13.22* (The holographic principle and AdS/CFT (conformal field
theory) as special cases). 't Hooft's 1993 proposal that quantum gravity
has a holographic structure reducing the bulk to a boundary was inferred
from black-hole entropy considerations without specifying the encoding
mechanism. Susskind's 1995 extension added gauge-theoretic and
string-theoretic structure but supplied no physical reason why
holography should hold. Maldacena's 1997 AdS/CFT correspondence gave a
concrete duality in anti-de Sitter geometry but the general mechanism
remained open. Bousso 2002 stated plainly: the principle is
"uncontradicted and unexplained."
Theorem [13.21](#thm:huygens-equals-holography){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:huygens-equals-holography"} supplies the explanation: the
bulk-to-boundary encoding is the surface-sourcing of bulk wavefronts by
Huygens secondary wavelets emitted from the surface of the McGucken
Sphere. The universal applicability --- at every spacetime event ---
follows because every event is the apex of a McGucken Sphere, and every
Sphere is a holographic screen for the bulk physics it encloses. The
mechanism is $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ acting at every event.
:::

### Relation to prior categorical frameworks {#sec:relation-prior-frameworks}

[@MG-McG6-Amplituhedron-2026] §8 audits four contemporary categorical
frameworks operating in the same territory:

## McGucken General Relativity: Split Metric, ADM Foliation, Refractive-Index Principle, and the Schwarzschild Metric from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ {#ch:mcgucken-GR}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


*Recall.* the McGucken Principle ($\mathrm{McP}$:
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$) asserts that the fourth spacetime dimension
$x_4$ expands at the velocity of light $c$, carrying the
perpendicularity marker $i$ that distinguishes it from the spatial
three. Throughout this chapter, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ refers to this
principle and to the five-clause content (i)--(v) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}: (i) *invariance* --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content; (ii) *spherical symmetry* --- the
expansion is isotropic in the spatial three, with the set of events
reachable from $p$ in proper time $\tau$ being a 2-sphere of radius
$c\tau$; (iii) *monotonicity* --- the integral curve is strictly
monotonically increasing in $t$, fixing the arrow of $x_4$-advance; (iv)
*Lorentz consistency* --- the structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on
$M_{G}$; (v) *global validity* --- $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at
every event of $M_{G}$. The integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ (Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) is the kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; the dynamical principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the central fact.

::: flushright
*"The metric tensor $g_{\mu\nu}$ is the refractive index of
three-dimensional space for $x_4$'s invariant expansion. Where space is
curved (dense, stretched) by the presence of mass, $x_4$'s expansion
wavefront must traverse a longer optical path."\
--- [@MG-GR-2026] §X.1.*
:::

This chapter reproduces the content of [@MG-GR-2026] for the
