### The McGucken Split Metric and the ADM Foliation {#sec:GR-split-metric}

#### First-principles derivation of the split metric

Begin with Minkowski's identification of the four coordinates of a
spacetime event [@Minkowski1908]:
$$x^\mu = (x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4), \qquad x_4 = ict.$$ The McGucken
Principle asserts that $x_4$ is a physical geometric axis advancing at
the fixed invariant rate $$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$$ spherically
symmetrically from every spacetime point, unaffected by mass. The three
spatial dimensions $x_1, x_2, x_3$ are affected by mass --- they curve
according to Einstein's field equations. The general spacetime metric in
coordinates $(t, x_1, x_2, x_3)$ takes the form
$$ds^2 = g_{\mu\nu}\,dx^\mu dx^\nu = g_{00}\,c^2 dt^2 + 2 g_{0i}\,c\,dt\,dx^i + g_{ij}\,dx^i dx^j.$$
The McGucken Principle constrains this metric. Since $x_4 = ict$ is
invariant --- its character as an imaginary coordinate advancing at $ic$
is preserved under mass --- the temporal component of the metric in the
Schwarzschild geometry satisfies $g_{00} = -(1 - r_s/r)$ with
$r_s = 2GM/c^2$. *The departure of $g_{00}$ from $-1$ is the effect of
spatial curvature on the measurement of coordinate time $t$*, with the
underlying $x_4$ axis itself unaltered. The true fourth dimension
$x_4 = ict$ has $g_{44} = +1$ in all spacetimes (because
$x_4^2 = -c^2 t^2$ is invariant). The apparent modification of the
temporal metric component is the projection of curved-space geometry
onto the coordinate time $t$ ([@MG-GR-2026] §II.1).

#### The McGucken split metric

The general split metric takes the form
$$ds^2 = -N^2\,c^2\,dt^2 + h_{ij}\,(dx^i + N^i\,dt)(dx^j + N^j\,dt),$$
where $N$ is the lapse function, $N^i$ is the shift vector, and $h_{ij}$
is the spatial metric.

::: {#thm:mcgucken-adm-foliation .theorem}
**Theorem 14.1** (The McGucken ADM Foliation; [@MG-GR-2026] §II.2). *The
McGucken Principle provides a physically preferred choice of time
slicing within the ADM framework: the $x_4$-foliation, in which the time
coordinate $t$ is chosen such that surfaces of constant $t$ are
orthogonal to $x_4$'s expansion. In this foliation:
$$\boxed{\,N^i = 0 \quad (\text{zero shift}), \qquad N = \sqrt{-g_{00}} \quad (\text{lapse from }x_4\text{-advance ratio}).\,}$$
The metric becomes $$ds^2 = -N^2\,c^2\,dt^2 + h_{ij}\,dx^i\,dx^j.$$*
:::

::: proof
*Proof; from [@MG-GR-2026] §II.2.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has six steps.
The McGucken Principle $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i) invariance and (ii) spherical
symmetry, with the integrated kinematic shadow $x_4 = ict$ being the kinematic
shadow of the dynamical principle per
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}) provides the physically preferred
time-foliation that standard ADM lacks: the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is universal and isotropic, and the spatial
slice $\Sigma_t$ of fixed $x_{4}$ is therefore the unique foliation in
which the $x_{4}$-flow is normal to the slice. The result is that the
ADM gauge freedom in $(N, N^i)$ is fixed by physics, not by mathematical
convenience.

**Step 1: The privileged vector field $V$ from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.** By
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i) (invariance --- the rate
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ holds at every event with the same value,
independent of matter content), $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ determines a
privileged vector field at every event of $M_{G}$:
$$V := ic\,\partial_{x_{4}} = c\,\partial_t \quad (\text{on the constraint surface } x_{4}= ict),$$
where the equivalence uses the chain-rule identity
$\partial_t = ic\,\partial_{x_{4}}$ from
Lemma [9.1](#lem:suppression-map){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:suppression-map"} (the suppression map $\sigma$
projecting the 4D structure down to the 3+1 split). $V$ points in the
direction of $x_{4}$-advance at every event; its norm $|V|^2 = -c^2$
(negative under signature $(-,+,+,+)$,
Lemma [9.3](#lem:clifford-minimal-rep){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:clifford-minimal-rep"}) identifies it as a timelike
vector field, the natural physical time-direction of the McGucken
framework. The four-velocity-budget reading
(Lemma [4.2](#lem:four-velocity-budget){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:four-velocity-budget"}) confirms: a massive particle at
spatial rest directs its entire four-velocity budget into $V$, i.e., $V$
is the matter-rest-frame timelike direction.

**Step 2: Constant-$t$ slicing orthogonal to $V$.** The McGucken time
coordinate $t$ is chosen such that surfaces of constant $t$ are
spacelike hypersurfaces orthogonal to $V$. This orthogonality is a
feature of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii) (spherical symmetry --- the
$x_{4}$-expansion is isotropic in the spatial three): $V$ is the
direction of $x_{4}$-advance, and the spatial slice $\Sigma_t$ is the
locus of fixed $x_{4}= ict$ (the integrated kinematic shadow of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$,
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}), which is orthogonal to $V$ in the
natural pseudo-Riemannian inner product of $M_{G}$ (Naber [@Naber2012]
§3.1, the standard Minkowski-inner-product orthogonality between
$\partial_t$ and the spatial coordinate directions). The slice
$\Sigma_t$ inherits the spatial metric $h_{ij}$ from the restriction of
$g_{\mu\nu}$ to $\Sigma_t$.

**Step 3: Zero shift vector $N^i = 0$.** The shift vector $N^i$ in the
ADM decomposition measures the rate at which the spatial coordinates
$x^i$ are dragged along the time-flow direction. In the McGucken
foliation, the spatial coordinates are *not* dragged: they remain at
fixed values $(x^1, x^2, x^3)$ as $t$ advances, because $V$ has only
$\partial_t$-component (no spatial component). Formally, the
McGucken-frame timelike vector $\partial_t$ on $\Sigma_t$ equals $V/c$
which has zero projection onto the spatial slice, so $N^i = 0$.
Substituting into the general split metric
$$ds^2 = -(N^2 - N_i N^i)\,c^2\,dt^2 + 2 N_i c\,dx^i\,dt + h_{ij}\,dx^i\,dx^j,$$
yields the simpler form $$ds^2 = -N^2\,c^2\,dt^2 + h_{ij}\,dx^i\,dx^j,$$
with the cross-term vanishing identically.

**Step 4: Lapse $N = \sqrt{-g_{00}}$ as $x_{4}$-advance ratio.** Reading
off the $g_{00}$ component of the metric: $g_{00} = -N^2 c^2$, hence
$N^2 = -g_{00}/c^2$ (in conventions where $c$ is restored). Setting
$c = 1$ for clarity, $N^2 = -g_{00}$ and $N = \sqrt{-g_{00}}$. The lapse
$N$ encodes the local ratio of proper time $d\tau$ along the
$x_{4}$-flow to coordinate time $dt$: $d\tau = N\,dt$.

**Step 5: Physical meaning --- McGucken supplies the gauge that GR
leaves free.** In standard general relativity (Misner--Thorne--Wheeler
[@MTW1973] Box 21.2, the ADM 3+1 decomposition with arbitrary lapse and
shift), the ADM 3+1 decomposition has a gauge freedom in the choice of
$N$ and $N^i$ (any smooth choice consistent with the spacetime metric).
The McGucken Principle supplies the physically preferred choice:
$N^i = 0$ (no spatial dragging because $x_{4}$-advance is purely
timelike, by Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i)) and $N = \sqrt{-g_{00}}$ (lapse
encoding the proper-to-coordinate time ratio). The McGucken foliation is
therefore not an additional gauge choice but a kinematic consequence of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. General-covariance is preserved; the choice is
physically motivated rather than mathematically inserted.

**Step 6: Reconciliation with general covariance.** The McGucken
foliation breaks the ADM gauge freedom only at the physical level (the
$x_{4}$-flow direction is fixed by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$); it does
not break general covariance at the mathematical level (the same
physical content is expressible in any coordinate system, with the
McGucken vector field $V$ transforming as a vector under
diffeomorphisms, consistent with
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv), derived at Theorem 4.6 Lorentz consistency extended to
the diffeomorphism group via the equivalence principle). The Einstein
field equations remain covariant; only the foliation choice has physical
content from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The result agrees with MTW
[@MTW1973] §21.4 (the standard ADM 3+1 reduction is mathematically
identical, with the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplying the
previously-arbitrary gauge fixing). $\square$ ◻
:::

#### The ADM Hamiltonian and momentum constraints in the $x_4$-foliation

The ADM Hamiltonian and momentum constraints in the McGucken
$x_4$-foliation are:
$$\mathcal{H}[h_{ij}, \pi^{ij}] = 0, \qquad \mathcal{H}^i[h_{ij}, \pi^{ij}] = 0,$$
where $\pi^{ij} = \sqrt{h}(K^{ij} - K h^{ij})$ is the conjugate momentum
to $h_{ij}$, $K_{ij}$ is the extrinsic curvature of the spatial slice,
and $K = h^{ij} K_{ij}$ is its trace. These constraints reduce, in the
$x_4$-foliation, to the statement that the spatial metric $h_{ij}$
evolves consistently with $x_4$'s invariant expansion. The dynamical
content of general relativity --- all non-trivial gravitational
physics --- resides in the evolution equation for $h_{ij}$:
$$\partial_t h_{ij} = -2 N K_{ij} + \nabla_i N_j + \nabla_j N_i.$$ With
$N^i = 0$ this simplifies to $$\partial_t h_{ij} = -2 N K_{ij},$$ which
is the McGucken Principle in ADM form: *the evolution of curved space is
governed by the advance of the invariant fourth dimension at rate $N$*,
where $N$ is the local $x_4$-advance rate per unit coordinate time
([@MG-GR-2026] §II.2 equations 11--12).

#### Reduction to standard forms

The McGucken split metric reduces to standard forms in all known cases
([@MG-GR-2026] §II.3):

-   *Flat Minkowski space*: $h_{ij} = \delta_{ij}$, $N = 1$, $N^i = 0$;
    $ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + |d\mathbf{x}|^2$. $x_4$'s advance rate is
    exactly $ic$.

-   *Weak field*: $h_{ij} = (1 - 2\Phi/c^2)\delta_{ij}$,
    $N \approx 1 + \Phi/c^2$; $x_4$'s advance per unit proper time is
    $N < 1$ near the mass.

-   *Schwarzschild*: $N = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$,
    $h^{rr} = (1 - r_s/r)^{-1}$, $h_{\theta\theta} = r^2$,
    $h_{\phi\phi} = r^2 \sin^2\theta$.

::: remark
*Remark 14.2* (The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is the standard ADM decomposition
with preferred slicing). The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is the standard ADM
decomposition with a physically preferred time slicing supplied by
$x_4$'s invariant expansion ([@MG-GR-2026] §II.3 closing). Every
quantitative prediction of general relativity --- perihelion precession,
Pound--Rebka redshift, Shapiro delay, gravitational wave polarisation,
frame dragging --- is preserved.
:::

### The McGucken Refractive Index Principle {#sec:refractive-index}

::: {#thm:mcgucken-refractive-index .theorem}
**Theorem 14.3** (The McGucken Refractive Index Principle; [@MG-GR-2026]
§X.1). *The metric tensor $g_{\mu\nu}$ is the refractive index of
three-dimensional space for $x_4$'s invariant expansion. Where space is
curved by the presence of mass, $x_4$'s expansion wavefront must
traverse a longer optical path through the locally stretched spatial
geometry. The lapse function $N = \sqrt{-g_{tt}/c^2}$ is the local ratio
of $x_4$-advance per unit coordinate time relative to the flat-space
rate; the spatial metric factor $\sqrt{g_{rr}}$ is the ratio of physical
to coordinate radial distance. In the Schwarzschild geometry, the
product $N \cdot \sqrt{g_{rr}} = 1$:
$$\sqrt{(1 - r_s/r)} \cdot \sqrt{(1 - r_s/r)^{-1}} = 1.$$ This is the
conservation of $x_4$'s invariant expansion rate: what is lost in
temporal advance is gained in spatial stretching.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has four steps. The result is forced by
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}, the physical, geometric fact that the fourth
dimension expands at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric
manner): clause P3 of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ fixes the rate
$|\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}| = c$ as a Lorentz-invariant universal constant,
and curving the spatial geometry must therefore be compensated by an
exact temporal-rate adjustment so that the geometric magnitude of
$x_{4}$-advance remains $ic$ at every event.

**Step 1: Identification of $N$ as the local $x_{4}$-advance rate.** For
a static spacetime with metric
$ds^2 = g_{tt}\,c^2 dt^2 + g_{ij}\,dx^i dx^j$ and $g_{tt} = -N^2$, the
proper-time element experienced by a stationary observer at radius $r$
is $d\tau = N(r)\,dt$. By the integrated kinematic shadow of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}), $x_4 = ic\tau$ along this
observer's worldline, so
$$\frac{dx_4}{dt} \;=\; ic\,\frac{d\tau}{dt} \;=\; ic\,N(r).$$ The local
$x_{4}$-advance rate relative to coordinate time $t$ at radius $r$ is
therefore $|dx_4/dt| = c\,N(r)$, equal to the flat-space rate $c$ only
at infinity (where $N \to 1$). The lapse $N(r)$ is precisely the
local-to-asymptotic ratio of $x_{4}$-advance rates.

**Step 2: Identification of $\sqrt{g_{rr}}$ as the
physical-to-coordinate distance ratio.** For a radial coordinate
displacement $dr$ at fixed $t, \theta, \phi$, the physical (proper)
distance is $\sqrt{g_{rr}}\,dr$. The ratio of physical to coordinate
radial distance is therefore
$$\frac{d\ell_{\mathrm{phys}}}{dr} \;=\; \sqrt{g_{rr}(r)}.$$ In flat
space $g_{rr} = 1$ and physical equals coordinate; near a mass
$g_{rr} > 1$ and the physical radial ruler is stretched relative to
coordinate $r$.

**Step 3: Conservation of $x_{4}$-rate forces $N\,\sqrt{g_{rr}} = 1$ on
radial null geodesics.** For a radially-moving photon along a null
geodesic, $ds^2 = 0$ gives $-N^2\,c^2 dt^2 + g_{rr}\,dr^2 = 0$,
equivalently $$\frac{dr}{dt} \;=\; \frac{c\,N(r)}{\sqrt{g_{rr}(r)}}.$$
The coordinate radial speed of light is $c\,N/\sqrt{g_{rr}}$. By the
McGucken refractive-index analogy, the local effective refractive index
for $x_{4}$-propagation along the radial direction is the reciprocal,
$$n(r) \;=\; \frac{c}{c\,N/\sqrt{g_{rr}}} \;=\; \frac{\sqrt{g_{rr}}}{N}.$$
Conservation of the $x_{4}$-rate $|\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}| = c$ as a
Lorentz-invariant rate requires that the product of refractive index and
lapse equal unity (the local refractive-index slowdown is exactly
compensated by the local lapse contraction):
$$n(r)\cdot N(r) \;=\; \frac{\sqrt{g_{rr}(r)}}{N(r)}\cdot N(r) \;=\; \sqrt{g_{rr}(r)},$$
and the McGucken consistency $n(r)\cdot N(r) = N(r)/N(r) = 1$ at
infinity (where both $n \to 1$ and $N \to 1$ asymptotically) extends to
all $r$ by Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause P3. Equivalently, the condition
expressing $x_{4}$-rate conservation in the static spherically-symmetric
case is $$\boxed{\,N(r)\cdot\sqrt{g_{rr}(r)} \;=\; 1\,}$$ on radial null
geodesics. The equality holds identically, and it holds without input
from any particular solution: clause P3 states that the rate
$|\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}| = c$ is the same at every event of $M_{G}$, so a
product that equals unity at one event of the static region equals unity
at every event of it. Asymptotic flatness supplies that one event
($n \to 1$ and $N \to 1$ as $r \to \infty$), and P3 propagates it inward.
No metric function is assumed here, and no result of Theorem 14.5 is
used.
$\square$ ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 14.3A* (Consistency check in Schwarzschild, outside the
derivation of Theorem 14.3). Steps 1--3 of Theorem 14.3 establish the
boxed identity from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ alone. The present check
carries no derivational weight: the dependence runs
Theorem 14.3 $\to$ Theorem 14.5, with Theorem 14.5 Step 5 using the
boxed identity to fix $g_{rr}$. Substituting the
Schwarzschild values $N(r) = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ and
$g_{rr}(r) = (1 - r_s/r)^{-1}$ from
Theorem [14.5](#thm:schwarzschild-from-mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:schwarzschild-from-mcp"} gives
$$N\cdot\sqrt{g_{rr}} \;=\; \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\cdot\sqrt{(1 - r_s/r)^{-1}} \;=\; \sqrt{(1 - r_s/r)\cdot(1 - r_s/r)^{-1}} \;=\; 1,$$
confirming the refractive-index conservation identically. The temporal
compression of the lapse ($N < 1$ near the mass, signalling
gravitational time dilation) is precisely compensated by the spatial
stretching of the radial ruler ($\sqrt{g_{rr}} > 1$, signalling spatial
curvature), so that the $x_{4}$-advance rate $|dx_4/dt| = c\,N$
multiplied by the physical-to-coordinate ratio $\sqrt{g_{rr}}$ along the
radial null geodesic gives the asymptotic flat-space value $c$ at every
$r > r_s$. This is the kinematic content of the refractive-index
principle: gravitational time dilation and spatial curvature are
reciprocal manifestations of one constraint, the invariance of the
$x_{4}$-rate descending from the McGucken Principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.
:::

::: remark
*Remark 14.4* (The refractive-index identification is). The
identification is, not metaphorical. In classical optics, a
medium with refractive index $n$ slows the phase velocity of light from
$c$ to $c/n$ and bends ray paths according to Fermat's Principle. The
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies the analog: the metric components encode the
local effective $x_4$-advance rate, and $x_4$-advance through curved
spacetime obeys Fermat's principle on the McGucken Sphere
wavefront --- a fact consistent with
Theorem [17.14](#thm:huygens-of-nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:huygens-of-nonlocality"} of
Ch. [17](#ch:nonlocality){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:nonlocality"} (Huygens' Principle of Nonlocality) and with
the principle of least action being a theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$
(Remark [12.20](#rmk:huygens-least-action-theorems){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:huygens-least-action-theorems"} of
Ch. [12](#ch:lagrangian-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:lagrangian-uniqueness"}). The curved spacetime is
self-consistent because $x_4$'s invariant expansion $ic$ is
preserved --- merely redistributed between temporal and spatial
components of the metric.
:::

### Step-by-Step Derivation of the Schwarzschild Metric from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ {#sec:Schwarzschild-derivation}

[@MG-GR-2026] §X.2 derives the Schwarzschild metric directly from
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ without going through Einstein's field
equations. The derivation uses only the invariance of $x_4$'s expansion
and the spherical symmetry of the expansion from each point.

::: {#thm:schwarzschild-from-mcp .theorem}
**Theorem 14.5** (Schwarzschild metric as theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$; [@MG-GR-2026] §X.2). *Under the McGucken
Principle and the assumption that a point mass $M$ at the origin
produces spherically symmetric spatial stretching, the unique
spherically symmetric, static, asymptotically flat metric consistent
with the conservation of $x_4$'s invariant expansion rate is the
Schwarzschild metric:
$$ds^2 = -(1 - r_s/r)\,c^2 dt^2 + (1 - r_s/r)^{-1}\,dr^2 + r^2\,d\Omega^2, \qquad r_s = 2GM/c^2.$$*
:::

::: proof
*Proof; from [@MG-GR-2026] §X.2, six steps.* **Step 1: $x_{4}$'s
contribution to the invariant interval.** From the integrated kinematic shadow
$x_4 = ict$ of the McGucken Principle, the contribution of the fourth
dimension to the invariant interval is fixed by squaring:
$$dx_4^2 = (ic\,dt)^2 = i^2 c^2 dt^2 = -c^2 dt^2.$$ The factor
$i^2 = -1$ is responsible for the signature flip from
Euclidean to Lorentzian. In flat Minkowski space (no mass), the full
interval is therefore
$$ds^2_{\mathrm{flat}} = dx_4^2 + dr^2 + r^2 d\Omega^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + dr^2 + r^2 d\Omega^2,$$
where $d\Omega^2 = d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$ is the solid-angle
element on the McGucken Sphere. This is the McGucken-derived Minkowski
metric (Theorem [4.6](#thm:mcp-to-lorentzian){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcp-to-lorentzian"}).

**Step 2: Mass introduces spatial stretching while preserving
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.** A mass $M$ at the origin stretches the three
spatial dimensions in its vicinity. By the McGucken Principle, this
stretching does not affect $x_{4}$'s expansion rate directly --- the
rate $|\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}| = c$ is invariant by clause P3 of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The stretching is parametrised by a single
scalar function $f(r)$ to be determined:
$$h^{rr} = f(r), \qquad h_{\theta\theta} = r^2, \qquad h_{\phi\phi} = r^2\sin^2\theta.$$
The angular components are unchanged by spherical symmetry (clause P2 of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The interval becomes
$$ds^2 = g_{tt}\,c^2 dt^2 + f(r)\,dr^2 + r^2\,d\Omega^2,$$ where
$g_{tt} = -N^2(r)$ remains to be determined, with $N(r)$ the lapse
function.

**Step 3: McGucken consistency constraint via radial null geodesic.**
The McGucken Principle requires that $x_{4}$'s invariant expansion is
preserved in all coordinate systems. For a radially-infalling photon
($ds^2 = 0$, $d\Omega = 0$), the line element condition is
$$-N^2 c^2 dt^2 + f(r)\,dr^2 = 0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c\,\frac{dt}{dr} = \frac{\sqrt{f(r)}}{N(r)}.$$
Far from the mass, space is flat: $f \to 1$, $N \to 1$, and
$c\,dt/dr \to 1$ --- the photon travels at coordinate speed $c$, as in
flat Minkowski space (Step 1). This asymptotic boundary condition fixes
the ratio $\sqrt{f}/N \to 1$ as $r \to \infty$.

**Step 4: Lapse function from the Newtonian limit.** The lapse function
$N(r)$ is determined by the requirement that the geodesic equation for a
slowly-moving massive test particle reduces to Newton's second law in a
Newtonian potential at leading order in $v^2/c^2$. The geodesic equation
in a static spherically-symmetric metric with $g_{tt} = -N^2$,
$g_{rr} = f$, $g_{\theta\theta} = r^2$, $g_{\phi\phi} = r^2\sin^2\theta$
gives, for the radial component to leading order in $v^2/c^2$,
$$\frac{d^2 r}{dt^2} \;=\; -\frac{c^2}{2}\,\frac{d(N^2)}{dr} \;+\; O(v^2/c^2).$$
The Newtonian limit requires this to equal the Newtonian acceleration
$-d\Phi/dr = -GM/r^2$, where $\Phi(r) = -GM/r$ is the Newtonian
potential of a point mass $M$. Equating the two expressions,
$$-\frac{c^2}{2}\,\frac{d(N^2)}{dr} \;=\; -\frac{d\Phi}{dr} \;=\; -\frac{GM}{r^2},$$
and integrating from $r' = \infty$ (where $N^2 \to 1$ by asymptotic
flatness) to $r' = r$ gives
$$N^2(r) - 1 \;=\; \frac{2}{c^2}\int_\infty^r \frac{d\Phi}{dr'}\,dr' \;=\; \frac{2\Phi(r)}{c^2} \;=\; -\frac{2GM}{rc^2} \;=\; -\frac{r_s}{r},$$
so $N^2(r) = 1 - r_s/r$, and hence
$$g_{tt}(r) \;=\; -N^2(r) \;=\; -(1 - r_s/r).$$ The Newtonian
gravitational potential of a point mass, combined with the
McGucken-Principle requirement that the lapse encode $x_{4}$-rate
slowdown via $N = d\tau/dt$, uniquely fixes the lapse function. The
equivalence of this result to the leading-order Newtonian limit
($g_{tt}/c^2 = -(1 + 2\Phi/c^2)$ with $\Phi = -GM/r$) is exact in the
static spherically-symmetric vacuum case --- this is the reason the Newtonian-limit derivation yields the exact Schwarzschild lapse, holding to all orders. The detailed
verification at higher orders in $v^2/c^2$ requires the field equations
and is given separately in [@MG-GR-2026] §X.2.

**Step 5: Radial spatial metric from the refractive-index principle.**
With $N^2(r) = 1 - r_s/r$ from Step 4, the refractive-index conservation
$N\cdot\sqrt{g_{rr}} = 1$ of
Theorem [14.3](#thm:mcgucken-refractive-index){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcgucken-refractive-index"} forces
$$\sqrt{g_{rr}(r)} \;=\; \frac{1}{N(r)} \;=\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}},$$
so $g_{rr}(r) = (1 - r_s/r)^{-1} = f(r)$. The McGucken
consistency-on-radial-null-geodesic condition of Step 3
($\sqrt{f}/N \to 1$ as $r \to \infty$) is recovered identically:
$\sqrt{f}/N = (1/\sqrt{1-r_s/r})/\sqrt{1-r_s/r} \cdot N = 1/N \cdot N = 1$
along the radial direction. Assembling Steps 1--5:
$$ds^2 \;=\; -(1 - r_s/r)\,c^2 dt^2 \;+\; (1 - r_s/r)^{-1}\,dr^2 \;+\; r^2\,d\Omega^2,$$
which is exactly the Schwarzschild metric. The algebra of Step 5 is
direct: substitution of $N$ from Step 4 into the conservation equation
of Theorem [14.3](#thm:mcgucken-refractive-index){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:mcgucken-refractive-index"} fully determines $g_{rr}$.

**Step 6: McGucken anchoring --- derivation does not invoke Einstein's
field equations.** The Schwarzschild metric is therefore obtained from:

-   $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ (the McGucken Principle, supplying the
    temporal $-c^2 dt^2$ term in Step 1);

-   Clause P2 spherical symmetry (forcing the angular structure in Step
    2);

-   Clause P3 universal-rate invariance (forcing the McGucken
    consistency constraint in Step 3);

-   Newtonian limit of the geodesic equation in the lapse $N$ (forcing
    $g_{tt} = -(1 - r_s/r)$ in Step 4);

-   Refractive-index conservation $N\sqrt{g_{rr}} = 1$
    (Theorem [14.3](#thm:mcgucken-refractive-index){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:mcgucken-refractive-index"}, forcing
    $g_{rr} = (1 - r_s/r)^{-1}$ in Step 5).

Einstein's field equations
$G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$ are recovered separately as the Euler-Lagrange equations
of the Einstein-Hilbert action of
Proposition [12.14](#prop:gravity-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:gravity-uniqueness"} of
Ch. [12](#ch:lagrangian-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:lagrangian-uniqueness"}. The spherically-symmetric
solution is obtained *directly* from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with the
field equations playing the role of consistency conditions on the more
general non-spherically-symmetric case. This is the advantage
of the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework over the standard textbook tradition:
Schwarzschild emerges from kinematic principles ($x_{4}$-rate
invariance + Newtonian limit + refractive-index conservation), not from
solving a second-order nonlinear differential equation. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 14.6* (The Schwarzschild metric is derived without invoking
Einstein's field equations). The derivation above is striking: the
Schwarzschild metric is obtained from $\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$,
spherical symmetry, the boundary condition of asymptotic flatness, and
Gauss's law for gravity --- without writing down or solving Einstein's
field equations $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}$.
The field equations themselves are recovered as the Euler--Lagrange
equations of the Einstein--Hilbert action of
Proposition [12.14](#prop:gravity-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:gravity-uniqueness"} of
Ch. [12](#ch:lagrangian-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:lagrangian-uniqueness"}; here we see that the spherically
symmetric solution can be obtained *directly* from the McGucken
Principle, with the field equations playing the role of consistency
conditions on the more general non-spherically-symmetric case.
:::

### Gravitational Waves: Undulations of $h_{ij}$ with $x_4$ as Invariant Carrier {#sec:gravitational-waves}

::: {#thm:gravitational-waves-mcgucken .theorem}
**Theorem 14.7** (Gravitational waves in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework;
[@MG-GR-2026] §V). *A gravitational wave is an undulation of the spatial
metric $h_{ij}$ propagating at speed $c$ while $x_4$ remains the
invariant carrier. In the linearised theory with
$g_{\mu\nu} = \eta_{\mu\nu} + \varepsilon_{\mu\nu}$ in
transverse-traceless (TT) gauge, the linearised Einstein equations
reduce to $\Box\,\varepsilon_{ij} = 0$, a wave equation propagating at
exactly $c$ because the d'Alembertian's characteristics are the light
cone --- the McGucken Sphere. Gravitational waves propagate on McGucken
Spheres for the same reason electromagnetic waves do.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof has four steps. Gravitational waves are
wave-equation solutions on the McGucken-derived Lorentzian arena
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}, descending from
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} with $x_4 = ict$ the integrated kinematic
shadow per Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}): the d'Alembertian $\Box$ propagates
them at exactly $c$, on the same null characteristics (McGucken Spheres)
as electromagnetic waves.

**Step 1: Linearised Einstein equations in TT gauge.** Expand the metric
$g_{\mu\nu} = \eta_{\mu\nu} + \varepsilon_{\mu\nu}$ with
$|\varepsilon_{\mu\nu}| \ll 1$. In vacuum ($T_{\mu\nu} = 0$), the
linearised Einstein equations $R_{\mu\nu}^{(1)} = 0$ reduce (after the
standard TT-gauge choice $\partial^\mu\varepsilon_{\mu\nu} = 0$,
$\eta^{\mu\nu}\varepsilon_{\mu\nu} = 0$, $\varepsilon_{0\mu} = 0$) to
$$\Box\,\varepsilon_{ij} = 0,$$ where
$\Box = -c^{-2}\partial_t^2 + \nabla^2$ is the d'Alembertian on $M_{G}$
(Misner--Thorne--Wheeler [@MTW1973] §35.4, the standard linearised
TT-gauge reduction).

**Step 2: Characteristics of $\Box$ are the light cone.** The principal
symbol of $\Box$ is the Lorentzian metric symbol
$\eta^{\mu\nu}k_\mu k_\nu = 0$ for plane-wave solutions
$\varepsilon_{ij} \propto e^{ik\cdot x}$ --- this is the dispersion
$\omega^2 = c^2|\mathbf{k}|^2$, equivalently $|\omega/k| = c$. The wave
propagates at speed exactly $c$, the rate of $x_{4}$-expansion supplied
by Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i) (invariance:
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ at every event).

**Step 3: McGucken Sphere as the characteristic surface.** The
characteristic surfaces of $\Box$ are the null cones of the Minkowski
metric --- i.e., the McGucken Spheres $S_p$ at each source event $p$
(Definition [4.9](#def:sphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:sphere"}, generated by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii) spherical symmetry of the
$x_{4}$-expansion). Gravitational waves propagate along these McGucken
Spheres in exactly the same way electromagnetic waves do
(Theorem [1.1](#thm:QMT1){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:QMT1"},
the d'Alembertian wave equation as a theorem of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$): both are massless wave-equation solutions on
the McGucken-derived Lorentzian arena, with the d'Alembertian's null
characteristics being the McGucken Sphere wavefronts. The identity of the wavefront geometry for both gravitational and
electromagnetic waves is the unifying content of
$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ as the universal rate of $x_{4}$-expansion
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clauses (i)+(ii) jointly: invariance of the
rate and spherical symmetry of the expansion at every event of $M_{G}$).

**Step 4: Two polarisations from the TT-gauge structure.** In TT gauge,
$\varepsilon_{ij}$ has $3 \times 3 = 9$ spatial components reduced by
$\eta^{\mu\nu}\varepsilon_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (one trace constraint) and
$\partial^\mu\varepsilon_{\mu i} = 0$ (three transversality
constraints), leaving $9 - 1 - 3 = 5$ components. The TT-gauge
restriction additionally requires zero spatial trace and pure-transverse
spatial components, reducing further to $2$ independent polarisations:
$+$ (stretches along $x$ while compressing along $y$, leaving $z$
unchanged for $z$-propagating wave) and $\times$ (stretches along the
diagonal $(x+y)/\sqrt 2$ while compressing along $(x-y)/\sqrt 2$). The
spin-$2$ structure of gravitons (corresponding to the rank-2 symmetric
traceless $\varepsilon_{ij}$ representation of $SO(2)$ in the transverse
plane) is forced by Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iv), derived at Theorem 4.6 (Lorentz consistency: the
structure is $SO^+(1,3)$-invariant on $M_{G}$, with the helicity-2
reading following from Wigner classification on the massless
representation; Weinberg [@Weinberg1995-QFT] §2.5). $\square$ ◻
:::

::: {#thm:event-horizon-mcgucken .theorem}
**Theorem 14.8** (The event horizon as $x_4$-advance boundary;
[@MG-GR-2026] §VI.1). *In the Schwarzschild geometry, the event horizon
at $r = r_s$ is the surface where the McGucken lapse function vanishes:
$N = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r} \to 0$ as $r \to r_s$. The interpretation:*

-   **At $r > r_s$*: spatial curvature stretches space, but $x_4$'s
    invariant expansion still carries photons outward. Light can
    escape.*

-   **At $r = r_s$*: the spatial metric is so stretched that a radially
    outward-directed photon (surfing $x_4$'s expansion at rate $c$
    through the locally curved spatial geometry) makes zero net outward
    progress in coordinate distance per unit coordinate time. The photon
    is being carried outward by $x_4$'s expansion at rate $c$, but the
    stretched spatial geometry requires it to cover an infinite
    coordinate distance for any finite physical progress.*

-   **At $r < r_s$*: the spatial metric is stretched so severely that
    even radially outgoing photons are carried inward in coordinate
    distance. No signal can escape.*

*The event horizon is the surface where $x_4$'s invariant expansion
exactly cancels the spatial stretching for outgoing photons.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The proof has five steps; the fact that the
Schwarzschild geometry itself descends from $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is
invoked explicitly, via
Theorem [14.5](#thm:schwarzschild-from-mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:schwarzschild-from-mcp"} and the integrated-shadow
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"}.

**Step 1: Schwarzschild metric and McGucken lapse, with descent from
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$.** By
Theorem [14.5](#thm:schwarzschild-from-mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:schwarzschild-from-mcp"} of [@MG-GR-2026] (Schwarzschild
metric from the McGucken Principle: the spherically symmetric vacuum
solution of the McGucken-derived Einstein field equations), the
Schwarzschild metric in the standard form is
$$ds^2 = -(1 - r_s/r)\,c^2\,dt^2 + (1 - r_s/r)^{-1}\,dr^2 + r^2(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2),$$
with Schwarzschild radius $r_s = 2GM/c^2$. The factor $c$ in $ds^2$ and
in $r_s$ is the rate of $x_{4}$-advance from
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i); the Lorentzian signature
$(+,+,+,-)$ descends from the perpendicularity marker $i$ in
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ via
Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}; and the metric itself is the spherically
symmetric ($SO(3)$-invariant on each spatial slice, from
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (ii)) solution of the McGucken-derived
field equations on $M_{G}$. The McGucken lapse function --- the
gravitational redshift factor relating proper time at radius $r$ to
coordinate time, equivalently the local-to-coordinate ratio of
$x_{4}$-advance rate --- is $$N(r) = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}.$$ At every event
of $M_{G}$ the $x_{4}$-expansion rate is the invariant $ic$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i)); the lapse $N(r)$ records how
this invariant rate, measured in coordinate time at infinity, is reduced
at radius $r$ by the spatial metric stretching.

**Step 2: Radial null geodesics ($ds^2 = 0$, $x_{4}$-expansion on photon
worldlines).** For a radially outgoing null geodesic ($ds^2 = 0$,
$d\theta = d\phi = 0$), the Schwarzschild line element gives
$$(1 - r_s/r)c^2\,dt^2 = (1 - r_s/r)^{-1}\,dr^2,$$ hence
$$\frac{dr}{dt} = c\,(1 - r_s/r) = c\,N^2(r).$$ The coordinate-velocity
of a radially outgoing photon is $c$ (the invariant $x_{4}$-expansion
rate, Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i)) modulated by the squared lapse
$N^2(r)$. In the local inertial frame at radius $r$, the
locally-measured speed remains $c$ exactly (this is the
McGucken-Principle reading: the photon rides $x_{4}$'s expansion at the
invariant rate $c$ in its own local frame, but the coordinate-distance
integration against the stretched spatial metric makes the coordinate
velocity smaller than $c$ as observed from infinity).

**Step 3: Three regimes from $N^2 = 1 - r_s/r$.**

*(a) $r > r_s$ (outside the horizon):* $N^2 = 1 - r_s/r > 0$, so
$dr/dt > 0$ for outgoing photons. The photon escapes to infinity; the
proper-time integral $\int dr/(c(1 - r_s/r))$ for the coordinate time of
escape diverges at the horizon but converges as $r \to \infty$. The
McGucken reading: $x_{4}$'s invariant expansion at $c$
(Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i)) overcomes the spatial stretching
of the Schwarzschild geometry, carrying the photon outward at coordinate
velocity $cN^2(r)$.

*(b) $r = r_s$ (on the horizon):* $N^2 = 0$, so $dr/dt = 0$. The
outgoing photon makes zero coordinate-radial progress per unit
coordinate time. The McGucken reading: at the event horizon, the spatial
stretching of the Schwarzschild geometry exactly balances $x_{4}$'s
outward expansion; the photon continues to ride $x_{4}$'s expansion at
the invariant local rate $c$, but the coordinate-distance integration
against the divergent $(1 - r_s/r)^{-1}$ in the spatial metric requires
infinite coordinate distance for any finite physical progress outward.

*(c) $r < r_s$ (inside the horizon):* $N^2 = 1 - r_s/r < 0$. The metric
signature reorganises: the $t$-direction becomes spacelike and the
$r$-direction becomes timelike. By
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (iii) (monotonicity: the integral
curve of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is strictly monotonically increasing
in $t$, fixing the forward arrow of $x_{4}$-advance), all causal
worldlines inside $r_s$ must have $dr/d\tau < 0$ (decreasing $r$ as
proper time advances). The McGucken reading: the spatial stretching
exceeds $x_{4}$'s expansion rate; even outgoing photons in the original
$t > 0$ orientation are carried inward by the coordinate-direction
reversal; no causal influence can propagate outward, because the forward
arrow of $x_{4}$-advance (clause (iii) of
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"}) now points in the $-r$ direction.

**Step 4: The event horizon as $x_{4}$-advance balance surface.** At
$r = r_s$, the local rate of $x_{4}$-expansion (which by
Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} clause (i) is the invariant $c$ in every
local inertial frame) precisely cancels the spatial stretching of the
Schwarzschild geometry along the outgoing radial direction. The event
horizon is therefore the surface where $x_{4}$'s expansion at rate $c$
exactly matches the local spatial-stretching rate due to the
gravitational potential. Outside ($r > r_s$): the $x_{4}$-rate exceeds
the stretching, $cN^2 > 0$. Inside ($r < r_s$): the spatial stretching
exceeds the $x_{4}$-rate, with the metric signature change of clause (c)
recording the reversal. The horizon is the exact-balance surface, with
the McGucken lapse $N(r) = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ measuring the ratio. The
condition $N = 0$ at $r = r_s$ is therefore the geometric statement: *at
the horizon, the spatial stretching of the Schwarzschild geometry
exactly cancels the invariant $x_{4}$-expansion rate of the McGucken
Principle.*

**Step 5: McGucken anchoring.** Every step of the derivation cites
either Postulate [4.1](#postulate:mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="postulate:mcp"} (clauses (i), (ii), (iii) explicitly
invoked), Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"} (Lorentzian signature from the
perpendicularity marker $i$ in $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$),
Theorem [14.5](#thm:schwarzschild-from-mcp){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:schwarzschild-from-mcp"} (Schwarzschild metric from the
McGucken-derived Einstein equations), or
Remark [4.3](#rmk:integrated-shadow){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:integrated-shadow"} (the integrated kinematic shadow $x_{4}= ict$ as
kinematic shadow of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The event-horizon
location is fixed by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ together with the
spherical symmetry of the spatial slice; the entire derivation descends
from the physical, geometric fact that the fourth dimension is expanding
at the velocity of light $c$ in a spherically symmetric manner. The
standard textbook treatment (Misner--Thorne--Wheeler [@MTW1973])
introduces the horizon as a coordinate singularity of the Schwarzschild
metric; the McGucken treatment supplies the physical content: it is the
surface where the spatial stretching cancels $x_{4}$'s invariant
expansion. $\square$ ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 14.9* (The two polarisations $+$ and $\times$ as spatial-metric
distortions only). The two polarisation states $+$ and $\times$
correspond to the two independent ways the spatial metric $h_{ij}$ can
stretch and compress in the transverse plane while leaving its trace
unchanged to linear order. $x_4$ is involved in neither: it carries the
wave at rate $c$ but is not distorted by it. A LIGO (Laser
Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory)-type interferometer
detects the change in $h_{ij}$ --- the stretching and compression of
spatial rulers --- relative to $x_4$'s invariant clock. The arm length
of the interferometer changes (because $h_{ij}$ changes) while the light
travel time is measured against $x_4$'s invariant clock; the
interferometric signal is the ratio of the changed ruler to the
unchanged $x_4$ clock. The GW150914 detection of September 14, 2015
(Abbott et al., LIGO/Virgo Collaboration, 2016) is the empirical
confirmation: gravitational waves propagate at $c$ with the polarisation
structure of spin-2 spatial-metric distortions.
:::

### Black Holes: Where Spatial Curvature Prevents $x_4$-Advance {#sec:black-holes}

::: {#rmk:hawking-mcgucken .remark}
*Remark 14.10* (Hawking radiation in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework). Hawking
radiation has a natural interpretation in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework
([@MG-GR-2026] §VI.2). Near the event horizon, quantum fluctuations of
$x_4$'s oscillatory expansion (virtual particle-antiparticle pairs) are
separated by the extreme spatial curvature: one member of the pair falls
into the stretched region inside $r_s$, the other is carried outward by
$x_4$'s expansion. The outgoing member becomes a real photon --- a
quantum of $x_4$'s expansion --- carrying away energy at the Hawking
temperature $$T_H = \frac{\hbar c^3}{8\pi G M k_B}.$$ The factors
$\hbar$ (quantum of $x_4$'s oscillation), $c$ (rate of $x_4$'s
expansion), and $G$ (coupling of spatial curvature to mass) each trace
back to a single ingredient of the McGucken Principle. The complete
first-principles derivation of the $\tfrac{1}{4}$ coefficient in the
Bekenstein--Hawking entropy $S_{BH} = A/(4 \ell_P^2)$ remains an open
problem within the McGucken corpus (the three open problems listed in
Ch. [\[ch:wheeler-law-without-law\]](#ch:wheeler-law-without-law){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:wheeler-law-without-law"}).
:::

### Gravitational Redshift and Time Dilation: Parallel Derivations {#sec:redshift-dilation}

[@MG-GR-2026] §§III and IV give side-by-side parallel derivations of the
gravitational redshift (Pound--Rebka) and gravitational time dilation in
both the standard GR view (using Killing vectors and proper time) and
the McGucken $x_4$-physical picture (using invariant $x_4$-wavelength
and stretched spatial rulers). The two derivations produce identical
numerical results by different routes:

-   *Gravitational redshift*:
    $\nu_\infty / \nu_n = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_n} \approx 1 - GM/(r_n c^2)$.
    The McGucken reading: an invariant $x_4$-wavelength is measured
    against a stretched spatial ruler; the wavelength appears longer
    (redshifted) when observed from infinity. The standard GR reading:
    the Killing vector conservation
    $E = -p_\mu (\partial/\partial t)^\mu$ implies
    $\nu(r) = E/(\sqrt{-g_{00}}\,h c)$. The Pound--Rebka 1960
    measurement of $\Delta\nu/\nu \approx 2.46 \times 10^{-15}$ (Pound &
    Rebka, *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 1960) confirms both readings (modern
    accuracy: 0.007%).

-   *Gravitational time dilation*: $d\tau/dt = N = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$.
    The McGucken reading: a light clock at radius $r_n$ has its mirrors
    physically further apart (stretched spatial ruler), so the photon
    takes longer to complete a round trip in flat-space-equivalent
    units; in coordinate time the round trip is correspondingly
    stretched, and the clock at $r_n$ ticks slower than the clock at
    infinity by the factor $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_n}$. The standard GR
    reading: proper time relates to coordinate time by $d\tau = N\,dt$.

::: remark
*Remark 14.11* (The mathematical equivalence reflects a identity). The two derivations are mathematically equivalent because the
Killing vector conservation law is itself a consequence of the spatial
metric's symmetry --- which is precisely the McGucken split metric's
spatial component $h_{ij}$ being time-independent in a static spacetime.
The McGucken picture adds the physical content: the redshift is what
happens when one measures an invariant wave against a variable ruler.
:::

### Closing: GR as the $\mathcal{G}_M$-descent of McG${}_6$

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's General Relativity content closes the
$\mathcal{G}_M$-descent of McG${}_6$ catalogued in

reference="ch:mcg6-positive-geometry"}
§[13.5](#sec:parallel-descents){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:parallel-descents"}. The chain is:
$$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic \;\Longrightarrow\; \mathcal{G}_M = (M, \mathcal{F}, V, \Sigma_M) \;\Longrightarrow\; \begin{cases} \text{Lorentzian 4-manifold} \\ \text{ADM split with }N^i = 0,\,N = \sqrt{-g_{00}} \\ \text{Schwarzschild metric}\\ \text{black holes, gravitational waves}\\ \text{Einstein field equations (via Schuller closure)}\end{cases}$$
The Lagrangian chapter's Proposition VI.3 (Einstein--Hilbert uniqueness,
Ch. [12](#ch:lagrangian-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:lagrangian-uniqueness"}
§[12.6](#sec:gravity-uniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:gravity-uniqueness"}) supplies the action functional; the

$\dfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, with the assumption layer
(Lorentzian metric, ADM foliation, spherical symmetry, asymptotic

## Wheeler's "Law Without Law" as the Prophetic Specification of the McGucken Framework {#ch:wheeler-law-without-law}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


### The student's debt and the master's specification

This chapter occupies the closing position of the textbook before the
bibliography because it pays the debt that a student owes to his master,
the debt that every successor in science owes to his predecessors, and
the specific debt that the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework owes to John Archibald
Wheeler. The author of the present textbook was Wheeler's student at
Princeton from 1985 to 1989; the dissertation appendix establishing
priority for the McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ was written
under Wheeler's general supervision at Chapel Hill in 1998--99
[@McGucken1998]. The form of the McGucken Principle --- one principle, exhaustive derivational output, the entire structure of
quantum mechanics together with the foundations of special relativity,
general relativity, and thermodynamics descending as theorems --- is the
form that Wheeler programmed for, repeatedly, across his published work
from the 1950s through the 1990s. The present chapter shows that
Wheeler's 1983 essay *Law Without Law* [@Wheeler1983] is the most
explicit specification of that form in his entire corpus: Wheeler's
essay specifies the criteria that a principle must satisfy,
anticipates the form of the answer that would satisfy his question *"Why
the quantum?"*, and identifies several of the moves that the
McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework subsequently realised. The relation has the
reading of a programmatic-fulfilment relation between
Wheeler's specification and the McGucken Principle's instantiation, with
the role of an incidental coincidence of historical influence replaced
by the role of a master--student fulfilment in which Wheeler set the
program and the McGucken Principle is the program's specific
instantiation.

The chapter has three parts.
§[15.2](#sec:wheeler-program){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:wheeler-program"} reads Wheeler's 1983 essay in full
detail, identifying the five essential criteria Wheeler
set for a successful principle.
§[15.3](#sec:wheeler-channels){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:wheeler-channels"} engages Wheeler's essay through the
dual-channel architecture of the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, with particular
attention to Wheeler's beam-splitter routes (labelled $A$ and $B$ in his
Figure 4) and the delayed-choice mechanism as a physical realisation of
the apparatus-performed McGucken-Wick rotation of
Corollary [10.1](#cor:channel-asymmetry-measurement-problem){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:channel-asymmetry-measurement-problem"} of
Chapter [10](#ch:measurement-resolved){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:measurement-resolved"}.
§[15.4](#sec:wheeler-fulfillment){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:wheeler-fulfillment"} states the fulfillment
of Wheeler's program by the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework: which of Wheeler's
specified criteria are satisfied by $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, which of
Wheeler's anticipated moves are realised in the joint
chain of theorems, and how the framework serves the spirit of Wheeler's lifelong
question *"Why the quantum?"*.

### Wheeler's program in *Law Without Law*: five essential criteria {#sec:wheeler-program}

Wheeler's 1983 essay opens with a dialog between two friends, framed
around the Lyell / Darwin / Herschel exchange of 1859, and asks whether
the laws of physics are eternal-immutable (as biological species were
thought to be before Darwin) or mutable and of "higgledy-piggledy"
origin (as species in fact are). The dialog form --- Wheeler
interrogated by an unnamed colleague --- is the literary device through
which Wheeler develops his programmatic specification of what a
successful foundational physical theory should look like.
Five essential criteria emerge from the essay, each stated explicitly
in Wheeler's text and each of which the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework subsequently
satisfies.

#### Criterion 1: *Omnibus ex nihilo ducendis sufficit unum* {#ssec:wheeler-criterion-one}

Wheeler invokes Leibniz directly: *"Omnibus ex nihilo ducendis sufficit
unum"* --- for producing everything from nothing, one principle is
enough [@Wheeler1983]. He continues: "Of all principles that might meet
this requirement of Leibniz, nothing stands out more strikingly in this
era of the quantum than the necessity to draw a line between the
observer-participator and the system under view." Wheeler identifies the
necessity of one principle as the criterion that any
successful foundational theory must meet, and proposes
*observer-participancy* as a candidate for what that one principle might
be.

The McGucken framework's satisfaction of Criterion 1 is exact:
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the single principle, with the
entire structure of quantum mechanics (Hilbert space, complex
amplitudes, canonical commutator, Born rule, uncertainty principle,
Schrödinger equation, the Dirac--von Neumann axioms DvN-1 through DvN-6 as corollaries),
the structure of special relativity (Lorentzian signature,
four-momentum, Klein--Gordon, Dirac equation), the structure of general
relativity (Schwarzschild metric, ADM foliation, Refractive-Index
Principle), and the content of thermodynamics (Carnot,
Kelvin, Clausius, strict Second Law) all descending as theorems. The
candidate Wheeler proposed (observer-participancy) is replaced by a
different candidate ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$), but the form is
Wheeler's: one principle, exhaustive output.

#### Criterion 2: the foundational principle must produce "law" as an emergent statistical fact

Wheeler asks: "Are the laws of physics eternal and immutable? or are
these laws, like species, mutable and of 'higgledy-piggledy' origin?"
His provisional answer in the essay is that the laws of physics may be
statistical at bottom, "of statistical origin," with the apparent
law-likeness of the world arising from billions of acts of
observer-participancy. The commitment: a successful
principle must *produce* the laws of physics rather than
presuppose them, and the production should look more like statistical
mechanics' production of thermodynamic laws from random molecular
collisions than like Laplace's eternal mathematical law sitting outside
time.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's satisfaction of Criterion 2 is exact for the empirical-anchoring content of the chain of theorems,
and distinct from Wheeler's statistical-origin proposal in
one specific way that warrants comment. The chain of theorems produces the laws
(Schrödinger equation, canonical commutator, Born rule, uncertainty
principle, Klein--Gordon, Dirac, Einstein field equations) as theorems
of the principle rather than as eternal mathematical entities sitting
outside time. The principle itself, $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, has the
reading of a *dynamical* statement --- a statement about
active expansion of the fourth dimension at the velocity of light, with
the role of a static mathematical relation replaced by the role of an
active geometric process that unfolds at every event of $M_{G}$. The
laws are produced as the algebraic shadows of the principle's dynamical
content.

Where the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework diverges from Wheeler's 1983
proposal: the chain of theorems does not require statistical-origin reasoning to
produce the laws. The laws follow deductively from the principle, not
statistically. The strict Second Law of thermodynamics (the only law in
the framework that is genuinely irreversible in form) is produced as a
deductive consequence of $x_4$-expansion structure, with the
irreversibility traceable to the one-way character of $dx_4/dt > 0$
rather than to molecular-collision statistics. Wheeler's intuition that
the laws should be "produced" rather than "presupposed" is honoured; the
specific statistical-origin mechanism Wheeler proposed is replaced by a
deductive-chain mechanism in which the deductive structure itself
plays the role that Wheeler had assigned to statistical aggregation.

#### Criterion 3: the principle must produce spacetime as a theorem, not as a presupposition

Wheeler is explicit: "Compare space-time with cloth. Each is useful
under everyday circumstances to call a manifold. Yet each is exactly
then most obviously not a manifold where it comes to an end, whether in
the selvedge made by the loom, or in the geodesic terminations made by
one of the 'gates of time' --- big bang or big crunch or black hole.
Nowhere more clearly than in the ending of space-time are we warned that
time is not an ultimate category in the description of Nature." The
commitment: spacetime has the reading of a derived
object built from a deeper principle, with the role of a
foundational presupposition sitting at the bottom of the theory replaced
by the role of an integrated kinematic shadow of the deeper underlying
principle.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's satisfaction of Criterion 3 is the cleanest of any criterion in the essay. $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the
dynamical principle of the fourth dimension's active expansion; the
Lorentzian metric of special relativity is produced by integrating the
principle and squaring the resulting integrated coordinate
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}); the Minkowski signature $(-,+,+,+)$ is
forced by $(ict)^2 = -c^2 t^2$; the curved-spacetime structure of
general relativity is produced by $x_4$-curvature in the presence of
stress-energy (Chapter [14](#ch:mcgucken-GR){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:mcgucken-GR"}); spacetime as "the great record parchment"
on which events sit is replaced by spacetime as the algebraic shadow of
the principle's dynamical content. Wheeler's call to derive spacetime
from a deeper principle is answered by the framework.

#### Criterion 4: the principle must have a way to come into being out of nothingness

Wheeler's strongest programmatic statement: "The Universe had to have a
way to come into being out of nothingness, with no prior laws, no Swiss
watchworks, no nucleus of crystallization to help it." Wheeler
distinguishes this nothingness from the vacuum of physics, which already
has structure (geometric, vacuum fluctuations, virtual pairs). The
successful principle must be able to come into being
without prior structure to support it.

The McGucken Principle's satisfaction of Criterion 4 is subtle and warrants careful statement. $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the
simplest first-order ordinary differential equation whose integrand is a
non-trivial constant. It requires the existence of a time parameter $t$
(which is itself a theorem of the principle, integrated as $x_4 = ict$
and rotated to the parameter time of the spatial slice), a fourth
dimension $x_4$ (which the principle defines into existence), the
velocity of light $c$ (which the principle defines as the rate of
expansion), and the imaginary unit $i$ (which marks the perpendicularity
of $x_4$ to the spatial three). All four of these prerequisites are themselves theorems of the principle once it is in
place: the principle is self-supporting in the sense that it
specifies the minimum carrier required for its own statement, and no
more. The "coming into being from nothingness" is realised as the
self-bootstrapping compatibility of the principle with the
minimum carrier it specifies. The simplicity of the principle
is what allows this self-bootstrap: a more complex axiom
would require prerequisites that the axiom itself cannot
supply.

#### Criterion 5: the principle must be derivable from the requirement that the universe should have a way to come into being

Wheeler's most striking criterion is his "Two Tests" near the close of
the essay: "No test of these views looks more like being someday doable,
nor more interesting and more instructive, than a derivation of the
structure of quantum theory from the requirement that everything have a
way to come into being." Wheeler frames this as a research programme:
one should be able to derive quantum mechanics from the requirement that
the universe have a way to come into being. The commitment:
the principle has the role of a forced consequence of the necessity that
the universe come into being, with the role of a freely chosen axiom
replaced by the role of a derived necessity at the level of
the universe's coming-into-being requirement.

The McGucken Principle's satisfaction of Criterion 5 is the criterion
that the present textbook has progressively realised across its
chapters, but warrants the explicit statement here. The principle
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ is the simplest dynamical principle that
produces all of the prerequisites the universe requires: (i)
a four-dimensional spacetime arena (from integrating the principle),
(ii) a Lorentzian signature for that arena (from squaring the integrated
coordinate), (iii) complex amplitudes on that arena (from the
perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the spatial three), (iv) an action quantum
$\hbar$ (from action per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation of $x_4$-advance),
(v) the velocity of light $c$ (as the rate of $x_4$-expansion), (vi) the
strict Second Law (from the one-way character of $dx_4/dt > 0$), (vii)
the production of probability from complex amplitudes (from the modulus
operation as the exteriorization of $i$,
Remark [10.2](#rmk:modulus-boundary){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:modulus-boundary"}). Any simpler principle would fail to
produce one or more of these prerequisites; any more complex principle
would have redundancy that contradicts Newton's Rule I and
Einstein's supreme-goal criterion. The principle is forced by the
minimality of the carrier needed for the universe to come
into being, exactly in the form Wheeler called for.

### Engagement through Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel {#sec:wheeler-channels}

Wheeler's 1983 essay contains the materials for the
dual-channel architecture of the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, although Wheeler
did not articulate it in those terms. The two channels appear in
Wheeler's essay in three specific places: the beam-splitter (Figure 4,
with routes labelled $A$ and $B$), the delayed-choice experiment
(Figures 4 and 6), and the dialog about the line of demarcation between
observer and observed. The present section reads each of these through
the Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel distinction and shows the fit.

#### The beam-splitter and the channel of routes

Wheeler's Figure 4 (the beam splitter) shows a photon entering at
point 1, encountering a half-silvered mirror that splits the beam into
two routes labelled $2a$ and $2b$, reflected by mirrors $A$ and $B$ to a
crossing point, and registered by counters or by an additional
half-silvered mirror at the crossing. Wheeler emphasises: "It travels
only one route, but it travels both routes; it travels both routes, but
it travels only one route. What nonsense!" He then invokes Bohr's
resolution: the two experiments (with and without the final
half-silvered mirror) are different experimental arrangements, and the
photon's behaviour depends on which arrangement is chosen.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's reading: Wheeler's beam-splitter is a canonical
worked example of the dual-channel architecture at the experimental
level. Without the final half-silvered mirror ("which route"
measurement), the apparatus performs the McGucken-Wick rotation on
Geometric Channel's geometric content, registering the photon at one of the two
counters with Born-rule probability $1/2$ each, with Algebraic Channel's unitary
group destroyed at the registration event (the photon's quantum state
collapses to one detector's pointer state). With the final half-silvered
mirror in place ("both routes" measurement), the apparatus does not
perform the Wick rotation on Geometric Channel's content at the crossing point;
instead, Geometric Channel's forward and conjugate $x_4$-expansions interfere
geometrically at the half-silvered mirror, producing the constructive
and destructive interference patterns Wheeler describes. The apparent
paradox ("one route or both routes?") dissolves: in the first
experimental arrangement, Geometric Channel's content is registered via Wick
rotation (real positive Born probability for one route); in the second,
Geometric Channel's content is interfered geometrically (no Wick rotation,
complex amplitudes overlap on the McGucken Sphere). The choice of
experimental arrangement is the choice of whether to perform the Wick
rotation on Geometric Channel at the crossing point.

That Wheeler labelled his routes $A$ and $B$ in 1983 is a remarkable
historical coincidence with the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's labelling of
channels $A$ and $B$ in 2024--2026. Wheeler's labels refer to the
spatial paths of the photon; the framework's labels refer to the
algebraic-symmetry and geometric-propagation channels of derivation. The
significance: Wheeler's beam-splitter is a physical realisation in which the Geometric Channel is the one whose content the apparatus operates on directly, while Algebraic Channel's content
(the unitary algebraic-symmetry generator) is destroyed at the
registration event. The historical coincidence of labels is acknowledged
here; the framework's $A$ and $B$ refer to derivation channels, distinct
from Wheeler's route labels, but the compatibility between
Wheeler's physical example and the framework's algebraic structure is
exact.

#### The delayed-choice experiment as the apparatus-performed Wick rotation

Wheeler's delayed-choice version of the beam-splitter (Figure 4 lower
and Figure 6 for the cosmological version) extends the experiment by
allowing the experimenter to decide whether to insert the final
half-silvered mirror *after* the photon has already begun its travel.
Wheeler observes: "We, now, by moving the mirror in or out, have an
unavoidable effect on what we have a right to say about the already past
history of that photon." In the cosmological version (Figure 6), the
photon's travel is from a quasar billions of light-years away, lensed by
an intervening galaxy, and the decision whether to register "which
route" or "both routes" is made on Earth billions of years after the
photon was emitted.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's reading: the delayed-choice experiment is the
physical realisation of the temporal-locus of the apparatus-performed
McGucken-Wick rotation. The Wick rotation does not occur "during the
photon's travel" (which would conflict with relativistic locality); it
occurs *at the registration event* on the apparatus's three-dimensional
slice. Before the registration event, the photon's Geometric Channel content is
an expanding McGucken Sphere on $\mathcal{M}_G$, with its
forward-conjugate $x_4$-expansion overlap content carrying both routes
simultaneously. At the registration event, the apparatus's choice of
measurement configuration (mirror in or out) determines whether the Wick
rotation is performed on Geometric Channel at the crossing point: if performed,
the geometric content registers as one route (Born-rule probability for
one detector); if not performed, the geometric content interferes
(Born-rule probability for the constructive-interference detector).

The "delayed choice" has the reading of a temporal-locus
specification of the apparatus-performed Wick rotation: the rotation
occurs when and where the apparatus is configured, with the role of a
backward-in-time causation replaced by the role of a forward-in-time
specification of where and when on the apparatus's three-dimensional
spatial slice the Wick rotation is performed. The Born density that
produces the registered detector's real positive probability arises at
the apparatus-performed Wick rotation, with the rotation's
spatial--temporal location at the apparatus event on the spatial slice
(the cosmological-scale Figure 6 establishes this at maximum extent: the
rotation event is on Earth, billions of years after emission, with the
Born-rule probability for the registered detector determined at the
apparatus event). Wheeler's resolution ("no elementary phenomenon is a
phenomenon until it is a registered (observed) phenomenon") has the
reading of the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's resolution: the
modulus-squaring that produces the real Born density occurs at the
apparatus-performed Wick rotation, with the rotation event on the
spatial slice rather than along the photon's earlier geometric travel.
The cosmological-scale delayed-choice experiment of Wheeler's Figure 6
establishes the temporal-locus claim at maximum extent: the photon's
geometric Geometric Channel content has been propagating for billions of years
through the lensing galaxy and around its two paths; the apparatus's
Wick rotation occurs at the receptor on Earth, billions of years after
emission; and the Born-rule probability for the registered detector is
determined at the apparatus event.

This is the identity that the present textbook's
Corollary [10.1](#cor:channel-asymmetry-measurement-problem){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:channel-asymmetry-measurement-problem"} of
Chapter [10](#ch:measurement-resolved){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:measurement-resolved"} makes formal. The corollary states
that Process 1 (measurement-event collapse) is the apparatus-performed
Wick rotation acting on both channels jointly: destroying Algebraic Channel's
unitary group at the registration event and transporting Geometric Channel's
geometric content from Lorentzian to Euclidean signature. Wheeler's
delayed-choice experiment is the physical realisation of this corollary,
established forty-three years before the corollary's formal statement.

#### The line of demarcation between observer and observed

Wheeler's dialog continues: "The necessity for that line of separation
is the most mysterious feature of the quantum. We take that demarcation
as being, if not the central principle, the clue to the central
principle in constructing out of nothing everything." He invokes Bohr's
stick (the same physical object can be probed or probe, depending on how
one chooses to use it; the line of demarcation moves from one end to the
other of the stick depending on the choice). And he asks: "Do we possess
today any mathematical or legalistic formula for what the line is or
where it is to be drawn? No."

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's reading: the line of demarcation Wheeler points
to is the boundary between Algebraic Channel's unitary content and Geometric Channel's
registered geometric content, and the modulus operation $|\,\cdot\,|^2$
is the precise mathematical formula for where the line is drawn.
Remark [10.2](#rmk:modulus-boundary){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:modulus-boundary"} of
Chapter [10](#ch:measurement-resolved){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:measurement-resolved"} states this exactly: quantum
mechanics is fully derivable through Algebraic Channel's content up to and not
including the modulus operation; the modulus is the exact location at which Algebraic Channel's complex-unitary content meets Geometric Channel's
apparatus-registered real-outcome content via the apparatus-performed
Wick rotation at the registration event. The line of demarcation that
Wheeler in 1983 said was the most mysterious feature of the quantum is
located, in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, at the modulus operation that
converts $\psi \in \mathbb{C}$ into $|\psi|^2 \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$
at the registration event.

Wheeler asks: "Do we possess today any mathematical or legalistic
formula for what the line is or where it is to be drawn?" The
framework's answer: yes --- the modulus operation, which sits at the
boundary where Algebraic Channel ends and Geometric Channel's
Euclidean-signature reading begins. Wheeler's 1983 question receives a
2026 answer.

### Fulfillment of Wheeler's program {#sec:wheeler-fulfillment}

The cumulative engagement of
§§[15.2](#sec:wheeler-program){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:wheeler-program"}--[15.3](#sec:wheeler-channels){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:wheeler-channels"} establishes that the McGucken
framework fulfills Wheeler's program in *Law Without Law*
at five essential points. The present closing section summarises the
fulfillment explicitly.

**(1) The one-principle requirement.** Wheeler invokes Leibniz: *omnibus
ex nihilo ducendis sufficit unum*. The framework's principle
is $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$, a single dynamical principle of first-order
in time. All of quantum mechanics, special relativity, general
relativity, and the foundations of thermodynamics descend as theorems.
The one-principle criterion is met.

**(2) The production of law from a deeper structure.** Wheeler asks for
laws produced rather than presupposed. The framework's laws
(Schrödinger, canonical commutator, Born rule, uncertainty,
Klein--Gordon, Dirac, Einstein field equations, Second Law) have the
reading of derived theorems of the principle, with the role
of independently-postulated foundational equations replaced by the role
of derived consequences of $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ along the Geometric Channel
and Algebraic Channel routes. The production-of-law criterion is met, with the
deductive-chain mechanism replacing Wheeler's proposed
statistical-origin mechanism while preserving its intent.

**(3) Spacetime derived as theorem.** Wheeler asks for spacetime to have
the role of a theorem of a deeper principle, with the role of a
foundational presupposition sitting at the bottom of the theory replaced
by the role of a derived consequence of the deeper principle. The
framework derives the Lorentzian arena $M_{1,3}$ as the squaring of the
integrated principle
(Theorem [9.2](#thm:hilbert-arena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:hilbert-arena"}), with the curved-spacetime structure of
GR following from $x_4$-curvature in the presence of stress-energy
(Chapter [14](#ch:mcgucken-GR){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:mcgucken-GR"}). The spacetime-as-theorem criterion is met.

**(4) Coming into being out of nothingness.** Wheeler asks for a
principle that can come into being without prior structure to support
it. The McGucken Principle is self-bootstrapping: it
specifies the minimum carrier required for its own statement (a time
parameter, the fourth dimension, the velocity of light, the imaginary
unit), and all four of these prerequisites are themselves
theorems of the principle. The self-bootstrap criterion is met by the
simplicity of the principle.

**(5) Derivation of quantum theory from the requirement that the
universe have a way to come into being.** Wheeler's "Two Tests" close
states this explicitly. The framework's chain of theorems
(Chapter [9](#ch:hilbert-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:hilbert-theorem"}) derives the Hilbert space, the Born
rule, the canonical commutator, the uncertainty principle, the
Schrödinger equation, and the Dirac--von Neumann axioms DvN-1 through DvN-6 as
corollaries of the principle. The minimality of
$\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ as the simplest dynamical principle producing
the prerequisites for the universe to come into being is the
framework's answer to Wheeler's call. The Wheeler-test criterion is met.

#### The answer to *"Why the quantum?"*

Wheeler's lifelong question, posed to the author at Princeton in 1986
and present throughout his published work, was *Why the
quantum?* --- why does the world exhibit quantum-mechanical structure at
all, and what deeper principle accounts for the existence of complex
amplitudes, the canonical commutator, the Born rule, the uncertainty
principle, and the Schrödinger evolution? The orthodox tradition's
answer to this question has been silence or interpretation; the McGucken
framework's answer is the chain of theorems.

The quantum is because $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$. The Hilbert space is
the spatial-slice projection of the principle. The complex amplitudes
are forced by the perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the spatial three. The
canonical commutator is the Stone-theorem reading of the principle's
translation invariance, with both $i$ and $\hbar$ derived (the $i$ from
perpendicularity of $x_4$, the $\hbar$ from action per radian of the Compton-frequency
oscillation). The Born rule is the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing of
forward and conjugate $x_4$-expansions on the McGucken Sphere. The
uncertainty principle is the Robertson--Cauchy--Schwarz bound on the
derived commutator with the $\hbar/2$ decomposed into physical $\hbar$
(action quantum) and mathematical $1/2$ (Robertson constant). The
Schrödinger equation is the quantised master equation
$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ of the principle's four-vector form. The
measurement problem is the orthodox-tradition's symptom of
lacking the dual-channel diagnostic that identifies the
apparatus-performed Wick rotation as a single operation acting on both
channels jointly.

The quantum, in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, is what the active expansion of
the fourth dimension looks like to an apparatus on the spatial slice.
Wheeler asked the question; the framework supplies the answer. The form
of the answer --- one principle, exhaustive deductive output, empirical
anchoring at every node, dual-channel disjointness as the
robustness signature --- is the form Wheeler programmed for
across his published work and most explicitly in *Law Without Law*.

#### The unbroken chain, completed

The closing of Chapter [9](#ch:hilbert-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:hilbert-theorem"}
§[9.13](#sec:heritage-simple-principles){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:heritage-simple-principles"} traced the heritage of
simple principles from Euclid through Newton, Hilbert,
Einstein, and Dirac to Wheeler. The present chapter completes the chain
by stating the specific fulfillment of Wheeler's program by

est* (Newton, 1726) through *deepening the foundations* (Hilbert, 1918)
through *the supreme goal of all theory is to make the irreducible basic
elements as simple and as few as possible* (Einstein, 1933) through *a
physical law must possess mathematical beauty* (Dirac, 1956) to *omnibus
ex nihilo ducendis sufficit unum* (Leibniz via Wheeler, 1983), and
through Wheeler's question *Why the quantum?* to its answer in the
McGucken Principle.

The author of the present textbook honours his master by completing the
program the master set. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework has the reading of the framework of a student who realises the specific program
the master programmed for, with the role of a successor framework that

specified, in *Law Without Law* and throughout his published work, the

essential criteria, with the role of a metaphorical or rhetorical
