## The Six Wightman Axioms of Relativistic Quantum Field Theory (W1–W6) as Forced Theorems of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ {#ch:wightman-axioms}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


The Wightman axioms (Wightman 1956; Streater–Wightman 1964, *PCT, Spin
and Statistics, and All That*) are the standard axiomatic framework for
relativistic quantum field theory. Six axioms — W1 (separable complex
Hilbert space), W2 (Poincaré covariance via a strongly continuous
unitary representation), W3 (microcausality — field operators at
spacelike separation (anti-)commute), W4 (field operators as
operator-valued distributions on a dense domain), W5 (existence and
uniqueness of a Poincaré-invariant vacuum vector), W6 (Spectrum
Condition — joint spectrum of the four-momentum operator contained in
the closed forward light cone) — supply the algebraic scaffolding on
which seventy years (1956–2026) of axiomatic and constructive QFT
have rested.

Of the six, W1–W5 are sign-blind on the $+ic$ orientation: each is
invariant under the $+ic \leftrightarrow -ic$ involution. **W6 is not
sign-blind**: the Spectrum Condition explicitly selects the forward
light cone, excluding negative-energy states. Wightman 1956 imposed W6
as an independent axiom — it cannot be derived from W1–W5 alone
(Streater–Wightman 1964; Haag 1992, *Local Quantum Physics*). This
imposed-axiom status has stood for seventy years as an unexplained
fact of axiomatic QFT: the sixth axiom carries the
directional content of quantum field theory without further
mathematical justification within the algebraic apparatus.

The present chapter establishes that **all six Wightman axioms are
forced theorems of the McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$**,
derived via the chain of theorems $\mathcal{M}_G \to \mathcal{C}_M
\to \mathbb{M}_{1,3} \to \text{Sphere bundle} \to \mathcal{V} \to
\mathcal{H}$ from the source paper *Minkowski Space and Hilbert Space
Derived and Unified via the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic* (McGucken,
E., 2026, v138; elliotmcguckenphysics.com; hereafter [MG-MH-2026] with
theorem-level cross-reference at §16.15.13). Six operative components
(C1)–(C6) of the McGucken Principle are invoked at specified chain of theorems
levels, with each Wightman sub-axiom traceable to one or more
components with rigorous derivation. **The seventy-year-unexplained
W6 descends specifically as the algebraic expression of the McGucken
Sphere's $+ic$ forward-orientation at every event of Minkowski space,
supplying the derivation Wightman could not produce from within the
sign-blind algebraic apparatus.**


### Prior work on the Wightman axioms: what has been attempted {#sec:wightman-prior}

Chapter [9](#ch:hilbert-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:hilbert-theorem"} catalogues twenty-three programmes that
attempted to derive the complex separable Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H}$ (§[9.6](#sec:hilbert-prior){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:hilbert-prior"}). The corresponding survey for W1--W6 is
shorter, and the scope of each entry is stated here so that the claim of
the present chapter can be located against it. Six lines of work bear on
the axioms. Each reformulates them, reconstructs a theory from them,
establishes a consequence of them, or constructs models satisfying them.
None derives them from a statement about spacetime.

**(1) Wightman 1956: the axioms and the reconstruction theorem.**
Wightman's *Quantum Field Theory in Terms of Vacuum Expectation Values*
(*Phys. Rev.* **101**, 860--866, 1956) introduced the axioms together
with the reconstruction theorem: a set of vacuum expectation values
satisfying the axioms determines a field theory --- Hilbert space,
fields, and vacuum vector --- uniquely up to unitary equivalence. The
direction of that theorem is from the axioms to the theory. The axioms
themselves are stated as conditions abstracted from practice; in
Summers's survey of the programme they are described as "a rigorous
formulation of tacit assumptions made in nearly all heuristic field
theories" (Summers, *A Perspective on Constructive Quantum Field
Theory*, arXiv:1203.3991, 2012). *Scope: reconstructs a theory from the
axioms; supplies no derivation of the axioms.*

**(2) Osterwalder--Schrader 1973, 1975: translation between axiom
systems.** The Osterwalder--Schrader theorem (*Commun. Math. Phys.*
**31**, 83, 1973; **42**, 281, 1975) gives conditions on Euclidean
$n$-point functions --- regularity, Euclidean invariance, reflection
positivity, symmetry, cluster property --- under which analytic
continuation produces Wightman functions. In Summers's statement,
"Osterwalder and Schrader showed that an inductive construction of
analytic continuations applied to these Schwinger functions yields a set
of Wightman functions satisfying the Wightman axioms." This is the
closest result in the literature to a derivation of W1--W6, and it
derives them from a second axiom set rather than from physical content:
reflection positivity is itself imposed, and
§[Wick.6](#sec:OS-reflection-positivity-as-W6-inverse){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:OS-reflection-positivity-as-W6-inverse"} of the present
book identifies it as the Wick-inverse image of W6, so the orientation
content is carried across the translation rather than explained by it.
*Scope: axiom set to axiom set, with the directional content preserved
and unexplained on both sides.*

**(3) Haag--Kastler 1964: a parallel axiomatization.** *An Algebraic
Approach to Quantum Field Theory* (*J. Math. Phys.* **5**, 848, 1964)
replaces fields with a net of local algebras indexed by spacetime
regions. The relation between the two systems is close without either
producing the other: a Wightman theory yields a Haag--Kastler net under
additional technical assumptions, and the reverse passage requires
recovering pointlike fields from the net. Summers records the
relationship and the preference within the algebraic programme, holding
that nets are "more *intrinsic* than the associated quantum fields,
which are used primarily for computational convenience." *Scope: an
alternative axiom system at the same level; the Poincaré covariance and
spectrum conditions reappear in it as assumptions on the net.*

**(4) Bisognano--Wichmann 1975: a consequence drawn from the axioms.**
*On the duality condition for a Hermitian scalar field* (*J. Math.
Phys.* **16**, 985--1007, 1975) takes a Wightman theory as input and
derives modular structure from it: the modular group of a wedge algebra
with the vacuum vector coincides with the Lorentz boosts preserving the
wedge, the modular conjugation is $J_W = \Theta\,U(R_W(\pi))$ with
$\Theta$ the PCT operator, and wedge duality holds. The Reeh--Schlieder
theorem (Reeh--Schlieder 1961), which gives the vacuum as a cyclic
vector for the algebra of any open region, sits in the same relation.
*Scope: theorems downstream of W1--W6, with the axioms as hypotheses.*

**(5) Constructive quantum field theory: models satisfying the axioms.**
The constructive programme (Glimm--Jaffe and successors) builds models
and verifies the axioms of them. Its record is dimension-dependent:
$P(\phi)_2$, Yukawa$_2$, $\phi^4_3$ and the sine-Gordon model have been
constructed with nontrivial $S$-matrices, while in four spacetime
dimensions Summers records that "at this point in time only a few models
have been constructed in four spacetime dimensions." *Scope: existence
of theories satisfying the axioms, which presupposes the axioms as the
criterion of success.*

**(6) Weinberg 1995: fields from symmetry, given quantum mechanics.**
Weinberg's construction (*The Quantum Theory of Fields*, Vol. I, 1995)
builds the field content of relativistic quantum theory from Lorentz
invariance, the Wigner classification of Poincaré representations, and
cluster decomposition. Of the six lines listed here this is the nearest
to a derivation from principles, and its inputs are the quantum
formalism itself: a Hilbert space of states, unitary evolution, and the
probability interpretation --- which is to say the Dirac--von Neumann
axioms of
Chapter [9](#ch:hilbert-theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:hilbert-theorem"}. W1 and W2 are among its premises rather
than among its results. *Scope: derives field structure given the
quantum formalism and Poincaré symmetry.*

### The Wightman 1956 axiomatic system: verbatim statement {#sec:wightman-1956-statement}

The six Wightman axioms with sub-axiom decomposition, as stated in
[MG-MH-2026 §16.15.13]:

**Axiom W1 (Hilbert space).** *The states of the system form a
separable complex Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$:*

- *(W1.a) Complex vector space structure: $\mathcal{H}$ is a vector
  space over $\mathbb{C}$.*
- *(W1.b) Sesquilinear inner product:
  $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle: \mathcal{H} \times \mathcal{H} \to
  \mathbb{C}$ is conjugate-linear in the first argument and linear in
  the second.*
- *(W1.c) Conjugate symmetry:
  $\langle \varphi, \psi \rangle = \overline{\langle \psi, \varphi
  \rangle}$.*
- *(W1.d) Positive-definiteness:
  $\langle \psi, \psi \rangle \geq 0$ with equality iff $\psi = 0$.*
- *(W1.e) Cauchy-completeness in the norm
  $\|\psi\| = \sqrt{\langle \psi, \psi \rangle}$, giving Hilbert
  structure when combined with the parallelogram identity.*
- *(W1.f) Separability: $\mathcal{H}$ admits a countable dense subset.*

**Axiom W2 (Poincaré covariance).** *The Poincaré group
$\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3) = \mathbb{R}^{1,3} \rtimes \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$
acts on $\mathcal{H}$ via a strongly continuous unitary representation
$U(a, \Lambda)$:*

- *(W2.a) Group homomorphism: $U(g_1 g_2) = U(g_1) U(g_2)$ for all
  $g_1, g_2 \in \mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$.*
- *(W2.b) Identity: $U(e) = \mathbb{1}_{\mathcal{H}}$.*
- *(W2.c) Unitarity:
  $U(g)^\dagger U(g) = U(g) U(g)^\dagger = \mathbb{1}_{\mathcal{H}}$.*
- *(W2.d) Strong continuity: for each $\psi \in \mathcal{H}$, the map
  $g \mapsto U(g) \psi$ is norm-continuous.*

**Axiom W3 (Microcausality).** *Field operators at spacelike-separated
spacetime points (anti-)commute:*

- *(W3.a) Bosonic commutation:
  $[\hat{\phi}(x), \hat{\phi}(y)] = 0$ for spacelike $(x - y)^2 > 0$.*
- *(W3.b) Fermionic anticommutation:
  $\{\hat{\psi}(x), \hat{\psi}(y)\} = 0$ for spacelike
  $(x - y)^2 > 0$.*
- *(W3.c) Spin-statistics correlation: integer-spin fields are bosonic;
  half-integer-spin fields are fermionic.*

**Axiom W4 (Operator-valued distributions on dense domain).** *Field
operators $\hat{\phi}(x)$ are operator-valued distributions on a dense
domain $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{H}$:*

- *(W4.a) Operator-valuedness: for each $x \in \mathbb{M}_{1,3}$,
  $\hat{\phi}(x)$ is a generator of Hilbert-space content, not a
  scalar.*
- *(W4.b) Distributional character: $\hat{\phi}(x)$ at sharp $x$ is
  unbounded; only smeared
  $\hat{\phi}(f) = \int f(x) \hat{\phi}(x)\, d^4x$ for
  $f \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{M}_{1,3})$ is densely defined.*
- *(W4.c) Dense domain: there is a dense subspace
  $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{H}$ such that
  $\hat{\phi}(f) \mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{D}$ for all
  $f \in \mathcal{S}$.*
- *(W4.d) Linearity in test function:
  $\hat{\phi}(\alpha f + \beta g) = \alpha \hat{\phi}(f) + \beta
  \hat{\phi}(g)$.*

**Axiom W5 (Unique Poincaré-invariant vacuum).** *There exists a unique
Poincaré-invariant unit vector $|0\rangle \in \mathcal{H}$ (the
vacuum):*

- *(W5.a) Existence: $\exists\, |0\rangle \in \mathcal{H}$ with
  $\||0\rangle\| = 1$.*
- *(W5.b) Poincaré invariance: $U(g) |0\rangle = |0\rangle$ for all
  $g \in \mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$.*
- *(W5.c) Uniqueness up to phase.*

**Axiom W6 (Spectrum Condition).** *The joint spectrum of the
four-momentum operator $P^\mu = (\hat{H}/c, \hat{\mathbf{P}})$ is
contained in the closed forward light cone $\overline{V_+}$ in
momentum space:*

- *(W6.a) $P^\mu$ are commuting self-adjoint operators.*
- *(W6.b) $\hat{H}$ has non-negative spectrum:
  $\mathrm{Spec}(\hat{H}) \subset [0, \infty)$.*
- *(W6.c) Joint spectrum in closed forward light cone:
  $\mathrm{Spec}(P^\mu) \subset \overline{V_+} = \{p^\mu : p^\mu p_\mu
  \leq 0,\ p^0 \geq 0\}$.*
- *(W6.d) One-particle sector supported on positive-mass-shell
  hyperboloid $H_m^+ = \{p^\mu : p^\mu p_\mu = -m^2 c^2,\ p^0 > 0\}$.*

### The chain of theorems: six operative components (C1)–(C6) of the McGucken Principle {#sec:six-components}

The McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ asserted at every event
of a formal 4D arena unpacks into six components, each invoked at
specific levels of the chain of the derivations to follow [MG-MH-2026
§16.15.13.0]:

- **(C1) Rate clause**: $|dx_4/dt| = c$ — the invariant rate of
  $x_4$-advance, supplying the constant $c$.
- **(C2) Perpendicularity marker $i$**: $i^2 = -1$ marks $x_4 \perp
  (x_1, x_2, x_3)$, encoding the perpendicularity squared flipping from
  Euclidean $+1$ to Lorentzian $-1$ on the constraint surface.
- **(C3) Action quantum $\hbar$**: per radian of the Compton-frequency oscillation of
  $x_4$-advance.
- **(C4) Per-event universality**: the principle holds at every event
  of the formal arena identically with no preferred event.
- **(C5) Sphere-generation clause**: at every event, the McGucken
  Sphere $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ is the null wavefront expanding from $E$ at
  rate $+ic$.
- **(C6) Sphere self-replication (Huygens–Fresnel–Kirchhoff)**: every
  point of a Sphere is the center of a new Sphere, supplying a
  continuum-of-Spheres at every event of the wavefront.

The directional clause "$+ic$ rather than $\pm ic$" is implicit in (C5)
(Sphere expansion has forward-direction orientation) and in (C1) read
together with the principle's sign. When invoked explicitly it is
labeled *(C1 directional)*.

The chain of theorems is:

$$\mathcal{M}_G \xrightarrow{\Phi_M = 0} \mathcal{C}_M
\xrightarrow{\eta_{\mu\nu}} \mathbb{M}_{1,3}
\xrightarrow{\mathcal{M}_E(t)} \text{(Sphere bundle)}
\xrightarrow{\text{Def 2.6}} \mathcal{V} \xrightarrow{L^2} \mathcal{H}$$

with each level of the chain constructed from the prior by a specific
operation forced by the McGucken content at that level. Level 2 is the
constraint surface $\mathcal{C}_M = \{\Phi_M = x_4 - ict = 0\}$ where
the integrating substitution holds. Level 3 equips the surface with the
Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-c^2, +1, +1, +1)$
from $(ic)^2 = -c^2$ (Lemma 2.5 of [MG-MH-2026]). Level 4 generates
the McGucken Sphere $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ at every event as the null
wavefront at $+ic$. Level 5 constructs the wavefunction space
$\mathcal{V} = \{\psi: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{C}\}$ by
path-integrating $\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$ over Sphere-wavefront paths
(Definition 2.6 with Theorem 3.1 supplying the imaginary unit and
Frobenius $\mathbb{C}$ selection). Level 6 is the L²-Cauchy completion
$\mathcal{H} = L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ (non-relativistic
spatial-slice case) or $\mathcal{H}_{m,s} = L^2(H_m^+, d\mu_m) \otimes
V_s$ (relativistic one-particle case with mass $m$ and spin $s$).

The integrating substitution $x_4 = ict$ (Lemma 2.5 of [MG-MH-2026])
is the Wick rotation that identifies the physical-spacetime constraint
surface as the image of the imaginary-time slice. The Wick-rotation
framing is therefore the chain of theorems's own internal content: the
principle's directional content $+ic$ defines the rotation from formal
Euclidean to physical Lorentzian.

**Theorem 2.4.5 as the base for Poincaré covariance.**
Theorem 2.4.5 of [MG-MH-2026] establishes that both postulates of
special relativity descend from the McGucken Principle: (P1) the
principle of relativity descends from (C4) per-event universality; (P2)
the constancy of $c$ descends from (C1) rate clause. This theorem is
the base for all Poincaré-covariance content of the
Wightman-axiom derivations to follow.

**Dependency order of the six derivations.** The six theorems are not
independent of one another, and the order in which they may be read is
fixed. Theorem W.1 depends on the McGucken Principle alone. Theorem W.2
depends on W.1 for the space it represents. Theorem W.6 uses W.2 for the translation subgroup and
its orthochronous restriction. Theorem W.3 uses W.2 for the Lorentz
frame in which spacelike separation is put at equal parameter time, and
uses W.6 for the mass-shell support $p^0 = E_\mathbf{p}$ on which its
mode expansion is written. Theorem W.5 uses W.2 for invariance and the
positive-energy result of W.6 for uniqueness. Theorem W.4 depends
on W.1 alone. The order is therefore
$$\text{W.1} \longrightarrow \text{W.2} \longrightarrow \text{W.6} \longrightarrow \{\text{W.3},\ \text{W.5}\},
\qquad \text{W.1} \longrightarrow \text{W.4},$$
with no theorem depending on one that depends on it. The chain is
acyclic, and each arrow is a dependence on a derived result rather than
on an axiom of the system being derived.

### Theorem W.1: W1 (Hilbert space) as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ {#sec:W1-derivation}

::: {#thm:W1-hilbert-space .theorem}
**Theorem W.1** (W1 as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$;
[MG-MH-2026] Theorem 16.15.13.1). *The theorem Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H} = L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ (non-relativistic spatial-slice
case) or $\mathcal{H}_{m,s} = L^2(H_m^+, d\mu_m) \otimes V_s$
(relativistic one-particle case) satisfies sub-axioms W1.a–W1.f as
forced consequences of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ via the joint derivation
chain of theorems.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (six sub-derivations, one per sub-axiom).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**(W1.a — Complex vector space structure.)** The wavefunction space
$\mathcal{V}$ of Definition 2.6 [MG-MH-2026] consists of complex-valued
functions $\psi: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{C}$ obtained by
path-integrating the McGucken-Principle action-quantized phase
$\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$ over Sphere-wavefront paths $\gamma$ from
source events to spatial-slice points. The complex character of $\psi$
is supplied by Theorem 3.1 [MG-MH-2026]: the principle
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ carries the imaginary unit $i$ as the algebraic
marker for $x_4$-perpendicularity, with $\mathbb{C}$ selected from the
Frobenius enumeration $\{\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}\}$ by the
physical content of one perpendicular direction $x_4$ (Component C2).

Pointwise sum $(\psi_1 + \psi_2)(\mathbf{x}) := \psi_1(\mathbf{x}) +
\psi_2(\mathbf{x})$ is a valid path-integral configuration by linearity
of Sphere-wavefront contributions at each spatial-slice point (C5 + C6:
Sphere generation and self-replication preserve linearity of wavefront
addition). Scalar multiplication $(\alpha \psi)(\mathbf{x}) := \alpha
\psi(\mathbf{x})$ corresponds to scaling the action-quantization
amplitude of all Sphere wavefronts contributing to $\psi$ (C3). The
eight vector-space axioms hold pointwise on $\mathbb{R}^3$ from the
complex-vector-space structure of $\mathbb{C}$ (which is itself
selected by C2 via Frobenius). The L²-Cauchy completion $\mathcal{H}$
inherits this vector-space structure.

**McGucken-direct sources of W1.a**: C2 via Theorem 3.1 (Frobenius
selection of $\mathbb{C}$); C5 + C6 (path-integral linearity); C3
(action-quantization for scalar multiplication).

**(W1.b — Sesquilinear inner product.)** The inner product on
$\mathcal{V}$ is supplied by Lemma 7.1 [MG-MH-2026]: the rank-2
character of the Lorentzian metric on $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (which
descends from $(ic)^2 = -c^2$ via Lemma 2.5, in turn from the McGucken
Principle) forces

$$\langle \varphi, \psi \rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \varphi^*(\mathbf{x})\, \psi(\mathbf{x})\, d^3 x$$

with conjugate-linearity in the first argument from the antipodal-Sphere
PT-reading (Theorem 7.11 [MG-MH-2026]) and linearity in the second
from path-integral linearity (C5 + C6).

For $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{C}$:
$$\langle \alpha \varphi_1 + \beta \varphi_2, \psi \rangle = \bar\alpha \langle \varphi_1, \psi \rangle + \bar\beta \langle \varphi_2, \psi \rangle,$$
$$\langle \varphi, \alpha \psi_1 + \beta \psi_2 \rangle = \alpha \langle \varphi, \psi_1 \rangle + \beta \langle \varphi, \psi_2 \rangle.$$

The complex conjugation $\alpha \to \bar\alpha$ on scalars is the
algebraic shadow of the antipodal-Sphere PT-reading at the
scalar-multiplication level: $i \to -i$ corresponds to reading the
principle's directional content backward, equivalent to reading the
conjugate Sphere wavefront.

*Which slot carries the conjugation.* The PT-reading supplies the
involution $i \to -i$ but is symmetric between the two arguments and so
cannot by itself select a slot. Two further pieces of McGucken content
make the selection. First, that the pairing is sesquilinear rather than
complex-bilinear is forced by the complexification of the symmetric
rank-2 form $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ together with reality of the Born density
on the diagonal: of the two natural complex extensions of a symmetric
real bilinear form, only the sesquilinear one has a real diagonal for
every argument. Second, which of the two arguments carries the
conjugation is fixed by the emitter–absorber asymmetry of the head-on
$x_4$-collision (Theorem 7.7 [MG-MH-2026]): the conjugate factor is the
absorber's outgoing expansion read in the emitter's frame, so the
conjugation sits on the slot carrying absorber content. Naming that
slot the first argument is a labelling choice; the asymmetry it labels
is derived.

**McGucken-direct sources of W1.b**: Lemma 7.1 (rank-2 sesquilinearity
from $(ic)^2 = -c^2$, C1 + C2 applied to the metric construction);
Theorem 7.11 (antipodal-Sphere PT-reading).

**(W1.c — Conjugate symmetry.)** For $\varphi, \psi \in \mathcal{V}$:
$$\langle \psi, \varphi \rangle = \int \psi^* \varphi\, d^3x = \int (\varphi^* \psi)^*\, d^3x = \overline{\langle \varphi, \psi \rangle}.$$

Conjugate symmetry is forced by the antipodal-Sphere PT-reading: the
involution $i \to -i$ on the integrand is the algebraic shadow of the
PT-reversed Sphere reading, which on integration over $\mathbb{R}^3$
produces the conjugate scalar value.

**McGucken-direct sources of W1.c**: Theorem 7.11 (antipodal-Sphere
PT) + Lemma 7.1 (rank-2 sesquilinearity).

**(W1.d — Positive-definiteness.)** For $\psi \in \mathcal{V}$:
$$\langle \psi, \psi \rangle = \int |\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2\, d^3x \geq 0,$$
with equality iff $\psi = 0$ almost everywhere. Non-negativity is
forced by the geometric content of the Born density at each spatial
point: $|\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ is the McGucken Sphere wavefront overlap
with itself at $\mathbf{x}$ (Theorem 7.4 of [MG-MH-2026]: Born density
as $x_4$-collision of $\psi$ with $\psi^*$ at the spatial point), and
Sphere wavefront content at any spatial point has well-defined
non-negative modulus.

**McGucken-direct sources of W1.d**: Theorem 7.4 (Born density as
Sphere $\psi/\psi^*$ collision); C5 (Sphere generation supplying
well-defined wavefront content).

**(W1.e — Cauchy-completeness and Hilbert structure.)** Two sub-steps:

*Sub-step (i): Cauchy-completeness via Riesz–Fischer (1907).* The space
$L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ of equivalence classes of square-integrable
functions is complete in the norm $\|\psi\|_{L^2} = (\int |\psi|^2
d^3x)^{1/2}$. What the McGucken Principle supplies at this step is
*density*, not completeness. By C5 a Sphere is generated at every event,
and by C6 each wavefront reproduces itself as a superposition of
secondary wavefronts; iterating gives finite superpositions of
Sphere-wavefront contributions at arbitrarily fine resolution, and these
are dense in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$. Completion of a dense
inner-product space is then the standard Lebesgue construction, with
Riesz–Fischer the statement that the completion is $L^2$ itself. The
principle is what makes the pre-Hilbert space the right one to complete;
it does not replace the completion argument, and no claim is made here
that it does.

*Sub-step (ii): Hilbert structure via parallelogram identity.* The
parallelogram identity
$$\|x + y\|^2 + \|x - y\|^2 = 2(\|x\|^2 + \|y\|^2)$$
follows by direct two-line algebraic expansion from Lemma 7.1
[MG-MH-2026] (rank-2 sesquilinear inner product):
$$\|x+y\|^2 + \|x-y\|^2 = \langle x+y, x+y\rangle + \langle x-y, x-y\rangle$$
$$= 2\langle x,x\rangle + 2\langle y,y\rangle = 2(\|x\|^2 + \|y\|^2).$$
With the parallelogram identity established (Lemma 7.6 of [MG-MH-2026]),
the polarization identity
$$\langle x, y \rangle = \tfrac{1}{4}\left[\|x+y\|^2 - \|x-y\|^2 + i\|x+iy\|^2 - i\|x-iy\|^2\right]$$
recovers the inner product from the norm, upgrading the Banach space
to a Hilbert space.

**McGucken-direct sources of W1.e**: Lemma 7.6 (parallelogram identity
by direct two-line algebra from Lemma 7.1's rank-2 sesquilinearity,
which itself descends from $(ic)^2 = -c^2$ via Lemma 2.5, C1 + C2);
C5 + C6 (continuity of Sphere-wavefront propagation under L²-limits).
Riesz–Fischer supplies the real-analysis support.

**(W1.f — Separability.)** The rational-coordinate points $\mathbb{Q}^3
\subset \mathbb{R}^3$ are countable and dense. The three-dimensional
Hermite functions
$$h_{n_1, n_2, n_3}(\mathbf{x}) = H_{n_1}(x_1) H_{n_2}(x_2) H_{n_3}(x_3) e^{-|\mathbf{x}|^2/2}$$
for $(n_1, n_2, n_3) \in \mathbb{N}^3$ form a countable orthonormal
basis of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ with countability following from
$|\mathbb{N}^3| = \aleph_0$.

For the relativistic one-particle case, the positive-mass-shell
hyperboloid $H_m^+$ is a 3-manifold diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$
(parameterized by $\mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ with $p^0 =
E_\mathbf{p} = +\sqrt{|\mathbf{p}|^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4}$), and the
Lorentz-invariant measure $d\mu_m = d^3p/(2 E_\mathbf{p})$ gives
separable $L^2(H_m^+, d\mu_m)$. The spin factor $V_s$ is
finite-dimensional.

The McGucken source of separability is C5, not homogeneity. Per-event
universality by itself places no bound on cardinality: a homogeneous
space need not be separable. What bounds the index set is the structure
of the wavefront. By C5 the Sphere at each event is a $2$-sphere, and by
Proposition 10.7 [MG-MH-2026] the perpendicular $x_4$-radii arriving at
a spatial slice are indexed by solid angle together with source event —
a second-countable index set. A function space over a second-countable
index set has a countable dense subset. Separability is therefore the
cardinality reading of the Sphere's own topology, and the Hermite basis
exhibits one such countable basis explicitly.

**McGucken-direct sources of W1.f**: C5 (Sphere generation, giving a
second-countable wavefront index set via Proposition 10.7); C4
(per-event universality, so the same index structure holds at every
event); countable orthonormal Hermite basis (explicit witness).

Sub-axioms W1.a–W1.f are all forced theorems of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ via the chain of theorems. $\square$
:::

::: {#rmk:W1-summary .remark}
*Remark W.1.A* (Summary of W1 McGucken machinery). W1.a from C2 +
Theorem 3.1 (perpendicularity selection of $\mathbb{C}$), C3 (action quantum),
C5 + C6 (Sphere linearity); W1.b from Lemma 7.1 (C1 + C2 rank-2 metric)
+ Theorem 7.11 (antipodal-Sphere PT); W1.c from Theorem 7.11 + Lemma
7.1; W1.d from Theorem 7.4 (Born density) + C5 (well-defined wavefront);
W1.e from Lemma 7.6 (parallelogram identity from Lemma 7.1) + C5 + C6
(continuity under L²-limits); W1.f from C4 (per-event universality
supplies dense rational structure). Chain of theorems output:
$\mathcal{H} = L^2(\mathbb{R}^3, d^3x)$ (non-relativistic) or
$\mathcal{H}_{m,s} = L^2(H_m^+, d\mu_m) \otimes V_s$ (relativistic
one-particle).
:::

### Theorem W.2: W2 (Poincaré covariance) as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ {#sec:W2-derivation}

::: {#thm:W2-poincare-covariance .theorem}
**Theorem W.2** (W2 as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$;
[MG-MH-2026] Theorem 16.15.13.2). *On the theorem Hilbert space,
the Poincaré group $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$ acts as a strongly continuous
unitary representation satisfying W2.a–W2.d. The representation is
constructed in three settings — covariant field configurations on
$\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, relativistic one-particle Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H}_{m,s}$, non-relativistic spatial-slice $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$
— with each setting internally forced by the McGucken
Principle.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The base for Poincaré-covariance content is
Theorem 2.4.5 [MG-MH-2026]: (P1) the principle of relativity from (C4)
per-event universality; (P2) the constancy of $c$ from (C1) rate
clause. The full ten-parameter Poincaré group $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3) =
\mathbb{R}^{1,3} \rtimes \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ — four translations + six
Lorentz — is the maximal symmetry group of $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$
preserving the Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$, which descends from
$(ic)^2 = -c^2$ via Lemma 2.5. Therefore $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$ is the
theorem symmetry group, with Poincaré-invariance a forced
consequence of C1 + C4.

**Setting 1: Covariant field configurations on $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$.**
This setting is the covariant configuration space of field
configurations on $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, not the one-particle state space
constructed in Theorem W.1; the two are related by the level
identification of Theorem 10.6 [MG-MH-2026], and the $4$-measure used
below is the configuration-space measure rather than the spatial-slice
measure $d^3x$ of W1.
For $(a, \Lambda) \in \mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$, the action
$$[U(a, \Lambda) \Phi](x) := \Phi(\Lambda^{-1}(x - a))$$
is well-defined by C4 (per-event universality: the transformed
configuration is still McGucken-Principle-consistent at every event).

*(W2.a Group homomorphism.)* For $(a_1, \Lambda_1)(a_2, \Lambda_2) =
(a_1 + \Lambda_1 a_2, \Lambda_1 \Lambda_2)$:
$$[U(a_1, \Lambda_1) U(a_2, \Lambda_2) \Phi](x) = \Phi((\Lambda_1 \Lambda_2)^{-1}(x - a_1 - \Lambda_1 a_2)) = [U((a_1, \Lambda_1)(a_2, \Lambda_2)) \Phi](x).$$

*(W2.b Identity.)* $U(0, \mathbb{1}) \Phi(x) = \Phi(\mathbb{1}^{-1}(x
- 0)) = \Phi(x)$.

**McGucken-direct sources of W2.a and W2.b**: C4 (per-event
universality). The principle holds identically at every event, so
relabelling events by a Poincaré element carries a
principle-consistent configuration to a principle-consistent
configuration; composing two relabellings is relabelling by the
product, which is the homomorphism property, and relabelling by the
identity changes nothing. The group law is inherited from the event
set, not imposed on the representation.

*(W2.c Unitarity.)* The 4-measure $c\,d^4x$ on $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is
Lorentz-invariant: $|\det \Lambda| = 1$ for $\Lambda \in
\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ (definition of the connected component preserving
the Lorentzian metric, derived from $(ic)^2 = -c^2$). By change
of variables:
$$\langle U(a, \Lambda) \Phi, U(a, \Lambda) \Psi \rangle = \int \Phi^*(y) \Psi(y) c\,d^4y = \langle \Phi, \Psi \rangle.$$

**McGucken-direct sources of W2.c**: C1 + C2 via Lemma 2.5 and Lemma
7.1 [MG-MH-2026]. The inner product of Theorem W.1 is the rank-2
metric pairing supplied by Lemma 7.1, which descends from
$(ic)^2 = -c^2$ through Lemma 2.5. Any transformation preserving
$\eta_{\mu\nu}$ therefore preserves the pairing, and
$\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ is by construction the group of such
transformations. Unitarity is inherited from the metric that the
principle generates; the determinant condition $|\det \Lambda| = 1$
is the same statement read on the measure.

*(W2.d Strong continuity.)* For $\Phi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{M}_{1,3})$
(dense in $L^2$), translation and Lorentz action converge uniformly to
identity as $g \to e$, hence in L². The active McGucken Sphere at every
event varies smoothly with source location (C4 + C5); the L²-Cauchy
completion inherits smoothness as strong continuity.

**McGucken-direct sources of W2.d**: C1 (the rate of advance is the
same constant $c$ at every event, so the wavefront generated at $E$
depends on $E$ without jump); C5 (a Sphere is generated at every
event, so the map from source event to wavefront is defined
everywhere); C4 (per-event universality, so that dependence is the
same function of the displacement at every event). Continuity of the
group action in the state is the function-space reading of continuity
of the Sphere in its source event.

**Setting 2: Relativistic one-particle Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H}_{m,s} = L^2(H_m^+, d\mu_m) \otimes V_s$.** This is the
natural setting for Wightman's W2 in its original formulation. The
Wigner-induced representation:
$$[U(a, \Lambda) \psi](p) = e^{-i p \cdot a/\hbar}\, D^{(s)}(W(\Lambda, p))\, \psi(\Lambda^{-1} p)$$
where $W(\Lambda, p) = L(\Lambda p)^{-1} \Lambda L(p) \in \mathrm{SO}(3)$
is the little-group element. Group homomorphism follows by the
cocycle condition; unitarity from Lorentz-invariance of
$d\mu_m = d^3p/(2E_\mathbf{p})$ (derived: $H_m^+$ is the
McGucken-derived positive-mass-shell hyperboloid).

**McGucken-internal source of the little group.** The stabilizer of a
timelike $p \in H_m^+$ is the rotation group of the rest-frame spatial
slice at the event where $p$ is realized. By C5 the active McGucken
Sphere at that event is a $2$-sphere carrying a transitive
$\mathrm{SO}(3)$ action, and by C4 the same $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ is
present at every event; the double cover $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is the
Sphere's own spinor structure (the identification used in Theorem W.3
Step 4). The little group is therefore the McGucken Sphere's rotation
group read at the level of four-momentum, rather than an external
construction imposed on the representation.

*The Wigner classification internally.* The unitary irreducible
representations of $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$ are classified by two Casimirs
$C_1 = P^\mu P_\mu = -m^2 c^2$ (mass) and $C_2 = W^\mu W_\mu = -m^2
s(s+1)$ (spin, for $m > 0$). In the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework:

- Mass $m$ parametrizes the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$
  of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront content at the particle (C3 +
  species-independence of C1).
- Spin $s$ parametrizes the universal non-closure quantum's
  rotation-cycle length: $4\pi$ for $s = 1/2$, $2\pi$ for integer spin
  (Theorem 12.11 [MG-MH-2026]).

Scope of this identification. What the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework supplies is
the *content of the labels*: $m$ is the Compton frequency of the
Sphere wavefront (C3, above), and $s$ is the closure length of the
universal non-closure quantum (Theorem 12.11 [MG-MH-2026], above).
What the framework does not supply is the *exhaustiveness* of the
$(m,s)$ list — that every unitary irreducible representation of
$\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$ carries one of these labels is the
Bargmann–Wigner classification (1939, 1947), which enters here as a
consistency check on the labelling rather than as its source.

**Setting 3: Non-relativistic spatial-slice $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$.** At
fixed parameter time $t_0$, the spatial Euclidean subgroup
$\mathrm{ISO}(3) = \mathrm{SO}(3) \rtimes \mathbb{R}^3$ acts unitarily
via $[U(\mathbf{a}, R) \psi](\mathbf{x}) = \psi(R^{-1}(\mathbf{x} -
\mathbf{a}))$; time translations $\psi \mapsto e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}
\psi$ are unitary, with the one-parameter flow supplied by C1 (advance
at constant rate) and its direction by C1 directional; Stone's theorem
packages that flow as $e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}$ with self-adjoint
generator, in the confirmatory role assigned to it by
Remark 4.36 rather than as an external premise. Lorentz boosts
require lifting to Setting 2 via the level identification
(Theorem 10.6 [MG-MH-2026]: $\mathcal{H}$ is the function-space-level
representation of $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$).

Sub-axioms W2.a–W2.d are derived in all three settings as forced
consequences of Poincaré symmetry, itself forced by (C1) rate clause +
(C4) per-event universality via Theorem 2.4.5.

**Principal McGucken Components for W2**: C1 (rate clause, giving the
invariance of $c$ and the one-parameter flows); C1 directional (fixing
the orthochronous component, used again in Theorem W.6); C2
(perpendicularity marker, entering the metric via Lemma 2.5); C4
(per-event universality, giving the group law, the relativity
principle, and strong continuity); C5 (Sphere generation at every
event, giving the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ little group and its
$\mathrm{SU}(2)$ cover); C3 (action quantum, entering the mass label
through $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$); Lemma 2.5 (Lorentzian metric);
Lemma 7.1 (rank-2 pairing); Theorem 2.4.5 (the two special-relativity
postulates); Theorem 12.11 (spin label). Stone's theorem and the
Bargmann–Wigner classification appear in confirmatory roles.
$\square$
:::

### Theorem W.3: W3 (microcausality) as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ {#sec:W3-derivation}

::: {#thm:W3-microcausality .theorem}
**Theorem W.3** (W3 as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$;
[MG-MH-2026] Theorem 16.15.13.3). *The (anti-)commutation of field
operators at spacelike separation, the bosonic vs. fermionic statistics
correlation, and the spin-statistics theorem are all forced
consequences of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ via (a) the spatial-slice
disjointness of McGucken Spheres at spacelike-separated events (C5 +
C1 + C4), (b) the universal non-closure quantum's spin-$s$ instances
of Theorem 12.11 [MG-MH-2026] with $s = 1/2$ instance supplying the
$4\pi$ closure, and (c) the level identity Theorem 10.6
relating manifold-level Sphere geometry to function-space-level
operator algebra.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.*

**Step 1: Spatial-slice disjointness of McGucken Spheres at spacelike
separation.** Consider two events $x, y \in \mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ with
$(x - y)^2 > 0$ (spacelike). By spacelike separation there exists
$\Lambda \in \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ taking $(x - y)$ to purely spatial
$(0, \mathbf{r})$ with $|\mathbf{r}| > 0$ (standard: any spacelike pair
has an equal-parameter-time frame). By Lorentz invariance (Theorem W.2)
it suffices to prove disjointness in this frame.

In equal-parameter-time frame, $x = (t_0, \mathbf{x}_0)$ and $y = (t_0,
\mathbf{y}_0)$ with $|\mathbf{x}_0 - \mathbf{y}_0| = |\mathbf{r}| > 0$.
At $t_0 + \delta$, both events host their own active McGucken Spheres
(C4 per-event universality + C5 Sphere generation). The Sphere
$\mathcal{M}_x(t_0 + \delta)$ has spatial-slice trace
$$S_{\mathbf{x}_0}^2(c\delta) := \{\mathbf{r}' \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |\mathbf{r}' - \mathbf{x}_0| = c\delta\},$$
forced by C1 (rate clause).

By triangle inequality, for $\mathbf{r}' \in S_{\mathbf{x}_0}^2(c\delta)$:
$$|\mathbf{r}' - \mathbf{y}_0| \geq |\mathbf{r}| - c\delta.$$
For $\delta < |\mathbf{r}|/(2c)$: $|\mathbf{r}' - \mathbf{y}_0| >
|\mathbf{r}|/2 > c\delta$, so $\mathbf{r}' \notin
S_{\mathbf{y}_0}^2(c\delta)$. The two Sphere wavefronts have disjoint
spatial-slice traces for parameter-time intervals shorter than the
spacelike-separation time scale.

*The statement at all parameter times.* Microcausality is required for
spacelike separation with no restriction on $\delta$, and C1 gives it
directly. The Sphere generated at $x = (t_0, \mathbf{x}_0)$ reaches the
spatial point $\mathbf{y}_0$ at parameter time $t_0 + |\mathbf{r}|/c$
and at no other, since the radius grows at exactly $c$. That time is
strictly later than $t_0$ because $|\mathbf{r}| > 0$. The event
$y = (t_0, \mathbf{y}_0)$ is therefore not on the Sphere generated at
$x$, at any $\delta$, and by the symmetry of the construction $x$ is
not on the Sphere generated at $y$. No Sphere-wavefront content
generated at either event is registered at the other. The short-time
computation above exhibits the disjointness of the two traces; the
present observation is the statement that Step 2 uses, and it holds for
all parameter times.

**McGucken-direct sources of Step 1**: C1 (rate $c$); C4 (per-event
universality); C5 (Sphere-generation clause).

**Step 2: Bosonic commutation from Sphere disjointness (W3.a).** The
bosonic scalar field on Fock space over $\mathcal{H}_{m,0}$ has mode
expansion
$$\hat{\phi}(x) = \int \frac{d^3p}{(2\pi)^{3/2}\sqrt{2 E_\mathbf{p}}} \left[ \hat{a}_\mathbf{p}\, e^{ip \cdot x/\hbar} + \hat{a}_\mathbf{p}^\dagger\, e^{-ip \cdot x/\hbar} \right]_{p^0 = E_\mathbf{p}}.$$
The restriction $p^0 = E_\mathbf{p}$ is the positive-energy mass-shell
support established in Theorem W.6 (W6.b and W6.d) from C1 directional;
W.6 uses W.2 alone, so the dependence W.6 $\to$ W.3 recorded in the
dependency order above introduces no cycle.
The Pauli–Jordan distribution
$$i \Delta(x - y) = [\hat{\phi}(x), \hat{\phi}(y)] = \int \frac{d^3p}{(2\pi)^3\, 2E_\mathbf{p}} \left[e^{ip \cdot (x-y)/\hbar} - e^{-ip \cdot (x-y)/\hbar}\right]_{p^0 = E_\mathbf{p}}$$
vanishes for spacelike $(x - y)^2 > 0$: by explicit computation in the
equal-parameter-time frame ($x - y = (0, \mathbf{r})$), $\Delta$ becomes
an odd function under $\mathbf{p} \to -\mathbf{p}$ of an integrand that
is even, so the integral vanishes.

The vanishing of the Pauli–Jordan distribution at spacelike separation
is the algebraic manifestation of Sphere disjointness at Step 1: no
Sphere-wavefront content from $x$ has reached $y$ (and vice versa),
so the operator content at $x$ and $y$ carries no mutual algebraic
commutation obstruction.

**Step 3: Fermionic anticommutation from spin-1/2 $4\pi$ closure
(W3.b).** For fermions ($s = 1/2$), the mode expansion involves
Dirac spinors and the round-trip on Sphere geometry closes at $4\pi$
rather than $2\pi$ (Theorem 12.11 instance (4) [MG-MH-2026]: universal
non-closure quantum at spin-$1/2$ instances). The round-trip operator
$\hat{\psi}(x)$-then-$\hat{\psi}(y)$-then-back accumulates a sign from
the half-cycle at $\pi$, producing anticommutation:
$$\{\hat{\psi}(x), \hat{\psi}(y)\} = 0 \text{ for spacelike } (x - y)^2 > 0.$$

**Step 4: Spin-statistics correlation (W3.c) via Theorem 12.11.** The
correlation:
$$s \in \mathbb{Z} \Longleftrightarrow 2\pi\text{ closure} \Longleftrightarrow \text{bosonic} \Longleftrightarrow \text{commutator}.$$
$$s \in \mathbb{Z} + 1/2 \Longleftrightarrow 4\pi\text{ closure} \Longleftrightarrow \text{fermionic} \Longleftrightarrow \text{anticommutator}.$$

The internal source is the Sphere's own rotation symmetry. By C5 the
active McGucken Sphere at every event is $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetric on
the spatial $2$-sphere $S^2$, and by C4 the same symmetry is present at
every event; the double cover $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is the Sphere's spinor
structure, and the two closure lengths $2\pi$ and $4\pi$ are the two
instances of the universal non-closure quantum of Theorem 12.11
[MG-MH-2026]. The representation theory of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ —
irreducibles labelled by $s = 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2, \ldots$, single-valued on
$\mathrm{SO}(3)$ for integer $s$ and double-valued for half-integer —
then confirms that this labelling is complete, in the confirmatory role
of Remark 4.36 rather than as the source of the correlation.

**Principal McGucken Components**: Theorem 12.11 (universal non-closure
quantum classification); C4 + C5 (spatial rotation symmetry of McGucken
Sphere as source of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ little-group structure). $\square$
:::

### Theorem W.4: W4 (operator-valued distributions on dense domain) as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ {#sec:W4-derivation}

::: {#thm:W4-distributions .theorem}
**Theorem W.4** (W4 as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$;
[MG-MH-2026] Theorem 16.15.13.4). *The operator-valued distributional
character of field operators on the theorem Hilbert space is
forced by (a) the active McGucken Sphere wavefront content at every
event of $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (Components C4 + C5), (b) the continuum
cardinality of perpendicular $x_4$-radii at every event (Proposition
10.7 [MG-MH-2026]), (c) the action quantum $\hbar$ supplying the de
Broglie wavelength as natural cutoff scale (Component C3), and (d) the
universal non-closure quantum's canonical-commutator instance (Theorem
12.11 instance (1) [MG-MH-2026]) supplying the unbounded operator
content at sharp points.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.*

**(W4.a — Operator-valuedness.)** The field operator $\hat{\phi}(x)$
at event $x \in \mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is the theorem realization of
the active McGucken Sphere wavefront content at $x$. By C5, every event
generates a McGucken Sphere $\mathcal{M}_x(t)$ whose wavefront
propagates outward at $+ic$; Theorem 10.6 [MG-MH-2026] maps this
manifold-level content to function-space-level operator content:
$\hat{\phi}(x)$ generates or annihilates the Hilbert-space configuration
corresponding to a unit Sphere-wavefront amplitude at $x$.

Concretely in Fock space over $\mathcal{H}_{m,s}$:
$$\hat{\phi}(x) = \int \frac{d^3p}{(2\pi)^{3/2}\sqrt{2E_\mathbf{p}}} \left[ \hat{a}_\mathbf{p}\, e^{ip\cdot x/\hbar} + \hat{a}_\mathbf{p}^\dagger\, e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar} \right]_{p^0 = E_\mathbf{p}}.$$
Both $\hat{a}_\mathbf{p}$ and $\hat{a}_\mathbf{p}^\dagger$ are
operator-valued; their linear combination is operator-valued.

**McGucken-direct sources of W4.a**: C5 (Sphere generation at every
event) supplies the physical content of $\hat{\phi}(x)$; Theorem 10.6
maps to function-space level.

**(W4.b — Distributional character via unboundedness at sharp points.)**
Two equivalent derivations:

*Derivation 1: Via canonical commutator.* $[\hat{\phi}(t, \mathbf{x}),
\hat{\pi}(t, \mathbf{y})] = i\hbar\, \delta^3(\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y})$
implies at least one of $\hat{\phi}, \hat{\pi}$ is unbounded at sharp
points: if both were bounded, their commutator would be bounded, but
$i\hbar\,\delta^3$ is a singular distribution with no bounded
operator-valued realization. By symmetry both are unbounded. The
McGucken-internal source: Theorem 12.11 instance (1) [MG-MH-2026] —
canonical commutator as universal non-closure quantum. The $i$ is the
perpendicularity marker (C2); $\hbar$ is the action quantum (C3);
$\delta^3$ is per-event universality (C4) localized to a single spatial
point.

*Derivation 2: Via continuum of Sphere wavefronts.* At sharp
spacetime point $x$, by Proposition 10.7 [MG-MH-2026] (continuum of
perpendicular $x_4$-radii at every event), the Sphere $\mathcal{M}_x(t)$
has continuum cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$ of outward-pointing radii,
each carrying its own wavelength-frequency-phase-action content (C5).
Accessing all at a sharp point requires integrating over the full
continuum of momentum modes, producing unbounded high-momentum content.
By C6 (Sphere self-replication), every point of every wavefront is
itself the center of a new Sphere, so the continuum accumulates
contributions from a continuum of source events (every event in the
past light cone contributes). The unbounded operator content at sharp
$x$ is the theorem reflection of this multi-source accumulation.

For $f \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{M}_{1,3})$:
$$\hat{\phi}(f) = \int f(x)\, \hat{\phi}(x)\, d^4x$$
converges absolutely by rapid decay of the Fourier transform
$\tilde{f}$, giving a well-defined operator. The smearing restricts
source-event content to $\mathrm{supp}(f)$; rapid decay of $\tilde{f}$
at high momentum corresponds to the natural cutoff supplied by C3 (de
Broglie wavelength $\lambda_{\rm dB} = \hbar c / E$).

**McGucken-direct sources of W4.b**: Theorem 12.11 instance (1)
(canonical commutator unboundedness, C2 + C3 + C4); C5 + C6
(multi-source-event accumulation); Proposition 10.7 (continuum of
perpendicular $x_4$-radii); C3 (de Broglie cutoff).

**(W4.c — Dense domain.)** The smeared field $\hat{\phi}(f)$ acts on
Schwartz space $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^3) \subset L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$
(dense in every $L^p$ by mollification with smooth bumps). Closure
under $\hat{\phi}(f)$: convolution of Schwartz functions is Schwartz.
McGucken-internal: per-event universality (C4) supplies mollification
via superposition of Sphere wavefronts from a continuum of source
events; Sphere-wavefront generation preserves de Broglie-wavelength
scale structure (C3), so smooth wavefunctions remain smooth under
field-operator action.

**McGucken-direct sources of W4.c**: C3 (de Broglie-wavelength scale);
C4 (per-event universality); C5 (Sphere generation preserving
smoothness).

**(W4.d — Linearity in test function.)** For $\alpha, \beta \in
\mathbb{C}$:
$$\hat{\phi}(\alpha f + \beta g) = \int (\alpha f + \beta g)(x)\, \hat{\phi}(x)\, d^4x = \alpha \hat{\phi}(f) + \beta \hat{\phi}(g),$$
by linearity of integration, which corresponds to linearity of
source-event superposition (C4: each source event contributes
independently; integration is the sum-over-events).

**McGucken-direct source of W4.d**: C4 (per-event universality +
linearity of source-event superposition). $\square$
:::

### Theorem W.5: W5 (unique Poincaré-invariant vacuum) as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ {#sec:W5-derivation}

::: {#thm:W5-vacuum .theorem}
**Theorem W.5** (W5 as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$;
[MG-MH-2026] Theorem 16.15.13.5). *The Poincaré-invariant unit vector
$|0\rangle$ exists in the theorem Fock space as the
free-expansion configuration with no McGucken-Sphere collision events;
is Poincaré-invariant by Component C4 (per-event universality)
combined with Lorentz-invariance of the theorem structure; and
is unique up to global phase by the trivial-representation
multiplicity-1 structure of the theorem Fock space.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.*

**(W5.a — Existence as free-expansion configuration.)** By C4, the
McGucken Principle holds at every event of $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$
identically. The *free-expansion configuration* is the theorem
where, at every event $E$, the McGucken Sphere $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$
expands at $+ic$ (C5) *without any Sphere-collision detection event*
anywhere in $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. In Fock space $\mathcal{F} =
\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} S_n^{\pm}[\mathcal{H}_{m,s}^{\otimes n}]$, the
free-expansion corresponds to the $n = 0$ sector $\mathcal{F}_0 =
\mathbb{C}$, with $|0\rangle$ the unit vector there.

The Wightman vacuum in the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework is *not "empty space"* —
it is the free-expansion configuration where active McGucken-Sphere
expansion at $+ic$ is happening at every event without collision. The
vacuum carries active $x_4$-expansion (C4 + C5), full McGucken-Sphere
wavefront content (C5 + C6), zero-point energy from $+ic$ expansion
(C1 + C3), and no Sphere-collision detection events.

**(W5.b — Poincaré invariance.)** By C4, the McGucken Principle is
translation-invariant: shifting every event by fixed $a \in
\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ produces a configuration satisfying the principle
identically at every translated event. So $U(a, \mathbb{1}) |0\rangle
= |0\rangle$.

For Lorentz transformations $\Lambda \in \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$: C1 rate
clause is Lorentz-invariant (Theorem 2.4.5(P2)); C2 perpendicularity
marker is Lorentz-invariant (algebraic structure preserved under
coordinate transformations); C1 directional ($+ic$) is preserved under
proper orthochronous Lorentz transformations (which preserve
time-orientation by definition). Therefore the McGucken Principle is
fully Lorentz-invariant under $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, and the
free-expansion configuration is Lorentz-invariant. Combining: $U(a,
\Lambda) |0\rangle = |0\rangle$ for all $(a, \Lambda) \in
\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$.

**(W5.c — Uniqueness up to phase via multiplicity-1.)**

**Lemma** (Trivial Poincaré representation has multiplicity 1). *The
Fock space $\mathcal{F}$ contains the trivial representation of
$\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$ with multiplicity 1, spanned by the $n = 0$
vacuum vector.*

*Proof.* Decompose into Fock sectors. The $n = 0$ sector $\mathcal{F}_0
= \mathbb{C}$ is one-dimensional with trivial Poincaré action: one copy
of trivial representation.

For $n \geq 1$ sectors: for the trivial representation to appear with
non-zero multiplicity in $\mathcal{F}_n$, $P^\mu = \sum_{i=1}^n p_i^\mu
= 0$ would be required. Each particle's $p_i \in H_m^+$ has $p_i^0 =
E_{\mathbf{p}_i} = +\sqrt{|\mathbf{p}_i|^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4} > 0$ for $m
> 0$ (selected by C1 directional: the $+ic$ orientation of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ gives $u^0 = +c$
and hence $p^0 = mc > 0$ in the rest frame, and the orthochronous group
of Theorem W.2 preserves that sign; Theorem W.6 Step 2 states the
argument in full, and no result of the present theorem is used there).
Total $P^0 =
\sum_i E_{\mathbf{p}_i} > 0$ on $\mathcal{F}_n$ for $n \geq 1$,
contradicting $P^\mu = 0$. The trivial representation does not appear
in $\mathcal{F}_n$ for $n \geq 1$. $\square$

Any normalized Poincaré-invariant vector lies in the one-dimensional
trivial-representation subspace $\mathcal{F}_0 = \mathbb{C}$, unique
up to phase.

**McGucken-internal content of uniqueness.** Any deviation from
free-expansion would introduce a Sphere-collision detection event
carrying positive 4-momentum content by the head-on $x_4$-collision
mechanism (Theorem 7.7 [MG-MH-2026]), breaking the $P^\mu = 0$
Poincaré-invariance condition. The trivial-representation sector is
physically the no-collision sector, one-dimensional by C4 universality
of the free-expansion. Uniqueness is the geometric content of "no
events, anywhere". $\square$
:::

### Theorem W.6: W6 (Spectrum Condition) as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ — the seventy-year-unexplained axiom derived {#sec:W6-derivation}

::: {#thm:W6-spectrum-condition .theorem}
**Theorem W.6** (W6 as forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$;
[MG-MH-2026] Theorem 16.15.13.6). *The Spectrum Condition W6.a–W6.d is
a forced theorem of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$: the $+ic$ orientation of
the McGucken Sphere expansion at every event of $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$
selects the positive-frequency Fourier modes on the mass-shell
hyperboloid, giving positive-energy support of the Hamiltonian and
joint spectrum in the closed forward light cone.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (six-step derivation).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**Step 1: Chain of theorems-output four-momentum operator.** Theorem W.2 supplies
the ten-parameter Poincaré representation $U(a, \Lambda)$ on
$\mathcal{H}_{m,s}$. By Stone's theorem applied to the strongly
continuous unitary translation subgroup $\{U(a, \mathbb{1}) : a \in
\mathbb{R}^{1,3}\}$, there exist self-adjoint operators $P^\mu = (P^0,
\mathbf{P}) = (\hat{H}/c, \hat{\mathbf{P}})$ with $U(a, \mathbb{1}) =
e^{-i a_\mu P^\mu/\hbar}$. The abelian translation subgroup gives
commuting generators $[P^\mu, P^\nu] = 0$ (W6.a).

**McGucken-internal source of Step 1**: C4 (per-event universality:
translating by $a_1$ then $a_2$ produces same configuration as
translating by $a_1 + a_2$, no path-dependence — additivity of
translations equivalent to commutation of generators). Stone's theorem
is the supporting machinery.

**Step 2: Forward-direction Sphere expansion selects positive-frequency
Fourier modes.** The Wigner classification supplied by Theorem W.2 labels
the irreducible representations of $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$ by $(m, s)$
together with a sign of energy: for each $m > 0$ and each $s$ there are
two inequivalent irreducible representations, one supported on $p^0 > 0$
and one on $p^0 < 0$. The Poincaré representation alone therefore does
not select between them. The selection is exactly the content of W6, and
the McGucken Sphere supplies it.

By C5 a McGucken Sphere is generated at every event $E \in
\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, and by C1 directional it expands at $+ic$ and not at
$-ic$. By QB4
(Axiom [4.23](#ax:QB4){reference-type="ref" reference="ax:QB4"}) the
$x_4$-phase carried by that wavefront advances at the Compton rate
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ in the rest frame at $E$, accumulating
$\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$ with $S = -mc^2\tau$, so the rest-frame Sphere
amplitude carries
$$\Psi_E \;\propto\; e^{-i\omega_C \tau}.$$
The sense of this rotation is fixed by the sign in $+ic$: an advance at
$-ic$ would give the complex conjugate $e^{+i\omega_C\tau}$. The
orientation clause therefore fixes a phase-rotation sense at every
event, and it is that sense which selects the Fourier branch.

Compare a plane-wave mode $e^{ip \cdot x/\hbar}$ with $p \cdot x = -p^0
x^0 + \mathbf{p} \cdot \mathbf{x}$. In the rest frame at $E$ one has
$\mathbf{p} = \mathbf{0}$ and $x^0 = c\tau$, so the mode reduces to
$e^{-i p^0 c\tau/\hbar}$. Matching its phase-rotation sense to the
Sphere's gives
$$p^0 c \;=\; \hbar\omega_C \;=\; mc^2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
p^0 \;=\; mc \;>\; 0 .$$
The mode whose phase rotates with the Sphere is exactly the $p^0 > 0$
mode; the $p^0 < 0$ mode is its complex conjugate, rotating against the
Sphere's orientation. Equivalently, read on the four-velocity through the
reverse-reading equivalence of
Lemma [4.7](#lem:reverse-reading-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:reverse-reading-equivalence"} (which supplies $d\tau = dt$
in the rest frame), the same orientation gives $u^0 = +c$ and $p^\mu = m
u^\mu$ with $p^0 = mc > 0$; the four-velocity norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$
of §2.3 fixes the magnitude and leaves the sign open, per the
architectural priority of
Remark [4.8](#rmk:bidirectional-equivalence){reference-type="ref"
reference="rmk:bidirectional-equivalence"}.

*Frame-independence of the sign.* Theorem W.2 delivers a representation
of $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$, the proper orthochronous Poincaré group.
Preservation of time-orientation is the defining property of the
orthochronous component: $\Lambda \in \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ carries every
future-directed causal vector to a future-directed causal vector, and
$\overline{V_+}\setminus\{0\}$ is by definition the set of such vectors.
Hence $(\Lambda p)^0 > 0$ for every $\Lambda$ in the group, and no
element of the group can reverse the sign established in the rest frame
at $E$. That the symmetry group is the orthochronous one rather than the
full Lorentz group is itself C1-directional content: the $+ic$
orientation of the advance is the same at every event, so the
transformations relating events preserve it. By C4 (per-event
universality) the same construction holds at every event of
$\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. Therefore
$$\mathrm{Spec}(P^\mu) \subset \{p^0 > 0\}$$
on the one-particle space, which is the positive-energy branch of the
Wigner classification.

**McGucken-internal source of Step 2**: C1 directional ($+ic$ and not
$-ic$, fixing the phase-rotation sense of the Sphere wavefront and the
orthochronous restriction on the symmetry group); C5 (Sphere generation
at every event, carrying the phase whose sense is selected); C3 via QB4
(Axiom [4.23](#ax:QB4){reference-type="ref" reference="ax:QB4"}, Compton
phase at $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$); C1 (rate); C4
(per-event universality, extending the rest-frame
result to every event); C2 (perpendicularity marker, via $x_4 = ix^0$).
Supporting machinery: Lemma 4.7 for the rest-frame four-velocity
reading, the budget $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ of §2.3 for magnitude alone,
and Theorem W.2 for the group. The sign is supplied by the Sphere.

*Remark on what this step does not use.* The argument does not proceed
by declaring negative-frequency Fourier modes backward-propagating. A
Fourier mode $e^{-ip^0 t/\hbar}$ is a basis function on all of $t$ and
carries no direction of propagation; the mode with $p^0 < 0$ is the
complex conjugate of the mode with $p^0 > 0$, not a wavefront running
backwards. Support in the forward light cone in position space and
support on $p^0 > 0$ in momentum space are independent conditions —
the retarded Green's function vanishes for $t < 0$ and nonetheless has
poles at both $p^0 = +\omega_\mathbf{p}$ and $p^0 = -\omega_\mathbf{p}$
— so propagation direction cannot by itself select the energy sign. The
selection is made by the phase-rotation sense that the Sphere's $+ic$
expansion carries at every event, which is where the orientation content
of the principle is located.

*Consistency with the conjugate expansion and with the $-ic$ branch.*
Negative-frequency content is assigned. The conjugate expansion $\psi^*$ of Theorem 7.11 and the
conjugate kernel entering the Born density of Theorem 7.4 carry the
$-ic$ orientation, and the $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = -ic$ branch of
Chapter [21](#ch:antimatter){reference-type="ref"
reference="ch:antimatter"} is the antimatter sector, realized in
second quantization as creation operators for antiparticles of positive
energy. W6 constrains the spectrum of $P^\mu$ on the physical Fock
space; it does not assert that the $-ic$ orientation is absent from the
theory.

**Step 3: Positive-mass-shell hyperboloid as theorem.** For a
free particle of mass $m \geq 0$, the mass-shell constraint $p^\mu p_\mu
= -m^2 c^2$ descends from the Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ via the
dispersion relation $E^2/c^2 = |\mathbf{p}|^2 + m^2 c^2$, itself
derived from $(ic)^2 = -c^2$ via Lemma 2.5 (C1 + C2).

Combining $p^\mu p_\mu = -m^2 c^2$ with $p^0 > 0$ (Step 2):
$$\mathrm{Spec}(P^\mu) \subset H_m^+ := \{p^\mu : p^\mu p_\mu = -m^2 c^2,\ p^0 > 0\}.$$

For $m > 0$: $H_m^+ \subset V_+ = \{p^0 > 0,\ p^\mu p_\mu < 0\}$
strictly. For $m = 0$: $H_0^+ = \partial V_+$ (forward null cone). This
is W6.d.

**Step 4: Hamiltonian spectrum non-negative (W6.b).** The Hamiltonian
$\hat{H}$ on $\mathcal{H}_{m,s}$ is the generator of time translations:
$U(t) = e^{-i\hat{H} t/\hbar}$ (C1 + C1 directional via Theorem W.2).
On momentum eigenstates $|p\rangle$ with $p \in H_m^+$:
$$\hat{H} |p\rangle = E_\mathbf{p} |p\rangle, \quad E_\mathbf{p} = +\sqrt{|\mathbf{p}|^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4} \geq mc^2 \geq 0.$$
Therefore $\mathrm{Spec}(\hat{H}) = [mc^2, \infty)$ (massive) or
$[0, \infty)$ (massless), contained in $[0, \infty)$.

**Step 5: Joint spectrum in closed forward light cone (W6.c,
Fock-space extension).** For multi-particle $\mathcal{F} = \bigoplus_n
S_n^{\pm}[\mathcal{H}_{m,s}^{\otimes n}]$, total 4-momentum on
$\mathcal{F}_n$ is $P^\mu = \sum_{i=1}^n p_i^\mu$ with each $p_i \in
H_m^+$. Sum of vectors in $H_m^+$ is in $\overline{V_+}$ by *convexity
of the closed forward light cone under addition* (fundamental property
of light cones in Lorentzian geometry, derived from Cauchy-Schwarz for
timelike/null vectors). Therefore
$$\mathrm{Spec}(P^\mu)\big|_{\mathcal{F}_n} \subset \overline{V_+}$$
for all $n$, and full Fock joint spectrum $\subset \overline{V_+}$.

**Step 6: Derivation of the seventy-year-unexplained axiom.**
Seventy years (1956–2026) of axiomatic QFT carried W6 as an
unexplained sixth axiom (Wightman 1956; Streater–Wightman 1964; Haag
1992). The axiomatic apparatus W1–W5 is sign-blind on $+ic$ vs $-ic$
at the algebraic level: the algebraic structure of Hilbert space,
Poincaré group, microcausality, distributional operators, and vacuum
existence does not specify time-orientation. W6 imported the
orientation as a separate algebraic axiom.

In the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, the orientation is supplied at the
*geometric* level by Component C1 directional ($+ic$, not $-ic$) of
the McGucken Principle. The Spectrum Condition is the algebraic
statement of this geometric orientation: when the sign-blind algebraic
apparatus W1–W5 is read with the McGucken Principle's directional
content, the positive-energy spectrum follows as a forced theorem, not
a separate axiom.

**This is the novelty of the McGucken contribution to
W6**: the orientation that has been imported as an algebraic axiom for
seventy years descends in the chain of theorems as the McGucken Sphere's
forward-direction expansion at every event of Minkowski space.

**Principal McGucken Components for W6**: C1 (rate clause); C1
directional ($+ic$, not $\pm ic$, supplying forward-time orientation of
the Sphere expansion, read on the four-velocity as $u^0 = +c$); C2
(perpendicularity marker via Lemma 2.5 for
metric); C3 (action quantum in plane-wave phase); C4 (per-event
universality); C5 (Sphere generation at every event). Supporting
machinery: Lemma 2.5 (Lorentzian metric); the four-velocity norm
$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ of §2.3, which fixes magnitude while the $+ic$
orientation fixes the sign; Theorem W.2 (Poincaré-covariance giving
translations and the orthochronous restriction); Stone's theorem.
$\square$
:::
