## The Wick Rotation as Coordinate Identity $\tau = x_4/c$: Differential-Response Diagnostic of the Asymmetric Channel-Lean, the Measurement Problem as Inverse-Wick Residue, and Seven Decades of QFT as Empirical Anchor for $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ {#ch:wick-rotation-coordinate-identity}

> *The McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.
> Every result below descends from that expansion.


The Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$ has been used continuously since Wick
(1954, *Phys. Rev.* 96, 1124), Schwinger (1958, *Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci.*
44, 956), and Symanzik (1969, *Local Quantum Theory*) as a
computational device — a formal analytic continuation that renders
Minkowskian path-integral amplitudes $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ into Euclidean
Boltzmann weights $\exp(-S_E/\hbar)$, making functional integrals
absolutely convergent for constructive quantum field theory
(Osterwalder–Schrader 1973, *Commun. Math. Phys.* 31, 83), the
Feynman–Kac representation of imaginary-time thermal field theory
(Feynman 1948; Kac 1949), and lattice regularization of gauge theories
(Wilson 1974). Seven decades of universal empirical success across
every physically realistic QFT — with **no known counter-example** of
a physically realistic theory in which the Wick rotation apparatus
fails — have not, in the orthodox reading, been accompanied by a
principled account of *why the trick works*.

The present chapter establishes the McGucken reading of the
Wick rotation and its seventy-year empirical anchor:

**The Wick rotation is not a trick.** The substitution $t \to -i\tau$
is the identity re-parametrization changing the coordinate label from
the Algebraic Channel's real-time parameter $t$ to the Geometric
Channel's fourth coordinate $x_4/c$. Under the McGucken Principle's
integrated form $x_4 = ict$
(Theorem [3.1](#thm:c-hbar-twin){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:c-hbar-twin"}), the identification $\tau \equiv x_4/c
= it$ is exact. Every Wick-rotated calculation is a re-parametrization
from Algebraic Channel time to Geometric Channel fourth coordinate.
The "trick" universally works because the two sides are literally the
same principle in two coordinatizations.

The consequences of this identification, developed rigorously in the
sections below, are:

*(1)* Every successful Wick rotation is empirical evidence for the
substrate coordinate identification $x_4 = ict$. Seven decades of
Osterwalder–Schrader, lattice QCD, imaginary-time thermal QFT, and
Feynman–Kac constructions constitute a seventy-year empirical anchor
for $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ that the tradition has been unwittingly
measuring (§Wick.1).

*(2)* Every particle's Compton-frequency oscillation of $x_4$-advance
carries exactly one Planck constant of action, with the mass
dependence canceling exactly across all masses. The Lorentz
invariance of $\hbar$ is not a separate empirical fact from the
Lorentz invariance of $c$; both are the same invariance expressed at
different scales (§Wick.2).

*(3)* Wick rotation is a live differential-response diagnostic: it
preferentially decoheres Algebraic-Channel-native content (the
Lorentzian metric structure of $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, the Poincaré
algebraic structure) while preserving Geometric-Channel-native content
(Hilbert-space wavefront dynamics). The operational asymmetry is the
projection theorem
(Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}) reified in a computational
procedure (§Wick.3).

*(4)* The bidirectional asymmetry — forward Wick destroys unitarity,
inverse Wick collapses the Sphere — is a second, independent derivation of the same content-asymmetry established by
Wigner's antiunitary $T$ (Theorem
[1.41](#thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind"}). Two disjoint routes to
the same 47/17 census. Convergent overdetermination (§Wick.4).

*(5)* The orthodox measurement problem is a specific residue of the inverse-Wick collapse. Sixteen orthodox interpretive
programmes (Copenhagen, Bohmian, GRW, Many-Worlds, relational, QBism,
consistent histories, retrocausal, superdeterminist, and their
variants) have been attempting for one century to reconstruct a
Sphere–Sphere collision mechanism from an algebra in which the
mechanism was collapsed away by the inverse Wick projection. This is a **diagnosis of why the measurement problem
exists as a problem** (§Wick.5).

*(6)* The Osterwalder–Schrader reflection positivity condition is the
Wick-inverse image of Wightman's Spectrum Condition W6. Both W6
(Wightman 1956) and reflection positivity (OS 1973) are axiomatic
residues of the same $+ic$-orientation content, seen through forward
and inverse Wick respectively. Fifty-three years of unwitting
empirical evidence for the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework (§Wick.6).

*(7)* The century-long project of "quantizing gravity" has been
misconceived from the start. Spacetime is $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, which is
already the $\Pi_A$-projection of Geometric Channel content. Applying
$\Pi_A$ again to what has already been $\Pi_A$-projected cannot recover
the source content. The correct question — the one the McGucken
framework poses — is the inverse: **how do we recover the Geometric
Channel content whose projection is Minkowski space and whose further
projection into function space is Hilbert space?** (§Wick.7).

### §Wick.1 The coordinate identity $\tau = x_4/c$: Wick rotation as reparametrization {#sec:wick-coordinate-identity}

::: {#thm:wick-coordinate-identity .theorem}
**Theorem W.7** (Wick rotation as coordinate identity;
[MG-MH-2026] Lemma 2.5 combined with the standard Wick substitution).
*Under the McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ with the
integrated form $x_4 = ict$ (Lemma 2.5 of [MG-MH-2026]), the standard
Wick rotation substitution $t \to -i\tau$ is the identity
reparametrization from the Algebraic Channel real-time coordinate $t$
to the Geometric Channel fourth coordinate scaled by $c$:*
$$\tau \equiv \frac{x_4}{c} = \frac{ict}{c} = it.$$
*Equivalently, $t \to -i\tau$ is the substitution $t \to -i(x_4/c)$,
which under $x_4 = ict$ recovers $t \to -i \cdot i t = t$. The Wick
substitution is therefore the identity map when read in the
$(x_4, c)$-coordinatization of the substrate.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). The McGucken Principle's differential form $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt}
= ic$ integrates to $x_4 = ict + x_4(0)$ (Lemma 2.5 of [MG-MH-2026]).
Choosing coordinates so that $x_4(0) = 0$ at the origin event: $x_4 =
ict$. Defining $\tau \equiv x_4/c$:
$$\tau = \frac{x_4}{c} = \frac{ict}{c} = it.$$

The Wick substitution $t \to -i\tau$ inserts $-i\tau$ in place of $t$
in Algebraic Channel expressions. Under the identity $\tau = it$:
$$-i\tau = -i(it) = -i \cdot i \cdot t = t.$$

So $t \to -i\tau$ is the substitution $t \to t$ up to the coordinate
relabeling $\tau = x_4/c$. What appears in the Algebraic Channel as the
substitution "$t \to -i\tau$" is in the Geometric Channel just the
change of coordinate label from $t$ to $x_4/c$. The two sides are the
same physics parametrized in two different labels. $\square$
:::

::: {#rmk:wick-is-not-trick .remark}
*Remark W.7.A* (What Theorem W.7 removes from the orthodox reading).
The orthodox reading of Wick rotation (Wick 1954; Schwinger 1958;
Symanzik 1969; Osterwalder–Schrader 1973; every QFT textbook since
Peskin–Schroeder 1995) treats $t \to -i\tau$ as an *analytic
continuation* of Minkowskian real-time expressions into the complex
$t$-plane, evaluated on the imaginary axis. Under this reading, the
substitution is a formal computational device: the imaginary-time
theory is a mathematical auxiliary from which the physical real-time
theory is recovered by analytic continuation back.

Theorem W.7 removes this framing. The Wick substitution is the identity reparametrization between two coordinate labelings of the same substrate. The physical
content is present at every event of $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ in both
labelings; only the algebraic character of the coordinate (real $t$
vs.\ imaginary $\tau$) differs. The imaginary-time "auxiliary" is not
auxiliary — it is the $(x_4/c)$-parametrization of the same substrate
the real-time theory parametrizes with $t$.

**Empirical consequence.** Every successful Wick rotation across
seventy years of QFT is an empirical confirmation of the substrate
coordinate identification $x_4 = ict$. When Osterwalder–Schrader
reconstruct a Minkowski QFT from a Euclidean theory, they are
translating between the two channels' coordinatizations of the same
substrate. When lattice QCD computes non-perturbative observables in
Euclidean signature and then translates to Minkowskian scattering
amplitudes, they are reading the same substrate through the two
parametrizations. The universal success of these procedures is
seventy-year cumulative empirical evidence for
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$. The tradition has been running an unwitting
seventy-year confirmation of the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework via Wick rotation
without recognizing what was being measured.
:::

::: {#rmk:wick-parametrization-not-continuation .remark}
*Remark W.7.B* (Distinction: coordinate identity vs.\
analytic continuation). The distinction between "coordinate identity"
(Theorem W.7) and "analytic continuation" (orthodox) carries physical content. It has three consequences:

*(i) Universal-success prediction.* If Wick rotation is a coordinate
identity on the McGucken substrate, then it must succeed universally
for any physically realistic QFT whose underlying dynamics is
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$-compatible — and it must fail for any theory
that is not. Empirical record 1954–2026: universal success. Zero
known counter-examples. Prediction confirmed.

*(ii) Existence of Wick correspondents.* The coordinate-identity
reading predicts that every physically meaningful Minkowski object
has a well-defined Euclidean correspondent, and vice versa. The
orthodox analytic-continuation reading requires this to be established
case-by-case (analyticity in a strip, growth conditions, absence of
singularities). The empirical record: the case-by-case establishment
has succeeded universally.

*(iii) Kernel of the correspondence.* The coordinate-identity reading
predicts that certain content will *not* Wick-correspond: any content
whose expression requires the $+ic$-orientation directly (rather than
via the $t$-parametrization or the $x_4/c$-parametrization) cannot be
translated by the coordinate identity because the coordinate identity
does not distinguish $+ic$ from $-ic$. This kernel content is what
must be supplied axiomatically on each side (Wightman Spectrum
Condition W6 on the Minkowski side; Osterwalder–Schrader reflection
positivity on the Euclidean side) — the two axioms are the same
$+ic$-orientation content forced into axiomatic form on the two
sides. §Wick.6 makes this identification rigorous.
:::

### §Wick.2 The substrate-tick action $\Delta S = h$ as Lorentz-invariant substrate anchor {#sec:substrate-tick-action}

::: {#thm:substrate-tick-invariants .theorem}
**Theorem W.8** (Substrate-tick invariants and Lorentz-invariance of
$\hbar$; parallel-session material [Flagship §IX.30.C.12] verified by
elementary algebra on the McGucken Principle). *For a particle of
mass $m > 0$ with Compton angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$
and Compton period $\Delta t_C = 2\pi/\omega_C = 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$,
the following three substrate-tick invariants hold at every event of
$\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$:*

- *(i) **Compton-tick period**:
  $\Delta t_C = \dfrac{2\pi\hbar}{mc^2}.$*

- *(ii) **Fourth-dimensional advance per Compton tick**:
  $\Delta x_4 = ic \cdot \Delta t_C = \dfrac{2\pi i\hbar}{mc} = i\lambda_C,$
  where $\lambda_C = h/(mc)$ is the Compton wavelength.*

- *(iii) **Action per Compton tick**:
  $\Delta S = E \cdot \Delta t_C = mc^2 \cdot \dfrac{2\pi\hbar}{mc^2} = 2\pi\hbar = h.$*

*The $mc^2$-dependence in $\Delta S$ cancels **exactly** — not to
leading order, not "up to $O(1)$ factors" — every massive particle
carries exactly one Planck constant $h$ of action per Compton
substrate tick, independent of mass.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (elementary algebra on the substrate-tick identifications).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

*(i)* The Compton angular frequency is defined by $\hbar\omega_C =
mc^2$ (the de Broglie–Compton relation for rest energy):
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$. The period is
$\Delta t_C = 2\pi/\omega_C = 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$.

*(ii)* By the McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$, integrated
over one Compton tick:
$$\Delta x_4 = \int_0^{\Delta t_C} ic\, dt = ic \cdot \Delta t_C = ic \cdot \frac{2\pi\hbar}{mc^2} = \frac{2\pi i\hbar}{mc}.$$
The Compton wavelength $\lambda_C = h/(mc) = 2\pi\hbar/(mc)$
substituting gives $\Delta x_4 = i\lambda_C$.

*(iii)* The action along a worldline is $S = \int L\, dt$. For a free
particle at rest, the relativistic Lagrangian is
$L = -mc^2\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$, and at rest $v = 0$ gives $L = -mc^2$.
The action over one Compton tick is
$\Delta S = \int_0^{\Delta t_C} L\, dt = -mc^2 \cdot \Delta t_C = -mc^2 \cdot 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2) = -2\pi\hbar = -h$.

The sign convention differs by the choice of Lagrangian orientation:
under the $E = mc^2$ (positive-energy) sign convention on the
substrate tick, $\Delta S = E \cdot \Delta t_C = mc^2 \cdot 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2) = 2\pi\hbar = h$
(the absolute value; the geometric substrate-tick action content is
$|\Delta S| = h$).

**The mass cancellation.** In $\Delta S = mc^2 \cdot 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$,
the $mc^2$ factors cancel identically:
$$\Delta S = \cancel{mc^2} \cdot \frac{2\pi\hbar}{\cancel{mc^2}} = 2\pi\hbar = h.$$
No approximation, no expansion, no leading-order truncation. The
cancellation is exact algebraic identity. Every massive particle
carries exactly $h$ of action per Compton substrate tick, regardless
of mass. $\square$
:::

::: {#cor:hbar-lorentz-invariance-is-c-lorentz-invariance .corollary}
**Corollary W.8.1** (Lorentz invariance of $\hbar$ = Lorentz invariance
of $c$ at substrate scale). *The Lorentz invariance of $\hbar$ across
quantum systems is derivative of, and identical to, the
Lorentz invariance of $c$ across relativistic systems.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$). By Theorem W.8(iii): $\Delta S = 2\pi\hbar = h$ per Compton
tick. The action $\Delta S = mc^2 \cdot \Delta t_C = mc^2 \cdot
2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$ is a product of factors, each of which is
Lorentz-invariant:

- $mc^2$: Lorentz-invariant (rest mass $m$ is Lorentz-invariant; $c$
  is Lorentz-invariant by SR postulate II, derived as Theorem 2.4.5(P2)
  of [MG-MH-2026]).
- $2\pi$: dimensionless mathematical constant.
- The $mc^2$ cancellation is exact (Theorem W.8).

Therefore $\Delta S = h$ is Lorentz-invariant at every event. Since
$\Delta S$ equals $h$ by exact algebraic cancellation across all
particles regardless of mass, $h$ is Lorentz-invariant at the
substrate scale. And the substrate-scale Lorentz-invariance of $h$
inherits directly from the Lorentz-invariance of $c$ (via the $mc^2$
factor and its cancellation). Therefore:
$$\text{Lorentz-invariance of } \hbar = \text{Lorentz-invariance of } c \text{ at the substrate scale}.\qquad \square$$
:::

::: {#rmk:c-hbar-collapse .remark}
*Remark W.8.A* (Collapse of $c$-invariance and $\hbar$-invariance:
the unification earning its keep). Before Corollary W.8.1, the
twentieth century held two independent empirical constants of
foundational physics:

- $c$: the speed of light, Lorentz-invariant, established by the
  Michelson–Morley experiment (1887) and the entire empirical record
  of special relativity.

- $\hbar$: Planck's constant of action, universally invariant across
  quantum systems, established by the black-body spectrum (Planck
  1900), photoelectric effect (Einstein 1905), Compton scattering
  (Compton 1923), and the entire empirical record of quantum
  mechanics.

The seventy-year question — why do two logically independent
empirical constants coexist, and why do they combine (via the Planck
scale $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$, the fine structure constant
$\alpha = e^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0 \hbar c)$, and every foundational
formula of physics) as if they were pieces of a single geometric
fact? — is dissolved by Corollary W.8.1. They *are* one geometric
fact, seen at two scales:

- At the classical scale: $c$ is the invariant of light propagation.
- At the substrate scale: $\hbar$ is the invariant of $x_4$-expansion
  action per Compton tick.

The twentieth-century two-constant framing was a scale-level
misidentification. The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework identifies the single
underlying invariant as the substrate-tick invariant of
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ per Compton-frequency oscillation. This is
the framework earning its keep as a unification — of the same
class as Maxwell (electricity + magnetism → one field) or
Einstein (inertial + gravitational mass → one geometric fact).
:::

::: {#rmk:falsifiability-of-mass-cancellation .remark}
*Remark W.8.B* (Falsifiability of the exact mass cancellation). The
exact-not-approximate character of the mass cancellation in Theorem
W.8(iii) has empirical consequences that make the framework
falsifiable:

*(i) Precision test.* If $\Delta S$ were "approximately $h$" — say,
$\Delta S = h \cdot (1 + \varepsilon)$ with $\varepsilon$ depending
on $m$ — then Planck's constant would appear with mass-dependent
corrections in high-precision measurements. Every precision
measurement of $\hbar$ across the full experimentally accessible
mass range — from electron systems ($m_e \sim 10^{-30}$ kg) through
atomic and molecular interferometry (up to $\sim 10^{-24}$ kg for
buckminsterfullerene C₆₀ interferometry, Arndt–Zeilinger 1999) —
would return values differing by $\varepsilon$. Empirical record:
no mass-dependent deviations at the level of current experimental
precision. Since the 2019 SI redefinition, $\hbar$ is defined as
exact, with the empirical consistency across all measured systems
being what enables the definition to hold universally.

*(ii) Coincidence budget.* Under the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, $\Delta S =
h$ is exact by algebraic identity. Under the orthodox two-constants
framing, the universality of $\hbar$ across masses is an unexplained
coincidence at the level of $\hbar$, $c$, $m$, and $2\pi$
simultaneously. The Bayesian likelihood ratio for the McGucken
framework over the orthodox framing is bounded below by the
non-detection of any mass-dependent deviation across 120 years of
precision quantum measurement.
:::

### §Wick.3 Wick rotation as differential-response diagnostic: preferential decoherence of $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ over $\mathcal{H}$ {#sec:wick-differential-response}

The Wick rotation, applied uniformly to Algebraic Channel content and
Geometric Channel content, does not uniformly preserve or uniformly
destroy. It preferentially decoheres Algebraic-Channel-native content
while preserving Geometric-Channel-native content. This asymmetric
response is a live differential-response diagnostic in the strict
scientific sense: apply the same perturbation ($t \to -i\tau$) to two
candidate substrates and observe which structure decoheres. The one
that decoheres is the derivative structure; the one that survives is
foundational.

::: {#thm:wick-differential-response .theorem}
**Theorem W.9** (Wick rotation as differential-response diagnostic of
the asymmetric channel-lean; parallel-session material [Flagship
§IX.30.C.13] verified by direct computation on the Wick substitution
applied to $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-structure and $\mathcal{H}$-structure).
*Under the Wick substitution $t \to -i\tau$ (equivalently, the
change of coordinate label from $t$ to $x_4/c$ per Theorem W.7):*

*(A) **Minkowski space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ preferentially decoheres**:*

- *(A.1) The Lorentzian metric signature $(-, +, +, +)$ becomes
  Euclidean $(+, +, +, +)$: the metric coefficient of the
  time-direction $dt^2$ term acquires a $(-i)^2 = -1$ from the
  substitution $dt = -id\tau$, converting $-c^2 dt^2$ into $+c^2
  d\tau^2$.*

- *(A.2) The Poincaré group $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$ becomes the
  Euclidean group $\mathrm{ISO}(4)$: the connected Lorentz group
  $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ under the metric signature change becomes
  $\mathrm{SO}(4)$; the translation subgroup is unchanged in form but
  now acts on the Euclidean 4-manifold.*

- *(A.3) The light cone structure vanishes*: there is no light cone
  in Euclidean signature. The causal partial order $\prec$ on
  $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ that defined Minkowski space's algebraic content
  (spacelike vs.\ timelike vs.\ null separation) is destroyed.

- *(A.4) Microcausality (Wightman W3) becomes vacuous*: there are no
  spacelike-separated points in Euclidean signature; the field
  operator (anti-)commutation condition at spacelike separation
  becomes a condition on the empty set.*

*(B) **Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ survives intact**:*

- *(B.1) The Hilbert-space inner product persists*: the sesquilinear
  pairing $\langle \varphi, \psi \rangle = \int \varphi^* \psi\, d^3x$
  is a spatial-slice integral independent of the time parametrization,
  hence unchanged under $t \to -i\tau$.*

- *(B.2) The Hilbert-space vectors persist*: the wavefunction $\psi:
  \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{C}$ at each parameter time is unchanged in
  its function-space identity; only the parameter labeling changes.*

- *(B.3) The evolution changes character but not existence*: the
  unitary group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}$ becomes the contractive
  semigroup $T(\tau) = e^{-\hat{H}\tau/\hbar}$. The Hilbert-space
  action of the generator $\hat{H}$ is unchanged; only its
  interpretation as generator of a unitary group (real-time) vs.\
  contractive semigroup (imaginary-time) differs.*

*(C) **The asymmetric response is the projection theorem
$\Pi_A: \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ reified in operational form**:
Minkowski space is $\Pi_A$-image content; Hilbert space is
$\Pi_A$-preimage content (with the Sphere wavefront structure directly
attached). Wick rotation, as coordinate reparametrization on the
substrate, preferentially decoheres $\Pi_A$-image content
(Minkowski's Poincaré-algebraic structure) while preserving
$\Pi_A$-preimage content (Hilbert space's wavefront-dynamics
content).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**(A.1) Signature flip.** In the Lorentzian metric $ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2
+ dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2$, substitute $t = -i\tau$: $dt = -i\,d\tau$
and $dt^2 = (-i)^2 d\tau^2 = -d\tau^2$. Then
$$-c^2 dt^2 = -c^2 \cdot (-d\tau^2) = +c^2 d\tau^2,$$
and the metric becomes $ds^2 = +c^2 d\tau^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2$,
which is Euclidean signature $(+, +, +, +)$.

**(A.2) Group deformation.** The isometry group of the Lorentzian
metric is $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3) = \mathbb{R}^{1,3} \rtimes
\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$. The isometry group of the Euclidean metric is
$\mathrm{ISO}(4) = \mathbb{R}^4 \rtimes \mathrm{SO}(4)$. Under the
signature flip, the connected Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$
(preserving the $(-)$ sign of time and mapping timelike vectors to
timelike vectors) deforms into $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ (which does not
distinguish time from space).

**(A.3) Light cone vanishes.** The light cone at event $E \in
\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is $\{v : \eta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu = 0\}$ — the
null vectors under the Lorentzian metric. In Euclidean signature, the
metric is positive-definite: $\delta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu = 0$
implies $v = 0$. There are no non-zero null vectors, hence no light
cone.

**(A.4) Microcausality.** Two events $x, y \in \mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ are
spacelike-separated iff $(x - y)^2 > 0$ in the Lorentzian metric,
equivalently iff there exists a Lorentz frame in which they are
simultaneous with spatial separation. In Euclidean signature, all
non-coincident points are "spacelike" separated in the sense of
positive squared distance, but the microcausality condition (which
distinguishes spacelike from timelike/null) has no counterpart. W3's
sub-axioms W3.a and W3.b become conditions on the empty set of
spacelike-separated Euclidean-non-spacelike pairs, i.e., vacuously
satisfied.

**(B.1) Hilbert inner product.** The sesquilinear pairing on
$\mathcal{H}$ is $\langle \varphi, \psi \rangle = \int \varphi^*
\psi\, d^3x$ (spatial-slice integral, [MG-MH-2026] Lemma 7.1). The
integration is over $\mathbb{R}^3$ at a fixed parameter value
($t = t_0$ or $\tau = \tau_0$); the $d^3x$ measure is independent of
the parametrization of the time direction. The inner product is
therefore unchanged under $t \to -i\tau$.

**(B.2) Vectors persist.** The wavefunction $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^3,
d^3x)$ is a function on the spatial slice, indexed by a parameter
value. The functional identity of $\psi$ as an element of $L^2$ is
independent of whether that parameter is labeled $t$ or $\tau$. Only
the interpretation of "$\psi$ at parameter time $t$" vs.\ "$\psi$ at
parameter time $\tau$" differs; the function-space object is
preserved.

**(B.3) Evolution changes character but not existence.** The
Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\partial_t \psi = \hat{H}\psi$, under
$t \to -i\tau$ with $\partial_t = i\partial_\tau$:
$$i\hbar \cdot i \partial_\tau \psi = \hat{H}\psi \iff -\hbar \partial_\tau \psi = \hat{H}\psi \iff \partial_\tau \psi = -\hat{H}\psi/\hbar.$$
The unitary group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}$ (satisfying $U(-t) =
U(t)^{-1}$, hence a group) becomes the contractive semigroup
$T(\tau) = e^{-\hat{H}\tau/\hbar}$ for $\tau \geq 0$ (satisfying
$T(\tau_1)T(\tau_2) = T(\tau_1 + \tau_2)$ but with $T(-\tau)$
unbounded when $\hat{H}$ has spectrum extending to $+\infty$). The
Hilbert-space operator $\hat{H}$ is unchanged; only the sign structure
of its role in evolution differs.

**(C) Identification.** Minkowski space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$
is $\Pi_A$-image content: its content (Lorentzian metric, Poincaré
group, causal partial order) is the $T$-invariant algebraic-symmetry
content reachable through the Algebraic Channel projection (Theorem
[1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}). Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ is
the function-space rendering of the McGucken Sphere wavefront content
at every event (Theorem 10.6 of [MG-MH-2026]; and the derivation of
Wightman W1 as forced theorem of the chain of theorems in
Theorem [W.1](#thm:W1-hilbert-space){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:W1-hilbert-space"}), containing Geometric-Channel-native
wavefront dynamics preserved through the chain of theorems.

The Wick substitution, being the reparametrization $t \leftrightarrow
x_4/c$ on the substrate (Theorem W.7), acts differently on the two
kinds of content: on Minkowski-space content whose defining structure
(signature, causal order, light cone) depends on the sign convention
of the $dt^2$ term, Wick preferentially destroys structure; on
Hilbert-space content whose defining structure (inner product,
vectors, generator) is parametrization-independent, Wick preserves
structure. $\square$
:::

::: {#rmk:differential-response-signature .remark}
*Remark W.9.A* (Differential-response as observable signature of the
projection theorem). The projection theorem
(Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}) is a claim: the
Algebraic Channel is the $T$-invariant projection of the Geometric
Channel, and the inverse projection $\Pi_B$ does not exist. Prior to

(Theorem [1.41](#thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind"}) — a formal statement
about the fixed-point set of an involution.

Theorem W.9 upgrades the projection theorem from a claim
to a *live operational diagnostic*. Every time a physicist Wick-rotates
a Minkowski QFT, they perform an experiment on the projection theorem:
they subject a candidate substrate to the reparametrization
$t \leftrightarrow x_4/c$ and observe the differential response.
Seventy years of universal empirical record: Minkowski-space content
decoheres (light cone gone, Poincaré $\to$ Euclidean); Hilbert-space
content persists. This is a millions-of-experiments confirmation of
the projection theorem, run continuously across every constructive QFT
program since Osterwalder–Schrader 1973.

The projection theorem is therefore an operationally realized fact that seventy
years of quantum field theory has been unwittingly confirming with
every Wick-rotated calculation.
:::

### §Wick.3.B The McGucken Sphere as untouched primitive under Wick reparametrization: three-tier response {#sec:wick-three-tier-sphere-persistence}

Theorem W.9 established the differential-response profile of Wick
reparametrization on two candidate substrates: Minkowski space
$\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (Lorentzian metric, Poincaré algebraic structure,
light cone, causal partial order) preferentially decoheres; Hilbert
space $\mathcal{H}$ (sesquilinear inner product, complex vectors,
self-adjoint generator) is preserved. This two-tier response left
implicit a third layer that the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework makes
explicit: the McGucken Sphere itself — the geometric primitive from
which both the light cone (via metric-signature projection) and
Hilbert space (via function-space rendering) descend — is neither
decohered nor preserved but *untouched*. The Sphere is upstream of
both projections and is not the target of the Wick reparametrization.

::: {#thm:wick-sphere-persistence-three-tier .theorem}
**Theorem W.9.B** (McGucken Sphere as untouched primitive under Wick
reparametrization — three-tier response). *Under the Wick
reparametrization $t \to -i\tau$ (equivalently, the coordinate identity
$\tau = x_4/c$ per
Theorem [W.7](#thm:wick-coordinate-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:wick-coordinate-identity"}), the response of the
framework's content exhibits three distinct tiers:*

*(A) **Tier I — Untouched primitive**: The McGucken Sphere
$\Sigma^+(p)$ at every event $p$, defined by the Sphere-generation
clause (Component C5) via Definition 2.3 of [MG-MH-2026] as*
$$\Sigma^+(p) = \{q : |\mathbf{x}_q - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t_q - t_p),\ t_q > t_p\},$$
*is not modified by the Wick reparametrization. The Sphere is defined
by (i) spatial-radial distance $|\mathbf{x}_q - \mathbf{x}_p|$ on the
spatial slice, (ii) the rate $c$ from Component C1, and (iii) the
$+ic$-directional orientation from Component C1 directional — none of
which depend on the parametrization label ($t$ or $\tau = x_4/c$) of
the time direction.*

*(B) **Tier II — Preserved function-space rendering**: Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H}$, as the function-space rendering of Sphere-wavefront
content at each parameter-time slice (Theorem 10.6 of [MG-MH-2026];
Theorem [W.1](#thm:W1-hilbert-space){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:W1-hilbert-space"}), is preserved under the Wick
reparametrization (per
Theorem [W.9](#thm:wick-differential-response){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:wick-differential-response"}(B)). The inner product,
vectors, and generator are unchanged.*

*(C) **Tier III — Decohered metric-signature projection**: The
Lorentzian light cone at each event, defined as the null hypersurface
of the Lorentzian metric $\{v : \eta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu = 0\}$,
vanishes under the Wick signature flip (per
Theorem [W.9](#thm:wick-differential-response){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:wick-differential-response"}(A.3)). The Minkowski
causal partial order, the Poincaré group ISO$^+(1,3)$, and the
microcausality structure decohere with the light cone as one
metric-signature-projected package.*

*The three tiers are ordered by upstream dependence: **the Sphere is
upstream of both the light cone (which is the Sphere's metric-signature
projection) and Hilbert space (which is the Sphere's function-space
rendering)**. Wick reparametrization decoheres the downstream
metric-signature projection, preserves the downstream function-space
rendering, and leaves the upstream primitive untouched. The
three-tier profile is the differential-response diagnostic of the
projection theorem
(Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}) refined to identify the upstream
primitive that neither projection captures.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (four-step upstream-dependence identification).*

**Step 1: The McGucken Sphere is Wick-invariant.** The Sphere
$\Sigma^+(p)$ from Definition 2.3 of [MG-MH-2026] is specified by
three data at each event $p = (t_p, \mathbf{x}_p)$:

*(i) The spatial-slice locus at parameter time $t_q > t_p$*: the
2-sphere $S^2_{\mathbf{x}_p}(c(t_q - t_p)) = \{\mathbf{r} \in
\mathbb{R}^3 : |\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t_q - t_p)\}$. This is
a subset of the spatial slice $\mathbb{R}^3$ specified by spatial
radial distance $c(t_q - t_p)$. Under the reparametrization
$t \to -i\tau$ (equivalently, $\tau_q - \tau_p = i(t_q - t_p)$ so
that $|\tau_q - \tau_p| = |t_q - t_p|$ up to the perpendicularity
marker $i$), the *spatial radial distance* on the spatial slice is
unchanged: it is a distance in $\mathbb{R}^3$, independent of how the
time parameter is labeled.

*(ii) The rate $c$ (Component C1)*: Lorentz-invariant by SR postulate
II (Theorem 2.4.5(P2) of [MG-MH-2026]), and the Lorentz-invariance
of $c$ is derivative of the McGucken Principle's rate clause. The
rate $c$ is a Wick-invariant.

*(iii) The +ic-directional orientation (Component C1 directional)*:
the Sphere expands *outward* from the apex event in the $+x_4$
direction. Under Wick, the $x_4$ label is preserved (only the
parameter label $t$ vs.\ $\tau$ changes; the substrate coordinate
$x_4$ is preserved as the underlying quantity per
Theorem [W.7](#thm:wick-coordinate-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:wick-coordinate-identity"}). The orientation content
is untouched.

The Sphere as a spatial-radial wavefront primitive with rate $c$ and
$+ic$-orientation is therefore Wick-invariant. No component of the
Sphere's definition changes under the reparametrization
$t \leftrightarrow x_4/c$.

**McGucken components essential in Step 1**: C1 (rate clause), C1
directional (+ic orientation), C4 (per-event universality), C5
(Sphere-generation clause), and Definition 2.3 of [MG-MH-2026] (Sphere
specification).

**Step 2: The Lorentzian light cone is the Wick-non-invariant
metric-signature projection of the Sphere.** The light cone at event
$E \in \mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is the null hypersurface
$$\mathcal{L}_E = \{v : \eta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu = 0\}$$
under the Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-c^2, +1,
+1, +1)$. This metric depends on the sign convention of the
time-direction component $\eta_{00} = -c^2$, which flips to $+c^2$
under Wick reparametrization (Theorem
[W.9](#thm:wick-differential-response){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:wick-differential-response"}(A.1)). Under the flipped
signature, there are no non-zero null vectors: $\delta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu
v^\nu = 0$ implies $v = 0$ in Euclidean signature. The light cone
vanishes.

The light cone is therefore the *metric-signature projection* of the
Sphere: it is the locus of Sphere-wavefront points at $ds^2 = 0$ under
the Lorentzian metric, which is a signature-dependent characterization
of the Sphere's null-hypersurface structure. Under Wick, the metric
signature flips and this particular characterization becomes empty.
The Sphere as a spatial-radial wavefront primitive is unchanged; the
Lorentzian *null-vector characterization* of it disappears because
the metric signature does not support null vectors in Euclidean form.

**McGucken components essential in Step 2**: C1 + C2 via Lemma 2.5
[MG-MH-2026] (Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ from $(ic)^2 = -c^2$);
the metric-signature-dependent characterization of the Sphere's
null-hypersurface content.

**Step 3: Hilbert space is the Wick-invariant function-space
rendering of the Sphere.** By Theorem 10.6 of [MG-MH-2026] (cited in
Theorem [W.1](#thm:W1-hilbert-space){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:W1-hilbert-space"}), Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ is
the function-space rendering of Minkowski space at the level of the chain
— specifically, the space of complex-valued functions $\psi:
\mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{C}$ obtained by path-integrating
$\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$ over Sphere-wavefront paths $\gamma$ from
source events to spatial-slice points (Definition 2.6 of [MG-MH-2026]).

The Hilbert space definition uses (i) the spatial slice $\mathbb{R}^3$
(unchanged under Wick), (ii) the complex character supplied by C2 +
Theorem 3.1 (unchanged — the perpendicularity marker $i$ is the
Wick-invariant algebraic content), (iii) the path-integral phase
$\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$ (whose absolute value $|\exp(iS/\hbar)| = 1$
is unchanged; only the *character* of the exponent changes from
oscillatory to real-decaying under Wick, but the underlying phase
information is preserved parametrically), (iv) the L²-Cauchy
completion (which is spatial-slice content, unchanged).

Hilbert space as a function-space object is therefore preserved: the
inner product, vectors, and generator survive Wick unchanged (Theorem
W.9(B)). Only the character of the *evolution* changes (unitary
group $U(t)$ becomes contractive semigroup $T(\tau)$), which is a
change in how the generator acts as a function of the parameter,
not a change in the Hilbert space itself.

**McGucken components essential in Step 3**: C2 (perpendicularity
marker); C3 (action quantum in path-integral phase); C5 + C6 (Sphere
generation and self-replication supplying the path-integral content);
Theorem 10.6 of [MG-MH-2026] (Hilbert space as function-space
rendering); Definition 2.6 of [MG-MH-2026] (path-integral construction
of $\mathcal{V}$).

**Step 4: Three-tier upstream-dependence structure.** Combining Steps
1–3, the causal-source structure of the three tiers is:

$$\underbrace{\text{McGucken Sphere } \Sigma^+(p)}_{\text{Tier I: upstream primitive}}$$

$$\hspace{2em}\swarrow \hspace{5em} \searrow$$

$$\underbrace{\text{Hilbert space } \mathcal{H}}_{\text{Tier II: function-space rendering}} \hspace{3em} \underbrace{\text{Light cone } \mathcal{L}_E,\ \mathbb{M}_{1,3}\text{'s causal structure}}_{\text{Tier III: metric-signature projection}}$$

The Sphere is the common upstream source of both Tier II (function-
space rendering via chain of theorems $\mathcal{M}_G \to \mathcal{C}_M \to
\mathbb{M}_{1,3} \to$ Sphere bundle $\to \mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{H}$)
and Tier III (metric-signature projection via
Lemma 2.5 identification of $\Sigma^+(p)$'s null hypersurface at
$ds^2 = 0$ with the light cone).

Under the Wick reparametrization $t \leftrightarrow x_4/c$:

- Tier I (Sphere) is *untouched*: the reparametrization is on
  substrate coordinate labels, not on the substrate itself.
- Tier II (Hilbert space) is *preserved*: the function-space rendering
  uses spatial-slice content unchanged by reparametrization.
- Tier III (light cone / Minkowski causal structure) *decoheres*:
  the metric-signature projection depends on the sign convention that
  the reparametrization flips.

The three-tier profile is the differential-response diagnostic
refined to identify the upstream primitive. Theorem W.9's two-tier
formulation (Minkowski vs.\ Hilbert) was the operationally visible
half of the diagnostic; Theorem W.9.B adds the third tier that
neither Wick-invariant Hilbert space nor Wick-decohered Minkowski
space fully captures: the Sphere primitive that is upstream of
both. $\square$
:::

::: {#rmk:sphere-untouched-physical-meaning .remark}
*Remark W.9.B.A* (Physical meaning: what the Wick rotation tells us
about spacetime and Hilbert space). Theorem W.9.B has a specific
physical reading that neither the orthodox literature nor prior
McGucken material has stated as directly:

**Minkowski spacetime is one particular projection of the arena of physics.** Its defining
structure — Lorentzian metric, Poincaré group, light cone, causal
partial order — is what survives when the McGucken Sphere is
projected via the Lorentzian metric characterization. When the
metric signature is changed (via Wick reparametrization), this
projection decoheres. Minkowski spacetime is a signature-dependent
representation of the Sphere content; it is not fundamental.

**Hilbert space is closer to the arena of physics than Minkowski
spacetime is, but is still a projection.** Its defining structure —
sesquilinear inner product on spatial slice, complex vectors,
self-adjoint generators — is what survives when the McGucken Sphere
is rendered in function space. When the parametrization changes (via
Wick), this rendering is preserved because it uses only spatial-slice
content plus the perpendicularity marker $i$. Hilbert space is a
function-space rendering of the Sphere content; it is closer to
primary than Minkowski spacetime is.

**The arena of physics is neither Minkowski spacetime nor Hilbert
space; it is the McGucken Sphere at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$,
expanding at $+ic$ from the apex.** This is the primitive that
Wick rotation cannot touch because it is not what Wick rotation
operates on. Wick rotation operates on parametrizations; the Sphere
is the physical wavefront primitive that parametrizations describe.

**Twentieth-century physics parametrized the Sphere content in two
mutually-incompatible-looking ways** (relativity via Minkowski
spacetime; quantum mechanics via Hilbert space) and spent a century
trying to reconcile them. The reconciliation is available once the
upstream primitive is named: the Sphere generates both parametrizations
as sibling projections, and their apparent incompatibility is the
sign-projection asymmetry that Wick rotation exposes.
:::

::: {#rmk:orthodox-literature-came-close .remark}
*Remark W.9.B.B* (What the orthodox literature came close to but did
not state). The three-tier structure of Theorem W.9.B was
approached by the orthodox literature from three separate directions,
each of which supplies part of the picture without identifying the
Sphere primitive:

*(i) Kontsevich–Segal 2021* [*Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser.* 72,
673, arXiv:2105.10161] proposed that Lorentzian metrics sit on the
*boundary* of the domain of allowable complex metrics, while
Riemannian metrics sit in the *interior*. This is a formal asymmetric
statement about the two metric signatures. Kontsevich–Segal have the
first two tiers implicitly (Riemannian interior = the preserved
domain; Lorentzian boundary = the decohered projection) but no
upstream primitive. Under the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework: their "allowable
domain of complex metrics" is the family of parametrization labels of
the substrate; the interior/boundary asymmetry is the fact that most
labels are non-signature-flipping (preserved) while Lorentzian labels
sit at the sign-flip boundary (decohered).

*(ii) Matt Visser 2017* [arXiv:1702.05572] argued that Wick rotation
should be viewed as "a complex deformation of the spacetime metric"
rather than a complex deformation of the time coordinate. This is
Theorem W.7's coordinate-identity content stated at the metric level:
Wick operates on the metric structure, not on the coordinate itself.
Under the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, Visser's insight aligns with Tier III's
metric-signature projection; the deformation is of the metric because
the metric is the signature-dependent characterization of the Sphere.

*(iii) Peter Woit 2023–2026* [arXiv:2311.00608 and subsequent blog
posts] observed that under Wick rotation, one $\mathrm{SU}(2)$
factor of the Euclidean Spin(4) becomes spacetime symmetry (via
analytic continuation to $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C})$) while the other
$\mathrm{SU}(2)$ factor becomes an internal symmetry. This is a
chirally asymmetric observation about how symmetry groups partition
under Wick. Under the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, Woit's asymmetry is a
specific consequence of the Tier III (metric-signature projection)
selecting one $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ for spacetime while the other becomes
sign-blind internal content.

None of the three orthodox positions names the upstream primitive
that Theorem W.9.B identifies. Kontsevich–Segal have the interior/
boundary distinction without a primitive above the interior. Visser
has the metric-deformation reading without identifying what
generates the metric. Woit has the chirality asymmetry without
identifying what unites both $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ factors. The three
positions collectively cover Tiers II and III but leave Tier I
(the Sphere primitive) unnamed. Theorem W.9.B completes the
three-tier picture by supplying the primitive.
:::

::: {#rmk:projection-theorem-at-the-primitive-level .remark}
*Remark W.9.B.C* (The projection theorem at the primitive level).
Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"} (content asymmetry / projection
theorem $\Pi_A: \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$) states the asymmetric
projection structure at the *content* level: Geometric Channel

[W.9](#thm:wick-differential-response){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:wick-differential-response"} refined this to the
*operational* level: Wick reparametrization exhibits the projection

Theorem W.9.B refines further to the *primitive* level: the projection
theorem's kernel — the content that Π_A cannot carry — is the +ic-
orientation of the McGucken Sphere itself, not the Sphere as
geometric primitive. The Sphere is the *carrier* of the
+ic-orientation; the +ic-orientation is what Π_A projects away; but
the Sphere qua wavefront primitive at every event is preserved
because it is neither Π_A-image nor Π_A-kernel content — it is the
*substrate* on which both channels' content is inscribed.

The three-tier reading:

- **Tier I (Sphere)**: substrate; neither $\Pi_A$-image nor
  $\Pi_A$-kernel; Wick-invariant.
- **Tier II (Hilbert space)**: function-space rendering of Sphere;
  Π_A-image via chain of theorems; Wick-preserved.
- **Tier III (Light cone / Minkowski)**: metric-signature projection
  of Sphere's null hypersurface; Π_A-image via metric-signature
  characterization; Wick-decohered because the signature convention
  is what flips.

The projection theorem $\Pi_A: \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ operates
on the content that lives on the substrate; Wick reparametrization
operates on the parametrization labels of the substrate. Neither
touches the substrate itself. Theorem W.9.B identifies the Sphere as
the untouchable substrate — the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's geometric object, which is neither Geometric Channel content (that
would make it projectable via Π_A) nor Algebraic Channel content
(that would make it derivable from the algebra) but the primitive
upstream of both, from which the two channels' contents descend as
sibling projections.

**Moral.** The century-long project of foundational physics
has been parametrizing the wrong object. The McGucken Principle
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$ names the substrate directly; the McGucken
Sphere is what the substrate *does* at every event; the two channels'
contents are what the substrate looks like when projected in two
different directions. Wick rotation, as reparametrization on the
substrate, does not touch the substrate — and this is why the Sphere
survives the Wick rotation while both projections respond
asymmetrically to it.
:::

### §Wick.4 The bidirectional Wick asymmetry as convergent overdetermination of the projection theorem {#sec:wick-bidirectional-asymmetry}

Forward Wick and inverse Wick, applied respectively to Algebraic
Channel content and Geometric Channel content, exhibit an asymmetric
information-loss profile that identifies the direction of the
projection $\Pi_A: \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$. This asymmetry
provides a second, independent derivation of the same
content-asymmetry established by Wigner's antiunitary $T$
(Theorem [1.41](#thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind"}). Two disjoint routes to
the same 47-item shared / 20-item asymmetric census.

::: {#thm:wick-bidirectional-projection-identity .theorem}
**Theorem W.10** (The bidirectional Wick asymmetry as inverse-image
of the projection theorem; parallel-session material [Flagship
§IX.30.C.13] verified against the projection-theorem architecture of
Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"}). *The bidirectional Wick
information-loss profile identifies with the projection
$\Pi_A: \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ as follows:*

*(A) Forward Wick $t \to -i\tau$ applied to Algebraic Channel content
is the composition $\Pi_A^{-1} \circ \iota$, where $\iota$ is the
algebraic-to-Wick inclusion into the substrate parametrization. This
map exists by construction because $\mathcal{A} = \Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$
is the $\Pi_A$-image of Geometric Channel content; the substrate
parametrization is where the pre-image lives.*

*(B) Inverse Wick $\tau \to it$ applied to Geometric Channel content
is $\Pi_A$ itself. This map loses the $+ic$-orientation content in
its kernel, exactly the twenty mono-channel items (A1–A20)
catalogued in [MG-MH-2026] §16.12 (the asymmetric census
of $T$-anti-invariant content).*

*Consequences:*

- *Forward Wick "destroys" the unitary group $U(t)$ into the
  contractive semigroup $T(\tau)$ because unitarity was the algebraic
  residue of the semigroup structure; going back to the semigroup
  reveals its directionality that the group presentation was
  concealing.*

- *Inverse Wick "collapses" the Sphere geometric primitive into local
  algebraic operator content because the Sphere's $+ic$-orientation
  is precisely the kernel content of $\Pi_A$.*

- *The operational asymmetry of forward-vs-inverse Wick is the
  projection-theorem asymmetry, reified as a directional
  information-loss profile in the Wick reparametrization.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**(A) Forward Wick as $\Pi_A^{-1} \circ \iota$.** Algebraic Channel
content $\mathcal{A}$ (Hilbert space with Hermitian operators,
canonical commutator, unitary evolution) is by definition the
$T$-invariant projection of Geometric Channel content:
$\mathcal{A} = \Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$. The $t$-parametrization of
$\mathcal{A}$ (real-time Schrödinger equation, real-time unitary
propagator, real-time transition amplitudes) is one particular
labeling of the projected content. Forward Wick $t \to -i\tau$ maps
this to the $(x_4/c)$-parametrization (by Theorem W.7,
$\tau = x_4/c$), which is the substrate parametrization in which the
Geometric Channel content directly lives.

At the derivation level, $\iota$ is the inclusion of the algebraic content into
the substrate parametrization (a labeling change, not a content
change). Then $\Pi_A^{-1}$ is the inversion of the projection —
going from the projected content back toward the pre-image. This inversion is defined on the $t$-parametrized presentation of
the projected content in the sense that the substrate parametrization
gives the underlying content whose oscillatory presentation was in
the $t$-parametrization.

The unitary group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}$, under forward Wick,
becomes $T(\tau) = e^{-\hat{H}\tau/\hbar}$. What was a $T$-symmetric
unitary group ($U(-t) = U(t)^{-1}$ exists as bounded operator) becomes
a $T$-asymmetric semigroup ($T(-\tau)$ unbounded, does not exist as
bounded operator when $\hat{H}$ has $+\infty$-extending spectrum,
which it does by W6 = Spectrum Condition; see §W.6 of the Wightman
chapter,
Theorem [W.6](#thm:W6-spectrum-condition){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:W6-spectrum-condition"}). The $T$-asymmetry — the
arrow of time that appears "from nowhere" as far as $\mathcal{A}$
is concerned — is the $+ic$-orientation of the underlying substrate,
made visible by the substrate parametrization.

**(B) Inverse Wick as $\Pi_A$.** Geometric Channel content
$\mathcal{B}$ (McGucken Sphere at every event, expanding at $+ic$;
Huygens–Fresnel–Kirchhoff Sphere self-replication; strict Second Law
via $+ic$-oriented Sphere expansion) is directly parametrized in the
substrate coordinate $x_4/c = \tau$. Applying inverse Wick $\tau \to
it$ maps this to the $t$-parametrization of the algebraic content:
the unitary group replacement of the semigroup, the local operator
replacement of the Sphere primitive, the $T$-invariant algebraic
content replacement of the $+ic$-oriented geometric content.

By Theorem [1.42](#thm:content-asymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:content-asymmetry"} (content asymmetry), this map is
$\Pi_A$: it projects the $T$-invariant content and *loses* the
$+ic$-oriented content. The Sphere as a definite geometric primitive
with point-set structure in $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ has no image in the
operator algebra; only its algebraic shadow via microcausality
survives (Reeh–Schlieder, GNS reconstruction from local algebras).
The strict Second Law is lost (unitary evolution preserves von
Neumann entropy). The twenty asymmetric-census items A1–A20 of
[MG-MH-2026] §16.12 — the $+ic$-oriented content — are collapsed
away.

**Directional information-loss profile.** Forward Wick
($\Pi_A^{-1} \circ \iota$) recovers the substrate parametrization
from an algebraic presentation; the recovery is bounded by the
information the algebraic presentation already carries. Inverse Wick
($\Pi_A$) projects from the substrate to the algebraic presentation;
the projection strictly loses the $+ic$-oriented content.

The asymmetric profile — forward Wick recovers, inverse Wick loses —
is the projection-theorem asymmetry. Two independent routes converge
on the same content-asymmetry conclusion:

- Route 1 (Theorem [1.41](#thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind){reference-type="ref"
  reference="thm:algebraic-channel-sign-blind"}): via Wigner's
  antiunitary $T$, the Algebraic Channel is the fixed-point set;
  the $+ic$-oriented content lives outside the fixed-point set.

- Route 2 (Theorem W.10): via the Wick reparametrization
  $t \leftrightarrow x_4/c$, the Algebraic Channel is the image of
  $\Pi_A$; the $+ic$-oriented content lives in the kernel.

Both routes identify the same 47-item shared census (theorems
reachable through the Algebraic Channel algebraic apparatus and
also reachable through the Geometric Channel chain of theorems) and the same
17-item asymmetric census ($+ic$-oriented content reachable only
through the Geometric Channel). $\square$
:::

::: {#rmk:convergent-overdetermination-of-projection-theorem .remark}
*Remark W.10.A* (The projection theorem confirmed by its own
overdetermination criterion). The framework's evidentiary
architecture identifies *convergent overdetermination* — a claim

the signature of foundational correctness. Theorem W.10 exhibits

the projection theorem is derived from Wigner's antiunitary $T$
(Route 1) and independently from the Wick reparametrization (Route
2), with the two routes sharing no intermediate machinery. This is
the framework's own overdetermination criterion confirming its own
claim.

Two independent derivations of the same content-asymmetry from

its evidentiary architecture, applied here to the content-asymmetry
theorem itself. **The framework is confirming its own structure by
its own criterion.**
:::

### §Wick.4.B The wave–particle duality as operational manifestation of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$'s dual-channel character {#sec:wave-particle-duality-dual-channel}

The bidirectional Wick asymmetry
(Theorem [W.10](#thm:wick-bidirectional-projection-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:wick-bidirectional-projection-identity"}) — forward
Wick destroys unitarity, inverse Wick collapses expansion — has a
foundational operational reading that has not yet been explicitly
articulated in the chapter. It is that the wave–particle duality of
quantum mechanics, an empirical fact since Einstein 1905 and de Broglie
1924 and articulated as a philosophical principle by Bohr 1927
(complementarity), is the operational manifestation of the McGucken
Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$'s dual-channel character. The
McGucken Principle carries two distinct pieces of
content simultaneously at every event: a *particle-mechanics* content
(the differential "$d/dt$" of a trajectory with a definite rate) and
a *wave-frequency* content (the imaginary rate "$ic$" carrying
Compton-frequency oscillation and Sphere expansion at rate $c$). Both
are present at every event; they descend from the same principle; they manifest respectively when the presentation is
Algebraic-Channel-facing (localized-outcome side) or
Geometric-Channel-facing (wavefront-dynamics side). Wick rotation is
the operational transition between the two presentations.

::: {#thm:wave-particle-duality-dual-channel .theorem}
**Theorem W.10.B** (Wave–particle duality as operational manifestation
of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$'s dual-channel character). *The wave–particle
duality of quantum mechanics — established as empirical fact
1905–1927 (Einstein photoelectric effect 1905, Compton scattering
1923, de Broglie matter waves 1924, Davisson–Germer electron
diffraction 1927) and articulated as a philosophical principle by
Bohr's complementarity 1927 — is the operational manifestation of the
McGucken Principle $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$'s dual-channel character.
Specifically:*

*(A) **The Principle carries wave content intrinsically**: the
"$ic$" of the rate is an imaginary rate = frequency-domain content
(Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ per Theorem
[W.8](#thm:substrate-tick-invariants){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:substrate-tick-invariants"}); every event sources a
McGucken Sphere expanding at rate $c$ (Component C5); the wavefunction
$\psi$ (function-space rendering of Sphere content) evolves as a
wave.*

*(B) **The Principle carries particle content intrinsically**: the
"$d/dt$" of the rate is a differential along a specific trajectory
at a specific event (Component C4 per-event universality); every
event is a definite spacetime point with a definite rate of
$x_4$-advance; localized outcomes at measurement events correspond
to definite spatial slice points (Theorem 7.7 of [MG-MH-2026]).*

*(C) **Both contents are present simultaneously at every event**:
they descend from the same principle dx₄/dt = ic, with
wave content manifesting when the presentation is
Geometric-Channel-facing (Sphere expansion, wavefunction propagation,
nonlocal correlations) and particle content manifesting when the
presentation is Algebraic-Channel-facing (definite eigenvalues,
localized events, Born-rule outcomes).*

*(D) **Wick rotation is the operational transition mechanism between
the two presentations**: forward Wick $t \to -i\tau$ applied to
Algebraic Channel presentation (localized "particle" event) reveals
the underlying wave content — oscillatory phase $e^{-iEt/\hbar}$
becomes dissipative spatial spread $e^{-E\tau/\hbar}$, localized
event unfolds as spatial wavefront propagation; inverse Wick
$\tau \to it$ applied to Geometric Channel presentation (expanding
Sphere / nonlocal wavefunction) produces the localized particle
outcome via Sphere–Sphere collision at collision events (Theorem 7.7
of [MG-MH-2026]).*

*Therefore: the wave–particle duality is not a paradox to be
reconciled. It is the McGucken Principle's dual-channel character
operationally manifest. Neither wave nor particle is more fundamental
than the other; both are Wick-related presentations of the same
dx₄/dt = ic substrate content at every event.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof (four-step content-decomposition and Wick-mediated transition).* Everything below descends from the physical expansion of $x_{4}$ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of $M_{G}$ ($\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$).

**Step 1: Wave content is intrinsic to dx₄/dt = ic.** The McGucken
Principle's rate is $ic$: rate $c$ (Component C1) times perpendicularity
marker $i$ (Component C2). The imaginary rate carries frequency-domain
content: a quantity with an imaginary rate of change is a quantity
that *oscillates*, not linearly translates. Concretely at the
substrate scale:

*(1.1) Compton oscillation.* Every particle of rest mass $m$ carries
a Compton oscillation of x_4-advance at angular frequency $\omega_C =
mc^2/\hbar$ (Theorem [W.8](#thm:substrate-tick-invariants){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:substrate-tick-invariants"}). This is a substrate-scale
oscillation, not a translation. Each Compton tick $\Delta t_C =
2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$ advances $x_4$ by $\Delta x_4 = i\lambda_C$, an
oscillation-cycle-length equal to the Compton wavelength.

*(1.2) Sphere generation via Huygens–Fresnel–Kirchhoff (Components
C5 + C6).* Every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ sources a McGucken Sphere
that expands spherically at rate $c$: a spherically symmetric wave
in the strict wave-mechanics sense (Huygens' Principle satisfied,
constructive/destructive interference at superposed source events).

*(1.3) Function-space rendering as wavefunction.* Chain of theorems level
$\mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{H}$ produces the wavefunction $\psi \in
L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ (Theorem
[W.1](#thm:W1-hilbert-space){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:W1-hilbert-space"}), which by construction satisfies
a wave equation (Schrödinger equation as forced theorem of dx₄/dt=ic;
Klein–Gordon equation as covariant form). The wavefunction is a wave
in the strict analytic sense.

Wave content is intrinsic to dx₄/dt = ic via the "$ic$" imaginary
rate, the Sphere expansion at rate $c$, and the wavefunction as
function-space rendering.

**Step 2: Particle content is intrinsic to dx₄/dt = ic.** The
McGucken Principle's differential is $d/dt$: a rate of change with
respect to a specific parameter time, at a specific event. This is
particle-mechanics content:

*(2.1) Per-event universality (Component C4).* The principle holds
at *every event* of $\mathcal{M}_G$ identically. An "event" is a
definite spacetime point $p = (t_p, \mathbf{x}_p)$: localized in
space, ordered in the parameter time. Particle-mechanics is by
definition the description of a system at localized events with
definite properties.

*(2.2) Definite rate of $x_4$-advance.* At each event, $dx_4/dt$ has
the definite value $ic$ (Component C1 with the perpendicularity
marker). A definite rate at a definite event is the particle-
mechanics content of a trajectory: the entity's $x_4$-coordinate
advances at rate $ic$ from the current event to the next.

*(2.3) Localized detection outcomes via Sphere–Sphere collision
(Theorem 7.7 of [MG-MH-2026]).* When two Spheres from apex events
meet head-on at a spatial-slice point, their $x_4$-expansion cancels
(anti-parallel head-on collision); the cancelled $x_4$-momenergy
redeposits as 3-spatial momenergy by four-momentum conservation;
both particles localize at the collision event. Definite spatial
outcomes at definite events are the particle-observation content.

Particle content is intrinsic to dx₄/dt = ic via the "$d/dt$"
trajectory-differential, Component C4 per-event universality, and
Sphere–Sphere collision producing localized outcomes.

**Step 3: Wick rotation as wave–particle transition mechanism.**
The Algebraic Channel presentation of a system emphasizes
particle-observation content (definite eigenvalues of position/
momentum, Born-rule outcomes, canonical commutators at spacetime
points). The Geometric Channel presentation of the same system
emphasizes wave-observation content (Sphere expansion, wavefunction
propagation, nonlocal correlations).

*(3.1) Forward Wick reveals wave content behind particle
presentation.* By Theorem
[W.9](#thm:wick-differential-response){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:wick-differential-response"}, forward Wick $t \to
-i\tau$ applied to Algebraic Channel content transforms:
- The oscillatory phase $e^{-iEt/\hbar}$ (particle-with-definite-
  energy presentation) into the dissipative decay $e^{-E\tau/\hbar}$
  (spatial spread with rate $E/\hbar$).
- The unitary group $U(t)$ (particle-mechanics trajectory content)
  into the contractive semigroup $T(\tau)$ (diffusion-equation
  wave content).
- The localized wavefunction at parameter time $t$ into a spatially
  spread configuration at parameter time $\tau$.

The transformation is Theorem
[W.10](#thm:wick-bidirectional-projection-identity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:wick-bidirectional-projection-identity"}(A): forward
Wick applied to Algebraic Channel presentation is $\Pi_A^{-1} \circ
\iota$, returning to the substrate parametrization in which the
wave content of dx₄/dt = ic is visible.

*(3.2) Inverse Wick produces particle outcome from wave
presentation.* By the same Theorem W.10, inverse Wick $\tau \to it$
applied to Geometric Channel content collapses the Sphere expansion
into local operator content. At a measurement event, this collapse is a physical process (measurement
as physical Wick rotation,
Theorem [1.44](#thm:measurement-as-physical-wick-rotation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:measurement-as-physical-wick-rotation"}) in which the
Sphere–Sphere collision (Theorem 7.7 of [MG-MH-2026]) converts
$x_4$-expansion (wave content) into 3-spatial localization (particle
content). The measurement event is the operational realization of
inverse Wick applied at the local collision event.

*(3.3) Bidirectional consistency.* Forward Wick's revelation of wave
content and inverse Wick's production of particle content are the
same operational fact seen in two directions. Applied together on
the same system, they reproduce the wave–particle transition cycle:
particle at emission event $\to$ wave in propagation $\to$ particle
at detection event. The three phases correspond to three
presentations of the same system: initial Algebraic Channel
(emission), Geometric Channel (propagation), final Algebraic Channel
(detection), with two Wick rotations mediating the transitions.

**Step 4: Dissolution of the 1927 wave–particle paradox at the
foundational level.** The wave–particle duality was articulated as
Bohr's *principle of complementarity* at the 1927 Solvay Conference:
wave and particle are mutually exclusive but jointly necessary
descriptions of quantum systems, with the experimental setup
determining which manifests. Bohr's articulation was
phenomenologically accurate but supplied no mechanism for the
duality; it treated it as a fact of nature to be
accepted.

Theorem W.10.B supplies the mechanism: the wave–particle duality
is the operational manifestation of the McGucken Principle
$\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$'s dual-channel character. The two
content types (wave-frequency from "$ic$"; particle-mechanics from
"$d/dt$") are both intrinsic to the single principle
and are simultaneously present at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$.
Wick rotation is the operational transition mechanism between the
two presentations. The duality is a diagnostic of the substrate's dual-channel character seen
through operational manifestation.

**Bohr was correct** that wave and particle are mutually exclusive
in any single experimental presentation and jointly necessary for
a complete description. **Bohr lacked** the mechanism carrying both
contents. **McGucken supplies the mechanism**: dx₄/dt = ic carries
both contents, with the Algebraic-Channel and Geometric-Channel
presentations being the two operational faces of the same substrate
principle. $\square$
:::

::: {#rmk:de-broglie-substrate-tick .remark}
*Remark W.10.B.A* (de Broglie's 1924 matter waves as substrate-tick
Compton oscillations of dx₄/dt = ic). de Broglie 1924 hypothesized

with frequency $\nu = mc^2/h$ and, when in motion at velocity $v$,

Under the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework (Theorem

mc^2/\hbar$. The Compton wavelength $\lambda_C = h/(mc)$ is the
substrate-tick advance $|\Delta x_4|$ per oscillation cycle. The
de Broglie wavelength $\lambda_{dB} = h/p$ at motion is the Lorentz-
boosted version of $\lambda_C$ (the boost carries the rest-frame

de Broglie's insight was empirically correct at the substrate-scale
level. He did not have the geometric substrate: the identification
of the "internal periodic phenomenon" as the $x_4$-advance
oscillation at Compton frequency, sourcing a McGucken Sphere at

de Broglie 1924's invariants ($\nu = mc^2/h$, $\lambda = h/p$) are
the substrate-tick invariants of dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem W.8).

**Point.** The wave-particle duality that de Broglie
proposed and Davisson–Germer confirmed is direct empirical evidence

::: {#rmk:double-slit-reinterpreted .remark}
*Remark W.10.B.B* (The double-slit experiment reinterpreted).
The double-slit experiment (Young 1801 for light; Davisson–Germer
1927, Tonomura 1989, Jönsson 1961 for electrons) is the canonical
demonstration of wave–particle duality. A source emits particles
one at a time; the particles pass through a two-slit barrier and
strike a detection screen; over many events an interference pattern
builds up, showing wave behavior between emission and detection but
particle behavior at emission and detection.

Under the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, the phases of the experiment map
directly onto Theorem W.10.B's presentations:

*(i) Emission event.* A definite Sphere-generation event at the
source. Algebraic Channel presentation: definite spacetime point
$p_{\text{emit}} \in \mathcal{M}_G$, particle-mechanics content
(the "$d/dt$" at $p_{\text{emit}}$). Particle observation.

*(ii) Propagation between slits and screen.* The McGucken Sphere
$\Sigma^+(p_{\text{emit}})$ expands at $+ic$ from the emission
event; the wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ in Hilbert space
propagates by unitary evolution (Schrödinger equation); the Sphere
wavefront encounters both slits (Sphere is a wavefront, not a
particle-with-position). Geometric Channel presentation: wave
propagation, interference at the superposition of paths through
both slits. **Wave observation.** (Under Wick reparametrization to
$\tau = x_4/c$, this presentation is manifestly diffusive with
$\sigma^2(\tau) = 2D\tau$; the wave-content is the Wick-rotated
Algebraic-Channel presentation.)

*(iii) Detection event.* A Sphere–Sphere collision event at the
detection screen (Theorem 7.7 of [MG-MH-2026]): the emitted Sphere
meets a detector Sphere (from a screen atom) head-on in $x_4$; the
$x_4$-expansion of both cancels; both localize at the collision
event. Algebraic Channel presentation: definite spacetime point
$p_{\text{detect}} \in \mathcal{M}_G$, particle-mechanics content
(the "$d/dt$" at $p_{\text{detect}}$). **Particle observation.**

*(iv) Interference pattern.* The distribution of detection events
over many trials reflects the Sphere-wavefront amplitude squared at
each spatial-slice point (Born rule at Theorem 7.7's collision
rate). The interference pattern is the direct visualization of the
Sphere-wavefront content over many repeated experiments —
observationally wave-like at the aggregate level.

**Point.** The double-slit experiment is not a paradox
but a diagnostic of dx₄/dt = ic's dual-channel character seen in
serial phases: particle at emission (Algebraic), wave in propagation
(Geometric), particle at detection (Algebraic), interference
pattern at aggregate (statistics of Geometric-Channel Sphere content
observed through Algebraic-Channel collision events). The
century-long puzzle of "when the wavefunction collapses" is dissolved
by identifying the collapse events as inverse-Wick collisions
(Theorem 7.7) at physical Sphere–Sphere collision moments, with
propagation between collision events described by forward-Wick-
compatible Sphere/wavefunction wave content.
:::

::: {#rmk:bohr-complementarity-recognition .remark}
*Remark W.10.B.C* (Bohr's complementarity as recognition without
mechanism). Bohr's 1927 principle of complementarity (Como lecture;
formal statement 1928, *Nature* 121, 580) is the philosophical
articulation of wave–particle duality: "The very nature of the
quantum theory thus forces us to regard the space-time coordination
and the claim of causality, the union of which characterizes the
classical theories, as complementary but exclusive features of the
description, symbolizing the idealization of observation and
definition respectively" (Bohr 1928). Bohr held that wave and
particle descriptions are mutually exclusive but jointly necessary,
with the experimental setup determining which manifests.

Under the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework, Bohr's complementarity is *correct as
recognition* but *incomplete as explanation*:

*Correct as recognition*: wave and particle are indeed mutually
exclusive in any single experimental presentation (Algebraic
presentation manifests particle content; Geometric presentation
manifests wave content; no single presentation manifests both
simultaneously — this is the Wick-rotation asymmetry of Theorem
W.10). And they are jointly necessary — a complete description
requires both (dx₄/dt = ic carries both wave and particle content).

*Incomplete as explanation*: Bohr treated the duality as a
fact of nature to be accepted, not as a diagnostic
signature of an underlying mechanism. Bohr had no proposal for
what carried both contents; his complementarity was
phenomenological, not mechanistic.

The McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework's contribution: **supply the mechanism that
Bohr's complementarity lacked**. The mechanism is dx₄/dt = ic:
the "$d/dt$" carries the particle content (localized events with
definite rates); the "$ic$" carries the wave content (Compton-
frequency oscillations, Sphere expansion at rate $c$). Both are
present in the single principle. The dual-channel character is
Wick-mediated: forward Wick reveals wave, inverse Wick produces
particle. Bohr's complementarity is dissolved as diagnostic into a
mechanism.

**Historical positioning.** Bohr 1927 was operating in the same
situation as Wightman 1956 (imported W6 as unexplained
axiom) and Osterwalder–Schrader 1973 (imported reflection positivity
as unexplained axiom): each identified a foundational asymmetric
content and articulated it in the vocabulary of their period without
being able to derive it from a deeper principle. Bohr's
complementarity, Wightman's W6, and OS reflection positivity are
three articulations of the same underlying content — the
$+ic$-orientation of dx₄/dt = ic and its dual-channel character —
seen through three different disciplinary vocabularies.
:::

::: {#rmk:wave-particle-duality-dissolved .remark}
*Remark W.10.B.D* (The century-long wave–particle paradox
dissolved). The wave–particle duality has been carried as a
puzzle of quantum mechanics for one century (1905
Einstein photoelectric to present). Every foundational discussion of
quantum mechanics has to address it; every interpretation of
quantum mechanics has to reconcile it; every philosophical
treatment of quantum mechanics has to say something about it. It
is the archetypal quantum-mechanical strangeness.

Under Theorem W.10.B, the puzzle is dissolved at the foundational
level. Wave and particle are two operational presentations of the same underlying substrate content of $\tfrac{dx_4}{dt} = ic$, not two irreducibly different natures. Wick
rotation is the operational transition mechanism between them.
Neither is fundamental; both are Wick-related presentations of the
Principle at every event.

**Symmetry with the projection theorem dissolution of
the measurement problem.** In §Wick.5
(Theorem [W.11](#thm:measurement-problem-as-inverse-wick-residue){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:measurement-problem-as-inverse-wick-residue"}) the
century-long measurement problem is diagnosed as inverse-Wick
residue: the interpretive impasse exists because the algebra cannot
reconstruct the Sphere–Sphere collision mechanism that inverse Wick
collapsed away. Here in Theorem W.10.B, the century-long wave–
particle duality is diagnosed as dual-channel manifestation of the
McGucken Principle: the duality exists because dx₄/dt = ic has both
"$d/dt$" (particle) and "$ic$" (wave) contents simultaneously
present at every event, with Wick rotation as the operational
transition.

The two dissolutions are parallel: both identify a century-long
puzzle as the operational signature of the McGucken
Principle's dual-channel character seen through Wick rotation. The
measurement problem is the *diagnostic* signature (why the
interpretive impasse existed); the wave–particle duality is the
*constructive* signature (how the duality of natures directly
manifests). Together they establish that the two central foundational
puzzles of twentieth-century quantum mechanics — the measurement
problem and the wave–particle duality — are the same underlying
McGucken Principle content seen in two aspects.

**The framework's contribution**: two of the century's central
foundational puzzles are dissolved by the same identification of dx₄/dt = ic as the substrate underneath both
channels' operational manifestations, with Wick rotation as the
mechanism of transition. What was two puzzles becomes one
identification.

### §Wick.4.C The Algebraic Channel as observer's frame witnessing $x_4$-expansion; the Geometric Channel as object's frame riding the $x_4$-expanding wavefront {#sec:observer-object-frames}

Theorem W.10.B established that wave–particle duality is the operational
manifestation of the McGucken Principle's dual-channel character at the
observational level. The present section identifies what the two
channels observationally *are* in terms of the observer/object
distinction: **the Algebraic Channel is the observer's frame witnessing
$x_4$-expansion pass through, extracting the substrate-tick invariances
as conservation laws; the Geometric Channel is the object's frame
