classes, and the global-section/triviality equivalence used in the
bundle-triviality theorem for magnetic monopole absence.

**Naber, G. L.** (2012). *The Geometry of Minkowski Spacetime: An
Introduction to the Mathematics of the Special Theory of Relativity*,
2nd edition. Springer, Applied Mathematical Sciences vol. 92.
<https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4419-7838-7>. Standard
graduate reference for the Minkowski metric, the $SO^+(1,3)$ symmetry
group, and the signature-$(+,+,+,-)$ versus signature-$(+,-,-,-)$
conventions for Lorentzian spacetime.

**Misner, C. W., Thorne, K. S. & Wheeler, J. A.** (1973). *Gravitation*.
W. H. Freeman; reprinted Princeton University Press (2017).
<https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691177793/gravitation>.
The standard graduate reference for general relativity, including the
Schwarzschild geometry, the event horizon as coordinate singularity at
$r = 2GM/c^2$, and the geometric-optics treatment of radial null
geodesics in spherically symmetric vacuum spacetimes.

**Faraday, M.** (1832). *Experimental Researches in Electricity*. First
Series, *Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London* 122:
125--162; collected as *Experimental Researches in Electricity*, 3
vols., London: Bernard Quaritch, 1839--1855. Reprinted Dover
Publications, New York (1965). Faraday's articulation of lines of force
as a real physical structure threading space --- the foundational
geometric-propagation reading of electromagnetism, prefiguring the
Geometric Channel (geometric) tradition.
<https://doi.org/10.1098/rstl.1832.0006>

**Roberval, G. P. de** (posthumous, 1693). *Traité de géométrie* and
works in the synthetic-geometric tradition opposed to Cartesian
algebraic geometry. Mathematician at the Collège Royal in Paris, one of
the principal proponents of the view that Greek synthetic geometry was
the highest form of mathematical reasoning, against Descartes' programme
of algebraic reduction. See L. Auger, *Un savant méconnu, Gilles
Personne de Roberval (1602--1675)*, Paris: Blanchard (1962).

**Desargues, G.** (1639). *Brouillon project d'une atteinte aux
événements des rencontres du cone avec un plan*. Paris. The founding
text of projective geometry; Desargues, like Roberval, regarded Greek
synthetic geometry as the superior mathematical method and resisted the
Cartesian algebraic reduction. Modern critical edition: R. Taton,
*L'œuvre mathématique de G. Desargues*, Presses Universitaires de France
(1951).

**Pais, A.** (1982). *Subtle Is the Lord: The Science and the Life of
Albert Einstein.* Oxford University Press. ISBN 0-19-853907-X. The
canonical scientific biography of Einstein, including detailed
historical analysis of the development of special relativity, general
relativity, and the deepening of the geometric reading of physics.
<https://global.oup.com/academic/product/subtle-is-the-lord-9780192806727>

**Mermin, N. D.** (April 1985). *Is the Moon There When Nobody Looks?
Reality and the Quantum Theory.* Physics Today 38(4): 38--47. The
classic exposition of Bell's theorem and quantum nonlocality for a wide
physics audience, framing the EPR-Bohm-Bell experimental signature as
the empirical signature of nonlocal correlations.
<https://doi.org/10.1063/1.880968>

**Joos, E. & Zeh, H. D.** (1985). The emergence of classical properties
through interaction with the environment. *Zeitschrift für Physik B
Condensed Matter* **59**, 223--243.
<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01725541>. The foundational
paper on environment-induced decoherence as the mechanism by which
classical properties emerge from quantum systems through entanglement
with environmental degrees of freedom; widely cited as the canonical
reference for the decoherence programme alongside Zurek's
contemporaneous work.

**Maudlin, T.** (1996). Space-Time in the Quantum World. In *Bohmian
Mechanics and Quantum Theory: An Appraisal*, eds. J. T. Cushing,
A. Fine, and S. Goldstein, Boston Studies in the Philosophy of Science
vol. 184, Kluwer/Springer, pp. 285--307.
<https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-94-015-8715-0_19>. The
foundational philosophical critique of Bohmian mechanics on the
preferred-foliation problem: any Bohmian theory compatible with
relativistic phenomena requires a distinguished foliation of spacetime,
which is either additional absolute structure in tension with the spirit
of Lorentz invariance or covariantly-derived in ways that have not
achieved consensus acceptance. The critique has generated a substantial
Bohmian response literature (Dürr--Goldstein--Münch-Berndl--Zanghì;
Nikolić; Galvan; Struyve--Tumulka) and remains unresolved to consensus
satisfaction in thirty years. See also Maudlin's *Quantum Non-Locality
and Relativity* (Blackwell, 1st ed. 1994; 3rd ed. 2011) for the full
programmatic treatment of nonlocality, relativity, and the requirements of any satisfactory resolution.

**Maudlin, T.** (2011). *Quantum Non-Locality and Relativity:
Metaphysical Intimations of Modern Physics*, 3rd edition.
Wiley-Blackwell. ISBN 978-1-4443-3127-5. The systematic monograph
developing Maudlin's four programmatic theses (T1)--(T4) on the
relationship between quantum nonlocality and special relativity.
<https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9781444396973>

**Bohm, D.** (1952). *A Suggested Interpretation of the Quantum Theory
in Terms of "Hidden" Variables. I, II.* Physical Review, 85(2):
166--179, 180--193. The foundational papers of Bohmian mechanics,
recovering and extending de Broglie's 1927 pilot-wave theory.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.85.166>,
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.85.180>

**Dürr, D., Goldstein, S., & Zanghì, N.** (1992). *Quantum Equilibrium
and the Origin of Absolute Uncertainty.* Journal of Statistical Physics,
67(5--6): 843--907. The typicality-argument derivation of the Born rule
within Bohmian mechanics. <https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01049004>

**Dürr, D., Goldstein, S., Münch-Berndl, K., & Zanghì, N.** (1999).
*Hypersurface Bohm--Dirac Models.* Physical Review A, 60(4): 2729--2736.
The proposal to introduce a preferred foliation as additional
fundamental structure in relativistic Bohmian mechanics.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.60.2729>

**Nikolić, H.** (2012). *Bohmian mechanics in relativistic quantum
mechanics, quantum field theory and string theory.* Journal of Physics:
Conference Series, 67: 012035. The proposal that a Lorentz-covariant
foliation can be determined from the wave function itself.
<https://doi.org/10.1088/1742-6596/67/1/012035>

**Weinberg, S.** (1995). *The Quantum Theory of Fields*, Vol. I:
Foundations. Cambridge University Press.
<https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/quantum-theory-of-fields/22988A1ED7BA0C7D7A5E15BBAF4F7C0D>

**Uhlenbeck, G. E. & Ornstein, L. S.** (1930). *On the theory of the

Penrose, R. (1979). Singularities and Time-Asymmetry, in *General

<https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/general-relativity/A55EE5BFD8B3D04A8C04C5F0E81DCA17>
Wheeler, J. A. (1989--1993). Princeton physics; Schwarzschild

<https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/4958>
Einstein, A. (1915). Die Feldgleichungen der Gravitation.
*Sitzungsberichte der Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu
Berlin*, 844. <https://einsteinpapers.press.princeton.edu/vol6-doc/>
Einstein, A. (1905). Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper. *Annalen der
Physik* **17**, 891.
<https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/andp.19053221004>

**Einstein, A.** (10 June 1933). *On the Method of Theoretical Physics.*
The Herbert Spencer Lecture, delivered at Oxford, 10 June 1933.
Published Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1933; reprinted in *Philosophy of
Science* 1(2): 163--169 (April 1934), see p. 165 for the canonical
formulation; reprinted in *Mein Weltbild* (Amsterdam: Querido Verlag,
1934) and in *Ideas and Opinions* (Crown, 1954). The canonical statement
(p. 165): "It can scarcely be denied that the supreme goal of all theory
is to make the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as
possible without having to surrender the adequate representation of a
single datum of experience." <https://doi.org/10.1086/286316>

**Einstein, A.** (27 January 1921). *Geometrie und Erfahrung (Geometry
and Experience).* Address to the Prussian Academy of Sciences, Berlin.
Published Berlin: Julius Springer, 1921. English translation in
*Sidelights on Relativity* (Methuen & Co. Ltd., 1922), pp. 25--56. The
address from which the canonical Einstein statement on Hilbert's
axiomatic method derives (p. 233 of the English translation): "As far as
the propositions of mathematics refer to reality, they are not certain;
and as far as they are certain, they do not refer to reality.
... Complete clarity as to this state of things became common property
only through that trend in mathematics, which is known by the name of
'axiomatics.' The progress achieved by axiomatics consists in its having
neatly separated the logical-formal from its objective or intuitive
content; according to axiomatics the logical-formal alone forms the
subject matter of mathematics, which is not concerned with the intuitive
or other content associated with the logical-formal."
<https://archive.org/details/sidelightsonrelativityeinstein>

**Descartes, R.** (1637). *La Géométrie.* Appendix to *Discours de la
méthode pour bien conduire sa raison, et chercher la vérité dans les
sciences* (*Discourse on the Method of Rightly Conducting One's Reason
and Seeking Truth in the Sciences*). Leiden: Jan Maire. The founding
text of analytic geometry; the first work to propose the unification of
algebra and geometry into a single subject, with geometric shapes
translated into algebraic equations and algebraic equations visualised
as geometric curves --- the synthesis whose differential dissolution
under the McGucken-Wick rotation distinguishes Algebraic Channel
(Cartesian/algebraic half) from Geometric Channel (geometric/shape half) in the
McGucken dual-channel architecture. English translation: D.E. Smith &
M.L. Latham (1925), *The Geometry of René Descartes*, Open Court / Dover
(1954). <https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/59>

**Hilbert, D.** (8 August 1900). *Mathematische Probleme: Vortrag,
gehalten auf dem internationalen Mathematiker-Kongreß zu Paris 1900.*
Address to the International Congress of Mathematicians, Sorbonne,
Paris. Published *Nachrichten von der Königlichen Gesellschaft der
Wissenschaften zu Göttingen*, 1900, pp. 253--297; English translation in
*Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society* 8 (1902): 437--479.
Problem 6 is "Mathematical Treatment of the Axioms of Physics": "The
investigations on the foundations of geometry suggest the problem: To
treat in the same manner, by means of axioms, those physical sciences in
which already today mathematics plays an important part; in the first
rank are the theory of probabilities and mechanics."
<https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9904-1902-00923-3>

**Hilbert, D.** (11 September 1917, published 1918). *Axiomatisches
Denken (Axiomatic Thinking).* Address delivered at the annual meeting of
the Swiss Mathematical Society in Zürich, 11 September 1917. Published
*Mathematische Annalen* 78 (1918): 405--415. English translation by
Joong Fang in *Hilbert--Towards a Philosophy of Modern Mathematics II*
(Paideia Press, 1970); reprinted in F. Ferreira, R. Kahle, G. Sommaruga,
eds., *Axiomatic Thinking I* (Springer, 2022), Ch. 1.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01457115>

**The Gospel According to John** 8:32 (King James Version, 1611). "And
ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free." Greek
original: *καὶ γνώσεσθε τὴν ἀλήθειαν, καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια ἐλευθερώσει ὑμᾶς.*
The Holy Bible, Authorized (King James) Version, public domain.
<https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John+8%3A32&version=KJV>

**Mitsch, C.** (2024). *Von Neumann's Axiomatic Completion of Quantum
Mechanics.* Lecture in the Foundations of Physics Seminar. Source of
Einstein's 1921 quote on Hilbert's axiomatic method as the cleanly
separating principle of mathematics from physical content, and of
Hilbert's 1917 statement on the role of axioms in the development of a
field of knowledge. <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vbIwPeIhiTc>

**Melville, H.** (1851). *Moby-Dick; or, The Whale.* Harper & Brothers,
New York. Project Gutenberg edition:
<https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2701>

**Homer.** (ca. 8th century BCE). *The Iliad of Homer.* Translated by
Richmond Lattimore (1951), University of Chicago Press. ISBN
978-0-226-46940-0. The Greek-text source for the Achillean concept of
*kleos* (κλέος), the imperishable glory pursued by the warrior who
chooses meaningful action and remembrance over comfortable longevity.
<https://press.uchicago.edu/ucp/books/book/chicago/I/bo3635806.html>

**Shakespeare, W.** (ca. 1599--1601). *The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of
Denmark.* Arden Shakespeare critical edition, ed. A. Thompson &
N. Taylor (2006). Bloomsbury. ISBN 978-1-904271-33-8. Act 1, Scene 5,
lines 189--190 (Folger lines 210--211): "The time is out of joint. O
cursèd spite, / That ever I was born to set it right!" --- Hamlet's
lament after the Ghost of his father charges him to set right the rotten
state of Denmark. <https://www.bloomsbury.com/uk/hamlet-9781472518385/>

**Einstein, A.** (1905). Ist die Trägheit eines Körpers von seinem
Energieinhalt abhängig? *Annalen der Physik* **18**, 639--641.
<https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/andp.19053231314>. The
inertia-of-energy paper, deriving $E_0 = mc^2$ from the relativity
principle and Maxwell's equations as a corollary of the
special-relativity paper. Klein, F. (1872). Vergleichende Betrachtungen
über neuere geometrische Forschungen (Erlangen Programme). *Math. Ann.*
**43**, 63 (publ. 1893).
<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01446615> Gödel, K. (1931).
Über formal unentscheidbare Sätze. *Monatsh. Math. Phys.* **38**, 173.
<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01700692> Newton, I.
(1687). *Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica*. Royal Society.
<https://archive.org/details/100878576> Euclid (c. 300 BCE). *Elements*.
<https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/Books/Euclid/Euclid.html> Le Verrier,
U. J. J. (1859). Lettre de M. Le Verrier sur la théorie de Mercure.
*Comptes Rendus* **49**, 379.
<https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3018f> Pound, R. V. & Rebka,
G. A. (1959). Gravitational Red-Shift in Nuclear Resonance.

and Feynman. *Physical Review* **75**, 486--502.
<https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.75.486>. The
foundational paper introducing the Dyson series expansion of the

together with Wick's 1950 theorem on time-ordered products, this paper
establishes the algebraic foundation of the Feynman-diagram apparatus of
perturbative quantum field theory. Boltzmann, L. (1872). Weitere Studien

<https://archive.org/details/elementaryprinci00gibbrich> Mac Lane, S.
(1971). *Categories for the Working Mathematician*. Springer-Verlag,
Graduate Texts in Mathematics 5. (2nd ed. 1998.)
<https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4757-4721-8> Penrose, R. &

and Relativistic Fields*. Cambridge University Press.

31. <https://doi.org/10.1017/9781316678626> Werner, R. F. & Wolf, M. M.
(2001). Bell inequalities and entanglement. *Quantum Information &
Computation* **1**(3), 1--25. <https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0107093>

**Aaronson, S.** (2004). Is Quantum Mechanics An Island In Theoryspace?
In A. Khrennikov (ed.), *Quantum Theory: Reconsideration of Foundations*
**2**, Växjö University Press. Preprint at arXiv:quant-ph/0401062.
<https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0401062>. Examines whether quantum
mechanics is theoretically isolated by varying the Born rule's exponent,
considering generalisations $P \propto |\psi|^p$ for $p \neq 2$ (in
particular the rank-$4$ pairing $|\psi|^4$) and other higher-rank
probability laws; finds that variants violate either no-signaling,
computational tractability of state evolution, or the polynomial scaling
of distinguishability. Cited in the present textbook
(Lemma [9.13](#lem:bilinearity-rank2){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:bilinearity-rank2"}) as the canonical reference for
higher-rank probability-law variants excluded by the rank-$2$ character
of the Minkowski metric.

**Wheeler, J. A.** (1983). Law Without Law. In J. A. Wheeler &
W. H. Zurek (eds.), *Quantum Theory and Measurement* (Princeton
University Press, Princeton, NJ), pp. 182--213. The 1983 essay
containing the beam-splitter and delayed-choice analysis (Wheeler's
Figure 4 with routes labelled $A$ and $B$), the cosmological-scale
delayed-choice experiment (Wheeler's Figure 6), the "self-excited
circuit" diagram (Wheeler's Figure 22.13), the Leibniz invocation
*omnibus ex nihilo ducendis sufficit unum*, and Wheeler's Two Tests close
calling for a derivation of quantum theory from the requirement that
everything have a way to come into being. The most explicit programmatic
statement in Wheeler's published corpus of the criteria a successful
foundational physical principle must satisfy.
<https://gwern.net/doc/science/physics/1983-wheeler.pdf>

**McGucken, E.** (1998--99). *Notes Towards a Dissertation Appendix on
the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$*. University of North Carolina at
Chapel Hill. Doctoral dissertation appendix establishing priority for
the foundational principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the fourth-dimensional
dynamical principle of which $x_4 = ict$ is the integrated coordinate
shadow. The principle was first formulated in correspondence and
lectures with John Archibald Wheeler at Princeton in the late 1980s and
formalised in the 1998--99 dissertation appendix as the foundational
principle of what was then called Moving Dimensions Theory, subsequently
developed as Light Time Dimension Theory and as the McGucken $\tfrac{dx_{4}}{dt}= ic$ framework.
ProQuest 9840958.

**Dirac, P. A. M.** (1930). *The Principles of Quantum Mechanics*.
Oxford University Press. (4th ed. 1958, revised printing 1967.) The
foundational text axiomatizing quantum mechanics in transformation-theory
form; bra-ket notation was introduced in Dirac (1939), *Math. Proc. Camb.
Phil. Soc.* **35**, 416--418, and entered the book at the 3rd edition
(1947). Establishes the position and momentum operators as having
continuous spectra, with the kinematical formalism built on
rigged-Hilbert-space distributional eigenvectors.
<https://archive.org/details/PrinciplesOfQuantumMechanics>

**Gelfand, I. M. & Vilenkin, N. Ya.** (1964). *Generalized Functions,
Volume 4: Applications of Harmonic Analysis*. Academic Press (English
translation of the Russian original). The rigorous mathematical
foundation of the rigged Hilbert space (Gelfand triple)
$\Phi \subset \mathcal{H}\subset \Phi^*$ accommodating distributional
eigenvectors of operators with continuous spectra; supplies the
distributional completeness relation
$\int |x\rangle\langle x|\,d^3x = \mathbb{1}$ and the orthonormality
$\langle x_0 | x_1 \rangle = \delta^3(x_0 - x_1)$ used throughout
standard quantum mechanics.
<https://archive.org/details/generalizedfunct0004gelf>

**Bohm, A.** (1978). *The Rigged Hilbert Space and Quantum Mechanics*.
Springer Lecture Notes in Physics, vol. 78. The standard reference for
the rigged Hilbert space (RHS) formulation of quantum mechanics,
providing the rigorous distributional framework for position and
momentum eigenstates and the continuous-spectrum operator theory used in
the Dirac--von Neumann axiomatization.
<https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-08843-7>

**Born, M., Heisenberg, W. & Jordan, P.** (1925). Zur Quantenmechanik
II. *Z. Phys.* **35**, 557--615.
<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01379806> The
"Dreimänner"-paper completing matrix mechanics: the canonical
commutation relation $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ is derived as a
consequence of the matrix-mechanical noncommutativity
established in Born--Jordan (1925) and Heisenberg (1925); the canonical
commutator with the explicit factor $i\hbar$ first appears here as the
foundational algebraic structure of quantum mechanics.

**Robertson, H. P.** (1929). The Uncertainty Principle. *Phys. Rev.*
**34**, 163--164.
<https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.34.163>
Robertson's generalisation of the Heisenberg uncertainty principle:
$\sigma_A \sigma_B \geq \tfrac{1}{2}|\langle [\hat{A}, \hat{B}] \rangle|$
for any two Hermitian operators $\hat{A}, \hat{B}$. The factor $1/2$ on
the right-hand side of $\sigma_q \sigma_p \geq \hbar/2$ is supplied by
the Cauchy--Schwarz step applied to the commutator
$[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$.

**Thomas, L. H.** (1927). The Motion of the Spinning Electron. *Nature*
**117**, 514. <https://www.nature.com/articles/117514a0> The Thomas
precession: a relativistic kinematic correction that supplies the factor
of $1/2$ in the spin-orbit coupling of atomic spectra. In the McGucken
framework, Thomas precession is the empirical record of the Wigner
rotation (composition of non-parallel Lorentz boosts) at the chain of theorems
level of electronic orbital motion.

**Wigner, E. P.** (1939). Wigner rotation content of [@Wigner1939]. The
non-parallel-boost composition residual rotation, derived as part of
Wigner's analysis of the inhomogeneous Lorentz group representations.

**Maslov, V. P.** (1965). *Theory of Perturbations and Asymptotic
Methods.* Moscow State University (Russian original); English
translation later expanded as *Théorie des perturbations et méthodes
asymptotiques* (Dunod, Paris, 1972). The introduction of the Maslov
index $\mu$ measuring the topological invariants of Lagrangian
submanifolds, correcting the Bohr--Sommerfeld semiclassical quantisation
rule to $\oint p\,dq = (n + \mu/4)h$. Each classical turning-point
traversal contributes $\mu/4$ to the corrected quantisation, supplying a
quarter-quantum of action per turning point.

**Arnold, V. I.** (1967). Characteristic class entering in quantization
conditions. *Funct. Anal. Appl.* **1**, 1--14.
<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01075861> Topological
reformulation of the Maslov index as a characteristic class on
Lagrangian submanifolds; the $\mu/4$ correction to Bohr--Sommerfeld is
identified as the first Chern class of the canonical bundle.

**Rauch, H., Treimer, W. & Bonse, U.** (1974) and **Rauch, H.,
Zeilinger, A., Badurek, G., Wilfing, A., Bauspiess, W. & Bonse, U.**
(1975). Verification of coherent spinor rotation of fermions.
*Phys. Lett. A* **54**, 425--427.
<https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0375960175907025>
Neutron-interferometric demonstration of the $4\pi$-rotation closure of
spin-1/2: a $2\pi$ rotation of the spinor wavefunction produces a sign
change (phase factor $-1$), requiring a full $4\pi$ for full closure.
Empirical confirmation of the $SU(2) \to SO(3)$ double-cover topology.

**Werner, S. A., Colella, R., Overhauser, A. W. & Eagen, C. F.** (1975).
Observation of the Phase Shift of a Neutron Due to Precession in a
Magnetic Field. *Phys. Rev. Lett.* **35**, 1053--1055.
<https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.35.1053>
Independent neutron-interferometric measurement of the spin-1/2
$4\pi$-rotation closure, simultaneous with
[@RauchWernerColellaOverhauser1975]. The two experiments together
established the empirical content of the $SU(2) \to SO(3)$ double cover.

**Tonomura, A., Osakabe, N., Matsuda, T., Kawasaki, T., Endo, J., Yano,
S. & Yamada, H.** (1986). Evidence for Aharonov--Bohm effect with
magnetic field completely shielded from electron wave.
*Phys. Rev. Lett.* **56**, 792--795.
<https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.792>
Definitive empirical confirmation of the Aharonov--Bohm effect using
superconducting magnetic-flux shielding and electron holography;
established that the phase shift $\exp(ie\Phi/\hbar)$ around a region of
confined magnetic flux is physical, with the electron wave never
traversing a region of non-zero magnetic field.

**Wu, T. T. & Yang, C. N.** (1975). Concept of nonintegrable phase
factors and global formulation of gauge fields. *Phys. Rev. D* **12**,
3845--3857.
<https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.12.3845>
Reformulation of the Aharonov--Bohm phase and the Dirac monopole
quantisation condition as manifestations of a single mathematical
structure: the holonomy of a connection on a $U(1)$ principal fiber
bundle over spacetime. The most ambitious pre-Berry unification of
gauge-theoretic non-closures.

**Simon, B.** (1983). Holonomy, the quantum adiabatic theorem, and
Berry's phase. *Phys. Rev. Lett.* **51**, 2167--2170.
<https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.51.2167>
Identification of Berry's phase as the holonomy of a connection on a
principal $U(1)$ bundle over parameter space; completes the mathematical
formulation of the geometric-phase phenomenon.

**Wilczek, F. & Zee, A.** (1984). Appearance of gauge structure in
simple dynamical systems. *Phys. Rev. Lett.* **52**, 2111--2114.
<https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111>
Extension of Berry's framework to non-Abelian gauge structures and
degenerate adiabatic evolution; the non-Abelian Wilczek--Zee phase
generalises Berry's $U(1)$ holonomy to higher-rank holonomy on
degenerate-eigenspace bundles.
:::
